examples.igbo: Biko kpọmì ntu a n'elu osisi ahụ.
examples.english: Please knock this nail into that wood.

examples.igbo: Onye kpọmì ntu ahụ n'ọgbọ a?
examples.english: Who knocked that nail into this floor?

note: Standard usage of the verb stem -kpọmì.

examples.igbo: Ndị okenye nòkọba ọnū n'èzí n'ehihie.
examples.english: The elders sat together outside in the afternoon.

examples.igbo: Gịnị ka ha nòkọba ọnū na-ekwurịta?
examples.english: What are they sitting together discussing?

note: Compound verb describing group assembly.

examples.igbo: Òji uwe ahụ pụtara ìhè n'anyanwụ.
examples.english: The blackness of that dress stood out in the sun.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ òji anwụrụ ọkụ ahụ na mbara igwe?
examples.english: Do you see the blackness of that smoke in the sky?

note: Noun denoting blackness.

examples.igbo: Onye ozi ahụ lu àrụ ozi ọma n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: The messenger received the good news in the morning.

examples.igbo: Ego ahụ ò lu àrụ onye nwe ya?
examples.english: Did that money reach its owner?

note: Covers both senses of receiving and reaching.

examples.igbo: Debe afà nnà ị n'elu akwụkwọ ahụ.
examples.english: Write your surname on top of that paper.

examples.igbo: Gịnị bụ afà nnà ị n'ezie?
examples.english: What is your father's name really?

note: Refers to surname or father's name.

examples.igbo: Nne m na-akọrọ m akụkọ irò n'abalị.
examples.english: My mother tells me fables at night.

examples.igbo: Otu akụkọ irò kwuru na mbe nwere eze.
examples.english: A certain myth said that tortoises have teeth.

note: Standard folk story and fable term.

examples.igbo: Nàrị̀gà mmadụ bịara n'ememe ahụ taa.
examples.english: Hundreds of people came to the festival today.

examples.igbo: E nwere nàrị̀gà ji n'ogbè ahụ?
examples.english: Are there hundreds of yams in that barn?

note: Used to denote hundreds.

gloss: set fire to; burn off with fire

examples.igbo: Ndị ọrụ ugbo kpọ̄nyē ọ̄kụ̄ n'ahịhịa ahụ.
examples.english: The farmers set fire to that weed.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara i ji kpọ̄nyē ọ̄kụ̄ n'etiti ubi?
examples.english: Why did you burn off the middle of the farm with fire?

note: Action of burning off land or setting fire.

gloss: (fig.) have a say in; have influence

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ na-enwe àgbà n'ihe gbasara ala.
examples.english: That man has a say in land matters.

examples.igbo: Onye nwere àgbà n'ime ezinụlọ a?
examples.english: Who has influence in this family?

note: Idiomatic use meaning to have influence or a say.

gloss: fall upon violently; pounce upon (of people fighting)

examples.igbo: Ndị ọhi ahụ dakpọrọ ya n'ime ụlọ ya
examples.english: The thieves pounced upon him violently inside his house.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere unu ji dakpọọ nwoke ahụ n'okporo ụzọ?
examples.english: Why did you people fall upon that man violently on the road?

note: dakpò is relatively uncommon, but the usage matches regional violence contexts.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-egwu nwa òlukpùlu n'ezi n'uhuruchi
examples.english: Children are playing blindman's buff outside in the evening.

examples.igbo: Ò nwere onye ma otu esi egwu nwa òlukpùlu a?
examples.english: Is there anyone who knows how to play this blindman's buff?

note: Traditional children's game term.

examples.igbo: Ọ tichàpụ̀rụ́ agwọ ahụ tupu o ruo n'ụlọ
examples.english: He beat the snake off entirely before it reached the house.

examples.igbo: Ndị agha tichàpụ̀rụ́ ndị iro nọ n'ebe ahụ
examples.english: The soldiers beat the enemies there off entirely.

note: Verb suffix combination is idiomatic.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ gbatọrọ eriri dị n'aka ya
examples.english: The child broke the rope in his hand.

examples.igbo: Ònye gbatọrọ akwa ọhụrụ a m kwụnyere?
examples.english: Who tore this new cloth I hung up?

note: Standard transitive verb usage.

gloss: live to fill up a place; occupy enough

examples.igbo: Ewu na atụrụ bijuru n'ogige ebe ahụ
examples.english: Goats and sheep lived to fill up the space in that compound.

examples.igbo: Ndị mmadụ bijuru n'ahịa tupu mmiri ezoro
examples.english: People occupied enough space in the market before it rained.

note: biju is a rare regional verb meaning to occupy or fill a space fully.

examples.igbo: Nwa nwoke ahụ dị kà àgàsị ọ na-arịa ọrịa
examples.english: That boy is as if he is sick.

examples.igbo: Ihe o kwuru dị kà àgàsị ọ maara ihe gbasara anyị
examples.english: What he said is as if he knew what concerns us.

note: Idiomatic phrasal construction.

examples.igbo: Ha ga-enye ụgbọ ala ahụ n'ọkshòm echi
examples.english: They will put that car up for auction tomorrow.

examples.igbo: Ònye nwetara ihe ahụ n'ọkshòm nke taa?
examples.english: Who won that item at today's auction?

note: Loan word from English commonly used in trade.

gloss: breaking something by stepping on it

examples.igbo: Zọbì akwa m dina n'ala ozugbo
examples.english: Stop breaking my cloth on the ground by stepping on it immediately.

examples.igbo: Ọ zọbìrị mkpụrụ osisi ndị ahụ site n'amaghị ama
examples.english: He broke those fruits by stepping on them unknowingly.

note: Action describes destructive stepping.

gloss: cause an abomination; do a taboo, do evil

examples.igbo: O mere arụ̄ n'ime obodo mgbe o zuuru ehi
examples.english: He caused an abomination in the town when he stole a cow.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere o ji mee arụ̄ dị otú a?
examples.english: Why did he do such an abomination?

note: Standard cultural phrasing for committing a taboo.

examples.igbo: Biko tikùo nne gị ka o nyere gị aka
examples.english: Please call upon your mother so she can help you.

examples.igbo: Onye ka ọ tikùrụ n'etiti abalị?
examples.english: Who did he call upon in the middle of the night?

note: Standard verb for shouting out or calling upon someone.

examples.igbo: Biko, chìchapụ ihe ahụ edere n'elu osisi ojii.
examples.english: Please, wipe off what was written on the blackboard.

examples.igbo: Onye nkuzi anyị chìchapụrụ ahịrị ndị ahụ n'akwụkwọ m.
examples.english: Our teacher ruled off those lines in my book.

gloss: wealth; riches; possession; inheritance (from -kù bring into use)

examples.igbo: Ọkụ nna ya riri baara ya uru n'oge ndụ.
examples.english: The inheritance of his father's wealth benefited him in life.

examples.igbo: Nwa agbọghọ a nwere ọkụ dị ukwuu n'aka ya.
examples.english: This young woman possesses great riches in her hands.

note: The word ọkù for wealth is less common in everyday spoken Igbo compared to aku, but valid.

gloss: cause laughter; be absurd; jest; trifle; amuse

examples.igbo: Atụmatụ ya na-akpa amụ n'ihu ọha.
examples.english: His plan causes laughter in public.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka nwatakịrị a kpa amụ mgbe ọ na-arụ ọrụ.
examples.english: Do not let this child trifle while working.

examples.igbo: Yipụ uwe ruru unyi tupu i banye n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: Take off the dirty clothes before you enter the house.

examples.igbo: Onye na-egwu egwu yipụrụ okpu ya ijikele ndị mmadụ.
examples.english: The performer took off his cap to greet the people.

examples.igbo: Àpàtàpà ụkwụ ya bu ibu n'ihi ọrụ ugbo.
examples.english: His thighs are large because of farming.

examples.igbo: Ọ nọdụrụ ala wee kechie ákwà n'àpàtàpà ụkwụ ya.
examples.english: She sat down and tied a cloth around her thigh.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-awụ ọsọ n'ezi n'ụtụtụ taa.
examples.english: The children are racing outside this morning.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere o ji wụọ ọsọ mgbe ọ hụrụ nkịta ahụ?
examples.english: Why did he race when he saw that dog?

examples.igbo: Anụ e siri esi na-atọ ākpị̄rị̄ n'ahịa.
examples.english: The cooked meat is appetizing at the market.

examples.igbo: Ihe ụtọ a ọ̀ na-atọ gị ākpị̄rị̄ n'ọnụ?
examples.english: Does this sweet thing appeal to your palate?

gloss: exclamation of pleasure on meeting a friend after long separation

examples.igbo: Anya ī! Ebe a ka i nọ kemgbe afọ ole na ole?
examples.english: Oh, what a surprise! Is this where you have been for these past few years?

examples.igbo: Anya ī! Ọ bụ ezie na m hụrụ gị taa n'okporo ụzọ?
examples.english: Oh wonderful! Is it true that I saw you on the road today?

note: Interjections are sometimes difficult to contextualize with precise length constraints.

examples.igbo: Onye ohi ahụ nọ na-egbelèghalị n'azụ ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: The thief was creeping about behind our house.

examples.igbo: Gịnị ka nwoke ahụ na-egbelèghalị n'ebe a na-eme?
examples.english: What is that man loitered around here for?

examples.igbo: Azụmahịa anyị malitere ili ulù n'izu a.
examples.english: Our business started to make a profit this week.

examples.igbo: Ònye na-ali ulù n'etiti ndị ọrụ ugbo a?
examples.english: Who is gaining benefits among these farmers?

examples.igbo: Òkèṅkà a na-èbu ụzọ ịchụ àkwa ka o nwee ike ịbụ àkwa.
examples.english: This hen is starting to brood eggs so that it can hatch eggs.

examples.igbo: Ì hụla ka nnụnụ ahụ si nwayọọ na-èbụ àkwa ya n'àlà?
examples.english: Have you seen how that bird slowly hatches its eggs on the ground?

note: Using -bụ àkwa properly inflected as a verb phrase.

gloss: press into a mess (e.g. ripe fruit)

examples.igbo: E nwere ike ịkpàtò unere ahụ chara acha n'ime akpa.
examples.english: One can press the ripe bananas into a mess inside the bag.

examples.igbo: Mkpụrụ osisi ahụ gbawara ma kpàtò n'elu okwute.
examples.english: The fruit burst and got pressed into a mess on top of the stone.

note: Standard idiomatic usage for crushing ripe fruit.

examples.igbo: Eke ahụ tụnìdo onwe ya n'etiti alaka osisi.
examples.english: The python entangled itself in the middle of the tree branches.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara eriri a ji tụnìdo n'olu akpa m?
examples.english: Why did this rope get entangled around the mouth of my bag?

note: Illustrates both physical entanglement and the state of being entangled.

gloss: break or snap something (shaft or stick) by stepping on it

examples.igbo: O zọ̀jì mkpisi osisi ahụ mgbe ọ na-aga n'ọhịa.
examples.english: He snapped the stick by stepping on it while walking in the bush.

examples.igbo: Ònye zọ̀jì mkpọrọhịhị m n'èzí n'abalị ụnyaahụ?
examples.english: Who broke my shaft by stepping on it outside last night?

note: Specific action of breaking a shaft or stick underfoot.

examples.igbo: A chọrọ m ka ị kwụchìgha m ego m n'echi.
examples.english: I want you to refund my money to me tomorrow.

examples.igbo: Olee mgbe ị ga-ekwụchìgha ya ụgwọ o ji gị?
examples.english: When will you pay him back the debt he owes you?

note: Refers to financial repayment.

gloss: interfere; stand in the way of

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka onye ọ bụla kwụbìdo gị n'ọrụ gị.
examples.english: Do not let anyone stand in the way of your work.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere o ji kwụbìdo n'ụzọ mgbe ụgbọ ala na-aga?
examples.english: Why did he interfere and stand in the way when the car was moving?

note: Expresses physical or metaphorical interference.

examples.igbo: Mkpokọta ego ahụ ruru puku naira ise.
examples.english: The total amount of money reached five thousand naira.

examples.igbo: Nye m mkpokọta ngwongwo niile anyị rere taa.
examples.english: Give me the total of all the goods we sold today.

note: Simple arithmetic or aggregate total.

gloss: failure to know the people to be avoided

examples.igbo: Amā ndị a nà-ezè na-ebute nnukwu nsogbu n'obodo.
examples.english: Failure to know the people to be avoided brings big trouble in the town.

examples.igbo: O nwere amā ndị a nà-ezè mere o ji banye n'ọnyà.
examples.english: It was his failure to know the people to be avoided that made him fall into a trap.

note: Complex nominal phrase used in social context.

examples.igbo: Anyị hụrụ ìkpoòkpò ọnụ ogonogo n'ime osimiri ahụ.
examples.english: আমরা saw a Hemichromis fasciatus inside that river.

examples.igbo: Nwa azụ a hà ka ìkpoòkpò ọnụ ogonogo?
examples.english: Is this small fish the size of a Hemichromis fasciatus?

note: Local fish name, used in river fishing contexts.

examples.igbo: Ihe mberede ahụ chọrọ iwụsa ma rukpọ anya nwoke ahụ.
examples.english: The accident almost burst out and gouged out the man's eye.

examples.igbo: O jiri osisi sie ike rukpọ anụ ọhịa ahụ anya.
examples.english: He used a hard stick to gouge out the wild animal's eye.

note: Accurate rendering of the violent verb action.

examples.igbo: Anụ a jụrụ oyi nwere ìkpulū n'ime ya.
examples.english: This cold meat has worms inside it.

examples.igbo: Ìkpulū na-eri akwụkwọ nri ndị a rere ure.
examples.english: Maggots are eating these rotten vegetables.

note: Standard terms for worms and maggots.

examples.igbo: O nwetara nnukwu èlìlè n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: He made a big gain at the market today.

examples.igbo: Èlìlè ọ bụla chọrọ nnukwu ndidi na mbọ.
examples.english: Every gain requires great patience and effort.

note: Cognate noun construction for -li èlìlè.

examples.igbo: Nne m mụrụ ụmụ nwoke abụọ bụ èjìma.
examples.english: My mother gave birth to two boys who are twins.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụrụ na ịchọrọ ịmụ èjìma, gaa n'ụlọ nne gị.
examples.english: If you want to have twins, go to your mother's house.

note: Common usage for twins.

examples.igbo: Òzịza dị n'ụkwụ ya na-egbu ya mgbu.
examples.english: The swelling on his foot is paining him.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara òzịza a n'elu aka gị?
examples.english: What caused this lump on your hand?

note: Refers to physical swelling or lump.

examples.igbo: Dinta ahụ chọrọ ịgba ụta n'ọhịa.
examples.english: That hunter wants to shoot an arrow with a bow in the forest.

examples.igbo: O ji ụta gbaa anụ ọhịa ahụ n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: He used a bow to shoot the wild animal this morning.

note: Clear archery action.

examples.igbo: Nwatakịrị ahụ ji gbalagbala zere moto ahụ.
examples.english: The child used agility to avoid that car.

examples.igbo: Gbalagbala ya mere o ji merie n'asọmpi ahụ.
examples.english: His smartness is why he won that competition.

note: Captures cleverness and agility.

examples.igbo: Ndị na-agba egwu malitere ịte egwu pụrụ iche.
examples.english: The dancers started to dance in a peculiar way.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere o ji nwee ụdị otu o siri te egwu a?
examples.english: Why is there such a way that she danced this peculiar dance?

note: Cognate object verb structure.

examples.igbo: Nne nyochara nwa ahụ mamalite ịkwọ ìgbì ya.
examples.english: The mother examined the child and started to rub its gums.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-ebe ákwá n'ihi na eze na-apụta n'ìgbì ya.
examples.english: The child is crying because a tooth is coming out of its gums.

note: Refers to soothing a teething baby's gums.

gloss: pus; the thick yellowish liquid produced by infected body tissue

examples.igbo: Ọnya ya nwere abụ nke na-asọ aṣọ.
examples.english: His wound has pus which is flowing out.

examples.igbo: Dọkịta pịrị ọnya ahụ iji wepụ abụ dị n'ime.
examples.english: The doctor squeezed the wound to remove the pus inside.

note: Accurate medical context for pus.

examples.igbo: Nne m tinyere ìtè mmīli ahụ n'elu ọkụ.
examples.english: My mother placed that water pot on the fire.

examples.igbo: Ònye gbasara ìtè mmīli jupụtara n'ụzọ ebe a?
examples.english: Who broke the water pot filled with water on this path?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-enwe àrụ mfe mgbe niile n'oge udu mmiri.
examples.english: She always enjoys good health during the rainy season.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ ji àrụ mfe na-agba ọsọ n'ezi.
examples.english: That child with much activity is running outside.

examples.igbo: Ube a chatọtara n'osisi n'ihi nnukwu anwụ.
examples.english: This pear has become over-ripe on the tree because of much sun.

examples.igbo: Atụla akpụ ndị chatọtara n'ahịa n'ihi na ha emebiwo.
examples.english: Do not buy cassava tubers that are over-ripe in the market because they have spoiled.

examples.igbo: O nyere nwa ya nwoke otù nnī fufu.
examples.english: He gave his son a big lump of fufu.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eri otù nnī garị a niile naanị gị?
examples.english: Will you eat this entire big lump of garri all by yourself?

examples.igbo: Gụgidē akwụkwọ gị ruo mgbe elekere asatọ ga-akụ.
examples.english: Read your book until eight o'clock strikes.

examples.igbo: Ọ ga-agụgidē ọrụ ya tupu ya aga n'ezi.
examples.english: He will read until he finishes his work before going outside.

gloss: female tortoise, especially used in folk tales

examples.igbo: Nna ochie kọrọ akụkọ banyere àlịyà na mgbada.
examples.english: Grandfather told a story about the female tortoise and the antelope.

examples.igbo: Gịnị ka àlịyà gwara mbe n'akụkọ ifo ahụ?
examples.english: What did the female tortoise tell the tortoise in that folk tale?

examples.igbo: Ndị obodo mere afọ òrà tupu ha amalite ịkọ ugbo.
examples.english: The villagers performed the sacrifice before cultivation before they began farming.

examples.igbo: Ebee ka ha ga-eme afọ òrà n'afọ a?
examples.english: Where will they perform the sacrifice before cultivation this year?

examples.igbo: Ha kpebiri ịnụsọ ndị iro nọ n'obodo gbara agbata.
examples.english: They decided to wage war against the enemies in the neighboring town.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere e ji nụsọ ezinụlọ ahụ n'afọ gara aga?
examples.english: Why was war waged against that family last year?

examples.igbo: Ikpe ahụ wetaara ya àmàmikpe n'ihu onye ọka ikpe.
examples.english: That case brought him condemnation before the judge.

examples.igbo: Ọ nwetara àmàmikpe n'ihi na o mere ajọ omume.
examples.english: He received conviction because he did an evil deed.

examples.igbo: Ajụjụ siri ike ahụ gbagwọjuru ya anyā n'ule.
examples.english: That difficult question confused him in the exam.

examples.igbo: Okwu onye isi obodo ahụ gbagwọjuru ndi mmadụ anyā.
examples.english: The speech of the town chief abashed the people.

gloss: soothe; comfort; soothe to make stop crying (small child)

examples.igbo: Nne gùgùtàrà nwa ahụ na-akwa ákwá ruo mgbe o biri.
examples.english: The mother soothed the crying child until he stopped.

examples.igbo: Biko gùgùta nwa ahụ ka o wee kwụsị iti mkpu.
examples.english: Please comfort that child so that she will stop shouting.

examples.igbo: Ndị agha kpọrọ ndị iro ole na ole n'agha n'abalị ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: The soldiers took a few enemies prisoner in the war last night.

examples.igbo: Ònye kpara onye isi ha n'agha a lụrụ n'ugbo?
examples.english: Who took their leader prisoner in this battle fought at the farm?

gloss: light fire; kindle by blowing; raise light

examples.igbo: Fùnwu ọkụ n'ime ulo ka anyị kpoo ọkụ ozugbo.
examples.english: Light a fire inside the house so that we warm ourselves immediately.

examples.igbo: O ji ọnụ fùnwu unere nkụ ahụ ruo mgbe ọ kpọrọ ọkụ.
examples.english: He blew on the dry firewood to kindle it until it caught fire.

examples.igbo: Bèka akwa ahụ n'obere obere iberibe maka akwa ụmụaka.
examples.english: Cut that cloth into small pieces for children's clothes.

examples.igbo: O bereka nnukwu anụ a ka anyị kesaa ya.
examples.english: She cut up this large meat so that we could share it.

examples.igbo: Kpakpan do na-acha gbukapụrụ n'elu igwe n'ụtụtụ taa.
examples.english: The morning star is shining brightly in the sky this morning.

examples.igbo: Mgbe kpakpan do pụtara, ndị ọrụ ugbo na-aga n'ubi.
examples.english: When the morning star appears, farmers go to the farm.

examples.igbo: Nwatakịrị ahụ riri nri n'òfelè n'emeghị mkpọtụ ọ bụla.
examples.english: The child ate the food easily without making any noise.

examples.igbo: Ọ rụchara ọrụ ya n'òfelè tupu anyanwụ eruo etiti.
examples.english: He finished his work easily before the sun reached the middle.

examples.igbo: Ndi nna ochie do ànì a ma biri ebe a ugbua.
examples.english: The ancestors settled this land and live here now.

examples.igbo: Ha ga-edo ànì ọhụrụ tupu oge mmiri ezo rue.
examples.english: They will establish a new settlement before the rainy season arrives.

examples.igbo: Ehi ahụ kwòjiliri n'ime ahịa wee gbasaa ngwongwo mmadụ.
examples.english: The cow rushed violently into the market and scattered people's wares.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara nwa okorobịa ahụ ji kwòjiliri gaa n'ọdọ mmiri?
examples.english: Why did that young man rush violently towards the stream?

examples.igbo: Ọ turube ji n'akụkụ akwa niile iji chebe ha.
examples.english: He planted yams all around the ridge edges to protect them.

examples.igbo: Biko turube akwụkwọ nri gburugburu osisi a dị n'ubi.
examples.english: Please plant vegetables all around this tree on the farm.

examples.igbo: Ha abịala abụ mgbasà n'ebe ahịa gbasara.
examples.english: They have come with the dismissal song where the market dispersed.

examples.igbo: Gịnị ka ha ji abụ mgbasà a taa?

examples.english: This bag cannot accommodate all my books.

examples.english: That very small child is looking for food by the roadside.

examples.igbo: Ònye nwe nwa pe a na-akwa akwa ebe a?
examples.english: Who owns this tiny baby crying here?

examples.english: My father is coughing tonight.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere o ji na-ụkwalà otu a?
examples.english: Why is he coughing like this?

note: Refers to the precise middle or centre.

examples.english: Please, do not get angry because of what I said.

examples.english: That Nri titleholder entered the market square.

examples.igbo: Anyị natara nwa Ǹrì n'ụlọ n'ụtụtụ taa.
examples.english: We received an Nri dignitary at home this morning.

note: Refers to the traditional Nri traveler with ritual authority.

gloss: to remove the outer covering or skin from (a fruit or vegetable); peel

examples.english: Please peel this yam so we can cook.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-atụ̀cha akpụ tupu o tee ya.
examples.english: She is peeling cassava before grinding it.

note: Used for removing outer skins of tubers and vegetables.

examples.igbo: Ndị uwe ojii jidere ndị na-gba àkwụ̀nà n'abalị.
examples.english: The police caught those engaging in prostitution at night.

examples.igbo: Ọ ghọrọ onye na-gba àkwụ̀nà n'obodo ukwu.

note: Standard phrase for selling sex.

examples.english: Please do not carry that heavy bag all by yourself.

note: Verb stem for carrying burdens or children.

examples.english: Where are we going to meet tomorrow?

note: Standard interrogative for location.

gloss: friend; lover; mistress; adultery (more common than enyì and òwì)

examples.english: He has been my good friend since primary school.

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ nwere òyì na nzuzo.
examples.english: That man keeps a secret mistress.

note: Refers to a close friend or lover.

examples.igbo: Kèdu kà i mèlù n'ụtụtụ taa?
examples.english: How are you this morning?

examples.igbo: Kèdu kà i mèlù tupu anyị ezute n'ahịa?
examples.english: How were you before we met at the market?

examples.igbo: Èkwulèkwu nwa a na-ewe ndị mmadụ iwe n'ezi.
examples.english: This child's talkativeness angers people outside.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere o ji jiri èkwulèkwu mebie ihe taa?
examples.english: Why did he use talkativeness to ruin things today?

examples.english: He doubts stubbornly whenever he is told the truth.

examples.igbo: Egbula oge ịtụ n'ihi na ọ naghị esi ngọ.
examples.english: Do not waste time doubting because she does not doubt obstinately.

examples.igbo: Biko buru nkata akpụ a gaa n'm̀wọ̣.
examples.english: Please carry this basket of yams to the cocoyam storage place.

examples.igbo: E nwere nnukwu akpụ n'ime m̀wọ̣ anyị nọ n'ime obodo.
examples.english: There are big cocoyams inside our storage place in the village.

gloss: soft body feathers or down of fowl

examples.english: My mother gathers the soft body feathers of a fowl to work.

examples.igbo: Febe ǹtu ōkụkò ndị ahụ pụọ n'elu efere nri.
examples.english: Blow those down feathers away from the food plate.

examples.igbo: Ọbụna nwa obere nwa ghọtara ihe nkuzi ahụ.
examples.english: Even a small child understood the lesson.

examples.igbo: O nweghị onye bịara, ọbụna nwanne ya nwoke pụrụ.
examples.english: Nobody came, even his brother left.

examples.igbo: Mmiri a na-achị òmù nke ukwuu n'oge udu mmiri.
examples.english: This river has a very strong current during the rainy season.

examples.igbo: Egbula oge ịgafe mgbe osimiri na-achị òmù.
examples.english: Do not attempt to cross when the river has a strong current.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ dara àba n'ala mgbe ọ na-agba ọsọ.
examples.english: That child fell on his back on the ground while running.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara o ji daa àba n'elu ájá ahụ?
examples.english: Why did he fall flat on his back on that sand?

examples.english: The children are having fun outside this evening.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ naanị oghū ka ha na-achọ n'ubi.
examples.english: It is only play that they are looking for on the farm.

examples.igbo: O nyere m nleanyā otu mgbe ọ gafere.
examples.english: He gave me a glance once as he passed by.

examples.igbo: Nleanyā otu zuru iji mara ihe mere n'ụlọ.
examples.english: A single glance was enough to know what happened in the house.

examples.igbo: Ìgwùlùbè buru ibu rie akwụkwọ nile n'ubi a.
examples.english: A large swarm of locusts ate all the leaves in this farm.

examples.igbo: Ndị ugbo ò hụrụ otu ìgwùlùbè na-ebi n'akwụkwọ?
examples.english: Did the farmers see a single locust living on the leaves?

examples.igbo: Biko tụnye nnu ole na ole n'ofe ahụ.
examples.english: Please throw a little salt into that soup.

examples.igbo: O nwere onye tụnyere ego n'ime igbe ahụ?
examples.english: Is there anyone who threw money into that box?

examples.igbo: Aha mmụọ inyī adịghị mma n'etiti ndị mmadụ.
examples.english: The reputation of an unclean spirit is not good among people.

examples.igbo: Mmụọ inyī ọ na-abata n'ụlọ nwere udo?
examples.english: Does an unclean spirit ever enter a peaceful home?

gloss: torch; firebrand; ember; half-burnt piece of wood

examples.igbo: Wepụ ònòkò ahụ n'ọnụ ọkụ ka o ghara ịchịcha.
examples.english: Remove that half-burnt piece of wood from the fire so it doesn't burn out completely.

examples.igbo: Gịnị ka nwoke ahụ na-eji ònòkò a eke n'ọkụ?
examples.english: What is that man using this firebrand to do in the fire?

examples.english: Do these two goats look alike in color and behavior?

examples.english: That young girl smiled when she saw her friend.

examples.english: Taste the mouth of this soup to see if it has salt.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ detụrụ nri ya ma jụ ikpe.
examples.english: The child tasted his food and refused to eat.

gloss: visit and look after sick person

examples.igbo: Ònye ga-negalụ nne ochie nọ n'ụlọ ọgwụ taa?
examples.english: Who will go and look after grandmother in the hospital today?

examples.igbo: Nne m chachara ụlọ niile tupu anyị teta.

examples.igbo: Olee onye mepere ntipu a n'elu mgbidi?
examples.english: Who opened this gap high up on the wall?

gloss: appear strongly built and firm on the ground; sturdy

examples.english: That young man appears strongly built among his friends.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere o ji gba agidigi otu a n'ala?
examples.english: Why is he standing so firmly and solidly on the ground like that?

note: Idiomatic description of a sturdy and well-grounded physical appearance.

examples.igbo: Onye nche ahụ ji m̀kpànaaka siri ike n'aka.
examples.english: The security guard held a strong baton in his hand.

examples.igbo: Zụta m̀kpànaaka osisi ka anyị jiri jee ije.
examples.english: Buy a wooden walking stick so we can use it for our journey.

note: Refers to a rod or baton used for walking or guarding.

examples.igbo: Aka nri ya nwere akpù akā ukwu.
examples.english: His right arm has a large biceps.

examples.igbo: Gosi m akpù akā gị ma ị na-ebuli ibu.
examples.english: Show me your biceps when you are lifting heavy loads.

note: Refers to the muscle of the upper arm.

examples.igbo: Igwe ojii na-rùrube tupu mmiri ezo.
examples.english: The dark sky is rumbling before the rain falls.

examples.igbo: Anụrụ m egbe na-rùrube n'ugwu ahụ.
examples.english: I heard thunder rumbling on that hill.

note: Describes the deep rumbling sound of thunder.

examples.igbo: Ụkwụ m na-egbu m mgbe m si n'ahịa lọta.
examples.english: My foot is paining me after I returned from the market.

examples.igbo: Sacha ụkwụ gị tupu ị banye n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: Wash your leg before you enter the house.

note: Common everyday usage referring to foot or leg.

gloss: fighting between people of same town or village

examples.igbo: Ọ̀gụụlọ̀ bilitere n'etiti obodo abụọ ndị agbata obi.
examples.english: Fighting broke out between the two neighboring villages.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara ọ̀gụụlọ̀ a n'etiti ụmụnna n'oge a?
examples.english: What caused this communal fight among kinsmen at this time?

note: Refers specifically to clashes or fights between people of the same town.

gloss: hiss; make a squeaky sound by forcefully sucking in air through the gap between a tight closed teeth, especially to show disappointment (typically African)

examples.igbo: Ọ gbara ma ọsụ̀ mgbe ọ nụrụ akụkọ ọjọọ ahụ.
examples.english: He hissed through his teeth when he heard the bad news.

examples.igbo: Egbula oge ịtụgharị ma ọsụ̀ mgbe a na-agwa gị okwu.
examples.english: Do not hesitate to hiss in disappointment when people talk to you.

note: Refers to the specific sucking hiss showing disappointment.

examples.igbo: Ndị ikom ahụ na-kpụ aja iji wuo ụlọ ọhụrụ.
examples.english: The men are making mud walls to build a new house.

examples.igbo: Ha kpụrụ aja ahụ tupu oge mmiri ezo malite.
examples.english: They made the mud wall before the rainy season began.

note: Inflected form of the verb stem for making mud walls.

gloss: carry up; lift up; (fig.); stir up; begin

examples.igbo: Biko bulite akpa ahụ ka m weere ya gaa ahịa.
examples.english: Please lift up that bag so I can take it to the market.

examples.igbo: Onye bulitere okwu a n'etiti anyị taa?
examples.english: Who stirred up this matter among us today?

note: Covers physical lifting and figurative stirring up.

examples.igbo: O wetaara m ji nke ahu kuta.
examples.english: He brought me that yam completely.

examples.igbo: Ego ole ka i siri kuta?
examples.english: How much money did you bring completely?

note: The verb stem -ku-ta with the meaning completely is ambiguous and unusual in standard modern usage.

examples.igbo: Àda ìbà ahụ ga-alụ di n'ime obodo ọzọ.
examples.english: That daughter of the family will marry in another town.

examples.igbo: Ònye bụ àda ìbà na-esi nri n'ebe a?
examples.english: Who is the daughter of the family cooking food here?

note: Used naturally in family contexts.

gloss: charcoal; black remnant of a burnt thing

examples.igbo: Wepụ unyi niile dị n'ime ite ahụ.
examples.english: Remove all the charcoal inside that pot.

examples.igbo: O ji unyi detuo akara n'elu mgbidi.
examples.english: He used charcoal to draw a mark on the wall.

note: Common everyday word for charcoal.

examples.igbo: Kpachara anya ka i ghara ịta ire gị.
examples.english: Be careful so that you do not bite your tongue.

examples.igbo: O tiri mkpu mgbe o tare ire ya.
examples.english: He screamed when he bit his tongue.

note: Standard idiom for biting one's tongue.

examples.igbo: Ìhè anyanwụ ahụ nwere ike ịnwụchita anya mmadụ.
examples.english: That sunlight can dazzle a person's eyes.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara ìhè na-nwụchita anya m ugbu a?
examples.english: Why is the light dazzling my eyes right now?

note: Inflected form is logical, though the compound verb stem is uncommon.

examples.igbo: Nwatakịrị ahụ dara adà n'elu ájá.
examples.english: The child fell down on the sand.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere o ji daa adà n'ụzọ?
examples.english: Why did he fall down on the way?

note: Cognate accusative construction common for falling.

examples.igbo: Ọ kwōpụ̀rụ alaka osisi ahụ site n'osisi.
examples.english: He forcibly plucked off that tree branch from the tree.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji kwōpụ̀ akwụkwọ ahụ?
examples.english: Why did you forcefully detach those leaves?

note: Standard directional verb usage for forceful detaching.

examples.igbo: Weta ìgùlùbè ka m rịgoro n'elu ụlọ.
examples.english: Bring the ladder so I can climb up to the roof.

examples.igbo: Ònye kwadoro ìgùlùbè a n'akụkụ mgbidi?
examples.english: Who leaned this ladder against the wall?

note: Standard word for ladder.

examples.igbo: Ndị nna nna anyị na-eme ịgōmmụọ n'oge ochie.
examples.english: Our grandfathers practiced worshipping spirits in olden times.

examples.igbo: Ịgōmmụọ adịghị mma n'anya Chineke taa.
examples.english: Worshipping spirits is not good in God's eyes today.

note: Refers to traditional spirit worship.

gloss: violent writhing in pains by body twists, turning backwards and forwards as a result of great pain or discomfort, which often ends in death.

examples.igbo: Nwatakịrị ahụ nọ n'àkpị̀rị̀ n'ihi nnukwu afọ ọsịsa.
examples.english: The child was writhing in violent pain due to severe stomach ache.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara àkpị̀rị̀ ahụ nwoke ahụ nwere tupu ọ nwụọ?
examples.english: What caused that violent body twisting the man experienced before he died?

note: A very specific medical or extreme pain term.

examples.igbo: Ndị agha obodo anyị na-aga -bu agha n'ókè.
examples.english: Our country's soldiers are going to fight at the border.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere unu ji achọ ibu agha taa?
examples.english: Why do you want to fight today?

note: Verb phrase for waging or fighting war.

examples.igbo: Nwa agbọghọ ahụ tụtụtụ òkutā n'ala.
examples.english: The young girl picked up a stone from the ground.

examples.igbo: Ebe a juputara na òkutā siri ike.
examples.english: This place is full of hard stones.

note: Variant spelling of òkwutē.

gloss: hold by fastening with a belt, pin, clip etc.

examples.igbo: Gbado akpa gị nke ọma tupu gị agbaga ọsọ.
examples.english: Fasten your bag securely before you run.

examples.igbo: O ji eriri gbaduo ibu ahụ n'isi ya.
examples.english: He fastened that load to his head with a rope.

note: Verb meaning to fasten or hold securely.

examples.igbo: Ugbo ala m gbafere ma gbaghàa nke ya.
examples.english: My car sped past and overtook his own.

examples.igbo: Ònye gbaghàrụ onye ọzọ n'ọsịsa agbaba?
examples.english: Who overtook the other in the race?

note: Verb meaning to overtake.

examples.igbo: Mkpịsị osisi ahụ nyaara n'etiti abalị.
examples.english: That wooden stick broke in the middle of the night.

examples.igbo: Kpachara anya ka eriri ahụ ghara ịnya.
examples.english: Be careful so that rope does not break.

note: Verb stem for breaking, often for long or flexible objects.

examples.igbo: Nwatakịrị ahụ na-arịa ụkwalà ntụrịiri siri ike.
examples.english: That child is suffering from a severe whooping-cough.

examples.igbo: Ò nwere ọgwụ a na-enye maka ụkwalà ntụrịiri?
examples.english: Is there any medicine given for whooping-cough?

note: Specific medical term for whooping cough.

examples.igbo: Nna ochie nwere otu ochie òkụ ụtabà n'akpa ya.
examples.english: The grandfather has an old snuff-box in his pocket.

examples.igbo: Weta òkụ ụtabà ka m weere ntakịrị sịga.
examples.english: Bring the tobacco pipe so I can take a little tobacco.

note: Refers to traditional smoking pipe or snuff container.

examples.igbo: Nwa akwụkwọ ahụ nwara maa amụma ọnụ ahịa ya.
examples.english: The student tried to guess its price.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere ike maa amụma onye mmeri taa?
examples.english: Can you guess today's winner?

examples.igbo: Ndị mụlụ ya zụtara ya akwụkwọ ọhụrụ.
examples.english: His parents bought him a new book.

examples.igbo: Biko, kpọọ ndị mụlụ gị ka ha bịa ebe a.
examples.english: Please, call your parents to come here.

examples.igbo: Anyị jụrụ nghagbu n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: We rejected trickery in the market today.

examples.igbo: Nghagbu mere ka ọ tụfuo ego ya niile.
examples.english: Cheating made him lose all his money.

examples.igbo: Biko, dị ǹdìdì ka anyị na-arụ ọrụ a.
examples.english: Please, be patient while we do this work.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụrụ na ị dị ǹdìdì, ihe ga-agara gị nke ọma.
examples.english: If you are patient, things will go well for you.

examples.igbo: Mmiri ozuzo na-ezusoro mgbe mmiri gbakọrọ n'ụzọ.
examples.english: Rain water splashes when water runs together on the path.

examples.igbo: Mkpụrụ osisi ahụ gbakọrọ n'ime akpa ahụ.
examples.english: The fruits ran together inside the bag.

examples.igbo: Ọ fanyere uwe ya n'ime obere akpa ahụ.
examples.english: He squeezed his clothes into the small bag.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere o ji fanyere onwe ya n'ebe ahụ?
examples.english: Why did he squeeze himself into that place?

examples.igbo: Anyị nwere ntubu n'ịchọta nri taa.
examples.english: We had difficulty in finding food today.

examples.igbo: Ntubu dị n'ụzọ ahụ mere ka anyị gee nti.
examples.english: The difficulty on that road made us pay attention.

examples.igbo: Òne ka akwụkwọ a?
examples.english: How much is this book?

examples.igbo: Òne n'ime ha ka ị chọrọ n'ezie?
examples.english: Which of them do you really want?

examples.igbo: Weta ìtè ọkụ ka anyị hụ ụzọ n'abalị.
examples.english: Bring the lamp so that we can see the way at night.

examples.igbo: Ìtè ọkụ a nyere anyị ọkụ n'oge oku a.
examples.english: This lamp provided light for us during this outage.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-ekwe ùkwe n'ụtụtụ mgbe ha na-asacha efere.
examples.english: The children sing songs in the morning while washing dishes.

examples.igbo: Olee onye na-ekwe ùkwe a n'abalị?
examples.english: Who is singing this song in the night?

examples.igbo: Mgbè ǹcha ka o nwere akwụkwọ n'aka ya.
examples.english: Always he has a book in his hand.

examples.igbo: Nwa a na-ebe ákwá mgbè ǹcha n'oge nri.
examples.english: This child cries at all times during mealtime.

examples.igbo: Nwa okorobịa ahụ fùkpọrọ fùpụrụ bọọlụ ahụ n'ike.
examples.english: That young man blew the ball until it burst with force.

examples.igbo: Egbula oge, fùkpọo fùpụọ ya tupu anyị pụọ.
examples.english: Do not waste time, blow it until it bursts before we leave.

note: Constructed with verb suffix pattern for completion.

examples.igbo: Onye na-akwa nchara ji anyụ ǹkà akpụ mma.
examples.english: The blacksmith uses a small hammer to forge a knife.

examples.igbo: Chọta anyụ ǹkà m ka m rụọ ọrụ a.
examples.english: Find my small hammer for me so I can do this work.

examples.igbo: Nutù osisi ahụ ala ka anyị nwee ike ịnọdụ ala.
examples.english: Push that piece of wood down so we can sit.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere o ji nutù akpa ahụ n'ala?
examples.english: Why did he push that bag down to the ground?

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ ṅụbịga mmanya okè n'ememe ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: That man got drunk heavily at yesterday's ceremony.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụrụ na ị ṅụbịga mmanya okè, ị ga-arịa ọrịa.
examples.english: If you get drunk, you will fall ill.

gloss: outside; compound outside walls (= èzi amā, contrast mbala ēzi); area in village not occupied by houses (includes but is wider than èzi)

examples.igbo: Nne m na-esi nri n'ìlo taa.
examples.english: My mother is cooking food outside in the compound today.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-egwu egwuregwu n'ìlo mgbe e mesịrị.
examples.english: The children are playing games in the open compound later.

gloss: gaze; place eyes on; look upon

examples.igbo: Lekwàsà anya n'elu osisi ahụ ka ị hụ nnụnụ.
examples.english: Gaze upon the top of that tree so you can see the bird.

examples.igbo: O lekwasara anya n'ihe ọ na-ede.
examples.english: He placed his eyes upon what he was writing.

examples.igbo: Jiri ndọta chọta obere agịga a rutara n'ala.
examples.english: Use the magnet to find this small needle that fell to the ground.

examples.igbo: Ndọta na-adọta igwe nso n'onwe ya.
examples.english: A magnet attracts iron close to itself.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ gbasọrọ nne ya n'ime ahịa.
examples.english: That child ran after his mother inside the market.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ị ji gbasọ ohi?
examples.english: Why did you run to join in the theft?

examples.igbo: Ajọ ndị enyi dufịere nwa okorobịa ahụ.
examples.english: Bad friends misled that young man.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka onye ọ bụla dufịe gị n'ụzọ.
examples.english: Do not let anyone mislead you on the way.

examples.igbo: Nkpata egwu mere ka ọ kubie ume nwa oge.
examples.english: A sudden scare made him stop breathing for a moment.

examples.igbo: Ọrịa obi mere ka anụmanụ ahụ kubie.
examples.english: Heart disease caused that animal to stop breathing suddenly.

examples.igbo: Onye ohi ahụ gbaghàràga n'ihu ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: That thief ran past the front of our house.

examples.igbo: M gbaghàràga n'ahịa n'ihi na oge na-aga.
examples.english: I ran past the market because time was running out.

examples.igbo: Ndị bi n'ndìdà na-enwe mmiri ozuzo ugboro ugboro.
examples.english: People living down-river experience rainfall very often.

examples.igbo: Ha na-aga njem ruo n'ala ndìdà.
examples.english: They are travelling all the way to the southern low-lying country.

examples.igbo: Nna m kpụrụ isi ya n'ụtụtụ taa.
examples.english: My father shaved the hair of his head this morning.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-akpụ isi tupu ị gaa n'ọrụ?
examples.english: Will you shave your head before going to work?

examples.igbo: Mmiri ozuzo maliri àmalì tupu m ruo ụlọ.
examples.english: The rain drenched me thoroughly before I reached home.

examples.igbo: Uwe ya maliri àmalì n'ihi oke mmiri ahụ.
examples.english: His clothes were drenched thoroughly because of the heavy flood.

examples.igbo: Ndị ọrụ ugbo chọtara ebe mgbabà n'okwu osisi.
examples.english: The farmers found a place of refuge under the tree.

examples.igbo: Ebe mgbabà dị nso ma ọ bụrụ na mmiri ezo.
examples.english: There is a refuge nearby in case it rains.

gloss: Canarium schweinfurthii Engl. See also ùbe ōkpoko.

examples.igbo: Nwa agbọghọ ahụ sooro m werie ùbe òsà n'ubi.
examples.english: That girl helped me pick African pear in the farm.

examples.igbo: Ùbe òsà na-atọ ụtọ mgbe a ṅụrụ ya na nnu.
examples.english: Canarium fruit tastes delicious when eaten with salt.

examples.igbo: Anyị riri ji ọfụū n'ememe afọ ọhụrụ.
examples.english: we ate new yam during the new year festival.

examples.igbo: Olee mgbe unu ga-ewepụta ji ọfụū n'ahịa?
examples.english: When will you bring new yam out to the market?

gloss: keep or hold something in the mind; bear in mind; harbor something in the mind

examples.igbo: Biko, buo ihe a n'obì ka ị ghara ichefu ya.
examples.english: Please, keep this thing in mind so that you won't forget it.

examples.igbo: O bu ihe ọjọọ n'obì ya ruo mgbe o kwuru ya.
examples.english: He harbored evil in his mind until he spoke out.

examples.igbo: Nwatakịrị ahụ kwụtù site n'elu osisi n'ụjọ.
examples.english: The child jumped down from the tree top in fear.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji kwụtù ngwa ngwa mgbe m bịara?
examples.english: Why did you jump down quickly when I arrived?

examples.igbo: Òwì m bịara n'ụlọ m taa iji kelee m.
examples.english: My friend came to my house today to greet me.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ òwì m ezigbo mma ka anyị na-aga ahịa.
examples.english: It is my very good friend that we are going to the market with.

examples.igbo: Nwa okorobịa ahụ nwere ụkwụ ọlọgbà kemgbe o mere agadi.
examples.english: That young man has had knock-kneed legs since he grew up.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara na nwa ahụ nwere ụkwụ ọlọgbà?
examples.english: What is the reason that the child has crooked legs?

gloss: information, especially that which is not commonly known

examples.igbo: Ọ chọtara ùmà gbasara azụmahịa ahụ n'ime obodo.
examples.english: He found secret information concerning the business in the town.

examples.igbo: E nwere ùmà ọ bụla ọhụrụ gbasara ego ahụ?
examples.english: Is there any new insider information concerning the money?

note: ùmà is dialectal in some regions, but well understood as confidential info.

examples.igbo: Nwa okorobịa ahụ wị̀ ara mgbe o furu ego ya.
examples.english: The young man went mad when he lost his money.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ gịnị mere nwoke a ji wị̀ ara n'etiti ahịa?
examples.english: What made this man go mad in the middle of the market?

examples.igbo: Biko, gwaghalị m akụkọ ahụ ka m ghọta ya nke ọma.
examples.english: Please, tell me the story again so that I will understand it well.

examples.igbo: O kwuru ya otu ugboro ma jụ ịgwaghalị ya ọzọ.
examples.english: He said it once and refused to tell it again.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-sọ ìsì n'ọchịchịrị n'ihi egwu.
examples.english: The child walked as though blind in the darkness due to fear.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere o ji sọ ìsì gafee n'akụkụ ụzọ?
examples.english: Why did he walk as though blind past the roadside?

note: Idiomatic usage for moving blindly or groping.

examples.igbo: Kèji ji a n'etiti ka anyị wee rie ya abụọ.
examples.english: Divide this yam into two so that both of us can eat it.

examples.igbo: O kèjiwo osisi ahụ ụzọ abụọ n'ogige ya.
examples.english: He has divided the wood into two parts in his compound.

examples.igbo: Ezinụlọ anyị bimì n'ime obodo dị anya.
examples.english: Our family lives far in within a distant village.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ n'ebe ahụ ka ha na-bimì ruo taa.
examples.english: It is in that place that they live far in up till today.

note: Compound verb stem -bimì means living deep inside or far away.

examples.igbo: Nwadị nkwụ enū ka m na-achọ taa.
examples.english: It is fresh up-wine from the palm tree that I am looking for today.

examples.igbo: Ònye ṅụrụ nkwụ enū ahụ n'ụtụtụ a?
examples.english: Who drank that up-wine from the crown of the tree this morning?

examples.igbo: Wepụta akpụ ji ahụ ka anyị kụọ ya n'ubi.
examples.english: Bring out those second yams for re-planting so we can plant them on the farm.

examples.igbo: Ànyị ga-eji akpụ ji a mee nri ma ọ bụ kụọ ya?
examples.english: Will we use this yam for re-planting as food or plant it?

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara na ọ bụ gị na-kpè àzụ n'ọsọ ahụ?
examples.english: Why is it that you are the one being last in that race?

examples.igbo: Egbula oge ka ị ghara kpè àzụ n'ọrụ.
examples.english: Do not waste time so that you will not be last at work.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ kpọrọ isi ànì n'ihu eze n'ụtụtụ a.
examples.english: That child prostrated before the king this morning.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere o ji kpọọ isi ànì nye ha n'ezi?
examples.english: Why did he prostrate and beg them outside?

gloss: go and sleep with a friend or relative away from one's home

examples.igbo: Nwa m nwoke gakwara ṅụọ ùla n'ụlọ nwanne nne ya.
examples.english: My son went and slept at his aunt's place away from home.

examples.igbo: Ọ ga-aga sa ùla n'aka enyi ya n'abalị a?
examples.english: Will he go and sleep at his friend's house tonight?

examples.igbo: Nwatakịrị ahụ na-rikarị nwanne ya nri n'efere.
examples.english: That child eats more food than his sibling from the plate.

examples.igbo: Biko, emekwala ka onye na-rikarị ndị ọzọ nri.
examples.english: Please, do not act like someone who eats more than other people.

examples.igbo: Nna m na-lò otú o si zụta ala ahụ.
examples.english: My father is thinking about how he bought that land.

examples.igbo: Lò banyere nsogbu a tupu i nye azịza.
examples.english: Think about this problem before you give an answer.

gloss: ruminate; chew the cud (a ruminant animal)

examples.igbo: Ehi ahụ na-ta ụ̀za n'akụkụ ubi n'ehihie.
examples.english: That cow is chewing the cud by the side of the farm in the afternoon.

examples.igbo: Lee ehi na-ta ụ̀za n'etiti ahịhịa ndụ.
examples.english: Look at the cow ruminating in the middle of the green grass.

examples.igbo: Nne m na-gbe àkàmụ̀ maka nri ụtụtụ ụmụaka.
examples.english: My mother is preparing liquid pap for the children's breakfast.

examples.igbo: Gbe àkàmụ̀ ahụ nke ọma ka o ghara ịnwe mkpụrụ.
examples.english: Mix that liquid pap properly so it does not have lumps.

examples.igbo: Nna m chiri echi n'obodo anyị n'afọ gara aga.
examples.english: My father took a title in our town last year.

examples.igbo: Eze anyị ga-echi onye ọhụrụ echi n'izu a.
examples.english: Our king will bestow a title on a new person this week.

gloss: be foolish, stupid; act stupidly, foolishly

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara o ji eme nzuzù n'ihu ndị mmadụ?
examples.english: Why is he acting foolishly in front of people?

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka onye ọ bụla mee nzuzù ebe a.
examples.english: Do not let anyone behave foolishly here.

gloss: knock and cut, hurt, abrase toe by knocking it against an object (usually by accident)

examples.igbo: Kpachara anya ka ụkwụ gị ghara ịnụ mgbu ma ọ bụrụ na ị kpakọbè ụkwụ gị n'elu nkume.
examples.english: Be careful so your foot won't hurt if you knock and hurt your toe against a stone.

examples.igbo: Ọ kpakọbè ụkwụ ya n'ọnụ ụzọ mgbe ọ na-agba ọsọ.
examples.english: She accidentally hit and bruised her toe at the doorway while running.

note: Inflected as kpakọbè to fit standard idiomatic usage.

gloss: gather, collect (from different points but same area, e.g. farm) and bring Achòlù m kà ụnù jee kpakọta nkụ  I want you (pl.) to go and fetch firewood

examples.igbo: Achọrọ m ka ụnụ jee kpakọta nkụ n'ugbo.
examples.english: I want you all to go and collect firewood on the farm.

examples.igbo: Biko kpakọta akwa gị niile nọ n'ala.
examples.english: Please gather all your clothes lying on the ground.

examples.igbo: Ha nòsịrị n'ebe ahụ tupu ha alọta n'ụlọ.
examples.english: They finished staying there before coming back home.

examples.igbo: Olee mgbe unu ga-anòsị n'obodo a?
examples.english: When will you finish your stay in this town?

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ wụchapụrụ aụ ya tupu ya erie nri.
examples.english: That child washed his body thoroughly before eating food.

examples.igbo: Gaa wụchapụ arụ gị ka anyị wee pụọ.
examples.english: Go and wash your body thoroughly so we can leave.

examples.igbo: Ndị okenye obodo gara ibè okwu n'etiti ezinụlọ abụọ ahụ.
examples.english: The village elders went to settle the dispute between the two families.

examples.igbo: Ọ dị mfe ibè okwu ma ọ bụrụ na mmadụ abụọ kweta.
examples.english: It is easy to settle a dispute if both people agree.

examples.igbo: Ha tinyere ya n'nsụpụ n'ihi omume ọjọọ ya.
examples.english: They subjected him to ostracism because of his evil behavior.

examples.igbo: Nsụpụ a metụtara ezinụlọ ya niile n'obodo.
examples.english: This excommunication affected his entire family in the village.

examples.igbo: Tụfù unun ahụ dị n'ite nri.
examples.english: Throw away that dirt inside the cooking pot.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ị ji tụfù akwụkwọ gị?
examples.english: Why did you throw away your book?

examples.igbo: Nkita hụrụ akàm̀kpọ̀ n'ọhịa wee malite ịchụ ya.
examples.english: The dog saw a pangolin in the bush and started chasing it.

examples.igbo: Akàm̀kpọ̀ na-agba ọnụ ala mgbe ụjọ tụrụ ya.
examples.english: The pangolin rolls into a ball when it is afraid.

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ wụfere mmiri ahụ n'ụzọ dị mfe.
examples.english: The child jumped over the water easily.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere ike wụfere oghere a?

examples.english: Why did you people reschedule that trip?

examples.igbo: Onye nga ahụ gbapụrụ n'abalị ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: The prisoner escaped last night.

examples.igbo: Ndị uwe ojii kpọghachiri onye nga ahụ n'ụlọ mkpọrọ.
examples.english: The police brought the prisoner back to prison.

examples.igbo: Ndịn̄kị̄tị̄ nwere ike ịpụta n'okporo ámá ugbua.
examples.english: Civilians can come out to the street now.

examples.igbo: Ndị agha na-echebe ndịn̄kị̄tị̄ n'oge agha.
examples.english: Soldiers protect the common people during war.

note: Standard tonal markings applied to ndịn̄kị̄tị̄.

gloss: crop, shave, cut hair of animal

examples.igbo: Nna m kpàchara ajị anụ ewu ahụ n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: My father cropped the hair of that goat in the morning.

examples.igbo: Ì kpàchara ajị anụ nkịta ahụ nke ọma?
examples.english: Did you cut the hair of that dog properly?

gloss: dust an item by beating it with a soft duster

examples.igbo: Biko pịàchaa oche ahụ tupu ndị ọbịa abịa.
examples.english: Please dust that chair by beating it before guests arrive.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-pịàcha akwa ákwà n'ụtụtụ ọ bụla.
examples.english: She dusts the cloth item by beating it every morning.

note: Verb inflected in context.

gloss: strain the limbs or joints; mistakenly stretch limbs or joints such that it gets strained, especially when they are in use

examples.igbo: Ụkwụ m sọjiri mgbe m siri n'elu wụda.
examples.english: My leg got strained when I jumped down from above.

examples.igbo: Egbula ọsọ ka aka gị ghara ịsọji.
examples.english: Do not run so that your arm does not get strained.

note: Interpreted in the sense of a joint or limb getting accidentally strained.

examples.igbo: Anyị zutere n'ahịa n'etiti ehihie.
examples.english: We met at the market in the afternoon.

examples.igbo: Ònye ka ị zutere n'ụzọ taa?
examples.english: Who did you encounter on the way today?

examples.igbo: O ji nkịlịka akwà hicha ázụ̀ tebụlụ.
examples.english: He used a ragged cloth to wipe the back of the table.

examples.igbo: À ga-atụfu nkịlịka akwà a niile n'ime ọkụ?
examples.english: Will all these rags be thrown into the fire?

examples.igbo: Àrị̀rịa a gbakara nwa ahụ arụ n'abalị.
examples.english: This fever tormented the child all night.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara na e ji gbakawa ya arụ ugbu a?
examples.english: Why is he being afflicted now?

note: Using -gbakà arụ for torment/afflict.

examples.igbo: Nwoke enwē ifelē ahụ na-ekwupụta okwu n'ihu ọha.
examples.english: That unabashed man speaks openly in public.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere o ji bụrụ onye enwē ifelē taa?
examples.english: Why is he so unrestrained today?

examples.igbo: Ọgwụ ọjọọ ahụ chọrọ iwepụ ime n'afọ ya.
examples.english: That bad medicine nearly caused an abortion in her.

examples.igbo: Ònye kpatara iwepụ ime nwa agbọghọ a?
examples.english: Who caused this young woman's abortion?

note: Inflected using the common causative or descriptive equivalent for abortion.

examples.igbo: Alaka osisi ahụ kpọrọ nkụ wee hịkpọọ kpamkpam.
examples.english: That tree branch dried up completely and withered away.

examples.igbo: Mkpụrụ osisi hịkpọrọ n'oge anwụ siri ike.
examples.english: The plant stems withered and broke during the severe sun.

note: Used in the context of withered vegetation.

examples.igbo: Anyị riri nri, o mesịzịa anyị gawa ahịa.
examples.english: We ate food, and afterwards we went to the market.

examples.igbo: O buru ụzọ nwee nnukwu nsogbu, o mesịzịa udo trị.
examples.english: He first had big problems, but eventually peace reigned.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ dọlịsịrị akwụkwọ m nile n'iberibe.
examples.english: That child tore all my papers into tiny pieces.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara i ji dọlịa uwe ọhụrụ ahụ?
examples.english: Why did you tear the new cloth into pieces?

examples.igbo: Ọ dịghị mma imekwọlụ onye mere gị ihe ọjọọ.
examples.english: It is not good to take revenge on someone who wronged you.

examples.igbo: Olee mgbe i kpebiri imekwọlụ nwanne gị nwoke?
examples.english: When did you decide to take revenge on your brother?

gloss: make, mold or shape metal especially by heating and hitting

examples.igbo: Nna m na-akpụ ụzụ n'ahịa n'oge ochie.
examples.english: My father used to smith metal at the market in the old days.

examples.igbo: Onye na-akpụ ụzụ nọ n'ọnụ ụzọ ámá ugbu a.
examples.english: The blacksmith is at the village gate right now.

examples.igbo: Ndị ikom na-akpà ji n'abalị tupu mmiri ezo.
examples.english: The men are stacking yams in the barn before the rain falls.

examples.igbo: Biko, kpàta m ji ndị a nke ọma n'obí.
examples.english: Please, stack these yams properly for me in the barn.

gloss: dive or plunge into something, especially water

examples.igbo: Nwa okorobịa ahụ kpọrọ òmìmì n'ime osimiri miri emi.
examples.english: The young man plunged deep into the river.

examples.igbo: Ì kpebisiri ike ịchọrọ ịpụ kpọọ òmìmì n'ime mmiri?
examples.english: Are you determined to go and dive straight into the water?

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ gbọtọrọ n'ala ụlọ wee pụọ n'èzí.
examples.english: The child vomited on the floor and walked outside, leaving the mess.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ eziokwu na o gbọtọrọ ebe ahụ ma jụ ihicha ya?
examples.english: Is it true that he vomited there and refused to clean it?

examples.igbo: Chineke maara ife dum anyị na-eme n'ụwa.
examples.english: God knows all things that we do on earth.

examples.igbo: Ọ gwara m ife dum mere n'ugbo ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: He told me all things that happened on the farm yesterday.

examples.igbo: O nyeere m aka nebà n'ime igbe ahụ.
examples.english: He helped me look into that box.

examples.igbo: Gịnị ka ị na-achọ nebà n'ime nkata ahụ?
examples.english: What are you looking into that basket for?

gloss: to continue resolutely or stubbornly  in spite of warning or opposition; persist

examples.igbo: Ọ kachiri obì gaa n'ihu n'agbanyeghị ịdọ aka ná ntị.
examples.english: He stubbornly continued forward despite the warning.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji kachi obì na-eme ihe a a sị gị kwụsị?
examples.english: Why do you persist in doing this thing you were told to stop?

examples.igbo: O wepụrụ anya mgbe nwa ya nwoke na-ezuru ohi.
examples.english: He connived at it when his son was stealing.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara i ji wepụ anya n'ihe ọjọọ ahụ mere?
examples.english: Why did you overlook that bad thing that happened?

note: The idiom -wepụ anya means to intentionally overlook or ignore something wrong.

examples.igbo: Biko bịa nso ka m gwa gị okwu a.
examples.english: Please approach so that I can tell you this word.

examples.igbo: Ò nwere onye na-abịa nso n'ụlọ anyị ugbu a?
examples.english: Is anyone approaching our house now?

note: Verb stem properly inflected in both sentences.

examples.igbo: Ee! M nọ ebe a n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: Yes? I am here inside the house.

examples.igbo: Nna anyị kpọrọ gị, sị 'Ee?'
examples.english: Our father called you, did you answer 'Yes?'

note: Illustrates the responsive exclamation 'ee' when called.

gloss: the act of flying away; flying away

examples.igbo: Mfepụ̀ nnụnụ ahụ n'elu osisi tụrụ nwa ahụ ụjọ.
examples.english: The flying away of that bird from the tree frightened the child.

examples.igbo: Anyị hụrụ mfepụ̀ ngwa ngwa nke igurube n'ubi ahụ.
examples.english: We saw the quick flying away of the locusts in the farm.

note: Mfepụ̀ used correctly as a nominalized action of flying away.

examples.igbo: Nna anyị nyere m isi ọjī iji gọzie ezinụlọ.
examples.english: Our father gave me the germinal sprout of kola to bless the family.

examples.igbo: Ònye ji isi ọjī a mee ihe n'ememe ahụ?
examples.english: Who used this germinal sprout of kola in the ceremony?

note: Refers specifically to the small germinal sprout found in kola nut pieces.

gloss: reckon with; regard; care for; consider (as important)

examples.igbo: Ọ naghị agbanye ihe m na-agwa ya ma ọlị.
examples.english: He does not reckon with what I am telling him at all.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere na ị gaghị agbanye ndụmọdụ ndi okenye?
examples.english: Why is it that you will not care for the advice of elders?

note: Verb -gbànye properly inflected in both examples.

gloss: you; thou; thee (less common than gị)

examples.igbo: Yụ bụ nwoke maara ihe nke ukwuu n'obodo.
examples.english: Thou art a man who knows things very much in the town.

examples.igbo: Gịnị ka yụ chọrọ n'aka nwanne gị taa?
examples.english: What do you want from your sibling today?

note: Archaic/dialectal pronoun 'yụ' used for 'you', though rare.

examples.igbo: Chi èjiri mgbe anyị ka nọ n'ụzọ.
examples.english: The day declines while we are still on the way.

examples.igbo: Ozugbo chi èjiri, ndị mmadụ laghachiri n'ụlọ ha.
examples.english: As soon as the day declines, people returned to their houses.

note: Refers to the declining of daylight towards evening.

examples.igbo: Ịgba ọsọ n'anwụ a bụ ajọ ọlụ.
examples.english: Running under this sun is very hard work.

examples.igbo: Ọ dị ajọ ọlụ ịchọta ego n'oge a.
examples.english: It is very hard to find money nowadays.

note: Standard idiomatic usage for expressing difficulty.

examples.igbo: Akpa nri ahụ fụwara n'ihi ibu ya.
examples.english: That food bag burst because of its weight.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara akpa a ji fụwa n'ala?
examples.english: Why did this bag burst on the ground?

note: Used correctly for bags bursting open.

gloss: name by which someone is called on solemn occasions; praise-name

examples.igbo: Nna ya kpọrọ ya afā ôtutu n'oge mmemme ahụ.
examples.english: His father called him by his praise-name during the ceremony.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ onye nwere afā ôtutu n'ala Igbo.
examples.english: He is someone with a well-known praise-name in Igbo land.

note: Refers to traditional praise names.

gloss: open; uncover Chèkwube Chine kè Trust in God

examples.igbo: Nwa agbọghọ ahụ kwụghetere nnukwu windo ụlọ ya.
examples.english: The young woman opened the big window of her house.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji kwụghe ite nri ahụ?
examples.english: Why did you uncover that pot of food?

note: Handled the compound-like meanings of opening and uncovering.

examples.igbo: Nwa okorobịa ahụ rịgoro n'elu osisi ukwa.
examples.english: The young man climbed up the breadfruit tree.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-arịgo n'ugwu ahụ n'ụtụtụ a?
examples.english: Will you climb that hill this morning?

note: Standard verb inflection for climbing.

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ nọ n'ọnụnụ okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: The man was sitting at the edge of the road.

examples.igbo: Wepụ ite ahụ n'ọnụnụ oche.
examples.english: Remove that pot from the tip of the chair.

note: Refers to edge, tip, or apex.

gloss: go on a message or errand

examples.igbo: Nne m zitere nwa nwanne m ka o jee ozi.
examples.english: My mother sent my cousin to go on an errand.

examples.igbo: Ọ dị njikere ije ozi maka nna ya.
examples.english: He is ready to go on a message for his father.

note: Standard collocation for running errands.

examples.igbo: Ha bidoro ibi n'obodo ahụ afọ gara aga.
examples.english: They began to live in that town last year.

examples.igbo: Ọ dị mma ka anyị bidola ibi ebe a.
examples.english: It is good that we have begun to live here.

note: Approximated -dịba with standard beginning to live/settle.

examples.igbo: Nwaanyị ahụ gbariri ji ahụ n'ite.
examples.english: The woman crushed the yam in the pot.

examples.igbo: Biko gbarịa ngaji nkụ a n'obere obere.
examples.english: Please crush this piece of firewood into small bits.

note: Used correctly for crushing or breaking into small pieces.

examples.igbo: Nwa akwụkwọ ahụ gọrọ na ya ezuru akwụkwọ.
examples.english: The student denied that he stole the book.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji gọọ ikpe a?
examples.english: Why did you deny this case/charge?

note: Standard verb usage for denial.

examples.igbo: Welie aka ekpè gị elu ma hụ ya.
examples.english: Lift your left hand up and see it.

examples.igbo: O ji ụkwụ ekpè gba bọọlụ ahụ.
examples.english: He kicked the ball with his left foot.

gloss: the act of using the teeth to cut into or through something, especially in an attack; bite

examples.igbo: Nkịta ahụ nyere nwa okorobịa ahụ arụ n'ụkwụ.
examples.english: The dog gave the young man a bite on the leg.

examples.igbo: Arụ ọ tara m na-egbu m mgbu.
examples.english: The bite it gave me is paining me.

examples.igbo: Jị a dị oke ọnụ n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: This yam is very expensive in the market today.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere akwa a ji dị oke ọnụ otu a?
examples.english: Why is this cloth so expensive like this?

examples.igbo: Efere m dara wa n'ala ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: My plate fell and broke on the floor yesterday.

examples.igbo: Kpachara anya ka iko ahụ ghara ịda wa.
examples.english: Be careful so that cup does not fall and break.

examples.igbo: Biko, gbàzi ụzọ ahụ ka ọ kwụ ọtọ.
examples.english: Please, make that path straight so it stands upright.

examples.igbo: Nna anyị gbàzi ruru anyị ala n'ezi okwu.
examples.english: Our father advised us properly with true words.

examples.igbo: O tiri nwa ahụ ihe ma suo ya ụra.
examples.english: He beat the child and gave him a punch.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ị ji chọọ ịsuo m n'ihu?
examples.english: Why did you want to punch me in the face?

examples.igbo: Dibia ahụ maara otú esi gwọ ọrịà.
examples.english: That native doctor knows how to cure disease.

examples.igbo: Ọgwụ a ọ ga-egwọ ọrịà a n'oge?
examples.english: Will this medicine cure this disease on time?

examples.igbo: Eze nọ n'elu ùkpò ezè ya.
examples.english: The king is sitting on his royal throne.

examples.igbo: Ha rụrụ ọhụrụ ùkpò ezè maka emume ahụ.
examples.english: They built a new royal throne for the festival.

gloss: mix wine with water or other wine

examples.igbo: O ji mmiri gwa mmanya ahụ ka ọ ghara isi ike.
examples.english: He mixed water with that wine so it would not be too strong.

examples.igbo: Egbula oge ịgwa mmanya ahụ maka ndị ọbịa.
examples.english: Do not waste time mixing that wine for the guests.

examples.igbo: O mere ajō ife nime ōgbe nwaa
examples.english: He committed a crime in this neighborhood

examples.igbo: Ha kpọrọ omume ahụ ajō ife dị arọ
examples.english: They called that act a heavy abomination

examples.igbo: Ndị ukwe na-abụ abụ òtùto nime chọọchị
examples.english: The choir sings songs of praise inside the church

examples.igbo: Anyị nụrụ abụ òtùto tupu mmemme amalite
examples.english: We heard songs of praise before the event began

examples.igbo: Biko kekọta osisi ndia abụọ ọnụ
examples.english: Please join these two sticks together

examples.igbo: O kekọtara eriri abụọ ahụ siri ike
examples.english: She joined the two ropes together tightly

examples.igbo: Ndị nwoke na-agbu aja ụnọ nụ n'ụtụtụ
examples.english: The men are building walls of the mud building this morning

examples.igbo: Ha gwụchara agba mbụ nke igbu aja ụnọ
examples.english: They finished the first phase of building walls of the mud house

examples.igbo: Bịakwute m ka m gwa gị okwu
examples.english: Come near to me so I can speak to you

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji bịakwute ya ugbu a?
examples.english: Why did you come near to him now?

gloss: obstacle under water, such as tree-trunk or stone

examples.igbo: Ụgbọ mmiri kụrụ n'ọdò nọ n'osimiri
examples.english: The boat hit an obstacle under water in the river

examples.igbo: Ndị ọkụ azụ ziri ebe ọdò dị n'osimiri ahụ
examples.english: The fishermen pointed out where the underwater tree-trunk is in the river

gloss: rest or place hand upon something

examples.igbo: Bìdò aka gị n'elu tebụl ahụ
examples.english: Rest your hand upon that table

examples.igbo: O bìdọtara n'osisi iji zuo ike
examples.english: He rested his hand upon the tree to take a rest

examples.igbo: Chụni nnụnụ ndị ahụ n'ubi ọka
examples.english: Stir up those birds in the corn farm

examples.igbo: Nwa okorobịa ahụ chụniri nnụnụ site n'osisi
examples.english: The young man stirred up the birds from the tree

examples.igbo: Nwaanyị ahụ nwere ime òpùpù n'izu gara aga
examples.english: That woman had a miscarriage last week

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara ime òpùpù nye nwaanyị dị ime?
examples.english: What causes a miscarriage for a pregnant woman?

examples.igbo: Taabụ bụ oke ụbọsị nye ezinụlọ anyị
examples.english: Today is a great day for our family

examples.igbo: Ha mere mmemme dị ukwuu n'oke ụbọsị ahụ
examples.english: They held a grand celebration on that great day

examples.igbo: Biko, gosi m ebe àzụ ụnò dị.
examples.english: Please, show me where the toilet is.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ nọ n'àzụ ụnò a na-asa ákwú.
examples.english: That child is at the back of this house washing clothes.

examples.igbo: Onye nkụzi anyị kọwara ihe atọm bụ taa.
examples.english: Our teacher explained what an atom is today.

examples.igbo: Atọm pere mpe nke ukwuu n'ime ihe niile.
examples.english: An atom is very small in everything.

note: Scientific terms in Igbo can sometimes sound academic rather than everyday.

examples.igbo: Nwà kene! Gbalịa welie ibu ahụ.
examples.english: Just try! Try to lift that load.

examples.igbo: O kwuru na ya ga-emeri, nwà kene!
examples.english: He said he will win, just try!

examples.igbo: Nne m na-ati mkpụrụ aki n'ezi.
examples.english: My mother is cracking palm kernels outside.

examples.igbo: Onye zụtara nkume a iji tìe aki?
examples.english: Who bought this stone to crack nuts?

examples.igbo: O ji mma mapu anu ahụ n'ite.
examples.english: He used a knife to pierce the meat in the pot.

examples.igbo: Kpachara anya ka mma ghara imapu gị.
examples.english: Be careful so the knife does not pierce you.

examples.igbo: Ohi zuru ehi nna m n'abalị ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: A thief stole my father's cow last night.

examples.igbo: Gịnị ka nwata ahụ zuru n'ahịa?
examples.english: What did that child steal at the market?

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-akwa akwa n'ihi na agụụ na-agụ ya.
examples.english: That child is crying because he is hungry.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere o ji kwaa akwa mgbe e funahụrụ ya?
examples.english: Why did she weep when she got lost?

examples.igbo: Jiri eriri makwụ osisi a n'ime ogige.
examples.english: Use a rope to tie this tree inside the fence.

examples.igbo: O makwụ nwa ehi ahụ n'elu osisi.
examples.english: He tied the calf to the tree.

examples.igbo: Ụgbọ mmiri ahụ gbàgha mgbe ifufe siri ike bilitere.
examples.english: The boat turned round when a strong wind arose.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara ụgbọ ahụ iji gbàgha na mmiri?
examples.english: Why did that boat turn round in the water?

examples.igbo: Òwùwè ego a na-ewe iwe na-eweta nsogbu.
examples.english: Taking this money by force brings trouble.

examples.igbo: Òwùwè ihe ubi amaliteela n'ubi anyị.
examples.english: The harvesting of crops has started on our farm.

note: Depending on dialect, òwùwè can also mean harvest.

examples.igbo: Uwe ya na-eji oji nke ukwuu.
examples.english: His clothes are very black.

examples.igbo: Àkpa ahụ ọ zụrụ ọ na-eji oji?
examples.english: Is that bag she bought black?

examples.igbo: Ha na-agụ nwa ahụ afà n'ụlọ ụka.
examples.english: They are naming the child at the church.

examples.igbo: Gịnị ka ị ga-agụ nwa gị afà?
examples.english: What name will you give your child?

examples.igbo: Nna m ji mkpọ aga ije n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: My father uses a walking-stick to walk in the morning.

examples.igbo: Biko, nye m mkpọ ahụ ka m jiri kwado.
examples.english: Please, give me that walking-stick so I can support myself.

examples.igbo: Nne milichukwu m na-elekọta m nke ọma.
examples.english: My godmother takes good care of me.

examples.igbo: Ònye bụ nne milichukwu nwa gị?
examples.english: Who is your child's godmother?

examples.igbo: O nwere ìjèrìgà ego n'aka ya.
examples.english: He has billions of money in his hand.

examples.igbo: Ìjèrìgà mmadụ bi n'ụwa a.
examples.english: Billions of people live in this world.

examples.igbo: Ọ naghị aṅụ mmanyiikē n'ụlọ ya.
examples.english: He does not drink alcohol in his house.

examples.igbo: Mmanyiikē na-emerụ ahụ ma e jiri ya eme ihe.
examples.english: Alcohol is harmful when it is misused.

examples.igbo: Egwu ahụ wù n'obodo anyị ugbu a.
examples.english: That song is popular in our town now.

examples.english: Have you taken a quick breakfast before school starts?
