examples.igbo: O ji ǹgwu ànì gwuo olulu n'ubi.
examples.english: He used a digging tool to dig a hole on the farm.

examples.igbo: Biko, nye m ǹgwu ànì m ga-eji kụọ ji.
examples.english: Please, give me the digging tool I will use to plant yams.

gloss: money ritually offered to the dead

examples.igbo: Ha tụbara ego mmūọ n'ime ili nna ha.
examples.english: They threw ritual money for the dead into their father's grave.

examples.igbo: Ego mmūọ a ọ̀ bụ maka emume olili ozu?
examples.english: Is this ritual money for the burial ceremony?

gloss: empty; vain; useless (usually of a person)

examples.igbo: Nwa okorobịa ahụ bụ onye efùlefù n'obodo.
examples.english: That young man is a useless person in the village.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji na-akpa àgwà efùlefù otú a?
examples.english: Why are you behaving in such a vain manner?

gloss: to be resolute; refuse to budge; insist; stand firm

examples.igbo: Ọ kwụsi ikē na ọ gaghị ere ala ya.
examples.english: He stood firm that he would not sell his land.

examples.igbo: Biko, kwụsi ikē n'ihe ị kpebiri ime.
examples.english: Please, be resolute in what you decided to do.

gloss: act as or be a young woman

examples.igbo: Ọ na-eme àgbọghò n'agbanyeghị na ọ bụ nne.
examples.english: She acts like a young woman even though she is a mother.

examples.igbo: Nwaanyị ahụ na-eme àgbọghò n'ụzọ na-atọ ọchị.
examples.english: That woman is acting like a young woman in a funny way.

examples.igbo: Ùlumē ọkụkọ ahụ fepụrụ n'ikuku.
examples.english: The chicken's down feathers flew away in the wind.

examples.igbo: Àkwà a jupụtara n'ùlumē dị nro.
examples.english: This bed is filled with soft down feathers.

examples.igbo: Uwe ahụ na-akwụfèghalị n'elu eriri.
examples.english: The clothes are swinging on the line.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji na-akwụfèghalị n'ọnụ ụzọ?
examples.english: Why are you hanging around the doorway?

examples.igbo: Ụlọ a nādō mmadụ iri n'ime ya.
examples.english: This house can accommodate ten people inside it.

examples.igbo: Akpa a nādō akwụkwọ niile m nwere.
examples.english: This bag contains all the books I have.

examples.igbo: Onye ọchịchị ahụ chịkọbara obodo anyị nke ọma.
examples.english: That ruler governed our town well.

examples.igbo: Ọ chịkọbara ndị mmadụ n'udo na n'ịhụnanya.
examples.english: He ruled the people with peace and love.

examples.igbo: O kwere ka ya lògha n'uche ya ozugbo.
examples.english: He agreed to change his mind immediately.

examples.igbo: Nwa akwụkwọ ahụ lọtara ma lògha n'ime mmehie ya.
examples.english: The student came back and repented of his sins.

examples.igbo: Ụkwalà siri ike na-enye nwa ahụ nsogbu n'abalị.
examples.english: Severe cough is disturbing the child at night.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara na ụkwalà gị anaghị akwụsị taa?
examples.english: Why is your cough not stopping today?

examples.igbo: O kwesịrị iwedàta ànì n'ihu ndị okenye obodo.
examples.english: He needs to humble himself before the elders of the community.

examples.igbo: Eze ahụ chọrọ iwedàta ànì ndị na-ebuso ya agha.
examples.english: The king wanted to humiliate those waging war against him.

examples.igbo: Nkịta anyị na-gbọ ùja mgbe ọ bụla ọ hụrụ onye ọbịa.
examples.english: Our dog barks whenever it sees a stranger.

examples.igbo: Kpachara anya ka agụ ahụ wee ghara igbọ ùja ugbu a.
examples.english: Be careful so that the leopard does not roar now.

examples.igbo: Biko fesàsị mmiri a n'elu ákwà ndị ahụ.
examples.english: Please sprinkle this water completely on those clothes.

examples.igbo: O mere ka ọ fesàsị nnu n'ofe ahụ niile.
examples.english: She made sure to sprinkle salt all over the soup.

examples.igbo: Òdòdò mara mma na-acha n'ubi nne m n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: Beautiful flowers bloom in my mother's garden in the morning.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ụdị òdòdò ọhụrụ a toro n'ámá?
examples.english: Did you see this new kind of flower that grew in the compound?

examples.igbo: Kpachara anya n'ọkìlìkà nọ n'ụzọ ugbo ahụ.
examples.english: Be careful of the thorny climbing plant on that farm path.

examples.igbo: Ogwu sitere na ọkìlìkà nwere ike ịkpata nnukwu mmerụ ahụ.
examples.english: Thorns from the thorny climbing plant can cause serious injury.

note: Used in the context of farm paths and injury.

examples.igbo: Nwatakịrị ahụ chịnita aka ya ịchọ enyemaka.
examples.english: The child held up his hands to ask for help.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere o ji chịnita aka ya n'etiti igwe mmadụ?
examples.english: Why did he hold up his hands in the middle of the crowd?

examples.igbo: O kpebiri igatè aka ịchọ ebe ọrụ ka mma.
examples.english: He decided to go far away to look for a better job.

examples.igbo: Ebe ole ka ị chọrọ igatè aka taa?
examples.english: How far do you want to go today?

note: Metaphorical or physical distance.

examples.igbo: Were akwā ōmụma kpuchie nwa ahụ ka o wee ghara ịtụ oyi.
examples.english: Use the blanket to cover the child so that he will not feel cold.

examples.igbo: Nne zụtara akwā ōmụma ọhụrụ maka oge oyi a.
examples.english: Mother bought a new wrapper for this cold season.

examples.igbo: O nwere mgbasịlị akā ọlaedo n'mkpịsị aka ya.
examples.english: She has a gold finger-ring on her finger.

examples.igbo: Ì zụtara mgbasịlị akā ọhụrụ n'ahịa taa?
examples.english: Did you buy a new finger-ring at the market today?

gloss: nausea; cause a feeling to vomit

examples.igbo: Isi ọwụwa ahụ na-enye m nù agbọọ̄.
examples.english: That headache is causing me nausea.

examples.igbo: Ihe ahụ o riri na-enye ya nù agbọọ̄.
examples.english: The thing he ate is causing him nausea.

examples.igbo: Ndị ọrụ ahụ kpebiri ịshi ùshī n'ihu onye isi.
examples.english: The workers decided to lodge a protest before the boss.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere unu ji shi ùshī n'okwu a?
examples.english: Why did you all lodge a protest about this matter?

gloss: upward; upward to a desired level

examples.igbo: Biko, welite ite ahụ n'elu ọkụ.
examples.english: Please, lift that pot upward onto the fire.

examples.igbo: O welitere aka ya elu mgbe ọ hụrụ ya.
examples.english: He lifted his hand upward when he saw him.

examples.igbo: Mama ji aka ōkwute na-egweri ọka ahụ.
examples.english: Mother is using the stone for grinding corn to grind the corn.

examples.igbo: Ebee ka ị tinyere aka ōkwute ahụ?
examples.english: Where did you put that stone for grinding corn?

examples.igbo: A na-eji mma mbèbèlè n'ịcha ji.
examples.english: A knife is used in peeling yam.

examples.igbo: Ego a bụ nke mbèbèlè n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: This money is for use in school.

gloss: to reduce; to lower; to bring down; to demote

examples.igbo: Ha ga-eweda àlà ọnụ ahịa nri n'ahịa.
examples.english: They will reduce the price of food in the market.

examples.igbo: Biko, weda àlà olu redio ahụ.
examples.english: Please, lower the volume of that radio.

examples.igbo: O ŋefetara mmiri ahụ n'ụzọ ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: He stepped over that water quickly.

examples.igbo: Emela ka nwatakịrị ŋefeta ihe ahụ n'ala.
examples.english: Do not let the child step over that thing on the floor.

examples.igbo: Nne m na-afụ ji n'ime kichin.
examples.english: My mother is peeling yam in the kitchen.

examples.igbo: Ì fụrụla ji ahụ maka nri ehihie?
examples.english: Have you peeled the yam for lunch?

gloss: shrink; squeeze self in order to achieve a smaller size

examples.igbo: O shịkọrọ onwe ya ka o banye n'ụgbọala.
examples.english: He shrank himself to enter the car.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ shịkọrọ n'akụkụ m n'ihi oyi.
examples.english: The child shrank beside me because of the cold.

examples.igbo: Nínye akwụkwọ ahụ n'elu tebụl.
examples.english: Lay that book down on the table.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji nínye akpa gị n'ala?
examples.english: Why did you lay your bag down on the ground?

examples.igbo: Tinye ite n'elu akwùkwà ahụ.
examples.english: Put the pot on that cooking-stand.

examples.igbo: Akwùkwà a agbajiela n'ihi ọkụ.
examples.english: This cooking-stand has broken because of the fire.

gloss: go a short distance; go aside (especially for discussion)

examples.igbo: Biko, garụka ebe a ka anyị kwuo okwu.
examples.english: Please, go aside here so we can talk.

examples.igbo: O garụka n'akụkụ ụlọ ka ọ kpọọ oku.
examples.english: He went a short distance to the side of the house to make a call.

examples.igbo: Nna m na-aga n'ògò ya taa.
examples.english: My father is going to his farm today.

examples.igbo: Ògò a ọ̀ bụ nke gị ka ọ̀ bụ nke nwanne gị?
examples.english: Is this farm yours or is it your sibling's?

examples.igbo: Nwa okorobịa ahụ amalitela ịgba àfụ̀ọnụ̄.
examples.english: That young man has started to grow a beard.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-amasị ya ịgba àfụ̀ọnụ̄ nke ukwuu.
examples.english: He likes growing a beard very much.

examples.igbo: Ọgịlịga ya na-egbu ya mgbe ọ na-eku ume.
examples.english: His rib hurts him when he breathes.

examples.igbo: Dọkịta kwuru na ọgịlịga ya agbajiela.
examples.english: The doctor said that his rib is broken.

examples.igbo: Ọbàlà osisi a na-agwọ ọrịa afọ.
examples.english: The bark of this tree cures stomach ailments.

examples.igbo: Ị̀ chọrọ ọbàlà ọfòlò maka ọgwụ?
examples.english: Do you need the bark of the ọfòlò tree for medicine?

gloss: shout at suddenly (so as to frighten)

examples.igbo: Egbọjala nwa ahụ ụjọ n'ihi na ọ na-ebe ákwá.
examples.english: Do not shout at the child suddenly because he is crying.

examples.igbo: O gbọjara m ụjọ mgbe m na-ehi ụra.
examples.english: He shouted at me suddenly while I was sleeping.

examples.igbo: Kpọchie ụzọ ahụ na ùgòdì ya.
examples.english: Lock that door with its key.

examples.igbo: Ebee ka ị tinyere ùgòdì ụlọ a?
examples.english: Where did you put the key to this house?

gloss: believe in or agree to something

examples.igbo: Ekwenyere m na ihe niile ị gwara m.
examples.english: I believe in everything you told me.

examples.igbo: Ị̀ kwenyere na ihe ọ na-ekwu?
examples.english: Do you agree with what he is saying?

examples.igbo: Akòm na-enye nwa ahụ nsogbu n'abalị.
examples.english: Fever is bothering that child at night.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eche na ọ bụ akòm na-arịa ya?
examples.english: Do you think it is malaria that he is suffering from?

examples.igbo: Mwopū àfè tupu ị banye n'ime mmiri.
examples.english: Take off your clothes before you enter the water.

examples.igbo: Mwopū àfè ahụ mere ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: That taking off of clothes happened quickly.

examples.igbo: Onye na-anya ụgbọ mmiri ga-ayido ndị njem n'ọdụ.
examples.english: The boat driver will put the passengers ashore at the port.

examples.igbo: Biko, yido anyị n'akụkụ osimiri ahụ.
examples.english: Please, put us ashore by that riverbank.

examples.igbo: Ụmù ọkpū bịara emume ahụ n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: The married daughters came to the ceremony in the morning.

examples.igbo: Ebee ka ụmù ọkpū nọdụrụ?
examples.english: Where did the married daughters sit?

examples.igbo: Ọkwùlù ezì ahụ chara acha n'elu osisi.
examples.english: That pawpaw is ripe on the tree.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ ịzụta ọkwùlù ezì n'ahịa?
examples.english: Do you want to buy pawpaw at the market?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-achagbu ọnya ya na mmiri ọkụ.
examples.english: She is healing her sore by washing it with hot water.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-achagbu ọnya ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: You will heal that sore by washing it well.

gloss: can; small pot used for keeping oil, etc.

examples.igbo: Weta okpòkolo mmanụ ahụ ebe a.
examples.english: Bring that oil can here.

examples.igbo: Okpòkolo a ọ̀ dị mma maka nchekwa?
examples.english: Is this small pot good for storage?

examples.igbo: Arụrụ nkwū na-ebi n'ime osisi nkwū.
examples.english: The earwig lives inside the palm tree.

examples.igbo: Lee, arụrụ nkwū nọ n'elu akwụkwọ a.
examples.english: Look, an earwig is on this leaf.

examples.igbo: Ụmụ okorobịa ga-abọ ìlo n'ụtụtụ echi.
examples.english: The young men will clear the village square tomorrow morning.

examples.igbo: Onye ga-abọ ìlo taa?
examples.english: Who will clear the village square today?

gloss: fruit of iroko (used for feeding goats, sheep, etc.)

examples.igbo: Àbalà ọjì dị mma maka nri ewu.
examples.english: Iroko fruit is good for goat feed.

examples.igbo: Ị chịkọtara àbalà ọjì maka ewu gị?
examples.english: Did you gather iroko fruit for your goats?

examples.igbo: Kotù uwe ahụ n'elu eriri.
examples.english: Unhang that cloth from the line.

examples.igbo: Biko, kotù uwe ndị a n'ebe ahụ.
examples.english: Please, unhang these clothes from there.

examples.igbo: Nne m zụrụ kukuǹdùku n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: My mother bought sweet potato at the market today.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ iri kukuǹdùku a esiiri esi?
examples.english: Do you want to eat this boiled sweet potato?

examples.igbo: Akwa a ji òji nke ukwuu.
examples.english: This cloth is very dark-coloured.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere akpa gị ji òji otú a?
examples.english: Why is your bag dark-coloured like this?

gloss: boil very high to the level of having so much bubbles and sound(of the bubbles).

examples.igbo: Mmiri ahụ na-sụ̄ pụ̀tụ̀pụ̀tụ̀ n'ime ite.
examples.english: The water is boiling vigorously in the pot.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka ofe ahụ sụ̄ pụ̀tụ̀pụ̀tụ̀ n'ọkụ.
examples.english: Do not let the soup boil over on the fire.

examples.igbo: Kpọdo osisi ahụ n'elu mgbidi.
examples.english: Nail that wood onto the wall.

examples.igbo: Onye kpọdooro ụzọ a n'ebe a?
examples.english: Who fastened this door here?

gloss: (colloq.) be smoking a pipe, cigarette, etc. colloq. Ibè kpù òkù nónụ  Ibe is smoking at present

examples.igbo: Nna m na-ekpù òkù nónụ n'ezi.
examples.english: My father is smoking a pipe outside.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ekpù òkù nónụ mgbe niile.
examples.english: He is always smoking a cigarette.

examples.igbo: Ewetara m ikpo akwụkwọ gị n'ụlọ.
examples.english: I brought your set of books home.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ikpo akwụkwọ m n'elu tebụl?
examples.english: Did you see my set of books on the table?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-aga ịkọcha isi ya n'ahịa.
examples.english: He is going to shave his head at the market.

examples.igbo: Biko, kọchaa isi gị tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Please, shave your head before you go out.

gloss: secret cult with tendency to harm

examples.igbo: Ndị òtunzuzo ahụ na-eme ihe ọjọọ.
examples.english: Those members of the secret cult are doing evil things.

examples.igbo: Egwula egwu na ndị òtunzuzo ahụ.
examples.english: Do not play with those members of the secret cult.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-egbu imē n'ụlọ ọgwụ.
examples.english: She is aborting at the hospital.

examples.igbo: Ọ dị njọ ịgba imē n'ụzọ na-ezighị ezi.
examples.english: It is bad to commit abortion in an improper way.

examples.igbo: Onye ohi ahụ na-amịgharị n'azụ ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: That thief is sneaking around behind our house.

examples.igbo: Mmiri ahụ na-amịgharị n'ime ọhịa ahụ.
examples.english: The water meanders through the forest.

examples.igbo: Nna m zụrụ m igwè ọhụrụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: My father bought me a new bicycle at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eji igwè gaa ụlọ akwụkwọ echi?
examples.english: Will you go to school by bicycle tomorrow?

examples.igbo: Anyị hụrụ òtòbò n'ime osimiri ahụ.
examples.english: We saw a hippopotamus in that river.

examples.igbo: Òtòbò na-eri ahịhịa n'akụkụ mmiri.
examples.english: The hippopotamus is eating grass by the water.

examples.igbo: Ụgbọala anyị tọkị̀rị̀ n'ime apịtị ahụ.
examples.english: Our car got stuck in that mud.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ụkwụ gị ji tọkị̀rị̀ n'ebe ahụ?
examples.english: Why did your foot get stuck in that place?

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ yị̀rị̀ ara n'etiti obodo.
examples.english: That man became mad in the middle of the village.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụrụ na ị ṅụọ ọgwụ ahụ, ị ga-ayị̀ ara.
examples.english: If you drink that medicine, you will become mad.

examples.igbo: Ụlọ ahụ nwere ònwunwu mgbe anyị sachara ya.
examples.english: The house has brightness after we cleaned it.

examples.igbo: Anyanwụ na-enye ònwunwu n'elu mmiri.
examples.english: The sun gives a shining on the water.

examples.igbo: Buli elū akpa ahụ dị n'ala.
examples.english: Lift up that bag on the ground.

examples.igbo: Biko, buli elū nwa ahụ n'aka gị.
examples.english: Please, lift up that child in your arms.

gloss: be soft; be watery (especially of food)

examples.igbo: Nri a gbara nlò, ọ dịghị mma iri.
examples.english: This food is soft and watery, it is not good to eat.

examples.igbo: Esiila nri ahụ nke ukwuu ka ọ ghara ịgba nlò.
examples.english: Do not cook that food too much so it does not become watery.

examples.igbo: Anyị ga-agbana mgbe mmiri malitere izo.
examples.english: We will run home when the rain starts to fall.

examples.igbo: Gbaa n'ụlọ ngwa ngwa tupu ọ gbaa ọchịchịrị.
examples.english: Run home quickly before it gets dark.

examples.igbo: O dere aha ya dedoo n'akwụkwọ ahụ.
examples.english: He wrote his name upon that book.

examples.igbo: Biko, dedoo nọmba ekwentị gị n'elu tebụl.
examples.english: Please, write your phone number upon the table.

examples.igbo: Awelē bịara ya n'oge ọ na-achọ ọrụ.
examples.english: Good fortune came to him when he was looking for work.

examples.igbo: Ị̀ hụrụ awelē n'ihe ọrụ a ọ rụrụ?
examples.english: Did you see good luck in this work he did?

gloss: make food loose moisture, by exposing it to heat (fire or sun) or smoke, in order to preserve it; dry; smoke

examples.igbo: Mịa azụ̀ ndị a n'elu ọkụ ka ha ghara ire ure.
examples.english: Smoke these fish over the fire so they do not rot.

examples.igbo: Anyanwụ na-amị ji ndị a n'ezi.
examples.english: The sun is drying these yams outside.

gloss: lay foundation; establish underlying basis or principle

examples.igbo: Ha tọ̀rọ̀ ǹtọàlà ụlọ akwụkwọ ọhụrụ a n'izuụka gara aga.
examples.english: They laid the foundation of this new school last week.

examples.igbo: Anyị ga-atọ̀ ǹtọàlà maka ọrụ a taa.
examples.english: We will establish the underlying basis for this work today.

examples.igbo: O nyere m ego naatō maka nri ahụ.
examples.english: He gave me eighteen cowries for the food.

examples.igbo: Ị̀ ga-akwụ ego naatō maka akwụkwọ a?
examples.english: Will you pay eighteen cowries for this book?

examples.igbo: Ọ charàpụ̀rụ anya mgbe ọ hụrụ ihe ịtụnanya ahụ.
examples.english: He looked with eyes wide open when he saw that wonder.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji charàpụ̀ anya na-ele m?
examples.english: Why are you looking at me with eyes wide open?

examples.igbo: Kùdaa ite ahụ n'elu ọkụ ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Bring that pot down from the fire quickly.

examples.igbo: Ha kùdara ihe ndị ahụ n'elu ụlọ.
examples.english: They brought those things down from the roof.

examples.igbo: O kwuru ya sò òfu akpō n'ihu anyị niile.
examples.english: He said it once for all in front of us all.

examples.igbo: Ị̀ ga-eme ya sò òfu akpō ka ọ gwụ?
examples.english: Will you do it once only so it ends?

examples.igbo: Ha lụrụ anì na nkwekọrịta ọhụrụ n'ụtụtụ a.
examples.english: They arrived at a new agreement this morning.

examples.igbo: O gbabiri osisi ahụ n'etiti.
examples.english: He broke the stick in two.

examples.igbo: Biko, gbabie osisi a ka anyị nwee ọkụ.
examples.english: Please, break this wood in two so we can have fire.

examples.igbo: Mmanụ anwụ a na-atọ ụtọ nke ukwuu.
examples.english: This honey tastes very sweet.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara mmanụ anwụ n'ahịa taa?
examples.english: Did you buy honey at the market today?

examples.igbo: Ìkpò juru n'akụkụ ụzọ ugbo anyị.
examples.english: Tall coarse grass is full by the side of our farm path.

examples.igbo: Anyị ga-egbutu ìkpò ahụ n'ụtụtụ echi.
examples.english: We will cut down that tall grass tomorrow morning.

gloss: plunge; sink in; enter stealthily; sneak in

examples.igbo: Onye ohi ahụ mịbara n'ụlọ anyị n'abalị.
examples.english: The thief sneaked into our house at night.

examples.igbo: Mịba n'ime ụlọ ahụ tupu mmiri amalite izo.
examples.english: Sneak into that house before the rain starts falling.

examples.igbo: Nwa okorobịa ahụ na-akpa n gàn gà mgbe niile.
examples.english: That young man is always joking and boasting.

examples.igbo: Kwụsị ịkpa n gàn gà n'ihu ndị okenye.
examples.english: Stop joking and boasting in front of elders.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ada ǹdamanya n'ụlọ ọrụ kwa ụbọchị.
examples.english: He loafs about at the office every day.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji na-ada ǹdamanya n'ebe a?
examples.english: Why are you loafing about here?

gloss: kind of bean - small and round. Unlike other beans, the plant is a shrub and not a creeping plant

examples.igbo: Nne m na-akụ mkpùlù n'azụ ụlọ.
examples.english: My mother is planting small round beans behind the house.

examples.igbo: Mkpùlù a na-esi ísì ụtọ mgbe a na-esi ya.
examples.english: These small round beans smell good when being cooked.

examples.igbo: Agụụ na-agụ nwa ahụ nke ukwuu.
examples.english: The child is very hungry.

examples.igbo: Agụụ ọ na-agụ gị ma ị rụchaa ọrụ?
examples.english: Are you hungry when you finish working?

examples.igbo: Nne m siri ọfe egusi taa.
examples.english: My mother cooked egusi soup today.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eri ọfe a na-atọ ụtọ?
examples.english: Will you eat this delicious soup?

note: Standard spelling for soup.

examples.igbo: Mmiri na-ezo, n'ihi ya, anyị agaghị apụ.
examples.english: It is raining, thus we will not go out.

examples.igbo: Ọ rịara ọrịa, n'ihi ya, ọ bịaghị ọrụ.
examples.english: He was sick, thus he did not come to work.

examples.igbo: Òkụkū ìkìkè ahụ na-achọ nri n'ogige.
examples.english: That pullet is looking for food in the garden.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ òkụkū ìkìkè m n'azụ ụlọ?
examples.english: Did you see my pullet behind the house?

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-arịa ụkwalā nri kemgbe ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: That child has been suffering from whooping-cough since yesterday.

examples.igbo: Ụkwalā nri na-enye ụmụaka nsogbu nke ukwuu.
examples.english: Whooping-cough causes children a lot of trouble.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-anakọ n'ụlọ mgbe anyanwụ dara.
examples.english: We are going homewards when the sun sets.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ị na-anakọ n'ụlọ n'oge a?
examples.english: Why are you going homewards at this time?

gloss: knock the head with the knuckles; box

examples.igbo: Ọ kụrụ ya òkpọ n'isi n'ihi iwe.
examples.english: He knocked him on the head with his knuckles because of anger.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka onye ọ bụla kụọ gị òkpọ.
examples.english: Do not let anyone knock you on the head.

examples.igbo: Pukuga mmadụ bịara emume ahụ n'izu gara aga.
examples.english: Thousands of people came to the ceremony last week.

examples.igbo: Pukuga ego ka o ji wuo ụlọ ahụ.
examples.english: Thousands of money he used to build that house.

note: Pukuga is often used as an intensifier for large numbers.

gloss: instep of foot (literally the king’s baby never licks the sand)

examples.igbo: Nwa ezè alā aja m na-afụ ụfụ taa.
examples.english: My instep is hurting today.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ọnya dị n'elu nwa ezè alā aja ya?
examples.english: Did you see the sore on his instep?

examples.igbo: Ọnya ahụ ga-abo àpà n'ahụ ya.
examples.english: That wound will leave a scar on his body.

examples.igbo: Ọnya a ọ ga-abo àpà ma ọ gwọọ?
examples.english: Will this wound leave a scar when it heals?

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-egwùli egwu n'ezi ụlọ.
examples.english: The children are playing about in the compound.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ị na-egwùli egwu n'oge ọrụ?
examples.english: Why are you playing about during work time?

gloss: to organise, arrange or plan an activity or event

examples.igbo: Biko, hàzie oche ndị a maka nzukọ echi.
examples.english: Please, arrange these chairs for tomorrow's meeting.

examples.igbo: Anyị ga-ahàzi emume ahụ n'izu na-abịa.
examples.english: We will organize the ceremony next week.

examples.igbo: Dọkịta kwuru na ọ na-arịa ọrịa arị anyā.
examples.english: The doctor said he is suffering from filaria.

examples.igbo: Arị anyā na-ebute ọrịa n'anya mmadụ.
examples.english: Filaria causes disease in a person's eye.

examples.igbo: Kèpù ego ahụ n'ime akpa abụọ.
examples.english: Separate that money into two bags.

examples.igbo: O kèpùrù ụmụ ya n'ebe ọrụ.
examples.english: He separated his children at the workplace.

examples.igbo: Sighèe nri ahụ nke ọma tupu ndị ọbịa abịa.
examples.english: Cook that food properly before the guests arrive.

examples.igbo: Nne m na-asighè nri mgbe niile.
examples.english: My mother always cooks food properly.

gloss: ceremonial spear for ọzō ceremonies (= alò), and fighting or hunting spears, see asùduù and àgànà

examples.igbo: Onye ọzọ ahụ ji ubē ǹzè ya pụta.
examples.english: The titled man came out with his ceremonial spear.

examples.igbo: Ubē ǹzè a dị ezigbo ochie.
examples.english: This ceremonial spear is very old.

examples.igbo: Biko, dubà ndị ọbịa ahụ n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: Please, lead the guests into the house.

examples.igbo: O dubàrà m n'ime ọrụ ọhụrụ a.
examples.english: He introduced me into this new job.

examples.igbo: Gịnị ka ị na-eme n'ebe a?
examples.english: What are you doing here?

examples.igbo: M ga-eme ihe ọma taa.
examples.english: I will do a good thing today.

gloss: be playful towards someone or something; approach someone or something playfully

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-egwùsa egwū na-abịakwute nne ya.
examples.english: The child is playfully approaching his mother.

examples.igbo: Ị na-egwùsa egwū na-agwa m okwu?
examples.english: Are you being playful while talking to me?

examples.igbo: Nwa mkpùkpù umē ahụ na-ebe ákwá.
examples.english: The newborn infant is crying.

examples.igbo: Nne m mụrụ nwa mkpùkpù umē ọhụrụ.
examples.english: My mother gave birth to a new infant.

examples.igbo: Nne m zụrụ ugwùlùgwù anū n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: My mother bought breast of meat at the market today.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-esi ugwùlùgwù anū ahụ maka nri ehihie?
examples.english: Will you cook that breast of meat for lunch?

examples.igbo: Anyị ga-agba ụgbọ gaa obodo anyị echi.
examples.english: We will go by vehicle to our village tomorrow.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ ịgba ụgbọ gaa ụlọ akwụkwọ?
examples.english: Do you want to go by vehicle to school?

gloss: word asking for confirmation or denial of a report; e.g. A narrates to B something concerning C, and B turns to C saying 'Gbọò', which implies 'You have heard what A has said. Is it true?' B then expects C to confirm or deny A's statement

examples.igbo: O kwuru na ị tọrọ ya, gbọò?
examples.english: He said you stole from him, is it true?

examples.igbo: Ha sị na ị gaghị abịa ọrụ, gbọò?
examples.english: They said you will not come to work, is it true?

gloss: coming out of underground water, flooding the land of that area. An example is what sometimes occurs in buildings in swampy areas, where water sometimes appears and floods the floors

examples.igbo: Mmili ōwụwa mebiri ụlọ anyị n'ụtụtụ a.
examples.english: The rising underground water damaged our house this morning.

examples.igbo: Ebe a na-enwe mmili ōwụwa mgbe ọbụla.
examples.english: This place experiences rising underground water all the time.

examples.igbo: Eze ahụ yi akàlà ọkwā ya n'olu.
examples.english: The king wore his insignia of office on his neck.

examples.igbo: Onye isi ọhụrụ ahụ nwetara akàlà ọkwā ya.
examples.english: The new leader received his insignia of office.

examples.igbo: Lelee ọnụ egbè ahụ nke ọma tupu ị gbaa.
examples.english: Check the opening of that gun barrel well before you fire.

examples.igbo: Ọnụ egbè ahụ juru n'ájá.
examples.english: The opening of the gun barrel was full of sand.

gloss: to hold someone or something tightly closing your fingers  around them; clasp

examples.igbo: Tụkọ aka gị ka anyị jee ije.
examples.english: Clasp your hands so we can walk.

examples.igbo: Nwatakịrị ahụ tụkọ aka ya n'ihi ụjọ.
examples.english: The child clasped his hands because of fear.

examples.igbo: Uwe m ọhụrụ bụ akwụkwọ ndụ akwụkwọ ndụ.
examples.english: My new dress is green.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ akwụkwọ ndụ akwụkwọ ndụ n'ubi ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see the green in that garden?

examples.igbo: Akpa ahụ bụ ògùlu ògùlù.
examples.english: That bag is yellow.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere agba ògùlu ògùlù?
examples.english: Do you have yellow paint?

examples.igbo: Tūkwù n'ala ka anyị rie nri.
examples.english: Squat on the ground so we can eat.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji tūkwù n'ebe ahụ?
examples.english: Why are you squatting over there?

examples.igbo: Ọ binyelụ nwanne ya nwoke n'obodo ahụ.
examples.english: He lived with his brother in that town.

examples.igbo: Ị binyelụ onye n'ụlọ a tupu afọ a?
examples.english: Did you live with anyone in this house before this year?

gloss: speak the truth Ọ bù ezi okwu#kà m nà-èkwu I am speaking the truth

examples.igbo: Biko, kwuo ezi okwu gbasara ihe ahụ.
examples.english: Please, speak the truth about that matter.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ekwu ezi okwu mgbe niile.
examples.english: He speaks the truth at all times.

examples.igbo: Ji òyìbè a tọrọ ụtọ nke ukwuu.
examples.english: This yellow guinea yam is very delicious.

examples.igbo: Anyị kụrụ ji òyìbè n'ugbo anyị.
examples.english: We planted yellow guinea yam on our farm.

gloss: die a natural death Nwoke afù nwùlù ọnwụ Chiì ya The man died a natural death

examples.igbo: Nna nna m nwụrụ ọnwụ Chi ya n'udo.
examples.english: My grandfather died a natural death in peace.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ ihe ọma ịnwụ ọnwụ Chi mgbe agadi.
examples.english: It is a good thing to die a natural death in old age.

examples.igbo: Àrụ ikē bụ akụ na ụba.
examples.english: Good health is wealth.

examples.igbo: Iri nri ọma na-eweta àrụ ikē.
examples.english: Eating good food brings good health.

examples.igbo: Anyị riri àzịụ̄tụ̄tụ̀ n'ụtụtụ taa.
examples.english: We ate breakfast this morning.

examples.igbo: Ị kwadebewo àzịụ̄tụ̄tụ̀ maka ụmụaka?
examples.english: Have you prepared breakfast for the children?

gloss: Musk Shrew (Crocidura spp.), a small, sharp-nosed creature which feeds on insects and protects itself with an obnoxious smell

examples.igbo: ǹkakwū na-esi ísì ọjọọ n'ụlọ.
examples.english: The musk shrew smells bad in the house.

examples.igbo: Nwamba ahụ gburu ǹkakwū n'azụ ụlọ.
examples.english: The cat killed a musk shrew behind the house.

examples.igbo: O nwere ọgụ ego abụọ n'akpa ya.
examples.english: He has two scores of money in his pocket.

examples.igbo: Ọgụ mmadụ ole bịara n'ememme ahụ?
examples.english: How many scores of people came to the festival?

examples.igbo: Aṅụ ahụ na-akpo lìlìlì n'elu osisi.
examples.english: The bees are swarming on the tree.

examples.igbo: Lee, aṅụ na-akpo lìlìlì nso n'ụlọ anyị!
examples.english: Look, bees are swarming near our house!

examples.igbo: Ụzọ ahụ jupụtara na òpòtòpòtò mgbe mmiri zoro.
examples.english: The road was full of mud when it rained.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ụkwụ gị ji nọrọ na òpòtòpòtò?
examples.english: Why are your feet in the mud?

examples.igbo: Ọ lara afọ mmiri n'ụlọ oriri ahụ.
examples.english: He drank water to his satisfaction at the restaurant.

examples.igbo: Ị lara afọ mmiri ara ehi n'ụtụtụ a?
examples.english: Did you drink milk to your satisfaction this morning?

examples.igbo: Ezinụlọ ahụ na-eru ụjū maka nna ha nwụrụ.
examples.english: The family is mourning because their father died.

examples.igbo: Ha na-eru ụjū n'ụlọ ha kemgbe ụbọchị ahụ.
examples.english: They have been mourning in their house since that day.

examples.igbo: Onye àsìlì ahụ na-akọrọ ndị agbata obi anyị okwu.
examples.english: That gossip is telling our neighbors stories.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka onye àsìlì banye n'ụlọ gị.
examples.english: Do not let a gossip enter your house.

examples.igbo: Ụwà anya ọkū anaghị achọ ka ibe ya nwee ọganihu.
examples.english: An envious world does not want its neighbor to succeed.

examples.igbo: Anyị bi n'ụwà anya ọkū nke na-adịghị mma.
examples.english: We live in an envious world that is not good.

examples.igbo: Onye ọzụzụ atụrụ chụchìghara atụrụ ya n'ime ogige.
examples.english: The shepherd chased his sheep back into the pen.

examples.igbo: Chụchìghara ọkụkọ ahụ n'ime ụlọ ya ozugbo.
examples.english: Chase the chicken back into its coop immediately.

examples.igbo: Èbù emebiela akwa ndị a n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: Mildew has ruined these clothes inside the house.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ èbù n'elu achịcha ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see mildew on that bread?

examples.igbo: Chedebe nche n'ọnụ ụzọ ruo mgbe m ga-alọta.
examples.english: Stop waiting at the door until I return.

examples.igbo: O chedebeghị nche n'ebe ahụ ọzọ.
examples.english: He stopped waiting at that place again.

note: The verb is rarely used in this specific compound sense; usually 'kwụsị ichere' is preferred.

examples.igbo: Nna m tinyere ikō n'ime osimiri ahụ.
examples.english: My father put a fish-trap inside the river.

examples.igbo: Ikō ahụ jupụtara na azụ n'ụtụtụ a.
examples.english: The fish-trap was full of fish this morning.

examples.igbo: Ọ kwuwapụrụ eziokwu ahụ n'ihu ndị mmadụ niile.
examples.english: He spoke out the truth plainly before all the people.

examples.igbo: Biko, kwuwapụ ihe ọjọọ ahụ ị hụrụ.
examples.english: Please, speak out plainly about the bad thing you saw.

examples.igbo: Igbu mmadụ bụ nsọ Ànì n'ala Igbo.
examples.english: Killing a person is an abomination in Igbo land.

examples.igbo: Ịgha ụgha ọ bụ nsọ Ànì n'ala anyị?
examples.english: Is lying an abomination in our land?

examples.igbo: Dọgha oche ahụ ntakịrị n'akụkụ ọzọ.
examples.english: Move that chair a little to the other side.

examples.igbo: O dọghaara igbe ahụ n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: He moved the box into the house.

examples.igbo: O na-agba m ụgwọ ego ahụ m ji ya.
examples.english: He is demanding the money I owe him.

examples.igbo: Gbaa ya ụgwọ tupu ọ pụọ n'obodo.
examples.english: Demand his debt before he leaves town.

examples.igbo: N'oge emume, e mere òkìkà manya n'obodo.
examples.english: During the festival, ceremonial drinking was held in town.

examples.igbo: Ndị okenye na-eme òkìkà manya tupu alụmdi na nwunye.
examples.english: Elders perform ceremonial drinking before marriage.

examples.igbo: Dọkalịa akwụkwọ ahụ dị na mgbidi.
examples.english: Tear off that paper on the wall.

examples.igbo: O dọkalịrị ego n'aka nwanne ya.
examples.english: He snatched money from his brother's hand.

examples.igbo: Ọ dịghị m ànịnị n'akpa m.
examples.english: I do not have a tenth of a penny in my pocket.

examples.igbo: O nyere nwatakịrị ànịnị maka ihe ọṅụṅụ.
examples.english: He gave the child a tenth of a penny for a drink.

gloss: nose partly or wholly destroyed by disease; depressed nostril

examples.igbo: Ọrịa ahụ mebiri imi ya, ọ bụ imi mpīa ugbu a.
examples.english: The disease destroyed his nose; it is imi mpīa now.

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ nwere imi mpīa mgbe ọ rịasịrị ọrịa.
examples.english: That man had imi mpīa after he was ill.

gloss: kind of ant with painful bite and characteristic smell; stink-ant

examples.igbo: Aṅàafì tara nwa m n'ụkwụ aka ekpe.
examples.english: A stink-ant bit my child on the left leg.

examples.igbo: E nwere ọtụtụ aṅàafì n'akụkụ ụlọ ahụ.
examples.english: There are many stink-ants near that house.

gloss: small child; caressing words used by mothers to their children

examples.igbo: Nne m kpọrọ m ọbele nnwā mgbe m dị obere.
examples.english: My mother called me ọbele nnwā when I was small.

examples.igbo: Ọbele nnwā, bịa ebe a rie nri.
examples.english: Little child, come here and eat food.

gloss: rashes; itch; the act of scratching

examples.igbo: Ahụ nwa ahụ na-akọ ọkọ n'abalị.
examples.english: That child's body itches at night.

examples.igbo: Kpachara anya ka ọkọ ghara ịbịa n'ahụ gị.
examples.english: Be careful so rash does not come on your body.

note: The sense of ọkọ as itch/rash is known, but the phrasing may vary by dialect.

examples.igbo: O dàlụrụ nwa ya aka gafee okporo ámá.
examples.english: He took his child by the hand across the road.

examples.igbo: Dàlụ m aka ka anyị gaa ụlọ ahịa.
examples.english: Take me by the hand so we go to the market.

examples.igbo: Ehi na-ata ahịhịa n'ebe ịtā nni.
examples.english: Cows graze grass in the pasture.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-edu atụrụ gaa ebe ịtā nni.
examples.english: We lead sheep to the pasture.

note: The headword is understood as pasture, but the compound is not common in all areas.

examples.igbo: Ndị nche atụlū na-elekọta atụrụ n'abalị.
examples.english: Shepherds look after sheep at night.

examples.igbo: Ndị nche atụlū zọpụtara atụrụ furu efu.
examples.english: Shepherds rescued a lost sheep.

note: The spelling atụlū for sheep is less common than atụrụ.

examples.igbo: Anyị ga-ebi n'ụlọ a ọkpụtọ̀rọkpụ̄, ọ dịghị mgbe anyị ga-akwaga.
examples.english: We will live in this house forever; we will never move.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ kwuru na ọ ga-echeta nne ya ọkpụtọ̀rọkpụ̄.
examples.english: That child said he would remember his mother forever.

note: The headword is understood as forever, but its tone marking is unusual.

examples.igbo: Onye ahụ wepụtara mkpō ūtabà n'akpa ya.
examples.english: That person brought out a snuff-box from his bag.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-etinye ụtaba n'ime mkpō ūtabà.
examples.english: He puts snuff inside the snuff-box.

examples.igbo: O kọrọ nsi megide nwanne ya nwoke.
examples.english: He practised sorcery against his brother.

examples.igbo: Ekọla nsi megide onye ọ bụla n'ime obodo a.
examples.english: Do not practise sorcery against anyone in this town.

note: The verb is clear, but sorcery language varies by region.

examples.igbo: O fụjọrọ nwoke ahụ n'ihi okwu ya.
examples.english: He disliked that man because of his words.

examples.igbo: Afụjọla onye na-agwa gị eziokwu mgbe niile.
examples.english: Do not dislike the person who always tells you the truth.

note: The sense is clear, but the negative imperative form may be phrased differently by some speakers.

examples.igbo: Uwe a tosịrị gị nke ọma.
examples.english: This dress fits you well.

examples.igbo: Akpụkpọ ụkwụ a agaghị atosị nwa ahụ.
examples.english: These shoes will not fit that child.

examples.igbo: Onye nsụ ahụ na-ekwu okwu nwayọọ.
examples.english: That stammerer speaks slowly.

examples.igbo: Ekwela onye nsụ ọchị n'ihu ọha.
examples.english: Don't laugh at a stammerer in public.

examples.igbo: Ekenèegwùrùgwù pụtara n'elu igwe mgbe mmiri zọrọ.
examples.english: A rainbow appeared in the sky after it rained.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ekenèegwùrùgwù n'elu igwe ụnyaahụ?
examples.english: Did you see the rainbow in the sky yesterday?

examples.igbo: Dọpụ mkpara ahụ n'ime ọkụ.
examples.english: Draw that stick out of the fire.

examples.igbo: O dọpụrụ nkata ahụ n'ime olulu.
examples.english: He drew the basket out of the hole.

examples.igbo: Mmiri na-ezo ugbu a.
examples.english: It is raining now.

examples.igbo: Echi ọ ga-ezo?
examples.english: Will it rain tomorrow?

gloss: from time to time; now and then

examples.igbo: M na-aga ahịa ogē nā ogè.
examples.english: I go to the market from time to time.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eleta nne gị ogē nā ogè?
examples.english: Do you visit your mother now and then?

examples.igbo: Chìcha ihe odide ahụ n'akwụkwọ.
examples.english: Erase that writing from the book.

examples.igbo: O chìchara aha m na bọọdụ.
examples.english: He erased my name on the board.

examples.igbo: O detòrọ onye isi obodo n'akwụkwọ akụkọ.
examples.english: He lampooned the town chairman in the newspaper.

examples.igbo: Ndị na-ede akwụkwọ na-adetò ndị ọchịchị.
examples.english: Writers lampoon leaders.

note: Rare verb; the inflected forms are plausible but not common.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka nọsasịrị n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: The children sat scattered in the room.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ka ndị ọbịa nọsasịrị n'ogige?
examples.english: Did you see how the guests sat scattered in the compound?

note: Uncommon verb; the inflection is uncertain.

gloss: move things to somewhere else by packing them

examples.igbo: O kwafere ngwongwo ya n'ụlọ ọhụrụ.
examples.english: He moved his belongings to the new house.

examples.igbo: Ị kwafere akpa ndị a n'ụgbọala?
examples.english: Did you move these bags into the car?

note: Rare verb; meaning and inflection are inferred.

examples.igbo: Nne m na-eji n kwọ òsè egbu ose.
examples.english: My mother uses a pepper-grinder to grind pepper.

examples.igbo: Ebee ka ị zụtara n kwọ òsè?
examples.english: Where did you buy the pepper-grinder?

note: The headword spacing is unusual; kept as given.

examples.igbo: Anyị nwere nkwụsịtụ obere oge n'ọrụ.
examples.english: We had a short break in work.

examples.igbo: Nkwụsịtụ ahụ were nkeji iri?
examples.english: Did the break last ten minutes?

gloss: move backwards (of insects); flow back, down (of water)

examples.igbo: Mmiri na-arịchìgha n'ala mgbe o zoro.
examples.english: Water flows down on the ground when it rains.

examples.igbo: Ahụhụ ọ na-arịchìgha n'osisi?
examples.english: Does the insect move backwards on the tree?

examples.igbo: Ntà m na-akwa akwa.
examples.english: My younger one is crying.

examples.igbo: Ntà, bịa were nri gị.
examples.english: Little one, come and take your food.

gloss: the last day; the day of judgment

examples.igbo: Ụbòsị ìkpe āzụ ga-abịa.
examples.english: The last day will come.

examples.igbo: Ndị mmadụ na-eche ụbòsị ìkpe āzụ.
examples.english: People are waiting for the last day.

gloss: press using the hand (palm or fingers); imprint finger or hand

examples.igbo: Bị̀a aka gị n'akwụkwọ a.
examples.english: Press your hand on this paper.

examples.igbo: O bịara aka n'ọnụ ụzọ.
examples.english: She pressed her hand on the door.

examples.igbo: Elili ọfīa dị n'akụkụ ụlọ.
examples.english: A snake is beside the house.

examples.igbo: Ahụrụ m elili ọfīa n'ụzọ.
examples.english: I saw a snake on the road.

gloss: pull down the lower eyelids and widen the eyes as a form of mockery, to imply ‘I told you so!’ or ‘Just what I expected!’ (i.e. rejoicing over someone else’s misfortune)

examples.igbo: Ọ bòrò ntòọō mgbe m dara ule.
examples.english: She mocked me with an eyelid pull when I failed the exam.

examples.igbo: Ị bòrò ntòọō n'ihu ya?
examples.english: Did you mock him with an eyelid pull?

examples.igbo: O nọrọ ọgwù n'ahụ ya.
examples.english: She rubbed balm on her body.

examples.igbo: Nọọ ọgwù n'isi gị.
examples.english: Rub balm on your head.

gloss: scoop nonliquid materials present in a liquid; dredge;

examples.igbo: O gwọrọ azụ̀ n'ite.
examples.english: She scooped fish from the pot.

examples.igbo: Gwọọ akwụkwọ n'ime mmiri.
examples.english: Scoop the leaves out of the water.

examples.igbo: O lùnyere aka ya n'ime ntụ.
examples.english: She poked her finger into the ash.

examples.igbo: Lùnye aka gị n'ime oghere ahụ.
examples.english: Poke your finger into that hole.

gloss: send representative, ambassador, special messenger, middleman

examples.igbo: O raara ụkò ka ha bịa nzukọ.
examples.english: He sent a messenger to tell them to come to the meeting.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji ra ụkò n'obodo ọzọ?
examples.english: Why did you send a messenger to another town?

note: The verb -ra ụkò is uncommon; inflected forms are based on its plain sense of sending word or a representative.

gloss: tree bear or Ashanti tree-hyrax (Dendrohyrax dorsalis sylvestris Temm.)

examples.igbo: Nkịta ọfīa na-ebi n'ime ọhịa.
examples.english: The tree hyrax lives in the forest.

examples.igbo: Ị hụtụla nkịta ọfīa n'elu osisi?
examples.english: Have you seen a tree hyrax on a tree?

note: The animal name is specialized; the sentences are simple and literal.

examples.igbo: Òfịfị nke eriri ahụ siri ike.
examples.english: The twisting of that rope is strong.

examples.igbo: Lee òfịfị osisi a!
examples.english: Look at the twisting of this tree!

note: Òfịfị is a less common noun; the examples show its sense of twisting or winding.

gloss: carry child on the back Kwòlụ nnwā Carry the child on your back

examples.igbo: O kwòrọ nnwa ya n'azụ gaa ahịa.
examples.english: She carried her child on her back to the market.

examples.igbo: Kwòlụ nnwa gị, ọ na-ebe akwa.
examples.english: Carry your child on your back, he is crying.

note: The verb stem -kwò is shown with a past form and an imperative; nnwa is kept as in the entry.

examples.igbo: Àpà ụkwū ya dị n'ájá.
examples.english: His footprints are in the sand.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ àpà ụkwū n'ụzọ?
examples.english: Did you see footprints on the road?

examples.igbo: O kwetara na ọ ga-abịa.
examples.english: He agreed that he will come.

examples.igbo: Ị kwetara na anyị ga-akwụ ụgwọ?
examples.english: Do you agree that we will pay?

examples.igbo: O kpàchara isi ya tupu agbamakwụkwọ.
examples.english: He shaved his hair before the wedding.

examples.igbo: Kpàcha isi gị, ọ dị ogologo.
examples.english: Shave your hair, it is long.

note: The verb is shown inflected; kpàcha is used in the sense of cropping or shaving hair.

examples.igbo: Kèdụ ife ị na-achọ n'ahịa?
examples.english: What are you looking for in the market?

examples.igbo: Ọ maghị kèdụ ife ọ ga-azụ.
examples.english: He does not know what to buy.

note: The spelling ife follows the entry; standard modern Igbo often writes ihe.

examples.igbo: Òmùlù nwa nke ego ahụ dị oke.
examples.english: The interest on that money is too much.

examples.igbo: O nyere m ego na-enweghị òmùlù nwa.
examples.english: He gave me money without interest.

note: The form òmùlù nwa is a variant for interest on money; the examples keep the entry spelling.

gloss: the job of mixing or carrying sand or cement to the plasterer in a building construction site

examples.igbo: Ọ na-arụ ọrụ kimbom n'ebe a na-ewu ụlọ.
examples.english: He does kimbom work at the building site.

examples.igbo: Kimbom ahụ na-ebu ájá na simenti.
examples.english: That kimbom is carrying sand and cement.

note: Kimbom is a construction-site borrowing; the examples use it as the job of mixing or carrying materials.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-eme àghalā n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: That child is troublesome at school.

examples.igbo: Emela àghalā, gee ntị na nne gị.
examples.english: Don't be troublesome, listen to your mother.

examples.igbo: Onye ọrịa ahụ kụdebere ume n'abalị.
examples.english: The patient stopped breathing at night.

examples.igbo: Egwula ya ka ọ ghara ikụdebe ume.
examples.english: Don't shake him so he doesn't stop breathing.

note: Inflection of -kùdebe ume is uncertain; I used kụdebere/ikụdebe.

examples.igbo: Nye m ifeē nụfù, biko.
examples.english: Give me that thing yonder, please.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-enye m ifeē nụfù taa?
examples.english: Will you give me that thing yonder today?

note: ifeē nụfù appears dialectal; kept as given.

gloss: suck enough; to suck to fill; draw fluid (oil)

examples.igbo: Nwa ọhụrụ mịjuru mmiri ara nne ya.
examples.english: The baby sucked enough of its mother's milk.

examples.igbo: Mịjuo mmanụ n'ite ahụ tupu ọ jụọ oyi.
examples.english: Draw oil from that pot before it gets cold.

note: Oil sense is less common; phrasing may vary.

gloss: suffer greatly; see many tribulations; have hard experience

examples.igbo: Ndị njem ahụ hụsịrị anya n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: Those travelers suffered greatly on the road.

examples.igbo: Ị hụsịrị anya n'oge agha?
examples.english: Did you suffer greatly during the war?

examples.igbo: Dinta ahụ ghere nsi maka akụ ya.
examples.english: That hunter prepared poison for his arrow.

examples.igbo: Eghela nsi n'ụlọ a.
examples.english: Do not prepare poison in this house.

note: ghe nsi is uncommon; inflection may differ.

examples.igbo: Ọ jụrụ m ajụjụ.
examples.english: He asked me a question.

examples.igbo: Jụọ ya ihe mere o ji abịa.
examples.english: Ask him why he came.

examples.igbo: Àjàdù nwaànyì ahụ na-ere akwụkwọ n'ahịa.
examples.english: That widow sells vegetables in the market.

examples.igbo: Ị maara àjàdù nwaànyì bi n'ụlọ ahụ?
examples.english: Do you know the widow living in that house?

examples.igbo: Ọ kpụrụ òkpu ọhụrụ.
examples.english: He wore a new cap.

examples.igbo: Kpụọ òkpu gị, anyanwụ na-acha.
examples.english: Put on your cap, the sun is shining.

examples.igbo: Ọ rọrọ aka n'ụkwụ m.
examples.english: She massaged my leg.

examples.igbo: Rọọ aka n'olu m, biko.
examples.english: Massage my neck, please.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-akpagharị n'okporo ámá.
examples.english: The children are roaming around the street.

examples.igbo: Ị kpagharịrị ebe niile?
examples.english: Did you explore everywhere?

note: The past form kpagharịrị is used; the sense is move round/explore.

examples.igbo: Nrìba amā ahụ dị n'aka nwa ahụ.
examples.english: That mark is on the child's hand.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ nrìba amā n'azụ ehi ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see the mark on that cow's back?

note: nrìba amā is used here as a distinguishing mark or sign.

examples.igbo: Ụmụ nnụnụ fegara n'osisi ọzọ.
examples.english: The birds flew over to another tree.

examples.igbo: Fega n'ofe osimiri ahụ.
examples.english: Fly over to the other side of that river.

gloss: troublesome world; world of trials and tribulations (literally world of sands; any food or beautiful thing, once sand is spilt into it, is fouled)

examples.igbo: Anyị na-ebi n'ùwà aja āja.
examples.english: We live in a troublesome world.

examples.igbo: Ùwà aja āja a, olee mgbe ọ ga-agwụ?
examples.english: This troublesome world, when will it end?

note: The phrase is idiomatic and carries the sense of a world of trials.

examples.igbo: Nri a dị ọma.
examples.english: This food is good.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eme ọma?
examples.english: Are you doing well?

examples.igbo: Anyị na-abụ abù ọma n'ụka.
examples.english: We sing psalms in church.

examples.igbo: Gụọ abù ọma nke iri abụọ na atọ.
examples.english: Read Psalm 23.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-ebu àpà n'ihu ya.
examples.english: That child has a mark on his face.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ebu àpà n'aka?
examples.english: Do you have a mark on your hand?

note: The verb is used in the continuous form na-ebu àpà.

examples.igbo: Bọọlụ ahụ kpọrè n'ala.
examples.english: The ball rolled along the ground.

examples.igbo: Ị kpọrè mgbidi ahụ?
examples.english: Did you demolish that wall?

note: The first sentence shows rolling; the second shows flattening/demolishing.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ bụ enwēnneenwēnnà.
examples.english: That child is an orphan.

examples.igbo: Ị nyere enwēnneenwēnnà ahụ nri?
examples.english: Did you give that orphan food?

note: The long compound is treated as a noun meaning orphan.

examples.igbo: O fụ̀nyere taya ụgbọala ahụ umē.
examples.english: He inflated the car tyre.

examples.igbo: Fụ̀nye bọọlụ ahụ umē.
examples.english: Pump air into that ball.

examples.igbo: Hìcha ākā gị tupu i rie nri.
examples.english: Wipe your hands before you eat.

examples.igbo: O hìchara ākā ya na akwa ọcha.
examples.english: She wiped her hands on a white cloth.

examples.igbo: Fierube eriri n'úkwù gị.
examples.english: Tie the rope around your waist.

examples.igbo: O na-efierube akwa n'úkwù ya.
examples.english: She is tying a cloth around her waist.

note: Verb stem -fierube; forms used are imperative and present continuous.

examples.igbo: Nneta anyị bịara bụ maka onye ọrịa.
examples.english: Our visit is for the sick person.

examples.igbo: Ị na-aga nneta n'ụlọ ndị nwụrụ anwụ?
examples.english: Are you going to visit the bereaved?

note: nneta is a less common noun; used here in the sense of a visit to the sick or bereaved.

gloss: keep a heavy object in the wrong position

examples.igbo: O dọghàrị̀ nnukwu nkume n'ọnụ ụzọ.
examples.english: He kept a heavy stone at the doorway.

examples.igbo: E dọghàrị̀la igbe ahụ n'ebe ahụ.
examples.english: Don't keep that box there.

note: Uncertain about the exact inflection and usage of dọghàrị̀; examples are tentative.

examples.igbo: Elu-igwe gbara ọchịchịrị tupu mmiri ezoo.
examples.english: The sky was dark before it rained.

examples.igbo: Lee elu-igwe, ọ na-acha anụnụ anụnụ.
examples.english: Look at the sky, it is blue.

gloss: used to seek forgiveness or permission; please (when pleading);

examples.igbo: Bikō, nyere m mmiri.
examples.english: Please, give me water.

examples.igbo: Bikō, ị ga-enyere m aka?
examples.english: Please, will you help me?

gloss: clear; clean by burning Jèe kwànwue ọkụ a gà-èji kpọcha atụlụ  a nà-àkwadebe igbu#Go and make the fire with which the hair of the sheep that is about to be slaughtered will be burned off

examples.igbo: Jee kwanye ọkụ iji kpọcha ewu ahụ.
examples.english: Go and make fire to singe that goat.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-akpọcha ọkụkọ tupu anyị esi ya.
examples.english: We singe the chicken before we cook it.

examples.igbo: O kpọlịrị m n'ihu mmadụ.
examples.english: He reproached me in public.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji akpọlị nwanne gị?
examples.english: Why are you abusing your sibling?

note: Verb stem -kpòlị; inflected forms kpọlịrị and akpọlị are used.

examples.igbo: Ezè anụmànù bụ enyi, ọ kacha ibu n'ọhịa.
examples.english: The king of beasts is the elephant; it is the largest in the bush.

examples.igbo: Ndị njem ahụ hụrụ ezè anụmànù n'ụzọ?
examples.english: Did the travellers see the king of beasts on the way?

examples.igbo: Onye ọzụzụ chụdara atụrụ ya n'ugwu n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: The shepherd drove his sheep down the hill in the morning.

examples.igbo: Ị chụdara ewu gị n'ugwu?
examples.english: Did you drive your goat down the hill?

examples.igbo: Chụgọọ ewu gị n'elu ugwu.
examples.english: Chase your goat up the hill.

examples.igbo: Ọ chụgọrọ atụrụ ya n'elu ugwu.
examples.english: He chased his sheep up the hill.

note: The verb is uncommon; the inflected forms given are the ones I judge most likely.

gloss: press sprain, etc., with cloth dipped in hot water

examples.igbo: Ọ mara mmiri n'ụkwụ ya mgbe ọ zara aza.
examples.english: She applied a hot compress to her foot when it sprained.

examples.igbo: Maa mmiri n'azụ ya ugbu a.
examples.english: Apply a hot compress to his back now.

gloss: sleepover; a night spent at a hotel, motel, or home, especially while traveling

examples.igbo: Anyị mere nhibọọchī n'ụlọ enyi m n'abalị ahụ.
examples.english: We had a sleepover at my friend's house that night.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ ime nhibọọchī n'ụlọ nkwari akụ?
examples.english: Do you want to spend the night at a hotel?

gloss: to be able to do something

examples.igbo: Ọ meli iburu akpa ahụ.
examples.english: He was able to carry that bag.

examples.igbo: Ị meliri imecha ọrụ ahụ?
examples.english: Were you able to finish that work?

note: The sense is clear but the word is not common in everyday speech; the past form used is 'meliri'.

examples.igbo: Wughee ọnụ ụzọ ahụ.
examples.english: Open that door.

examples.igbo: Eze wughere ụlọ ọhụrụ ahụ n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: The king declared that new building open in the morning.

examples.igbo: Ọ gbajiri alaka osisi ahụ.
examples.english: He broke that tree branch.

examples.igbo: Gbajie osisi ahụ ma ọ dị ogologo.
examples.english: Break that stick if it is long.

examples.igbo: Ọ dara n'ama onwe mgbe ihe mberede ahụ mere.
examples.english: He fell into unconsciousness when that accident happened.

examples.igbo: Ị ma ihe kpatara ama onwe ya?
examples.english: Do you know what caused his unconsciousness?

examples.igbo: Nne ya zụzụrụ aka n'isi ya.
examples.english: His mother stroked his head.

examples.igbo: Zụzụ aka n'azụ nwa ahụ.
examples.english: Stroke the child's back.

examples.igbo: Ọ nwụrụ ọnwụ n'ụlọ ọgwụ n'abalị ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: He died in the hospital last night.

examples.igbo: Anyị anwụghị ọnwụ n'agha ahụ.
examples.english: We did not die in that war.

examples.igbo: O yòkpọrọ ya ihu n'ahịa n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: He slapped her face at the market this morning.

examples.igbo: Ekwela iyòkpọ nwa gị ihu n'ihu mmadụ.
examples.english: Don't slap your child's face in public.

note: Sense understood as slap in the face.

examples.igbo: O na-eduruka m ruo n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: He leads me a little way to the road.

examples.igbo: Biko duruka m ruo n'ọnụ ụzọ.
examples.english: Please lead me a little way to the door.

note: Conjugation/phrasing may vary.

examples.igbo: O biri akwụkwọ ahụ n'ụlọ ọrụ.
examples.english: He printed that book at the company.

examples.igbo: Ị biri akwụkwọ a n'izu gara aga?
examples.english: Did you print this book last week?

examples.igbo: Ebì ogwū na-aga n'ọhịa n'abalị na-achọ nri.
examples.english: The crested porcupine goes in the bush at night looking for food.

examples.igbo: Ị hụla ebì ogwū na mbụ?
examples.english: Have you seen a crested porcupine before?

gloss: press or compress something with hand to bend

examples.igbo: O pịgọrọ ígwè ahụ n'aka ya.
examples.english: He bent the metal with his hand.

examples.igbo: Pịgọ̀ osisi a nwayọọ n'aka gị.
examples.english: Bend this stick gently with your hand.

note: Tone/conjugation may vary.

examples.igbo: Nkụkọlịta ụgbọala mere n'okporo ụzọ ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: A car collision happened on the road yesterday.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ nkụkọlịta ahụ n'ụtụtụ taa?
examples.english: Did you see that collision this morning?

examples.igbo: O bịàjuru akpa ahụ n'ihe n'ahịa.
examples.english: He filled the bag by squeezing things in at the market.

examples.igbo: Bịàju ya n'ime akpa nke ọma.
examples.english: Fill it by squeezing it into the bag well.

note: Conjugation may vary.

examples.igbo: Ọ zụtara òwu maka ịkwa akwa.
examples.english: She bought thread for sewing.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere òwu ọzọ maka ịkwa akwa?
examples.english: Do you have another thread for sewing?

examples.igbo: Anyị riri erimeeri n'ụlọ nne m.
examples.english: We ate a feast at my mother's house.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eri erimeeri taa n'ụlọ anyị?
examples.english: Will you eat a feast at our house today?

examples.igbo: Anyị na-aga ahịa arò kwùlu arò.
examples.english: We go to the market year after year.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-anọ n'ebe a arò kwùlu arò?
examples.english: Will you stay here year after year?

note: The second element is written kwùlu in the entry; many speakers say kwuru. Sentences keep the entry's form.

examples.igbo: Nna m zụtara efi awụsa abụọ n'ahịa.
examples.english: My father bought two zebu cattle at the market.

examples.igbo: Efi awụsa hà na-enye mmiri ara ehi?
examples.english: Do zebu cattle give milk?

note: efi awụsa is understood as the humped zebu; spelling of awụsa varies.

examples.igbo: Ọ kụsiri bọọlụ ahụ ike n'ụkwụ.
examples.english: He hit that ball hard with his foot.

examples.igbo: Ònye kụsiri osisi ahụ ike?
examples.english: Who hit that tree hard?

note: kụsie ike is common in the sense 'try hard'; the gloss here is 'hit hard', and I have written the sentences for that sense only.

examples.igbo: Akwụkwọ ahụ makụdoro n'aka ya.
examples.english: The paper stuck to his hand.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-amakụdo n'úkwù nne ya.
examples.english: He clings to his mother's leg.

note: Sense of 'stick/cling to' is clear, but I am not fully sure of the past form makụdoro versus another inflection.

examples.igbo: Nne m zụtara ukpe ọhụrụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: My mother bought a new lamp at the market.

examples.igbo: Gbanye ukpe ahụ, ọchịchịrị abanyela.
examples.english: Light that lamp, darkness has set in.

note: ukpe for 'lamp' is found in some areas; ụkpe/ọkụ lamp is also heard.

examples.igbo: Àda nne nnà m bịara n'ụlọ anyị ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: My paternal aunt came to our house yesterday.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-aga ileta àda nne nnà gị?
examples.english: Will you go and visit your paternal aunt?

note: This compound term for a father's sister is not the everyday word for most speakers, who say nwanne nna or aunty.

examples.igbo: Enyere m nwa ahụ ọdū jī.
examples.english: I gave the child the tail-end of the yam.

examples.igbo: Ọdū jī a dị ụtọ karịa isi ya?
examples.english: Is this tail-end of the yam sweeter than its head?

examples.igbo: Amā ife ya tinyere anyị ná nnukwu nsogbu.
examples.english: His ignorance put us in great trouble.

examples.igbo: Ị na-achọ ka anyị nọrọ n'amā ife?
examples.english: Do you want us to remain in ignorance?

note: amā ife is close in sense to amaghị ife, 'knowing nothing'.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka ahụ likọrọ nri n'otu efere.
examples.english: The children ate together from one plate.

examples.igbo: Bịa likọọ anyị nri taa.
examples.english: Come and eat with us today.

note: Inflected as likọrọ (past) and likọọ (subjunctive/imperative).

gloss: a dish of pepper-sauced meat, especially goat head

examples.igbo: Nne m siri ǹgwọ̀ǹgwọ ewu n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: My mother cooked goat-head ngwongwo in the morning.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eri ǹgwọ̀ǹgwọ ma ọ bụ anụ ehi?
examples.english: Will you eat ngwongwo or beef?

note: The dish is well known, but the spelling and tone of the word vary between areas.

examples.igbo: Mkpọlọgwụgwụ osisi ahụ gbanyere n'ime ala.
examples.english: The root of that tree sank into the ground.

examples.igbo: Gwuo mkpọlọgwụgwụ ahụ were sie nri.
examples.english: Dig up that root and use it to cook.

note: Gloss 'root' followed; the word is uncommon and I am not fully certain of its exact reference.

examples.igbo: Ìbìli àchì ahụ zụtara azụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: That married woman bought fish at the market.

examples.igbo: Ndi ìbìli àchì na-ezukọ n'abalị taa?
examples.english: Are the adult women meeting tonight?

gloss: officers and leading members of a divinity's club or cult

examples.igbo: Ndị òkùtà na-ezukọ n'ụlọ arụsị ahụ.
examples.english: The officers of the divinity's club meet in that shrine.

examples.igbo: Ndị òkùtà niile bịara n'ọgbakọ?
examples.english: Did all the leading members of the club come to the meeting?

note: Written to the given sense of cult officers; the word also occurs in other senses.

gloss: one Igbo week; period of 4 days

examples.igbo: Ǹkwe ìzù nwere ụbọchị anọ.
examples.english: An Igbo week has four days.

examples.igbo: N'ǹkwe ìzù ọzọ, anyị ga-aga ahịa.
examples.english: In the next Igbo week, we shall go to the market.

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ bịara akpè àzụ n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: That child came last to school.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji bịa akpè àzụ taa?
examples.english: Why did you come last today?

note: The headword is a phrase; I have used the idiomatic form bịa akpè àzụ.

gloss: go astray; stray and get lost

examples.igbo: O sekpụrụ ala were zuo ume.
examples.english: He crouched down and rested.

examples.igbo: Sekpụrụ ala ka i hu nwa ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: Crouch down so that you can see that child well.

note: Inflected from the stem -se-kpù.

examples.igbo: Ọkụkọ mụrụ ùyòm ise taa.
examples.english: The hen hatched five chicks today.

examples.igbo: Nye ùyòm ndị a ntakịrị ọka.
examples.english: Give these chicks a little maize.

examples.igbo: O kwara ibe ya n'azụ.
examples.english: He pushed his companion on the back.

examples.igbo: Kwara ọnụ ụzọ ahụ ka o mepee.
examples.english: Push that door so that it opens.

examples.igbo: Nwata a na-emeka àrụ mgbe niile.
examples.english: This child is always causing trouble.

examples.igbo: Emekala àrụ, bịa nyere m aka.
examples.english: Stop troubling me, come and help me.

note: Inflected from the stem -mekà àrụ.

examples.igbo: O kwara ibe ya n'azụ.
examples.english: He pushed his companion on the back.

examples.igbo: Kwara ọnụ ụzọ ahụ ka o mepee.
examples.english: Push that door so that it opens.

examples.igbo: Ọ kùkpuru nwa ya bata n'ụlọ.
examples.english: She carried her child inside the house.

examples.igbo: Kùkpu nne gị bata n'ụlọ ọgwụ.
examples.english: Carry your mother inside the hospital.

note: Assumed sense: carry someone into a place.

examples.igbo: Ǹkaà nụnwà ka m chọrọ.
examples.english: This particular one is what I want.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ ǹkaà nụnwà?
examples.english: Do you want this particular one?

gloss: drag; draw; pull along (e.g. goat with rope round its neck)

examples.igbo: O jiri eriri dọkpụrụ ewu ahụ.
examples.english: He used a rope to drag that goat.

examples.igbo: Dọkpụ ya n'ụlọ ọgwụ ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Drag it to the hospital quickly.

examples.igbo: Akwa a bụ mmaji naàbò.
examples.english: This cloth is two-fold.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ mmaji naàbò ma ọ bụ otu?
examples.english: Is it two-fold or single?

note: Uncertain whether the phrase is used this way.

examples.igbo: Ǹnànwụ̀rède na-eri ọkụkọ n'abalị.
examples.english: The genet eats chickens at night.

examples.igbo: Ị hụtụla ǹnànwụ̀rède n'ọhịa?
examples.english: Have you seen a genet in the bush?

gloss: tie with a rope or such in order to confine or restrict movement; bind

examples.igbo: Kee ewu ahụ agbụ n'osisi.
examples.english: Tie that goat with a rope to the tree.

examples.igbo: E jiri agbụ kee onye ohi ahụ.
examples.english: They bound that thief with a rope.

examples.igbo: O zụpụtara ụmụ ya n'ụzọ ọma.
examples.english: She trained her children well.

examples.igbo: Zụpụta ọrụ ahụ ruo ọgwụgwụ.
examples.english: See that work through to the end.

note: Second sentence uses the 'see through' sense.

gloss: wipe or clean, especially difficult stain that requires more pressure; erase

examples.igbo: Chìchà ntụ ahụ n'ụkwụ gị.
examples.english: Wipe that dust off your feet.

examples.igbo: Chìchà aha gị na bọọdụ.
examples.english: Erase your name on the board.

gloss: No one has heard of him; he is unknown

examples.igbo: A mārọ afà ya n'obodo anyị.
examples.english: No one has heard of him in our town.

examples.igbo: A mārọ afà ya, ọ̀ bụ onye ọhụrụ?
examples.english: No one has heard of him; is he a newcomer?

examples.igbo: Nwa ọkụkọ a pē m̄pē nke ukwuu.
examples.english: This chick is very tiny.

examples.igbo: Ụlọ ha pē m̄pē, ọ́ bụghị?
examples.english: Their house is tiny, isn't it?

note: The word is ideophonic and its exact predicative use varies by dialect.

gloss: strain or break as a result of lying down

examples.igbo: O dīnàjì àkwà ahụ n'ihi ịdị arọ ya.
examples.english: He broke the bed by lying on it because of his weight.

examples.igbo: Àkwà ochie ahụ dīnàjì, ọ́ bụghị?
examples.english: That old bed broke from lying on it, didn't it?

note: I am not fully certain of the inflection and exact usage of dīnàjì.

gloss: send or request someone to buy something

examples.igbo: M tụ̀rụ nwanne m ahịa n'ọma ahịa.
examples.english: I asked my brother to buy something at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị tụ̀rụ ya ahịa ka ọ zụta mmanụ?
examples.english: Did you ask him to buy oil?

note: The verb phrase is clear, but tone marking on the inflected form may vary.

gloss: a human that can produce eggs and bear offspring; female (human)

examples.igbo: Ìnyòm ahụ mụrụ ụmụ abụọ.
examples.english: That woman gave birth to two children.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ ìnyòm ka a mụrụ n'ụlọ ọgwụ?
examples.english: Was it a female that was born in the hospital?

examples.igbo: Kwụdàa igbe ahụ n'ala nwayọọ.
examples.english: Lower that box to the ground gently.

examples.igbo: O kwụdàrà aka ya mgbe ọ hụrụ anyị.
examples.english: He lowered his hand when he saw us.

examples.igbo: Kpùchaa osisi a tupu ị kpụọ ya.
examples.english: Smooth this wood before you carve it.

examples.igbo: O kpùchàrà mgbidi ahụ ka ọ dị mma.
examples.english: He smoothed the wall so it would be nice.

gloss: have much Anà m ènweka letà I have a lot of mail

examples.igbo: Anà m ènweka ego ugbu a.
examples.english: I have a lot of money now.

examples.igbo: Ị na-enweka ndị enyi n'obodo a?
examples.english: Do you have many friends in this town?

gloss: alligator pepper (literally kola pepper, because usually chewed with kola)

examples.igbo: Anyị na-ata ose ọjī na ọjī.
examples.english: We chew alligator pepper with kola.

examples.igbo: Ose ọjī a na-esi ike?
examples.english: Is this alligator pepper hot?

examples.igbo: Lịfèta mgbidi ahụ nwayọọ.
examples.english: Climb over that wall carefully.

examples.igbo: Ọ lịfètàrà ogige ahụ gaa n'ubi.
examples.english: He climbed over the fence and went to the farm.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-ebikọ ọnụ n'otu ụlọ.
examples.english: We live together in one house.

examples.igbo: Bikọ ọnụ n'udo.
examples.english: Live together in peace.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-achọ ọnà ọcha nà ọnā n'ahịa.
examples.english: He is looking for silver and gold in the market.

examples.igbo: Ọnà ọcha nà ọnā adịghị n'ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: Silver and gold are not in our house.

examples.igbo: Ǹgị nwà ga-aga ahịa taa.
examples.english: You yourself will go to market today.

examples.igbo: Ǹgị nwà kọọrọ ya akụkọ ahụ?
examples.english: Did you yourself tell him that story?

gloss: boiled in tins (e.g. milk tins) instead of being wrapped in leaves

examples.igbo: A na-esi ọka èlèle īko èlèlè n'oge ọkọchị.
examples.english: Corn is boiled in tins during the dry season.

examples.igbo: Nne m na-esi ji èlèle īko èlèlè.
examples.english: My mother boils yam in tins.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-ebi èlèlè n'egwuregwu.
examples.english: The children are having fun in the play.

examples.igbo: Bịa ka anyị bi èlèlè taa.
examples.english: Come so we can have fun today.

examples.igbo: Ǹkè ụnù bụ akpa a?
examples.english: Is this bag yours?

examples.igbo: Ego a bụ ǹkè ụnù, ọ bụghị nke m.
examples.english: This money is yours, not mine.

examples.igbo: Arị̀rịọ ya maka mmejọ ahụ dara m mma.
examples.english: His apology for that mistake pleased me.

examples.igbo: O nyere anyị arị̀rịọ ka anyị gbaghara ya.
examples.english: He gave us a plea to forgive him.

examples.igbo: Mgbàdà gbara ọsọ n'ọhịa.
examples.english: A Maxwell's duiker ran in the bush.

examples.igbo: Dinta gburu mgbàdà n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: The hunter killed a Maxwell's duiker in the morning.

examples.igbo: Ha boro ya ebùbo izu ohi.
examples.english: They accused him of stealing.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ebo m ebùbo ụgha?
examples.english: Are you accusing me falsely?

gloss: hold up; waylay; intercept (literally run to a halt against)

examples.igbo: Ndị ohi gbabìdoro ya n'ụzọ.
examples.english: Thieves waylaid him on the road.

examples.igbo: Gbabìdo ụgbọala ahụ n'okporo ụzọ!
examples.english: Intercept that vehicle on the road!

examples.igbo: Onye nkụzi ụkà na-akụzi ụmụaka okwu Chineke.
examples.english: The catechist teaches the children the word of God.

examples.igbo: Ị ma onye nkụzi ụkà nke ụka anyị?
examples.english: Do you know the catechist of our church?

examples.igbo: N'eziokwu bụ na ọ lụrụ di.
examples.english: The fact is that she is married.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ n'eziokwu na ọ na-arụ ọrụ?
examples.english: Is it a fact that he works?

note: N'eziokwu is often adverbial; these examples use it in a fact/truth construction.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-atabè anya na nzuzo.
examples.english: He winks secretly.

examples.igbo: Tabè anya, ka m mara na ị nọ.
examples.english: Wink, so I know you are there.

note: The imperative tone is my best reconstruction; both sentences use the verb inflected.

gloss: surrounding; nearby; beside; the point where two things abut

examples.igbo: Ụlọ ya dị n'àgbàtà ahịa.
examples.english: His house is near the market.

examples.igbo: Anyị guzoro n'àgbàtà osimiri.
examples.english: We stood beside the river.

examples.igbo: Oké ifufe bọsàsịrị akwụkwọ n'ama.
examples.english: A strong wind scattered papers about the compound.

examples.igbo: Ị bọsàsịrị osikapa ahụ n'ala?
examples.english: Did you scatter that rice on the ground?

note: Past tense form bọsàsịrị is my best reconstruction.

examples.igbo: Ndị ohi sùgburu onye nche n'abalị.
examples.english: Thieves stabbed the guard to death at night.

examples.igbo: Ọ sùgburu ehi ahụ n'ụzọ?
examples.english: Did he stab that cow to death on the road?

note: The sense is violent, but the sentences illustrate the given meaning.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ere ọgwụ̀ n'ụlọ ahịa ya.
examples.english: She sells medicine in her shop.

examples.igbo: Reere m ọgwụ̀ maka ahụ ọkụ.
examples.english: Sell me medicine for fever.

examples.igbo: E kewara ala ahụ n'awa ànì atọ.
examples.english: That land was divided into three plots.

examples.igbo: Awa ànì ahụ dị obere maka ụlọ ahụ.
examples.english: That plot of land is small for the house.

examples.igbo: Mkpasu iwe ya kpatara ọgụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: His provocation caused a fight at the market.

examples.igbo: Zere mkpasu iwe n'ebe ụmụaka nọ.
examples.english: Avoid provocation around children.

examples.igbo: Ọzò dimgba dị n'ọhịa.
examples.english: A gorilla is in the forest.

examples.igbo: Ị hụtụla ọzò dimgba n'ogige anụmanụ?
examples.english: Have you seen a gorilla in the zoo?

gloss: build up a fire; set fire to; burn off with fire Ànyqị chòlù ịkpọ  ewu ọkụ We want to burn off (the hair of) a goat

examples.igbo: Ọ kpọnyere ewu ọkụ tupu o sie ya.
examples.english: He burned off the goat's hair before cooking it.

examples.igbo: Kpọnye ọkụ n'ahịhịa kpọrọ nkụ.
examples.english: Set fire to the dry grass.

examples.igbo: Ọ nwụdoro oke n'ọnyà.
examples.english: He caught a rat in a trap.

examples.igbo: Nwụdo oke ahụ tupu ọ gbapụ.
examples.english: Catch that rat before it escapes.

examples.igbo: Akwà ahụ na-achāghārị̄ n'ihi anyanwụ.
examples.english: That cloth is fading because of the sun.

examples.igbo: Uwe gị na-achāghārị̄?
examples.english: Is your dress fading?

gloss: slander (a person) to death; curse bitterly

examples.igbo: Ọ gwagburu nwanne ya n'okwu.
examples.english: He slandered his sibling with words.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ị ji agwagbu nwanne gị?
examples.english: Why are you slandering your sibling?

examples.igbo: Ọ gbobiri ha abụọ.
examples.english: He parted the two of them.

examples.igbo: Gbòbì ụmụaka ahụ tupu ha lụọ ọgụ.
examples.english: Separate those children before they fight.

gloss: post-partum haemorrhage; menorrhagia (excessive loss at menstrual period)

examples.igbo: Nwanyị ahụ nwere ife ōgbụgba mgbe ọ mụsịrị nwa.
examples.english: That woman had postpartum haemorrhage after she gave birth.

examples.igbo: Ife ōgbụgba na-emenye ndị na-amụ nwa ụjọ.
examples.english: Postpartum haemorrhage scares those giving birth.

examples.igbo: Edi ùmà na-esi isi ike.
examples.english: The civet-cat smells strongly.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ edi ùmà n'abalị?
examples.english: Did you see a civet-cat at night?

examples.igbo: Òròwù dị n'osimiri anyị.
examples.english: Oròwù is in our river.

examples.igbo: Anyị jidere òròwù abụọ n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: We caught two oròwù in the morning.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka kwụrube n'ọnụ ụzọ ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: The children stood around at the school gate.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ị na-akwụrube n'ebe a?
examples.english: Why are you standing around here?

gloss: shortened form of the name Nòdụlụm#or Nònyelụm#

examples.igbo: Ǹnòdụ gara ahịa taa.
examples.english: Nnọdụ went to the market today.

examples.igbo: Ǹnòdụ, bịa rie nri.
examples.english: Nnọdụ, come and eat.

note: Used here as a personal name, which is how the shortened form occurs in speech.

examples.igbo: Ọ jegburu enyi ya n'ihu ndị mmadụ.
examples.english: He denounced his friend before people.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-ejegbu m n'aka ndị uwe ojii?
examples.english: Will you betray me to the police?

examples.igbo: Ọ kụrụ ikpèlè ụkwū ya n'ala.
examples.english: He hit his knee on the ground.

examples.igbo: Ikpèlè ụkwū gị ọ ka na-egbu gị mgbu?
examples.english: Does your knee still hurt?

gloss: flow or gush out water; expel water

examples.igbo: Pọmpụ ahụ na-agba mmirī n'ike.
examples.english: That pump gushes out water strongly.

examples.igbo: Ọ dịghị mma ịgba mmirī n'ọnụ n'ihu ndị ọbịa.
examples.english: It is not good to expel water from your mouth in front of guests.

examples.igbo: Kalama a na-echedo mmirī.
examples.english: This bottle holds water.

examples.igbo: Ite nri a ọ na-echedo mmirī?
examples.english: Does this cooking pot hold water?

examples.igbo: Bedewe, nwa m, ọ dịghị ihe mere ị ga-eji akwa.
examples.english: Stop crying, my child, there is nothing for you to cry about.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ bere akwa, ma o mechara bedewe.
examples.english: That child cried, but in the end he stopped crying.

examples.igbo: Edemede a bụ edemede nkọwasị.
examples.english: This essay is a descriptive essay.

examples.igbo: Olee edemede nkọwasị ị dere?
examples.english: Which descriptive essay did you write?

examples.igbo: Ezinụlọ ahụ jupụtara n'ọṅụ ụbọchị ahụ.
examples.english: That family was filled with joy that day.

examples.igbo: Gịnị na-eweta ọṅụ n'obi gị?
examples.english: What brings joy to your heart?

examples.igbo: Kpọdèbe nwa gị ka o rie nri.
examples.english: Call your child near so that he can eat.

examples.igbo: Ọ kpọdèbere nwanne ya bịa n'akụkụ ya.
examples.english: He called his brother near to his side.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-agwu mmiri n'osimiri.
examples.english: The children are swimming in the river.

examples.igbo: Ị maara igwu mmiri?
examples.english: Do you know how to swim?

examples.igbo: O ji ife ntụchì mechie ụzọ ahụ.
examples.english: He used a bolt to shut that door.

examples.igbo: Ife ntụchì a adịghị arụ ọrụ.
examples.english: This bolt is not working.

gloss: pick iroko leaves (for feeding livestock, e.g. goats, sheep, etc.)

examples.igbo: Anyị na-atụtụ ọjì n'ọhịa maka atụrụ.
examples.english: We are picking iroko leaves in the bush for the sheep.

examples.igbo: Ị na-atụtụ ọjì maka ewu gị?
examples.english: Are you picking iroko leaves for your goat?

examples.igbo: Ha na-abidebe n'ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: They live near our house.

examples.igbo: Ònye na-abidebe ebe a?
examples.english: Who lives near here?

examples.igbo: Òtù ụmù òkoloọbìà zutere n'ama taa.
examples.english: The young men's society met in the village square today.

examples.igbo: Ị bụ onye òtù ụmù òkoloọbìà?
examples.english: Are you a member of the young men's society?

examples.igbo: Ọ gwọdebere nwa ya ọrịa ahụ.
examples.english: She stopped treating her child for that illness.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji gwọdebe ya?
examples.english: Why did you stop treating him?

examples.igbo: Ndị okenye n'obodo a na-eso ụkaọdịnala.
examples.english: The elders in this town follow the traditional religion.

examples.igbo: Ọ hapụrụ ụkaọdịnala banye na chọọchị.
examples.english: He left the traditional religion and joined the church.

examples.igbo: O kwuru ekpele ogologo tupu ọ laa.
examples.english: He said a long prayer before going home.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-ekwu ekpele taa?
examples.english: Will you say a prayer today?

examples.igbo: Mechi ọnụ, nwa ọhụrụ na-ehi ụra.
examples.english: Shut up, the baby is sleeping.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-emechi ọnụ mgbe nne ya na-ekwu okwu.
examples.english: He hushes when his mother is talking.

examples.igbo: Ìgbìlì ya na-egbu mgbu mgbe ọ na-ata nri.
examples.english: His gum hurts when he chews food.

examples.igbo: Dọkịta lere ìgbìlì ya anya.
examples.english: The doctor examined his gum.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ nyụrụ n'ime ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: That child passed wind in the classroom.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ gị nyụrụ? Gaa n'èzí!
examples.english: Was it you who passed wind? Go outside!

note: The stem -nyụ is used here intransitively in its simple past and perfective forms, which is how it is normally heard.

gloss: disrespectfully blink the eyes, usually accompanied by a 'kịm' sound made in the mouth

examples.igbo: Ọ gwuru ùdèlè mgbe m na-agwa ya okwu.
examples.english: She blinked disrespectfully at me while I was talking to her.

examples.igbo: Ị na-agwu m ùdèlè?
examples.english: Are you blinking disrespectfully at me?

note: The verb gwu takes ùdèlè as its object; the past and the progressive are both common in speech.

examples.igbo: O kọrọ akwa ya n'elu eriri.
examples.english: He hung his clothes on the line.

examples.igbo: Ole ebe i kọrọ akpa ahụ?
examples.english: Where did you hang that bag?

note: kò is used here in the sense of hanging something up; many speakers would also say kọnye.

examples.igbo: Nne m fụchara ọka taa.
