examples.english: My mother winnowed the corn thoroughly today.

examples.igbo: Fụchaa ọka ahụ tupu anyanwụ alaa.
examples.english: Winnow that corn thoroughly before the sun sets.

examples.igbo: Nne nne m nwere òlùkpù mgbe ọ dị ndụ.
examples.english: My grandmother had blackened teeth when she was alive.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ òlùkpù ya?
examples.english: Did you see her blackened teeth?

note: The noun refers to the old practice of staining the teeth black; the word is not common among younger speakers.

examples.igbo: Ha tikpọrọ ụlọ ochie ahụ.
examples.english: They demolished that old house.

examples.igbo: Ònye tikpọrọ mgbidi a?
examples.english: Who broke down this wall?

examples.igbo: Ewō! Ọ dara!
examples.english: Ewo! It fell!

examples.igbo: Ewō! I bịara ọzọ?
examples.english: Ewo! You came again?

note: The exclamation is written here with the tone mark on the final vowel as given.

examples.igbo: O hichapụrụ mmiri ahụ n'elu tebụl.
examples.english: She wiped the water off the table top.

examples.igbo: Hichapụ aka gị tupu i rie nri.
examples.english: Wipe off your hands before you eat.

examples.igbo: O wopụrụ àfè ya tupu ọ banye n'ime mmiri.
examples.english: He took off his clothes before he entered the water.

examples.igbo: Wopụ àfè gị, ọ na-ekpo ọkụ.
examples.english: Take off your clothes, it is hot.

note: Many speakers say wepụ uwe; the form given here (wopụ àfè) is also current.

gloss: do something completely or to the end; finish doing; finish

examples.igbo: O mechara ọrụ ubi taa.
examples.english: He finished the farm work today.

examples.igbo: Mechaa ihe ahụ tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Finish that thing before you leave.

gloss: burn; set ablaze; set on fire; light fire on something

examples.igbo: Ndị ohi kpọrọ ọkụ n'ụlọ ahịa anyị.
examples.english: The thieves set fire to our shop.

examples.igbo: Ị kpọrọ ọkụ n'ahịhịa n'ubi gị?
examples.english: Did you set fire to the grass on your farm?

examples.igbo: O goluru ụgbọ ala gaa ahịa.
examples.english: He hired a car to go to the market.

examples.igbo: Ị goluru ọkụkọ ole n'ahịa?
examples.english: How many chickens did you buy at the market?

note: The verb -golu is not common in all dialects; forms here follow regular inflection.

examples.igbo: O firi m ụgwọ ahụ n'ụlọ ahịa.
examples.english: He demanded that debt from me at the shop.

examples.igbo: Fie ya ụgwọ gị tupu ọ pụọ.
examples.english: Demand your debt from him before he leaves.

examples.igbo: O gburu egbugbu n'aka nwa ya.
examples.english: He tattooed marks on his child's hand.

examples.igbo: Ị gburu egbugbu n'ihu gị?
examples.english: Did you tattoo marks on your face?

note: The phrase is idiomatic but less common in everyday modern speech.

gloss: trick someone into missing something elsewhere

examples.igbo: O ghọdoro m ka m ghara ịga ahịa.
examples.english: He tricked me so I missed going to the market.

examples.igbo: Ha ghọdoro gị ka ị ghara ịzụta azụ?
examples.english: Did they trick you so you missed buying fish?

note: The verb -ghodo is rare; the examples follow its stated sense.

gloss: heal; save; defend; claim; side with; contest

examples.igbo: O zọrọ nwa ya n'ọnwụ ozugbo.
examples.english: He saved his child from death immediately.

examples.igbo: Ị zọrọ nwa gị n'ọnwụ?
examples.english: Did you save your child from death?

note: The entry lists several senses; these examples illustrate the 'save' sense.

examples.igbo: O yiri mgbà akā n'aka ekpe ya.
examples.english: She wore a ring on her left hand.

examples.igbo: Ị zụrụ mgbà akā ọhụrụ taa?
examples.english: Did you buy a new ring today?

examples.igbo: Mgbọ mmiri ahụ na-ehi mmiri n'ụlọ.
examples.english: The pipe is leaking water in the house.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ehi mmiri n'elu ụlọ gị?
examples.english: Is it leaking water on your roof?

note: The phrase is understood, though 'na-agbapụta mmiri' is also common for leaking.

gloss: a long stick used as a support while walking or as a sign of authority; staff

examples.igbo: O jiri ǹdèlè ogologo na-aga n'ụzọ.
examples.english: He walks on the road with a long staff.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ǹdèlè eze n'ụlọ eze?
examples.english: Did you see the king's staff in the king's palace?

examples.igbo: Nwaanyị ahụ nyòrò anya na windo.
examples.english: That woman peeped through the window.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji nyò anya n'ụlọ anyị?
examples.english: Why did you peep into our house?

examples.igbo: Ofe ahụ gbara ụka, ọ dịghịzi ụtọ.
examples.english: That soup has fermented; it is no longer tasty.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ofe ji agba ụka?
examples.english: Why is the soup fermenting?

gloss: attack with violence; force; persecute; assault

examples.igbo: O manyere nwa ya ịga ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: He forced his child to go to school.

examples.igbo: Ị manyere ya ka ọ kwuo eziokwu?
examples.english: Did you force him to tell the truth?

examples.igbo: Òbàlà na-agba ya n'imi.
examples.english: Blood is running from his nose.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere òbàlà ji agba n'aka gị?
examples.english: Why is blood flowing from your hand?

gloss: or else; otherwise; if not; failing this

examples.igbo: Jide ya aka, o mèzì ọ ga-ada.
examples.english: Hold it, or else it will fall.

examples.igbo: Ọ ga-akwụ ụgwọ, o mèzì anyị ga-akpọ ndị uwe ojii.
examples.english: He will pay, otherwise we will call the police.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka ahụ chọrọ ndàbere n'aka nne ha.
examples.english: The children sought support from their mother.

examples.igbo: Ò nwere ndàbere n'aka gị?
examples.english: Does he have support from you?

examples.igbo: Ndinyom na-ere akwụkwọ n'ahịa.
examples.english: Women are selling vegetables at the market.

examples.igbo: Ndinyom ole na ole bịara nzukọ taa?
examples.english: How many women came to the meeting today?

examples.igbo: M zụrụ azụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: I bought fish at the market.

examples.igbo: Gịnị ka ị zụrụ n'ahịa taa?
examples.english: What did you buy at the market today?

examples.igbo: Anyị hụrụ ajị iyī n'ikpere mmiri.
examples.english: We saw a crocodile at the riverbank.

examples.igbo: Ị hụla ajị iyī n'osimiri a?
examples.english: Have you seen a crocodile in this river?

gloss: period of daybreak as light grows stronger

examples.igbo: N'ōfufo, anyị na-aga n'ubi tupu ọkụkọ akwaa.
examples.english: At dawn, we go to the farm before the cock crows.

examples.igbo: Ōfufo bịara, anyị were ụzọ gaa ahịa.
examples.english: Dawn came, and we set off to the market.

gloss: begin to spread news in all directions

examples.igbo: O kwusasịbara akụkọ ahụ n'obodo niile.
examples.english: He began to spread that news throughout the town.

examples.igbo: Kwusasịba akụkọ a ngwa ngwa, ka mmadụ niile nụ.
examples.english: Spread this news quickly, so everyone hears.

examples.igbo: Osisi ahụ gbanyere mkpọlọgwụ n'ala a.
examples.english: That tree took root in this land.

examples.igbo: Ị kụrụ osisi ahụ, o gbanyere mkpọlọgwụ?
examples.english: You planted that tree; did it take root?

gloss: gather and give or put into

examples.igbo: O kpakọnyere ha ego niile n'aka.
examples.english: He gathered and gave them all the money.

examples.igbo: Kpakọnye mkpụrụ osisi ndị a n'ime nkata.
examples.english: Gather and put these fruits into the basket.

examples.igbo: Anyị rịgoro n'ọgbà ahụ gafee n'ubi.
examples.english: We climbed over that stile into the farm.

examples.igbo: Ọgbà a dị elu, ụmụaka agaghị arịgoro ya.
examples.english: This stile is high; children cannot climb it.

examples.igbo: Kpachapụ anya ka ị ghara ịda.
examples.english: Be careful so you don't fall.

examples.igbo: Ị kpachapụrụ anya tupu ị gafee okporo ụzọ?
examples.english: Did you take care before crossing the road?

gloss: bogeyman (a creature that will carry bad children away) (= ǹtaǹta)

examples.igbo: Gbapụ, mbùmbu na-abịa n'abalị a!
examples.english: Run away, the bogeyman is coming tonight!

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka ahụ na-atụ egwu mbùmbu n'abalị.
examples.english: Those children are afraid of the bogeyman at night.

gloss: speech in which statements gradually descend in order of importance; anticlimax

examples.igbo: Okwu onye isi obodo ahụ bụ mgbudòokwū.
examples.english: That town chief's speech was an anticlimax.

examples.igbo: Ọ dịghị mma ikwu okwu mgbudòokwū n'ọgbakọ.
examples.english: It is not good to give an anticlimactic speech at a meeting.

examples.igbo: O gwere agwa ntụ ọka na mmiri.
examples.english: She mixed the flour with water.

examples.igbo: Gwaa agwa ntụ ọka na mmiri.
examples.english: Mix the flour with water.

note: The sense of -gwa agwa as 'mix' is not common in every dialect; examples follow the given sense.

gloss: fall or collapse as a result of burning

examples.igbo: Ụlọ ahụ rēdà kpamkpam n'ọkụ ahụ.
examples.english: That house collapsed completely in that fire.

examples.igbo: Ụlọ ọ rēdà n'ọkụ ahụ n'abalị?
examples.english: Did the house collapse in that fire at night?

gloss: say something untrue; tell a lie

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ tụrụ àsị banyere ego.
examples.english: That child lied about money.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji atụ àsị?
examples.english: Why do you lie?

examples.igbo: Ọ làpụtara ile n'ebe m nọ.
examples.english: She stuck out her tongue at me.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka nwa gị làpụta ile.
examples.english: Don't let your child stick out tongue.

examples.igbo: Òkwè oyìbo na-eto ngwa ngwa n'ogige anyị.
examples.english: Moringa grows quickly in our garden.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akụ òkwè oyìbo n'ogige gị?
examples.english: Do you plant moringa in your garden?

examples.igbo: Dibịa ahụ gwọrọ ọgwụ maka ọrịa ahụ.
examples.english: That native doctor prepared medicine for that illness.

examples.igbo: Gwọọ ọgwụ ngwa ngwa maka nwa gị.
examples.english: Prepare medicine quickly for your child.

examples.igbo: Ndị ahịa rara nrā n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: The traders paid levy at the market today.

examples.igbo: Raa nrā tupu ị banye n'ahịa.
examples.english: Pay the levy before you enter the market.

examples.igbo: Ndị mmadụ ǹdègà bịara emume ahụ.
examples.english: Millions of people came to that ceremony.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere ǹdègà naira n'ụlọ akụ?
examples.english: Do you have millions of naira in the bank?

gloss: donkey; mule; ass; beast of burden

examples.igbo: Ànyìnyà ibū na-ebu osisi n'ugbo taa.
examples.english: The donkey carries wood on the farm today.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ànyìnyà ibū n'ụzọ ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see a donkey on that road?

examples.igbo: Mkpècha ya mebiri aha ya n'obodo.
examples.english: His slandering ruined his name in the town.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ekwu mkpècha banyere ya n'ụlọ?
examples.english: Are you saying slander about him in the house?

examples.igbo: Tọọ eriri akpa a, ka m hụ ihe dị n'ime.
examples.english: Untie this bag's rope so I can see what is inside.

examples.igbo: O tọrọ eriri ji osisi ahụ, osisi ahụ wee daa.
examples.english: He untied the rope that held that wood, and the wood fell.

examples.igbo: Ha zisara akụkọ ọhụrụ ahụ n'obodo niile.
examples.english: They spread that new report throughout the whole town.

examples.igbo: Zisaa ozi a n'ebe niile, ka mmadụ niile nụ.
examples.english: Broadcast this message everywhere so that everyone hears.

gloss: cooking tripod, typically made of steel

examples.igbo: Nne m tinyere ite ofe ahụ n'elu ekwiigwè.
examples.english: My mother placed that soup pot on the tripod.

examples.igbo: Zụta ekwiigwè siri ike n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: Buy a strong tripod at the market today.

examples.igbo: Anụrụ m òjiji alaka osisi n'abalị.
examples.english: I heard the snapping of a tree branch at night.

examples.igbo: Ị nụrụ òjiji alaka ahụ dị n'azụ ụlọ?
examples.english: Did you hear the snapping of that branch behind the house?

gloss: be useful; profit; benefit (compare -bà n’ife, -bà èlèlè)

examples.igbo: Ọrụ ugbo bara ulù nye ezinụlọ anyị.
examples.english: Farming was beneficial to our family.

examples.igbo: Okwu a abaghị ulù nye onye ọ bụla.
examples.english: This matter is of no benefit to anyone.

gloss: sacred cow (efi Ìgbò type) owned by village; cannot be killed; if it dies, it is given burial like a human

examples.igbo: Efi alūsị na-ata ahịhịa n'ama obodo.
examples.english: The sacred cow grazes in the village square.

examples.igbo: Emela efi alūsị ahụ ihe ọ bụla.
examples.english: Do not do anything to that sacred cow.

examples.igbo: Òmenàànì obodo anyị na-akwanyere ndị okenye ùgwù.
examples.english: Our town's custom respects elders.

examples.igbo: Ị maara òmenàànì ndị Igbo?
examples.english: Do you know the custom of the Igbo people?

examples.igbo: Mụnye ọkụ, ka anyị kpọọ nri.
examples.english: Light the fire so that we cook food.

examples.igbo: Ọkụ gbara ụlọ ahụ n'abalị.
examples.english: Fire burnt that house at night.

examples.igbo: Anyị fụtara ugwu ahụ n'ebe dị anya.
examples.english: We saw that hill from afar.

examples.igbo: Ị na-afụta ụgbọ ala na-abịa?
examples.english: Can you see the coming car from afar?

examples.igbo: O kwụbara ubube n'ahụ ụlọ.
examples.english: He placed the ladder against the house.

examples.igbo: Kwụbaa osisi ahụ n'akụkụ mgbidi.
examples.english: Place that stick against the wall.

examples.igbo: Ògàniiru na-apụta n'ọrụ ugbo anyị.
examples.english: Progress is showing in our farming.

examples.igbo: Ògàniiru adịghị n'obodo a ugbu a.
examples.english: There is no progress in this town now.

note: The given spelling of the progress term varies in modern usage; examples use the supplied form.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-agba aka ọlụ kemgbe ọ hapụrụ ọrụ.
examples.english: He has been unemployed since he left work.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji agba aka ọlụ?
examples.english: Why are you unemployed?

examples.igbo: Mgbelē akwụkwọ na-aga nke ọma n'ahịa anyị.
examples.english: Book trading is going well in our market.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eme mgbelē n'oge a?
examples.english: Are you doing trading at this time?

note: The term is uncommon; the examples are phrased carefully but may sound slightly formal.

examples.igbo: Biko kwudebe, anyị na-ege gị ntị.
examples.english: Please stop speaking, we are listening to you.

examples.igbo: Ọ kwudebeghị okwu ruo mgbe nna bịara.
examples.english: He did not stop speaking until father came.

examples.igbo: Mmiri ara ehi a na-atọ ụtọ.
examples.english: This cow milk is sweet.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara mmiri ara ehi n'ahịa?
examples.english: Did you buy cow milk at the market?

examples.igbo: Onwunwe anyị dị n'ụlọ ahụ ugbu a.
examples.english: Our property is in that house now.

examples.igbo: O ketara onwunwe nna ya n'afọ gara aga.
examples.english: He inherited his father's property last year.

examples.igbo: Ikpo afịfịa dị n'azụ ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: The rubbish heap is behind our house.

examples.igbo: O tụbara ya n'ikpo afịfịa n'ehihie a.
examples.english: He threw it on the rubbish heap this afternoon.

examples.igbo: Ori ifelē na-eweta ihere n'ezinụlọ anyị.
examples.english: Shameful theft brings shame to our family.

examples.igbo: O zuru ego n'ahịa, ọ bụ ori ifelē.
examples.english: He stole money at the market; it is shameful theft.

examples.igbo: Fili osisi a ka ifufe ghara ịkwatu ya.
examples.english: Support this tree so the wind does not uproot it.

examples.igbo: O na-efili nne ya mgbe ọ na-aga ahịa.
examples.english: He supports his mother when she goes to the market.

examples.igbo: Àgbàtà obì anyị dị jụụ nke ukwuu.
examples.english: Our neighbourhood is very quiet.

examples.igbo: Àgbàtà obì m bịara ileta anyị.
examples.english: My neighbour came to visit us.

examples.igbo: Oké ifufe bọsara anyị uzuzu.
examples.english: The strong wind spattered us with dust.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka ụmụaka bọsaa gị ájá n'anya.
examples.english: Don't let children spatter sand in your eyes.

note: The verb is not common; the inflected forms used are plausible.

examples.igbo: Ọ kwara isi ụkwū ya na nkume.
examples.english: He hit his big toe on a stone.

examples.igbo: Isi ụkwū gị na-egbu gị?
examples.english: Does your big toe hurt?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-eme nwanne ya ife mkpalị.
examples.english: He mocks his sibling.

examples.igbo: Emeela nne gị ife mkpalị n'ihu ọha.
examples.english: Don't mock your mother in public.

examples.igbo: Ndị ọbịa banyere n'ụzò ezi amā.
examples.english: The visitors entered through the main entrance.

examples.igbo: Kpọchie ụzò ezi amā tupu chi ejie.
examples.english: Close the main entrance before nightfall.

examples.igbo: Ọnā èdò dị oke ọnụ n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: Gold is very expensive in the market today.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ọnā èdò n'ime igbe ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see gold in that box?

examples.igbo: Ndàjina dị n'elu mgbidi ụlọ ya.
examples.english: There is a groove on the wall of his house.

examples.igbo: Lelee ndàjina dị n'ala mgbidi ahụ.
examples.english: Look at the groove at the base of that wall.

examples.igbo: Ùyòm ōkụkò na-eso nne ha.
examples.english: The chicks follow their mother.

examples.igbo: Nye ùyòm ōkụkò nri taa.
examples.english: Give the chicks food today.

gloss: return; do in return; take revenge

examples.igbo: Ọ mekwulu m ihe ọjọọ.
examples.english: He did evil to me in return.

examples.igbo: M ga-emekwulu gị obiọma gị.
examples.english: I will repay your kindness.

note: The stem is uncommon; the forms used are plausible.

gloss: (fig.) cause trouble; invite quarrel, dispute (usually deliberately); assault

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akọ okwu n'ụlọ ahịa.
examples.english: He causes trouble in the market.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji akọ okwu ebe a?
examples.english: Why are you causing trouble here?

examples.igbo: Ọ yi ụgbà n'ime mmiri.
examples.english: He dived into the water.

examples.igbo: Yie ụgbà nke ọma ka mmiri ghara imerụ gị ahụ.
examples.english: Dive well so the water doesn't hurt you.

examples.igbo: Nne m sijuru nri taa.
examples.english: My mother cooked plenty of food today.

examples.igbo: Sijuo nri ahụ tupu anyị erie.
examples.english: Cook that food enough before we eat.

examples.igbo: Ha kpọrọ ànì n'ubi ọhụrụ.
examples.english: They cleared the new farm by burning.

examples.igbo: Ị kpọrọ ànì n'ubi gị tupu ị kụọ ihe?
examples.english: Did you clear your farm by burning before planting?

examples.igbo: Onye ọzụzụ kpụkọnatara ụmụ ewu n'ụlọ.
examples.english: The shepherd led the goats home together.

examples.igbo: Kpụkọnata ụmụaka n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: Lead the children home together.

examples.igbo: O kwuru okwu āsị n'ụlọ ikpe.
examples.english: He spoke falsehood in court.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji kwuo okwu āsị?
examples.english: Why did you speak falsehood?

examples.igbo: Anyị gụtara ji ọtụtụ n'afọ a.
examples.english: We harvested many yams this year.

examples.igbo: Gụte ji n'ubi gị tupu mmiri abịa.
examples.english: Harvest yams in your farm before the rain comes.

examples.igbo: Bènyelụ okwu ahụ mgbe ha na-ekwu okwu.
examples.english: Join that discussion when they are talking.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-abènyelụ okwu ahụ?
examples.english: Will you join that discussion?

examples.igbo: Ahịhịa n'ubi anyị afịla.
examples.english: The grass in our farm has withered.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere osisi a na-afị?
examples.english: Why is this tree withering?

examples.igbo: O kwuchiri ọnụ ite ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: She covered the mouth of that pot well.

examples.igbo: Kwuchie ọnụ olulu ahụ ka mmiri ghara ịba.
examples.english: Plug the hole's opening so water won't enter.

examples.igbo: O nwere nnenì maka uwe ochie m.
examples.english: He has contempt for my old clothes.

examples.igbo: Nnenì adịghị mma n'etiti ụmụnne.
examples.english: Contempt is not good among siblings.

gloss: short for "if a road or path is good, it gets taken twice (ụzọ dị mma, a gaa ya nga abụọ)"

examples.igbo: A kpọrọ nwa ha Ụzọ̀dịmmā.
examples.english: They named their child Ụzọ̀dịmmā.

examples.igbo: Ụzọ̀dịmmā pụtara na ụzọ dị mma, a na-aga ya ugboro abụọ.
examples.english: Ụzọ̀dịmmā means that if a road is good, it is taken twice.

note: This entry is a shortened proverb and is also used as a personal name; the examples show both its name use and its meaning.

examples.igbo: O jiri ọgbụ kee ewu ahụ.
examples.english: He tied that goat with a rope.

examples.igbo: Ọgbụ a adịghị ike, ewu ga-agbapụ.
examples.english: This rope is not strong; the goat will escape.

examples.igbo: Taata abụ m àrụ efè, agaghị m arụ ọrụ.
examples.english: Today I am at leisure; I will not work.

examples.igbo: Ị nọ àrụ efè, bịa nyere m aka.
examples.english: You are free; come and help me.

examples.igbo: Biko kpụpụ akwà ahụ n'elu àkwà.
examples.english: Please take off that coverlet from the bed.

examples.igbo: O kpụpụrụ akwà tupu ọ dinara.
examples.english: She took off the coverlet before she lay down.

gloss: wages; salary; payment for work done

examples.igbo: Ndị ọrụ na-anata ụgwọ ọlū ha n'ụbọchị ụgwọ.
examples.english: Workers receive their wages on payday.

examples.igbo: Ego ole bụ ụgwọ ọlū gị kwa ọnwa?
examples.english: How much is your salary per month?

gloss: to lay, to place, to establish; to spread

examples.igbo: O tọrọ nkata ya n'ala.
examples.english: She placed her basket on the ground.

examples.igbo: Tọọ efere ndị ahụ n'elu tebụl.
examples.english: Put those plates on the table.

examples.igbo: Osisi ọka ahụ kpọnwụrụ n'ihi ọkọchị.
examples.english: That maize plant withered because of drought.

examples.igbo: Ì hụrụ na akwụkwọ ndị ahụ kpọnwụrụ?
examples.english: Did you see that those leaves withered?

examples.igbo: Ọ gara ànị mmadù ịchọ ọrụ.
examples.english: He went to a foreign land to look for work.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-aga ànị mmadù ọzọ?
examples.english: Will you go to a foreign land again?

examples.igbo: O kọrọ ònùmà mgbe nwa ya mebiri efere.
examples.english: She was angry when her child broke the plate.

examples.igbo: I kọrọ ònùmà, gịnị mere?
examples.english: You are angry; what happened?

examples.igbo: O kpọbara afịa ya n'ahịa.
examples.english: She displayed her wares in the market.

examples.igbo: Kpọba afịa gị n'ihu ụlọ.
examples.english: Display your wares in front of the house.

examples.igbo: Ọtụtụ mba dị n'Òbòdò Isi Ōji.
examples.english: Many countries are in Africa.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ ịga Òbòdò Isi Ōji?
examples.english: Do you want to go to Africa?

gloss: native woven cloth, very thick, rough and coarse

examples.igbo: Ọ zụtara akwà ajì n'ahịa.
examples.english: He bought coarse native cloth at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eji akwà ajì mee uwe?
examples.english: Will you use coarse native cloth to make clothes?

examples.igbo: Ùdu mmīli abịala, ndị ọrụ ugbo na-akụ ji.
examples.english: The rainy season has come, farmers are planting yams.

examples.igbo: Ị kụrụ ji tupu ùdu mmīli?
examples.english: Did you plant yams before the rainy season?

examples.igbo: Ọ kwabanyere akwụkwọ ya n'akpa.
examples.english: He pushed his book into the bag.

examples.igbo: Kwabanyenụ ha n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: Hustle them into the house.

examples.igbo: Mmanya ọkụ gbara ya ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Strong drink made him drunk quickly.

examples.igbo: Mmanya ọkụ gbara ya, ma mmanya dị nro agbaghị ya.
examples.english: Strong drink made him drunk, but mild drink did not.

note: The second sentence uses a contrast to show the same verb phrase in the negative.

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ dàbànyere n'ime mmiri.
examples.english: The child fell into water.

examples.igbo: Uwe a ọ dàbànyere gị?
examples.english: Does this dress fit you?

note: The second sentence illustrates the ‘match/correspond’ sense; it may be more idiomatic with dabara in some dialects.

examples.igbo: O tinyere ego n'akpa ya.
examples.english: He put money in his bag.

examples.igbo: Tinye nnu n'ofe.
examples.english: Put salt in the soup.

note: The stem -ti- is treated as the root seen in tinye ‘put’; a bare -ti- is not used as a free verb in standard modern Igbo.

examples.igbo: Ji a gbakara ntị n'ọnụ m.
examples.english: This yam tasted sour in my mouth.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-agbaka ntị mgbe ọ bụla i tara ya?
examples.english: Does it taste sour whenever you chew it?

note: The phrase is treated as gbaka ntị; the continuous form is given as na-agbaka ntị.

gloss: guard something so it remains stable in order; protect

examples.igbo: Chedo ego gị nke ọma.
examples.english: Guard your money well.

examples.igbo: Onye na-echedo ubi anyị?
examples.english: Who guards our farm?

examples.igbo: Engine ụgbọala m na-akụ ụda.
examples.english: My car engine is making noise.

examples.igbo: Gbanwuo engine ka anyị gaa.
examples.english: Start the engine so we go.

examples.igbo: Ndị bi n'ànì ezè ahụ na-akụ ji.
examples.english: People living in that kingdom plant yams.

examples.igbo: Ị ma ànì ezè dị n'akụkụ osimiri?
examples.english: Do you know the kingdom by the river?

note: Alaeze is the more common modern word for ‘kingdom’; ànì ezè is understood but less usual.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-amasị ya imenwò abụ ahụ.
examples.english: He likes to repeat that song.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-emenwò ihe ahụ ọzọ?
examples.english: Will you repeat that thing again?

examples.igbo: Agwọ ahụ kokwàsịrị n'alaka osisi.
examples.english: The snake hung on the tree branch.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka agwọ kokwàsị n'ụkwụ gị.
examples.english: Don't let a snake hang on your leg.

gloss: juice or stain of ụdalà fruit

examples.igbo: Àtụtụ ụdālà tere uwe ọcha ya.
examples.english: The udala juice stained his white cloth.

examples.igbo: Àtụtụ ụdālà dị n'aka gị?
examples.english: Is the udala stain on your hand?

examples.igbo: Ọgwụ a na-ebu ajụ̀.
examples.english: This medicine causes dizziness.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ebu ajụ̀ n'isi?
examples.english: Does it cause dizziness in the head?

examples.igbo: Òwụwa osisi ahụ were anyị ụtụtụ dum.
examples.english: Cutting that tree took us all morning.

examples.igbo: Bido òwụwa nkụ tupu anyanwụ awaa.
examples.english: Start cutting firewood before the sun rises.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-achọsà ya n'ahịa niile.
examples.english: We search everywhere for him in all the markets.

examples.igbo: Chọsaa mkpịsị ugodi m n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: Search everywhere for my key in the house.

examples.igbo: Dọpụ̀ta m ngwa ngwa n'ime mmiri.
examples.english: Pull me out of the water quickly.

examples.igbo: Ọ dọpụ̀tara nwa ya n'olulu miri.
examples.english: She pulled her child out of the well.

gloss: rush, run away (permanently; one is less likely to come back than with -kpọwa, which simply means run away)

examples.igbo: Ọ kpọwalụrụ n'obodo a mgbe ọ dị obere.
examples.english: He ran away permanently from this town when he was young.

examples.igbo: Ị kpọwalụrụ ebe a?
examples.english: Did you run away permanently from here?

examples.igbo: Ọ dara ọrịa, kà o si nà dị, ọ bịara ọrụ.
examples.english: He was sick, nevertheless, he came to work.

examples.igbo: Ọ rụrụ ọrụ, kà o si nà dị, e nyeghị ya ego?
examples.english: He worked, yet they did not pay him?

gloss: captivity; state of being a prisoner of war

examples.igbo: Ọdịdọ n'agha tara ya ahụhụ ogologo oge.
examples.english: Captivity in war tormented him for a long time.

examples.igbo: A tọhapụrụ ha n'ọdịdọ n'agha.
examples.english: They were released from captivity in war.

examples.igbo: Ọnwụ nna ya wutere ya nke ukwuu.
examples.english: His father's death pained him greatly.

examples.igbo: Ị̀ nụla akụkọ ọnwụ nne ya?
examples.english: Have you heard the news of her mother's death?

gloss: seek refuge; dodge a life threat

examples.igbo: O zere ndụ ya n'aka ndị ohi.
examples.english: He escaped with his life from the robbers.

examples.igbo: Zee ndụ gị, pụọ ngwa ngwa!
examples.english: Save your life and leave quickly!

note: The phrase is somewhat literary; I have used zere and zee as inflected forms of ze.

gloss: take out, extract teeth; lose tooth (teeth)

examples.igbo: Dọkịta kworo m eze abụọ taa.
examples.english: The doctor extracted two of my teeth today.

examples.igbo: Ị̀ chọrọ ka dọkịta kwo eze ahụ?
examples.english: Do you want the doctor to extract that tooth?

note: Both examples show the extracting sense; the 'lose a tooth' sense is harder to phrase unambiguously.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-anọ n'udo n'obodo a.
examples.english: We live in peace in this town.

examples.igbo: Nọrọ n'udo, echegbula banyere ya.
examples.english: Stay in peace and do not worry about him.

gloss: light fire; kindle by blowing; raise light

examples.igbo: O fụnwụrụ ọkụ n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: He kindled the fire in the morning.

examples.igbo: Ị fụnwụrụ ọkụ taa?
examples.english: Did you light the fire today?

note: I have written fụnwụ with standard ụ, though the headword shows u.

gloss: to collect tax or dues; to collect a form of payment

examples.igbo: Ndị ọrụ gọọmentị na-ana ụtụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: Government workers collect taxes at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ana ụtụ n'ahịa a?
examples.english: Do you collect tax in this market?

note: Examples use the usual verb phrase na-ana ụtụ for collecting tax.

examples.igbo: Nlòzọ ya mere ka o chefuo akpa ya.
examples.english: His forgetfulness made him forget his bag.

examples.igbo: Ị̀ na-ata nlòzọ ya ụta?
examples.english: Are you blaming him for his forgetfulness?

gloss: gather together and carry away; collect Ekpōkọlụgo m  òlòma diCnénu tebùlù I have collected (and taken away) the oranges on the table

examples.igbo: Ndị ọrụ kpokọlụrụ ahịhịa n'ubi.
examples.english: The workers gathered and carried away the weeds from the farm.

examples.igbo: Ị kpokọlụrụ akwụkwọ ndị ahụ?
examples.english: Did you gather and carry away those books?

note: The verb is less common; I have used kpokọlụrụ as its inflected form.

examples.igbo: O dùrù m ọdụ ka m ghara ịga.
examples.english: He advised me not to go.

examples.igbo: Dụrụ ya ọdụ banyere ego ahụ.
examples.english: Advise him about that money.

examples.igbo: O pụnalụrụ m akpa m n'aka.
examples.english: He snatched my bag from my hand.

examples.igbo: Pụnalụ ya akwụkwọ ahụ ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Snatch that book from him quickly.

note: I have used pụnalụrụ and pụnalụ as inflected forms of the verb stem.

gloss: a house with only a ground floor and the roof; bungalow

examples.igbo: Ụlāàlà ka ha wuru n'akụkụ ụlọ ahịa ahụ.
examples.english: They built a bungalow beside that shop.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ụlāàlà ọhụrụ ha wuru n'okporo ụzọ?
examples.english: Did you see the new bungalow they built on the road?

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-atụ ụ̀zụ̀ n'èzí ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: The children are making noise outside the school.

examples.igbo: Ndị mmadụ tụrụ ụ̀zụ̀ mgbe ọ banyere n'ọgbọ.
examples.english: The crowd roared when he entered the arena.

note: Spelling and tone of ụ̀zụ̀ kept as given; the phrase is idiomatic but I would normally say na-eme mkpọtụ.

examples.igbo: Ha na-asị àsị̀rị̀ banyere nwanne m n'ahịa.
examples.english: They gossip about my brother in the market.

examples.igbo: Kwụsị ịsị àsị̀rị̀ banyere ndị agbata obi gị.
examples.english: Stop gossiping about your neighbours.

examples.igbo: Nna nna ya kùbìrì ume n'abalị ahụ.
examples.english: His grandfather passed away that night.

examples.igbo: Ị nụla na ọ kùbìrì ume ụnyaahụ?
examples.english: Have you heard that he passed away yesterday?

note: The phrase is used for dying; the past form kùbìrì ume is my best reconstruction.

gloss: paralysis of one half of the body; hemiplegia and paraplegia

examples.igbo: Nna ya nwere ọtụlụ òkàlà mgbe ọ rịasịrị ọrịa ahụ.
examples.english: His father had paralysis after he suffered that illness.

examples.igbo: Ọtụlụ òkàlà gbochiri ya ije ije ọzọ.
examples.english: The paralysis stopped him from walking again.

note: Medical term; I am fairly sure of the sense but not fully of the standard spelling.

examples.igbo: M na-echeta nne m mgbe ọ bụla m riri nri ya.
examples.english: I remember my mother whenever I eat her food.

examples.igbo: Ị na-echeta ebe anyị zutere n'ahịa?
examples.english: Do you remember where we met at the market?

gloss: be clear; settle(particles); be serene; be calm

examples.igbo: Mmiri ahụ dọrọ, anyị na-aṅụ ya ugbu a.
examples.english: The water has settled; we are drinking it now.

examples.igbo: Obi dọrọ ya mgbe ọ nụrụ ozi ahụ.
examples.english: He was calm when he heard that news.

note: Past form dọrọ taken from doo; the 'settle/be calm' sense is idiomatic but tone marking of the stem is uncertain.

examples.igbo: Ha jìkọrọ aka n'ụka n'ụtụtụ taa.
examples.english: They joined hands in marriage in church this morning.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-ejikọ aka na ya n'ụka?
examples.english: Will you join hands in marriage with him in church?

examples.igbo: Agwọ ahụ kpụpụrụ n'olulu dị n'ugbo.
examples.english: That snake crept out of the hole in the farm.

examples.igbo: Kpụpụ n'ebe ahụ ozugbo, nwata!
examples.english: Crawl out of there at once, child!

examples.igbo: O jetere aka n'obodo ọzọ dị anya.
examples.english: He went far away to another town that is far.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-ejete aka n'ugbo anyị.
examples.english: We go far away to our farm.

note: Uncertain of the exact idiomatic force of -gatè/jetè aka; examples are plausible but not fully verified.

examples.igbo: Mmaji akwụkwọ a dị mfe nke ọma.
examples.english: The folding of this paper is quite easy.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-eme mmaji atọ n'akwa ahụ.
examples.english: She is making three folds in that cloth.

gloss: fowls kept by agricultural settlements and institutions. It is called European because it was introduced by the Agricultural Department and is also larger than the local type

examples.igbo: Òkụkò oyìbo buru ibu karịa ọkụkọ ọdịnala.
examples.english: The European fowl is bigger than the local fowl.

examples.igbo: Anyị zụrụ òkụkò oyìbo n'ugbo anyị.
examples.english: We bought European fowls at our farm.

gloss: spending more than the allotted time

examples.igbo: Ọ nọfere n'ọrụ taa ruo mgbede.
examples.english: He stayed beyond the allotted time at work today till evening.

examples.igbo: Nọfe ụmụaka n'ụlọ akwụkwọ adịghị mma.
examples.english: Children overstaying at school is not good.

examples.igbo: Ha nụsọrọ agha n'ime obodo ahụ.
examples.english: They warred in that town.

examples.igbo: O nụsọrọ onye agbata obi ya.
examples.english: He fought against his neighbor.

examples.igbo: O jezuru obodo niile n'ụtụtụ taa.
examples.english: He went all over the town this morning.

examples.igbo: Jezuo ụlọ ahụ niile tupu anyị apụọ.
examples.english: Go all over that house before we leave.

examples.igbo: Egulò na-akpa akwụ n'osisi elu ahụ.
examples.english: The weaverbird builds a nest in that tall tree.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ egulò n'osisi ahụ taa?
examples.english: Did you see a weaverbird on that tree today?

examples.igbo: O kènyere ha ego n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: He gave them a share of money at the market today.

examples.igbo: Kènye m nke m n'ime achịcha a.
examples.english: Give me my share of this bread.

examples.igbo: Mfùkọ akwà dị n'uwe m nke ọma.
examples.english: There is a crease in my clothes clearly.

examples.igbo: Gbọnwụ mfùkọ akwà ahụ tupu ị yinye ya.
examples.english: Iron out that crease before you wear it.

examples.igbo: Ọ kpọrọ ha òfu ōfu bata n'ụlọ.
examples.english: He called them one by one into the house.

examples.igbo: Gaanụ òfu ōfu ka ọ ghara ịdị oké mkpọtụ.
examples.english: Go one by one so it won't be too noisy.

examples.igbo: Ụgbọ mmiri ahụ kpùrù èkpù n'osimiri.
examples.english: That boat capsized in the river.

examples.igbo: Ị kpùrù èkpù ite nri ahụ?
examples.english: Did you overturn that pot of food?

examples.igbo: Bible na-ekwu banyere mbìnite n'ọnwụ nke ọma.
examples.english: The Bible talks about resurrection well.

examples.igbo: Ị kwere na mbìnite n'ọnwụ n'ezie?
examples.english: Do you truly believe in resurrection?

examples.igbo: Ọ mafèrè ogwe osisi ahụ.
examples.english: He leaped over that log.

examples.igbo: Mafèe ogwe osisi ahụ ka ị ghara ịda.
examples.english: Leap over that log so you don't fall.

examples.igbo: Ndị ohi na-eme mpùm n'okporo ụzọ ahụ.
examples.english: Robbers commit highway robbery on that road.

examples.igbo: Ị na-atụ egwu mpùm n'okporo ụzọ a?
examples.english: Are you afraid of highway robbery on this road?

gloss: the fruit of Black Velvet Tamarind (Dialium guineense)

gloss: peep; observe; stare; spy; look through (microscope, telescope, etc.)

examples.igbo: Nyòọ anya n'oghere ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: Peep through that hole well.

examples.igbo: Ndị ojii na-azụ ahịa n'ọma ahịa anyị.

examples.igbo: Kpọọ ndị ojii niile bịa nzukọ echi.
examples.english: Invite all black people to come to the meeting tomorrow.

examples.igbo: Wụnye ọnyà igwè n'akụkụ ọhịa.
examples.english: Set the steel trap at the edge of the bush.

examples.english: A wall surrounds our house.

examples.igbo: Kpuchie oghere dị n'aja ọdịdo ahụ.
examples.english: Close the hole in that wall.

note: The compound is uncommon; examples treat it as a wall.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-ekpe ikpe a taa?

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka onyemgbù duhie gị.
examples.english: Don't let a foolish person mislead you.

note: The word is uncommon in everyday speech.

examples.english: That great man died, and the whole town is mourning.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eleta oke ozū ahụ taa?
examples.english: Will you visit that great man today?

note: The exact sense of the compound is not fully clear to me.

gloss: backbite; slander; speak evil of. Much practised by the Egwu Ọjà dancers many years ago. The soloist in the course of her singing spoke to evil-doers who had been committing evil in secret, e.g. a thief or people involved in adultery, thereby bringing their anti-social practices to light

examples.english: She backbites her brother.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akpè ìkpe banyere m?
examples.english: Are you backbiting about me?

examples.igbo: Lee ka kpakpando na-agbuke n'abalị!
examples.english: Look how the stars shine at night!

examples.igbo: Ị ga-ewe ezumike n'ọkara afọ?
examples.english: Will you take a break at mid-year?

examples.igbo: Mama zụtara ọpị ụgbọgụlụ n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: Mother bought pumpkin leaf stalk in the market today.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-esi ọpị ụgbọgụlụ n'ofe?
examples.english: Will you cook pumpkin leaf stalk in soup?

gloss: kill by stepping on; tread to death; match to death

examples.igbo: Ọ zọ̀gbùrù ọkụkọ ahụ n'ụkwụ.
examples.english: He trampled that chicken to death.

examples.igbo: Ị zọ̀gbùrù ọkụkọ m?
examples.english: Did you trample my chicken to death?

examples.english: Will you print this book today?

examples.english: He read the second verse.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-abụ amà okwū ọhụrụ n'ụka.
examples.english: We sing a new verse in church.

examples.igbo: Ọ nọ n'ọnòdù ọjọō mgbe ọ dara.
examples.english: He was in a bad condition when he fell.

examples.igbo: Ọnòdù ọjọō nke okporo ụzọ na-egbu oge.
examples.english: The bad condition of the road causes delay.

examples.english: Restrain him from making noise.

note: The exact inflection and usage of -na-ghà are uncertain; verify before publishing.

examples.english: These goods are clothes and shoes.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ebu ahịa orirē gị n'ahịa?
examples.english: Are you carrying your goods to the market?

note: Not fully sure of the term's common usage.

examples.english: Why are you gnashing your teeth?

examples.english: He is overtaking us in the race.

examples.english: Overtake him quickly!

examples.igbo: Ị na-akụziri ha ihe gịnị?
examples.english: What are you teaching them?

examples.igbo: Ị na-ezu ego n'aka nna gị?

examples.english: He judged him unjustly.

examples.igbo: Ị kpegidere ya ikpe ọjọọ?
examples.english: Did you judge him wrongly?

note: Unsure of exact inflection.

examples.igbo: O fiedosiri ike na bolt.
examples.english: He tightened the bolt.

examples.igbo: Fiedosi ike eriri ahụ!
examples.english: Tighten that rope!

note: Unsure of tone on inflected form.

gloss: a consecrated area of the church where sacred objects are kept or where the clergy stays during service; sanctuary

examples.english: He asked a question in class.

examples.igbo: Jụọ ajụjụ ma ị ghọtara ihe.
examples.english: Ask a question if you understand.

gloss: damage caused by an act or neglect; waste; vain

examples.english: He spoke to him in vain.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ iyì ịzụta ya?
examples.english: Is it a waste to buy it?

note: The word iyì is used for 'waste' or 'vain'; the sentences are idiomatic but may vary by dialect.

examples.igbo: Ị rịrị ewu gị ntị?
examples.english: Did you mark your goat's ear?

note: The verb -rì is often used for marking animals; tone and usage are correct but could be phrased differently.

examples.igbo: Anyị chịpụrụ n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: We set off in the morning.

examples.igbo: Olee mgbe ị ga-achịpụ?
examples.english: When will you set off?

examples.igbo: Ha lụnwụrụ ụlọ ahụ.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-alụnwụ ụlọ gị?

note: Unsure whether rọgo is the usual standard verb; rịgo is more common.

gloss: bear a name; answer to one's name

examples.english: Be careful, that steam burns.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-agụ Àgbà Ochīè na chọọchị.
examples.english: We read the Old Testament in church.

examples.igbo: Ị maara akụkọ ndị dị n'Àgbà Ochīè?
examples.english: Do you know the stories in the Old Testament?

gloss: bush-candle tree (Canarium schweinfurthii Engl.). The fruits are cooked by being put in hot water. See also ùbe òsà.

examples.igbo: Nne m sara ùbe ōkpoko n'ime mmiri ọkụ.
examples.english: My mother cooked bush-candle fruits in hot water.

examples.igbo: Ùbe ōkpoko toro n'akụkụ ubi anyị.
examples.english: A bush-candle tree grew beside our farm.

gloss: urge; force someone to do something against his wish

examples.igbo: Ha nụrụ ya ēnū ịga ahịa.
examples.english: They forced him to go to the market.

examples.igbo: Ị na-anụ ya ēnū ịlụ nwaanyị ahụ?
examples.english: Are you forcing him to marry that woman?

note: The verb phrase is uncommon; examples show it with a direct object and an infinitive.

examples.igbo: Ọ gwara m ya, nya bù nà, ọ ga-abịa.
examples.english: He told me, that is to say, he will come.

examples.igbo: Nya bù nà ị jụrụ ọrụ ahụ?
examples.english: That is to say you refused that job?

gloss: regret I gà-àkwalụ n kaà mmààlù You’ll regret this Ọ kwàlù mmààlù nà o mèlù ya He’s sorry he did it

examples.igbo: Ị ga-akwalụ mmààlù ma ị ghara ige ntị.
examples.english: You will regret it if you don't listen.

examples.igbo: Ọ kwàlù mmààlù maka ihe o mere?
examples.english: Did he regret what he did?

gloss: used in -tụ àkpànì be bellicose, pugnacious

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-atụ àkpànì mgbe niile.
examples.english: That child is always pugnacious.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji atụ àkpànì n'ụlọ akwụkwọ?
examples.english: Why are you being pugnacious at school?

note: The headword is used in the phrase -tụ àkpànì; examples keep that construction.

examples.igbo: Nsògbu dị n'ahịa taa mere ka anyị lọta.
examples.english: The trouble in the market today made us return home.

examples.igbo: Gịnị na-akpata nsògbu a n'ụlọ anyị?
examples.english: What is causing this disturbance in our house?

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ tịrị àtị aka ya n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: That child stretched his hand in the morning.

examples.igbo: Tị àtị ụkwụ gị tupu ị gbaa ọsọ.
examples.english: Stretch your legs before you run.

gloss: steadfastness; sticking very fast; biting and holding on to

examples.igbo: Ntado ya n'ọrụ na-enye anyị obi ụtọ.
examples.english: His steadfastness at work makes us happy.

examples.igbo: Jide ya na ntado ka ọ ghara ịpụ.
examples.english: Hold it firmly so it does not leave.

examples.igbo: O tịpụrụ aka ya n'elu tebụl.
examples.english: He stretched his hand onto the table.

examples.igbo: Tịpụ aka gị ka m tinye ego n'ime ya.
examples.english: Stretch out your hand so I can put money in it.

gloss: ‘man-killer’; a much-coveted honour in the olden days conferred on anyone who possessed a human head

examples.igbo: N'oge ochie, ògbu mmādù bụ aha nsọpụrụ.
examples.english: In olden times, man-killer was an honourary title.

examples.igbo: Ndị dike na-achọ ògbu mmādù n'oge agha.
examples.english: Warriors sought the man-killer title in wartime.

note: Historical term; less common in modern everyday speech.

examples.igbo: Nne makuru nwa ya n'obi.
examples.english: The mother embraced her child to her chest.

examples.igbo: Makụọ nwa gị n'obi mgbe ọ na-ebe akwa.
examples.english: Embrace your child when he is crying.

gloss: cut up and bring together into

examples.igbo: O gbunyere ji n'ime ite.
examples.english: She cut yam into the pot.

examples.igbo: Gbunye anụ ahụ n'ime ite.
examples.english: Cut that meat into the pot.

examples.igbo: Ha na-enwe mbàgha mgbe niile.
examples.english: They always have arguments.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara mbàgha a?
examples.english: What caused this argument?

examples.igbo: O ritere nanị obere akụkụ nke ihe ubi.
examples.english: He harvested only a small fraction of the crop.

examples.igbo: Ego a bụ nanị akụkụ nke ụgwọ ahụ.
examples.english: This money is only a fraction of the debt.

gloss: fix; stick (as an arrow); hold tightly; choke; take by the throat; compress by pressing fingers firmly on

examples.igbo: O gbadoro akụ n'ime osisi.
examples.english: He stuck the arrow into the tree.

examples.igbo: Gbado akụ gị n'ala.
examples.english: Stick your arrow in the ground.

gloss: run hither and thither without anything being done; make fuss; dilly-dally

examples.igbo: O na-agbakili ànì n'ahịa, ọ zụtaghị ihe ọ bụla.
examples.english: She was running about the market and bought nothing.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji agbakili ànì n'ihi ọrụ a?
examples.english: Why are you making a fuss over this work?

examples.igbo: O gbara ehi anyị amù.
examples.english: He castrated our cow.

examples.igbo: Gbaa ezi ahụ amù tupu ọ too.
examples.english: Castrate that pig before it matures.

examples.igbo: O bekapụtara anụ n'ọkpụkpụ.
examples.english: He cut pieces of meat from the bone.

examples.igbo: Bekapụta anụ ahụ n'ọkpụkpụ.
examples.english: Cut that meat off the bone.

gloss: go off, especially electric power or fire

examples.igbo: Ọkụ nyụrụ n'abalị ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: The light went off last night.

examples.igbo: Kedu mgbe ọkụ nyụrụ n'ụlọ gị?
examples.english: When did the light go off in your house?

examples.igbo: Pụchaa n'ebe a, biko!
examples.english: Go away from here, please!

examples.igbo: Ha pụchara n'ụlọ anyị n'abalị.
examples.english: They went away from our house at night.

examples.igbo: Ọ zụtara ìyèli ọlaedo n'ahịa.
examples.english: She bought a gold earring at the market.

examples.igbo: Ebee ka ị zụtara ìyèli ọcha a?
examples.english: Where did you buy this white earring?

examples.igbo: Ede mmụọ na-eto n'ọhịa.
examples.english: Ede mmụọ grows in the bush.

examples.igbo: Ọ dịghị onye na-eri edē mmụọ.
examples.english: Nobody eats ede mmụọ.

gloss: shine, glitter, very brightly; be very white

examples.igbo: Uwe ọcha ya nwu gbàà n'anyanwụ.
examples.english: His white cloth shone brightly in the sun.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere uwe gị ji nwu gbàà otú a?
examples.english: Why is your dress so brightly white like this?

examples.igbo: Ha wùbèrè ụlọ ọhụrụ n'obodo anyị.
examples.english: They set up a new house in our town.

examples.igbo: Ònye wùbèrè ụlọ ahịa a?
examples.english: Who set up this shop?

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka nòrubèrè gburugburu nna ha.
examples.english: The children sat round their father.

examples.igbo: Nòrube gburugburu tebụl ahụ.
examples.english: Sit round that table.

gloss: rule; government; ruling (-chị 1. C. rule, govern)

examples.igbo: Ọchịchị eze ahụ dị ogologo.
examples.english: The king's rule lasted long.

examples.igbo: Òchịchị ọhụrụ ahụ wetara udo?
examples.english: Did the new government bring peace?

gloss: be famous; well known; be popular

examples.igbo: Ọ dērē ūdē n'ihi egwu ya.
examples.english: She became famous because of her music.

examples.igbo: Onye dērē ūdē n'obodo a?
examples.english: Who is famous in this town?

examples.igbo: O kụlịtara ụkwụ ya na nkume.
examples.english: He knocked his foot against a stone.

examples.igbo: Kụlịta iko abụọ a ọnụ.
examples.english: Knock these two cups together.

examples.igbo: Anyị riri oriri n'ụlọ nna m.
examples.english: We held a feast at my father's house.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eri oriri n'ụbọchị ọmụmụ gị?
examples.english: Will you hold a feast on your birthday?

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ dinara n'elu bed.
examples.english: The child lay on the bed.

examples.igbo: Biko, dozie bed gị tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Please, arrange your bed before you go out.

note: Loanword; standard Igbo often uses akwa for 'bed'.

gloss: give one thing and or to receive another; exchange;

examples.igbo: Anyị gbara onwe anyị akwa n'ahịa.
examples.english: We exchanged clothes at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-agba onwe gị na ya ego?
examples.english: Will you exchange money with him?

note: The phrase gba onwe is used for exchange, but I would phrase one sentence differently.

examples.igbo: Ewùù! Ọ dara n'ala.
examples.english: Oh no! He fell down.

examples.igbo: Ewùù! Ọ dị m nwute maka ihe mere gị.
examples.english: Oh! I am sorry for what happened to you.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-egwu bọọlụ n'elu pitch.
examples.english: The children are playing football on the pitch.

examples.igbo: Pitch ahụ dị n'akụkụ ụlọ akwụkwọ anyị.
examples.english: That pitch is beside our school.

note: Loanword; meaning 'playing field' assumed.

gloss: go to war; be recruited into army

examples.igbo: Ọ gara agha n'afọ gara aga.
examples.english: He went to war last year.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-aga agha ma a kpọọ gị?
examples.english: Will you go to war if you are called?

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-akpa àgwà ọjọọ n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: That child behaves badly at school.

examples.igbo: Akpọla àgwà ọjọọ n'ihu ndị ọbịa.
examples.english: Don't behave badly in front of guests.

examples.igbo: O sere chart maka ahịa anyị.
examples.english: He drew a chart for our market.

examples.igbo: Lee chart a na-egosi mgbanwe ọnụ ahịa.
examples.english: Look at this chart showing price changes.

note: Loanword; meaning 'chart' assumed.

examples.igbo: Ògùgù okwu a abịala.
examples.english: The end of this matter has come.

examples.igbo: Gịnị bụ ògùgù akụkọ ahụ?
examples.english: What is the end of that story?

note: Ògùgù is a variant of ògwùgwù; examples use the sense 'end'.

examples.igbo: O ji mmà ọdū bee osisi ahụ.
examples.english: He used a saw to cut that wood.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara mmà ọdū ọhụrụ n'ahịa?
examples.english: Did you buy a new saw at the market?

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka ìtènaānị nọ n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: Nine children are in the school.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara ọkụkọ ìtènaānị?
examples.english: Did you buy nine chickens?

note: The numeral is dialectal/less common than itoolu, but the examples use it as a numeral.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-anya isi na ọ ga-emeri.
examples.english: He boasts that he will win.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka ọ na-anya isi n'ihu ndị ọbịa.
examples.english: Don't let him boast in front of guests.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-aga ijè n'ahịa ụtụtụ a.
examples.english: We are walking to the market this morning.

examples.igbo: Ndị ntorobịa ahụ na-aga ijè maka ọrụ.
examples.english: Those youths are lobbying for jobs.

note: The figurative 'lobby' sense is less common, but the sentence uses the given meaning.

gloss: be dry; be hard; be difficult

examples.igbo: Akwa ahụ kpọrọ nkụ n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: That cloth dried in the morning.

examples.igbo: Ọrụ a kpọrọ nkụ, anyị agaghị emecha ya taa.
examples.english: This work is hard, we won't finish it today.

note: Both the literal 'dry' and figurative 'difficult' senses are illustrated.

examples.igbo: O mịnyere mma ya n'akpa.
examples.english: He sheathed his knife in the pouch.

examples.igbo: Mịnye mma gị tupu ị banye n'ụlọ.
examples.english: Sheathe your knife before you enter the house.

examples.igbo: Iko ahụ tiri n'ala.
examples.english: That cup broke on the ground.

examples.igbo: Ị tiri efere ahụ?
examples.english: Did you break that plate?

note: The past form tiri is used for the verb stem -tilì.

examples.igbo: Àwaka-ọnụ̄ pụtara n'egbugbere ọnụ ya.
examples.english: A mouth blister appeared on his lip.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eji ọgwụ gwọọ àwaka-ọnụ̄ ahụ.
examples.english: You should treat that mouth blister with medicine.

examples.igbo: Ọ gbara òsịālị n'ụlọ ikpe ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: He bore witness in court yesterday.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-agba òsịālị maka nwanne gị?
examples.english: Will you bear witness for your brother?

gloss: pay homage, especially present gifts in traditional style to ọkpala

examples.igbo: O fere ǹrù n'ụlọ ọkpala anyị.
examples.english: He paid homage at our ọkpala's house.

examples.igbo: Fee ǹrù tupu ị jụọ ihe ọ bụla.
examples.english: Pay homage before you ask anything.

note: Imperative tone on fee may vary by dialect.

gloss: grow root, especially the tap root;

examples.igbo: Osisi ahụ gbara m̀kpọ̀rọ̀gwụ̀ n'ala anyị.
examples.english: That tree grew a taproot in our land.

examples.igbo: Mkpụrụ ọka na-agba m̀kpọ̀rọ̀gwụ̀ ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Maize seed grows a taproot quickly.

examples.igbo: Ụlọ ọhụrụ a nwere mbalā nke ukwuu.
examples.english: This new house is very spacious.

examples.igbo: Mbalā nke ubi ahụ tụrụ anyị n'anya.
examples.english: The spaciousness of that farm surprised us.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-eji àmàmife ya akụziri ụmụ ya ihe.
examples.english: He uses his wisdom to teach his children.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere àmàmife zuru ezu maka ọrụ a?
examples.english: Do you have enough knowledge for this work?

examples.igbo: Òlìlè nke okwu ahụ mere anyị obi ụtọ.
examples.english: The fulfillment of that word made us happy.

examples.igbo: Ị na-atụ anya òlìlè nke nrọ gị?
examples.english: Are you expecting the fulfillment of your dream?

note: Sense is abstract but usage is standard.

gloss: be coy; hesitate to grant a request or favour which one actually wants to grant

examples.igbo: Ọ na-agò iru kama inye m ego.
examples.english: He is being coy instead of giving me money.

examples.igbo: Ị na-agò iru, gịnị mere?
examples.english: You are being coy, why?

note: Inflection of -gò iru is uncertain; present continuous used.

examples.igbo: Chinweike bịara n'ụlọ anyị ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: Chinweike came to our house yesterday.

examples.igbo: Chinweike, bịa lee ihe m chọtara.
examples.english: Chinweike, come and see what I found.

gloss: for emphasis the word can be repeated, meaning immediately, instantly

examples.igbo: Ọ bịara òzìgbo òzìgbo mgbe anyị kpọrọ ya.
examples.english: He came immediately when we called him.

examples.igbo: Mechie ụzọ òzìgbo òzìgbo tupu mmiri abịa.
examples.english: Close the door immediately before the rain comes.

examples.igbo: Ego m nwefọrọ ntakịrị.
examples.english: My money has a little remaining.

examples.igbo: Oge nwefọrọ anyị otu ụbọchị tupu emume ahụ.
examples.english: We have one day remaining before the ceremony.

note: Inflection of -nwefọ is less common but used here as past.

examples.igbo: O nwere ike ịligbàdo nri ahụ niile.
examples.english: He can eat all that food altogether.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-ligbàdo nri gị tupu ị pụọ?
examples.english: Will you eat your food altogether before you leave?

note: The sense is clear, but the verb stem is uncommon; inflection may vary by dialect.

examples.igbo: Mbìdo mkpụrụ osisi na-enyere anyị aka inweta mmiri.
examples.english: Pressing fruit helps us get juice.

examples.igbo: Mbìdo ya n'isi nwata ahụ wutere ya.
examples.english: His pressing on that child's head hurt him.

note: Noun usage is plausible, but I would phrase one sentence differently in ordinary speech.

examples.igbo: Ahụrụ m ògàzị mwù n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: I saw an African pike in the market today.

examples.igbo: Nne m zụtara ògàzị mwù maka ofe.
examples.english: My mother bought an African pike for soup.

note: The fish name is specialized; spelling follows the entry.

examples.igbo: O nwere isi awelē n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: He had good luck in the market today.

examples.igbo: Isi awelē gị ga-enyere gị aka n'ọrụ a.
examples.english: Your good luck will help you in this work.

examples.igbo: Di na nwunye ahụ na-enwe mkpakọ n'abalị.
examples.english: That couple has intercourse at night.

examples.igbo: Mkpakọ bụ akụkụ nke alụmdi na nwunye.
examples.english: Intercourse is part of marriage.

gloss: take out, extract teeth; lose tooth, teeth

examples.igbo: Dọkịta kworo eze m ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: The doctor extracted my tooth yesterday.

examples.igbo: Nwa m kworo eze mgbe ọ dara n'osisi.
examples.english: My child lost a tooth when he fell from a tree.

gloss: come to an agreement Ànyị èkwekọlịtago We have come to an agreement

examples.igbo: Anyị ekwekọlịtago n'okwu ahụ.
examples.english: We have come to an agreement on that matter.

examples.igbo: Ha ga-ekwekọlịta tupu ha arụ ọrụ ahụ.
examples.english: They will come to an agreement before they do that work.

examples.igbo: Mmiri na-anyụsịsị n'ala ahụ.
examples.english: Water is oozing out of that land.

examples.igbo: Ọbara na-anyụsịsị n'ọnyá ya.
examples.english: Blood is oozing from his wound.

note: The verb form is plausible; the stem is less common in everyday speech.

examples.igbo: O dufuru nwa agbọghọ ahụ.
examples.english: He seduced that girl.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka onye ọjọọ dufu gị.
examples.english: Don't let a bad person lead you astray.

examples.igbo: Ògbụgba ākwụkwọ a ga-ewe ogologo oge.
examples.english: This legal prosecution will take a long time.

examples.igbo: Ha na-eme ògbụgba ākwụkwọ megide ya.
examples.english: They are carrying out a legal prosecution against him.

note: The phrase is formal; examples are grammatical but somewhat specialized.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ ezie na mmiri zoro, anyị gara ahịa.
examples.english: Though it rained, we went to the market.

examples.igbo: Ezie na ọ gwụrụ agwụ, o nyere nwata ahụ nri.
examples.english: Though she was tired, she gave the child food.

note: The concessive 'ezie' usually appears in the frame 'ọ bụ ezie na'. The second sentence uses the shorter 'ezie na', which is heard but less fixed.

examples.igbo: Nne m zụtara afele ùkòlò ọhụrụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: My mother bought a new hollow plate at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị tinyere ofe n'ime afele ùkòlò ahụ?
examples.english: Did you put the soup in that hollow plate?

note: 'Efere' is the more common everyday form for plate; 'afele ùkòlò' is given as the headword and used as such.

examples.igbo: Ndị Igbo na-akpọ Chineke Òsebùlu-ùwà.
examples.english: The Igbo call God Òsebùlu-ùwà.

examples.igbo: Òsebùlu-ùwà, chebe anyị n'ụzọ.
examples.english: Great God, protect us on the journey.

note: This is a divine epithet/name rather than a common noun, so it is used in address and naming contexts; tone markings follow the entry as given.

examples.igbo: Ọ dara n'ala wee nweta nnwòji n'ụkwụ.
examples.english: He fell down and got a sprain in his foot.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ nnwòji ka ọ bụ mgbaji ọkpụkpụ?
examples.english: Is it a sprain or a broken bone?

note: The word is used correctly for a joint injury; I am less certain about the exact tone pattern given, so I kept the orthography of the entry.

examples.igbo: Mkpụrụ ọka ahụ apụla n'ala.
examples.english: That maize seed has sprouted in the ground.

examples.igbo: Ahịhịa ọjọọ na-apụ n'ubi mgbe mmiri zoro.
examples.english: Weeds sprout in the farm when it rains.

note: '-pụ' in this sense is often extended as '-pụta' when the focus is on coming up into view; the plain stem is used here as in the entry.

examples.igbo: Nwa ewu na-awụ ìkpòtọ n'ogige.
examples.english: The kid goat gambols in the yard.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ka nwa atụrụ si awụ ìkpòtọ?
examples.english: Did you see how the lamb gambols?

note: The stem appears inflected as 'awụ' with the object 'ìkpòtọ' as given; this is the expected construction for young animals at play.

examples.igbo: Anyị rụrụ ụlọ ahụ n'onwe āyị.
examples.english: We built that house ourselves.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-ekwu maka ònwe āyị?
examples.english: Are we talking about ourselves?

gloss: have epilepsy; be epileptic; have epileptic fits

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ dàrà àkwụkwụ̀ n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: That child had an epileptic fit at school.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ada àkwụkwụ̀ mgbe ọ na-ewe iwe?
examples.english: Does he have fits when he gets angry?

examples.igbo: O kèrè òkè n'ọrụ a.
examples.english: He took a share in this work.

examples.igbo: Kee òkè gị na anụ ahụ.
examples.english: Take your share of that meat.

gloss: form of greeting used by a person leaving a place to the person he is leaving; dàalụ zị nù such a greeting directed to more than one person

examples.igbo: Dàalụ zị, m na-apụ ugbu a.
examples.english: Goodbye, I am leaving now.

examples.igbo: Dàalụ zị nù, ndị enyi m.
examples.english: Goodbye to you all, my friends.

examples.igbo: M̀kpọmaasị̀ dị n'etiti ha abụọ.
examples.english: There is hatred between the two of them.

examples.igbo: Wepụ m̀kpọmaasị̀ n'obi gị.
examples.english: Remove hatred from your heart.

examples.igbo: O tụrụ ụ̀dọ̀ maka ijide ewu.
examples.english: He braided a rope to tie a goat.

examples.igbo: Tụọ ụ̀dọ̀ ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: Braid that rope well.

examples.igbo: Mmiri na-agbapụta n'ite ahụ.
examples.english: Water is pouring out of that pot.

examples.igbo: Ọbara na-agbapụ n'aka ya?
examples.english: Is blood exuding from his hand?

examples.igbo: Nwa mgbèyì ahụ na-ere ahịa n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: That orphan is hawking on the street.

examples.igbo: Ị maara nwa mgbèyì ahụ?
examples.english: Do you know that orphan?

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ chụliiri ụmụ nnụnụ n'osisi.
examples.english: That child stirred up the birds in the tree.

examples.igbo: Chụlia ụmụ nnụnụ ahụ ka ha fee.
examples.english: Stir up those birds so they fly.

examples.igbo: Anyị riri anụ ōghighe n'ahịa.
examples.english: We ate fried meat at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eri anụ ōghighe?
examples.english: Will you eat fried meat?

examples.igbo: Ọ gbasara iru mgbe ọ hụrụ anyị.
examples.english: He looked cheerful when he saw us.

examples.igbo: Gbasaa iru, ihe niile ga-adị mma.
examples.english: Look cheerful, everything will be fine.

gloss: thump on the ground; set down heavily

examples.igbo: O sùrù ụkwụ n'ànì mgbe ọ nụrụ akụkọ ahụ.
examples.english: He stamped his foot on the ground when he heard the news.

examples.igbo: Sù ụkwụ gị n'ànì, ka anyị hụ ike gị.
examples.english: Stamp your foot on the ground, let us see your strength.

note: Assumed the idiom sù ụkwụ n'ànì for thumping the ground.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ mehìrì, nne ya baara ya mba.
examples.english: The child did wrong, his mother scolded him.

examples.igbo: Emela mehiè ọzọ, gee ntị nke ọma.
examples.english: Do not do wrong again, listen well.

examples.igbo: Amāafịa na-ara m n'abalị niile.
examples.english: Toothache aches me all night.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ara amāafịa, gịnị mere ị naghị aga dọkịta?
examples.english: Are you having toothache, why aren't you going to the doctor?

examples.igbo: E nwere nkewa n'etiti ụmụ akwụkwọ abụọ ahụ.
examples.english: There is division between those two students.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara nkewa n'ezinụlọ a?
examples.english: What caused division in this family?

examples.igbo: O kpọchiri ụzọ mgbe ọ banyere n'ụlọ.
examples.english: He shut the door when he entered the house.

examples.igbo: Kpọchie ụzọ ahụ, ka ikuku ghara ịbata.
examples.english: Shut that door, so the wind will not enter.

gloss: a speech to a person who is not present or to a personified object; an apostrophe

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ kwuru ǹkwusara nye nne ya nọ n'ebe ọzọ.
examples.english: The child made an apostrophe to his mother who was elsewhere.

examples.igbo: Ị na-agwa osisi ahụ okwu — ọ bụ ǹkwusara?
examples.english: Are you talking to that tree — is it an apostrophe?

note: ǹkwusara is literary; examples illustrate speech to an absent person or personified object.

examples.igbo: Ha na-akpakọ ụkwụ mgbe ha na-aga ahịa.
examples.english: They walk together when they go to the market.

examples.igbo: Kpakọọ m ụkwụ, ebe anyị na-aga otu ebe.
examples.english: Walk together with me, since we are going to the same place.

note: Used kpakọ ụkwụ for walking together.

gloss: a period of time when an action or activity is yet to happen; future

examples.igbo: Anyị na-eche banyere ọ̀dị̀niihu ụmụ anyị.
examples.english: We think about our children's future.

examples.igbo: Kedu ihe ị chọrọ n'ọ̀dị̀niihu?
examples.english: What do you want in the future?

examples.igbo: Nne m na-eji akụ okwute egwe ọka.
examples.english: My mother uses a grinding stone to grind corn.

examples.igbo: Ebee ka akụ okwute dị?
examples.english: Where is the grinding stone?

note: Headword spelling is uncertain; used akụ okwute for the corn-grinding stone.

examples.igbo: Onye nghagbu ahụ ghaara m ụgha n'ahịa.
examples.english: That trickster lied to me at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị bụ onye nghagbu, gịnị mere ị jị ghọgbuo ya?
examples.english: You are a trickster, why did you deceive him?

examples.igbo: Nne ya kpọlụrụ ya maka ime mkpọtụ.
examples.english: His mother reproached him for making noise.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji na-akpọlụ nwa gị?
examples.english: Why are you abusing your child?

examples.igbo: Onye dibịa chịrị òkwè maka ọrịa nwa ahụ.
examples.english: The dibia divined with beads about that child's illness.

examples.igbo: Ị chịrị òkwè tupu i zụta ala ahụ?
examples.english: Did you divine with beads before you bought that land?

examples.igbo: Nri a zùrù anyị niile.
examples.english: This food was enough for us all.

examples.igbo: Ego a ọ zùrù ịzụ akwụkwọ?
examples.english: Is this money enough to buy books?

gloss: disease characterised by growth of kernel-like tumours visible under the skin or really prominent and hard on any part of the body, and diseases characterised by swelling and hardening of the glands of the body, which become hard and prominent and look like kernels (especially the lymphoid glands); may be malignant or non-malignant. This is another example of one of the Igbo methods of disease diagnosis. The disease is diagnosed by symptoms, so that numberless different diseases which appear to show similar signs can be given one name; thus three persons suffering from different diseases may be diagnosed as suffering from the same disease by this diagnostic method

examples.igbo: Ọyà mkpụlụ akū na-egbu ụmụaka n'ime obodo anyị.
examples.english: The kernel-like tumour disease is killing children in our town.

examples.igbo: Dọkịta hụrụ ọyà mkpụlụ akū n'olu nwata ahụ.
examples.english: The doctor saw the kernel-like tumour disease on that child's neck.

examples.igbo: Igwe ahụ gbara nchāla n'ihi mmiri.
examples.english: That metal rusted because of water.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụrụ na ị hapụ ya n'èzí, ọ ga-agba nchāla.
examples.english: If you leave it outside, it will rust.

examples.igbo: Ugọnọm bụ azụ dị n'osimiri Niger.
examples.english: Ugọnọm is a fish found in River Niger.

examples.igbo: Anyị zụtara ugọnọm abụọ n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: We bought two ugọnọm fish at the market today.

gloss: (trans. and intrans.) break asunder; snap (trans.) Ènwè afù nà-àchọ ịnyàjì alakā osisi The monkey is going to break the branch of the tree (intrans.) Alakā osisi afù gà-anyàji tupu ụtụtù echiì The branch of the tree will break before tomorrow morning

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ nyàjìrì alaka osisi.
examples.english: That child snapped the tree branch.

examples.igbo: Alaka osisi ahụ gà-anyàji ma ifufe fee.
examples.english: That tree branch will snap if wind blows.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-aga Fadaa ụtụtù Sọnde.
examples.english: We go to Church on Sunday morning.

examples.igbo: Fadaa dị n'obodo anyị.
examples.english: The Church is in our town.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ese sị̀ga n'ihu ụmụaka.
examples.english: He smokes cigarette in front of children.

examples.igbo: Esekwala sị̀ga ebe a.
examples.english: Don't smoke cigarette here.

examples.igbo: Anyị bịara ịkasị ya obì n'ihi ọnwụ nwa ya.
examples.english: We came to comfort her because of her child's death.

examples.igbo: Okwu ọ gwara m kasịrị m obì.
examples.english: The words he told me comforted me.

examples.igbo: Nne ya bụ ògụ ìsà, ọ na-akọ akụkọ ụbọchị niile.
examples.english: His mother is a chatterbox, she tells stories all day.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji bụrụ ògụ ìsà n'ụlọ akwụkwọ?
examples.english: Why are you a chatterbox at school?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-aṅụ tii n'ìko.
examples.english: He drinks tea from a cup.

examples.igbo: Were ìko ahụ wunye nna gị mmiri.
examples.english: Take that cup and pour your father water.

examples.igbo: O bèkanyere m otu iberibe achịcha.
examples.english: He cut off and gave me a piece of bread.

examples.igbo: Bèkanyere nwanne gị anụ ọkụkọ ahụ.
examples.english: Cut off and give your sibling that chicken meat.

examples.igbo: Nne m na-ekebe nri abalị.
examples.english: My mother is getting dinner ready.

examples.igbo: Kebe ụlọ ahụ tupu ọbịa abịa.
examples.english: Get that room ready before the guest arrives.

gloss: pluck; detach the leaf or flower of a plant from the plant

examples.igbo: Nwa m kụ̀rụ okooko osisi n'ubi.
examples.english: My child plucked a flower in the farm.

examples.igbo: Kụ̀a akwụkwọ ndụ were nye ewu.
examples.english: Pluck leaves and give the goat.

examples.igbo: Ọ kụjara elu mgbe ọ nụrụ ụda ahụ.
examples.english: He started up when he heard that noise.

examples.igbo: Kụjaa elu, ụda dị n'azụ ụlọ.
examples.english: Start up, there is a noise behind the house.

examples.igbo: Ọkụ ledoro n'ọhịa taa.
examples.english: Fire blazed in the bush today.

examples.igbo: Ọkụ na-aledo n'ọhịa, kpọọ ndị mgbanyụ ọkụ.
examples.english: Fire is blazing in the bush, call the firefighters.

examples.igbo: Anyị gafere n'osimiri ahụ n'ụgbọ mmiri.
examples.english: We crossed that river by boat.

examples.igbo: Gafee n'okporo ụzọ mgbe ụgbọala kwụsịrị.
examples.english: Cross the road when the car stops.

gloss: climb; crawl(animals); move flat on the floor or ground

examples.igbo: Nwa m rịrị n'elu osisi.
examples.english: My child climbed up the tree.

examples.igbo: Agwọ na-arị n'ala ahịhịa.
examples.english: The snake is crawling on the grass.

examples.igbo: Ọ mebere nri tupu ọbịa bịa.
examples.english: She prepared food before the guest arrived.

examples.igbo: Mebe ụlọ gị maka ọbịa.
examples.english: Prepare your house for the guest.

examples.igbo: Nne ya kwuru na ọ hụrụ ùwà ndị mmụọ na nrọ.
examples.english: His mother said he saw the world of spirits in a dream.

examples.igbo: Ùwà ndị mmụọ adịghị ka nke anyị.
examples.english: The world of spirits is not like ours.

examples.igbo: Ọ ji òche anwụ gaa ahịa.
examples.english: He took an umbrella to the market.

examples.igbo: Òche anwụ gị ọ dị n'akpa gị?
examples.english: Is your umbrella in your bag?

gloss: bandit (literally the night is dangerous) Onye àbànì dì egwù

examples.igbo: Ndị uwe ojii jidere otu onye àbànì dị egwu.
examples.english: The police arrested a bandit.

examples.igbo: Onye àbànì dị egwu zuru ego anyị n'abalị.
examples.english: A bandit stole our money at night.

note: The phrase is accepted, but I am not fully certain of its everyday frequency.

examples.igbo: Ọ kpụpụrụ okpu ya wee kelee anyị.
examples.english: He took off his cap and greeted us.

examples.igbo: Kpụpụ okpu gị tupu ị banye n'ụlọ.
examples.english: Take off your cap before you enter the house.

examples.igbo: Ọ kpere ụgbọ gafee osimiri.
examples.english: He steered the canoe across the river.

examples.igbo: Kpee ụgbọ ahụ nwayọ, mmiri na-asọ.
examples.english: Steer that canoe slowly, the water is flowing.

examples.igbo: Ndị otu anyị nwetara mmeli n'egwuregwu ahụ.
examples.english: Our team got victory in that match.

examples.igbo: Mmeli ọ bụ naanị ihe ị na-achọ?
examples.english: Is victory the only thing you want?

examples.igbo: Nwatakịrị ahụ nwere àkọ nke ukwuu.
examples.english: That child is very intelligent.

examples.igbo: Nwee àkọ mgbe ị na-azụ ahịa.
examples.english: Be intelligent when you are trading.

note: The idiom is understood, though the command form may be uncommon.

gloss: be striped, spotted, variegated; to vary

examples.igbo: Uwe ahụ tụgwarị tụgwa, ọ masịrị m.
examples.english: That dress is variegated; I like it.

examples.igbo: Ọnụ ahịa ya na-atụgwa kwa ụbọchị.
examples.english: Its price varies every day.

note: I am not fully sure of the first inflected form.

gloss: fall off from one's custody (especially hands)

examples.igbo: Akwụkwọ ahụ dànarịrị n'aka ya.
examples.english: The book fell from his hand.

examples.igbo: Jide ego ahụ aka, ka ọ ghara ịdànarị.
examples.english: Hold that money firmly, so it does not fall.

gloss: the day of judgement; the last day

examples.igbo: N'ụbọsị ikpe azụ, Chineke ga-ekpe mmadụ ikpe.
examples.english: On the day of judgement, God will judge people.

examples.igbo: Ị chetara na ụbọsị ikpe azụ na-abịa?
examples.english: Do you remember that the last day is coming?

examples.igbo: O na-agwu ala n'ubi ya ugbu a.
examples.english: He is digging the ground in his farm now.

examples.igbo: Gwu ala ahụ tupu mmiri abịa.
examples.english: Dig that ground before the rain comes.

note: Assumed gwu is the verb stem for 'dig' as in igwu ala.

examples.igbo: M riri ọkwùlù oyìbo n'ụtụtụ taa.
examples.english: I ate pawpaw this morning.

examples.igbo: Ị zụrụ ọkwùlù oyìbo n'ahịa ụnyaahụ?
examples.english: Did you buy pawpaw at the market yesterday?

gloss: accommodate the size of something; enter; take; fit

examples.igbo: Uwe a na-abà m nke ọma.
examples.english: This dress fits me well.

examples.igbo: Bà n'ime ụlọ ahụ ugbu a.
examples.english: Enter that house now.

examples.igbo: Òkwù m bịara ebe a ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: My friend came here yesterday.

examples.igbo: Òkwù gị ọ nọ n'ụlọ ugbu a?
examples.english: Is your friend at home now?

note: òkwù for 'friend' is not the most common standard term; enyi is more usual.

gloss: run hither and thither; make fuss; be dilatory, going hither and thither without anything being seen done by the person; dilly- dally

examples.igbo: Ọ na-agbakìlì ànì n'ahịa ogologo oge.
examples.english: He is running hither and thither in the market for a long time.

examples.igbo: Kwụsị ịgbakìlì ànì, rụọ ọrụ gị.
examples.english: Stop running hither and thither, do your work.

examples.igbo: Were ǹra na-acha ntutu gị ugbu a.
examples.english: Use a comb to comb your hair now.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ǹra m n'ụlọ taa?
examples.english: Did you see my comb in the house today?

examples.igbo: Anụ ahụ alighịrị, ọ siri ike ịta.
examples.english: That meat is lean and tough, it is hard to chew.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara anụ alighịrị n'ahịa ụnyaahụ?
examples.english: Did you buy lean and tough meat at the market yesterday?

examples.igbo: Ajō uchè ya mere ka anyị daa.
examples.english: His bad plan made us fail.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eche ajō uchè maka mmadụ?
examples.english: Are you thinking bad plans about people?

examples.igbo: Onye nkuzi dubara anyị n'ime ọnụ ụlọ.
examples.english: The teacher led us into the room.

examples.igbo: Duba ya n'ọrụ ọhụrụ ahụ taa.
examples.english: Introduce him into that new job today.

examples.igbo: O kewara ji ahụ n'ibe na abụọ.
examples.english: He divided that yam into two pieces.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara ibe na abụọ anụ?
examples.english: Did you buy two pieces of meat?

note: Headword given as ibe naàbò; examples use standard spelling ibe na abụọ.

gloss: to take an oath before a deity or supernatural being

examples.igbo: Ọ dọrọ iyi n'ihu chi na ọ ga-ekwu eziokwu.
examples.english: He swore an oath before the deity that he would tell the truth.

examples.igbo: Ị dọrọ iyi n'ihu chi gị?
examples.english: Did you swear an oath before your deity?

examples.igbo: Ndị inyom ahụ bụrụ abụ dị nwayọ.
examples.english: Those women sang a slow song.

examples.igbo: Bụọ abụ ọzọ dị nwayọ, biko.
examples.english: Sing another slow song, please.

gloss: be or get chaotic; be disorganized; be disorderly

examples.igbo: Ahịa ahụ gbara àghara n'ụtụtụ taa.
examples.english: That market was chaotic this morning.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka, unu na-agba àghara n'ụlọ!
examples.english: Children, you are being disorderly in the house!

examples.igbo: O zụtara ajụ ụtabà abụọ n'ahịa.
examples.english: He bought two rolls of tobacco at the market.

examples.igbo: Ajụ ụtabà a dị oke ọnụ?
examples.english: Is this roll of tobacco too expensive?

examples.igbo: Ọ dịkarịa ala otu awa iji ruo ebe ahụ.
examples.english: It takes at least one hour to reach there.

examples.igbo: Anyị ga-echere ya dịkarịa ala otu awa.
examples.english: We will wait for him at least one hour.

examples.igbo: Agwọ m ntụ ahụ na mmiri.
examples.english: I mixed that ash with water.

examples.igbo: Dọkịta gwọrọ ọrịa ya ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: The doctor cured his illness quickly.

note: First sentence illustrates 'mix'; second illustrates 'cure'.

gloss: describes something which is plentiful or falls plentifully Ogè m nà-agbà akwụkwọ ewēpùtàlù m òfu ụnō ūla màkà idēbe ife ōlili. Ị bàta nà ya ogè afù ife ōlili àdị pìtìì When I was getting married, I devoted one room to keeping foods. If you entered it at that time, the food looked very plentiful Akwụ dī n’iru īlo etègo o jìlì cha, kịtāà mkpụlū ya nà- adàsịsị pìtìì pìtìì The palm fruit in the front of the house has been ripe a long time, now the nuts fall pìtìì pìtìì

examples.igbo: Mkpụrụ osisi ahụ dàrị pìtìì n'ala.
examples.english: Those fruits fell plentifully on the ground.

examples.igbo: Nri dị pìtìì n'ụlọ oriri ahụ.
examples.english: Food was plentiful at that party.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-ekele Chukwu Ābịàmà maka nri a.
examples.english: We thank God the Provider for this food.

examples.igbo: Chukwu Ābịàmà, chebe anyị n'ụzọ.
examples.english: God the Provider, protect us on the journey.

examples.igbo: Ugbè ọkụkọ ahụ dị ọcha nke ọma.
examples.english: That chicken's feather is very clean.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ugbè ọhụrụ n'ọdụ nnụnụ?
examples.english: Did you see a new feather on the bird's tail?

examples.igbo: Nne m zụtara ife ọkụkụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: My mother bought planting materials at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị kụọla ife ọkụkụ n'ubi taa?
examples.english: Have you planted the planting materials in the farm today?

note: ife is a dialectal variant; examples use the headword as given.

examples.igbo: Nkịta wakuru onye ọbịa ahụ n'èzí.
examples.english: The dog rushed at that visitor outside.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka wakuru ibe ha n'egwuregwu n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: The children rushed at their mates in play at school.

note: Verb stem waku(lu); examples use wakuru.

examples.igbo: Ànùm ahụ na-aga nwayọọ nwayọọ n'ala.
examples.english: That female tortoise walks very slowly on the ground.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ànùm n'akụkụ mmiri taa?
examples.english: Did you see a female tortoise by the water today?

note: Sense of ànùm as female tortoise is uncommon; examples are tentative.

examples.igbo: Nwata a bụ gbaghaashi n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: This child is troublesome at school.

examples.igbo: Gbaghaashi gịnị ka ị na-eme n'ebe a?
examples.english: What trouble are you making here?

note: Sense and usage uncertain; examples are tentative.

examples.igbo: Ndị ègbènù ahụ lụrụ agha n'obodo.
examples.english: Those warriors fought a war in the town.

examples.igbo: Ì hụrụ ndị ègbènù n'obodo taa?
examples.english: Did you see the warriors in the town today?

note: ègbènù is archaic for warriors; examples are acceptable.

gloss: pick one's way; move on slowly; step; toddle (as child)

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ na-ranye ijè nwayọọ n'ụlọ.
examples.english: That child is toddling slowly in the house.

examples.igbo: Anyị ranyere ijè n'ụzọ dị warara.
