examples.english: We picked our way along the narrow road.

note: Verb phrase ranye ijè; examples use ranyere/na-ranye.

gloss: rub, smoothe, wet wall; paint wall

examples.igbo: Ha na-ete ajā n'ahụ ụlọ ọhụrụ.
examples.english: They are plastering mud on the new wall.

examples.igbo: O tee ajā n'ọnụ ụzọ ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: He plastered mud at the doorway yesterday.

note: Verb phrase te ajā; examples use ete/tee.

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ na-ebu ụkà n'obodo oge niile.
examples.english: That man makes trouble in the town all the time.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ebu ụkà maka ihe efu?
examples.english: Are you making trouble over nothing?

note: Verb phrase bu ụkà; examples use na-ebu.

gloss: quarrel noisily; make noise (in quarrel (= -fịọ ùzù)

examples.igbo: Ha na-atụ ùzù n'èzí n'abalị.
examples.english: They are quarrelling noisily outside at night.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka tụrụ ùzù n'ụlọ akwụkwọ taa.
examples.english: The children quarrelled noisily at school today.

note: Verb phrase tụ ùzù; examples use na-atụ/tụrụ.

gloss: worry greatly; wear out oneself with thinking

examples.igbo: Ọ na-enchekasị maka ụmụ ya mgbe niile.
examples.english: She worries greatly about her children all the time.

examples.igbo: Enchekasịla onwe gị maka ego n'efu.
examples.english: Don't wear yourself out thinking about money for nothing.

note: Headword seems to be nchekasị (noun); examples use related verb forms as instructed, but the verb inflection is uncertain.

gloss: mightiest; greatest; expert; specialist; used in

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ òkà n’ịkụ ọkpọ n’obodo a.
examples.english: He is an expert in boxing in this town.

examples.igbo: Ị bụ òkà n’ọrụ ugbo?
examples.english: Are you an expert in farming?

note: Standalone use of òkà is less common than in compounds; examples treat it as expert/specialist.

gloss: pour into a particular place (liquids, kernels)

examples.igbo: Wụsa mmiri n’ime ite ahụ.
examples.english: Pour water into that pot.

examples.igbo: Ị wụsara mmanụ n’ime ite?
examples.english: Did you pour oil into the pot?

examples.igbo: Ụgbọ ahụ bu ọtụtụ ndị njem.
examples.english: That vehicle carried many passengers.

examples.igbo: Ị na-anya ụgbọ gaa ọrụ?
examples.english: Do you drive a vehicle to work?

examples.igbo: Kpakpando na-amụsị n’eluigwe n’abalị.
examples.english: Stars glitter in the sky at night.

examples.igbo: Gịnị na-amụsị n’ebe ahụ?
examples.english: What is glittering there?

examples.igbo: Ndị agha anyị laghachiri azụ n’abalị ahụ.
examples.english: Our troops retreated that night.

examples.igbo: Ndị agha anyị laghachiri azụ, ma ndị iro esoghị ha.
examples.english: Our troops retreated, but the enemy did not follow them.

note: Given form is nonstandard; examples use standard 'laghachiri azụ'.

examples.igbo: Obì na-eri mkpụrụ osisi n’ọhịa.
examples.english: A porcupine eats fruit in the bush.

examples.igbo: Ị hụtụla obì n’ọhịa?
examples.english: Have you seen a porcupine in the bush?

examples.igbo: Anyị bilitere n’ùzọ ūtụtù.
examples.english: We woke up early morning.

examples.igbo: Ị na-aga ọrụ n’ùzọ ūtụtù?
examples.english: Do you go to work early morning?

examples.igbo: Mgbā ahụ rapaara n’aka m.
examples.english: That glue stuck to my hand.

examples.igbo: Were mgbā mechie akwụkwọ a.
examples.english: Use glue to seal this paper.

examples.igbo: Nne ya sutụrụ ọnū n’ihu nwa ahụ.
examples.english: His mother kissed the child's face.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-asutụ ọnū n’aka m?
examples.english: Will you kiss my hand?

examples.igbo: Nna m lụchara ànì ubi taa.
examples.english: My father cleared the farm land today.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-alụcha ànì ahụ echi?
examples.english: Will you clear that land tomorrow?

examples.igbo: O kwutere aha m n'ọgbakọ.
examples.english: He mentioned my name at the meeting.

examples.igbo: Kwutere ya okwu a mgbe ị hụrụ ya.
examples.english: Mention this matter to him when you see him.

examples.igbo: Nne m zụtara oke ākpa ọhụrụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: My mother bought a new long broom at the market.

examples.igbo: Were oke ākpa zaa ụlọ a.
examples.english: Use the long broom to sweep this house.

gloss: early; formerly; long ago; ancient; olden (times) (stronger than gboo)

examples.igbo: Gboo lì, anyị na-eji ụkwụ aga ahịa.
examples.english: Long ago, we used to go to the market on foot.

examples.igbo: Ị cheta ka e si ebi ndụ gboo lì?
examples.english: Do you remember how people lived long ago?

gloss: break, snap into several pieces by falling (of long objects with some weight, e.g. yam, pole)

examples.igbo: Osisi ahụ tijisịrị mgbe ifufe fesara ya.
examples.english: The tree snapped into pieces when the wind blew it down.

examples.igbo: Lee, okpara ahụ tijisịrị kpamkpam!
examples.english: Look, that pole has completely broken into pieces!

examples.igbo: Nchefù ya na-ewetara ya nsogbu n'ọrụ.
examples.english: His forgetfulness brings him trouble at work.

examples.igbo: Gịnị na-akpata nchefù gị?
examples.english: What causes your forgetfulness?

examples.igbo: Anyị liri nni wee laa.
examples.english: We ate food and went home.

examples.igbo: Nye nwa ahụ nni ka ọ lie.
examples.english: Give that child food so that he eats.

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ richara nni ya ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: The child finished his food quickly.

examples.igbo: Richaa nni gị tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Finish your food before you leave.

examples.igbo: Onye isi kpọrọ ìzù taa.
examples.english: The leader called a meeting today.

examples.igbo: Onye kpọrọ ìzù a?
examples.english: Who called this meeting?

gloss: go about (in a herd or crowd); push about

examples.igbo: Ehi na-anughalị n'ọhịa.
examples.english: The cattle roam about in the field.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ụmụ ehi ji anughalị n'ubi anyị?
examples.english: Why are the cows roaming about in our farm?

gloss: promote; enhance; raise; to lift or move something to a higher level

examples.igbo: Gọọmentị na-akwàlite ụgwọ ọrụ ndị nkuzi.
examples.english: The government is raising teachers' salaries.

examples.igbo: Kwàlite aka gị elu ma ọ bụrụ na ị maara azịza.
examples.english: Raise your hand if you know the answer.

gloss: the head child; the king child

examples.igbo: Ezènnwā na-elekọta ụmụnne ya mgbe nne na nna na-anọghị.
examples.english: The head child takes care of his siblings when the parents are away.

examples.igbo: Ònye bụ Ezènnwā n'ezinụlọ unu?
examples.english: Who is the head child in your family?

examples.igbo: Ọ kụrụ ya aka n'àgbà.
examples.english: He slapped him on the cheek.

examples.igbo: Àgbà gị ọ na-egbu mgbu?
examples.english: Does your jaw hurt?

gloss: deliberately call somebody or something a names that portrays less of the person or thing; curse; abuse

examples.igbo: Ọ kpọrọ ya iyī n'ihu mmadụ niile.
examples.english: He abused him in front of everyone.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka onye ọ bụla kpọọ gị iyī.
examples.english: Do not let anyone abuse you.

examples.igbo: Echiche anyị dakọrọ ọnụ n'okwu ahụ.
examples.english: Our opinions coincided on that matter.

examples.igbo: Olu unu na-adakọ ọnụ n'abụ a?
examples.english: Do your voices harmonize in this song?

examples.igbo: Anyị na-aga ọrụ kwà ụbòsì.
examples.english: We go to work every day.

examples.igbo: Ị na-asa efere kwà ụbòsì?
examples.english: Do you wash plates every day?

gloss: commit crime, offence; break law; sin

examples.igbo: Ọ mebiri iwū n'obodo anyị.
examples.english: He broke the law in our town.

examples.igbo: Ekwela imebi iwū.
examples.english: Do not break the law.

examples.igbo: O bekalụrụ nne ya achịcha.
examples.english: She cut a piece of bread for her mother.

examples.igbo: Bekalụ m anụ ahụ ntakịrị.
examples.english: Cut a little piece of that meat for me.

examples.igbo: Anya ikē ya mere ka o rie nri niile.
examples.english: His greed made him eat all the food.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere anya ikē ịga n'ime ọhịa ahụ?
examples.english: Do you have the boldness to go into that forest?

examples.igbo: Ị ma na ịkwa nne gị emo bụ ife izè?
examples.english: Do you know that mocking your mother is an offensive thing?

examples.igbo: Anyị na-ezere ihe ahụ n'ihi na ọ bụ ife izè.
examples.english: We avoid that thing because it is an offensive thing.

note: Sense understood as 'abominable/offensive thing'; usage is idiomatic but the noun is uncommon in everyday speech.

examples.igbo: Nnụnụ ahụ fedàtara n'ala ịchọ nri.
examples.english: That bird flew down to the ground to look for food.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ụgbọelu ji fedàta n'ebe a?
examples.english: Why is the plane flying down here?

gloss: be complete; be sufficient; be perfect

examples.igbo: Ọrụ ụlọ ahụ zuru òkè taa.
examples.english: The work on that house was complete today.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ na ego anyị zuru òkè?
examples.english: Is our money sufficient?

note: 'zu òkè' taken as 'be complete/sufficient'; the exact collocation varies by speaker.

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ bụrụ nwa ya mmiri n'ihu.
examples.english: That man spat at his child in the face.

examples.igbo: Ọ dịghị mma ịbụ mmiri n'ihu mmadụ.
examples.english: It is not good to spit in front of people.

note: Sense of 'bụ' as spitting is not common in my own speech; phrasing kept simple.

examples.igbo: M kwenyelụrụ ya n'ihe o kwuru.
examples.english: I agreed with him on what he said.

examples.igbo: Ị kwenyelụrụ m n'okwu a?
examples.english: Do you agree with me on this matter?

examples.igbo: Ndị inyom tụrụ ǹgòǹgò mgbe nwa ọhụrụ mụrụ.
examples.english: The women rejoiced when the new baby was born.

examples.igbo: Tụọ ǹgòǹgò, nwa anyị alọtala!
examples.english: Rejoice, our child has returned!

examples.igbo: Akụkụ abụọ nke tebụl ahụ ràrà ǹràmanya.
examples.english: The two sides of that table are equal.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ na ha abụọ ràrà ǹràmanya?
examples.english: Are the two of them equal?

note: The verb 'rà ǹràmanya' is known but its everyday use is limited.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-akwe ọnụ maka ego azụ ahụ.
examples.english: We are bargaining over the price of that fish.

examples.igbo: Kwe ọnụ tupu i zụta ya.
examples.english: Bargain before you buy it.

gloss: (literally beater of clothes) a club-like wooden instrument shaped like a short pestle and used by native washermen in place of an iron in smoothing thick heavy native clothes

examples.igbo: O ji ǹti àkwà na-akụ akwa ya.
examples.english: She uses a clothes beater to beat her cloth.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ǹti àkwà m n'ụlọ ịsa akwa?
examples.english: Did you see my clothes beater in the washing room?

gloss: percussion instrument designed like a closed basket with a flat bottom filled with small particles

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-akụ ọshà n'ememme.
examples.english: The children play the ọshà at the festival.

examples.igbo: Kụọ ọshà ka anyị bido egwu.
examples.english: Play the ọshà so we can begin the dance.

examples.igbo: Ndị agha busoro obodo anyị agha.
examples.english: The soldiers waged war against our town.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ha ji buso nwanne ha agha?
examples.english: Why did they wage war against their brother?

examples.igbo: O nwere efe ịga ahịa taa.
examples.english: He has a chance to go to the market today.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere efe ịbịa echi?
examples.english: Do you have a chance to come tomorrow?

gloss: a 3-4 feet wall usually used for defense during war

examples.igbo: Ha wuru ekpè gburugburu obodo ahụ.
examples.english: They built an ekpe wall around that town.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ekpè ha wuru n'ọnụ ụzọ obodo?
examples.english: Did you see the ekpe they built at the town gate?

gloss: pay a fine; levy a fine

examples.igbo: O raara nra maka ịbịa n'azụ oge.
examples.english: He paid a fine for coming late.

examples.igbo: Ọ raara nwa ya nra maka ịla azụ n'ụlọ akwụkwọ?
examples.english: Did he levy a fine on his child for being late to school?

examples.igbo: O mefiri ihe n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: He did wrong at school.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-emefie ihe ma ị ghara ige ntị?
examples.english: Will you do wrong if you do not listen?

gloss: cramp; numbness of part of body (compare tịtaǹgwèlè)

examples.igbo: Ụtanwaǹgwèlè jidere m n'ụkwụ mgbe m na-agba ọsọ.
examples.english: Cramp caught me in the leg while I was running.

examples.igbo: Gịnị na-akpata ụtanwaǹgwèlè n'aka gị?
examples.english: What causes cramp in your hand?

gloss: early hours of the morning, dawn

examples.igbo: O ji n'ọnụụ̄tụ̄tụ̀ pụọ ịga ọrụ.
examples.english: He left at dawn to go to work.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ere nri n'ọnụụ̄tụ̄tụ̀?
examples.english: Do you sell food at dawn?

examples.igbo: O nafere mba ọzọ ịchọ ọrụ.
examples.english: He went abroad to look for work.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-nafe mba ọzọ mgbe ị gụsịrị akwụkwọ?
examples.english: Will you go abroad after you finish school?

examples.igbo: Òtu àbànì dì egwù wakporo obodo anyị n'abalị.
examples.english: A gang of bandits attacked our town at night.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ òtu àbànì dì egwù n'okporo ụzọ?
examples.english: Did you see a gang of bandits on the road?

examples.igbo: Tọọ eriri eke ahụ.
examples.english: Untie that rope.

examples.igbo: Ị tọrọ akpa osikapa ahụ?
examples.english: Did you untie that bag of rice?

examples.igbo: O lere ọkụkọ ya afịa ọkshòm.
examples.english: He auctioned his chicken.

examples.igbo: Ị lere akwa gị afịa ọkshòm?
examples.english: Did you auction your cloth?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-atị ụkwụ ya mgbe ọ tetara.
examples.english: He stretches his leg when he wakes.

examples.igbo: Tịa eriri a ka ọ dị ogologo.
examples.english: Stretch this rope so that it is long.

examples.igbo: Azụtara m obì akwà abụọ n'ahịa.
examples.english: I bought two yards of cloth at the market.

examples.igbo: Ego ole ka obì akwà a na-eri?
examples.english: How much does this yard of cloth cost?

gloss: an appeal of a case in a higher court

examples.igbo: O gbara mkpegharị n'ụlọikpe elu.
examples.english: He filed an appeal in the higher court.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-agba mkpegharị n'ụlọikpe elu?
examples.english: Will you file an appeal in the higher court?

gloss: press, rub hard so as to break into pieces; crush with hand or foot

examples.igbo: Filia ose a maka ofe.
examples.english: Crush this pepper for the soup.

examples.igbo: O filìrì mkpụrụ osisi ahụ n'ụkwụ.
examples.english: He crushed that fruit seed with his foot.

examples.igbo: Òtị dị n'ime ji ahụ.
examples.english: There is a grub in that yam.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ òtị n'ime osisi a?
examples.english: Did you see a grub in this wood?

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka mere mmebì n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: The children made a mess in the room.

examples.igbo: Ònye kpatara mmebì a?
examples.english: Who caused this mess?

examples.igbo: Akwụkọ a ga-alo elo n'oge ọkọchị.
examples.english: This umbrella will be useful in the dry season.

examples.igbo: Olee ihe ga-alo elo n'ubi a?
examples.english: What will be useful on this farm?

note: The exact modern usage and inflection of -lo elo are uncertain to me.

examples.igbo: Nnụnụ ahụ fefuru n'elu osisi.
examples.english: That bird flew away out of sight above the tree.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ka ụgbọ elu ahụ fefuru?
examples.english: Did you see how the plane flew away out of sight?

gloss: take a person or pet home, especially because the person can't go alone

examples.igbo: Kpọla nwa gị gaa n'ụlọ.
examples.english: Take your child home.

examples.igbo: O kpọlara agadi nwanyị ahụ laa.
examples.english: He took that old woman home.

examples.igbo: Dozi akwụkwọ gị n'akpa.
examples.english: Keep your books in the bag.

examples.igbo: O doziri ubi ya nke ọma.
examples.english: He kept his farm well.

examples.igbo: Biko gbaghàlụ m.
examples.english: Please forgive me.

examples.igbo: Gbaghàlụ ya, ọ bụ naanị nwata.
examples.english: Leave him alone, he is only a child.

examples.igbo: Òke batara n'ime ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: A rat entered our house.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ òke n'okpuru àkwà?
examples.english: Did you see a rat under the bed?

examples.igbo: Anyị ga-eje n'iru n'okporo ụzọ a.
examples.english: We will go forward on this road.

examples.igbo: Jee n'iru, m na-eso gị.
examples.english: Go in front, I am following you.

examples.igbo: Mama na-akwọmù ose n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: Mother is grinding pepper in the morning.

examples.igbo: Kwọmù ọka a nke ọma.
examples.english: Grind this corn well.

note: The verb is uncommon; the inflected forms are plausible but I am not fully certain of everyday usage.

examples.igbo: Nwa mkpùkpù mmē na-ebe akwa n'abalị.
examples.english: The newborn infant cries at night.

examples.igbo: Ònye na-elekọta nwa mkpùkpù mmē?
examples.english: Who is caring for the newborn infant?

examples.igbo: O nyere m ùkwù naàbò maka akpụ.
examples.english: He gave me 120 cowries for cassava.

examples.igbo: Ùkwù naàbò zụtara ọtụtụ ihe n'ahịa.
examples.english: 120 cowries bought many things in the market.

note: This is a historical currency phrase; examples are plausible but the context is old.

examples.igbo: Atọfuru m ego n'ahịa.
examples.english: I lost money at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị tọfuru igodo ụlọ?
examples.english: Did you lose the house key?

examples.igbo: O jiri nkwukwù akā tie ya.
examples.english: He hit him with a fist.

examples.igbo: Nkwukwù akā ya dị ike.
examples.english: His fist is strong.

examples.igbo: Ìgwè atụlū na-ata ahịhịa n'ubi.
examples.english: The flock of sheep is grazing in the field.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ìgwè atụlū n'ụzọ?
examples.english: Did you see a flock of sheep on the road?

examples.igbo: Mmiri lukpùrù nwa ahụ n'ime osimiri.
examples.english: Water drowned that child inside the river.

examples.igbo: Dọọ mmiri ahụ ka ọ ghara ilukpù.
examples.english: Hold that water so it doesn't overflow.

examples.igbo: Agwọ nta na-akpụghalị n'ala ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: A small snake is creeping on the floor of our house.

examples.igbo: Kpụghalịa nwayọ n'ime ụlọ ka nwa ahụ ghara ịmụ anya.
examples.english: Creep slowly in the house so the child doesn't wake up.

note: Not fully certain about the imperative form 'Kpụghalịa'.

examples.igbo: Nụù bụ ụlọ m, ọ bụ ebe m bi.
examples.english: That yonder is my house, it is where I live.

examples.igbo: Lee nụù, ọ bụ ugbo ala anyị na-akwọ.
examples.english: Look at that yonder, it is our car that we are driving.

note: Unsure how common 'nụù' is in modern speech.

examples.igbo: Agwọ ahụ na-akpụgharị n'okpuru akwụkwọ n'ime ọhịa.
examples.english: That snake is wriggling under the leaves in the forest.

examples.igbo: Kpụgharịa nwayọ ka ị ghara imerụ ya.
examples.english: Creep slowly so you don't hurt it.

note: Not fully certain about the imperative form 'Kpụgharịa'.

gloss: for the sake of; because of

examples.igbo: Màkà ifì nwa ya, ọ rụrụ ọrụ ike.
examples.english: For the sake of her child, she worked hard.

examples.igbo: Ị na-arụ ọrụ màkà ifì gịnị?
examples.english: Are you working for the sake of what?

examples.igbo: Ọrịa ahụ gbakasịrị ya ahụ niile.
examples.english: That disease made spots on his whole body.

examples.igbo: Ọ gbakasịrị ahụ ya niile ka ọ na-egwu egwu?
examples.english: Did it make spots on his whole body while he was playing?

note: Not entirely sure about the past tense form 'gbakasịrị'.

gloss: exclamatory shout to frighten, call attention

examples.igbo: Yaà! Pụọ n'ebe ahụ, ọ dị ize ndụ!
examples.english: Yaà! Get out of there, it's dangerous!

examples.igbo: Yaà! Bịa ebe a ngwa ngwa!
examples.english: Yaà! Come here quickly!

examples.igbo: Ọ bụrụ ọnū n'ebe nwa ya nọ.
examples.english: She cursed at her child.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka ọ bụọ gị ọnū.
examples.english: Don't let him curse you.

gloss: obscure; move across and cover (as clouds the sun)

examples.igbo: Ojiji gbakpùrù anyanwụ n'ehihie taa dum.
examples.english: Clouds covered the sun all this afternoon.

examples.igbo: Igwe ojii na-agbakpù anyanwụ ugbu a?
examples.english: Are clouds covering the sun now?

note: Not fully certain about the continuous form 'na-agbakpù'.

examples.igbo: Nchọpụ̀tā ya gbasara ọrịa ahụ dị mkpa.
examples.english: His research about that disease is important.

examples.igbo: Ị mere nchọpụ̀tā ọ bụla n'afọ a?
examples.english: Did you do any research this year?

gloss: offer kolanuts to the ancestors or deities

examples.igbo: Nna m na-agọ ọjị n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: My father offers kola in the morning.

examples.igbo: Gọọ ọjị tupu anyị erie nri.
examples.english: Offer kola before we eat.

examples.igbo: Anyị tụtụrụ ọjì maka ewu.
examples.english: We picked iroko leaves for the goat.

examples.igbo: Tụtụọ ọjì maka ewu.
examples.english: Pick iroko leaves for the goat.

note: Rare term; examples follow the given sense.

examples.igbo: Ọ fịghalịrị eriri ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: He twisted that rope well.

examples.igbo: Fịghalịa akwa ahụ, ọ ka mmiri mmiri.
examples.english: Wring that cloth, it is still wet.

examples.igbo: Afọ òbàlà na-egbu ụmụaka n'oge ọkọchị.
examples.english: Dysentery kills children in the dry season.

examples.igbo: Kpọga nwa ahụ ụlọ ọgwụ, o nwere afọ òbàlà.
examples.english: Take that child to the hospital, he has dysentery.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-agba àzị ụtụtụ tupu anyị aga ọrụ.
examples.english: We take breakfast before we go to work.

examples.igbo: Gbaa àzị ụtụtụ, anyị ga-aga ahịa.
examples.english: Take breakfast, we will go to the market.

note: Phrase is idiomatic but less common in some areas.

examples.igbo: Ha kpokọtara ji n'òòbò n'azụ ụlọ.
examples.english: They gathered yams into a heap behind the house.

examples.igbo: Òòbò ji ahụ dị elu.
examples.english: That heap of yams is high.

note: Shortened form; examples follow the given sense.

gloss: round-shaped mass (of mud); cassava balls (from -kpụ 2. mould)

examples.igbo: Ọ kpụrụ òkpụkpụ ụrọ maka ịrụ ụlọ.
examples.english: He moulded a round mass of mud for building.

examples.igbo: Nne m na-akpụ òkpụkpụ akpụ.
examples.english: My mother is moulding cassava balls.

note: Examples cover the mud-mass and cassava-ball senses.

gloss: propitiate a deity for a broken taboo

examples.igbo: O jùrụ àrụ maka mmehie ya.
examples.english: He propitiated the deity for his sin.

examples.igbo: Jụọ àrụ maka mmehie gị.
examples.english: Propitiate the deity for your sin.

note: Ritual term; usage is based on the given sense.

examples.igbo: Nsọkwù ya mere ka anyị chịa ọchị.
examples.english: His awkwardness made us laugh.

examples.igbo: Emela nsọkwù n'ihu ndị ọzọ.
examples.english: Do not act foolishly in front of others.

examples.igbo: Àpàlì na-arị n'osisi dị n'ọhịa.
examples.english: The climbing fibre plant climbs on trees in the forest.

examples.igbo: Were àpàlì kee osisi ahụ.
examples.english: Use the climbing fibre plant to tie that tree.

note: Plant name; examples follow the given sense.

examples.igbo: Dọkịta gwọrọ ọyà nwa m n'ụlọ ọgwụ.
examples.english: The doctor cured my child's illness at the hospital.

examples.igbo: Kedu ọgwụ ga-agwọ ọyà a?
examples.english: Which medicine will cure this illness?

gloss: young palm-fronds; central spike of young raphia or oil palm (See Anyanwu, C.N. 'The uses of the ọmụ in Igbo culture'. Odenigbo 2.42-6, 1977)

examples.igbo: Pụta gbutuo òmụ n'osisi nkwụ ahụ.
examples.english: Go out and cut the young fronds from that palm tree.

examples.igbo: Òmụ ọhụrụ na-esi n'isi nkwụ apụta.
examples.english: New young fronds come out from the top of the palm.

note: òmụ is a specialist term; sentences are kept to the literal botanical sense.

examples.igbo: Ọ kwechiri na ya ga-akwụ ụgwọ ahụ taa.
examples.english: He insisted that he would pay that debt today.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji kwechi okwu a otú a?
examples.english: Why are you insisting on this matter like this?

examples.igbo: E nwere ji oru nà àbụa n'ọba ya.
examples.english: There are twenty-two yams in his barn.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara ọkụkọ oru nà àbụa n'ahịa?
examples.english: Did you buy twenty-two chickens at the market?

note: Vigesimal form; written as given, though iri abụọ na abụọ is the more common modern form.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ onye ọsi alị n'okwu ahụ.
examples.english: He was a witness in that case.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-abụ onye ọsi alị n'ụlọ ikpe echi?
examples.english: Will you be a witness in court tomorrow?

note: Tone marks on ọsi alị follow the entry form.

examples.igbo: Zìgota m akwụkwọ ahụ ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Send that book up to me quickly.

examples.igbo: Ọ zìgọtara m ego ahụ n'ụlọ ọrụ.
examples.english: He sent that money up to me at the office.

note: Past form written zìgọtara to match the -ta/-sịgota stem.

examples.igbo: Tọsịsị eriri ndị a niile.
examples.english: Untie all these ropes.

examples.igbo: Ọ tọsịsịrị eriri ji niile n'ọba.
examples.english: She untied all the ropes tying the yams in the barn.

note: Plural-object stem; past form tọsịsịrị.

gloss: respectful form of address to women

examples.igbo: Òme ākwụ, nnọọ n'ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: Madam, welcome to our house.

examples.igbo: Òme ākwụ, kedu ka ahụ dị gị?
examples.english: Madam, how are you feeling?

note: Used as a term of address, as the gloss specifies.

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ ji dòtị gbaa nnụnụ.
examples.english: That child used a catapult to shoot a bird.

examples.igbo: Olee ebe i tinyere dòtị m?
examples.english: Where did you put my catapult?

examples.igbo: Ị na-eli ngọ n'ọrụ gị?
examples.english: Do you accept bribes at your work?

examples.igbo: Onye uwe ojii liri ngọ n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: The policeman took a bribe on the road.

examples.igbo: Onyearị̀rịọ ahụ nọ n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: That beggar is on the road.

examples.igbo: Nye onyearị̀rịọ ahụ mmiri.
examples.english: Give that beggar water.

gloss: write; mark letters, symbols, or numbers on a surface, especially using a pen or stick

examples.igbo: Dee aha gị n'akwụkwọ.
examples.english: Write your name on the paper.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ede akwụkwọ ozi.
examples.english: She is writing a letter.

examples.igbo: Ọ kpọrọ anyị n'ètitiàbàlị̀.
examples.english: He called us at midnight.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eme mkpotu n'ètitiàbàlị̀?
examples.english: Are you making noise at midnight?

examples.igbo: Kpụdaa ọkọlọtọ ahụ.
examples.english: Pull down that flag.

examples.igbo: O kpụdara igbe ahụ n'osisi.
examples.english: He pulled the box down from the tree.

examples.igbo: Ìzùgà ahụ na-ekwu okwu nzuzu.
examples.english: That fool is talking nonsense.

examples.igbo: Ị bụ ìzùgà?
examples.english: Are you a fool?

gloss: soup prepared with okra, or ọgbọnọ, or both

examples.igbo: Anyị riri ofe onịnọ n'abalị ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: We ate ofe onịnọ last night.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-esi ofe onịnọ taa?
examples.english: Will you cook ofe onịnọ today?

examples.igbo: Ògba egwu ahụ na-agba egwu nke ọma.
examples.english: That dancer dances well.

examples.igbo: Ị bụ ògba egwu?
examples.english: Are you a dancer?

gloss: taking a snap shot, taking photograph

examples.igbo: Nsere foto na-amasị ya.
examples.english: He likes taking photos.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eme nsere foto?
examples.english: Are you taking photos?

examples.igbo: O na-ebo m iru.
examples.english: He is staring at me.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji na-ebo m iru?
examples.english: Why are you staring at me?

examples.igbo: Ndị uwe ojii gbasara ìgwè mmadụ ahụ.
examples.english: The police dispersed that crowd.

examples.igbo: Gbasaa ụmụaka ahụ, ha na-eme mkpọtụ.
examples.english: Dismiss those children, they are making noise.

gloss: roll up (of an object that rolls)

examples.igbo: Bọọlụ ahụ kpọlègọtara n'ụkwụ m.
examples.english: The ball rolled up to my foot.

examples.igbo: Kpọlègota bọọlụ ahụ n'ebe a.
examples.english: Roll the ball up here.

note: The stem's exact inflection is uncertain; I used kpọlègọtara/-gota as the usual form for motion towards the speaker.

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ na-arụ ọrụ n'ugbo.
examples.english: That man is working on the farm.

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ ọ bụ nwanne gị?
examples.english: Is that man your brother?

gloss: to loose appetite or interest; get tired of something or someone

examples.igbo: Afọ gbụrụ ya nri a.
examples.english: He has lost his appetite for this food.

examples.igbo: Egwu a gbụrụ m, agaghị m ege ya ọzọ.
examples.english: I am tired of this song, I will not listen to it again.

note: The sense is expressed idiomatically with afọ gbụrụ mmadụ; a second frame with a non-food object is less common.

examples.igbo: O jiri ike bọhe ọnụ ụzọ ahụ.
examples.english: He forced the door open with force.

examples.igbo: Bọhee ọnụ gị ka m hụ ezé gị.
examples.english: Open your mouth wide so I can see your teeth.

note: The verb form bọhe/bọhee is not fully familiar to me; the sentences follow the usual pattern for verbs of opening.

gloss: the rulers; members of the government

examples.igbo: Ndị na-achị achị kwuru okwu n'obodo anyị.
examples.english: The rulers spoke in our town.

examples.igbo: Ndị na-achị achị ọ na-enyere ndị ogbenye aka?
examples.english: Do the rulers help the poor?

examples.igbo: O nwere mgbaaka ọnà ọcha.
examples.english: She has a silver bracelet.

examples.igbo: Ọnà ọcha dị oke ọnụ ugbu a.
examples.english: Silver is very expensive now.

examples.igbo: Ebe niine dị mmiri mmiri mgbe mmiri zọsịrị.
examples.english: Everywhere was wet after the rain fell.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-achọ akwụkwọ ya ebe niine.
examples.english: He looks for his book everywhere.

examples.igbo: Ọ dara n'osisi wee nweta mmejọ n'ụkwụ ya.
examples.english: He fell from a tree and got an injury on his leg.

examples.igbo: Mmejọ ahụ ọ ka na-egbu gị?
examples.english: Does that injury still hurt you?

examples.igbo: Ọ jetera aka n'obodo ọzọ ịchọ ọrụ.
examples.english: He went far away to another town to look for work.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji jete aka otú a?
examples.english: Why did you go so far away like this?

note: The stem jete aka is uncommon; the inflected forms used here are my best reading of it.

examples.igbo: Ọ nọ na-atụ òlù ụla n'oche ya.
examples.english: He is dozing on his chair.

examples.igbo: Atụla òlù ụla n'oge ọrụ!
examples.english: Don't doze during work!

note: The idiom òlù ụla tụ is familiar; the exact tone pattern of òlù ụla may vary by speaker.

examples.igbo: Nwa m na-asa àrụ ugbu a.
examples.english: My child is taking a bath now.

examples.igbo: Saa àrụ gị, anyị ga-aga ahịa.
examples.english: Take your bath, we are going to the market.

examples.igbo: Ụgbọelu ahụ fefere osimiri ahụ.
examples.english: That aeroplane flew across that river.

examples.igbo: Nnụnụ ahụ ọ na-efefe n'elu osimiri?
examples.english: Is that bird flying across the river?

note: fefe is treated here as a verb 'fly across'; the stem form without a hyphen is unusual.

gloss: cheat; unlawfully use part of another's time in attending to one's needs (e.g. as a clerk who secretly fills in football coupons in the office); do petty job as a sideline

examples.igbo: Ndị odeakwụkwọ ụfọdụ na-achị jọọbù n'oge ọrụ.
examples.english: Some clerks do a sideline during working hours.

examples.igbo: Ị na-achị jọọbù n'oge ọrụ gị?
examples.english: Do you do a sideline during your working hours?

note: The compound chì jọòbù is colloquial; wording of the definition varies, but the sense of a work-time sideline is clear.

examples.igbo: Ha ji ìkpo see ofe taa.
examples.english: They used ìkpo fish to cook soup today.

examples.igbo: Ìkpo dị n'ahịa taa?
examples.english: Is ìkpo fish in the market today?

note: ìkpo is a fish name; which species it names is uncertain, so the sentences keep the reference generic.

examples.igbo: Gụọ ha: isii, naasaa, naasatọ, naitoolu, iri.
examples.english: Count them: six, seven, eight, nine, ten.

examples.igbo: Ị maara na naasaa na-esote isii?
examples.english: Do you know that seven comes after six?

note: naasaa is the counting/qualifying form used in the sequence after isii; it is not the ordinary numeral asaa.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka bụkọtara mkpụrụ osisi ahụ niile.
examples.english: The children scrambled and got all those fruits.

examples.igbo: Ị bụkọtara ha niile?
examples.english: Did you scramble and get all of them?

note: -bụkọ is a rare verb; the inflected forms bụkọtara/bụkọta are given as the natural perfectives.

gloss: take piece of yam, etc., from among many and eat; take stew or soup with morsel or piece of food

examples.igbo: Ọ na-asulu ofe ahụ ugbu a.
examples.english: He is taking that soup with a morsel right now.

examples.igbo: Suluo ji a tupu ọ jụọ oyi.
examples.english: Take a piece of this yam before it gets cold.

note: -sulu is a rare verb; the imperative suluo and progressive na-asulu are my best reading of its inflection.

examples.igbo: Nna m kụziri nwa ọlū otú e si akpụ nkụ.
examples.english: My father taught the apprentice how to cut firewood.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ nwa ọlū m n'ụlọ ahịa?
examples.english: Did you see my apprentice in the shop?

examples.igbo: O ji waya jikọọ igwe ahụ.
examples.english: He used wire to connect that machine.

examples.igbo: Jikọọ waya ndị a ọnụ.
examples.english: Connect these wires together.

gloss: import; bring in from a foreign country most especially goods and services

examples.igbo: Ụlọ ọrụ ahụ na-ebubata ngwa ọrụ si mba ọzọ.
examples.english: The company imports tools from abroad.

examples.igbo: Onye na-ebubata osikapa n'ahịa a?
examples.english: Who imports rice in this market?

gloss: put down a load from head or arms; lay down a load

examples.igbo: O ziri ibu ya n'ala were zu ike.
examples.english: He put down his load on the ground and rested.

examples.igbo: Zi ibu gị, anyị ezuola ike.
examples.english: Put down your load, we have rested enough.

gloss: be curious, inquisitive Ị nā-enyòchataka You are too inquisitive

examples.igbo: Nwata a na-enyòchata ihe niile.
examples.english: This child is inquisitive about everything.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji na-enyòchata okwu ndị okenye?
examples.english: Why are you inquisitive about adults' matters?

examples.igbo: O ji eriri gado osisi abụọ ahụ ọnụ.
examples.english: He used rope to hold the two sticks together.

examples.igbo: Gado osisi ndị a ọnụ ka ha ghara ịdapụ.
examples.english: Hold these sticks together so they do not fall.

note: gado is uncommon; examples follow the given sense of holding together.

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ na-enwe ifelē mgbe ọ na-ekwu okwu.
examples.english: That child is shy when speaking.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji enwe ifelē n'ihu ndị ọbịa?
examples.english: Why are you shy in front of guests?

gloss: wild or green amaranth (Amaranthus lividus Linn. and A. viridis Linn.)

examples.igbo: Anyị na-ata ìnìne mmee na nri.
examples.english: We eat wild amaranth with food.

examples.igbo: Ị kụrụ ìnìne mmee n'ubi?
examples.english: Did you plant wild amaranth in the farm?

gloss: play a string musical instrument; play a guitar

examples.igbo: Nna m na-akpọ ụ̄bọ̄ n'ụlọ.
examples.english: My father plays guitar at home.

examples.igbo: Kpọọ ụ̄bọ̄ ahụ ka anyị gee ntị.
examples.english: Play that guitar so we can listen.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-egbu ya ugwùlùgwù.
examples.english: His chest hurts him.

examples.igbo: Ọ dị ihe na-egbu gị n'ugwùlùgwù?
examples.english: Is something hurting you in the chest?

examples.igbo: Ọ pịrị mkpịsị odee ya.
examples.english: He sharpened his pencil.

examples.igbo: Pịa osisi a ka ọ dị nkọ.
examples.english: Sharpen this stick so it is sharp.

examples.igbo: Ọ megidere atụmatụ ahụ.
examples.english: He was against that plan.

examples.igbo: Ị na-emegide ihe anyị kwuru?
examples.english: Are you against what we said?

note: Examples use the inflected form megide, which contains the stem -gide.

examples.igbo: Afọ na-adụ ya adụ n'ụgbọala.
examples.english: He feels like retching in the vehicle.

examples.igbo: Ị na-adụ adụ mgbe ị nụrụ isi ya?
examples.english: Do you retch when you smell it?

gloss: colour something by soaking it in a solution mixed with a dye; dye; dye black

examples.igbo: O siji uwe ahụ na mmiri ojii.
examples.english: She dyed that cloth in black water.

examples.igbo: Siji akwa ọcha a ka ọ ghọọ oji.
examples.english: Dye this white cloth so it turns black.

gloss: gather sand, dust; play in and with the sand (of children)

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-akpo uzuzu n'ama.
examples.english: The children are playing with sand in the compound.

examples.igbo: Kpọọ uzuzu ahụ niile mee otu ebe.
examples.english: Gather all that sand together in one place.

examples.igbo: Bọọlụ ahụ kpọlèdà site n'elu ugwu.
examples.english: The ball rolled down from the hill.

examples.igbo: Kpọlèdà ya n'ugwu.
examples.english: Roll it down the hill.

note: I am not fully certain of the inflection and exact usage of -kpọlèdà; the examples use the form as given.

gloss: be well-grown; have more than average height

examples.igbo: Nwa ya etopụla ogologo.
examples.english: Her child has grown tall.

examples.igbo: Ọ topụrụ nwanne ya elu?
examples.english: Is he taller than his sibling?

gloss: a pithy speech, in form of a short story, that advises or states a general truth

examples.igbo: Nne m kọrọ anyị otu ụkàbụilu banyere ọrụ ugbo.
examples.english: My mother told us a pithy tale about farming.

examples.igbo: Ị mụtara ihe ọ bụla n'ụkàbụilu a?
examples.english: Did you learn anything from this pithy tale?

examples.igbo: Ọ nụfìèrè aha m.
examples.english: He misheard my name.

examples.igbo: Ị nụfìèrè ihe m kwuru?
examples.english: Did you mishear what I said?

examples.igbo: Ha liri òlili n'ụbọchị agbamakwụkwọ.
examples.english: They had a feast on the wedding day.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eli òlili n'ụlọ gị?
examples.english: Will you have a feast in your house?

examples.igbo: Ọ dàrà ùbìàm mgbe ọ tụfuru ọrụ ya.
examples.english: He became poor when he lost his job.

examples.igbo: Ndị dàrà ùbìàm na-achọ enyemaka.
examples.english: Those who became poor are looking for help.

examples.igbo: Doolu àrụ ànì, ihe ga-adị mma.
examples.english: Take things easy, things will be fine.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-adolu àrụ ànì kama ọ na-ewe iwe.
examples.english: He takes things easy instead of getting angry.

examples.igbo: Nkèji ụkwū ya gbajiri n'egwuregwu.
examples.english: His ankle broke in the game.

examples.igbo: Ị na-enwe mgbu nkèji ụkwū?
examples.english: Do you have ankle pain?

examples.igbo: Ọ kpèchara nwanne ya n'ihu ndị mmadụ.
examples.english: He slandered his brother before people.

examples.igbo: Akpèchala mmadụ n'okwu ụgha.
examples.english: Don't slander someone with lies.

examples.igbo: Ndị uwe ojii sùpùrù égbè n'ikuku.
examples.english: The police fired guns into the air.

examples.igbo: Ị sùpùrù égbè n'abalị?
examples.english: Did you fire a gun at night?

gloss: overwhelm, swallow up (of water, mud, etc.)

examples.igbo: Oke mmiri likpùrù ubi anyị.
examples.english: The flood swallowed our farm.

examples.igbo: Ụrọ na-alikpù ụkwụ anyị n'oge mmiri.
examples.english: Mud overwhelms our feet in the rainy season.

examples.igbo: Mpụ̀tàrà okwu ya bụ na ọ ga-ahapụ ọrụ.
examples.english: The implication of his words is that he will leave the job.

examples.igbo: Gịnị bụ mpụ̀tàrà nke a?
examples.english: What is the meaning of this?

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-amìlị ara nne ya.
examples.english: The baby is sucking its mother's breast.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka ọ mìlị mkpịsị aka ya.
examples.english: Don't let him suck his finger.

examples.igbo: Ikèì ahụ na-eje ije nwayọ.
examples.english: That old man walks slowly.

examples.igbo: Ị maara ikèì ahụ bi n'ụlọ ahụ?
examples.english: Do you know the old man living in that house?

examples.igbo: Òra mmadù chọrọ ka gọọmentị rụọ ụzọ.
examples.english: The public wants the government to build roads.

examples.igbo: Gịnị ka òra mmadù na-ekwu?
examples.english: What are the people saying?

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ nwere ọnụ, ọ na-ekwu okwu mgbe niile.
examples.english: That child is talkative; he talks all the time.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere ọnụ, gịnị mere i ji ekwu okwu na nnọkọ?
examples.english: You are talkative; why do you talk at gatherings?

examples.igbo: O tiri akụ ole na ole n’aka ya.
examples.english: He cracked a few kernels in his hand.

examples.igbo: Tịa akụ ndị a ka anyị rie ha.
examples.english: Crack these kernels so we can eat them.

examples.igbo: Nne nne ya mere àgadị, ọ na-eje nwayọ nwayọ.
examples.english: His grandmother became decrepit; she walks slowly.

examples.igbo: Ị mere àgadị, ị ga-ebu ibu a?
examples.english: You are decrepit; will you carry this load?

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ tozuru etozu, ọ na-eme mkpebi nke ya.
examples.english: That child is mature; he makes his own decisions.

examples.igbo: Tozuo etozu tupu i lụọ di.
examples.english: Be mature before you marry.

examples.igbo: O gwoo ọgwụ maka nwa ya.
examples.english: He prepared medicine for his child.

examples.igbo: Gwoo ọgwụ a ngwa ngwa, nwa m na-arịa.
examples.english: Prepare this medicine quickly; my child is sick.

gloss: bear a name; answer to one's name

examples.igbo: O zara ahà ya mgbe a kpọrọ ya.
examples.english: He answered to his name when he was called.

examples.igbo: Zaa ahà gị mgbe a kpọrọ gị.
examples.english: Answer your name when you are called.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ gbọpụrụ mmiri ara ehi niile.
examples.english: The child vomited out all the milk.

examples.igbo: Ị gbọpụrụ nri ahụ niile?
examples.english: Did you vomit out all that food?

examples.igbo: Anyị rutere n’ǹdèelī, obodo dị jụụ.
examples.english: We arrived at midnight; the town was quiet.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-ala n’ǹdèelī?
examples.english: Will you return at midnight?

gloss: to force one's way through a small doorway, small opening in wall, thicket

examples.igbo: O pio n’ọnụ ụzọ dị warara.
examples.english: He forced his way through the narrow doorway.

examples.igbo: Pio n’oghere ahụ ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Force your way through that hole quickly.

note: pio is uncommon; examples follow the given sense but usage may vary.

examples.igbo: Ọ chọrọ ịkàgha oche ahụ mebiri emebi.
examples.english: He wants to fix that broken chair again.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-akàgha nzukọ ahụ ruo echi?
examples.english: Will you postpone that meeting until tomorrow?

note: Inflection of -kàgha is somewhat uncertain.

examples.igbo: Nne m na-ehi ụra n’imelìme ụnò.
examples.english: My mother sleeps in the inner room.

examples.igbo: Kpọọ ya bata n’imelìme ụnò.
examples.english: Call him into the inner room.

examples.igbo: Kwakọba akwụkwọ ndị a n’ime igbe.
examples.english: Gather these books into the box.

examples.igbo: Ha na-ekwakọba ọka ha n’ọba.
examples.english: They are gathering their corn into the barn.

examples.igbo: Ọ tụfèrè otu ụkwụ ya n’elu ibe ya.
examples.english: He crossed one leg over the other.

examples.igbo: Ị na-atụfega ụkwụ n’oge nzukọ?
examples.english: Do you cross your legs during the meeting?

examples.igbo: Gụda akwụkwọ a tupu ị zaa.
examples.english: Read through this book before you answer.

examples.igbo: Ọ gụdara akwụkwọ ozi ahụ ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: He read through that letter quickly.

examples.igbo: Mmiri na-atụ pọm n’elu ụlọ.
examples.english: Water is dripping from the roof.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-atụ pọm n’imi ya.
examples.english: It is dripping from his nose.

gloss: one known but never fully (praise-name of God)

examples.igbo: Ndị Kraịst na-akpọ Chineke Àmà-àma-amāsị-amasị.
examples.english: Christians call God Àmà-àma-amāsị-amasị.

examples.igbo: Àmà-àma-amāsị-amasị bụ aha otito Chineke.
examples.english: Àmà-àma-amāsị-amasị is a praise name of God.

examples.igbo: Dọkịta lere nwantaǹta anyā ya.
examples.english: The doctor examined the pupil of his eye.

examples.igbo: Nwantaǹta anyā na-agbasa n’ìhè.
examples.english: The pupil dilates in light.

examples.igbo: O nwetara nturuùgò maka ọrụ ya.
examples.english: He received an award for his work.

examples.igbo: E nyere ya nturuùgò n’ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: They gave him an award at school.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka abụọ a bụ ejima.
examples.english: These two children are twins.

examples.igbo: Ị ma na ha bụ ejima?
examples.english: Did you know they are twins?

examples.igbo: Ọ nụrụ nwunyè mgbe ọ dị afọ iri atọ.
examples.english: He married when he was thirty.

examples.igbo: Olee mgbe ị ga-anụ nwunyè?
examples.english: When will you marry?

examples.igbo: Ijiji na-efebà n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: Flies are flying into the house.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka ijiji febà n'ihe oriri.
examples.english: Don't let flies fly into the food.

gloss: explain and set up new codes of ritual and political behaviour (especially of Nri man)

examples.igbo: Okenye Nri ahụ kọwara òdìnàànì obodo ha.
examples.english: That Nri elder explained and set up the codes of their town.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-akọwa òdìnàànì ebe a?
examples.english: Will you explain and set up the codes here?

note: Specialized Nri usage; examples are constructed.

examples.igbo: Ìrùrù mmanụ na-eto n'elu mmiri ọdọ.
examples.english: Water lettuce grows on the surface of the pond water.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka hụrụ ìrùrù mmanụ n'ọdọ mmiri.
examples.english: The children saw water lettuce in the pond.

examples.igbo: Ọ dụrụ m akā n'azụ.
examples.english: He poked me in the back.

examples.igbo: Dụ ya akā n'ubu, ọ ga-echeta.
examples.english: Poke him on the shoulder, he will remember.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-eme àkàjà nwata ahụ.
examples.english: The children are mocking that child.

examples.igbo: Emela àkàjà n'ebe nwanne gị nọ.
examples.english: Don't mock your brother.

gloss: kind of edible frog with long hind legs

examples.igbo: Anyị jidere mbàla n'ọhịa.
examples.english: We caught a mbala frog in the bush.

examples.igbo: Ị riri mbàla ahụ nne m siri?
examples.english: Did you eat that mbala frog my mother cooked?

examples.igbo: Ndị ọka ikpe kpebiri okwu ahụ.
examples.english: The judges concluded that case.

examples.igbo: Anyị ga-ekpebi okwu a taa.
examples.english: We will conclude this matter today.

examples.igbo: Nchara na-atagwu ígwè ahụ.
examples.english: Rust is eating away that metal.

examples.igbo: Gịnị na-atagwu akwụkwọ a?
examples.english: What is eating away this paper?

examples.igbo: Onye egwu ahụ na-akụ òjì.
examples.english: That musician is playing the drum.

examples.igbo: Ị nụrụ ụda òjì n'abalị?
examples.english: Did you hear the sound of the drum at night?

examples.igbo: Ụdọ tụnùrù n’ụkwụ ewu.
examples.english: The rope got entangled on the goat's leg.

examples.igbo: Lezie anya ka ụdọ ghara ịtụnù n’ụkwụ gị.
examples.english: Be careful so the rope does not get entangled on your leg.

examples.igbo: Ife mbụ m na-eme n’ụtụtụ bụ ịsa efere.
examples.english: The first thing I do in the morning is wash plates.

examples.igbo: Gịnị bụ ife mbụ anyị ga-azụ n’ahịa taa?
examples.english: What is the first thing we will buy in the market today?

examples.igbo: Ọ sekpùrù àlà n’ụlọ ụka kpee ekpere.
examples.english: She knelt down in church and prayed.

examples.igbo: Sekpụrụ àlà maka ekpere ụtụtụ.
examples.english: Kneel down for the morning prayer.

examples.igbo: Anyị riri èlèlè n’ahịa taa.
examples.english: We gained in the market today.

examples.igbo: Ị riri èlèlè n’ọrụ ugbo a?
examples.english: Did you gain in this farm work?

note: The idiom ri èlèlè is understood as gain/benefit, but usage may vary by dialect.

examples.igbo: Ùmì ọkpụkpụ ehi na-enye ahụ ike.
examples.english: Beef bone marrow gives the body strength.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ ịta ùmì ọkpụkpụ ewu?
examples.english: Do you want to chew goat bone marrow?

examples.igbo: Osisi ọka fịnwụrụ n’ihi ụkọ mmiri.
examples.english: The corn plant withered because of lack of water.

examples.igbo: Kwuo mmiri ka akwụkwọ ghara ịfịnwụ.
examples.english: Pour water so the leaves do not wither.

examples.igbo: Ha dọkọrọ eriri abụọ ahụ ọnụ.
examples.english: They pulled the two ropes together.

examples.igbo: Dọkọọ osisi ndị a ọnụ tupu anyị ebuo ha.
examples.english: Pull these logs together before we carry them.

note: The verb stem is less common; the forms used here are standard for pulling things together.

gloss: weighing; the process of measuring the weight of something

examples.igbo: Òsìsì ọka ahụ were ogologo oge.
examples.english: The weighing of that corn took a long time.

examples.igbo: Ebee ka òsìsì akpụ na-eme?
examples.english: Where is the weighing of cassava done?

examples.igbo: M gbudosara anya na ọ na-abịa.
examples.english: I observed that he is coming.

examples.igbo: Gbudo anya nke ọma tupu ị gafee okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: Observe carefully before you cross the road.

note: The inflected form gbudosara anya is idiomatic for observed/perceived, though usage can vary.

examples.igbo: Ụzò a na-aga ahịa dị warara.
examples.english: The road to the market is narrow.

examples.igbo: Olee ụzò anyị ga-esi gaa ugbo?
examples.english: Which way will we use to go to the farm?

examples.igbo: Tinye ntụpọ n'etiti abụọ na ise.
examples.english: Put the decimal point between two and five.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ntụpọ dị n'ọnụọgụ a?
examples.english: Do you see the decimal point in this number?

note: ntụpọ as 'decimal point' is modern school usage rather than everyday speech; the sentences are grammatical but a bit classroom-flavoured.

gloss: wear, tie wrapper; be dressed in wrapper

examples.igbo: Nne m mara ògòdò ọhụrụ gaa ahịa.
examples.english: My mother wore a new wrapper to the market.

examples.igbo: Mara ògòdò gị, anyị na-aga ahịa.
examples.english: Put on your wrapper, we are going to the market.

gloss: effect; cause; make to happen; bring about a reaction

examples.igbo: Oké ifufe kpatara mmebi n'ubi anyị.
examples.english: The strong wind caused damage on our farm.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara ọdịda ya n'ule ahụ?
examples.english: What caused his failure in that exam?

examples.igbo: Onye na-akpụ isi kpìchara isi m taa.
examples.english: The barber cut my hair very short today.

examples.igbo: Kpìcha isi gị tupu ị gaa oriri ahụ.
examples.english: Cut your hair very short before you go to that ceremony.

examples.igbo: Onye dibịa gbùrù òchi n'azụ ya.
examples.english: The native doctor cupped his back.

examples.igbo: Ha na-agbu òchi n'ahụ ndị ọrịa.
examples.english: They let blood on the patients' bodies.

examples.igbo: Nnụnụ bèdoro n'alaka osisi ahụ.
examples.english: The bird perched on the branch of that tree.

examples.igbo: Ebee ka ọkụkọ ahụ bèdoro?
examples.english: Where has that fowl perched?

examples.igbo: O ji àgà na akụ gaa ịchụ nta.
examples.english: He went hunting with a bow and arrows.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere àgà na akụ?
examples.english: Do you have a bow and arrows?

examples.igbo: Anyị lịrị ugwu ahụ n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: We climbed that hill in the morning.

examples.igbo: Lịa ugwu ahụ, ị ga-ahụ obodo ahụ niile.
examples.english: Climb that hill and you will see the whole town.

note: 'rị ugwu' is the more usual verb for climbing; 'lị ugwu' is kept as given.

examples.igbo: Òwụwụ akwa ahụ gwụrụ m ike.
examples.english: The washing of those clothes tired me out.

examples.igbo: Ị na-enyere mama aka n'òwụwụ akwa?
examples.english: Do you help mother with the washing of clothes?

examples.igbo: Ọ tụfèga bọọlụ n'ofe ụzọ ahụ.
examples.english: He threw the ball across that road.

examples.igbo: Tụfèga nkume ahụ n'ofe mmiri.
examples.english: Throw that stone across the river.

gloss: ring-worm of the head (literally barber who receives no pay)

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ nwere òkpụ isi eli ngo.
examples.english: That child has ringworm of the head.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eji ọgwụ agwọ òkpụ isi eli ngo?
examples.english: Are you using medicine to treat ringworm of the head?

note: Spelling of this phrase varies; examples use the common expanded form.

gloss: saw a piece of timber by pulling (this is usually done by two people -one in a pit across which the timber is laid, and the other at ground-level)

examples.igbo: Ha dọrọ mmà ọdū n'ogwe osisi ahụ.
examples.english: They pull-sawed that piece of timber.

examples.igbo: Otu nọ n'olulu, ibe ya n'elu, ha na-adọ mmà ọdū.
examples.english: One is in the pit, the other above, they are pull-sawing.

examples.igbo: Ọ kpụrụ àfụ̀ọnụ ya taa n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: He shaved his beard this morning.

examples.igbo: Kpụọ àfụ̀ọnụ gị tupu ị gaa ọrụ.
examples.english: Shave your beard before you go to work.

examples.igbo: Ọ dọrọ àrụ mgbe ọ rịasịrị ọrịa.
examples.english: He recuperated after he was sick.

examples.igbo: Nne m na-adọ àrụ n'ụlọ ugbu a.
examples.english: My mother is recuperating at home now.

examples.igbo: Ọ fiegburu ọkụkọ ahụ n'olu.
examples.english: He strangled that chicken by the neck.

examples.igbo: Efiegbula nnụnụ ahụ, hapụ ya ka ọ fee.
examples.english: Do not strangle that bird; let it fly.

gloss: be stronger than (literally hand to be greater than hand)

examples.igbo: Aka ya ka aka m n'ọrụ ubi.
examples.english: He is stronger than me in farm work.

examples.igbo: Aka gị ka aka ya n'ịgba ọsọ?
examples.english: Are you stronger than him in running?

gloss: the way or road or path is good

examples.igbo: Ụzọ dị mma, anyị ga-erute n'oge.
examples.english: The road is good; we will arrive on time.

examples.igbo: Ụzọ ọ dị mma n'oge mmiri?
examples.english: Is the road good in the rainy season?

note: Headword is written solid, but examples use the normal spaced phrase.

examples.igbo: Ọ dùgara nne ya gaa ahịa.
examples.english: He escorted his mother to the market.

examples.igbo: Dùga ụmụaka gaa ụlọ akwụkwọ taa.
examples.english: Lead the children to school today.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụrụ ọnụ mīli n'ala.
examples.english: He spat saliva on the ground.

examples.igbo: Bụọ ọnụ mīli n'èzí, ọ bụghị n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: Spit saliva outside, not inside the house.

examples.igbo: Òghùghò ihu igwe na-akpatakarị ọrịa n'oge mmiri.
examples.english: Weather change often causes illness in the rainy season.

examples.igbo: Ị hụla òghùghò ọ bụla n'ọnọdụ ahịa?
examples.english: Have you seen any change in the market situation?

note: òghùghò is less common than mgbanwe, but it is used for change/changing.

gloss: brother, sister (not of the same mother); relative; blood relation

examples.igbo: Nwa nnà m bịara n'ụlọ anyị ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: My relative came to our house yesterday.

examples.igbo: Ị ma nwa nnà gị nke ọma?
examples.english: Do you know your relative well?

examples.igbo: Walala nke ụzọ a na-egbochi ụgbọala ịgafe.
examples.english: The narrowness of this road prevents cars from passing.

examples.igbo: Walala nke ụzọ ahụ dị egwu.
examples.english: The narrowness of that road is terrible.

note: I am not certain walala is standard modern Igbo for narrowness; the usual expression is ịdị warara.

examples.igbo: M lafọrọ mmiri n'iko.
examples.english: I drank and left some water in the cup.

examples.igbo: Lafọọ mmanya ahụ, egbula ya niile.
examples.english: Drink and leave some of that wine, don't finish it all.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-egwuri egwu n'okporo ámá.
examples.english: Children are playing on the street.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ị ji echere n'okporo ámá?
examples.english: Why are you waiting on the street?

examples.igbo: Zụrọ m otu quart mmanụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: Buy me one quart of oil at the market.

examples.igbo: Otu quart mmiri ọ zuru ezu?
examples.english: Is one quart of water enough?

note: quart is used as a loanword in Igbo; some speakers may prefer kwọta.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-emeghalị ofe ahụ n'ọkụ.
examples.english: She is stirring that soup on the fire.

examples.igbo: Meghalịa ọka ahụ tupu ị wụsa ya.
examples.english: Stir that corn before you pour it.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-achụ ajù n'ihi agụụ.
examples.english: He is feeling giddy because of hunger.

examples.igbo: Chụrụ m ajù mgbe m bilitere n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: I felt giddy when I got up in the morning.

examples.igbo: E gosiri m òmụma ògò maka enyemaka gị.
examples.english: I showed gratitude for your help.

examples.igbo: Ì gosiri òmụma ògò nye onye nyere gị ego?
examples.english: Did you show gratitude to the person who gave you money?

gloss: smash something by falling on it

examples.igbo: Osisi dàwàrị ụgbọala anyị n'ụzọ.
examples.english: A tree fell and smashed our car on the road.

examples.igbo: Ònye dàwàrị ite ahụ?
examples.english: Who smashed that pot by falling on it?

examples.igbo: Ndị uwe ojii jidere onyeǹtọ̀ ahụ n'ụlọ ya.
examples.english: The police arrested that kidnapper in his house.

examples.igbo: Ị na-atụ egwu onyeǹtọ̀ n'ụzọ abalị?
examples.english: Are you afraid of a kidnapper on the night road?

note: The word is uncommon in everyday speech; sentences are idiomatic but the tone marking of the headword is as given.

gloss: outskirts of a town; bush around a town

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-egwu egwu n'òwèlè obodo anyị.
examples.english: The children play on the outskirts of our town.

examples.igbo: Gaa n'òwèlè were nkụ.
examples.english: Go to the outskirts and bring firewood.

examples.igbo: Ndị uwe ojii hụrụ ife orī n'ụlọ ya.
examples.english: The police found stolen goods in his house.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara ife orī n'ahịa?
examples.english: Did you buy stolen goods in the market?

examples.igbo: Nwanne m na-akwò ụra n'abalị.
examples.english: My brother snores at night.

examples.igbo: Nna m kwọrọ ụra nke ukwuu ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: My father snored loudly yesterday.

gloss: go with a message; serve; do housework

examples.igbo: Ada na-eje ozi n'ụlọ nne ya.
examples.english: Ada does housework at her mother's house.

examples.igbo: Jee ozi gwa ya na m na-abịa.
examples.english: Go and tell him that I am coming.

note: The headword covers several senses (run an errand, serve, do housework); the two sentences deliberately show two of them.

examples.igbo: Okeke bụ òsi ngọ, o kwenyereghị okwu ahụ.
examples.english: Okeke is a doubter; he did not believe that word.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụghị òsi ngọ, o kwenyere ozugbo.
examples.english: He is not a doubter; he believed at once.

note: Òsi ngọ is not common in everyday speech; the sentences are grammatical and clearly show the sense.

examples.igbo: O jiri mma bèpụ alaka osisi ahụ.
examples.english: He used a knife to cut off that tree branch.

examples.igbo: Bèpụ eriri ahụ, ọ dị ogologo.
examples.english: Cut off that rope; it is too long.

gloss: giant ants, with very big heads, seen among smaller ones

examples.igbo: Ìkeǹgà elùuluū na-ata ọka n'ubi anyị.
examples.english: Giant ants are eating the corn in our farm.

examples.igbo: Kpachara anya, ìkeǹgà elùuluū dị n'ụzọ.
examples.english: Be careful; there are giant ants on the path.

note: The name is known but not common in ordinary conversation; the compound is written as given.

examples.igbo: Ụzọ ahụ chịrị achị mgbe mmiri zọchara.
examples.english: The road was slippery after the rain fell.

examples.igbo: Azụ ahụ na-chị achị, jide ya nke ọma.
examples.english: That fish is slippery; hold it well.

note: The phrase is usually used of a slippery road or a fresh fish; the verb form chịrị achị is as heard locally.

examples.igbo: Ndị uwe ojii nwụchiri ohi ahụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: The police arrested that thief at the market.

examples.igbo: Ònye nwụchiri ọkụkọ m?
examples.english: Who captured my chicken?

note: Treated as a verb with the past form nwụchiri; if the word is a noun in your dialect, the sentences would need recasting.

examples.igbo: Nne ya gòrò akwa mgbe ọ nụrụ akụkọ ọjọọ ahụ.
examples.english: His mother lamented when she heard that bad news.

examples.igbo: I na-agò akwa n’ụtụtụ a?
examples.english: Are you lamenting this morning?

note: Tonal inflection of -gò akwa is uncertain; examples use the likely past and continuous forms.

examples.igbo: O kpàchasịrị ahịhịa niile n’ubi ahụ.
examples.english: He cut all the grass in that farm entirely.

examples.igbo: Kpàchasị ntutu gị tupu ị ga-aga akwụkwọ.
examples.english: Shave your hair completely before you go to school.

examples.igbo: Mmiri na-ada, anyị ga-anọ n’ụlọ taa.
examples.english: It is raining, we will stay home today.

examples.igbo: Jide aka nke ọma ka ị ghara ịda n’ala.
examples.english: Hold on well so you do not fall down.

note: The headword ada is used in the continuous na-ada and the infinitive ịda; standard Igbo often cites the stem as daa.

examples.igbo: O zufere m ego mgbe m na-azụ ahịa.
examples.english: He stole extra money from me when I was shopping.

examples.igbo: Ị zufere m ọka, kwụọ m ụgwọ ya.
examples.english: You stole extra corn from me, pay me for it.

note: The exact complement of zufè is not fully certain, but the sentences show the sense of stealing more than expected.

examples.igbo: Ndị obodo ahụ na-arụ alụsị n’oge emume.
examples.english: The people of that town venerate deities during the festival.

examples.igbo: Ị rụrụ alụsị tupu ị bịa ebe a?
examples.english: Did you venerate deities before you came here?

note: The spelling alụsị is a dialectal variant; the sense and verb inflection are otherwise clear.

examples.igbo: Èvì dị n’ahịa taa, zụta otu.
examples.english: Snakehead fish is in the market today, buy one.

examples.igbo: Anyị ji èvì esi ofe n’ụtụtụ a.
examples.english: We used snakehead fish to cook soup this morning.

examples.igbo: Òpìpì akwa ahụ mere ka mmiri pụta.
examples.english: The wringing of that cloth made water come out.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eme òpìpì oroma maka mmiri ọṅụṅụ?
examples.english: Are you squeezing oranges for juice?

examples.igbo: Ụmù nkịtā na-agba ọsọ n’okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: Dogs are running on the road.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ụmù nkịtā n’ogige anyị?
examples.english: Did you see dogs in our compound?

examples.igbo: O wuru ụnò ọhụrụ n’afọ a.
examples.english: He built a new house this year.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-ewu ụnò n’ime obodo ugbu a.
examples.english: We are building a house in the village now.

note: ụnò is a variant form; standard modern Igbo often writes ụlọ.

examples.igbo: Bịa ebe a kịtāà, anyị ga-aga ahịa.
examples.english: Come here now, we are going to the market.

examples.igbo: Gịnị na-eme gị kịtāà?
examples.english: What is happening to you now?

gloss: throw down by letting go; leave to fall down

examples.igbo: O tụhàrà akpa ya n'ala.
examples.english: He let his bag fall to the ground.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka nwa ahụ tụhàa ite ahụ.
examples.english: Don't let that child drop that pot.

gloss: a weak person who struggles in vain to beat a stronger opponent

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ sepànịpà, ọ na-agbali imeri Chidi.
examples.english: He is a weakling struggling in vain to beat Chidi.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji dị ka sepànịpà?
examples.english: Why are you acting like a weakling?

examples.igbo: Mkpụrụ osisi a churu ichuchu.
examples.english: This fruit is unripe.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-achu ichuchu, erila ya.
examples.english: It is unripe, don't eat it.

examples.igbo: Nchāla jupụtara n'igwe ahụ.
examples.english: Rust has covered that iron.

examples.igbo: Gịnị na-akpata nchāla?
examples.english: What causes rust?

gloss: break off; pluck off; miscarry (very severe and accidental)

examples.igbo: O gbọkwopùrù mkpụrụ ahụ n'alaka.
examples.english: He plucked that fruit off the branch.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji gbọkwopu okooko ahụ?
examples.english: Why did you pluck off that flower?

examples.igbo: Ndàkọlịta dị n'etiti ha abụọ.
examples.english: There is harmony between the two of them.

examples.igbo: Gịnị na-eweta ndàkọlịta n'ezinụlọ?
examples.english: What brings harmony in a family?

examples.igbo: Nne m gbara nnu n'ọnyá ahụ.
examples.english: My mother spat salt on the wound.

examples.igbo: Gbaa nnu n'ọnyá ahụ tupu i kechie ya.
examples.english: Spit salt on the wound before you bandage it.

examples.igbo: Ndị ọrụ tụrụ mkpūlu n'ubi ahụ.
examples.english: The workers made raised beds in that farm.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-atụ mkpūlu tupu mmiri abịa.
examples.english: We make raised beds before the rain comes.

examples.igbo: Ògùdu ànì na-atọ ụtọ.
examples.english: Wine from a felled palm tree is sweet.

examples.igbo: Ndị ikom ahụ na-aṅụ ògùdu ànì.
examples.english: Those men are drinking wine from a felled palm tree.

examples.igbo: Nne m tinyere jī n'ìtè.
examples.english: My mother put yam in the pot.

examples.igbo: Tinye ìtè ahụ n'ọkụ.
examples.english: Put that pot on the fire.

gloss: stepping over; step; threshold (of door or house)

examples.igbo: Nṅefèta ụlọ anyị dị warara.
examples.english: The threshold of our house is narrow.

examples.igbo: O guzoro na nṅefèta ụzọ.
examples.english: He stood at the doorway threshold.

note: Headword given as nŋefèta; rendered with standard ṅ.

gloss: cooked yam mashed to feed child or for sacrifice

examples.igbo: O nyere nwa ya àbùbùụ jī.
examples.english: She gave her child mashed yam.

examples.igbo: Ha ji àbùbùụ jī fee chi.
examples.english: They used mashed yam to sacrifice to the deity.

examples.igbo: Nne ya mụrụ ụmụ abụọ.
examples.english: Her mother gave birth to two children.

examples.igbo: Ị mụrụ nwa n'afọ a?
examples.english: Did you give birth this year?

examples.igbo: Ùmì osisi a na-atọ ụtọ.
examples.english: This fruit juice is sweet.

examples.igbo: Weta ùmì osisi ahụ ka anyị ṅụọ.
examples.english: Bring that fruit juice so we can drink.

examples.igbo: Ògwugwu n'ubi jị were anyị ụbọchị abụọ.
examples.english: Digging in the yam farm took us two days.

examples.igbo: Ị na-arụ ògwugwu taa?
examples.english: Are you digging today?

gloss: fine daughter (used to praise a small girl)

examples.igbo: Àda mmā, bịa ebe a.
examples.english: Fine daughter, come here.

examples.igbo: Ị bụ àda mmā n'ezie!
examples.english: You are a fine daughter indeed!

gloss: make a noise (by large number of people); make tumultuous noise1

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-afịọ n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: The children are making a noise at school.

examples.igbo: Ndị mmadụ fịọrọ n'ama ahịa.
examples.english: The people made a tumultuous noise at the market.

examples.igbo: Ụlọ anyị na-eche iru ụlọ ha.
examples.english: Our house is opposite their house.

examples.igbo: Gịnị na-eche iru ụlọ ahụ?
examples.english: What is opposite that house?

examples.igbo: Jepụ̀ akwa a n'úkwù gị.
examples.english: Untie this wrapper on your waist.

examples.igbo: O jepụrụ akwa n'úkwù nwa ya.
examples.english: She untied the wrapper on her child's waist.

examples.igbo: Gwatara ya ka ọ ghara iwe.
examples.english: Hint to him so that he does not get angry.

examples.igbo: O gwatara m na ọ ga-abịa.
examples.english: He hinted to me that he would come.

examples.igbo: Ọ gbàkwuru nne ya ozugbo.
examples.english: She ran to her mother immediately.

examples.igbo: Gbàkwuo m ngwa ngwa!
examples.english: Run to me quickly!

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ dara ogbī, ọ dịghị ekwu okwu.
examples.english: That child is dumb; he does not speak.

examples.igbo: Ị ma na nwa ahụ dara ogbī?
examples.english: Do you know that that child is dumb?

examples.igbo: Mkpụlụ anyā ya gbara ọbara.
examples.english: His eyeball is bloodshot.

examples.igbo: O nwere ntụ n'ime mkpụlụ anyā ya?
examples.english: Is there dirt in his eyeball?

examples.igbo: Nkịta ripụrụ anụ ahụ niile.
examples.english: The dog devoured all that meat.

examples.igbo: Ònye ripụrụ nri m n'ụlọ?
examples.english: Who ate up my food at home?

gloss: cause laughter Ife o kwùlù kpàlù ọchì His remark gave rise to laughter

examples.igbo: Okwu ya kpàlù ọchì n'ụlọ ahụ.
examples.english: His remark caused laughter in that house.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpàlù ọchì n'ụlọ akwụkwọ?
examples.english: What caused laughter at school?

examples.igbo: Nne m na-eyi ya egwu ǹtaǹta.
examples.english: My mother threatens him with the bogeyman.

examples.igbo: Ị tụrụ egwu ǹtaǹta n'abalị?
examples.english: Are you afraid of the bogeyman at night?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akwa ụta maka mmejọ ya.
examples.english: He is sorry for his mistake.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akwa ụta maka okwu i kwuru?
examples.english: Are you sorry for what you said?

examples.igbo: Ice ahụ gbazee ngwa ngwa n'ehihie.
examples.english: That ice melted quickly in the afternoon.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ ice n'ime mmiri gị?
examples.english: Do you want ice in your water?

gloss: double gong, pieces usually joined to each other at the tail

examples.igbo: Ọ kụrụ ògene mkpì naàbò n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: He sounded the double gong in the morning.

examples.igbo: Kụọ ògene mkpì naàbò ka ndị obodo zukọọ.
examples.english: Sound the double gong so that the townspeople gather.

note: Headword spelling followed as given; the term is specialised.

examples.igbo: Ndị ikènyà na-ezukọ n'ụlọ ọha.
examples.english: The elders gather in the community hall.

examples.igbo: Ndị ikènyà ọ̀ bịara nzukọ taa?
examples.english: Did the elders come to the meeting today?

examples.igbo: Uwe m zụtara bụ acha odo odo.
examples.english: The dress I bought is yellow.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ akwa acha odo odo n'ahịa?
examples.english: Did you see yellow cloth in the market?

gloss: be firm; stand firm; be firmly established or secure in a place (of person)

examples.igbo: O kwụrụ chìm n'ọnụ ụzọ.
examples.english: He stood firm at the doorway.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-akwụ chìm n'ọnọdụ gị?
examples.english: Will you stand firm in your position?

note: The verb phrase is uncommon; examples use it in a plain modern construction.

examples.igbo: Echetere m aha ya ozugbo.
examples.english: I remembered his name immediately.

examples.igbo: Ị chetara ebe anyị zutere?
examples.english: Do you remember where we met?

gloss: fig-tree planted near dwelling to represent one's chi

examples.igbo: E kụrụ ògbụ chī n'akụkụ ụlọ ha.
examples.english: A chi fig-tree was planted beside their house.

examples.igbo: Ògbụ chī ha ka dị n'akụkụ ụlọ?
examples.english: Is their chi fig-tree still beside the house?

gloss: any object shaped like a ramrod with pointed tip; spike

examples.igbo: Mkpịsī a dị nkọ nke ukwuu.
examples.english: This spike is very sharp.

examples.igbo: Were mkpịsī ahụ kụọ ya n'ala.
examples.english: Use that spike to drive it into the ground.

examples.igbo: Ufèlè na-eku n'ụtụtụ taa.
examples.english: The breeze is blowing this morning.

examples.igbo: Ị na-anụ ufèlè na-eku n'èzí?
examples.english: Do you feel the breeze blowing outside?

examples.igbo: O mere nzofù n'ime ọhịa, ọ pụtaghị.
examples.english: He hid away in the forest and did not come out.

examples.igbo: Mee nzofù n'ime ụlọ, ha agaghị achọta gị.
examples.english: Hide away in the house; they will not find you.

examples.igbo: Ebìogwū dị n'ọhịa na-eri mkpụrụ.
examples.english: The porcupine lives in the forest eating seeds.

examples.igbo: Ị hụtụla ebìogwū n'ụzọ?
examples.english: Have you ever seen a porcupine on the road?

examples.igbo: N'akụkọ ifo, òli mmadù na-eri ụmụ mmadụ.
examples.english: In folktales, a cannibal eats human beings.

examples.igbo: Ị na-atụ egwu òli mmadù n'abalị?
examples.english: Are you afraid of a cannibal at night?

examples.igbo: Nne ya kwọrọ ya n'àzụ gaa ahịa.
examples.english: His mother carried him on her back and went to market.

examples.igbo: Kwọọ nwa ahụ n'àzụ, ọ na-ebe akwa.
examples.english: Carry that child on your back, he is crying.

examples.igbo: Ego a bụ ego n'ezie, ọ bụghị ego adịgboroja.
examples.english: This money is real money, not counterfeit money.

examples.igbo: Ị jiri ego n'ezie zụta ya?
examples.english: Did you use real money to buy it?

gloss: cut (with knife or blade) to make a tear

examples.igbo: O ji mma beka akwa ahụ.
examples.english: He used a knife to tear that cloth.

examples.igbo: Beka akwụkwọ a abụọ, anyị ga-eji ya kee ihe.
examples.english: Tear this paper in two, we will use it to tie something.

examples.igbo: Nkịta a ma ùnò, ọ naghị ata aha.
examples.english: This dog is tame, it does not bite.

examples.igbo: Ewu a ọ ma ùnò ma ọ bụ ọhịa?
examples.english: Is this goat tame or wild?

examples.igbo: O pịkọrọ mkpụrụ osisi ahụ ọnụ.
examples.english: He pressed those fruits together.

examples.igbo: Pịkọ akpa a ọnụ ka o baa n'igbe.
examples.english: Press this bag together so it enters the box.

examples.igbo: Nye m òkàlà nke achịcha a.
examples.english: Give me half of this bread.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ òkàlà ọzọ nke ji?
examples.english: Do you want another portion of yam?

examples.igbo: Ndị uwe ojii kùrù ya ịgà.
examples.english: The police handcuffed him.

examples.igbo: Kùọ ya ịgà, ọ na-agba ọsọ.
examples.english: Handcuff him, he is running.

gloss: mark, make trail (e.g. with the foot to mark out foundation)

examples.igbo: O kpụrụ ụkpụlụ ụlọ ahụ n'ala.
examples.english: He marked the foundation of that house on the ground.

examples.igbo: Kpụọ ụkpụlụ ụzọ a, anyị ga-eso ya.
examples.english: Mark the trail of this road, we will follow it.

examples.igbo: Mmiri dị mkpa n'oge ọkọchị.
examples.english: Water is necessary in the dry season.

examples.igbo: Ọ dị mkpa ka m bịa echi?
examples.english: Is it necessary that I come tomorrow?

examples.igbo: Okāàbụ̀rụ̀ na-akpata esemokwu n'obodo anyị.
examples.english: Racism causes conflict in our town.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere okāàbụ̀rụ̀ ji dị n'ụlọ akwụkwọ a?
examples.english: Why does racism exist in this school?

note: The word is rare in everyday speech; the sentences are grammatical but a speaker might prefer a fuller phrase like 'ịkpọ oke asị'.

examples.igbo: Ọ yọọrọ m ego ụlọ akwụkwọ ya.
examples.english: He begged me for his school fees.

examples.igbo: Yọọ enyemaka n'aka ndị agbata obi gị.
examples.english: Beg your neighbours for help.

note: The stem -yọ is less common than -rịọ in modern usage; the forms given are correct but slightly literary.

examples.igbo: Arụrụ ọcha juru n'ime kichin anyị.
examples.english: Sugar ants filled our kitchen.

examples.igbo: Biko kpochapụ arụrụ ọcha niile n'elu tebụl.
examples.english: Please clear away all the sugar ants on the table.

note: Arụrụ ọcha is understood as the small sweet-eating ant, though some speakers call it 'arụrụ shuga'.

examples.igbo: Ha gbara òkpàǹga n'ili nna ha.
examples.english: They performed the mourning dance at their father's grave.

examples.igbo: Ị maara egwu òkpàǹga nke ọma?
examples.english: Do you know the òkpàǹga dance well?

note: The dance is a cultural practice; the phrase is correct but regional knowledge varies.

examples.igbo: Mbìàmbịa ahụ na-ebi n'ụlọ anyị n'efu.
examples.english: That squatter lives in our house for free.

examples.igbo: Ndị mbìàmbịa ole ka ha bịara n'obodo a?
examples.english: How many strangers came to this town?

note: The word covers both 'stranger' and 'squatter'; the two sentences show each shade.

gloss: anything giving shade (literally giver of shade)

examples.igbo: Osisi ukwu ahụ bụ òche ǹdò n'oge ọkọchị.
examples.english: That big tree is a shade-giver in the dry season.

examples.igbo: Nọdụ n'okpuru òche ǹdò ka anyanwụ ghara ịkụ gị.
examples.english: Sit under the shade so the sun does not beat you.

gloss: chase away to disperse; chase to scatter

examples.igbo: Chụsà ụmụ ọkụkọ ahụ n'ubi ọka.
examples.english: Chase those chicks away from the maize farm.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-achụsà ụmụaka na-abịa n'ubi ya.
examples.english: He chases away the children who come to his farm.

note: The verb is used mainly in imperative and continuous forms; the past form is less common.

gloss: It is late evening or night

examples.igbo: Chi emìeela, biko laa n'ụlọ.
examples.english: It is night already, please go home.

examples.igbo: Chi emìe, gịnị ka ị na-eme n'èzí?
examples.english: It is night, what are you doing outside?

examples.igbo: Anyị nọ n'òchiche ya kemgbe ụtụtụ.
examples.english: We have been waiting for him since morning.

examples.igbo: Ị ka nọ n'òchiche ya?
examples.english: Are you still waiting for him?

gloss: democratic system of leadership or governance

examples.igbo: Ọchịchị onye kwu oche ya na-enye ndị mmadụ ohere ikwu okwu.
examples.english: Democracy gives people the opportunity to speak.

examples.igbo: Ndị obodo anyị chọrọ ọchịchị onye kwu oche ya.
examples.english: Our community wants democracy.

note: Headword appears to be a compound; I use the standard spaced form.

examples.igbo: Bupụta oche ndị a n'ụlọ.
examples.english: Carry these chairs out of the house.

examples.igbo: Ọ bupụtara ngwongwo ya n'ụgbọala.
examples.english: He carried his goods out of the vehicle.

note: Used the standard spelling bupụta with ụ.

gloss: (= isi egō) unit of cowrie counting system, consisting of six single cowries (ego) mkpụlū

examples.igbo: Ego isii mejupụtara otu èkpète.
examples.english: Six cowries make one ekpete.

examples.igbo: O ji èkpète ego atọ zụta akwa.
examples.english: She used three ekpete of cowries to buy cloth.

examples.igbo: Ànị mmānya dị n'ala ite ahụ.
examples.english: The dregs of wine are at the bottom of that pot.

examples.igbo: Wụsara ànị mmānya ahụ n'ala.
examples.english: Pour the wine dregs on the ground.

examples.igbo: Lọta n'ụlọ tupu chi ebie.
examples.english: Come home before nightfall.

examples.igbo: Ọ lọtara n'ụlọ mgbe anyị na-eri nri.
examples.english: He came home while we were eating.

examples.igbo: Ọ chaara ọkụ n'ime ụlọ gbara ọchịchịrị.
examples.english: He flashed light in the dark room.

examples.igbo: Cha ọkụ n'okporo ụzọ ka anyị hụ ebe anyị na-aga.
examples.english: Flash light on the road so we can see where we are going.

gloss: abundance, large number (especially of small things)

examples.igbo: Ùgwulùgwu nnụnụ na-efe n'elu osisi.
examples.english: A multitude of birds is flying over the tree.

examples.igbo: Ùgwulùgwu anwụnta bịara n'ụlọ anyị n'abalị.
examples.english: A swarm of mosquitoes came to our house at night.

examples.igbo: Ụlọ ahụ zekpùdoro ya n'isi.
examples.english: The house collapsed over him.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka ala ahụ zekpùdo nwa ahụ.
examples.english: Don't let the ground collapse over the child.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka mechuru uwe ha n'apịtị.
examples.english: The children dirtied their clothes in the mud.

examples.igbo: Emechula aka gị na mmanụ.
examples.english: Do not soil your hands with oil.

gloss: war against; engage in battle against

examples.igbo: Ha nụsọrọ agha megide obodo ahụ.
examples.english: They waged war against that town.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-anụsọ agha megide ndị agbata obi?
examples.english: Will you wage war against your neighbours?
