examples.igbo: Bịa hụ ebe ùsọ ànì anyị dị.
examples.english: Come and see where our farmland boundary is.

examples.igbo: Nna m na-akpọ ụ̄tābà kwa ụtụtụ.
examples.english: My father takes snuff every morning.

examples.igbo: Kpọọ ụ̄tābà tupu ị gawa ọrụ.
examples.english: Take snuff before you go to work.

examples.igbo: O yi ụgbọ gafee osimiri ahụ.
examples.english: He paddled a canoe across that river.

examples.igbo: Yie ụgbọ ahụ nwayọ, mmiri na-asọ.
examples.english: Paddle that canoe slowly, the water is flowing.

examples.igbo: O makụrụ nwa ya n'obi.
examples.english: She hugged her child to her chest.

examples.igbo: Makụọ nwa gị mgbe ọ na-ebe akwa.
examples.english: Hug your child when he is crying.

examples.igbo: N'ezie, m ga-abịa n'oge.
examples.english: Of course, I will come early.

examples.igbo: N'ezie, gwa ya eziokwu.
examples.english: Of course, tell him the truth.

examples.igbo: O ji ùlù kpụọ ite.
examples.english: She used clay to mold a pot.

examples.igbo: Ụzọ ahụ jupụtara ùlù mgbe mmiri zisịrị.
examples.english: The road was full of mire after it rained.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka nabàra n'ụra n'oge ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: The children went to bed early yesterday.

examples.igbo: Nabàa n'ụra, echi ị ga-aga akwụkwọ.
examples.english: Go to bed; tomorrow you will go to school.

note: Inflected forms of -nabà vary; past and imperative forms given as best attested.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-asụ Igbo nke ọma.
examples.english: He speaks Igbo well.

examples.igbo: Ị na-asụ Bekee?
examples.english: Do you speak English?

gloss: move in a weak, flabby way

examples.igbo: Ọ na-atụ gwègèlègwègèlè n'ihi ọrịa.
examples.english: He moves weakly because of illness.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji atụ gwègèlègwègèlè?
examples.english: Why are you moving in that weak, flabby way?

note: Ideophonic verb; usage is idiomatic but not common in writing.

examples.igbo: Onye ọzụzụ chụnaara ehi n'ụlọ.
examples.english: The herdsman drove the cows home.

examples.igbo: Chụnaa ewu gị n'ụlọ, chi ejiela.
examples.english: Drive your goat home; it is getting dark.

gloss: cut side of something; trim hedges; peel bark

examples.igbo: O ji mma gbucha akụkụ osisi ahụ.
examples.english: He used a knife to trim the side of that tree.

examples.igbo: Gbucha ahịhịa n'akụkụ ụlọ ahụ.
examples.english: Trim the weeds at the side of that house.

examples.igbo: Dọdo aka nwa ahụ ike.
examples.english: Hold the child's hand fast.

examples.igbo: O dọdoro akpa ahụ ike n'aka ya.
examples.english: He held the bag fast in his hand.

gloss: something old, unpleasant looking, and useless

examples.igbo: Ụgbọala ànwụ̀rànwụ ka ọ na-akwọ.
examples.english: He is driving an old, useless car.

examples.igbo: Gịnị ka ị ga-eji ànwụ̀rànwụ a mee?
examples.english: What will you do with this old, useless thing?

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ ọnụ na-ekwulu ndị obodo anyị.
examples.english: He is the spokesman of our community.

examples.igbo: Onye bụ ọnụ na-ekwulu ndị ọrụ?
examples.english: Who is the spokesman of the workers?

examples.igbo: Ndị ọrụ na-agbu afịfịa n'ubi.
examples.english: The workers are clearing weeds in the farm.

examples.igbo: Gbuo afịfịa n'ubi tupu ị kụọ ihe.
examples.english: Clear the weeds in the farm before you plant.

gloss: cutting, clearing bush preparatory to farming

examples.igbo: Ha na-eme ọsụsụ ànì maka oge ịkụ ihe.
examples.english: They are clearing the land for the planting season.

examples.igbo: Ọsụsụ ànì were anyị ụbọchị atọ.
examples.english: Clearing the land took us three days.

gloss: pile up; store; board; cover up (literally press upon)

examples.igbo: O kpàdoro akwụkwọ n’elu tebụl.
examples.english: He piled the books on the table.

examples.igbo: Kpàdoo mkpụrụ ọka ndị a n’akpa.
examples.english: Store these maize seeds in the bag.

gloss: clan; tribe; kindred; the smallest kinship-cum-residential unit

examples.igbo: Ebo anyị na-akọ ugbo ọnụ.
examples.english: Our clan farms together.

examples.igbo: Ebo gị ọ dị n’obodo a?
examples.english: Is your clan in this town?

examples.igbo: Ntigwò iko ahụ kpasuru mama iwe.
examples.english: The breaking of that glass annoyed mother.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara ntigwò efere a?
examples.english: What caused the breaking of this plate?

note: Ntigwò is uncommon, but these uses fit the sense of breaking.

examples.igbo: Òchì agha ahụ nyere ndị agha iwu.
examples.english: That commanding officer gave the soldiers orders.

examples.igbo: Òchì agha ọzọ abịala n’ogige?
examples.english: Has another military officer arrived at the camp?

examples.igbo: Da ọkụ̄ ofe ahụ tupu anyị rie ya.
examples.english: Warm that soup before we eat it.

examples.igbo: Nne m na-ada ọkụ̄ nri n’ụtụtụ.
examples.english: My mother warms food in the morning.

gloss: pluck; remove (grains of maize, ripe palm-nuts, from cob or bunch); fall out (e.g. from the socket like a joint or ripe fruit)

examples.igbo: O nworo ọka n’ọkpụkpụ ya.
examples.english: He plucked maize from its cob.

examples.igbo: Nwoo mkpụrụ nkwụ ndị a tupu ha adaa.
examples.english: Pluck these palm nuts before they fall.

examples.igbo: O bìnyere m ego ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: He lent me money yesterday.

examples.igbo: Bìnye ya ego tupu ọ laa.
examples.english: Lend him money before he leaves.

examples.igbo: Ọ pụrụ omume na ọ ga-abịa echi.
examples.english: It is probable that he will come tomorrow.

examples.igbo: Ọ pụrụ omume na mmiri ga-ezo taa?
examples.english: Is it probable that it will rain today?

gloss: be book smart; be brainy; be intelligent

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ ma akwụkwọ nke ukwuu.
examples.english: That child is very book smart.

examples.igbo: Nwa gị ọ ma akwụkwọ?
examples.english: Is your child book smart?

examples.igbo: Ndị ohi ahụ kpọrọ àghalā n’ahịa.
examples.english: Those thieves caused confusion in the market.

examples.igbo: Akpọla àghalā n’obodo a.
examples.english: Don't cause confusion in this town.

examples.igbo: Jedebe ebe a, ka m hụ gị.
examples.english: Come near here so I can see you.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka jedere n'akụkụ ọkụ.
examples.english: The children went near the fire.

examples.igbo: Ọ kpọkọtara ichèlè n'ime ọhịa.
examples.english: He gathered palm-nut shells in the bush.

examples.igbo: Ichèlè ndị a ka anyị na-eji esi nri?
examples.english: Are these palm-nut shells what we use for cooking?

gloss: be correct; suffice; be complete, perfect, sufficient

examples.igbo: Nri ahụ zuru òkè.
examples.english: That food was sufficient.

examples.igbo: Ọrụ anyị ọ zuru òkè?
examples.english: Was our work complete?

gloss: moonfish; a general name for fish of the genus Citharinus

examples.igbo: Anyị zụtara ìpètè n'ọma ahịa.
examples.english: We bought moonfish at the market.

examples.igbo: Ìpètè a ọ dị ọcha?
examples.english: Is this moonfish fresh?

examples.igbo: E dinara nna ya n'inì ozū.
examples.english: His father was buried in the cemetery.

examples.igbo: Ha na-aga inì ozū ugbu a?
examples.english: Are they going to the cemetery now?

examples.igbo: Anyị buniri ijè n'isi ụtụtụ.
examples.english: We started the journey at dawn.

examples.igbo: Ọ buniri ijè taa?
examples.english: Did he start the journey today?

examples.igbo: Anyị na-ekele onye nnapùga anyị.
examples.english: We thank our Redeemer.

examples.igbo: Ị maara onye nnapùga anyị?
examples.english: Do you know our Redeemer?

examples.igbo: Ọ siri ùmà gbasara ahịa ahụ.
examples.english: He sought information about that market.

examples.igbo: Si ùmà tupu ị zụta ya.
examples.english: Seek information before you buy it.

examples.igbo: Ọ bàrà n'ime ụlọ ahụ ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: He entered that house quickly.

examples.igbo: Bà n'ụlọ ugbu a, mmiri na-ezo.
examples.english: Enter the house now, it is raining.

note: Inflected tone on bàrà is uncertain.

examples.igbo: Chinweuba bụ aha nwa anyị nwoke.
examples.english: Chinweuba is our son's name.

examples.igbo: Chinweuba ọ pụtara na Chineke nwe akụ?
examples.english: Does Chinweuba mean God owns wealth?

examples.igbo: Chineke chedoro anyị n'ụzọ anyị gara.
examples.english: God protected us on the journey we travelled.

examples.igbo: Chedo ụmụaka ahụ ka ha ghara ịdaba.
examples.english: Protect those children so they do not fall.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-anepù ewu ahụ furu efu.
examples.english: We are looking for the goat that got lost.

examples.igbo: Nepù akwụkwọ gị tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Look for your book before you leave.

note: Tone on imperative Nepù may need adjustment.

examples.igbo: Wụnye mmiri n'ime ite ahụ ozugbo.
examples.english: Pour water into that pot immediately.

examples.igbo: Ọ wụnyere ntakịrị mmanụ n'ime karama.
examples.english: She poured a little oil into the bottle.

gloss: wooden bowl; tray; wooden platter for cutting up meat

examples.igbo: Obi ji ọkwa were bee anụ.
examples.english: Obi used a wooden platter to cut meat.

examples.igbo: Ọkwa ahụ dị n'akụkụ ọkụ n'ụlọ.
examples.english: That wooden tray is near the fire in the house.

examples.igbo: Nne m mechara imi nwa ahụ.
examples.english: My mother wiped the child's nose.

examples.igbo: Mecha imi gị, ọ na-agba ọsọ.
examples.english: Wipe your nose, it is running.

gloss: woman of great influence or of strong, stout build

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ agbàlà nwaànyì n'obodo anyị.
examples.english: She is a woman of great influence in our town.

examples.igbo: Agbàlà nwaànyì ahụ buuru nnukwu osisi.
examples.english: That stout woman carried a big log.

gloss: log of wood on which the blacksmith’s anvil is set. It is buried in the ground with raffia fibres forming the base so that the log of wood jumps when the iron is hit by the blacksmith. This lightens the jarring of the hammer on the blacksmith’s hand

examples.igbo: Onye ọkụ kụrụ ígwè n'elu àkpaka ụzū.
examples.english: The blacksmith hammered iron on the anvil log.

examples.igbo: Àkpaka ụzū na-awụli elu mgbe a kụrụ ígwè.
examples.english: The anvil log jumps when iron is struck.

gloss: a prestigious king; an honorable king

examples.igbo: Ezūùgò bịara n'ọgbakọ ndị eze taa.
examples.english: The prestigious king came to the kings' meeting today.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-asọpụrụ Ezūùgò nke ukwuu n'obodo a.
examples.english: We respect the honorable king greatly in this town.

note: Use as title or name may vary by context.

examples.igbo: Ọ nò n'enu mmīli n'ihi ego ọ gbaziri.
examples.english: He is in trouble because of the money he borrowed.

examples.igbo: Ị nò n'enu mmīli maka ihe ahụ ị mere?
examples.english: Are you in trouble because of that thing you did?

examples.igbo: Mgbagò nke osisi ahụ juru m anya.
examples.english: The bending of that tree surprised me.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara mgbagò nke osisi a?
examples.english: What caused the bending of this tree?

examples.igbo: Onye ohi ahụ gbalagara n'abalị.
examples.english: That thief ran away at night.

examples.igbo: Gbalaga tupu ndị uwe ojii abịa!
examples.english: Run away before the police come!

gloss: spoil by driving or riding; ride violently

examples.igbo: Ọ nyàkàrà ụgbọala ya n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: He rode his car violently on the road.

examples.igbo: Nyàkala ịnyịnya ahụ, ọ ga-emebi!
examples.english: Don't ride that horse violently, it will spoil!

examples.igbo: Ha nìnyere nna ha n'ala.
examples.english: They buried their father in the ground.

examples.igbo: Nìnye ya n'ala ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Bury him in the ground quickly.

examples.igbo: M ga-akpọ ute n'ahịa.
examples.english: I will buy a mat in the market.

examples.igbo: Kpọọ ute abụọ maka ụmụaka.
examples.english: Buy two mats for the children.

gloss: the act of locking something with a key or bolt; locking

examples.igbo: Ntụchi ọnụ ụzọ ahụ siri ike.
examples.english: The locking of that door is strong.

examples.igbo: Ị maara ntụchi nke igbe a?
examples.english: Do you know the locking of this box?

gloss: be at or in a place(heavy or bulky object) ; stay (heavy or bulky object)

examples.igbo: Nkume ahụ dọ̀ n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: That stone is in the road.

examples.igbo: Ebee ka igbe ahụ dọ̀?
examples.english: Where is that box located?

examples.igbo: Ụlọ ahụ nwụrụ ọkụ n'abalị.
examples.english: That house caught fire at night.

examples.igbo: Osisi ahụ nwụrụ ọkụ?
examples.english: Did that tree catch fire?

examples.igbo: Onye ọkụ na-akụ ígwè n'osiamā.
examples.english: The blacksmith hammers iron on the anvil.

examples.igbo: Weta osiamā ahụ ebe a.
examples.english: Bring that anvil here.

examples.igbo: Nri ahụ mere ka ọ gbọọ ògbụgbọ.
examples.english: That food made him vomit.

examples.igbo: Ị gbọrọ ògbụgbọ n'ụtụtụ?
examples.english: Did you vomit in the morning?

gloss: at the same time; once upon a time

examples.igbo: Anyị rụrụ ọrụ n'òfu ogè.
examples.english: We worked at the same time.

examples.igbo: N'òfu ogè, e nwere agụ n'ime ọhịa.
examples.english: Once upon a time, there was a leopard in the forest.

note: Entry has two senses; examples cover 'at the same time' and 'once upon a time'.

examples.igbo: Okòm bụ ụdị ji anyị na-akọ n'ugbo.
examples.english: Okom is a type of yam we plant in the farm.

examples.igbo: Ị kọrọ okòm n'afọ a?
examples.english: Did you plant okom this year?

gloss: goat pepper, used by children to play cooking

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-eji osè nwamkpi egwu nri.
examples.english: Children use goat pepper to play cooking.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ osè nwamkpi n'ime ite egwuregwu ha?
examples.english: Did you see goat pepper in their play pot?

examples.igbo: N'oge okpomọkụ, anyị na-aṅụ mmiri oyi.
examples.english: In summer, we drink cold water.

examples.igbo: Ị na-aga osimiri n'oge okpomọkụ?
examples.english: Do you go to the river in summer?

examples.igbo: Akwụkwọ īwu dị n'elu tebụl.
examples.english: The law book is on the table.

examples.igbo: Ị gụrụ akwụkwọ īwu ahụ?
examples.english: Did you read that law book?

examples.igbo: N'ahịa, ha na-ere osikapa, agwa, dgz.
examples.english: At the market, they sell rice, beans, etc.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ji, ede, dgz n'ugbo?
examples.english: Did you see yams, cocoyams, etc. in the farm?

note: dgz is an abbreviation used in writing for 'etc.'; it is not a spoken word.

gloss: turn grey (of black hair turning grey)

examples.igbo: Nna m chaara isi awō mgbe ọ dị afọ iri ise.
examples.english: My father turned grey when he was fifty.

examples.igbo: Isi gị ọ na-acha awō?
examples.english: Is your hair turning grey?

examples.igbo: Fa niīne bịara n'ọgbakọ.
examples.english: All of them came to the meeting.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ fa niīne n'ahịa?
examples.english: Did you see all of them at the market?

note: fa is dialectal; standard Igbo would use ha niile.

gloss: dance very well in type of dance in which back muscles come into play

examples.igbo: Ọ na-agwo egwu nke ọma n'ememme obodo.
examples.english: He dances very well at the town festival.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji agwo egwu na-eji azụ eme ihe?
examples.english: Why do you dance using your back?

note: The specific dance term is uncertain; examples show the verb with egwu but may not fully capture the back-muscle dance sense.

gloss: feeling of hatred towards someone that last for a long time; enmity

examples.igbo: Ọ nwere uro n'ebe nwanne ya nwoke nọ.
examples.english: He has enmity toward his brother.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji enwe uro n'ebe m nọ?
examples.english: Why do you have enmity toward me?

examples.igbo: Òkùkù ọkụ na-enyere anyị aka isi nri.
examples.english: Blowing the fire helps us cook.

examples.igbo: Ị na-anụ òkùkù ume nwa ọhụrụ?
examples.english: Can you hear the baby's breathing?

examples.igbo: Ọ kụrụ ìkili akā ya n'ọnụ ụzọ.
examples.english: He hit his elbow on the door.

examples.igbo: Ìkili akā gị ọ na-egbu gị mgbu?
examples.english: Does your elbow hurt you?

examples.igbo: Ochie ahụ na-asọ gànàgànà n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: That old man staggers on the road.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji asọ gànàgànà?
examples.english: Why are you staggering?

gloss: cask; puncheon (of palm oil) (? from English)

examples.igbo: Ọ bu ponì mmanụ nkwụ abụọ n'isi.
examples.english: He carried two casks of palm oil on his head.

examples.igbo: Ponì mmanụ nkwụ a dị arọ.
examples.english: This cask of palm oil is heavy.

examples.igbo: Anyị jidere ǹcha ọcha abụọ n'osimiri.
examples.english: We caught two tilapia in the river.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ere ǹcha ọcha n'ahịa taa?
examples.english: Are you selling tilapia at the market today?

examples.igbo: Biko gacha ite ahụ n'ọkụ.
examples.english: Please take that pot off the fire.

examples.igbo: Ọ gachara ite osikapa n'ọkụ.
examples.english: She took the pot of rice off the fire.

gloss: break or cut by pulling, especially thread, rope, and elastic

examples.igbo: Ọ dọbiri eriri ahụ n'aka abụọ.
examples.english: He broke the rope with two hands.

examples.igbo: Dọbi eriri a, ọ dị obere.
examples.english: Break this thread, it is small.

examples.igbo: Òkwùdùkwudū nọ n'elu osisi, na-ele anya n'abalị.
examples.english: The owl is on the tree, watching at night.

examples.igbo: N'abalị, ị na-anụ ụda òkwùdùkwudū n'ime ọhịa?
examples.english: At night, do you hear the sound of an owl in the forest?

examples.igbo: Ọ fọrọ nke nta ka ọ gbàgbù mgbe ọ na-eri azụ.
examples.english: He nearly choked to death while eating fish.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka nwata gbàgbù n'ihi ọkpụkpụ azụ.
examples.english: Do not let a child choke to death because of a fish bone.

examples.igbo: Uwe m nwere ụkpụrụ mara mma.
examples.english: My dress has a beautiful pattern.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ụkpụrụ ọhụrụ e sere n'ahịa?
examples.english: Did you see the new pattern drawn at the market?

examples.igbo: Onye ọbịa ahụ kara anya rịọọ nri ọzọ.
examples.english: That guest was bold and asked for more food.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-aka anya were ego niile n'aka m?
examples.english: Will you be so bold as to take all the money from my hand?

examples.igbo: O ghụlụrụ nku ọkụkọ tupu o sie ya.
examples.english: She plucked the chicken's feathers before cooking it.

examples.igbo: Ghụlụ ahịhịa ndị a tupu ị kụọ osisi.
examples.english: Pull out these weeds before you plant trees.

gloss: greediness; lack of hospitality (literally crying for food)

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ nwere akwa nnī, ọ naghị enye ndị ọbịa nri.
examples.english: That man is greedy; he does not give visitors food.

examples.igbo: Akwa nnī adịghị mma n'ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: Greediness is not good in our house.

gloss: arch the lips in engrossment, disagreement, or to express hate

examples.igbo: Ọ mìrì ọnụ mgbe ọ hụrụ nri ahụ.
examples.english: He arched his lips when he saw that food.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji mì ọnụ mgbe a kpọrọ aha ya?
examples.english: Why did you arch your lips when his name was called?

examples.igbo: Anyị na-eme ògụgụ ego tupu anyị apụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: We count the money before we leave the market.

examples.igbo: Ògụgụ ụmụaka bịara bụ iri abụọ.
examples.english: The number of children who came is twenty.

examples.igbo: Onye ngàla ahụ anaghị ekele ndị okenye.
examples.english: That proud person does not greet elders.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere onye ngàla ji eleda ndị ọzọ anya?
examples.english: Why does a proud person look down on others?

examples.igbo: Anyị bi n'ụsọ oké osimiri ugbu a.
examples.english: We live at the coast now.

examples.igbo: Ị na-aga n'ụsọ oké osimiri n'oge okpomọkụ?
examples.english: Do you go to the coast in summer?

gloss: drop leaves or unripe fruit (of tree)

examples.igbo: Osisi mango ahụ na-anwosịsị mkpụrụ ya.
examples.english: That mango tree is dropping its fruit.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere osisi a ji anwosịsị akwụkwọ ya?
examples.english: Why is this tree dropping its leaves?

note: Verb inflection and tone marking may vary in usage.

examples.igbo: Ndị ikom ahụ nọ na aŋụlụma n'ụlọ mmanya.
examples.english: Those men are on a drinking spree in the bar.

examples.igbo: Ị na-achọ ịmalite aŋụlụma ọzọ?
examples.english: Are you looking to start another drinking spree?

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ kpuru ìsì mgbe ọ dị afọ iri.
examples.english: That man became blind when he was ten.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-enyere nwata kpuru ìsì aka ịgafe okporo ụzọ?
examples.english: Will you help the blind child cross the road?

examples.igbo: Papa m gbara ògìgè gburugburu ubi ya.
examples.english: My father fenced around his farm.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-agba ògìgè tupu ị kụọ ihe?
examples.english: Will you fence before you plant?

examples.igbo: Onye ohi mapuru taya ụgbọala m.
examples.english: A thief pierced my car tyre.

examples.igbo: Jiri nwayọ, ka ị ghara ịmapu akpa ahụ.
examples.english: Be careful so you don't pierce that bag.

note: Conjugation of -mapu may vary.

examples.igbo: Ọ tufuru uchè mgbe ego ya gwụrụ.
examples.english: He despaired when his money ran out.

examples.igbo: Ndị ọrụ ahụ tufuru uchè?
examples.english: Did those workers despair?

note: Spelling and tone of the inflected form may vary.

gloss: a display name for online platforms; username

examples.igbo: E deela ahāǹjìmārā gị n'elu profaịlụ.
examples.english: Your username has been written on the profile.

examples.igbo: Gịnị bụ ahāǹjìmārā gị na Facebook?
examples.english: What is your username on Facebook?

examples.igbo: Nnu oyìbo dị oke ọnụ n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: Sugar is expensive in the market today.

examples.igbo: Ị tinyela nnu oyìbo n'ime tii m?
examples.english: Have you put sugar in my tea?

gloss: change; change place of; re-arrange; reverse; turn (something) round

examples.igbo: Biko doghaa oche ahụ ka ọ chee ihu n'ọnụ ụzọ.
examples.english: Please turn that chair to face the door.

examples.igbo: Ha doghara tebụl ahụ n'ọnụ ụzọ.
examples.english: They turned the table to the door.

note: Inflected forms of -dogha may vary.

examples.igbo: Nwaāmili ahụ na-ere akwụkwọ n'ahịa.
examples.english: That woman sells books in the market.

examples.igbo: Ị maara nwaāmili ahụ bi n'ụlọ nke ahụ?
examples.english: Do you know that woman living in that house?

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-agba m̀gbā n'ogige ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: Children are wrestling in the school field.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-agba m̀gbā na nwanne gị?
examples.english: Will you wrestle with your brother?

gloss: wear, tie wrapper; be dressed in wrapper

examples.igbo: O mara akwà ọhụrụ taa.
examples.english: She wore a new wrapper today.

examples.igbo: Maa akwà gị ngwa ngwa!
examples.english: Wear your wrapper quickly!

examples.igbo: O ghasara ọka n'ubi ya.
examples.english: He scattered corn in his farm.

examples.igbo: Ghasàa mkpụrụ osisi ahụ n'ala.
examples.english: Scatter those seeds on the ground.

gloss: the eleventh letter of the Igbo language alphabet; the ninth consonant of the Igbo language alphabet

examples.igbo: Nwa m mụtara mkpụrụ okwu 'h' taa.
examples.english: My child learned the letter 'h' today.

examples.igbo: Ị maara mkpụrụ okwu 'h' dị n'asụsụ Igbo?
examples.english: Do you know the letter 'h' in Igbo?

examples.igbo: O wapụrụ nkụ ahụ n'ala.
examples.english: He pulled out that stick from the ground.

examples.igbo: Wapụ m ahịhịa a n'aka m.
examples.english: Pull this thorn out of my hand.

examples.igbo: Osimiri ahụ na-arùnye n'ọdọ mmiri.
examples.english: That river flows into the lake.

examples.igbo: Mmiri ọ na-arùnye n'ime ite?
examples.english: Is water flowing into the pot?

examples.igbo: Mkpụrụ osisi bàmìrì n'ala.
examples.english: The seed entered deeply into the ground.

examples.igbo: Bàmì n'ime mmiri ahụ.
examples.english: Enter deeply into that water.

gloss: squeeze something through a tight place, mostly in an attempt to place, remove or search;

examples.igbo: O fọrọ aka ya n'ọnụ ụzọ.
examples.english: He squeezed his hand through the doorway.

examples.igbo: Fọọ mkpụrụ ahụ n'oghere.
examples.english: Squeeze that seed through the hole.

note: Inflection of 'fọ' may vary; past tense and imperative forms are uncertain.

examples.igbo: O kwọjipụrụ alaka osisi ahụ.
examples.english: He sawed off that tree branch.

examples.igbo: Kwọjipụ m osisi a.
examples.english: Saw this wood off for me.

examples.igbo: O mere òzọ ọrụ ahụ.
examples.english: He did that work again.

examples.igbo: Biko mee òzọ ya.
examples.english: Please do it again.

gloss: plant with tiny thorns which yields strings, used to tie up seed-yams or to make àkwalī B.

examples.igbo: E jiri akūlu kee mkpụrụ ji n'ubi.
examples.english: They used akūlu to tie seed yams in the farm.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eji akūlu kee ji a?
examples.english: Will you use akūlu to tie these yams?

examples.igbo: Anyị nwere naasātọ mmadụ n'ọrụ a.
examples.english: We have eight people in this work.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara naasātọ ọkụkọ?
examples.english: Did you buy eight chickens?

examples.igbo: Anyanwụ na-anwu màlàmàlà n'ehihie.
examples.english: The sun is dazzling in the afternoon.

examples.igbo: Ihe ahụ na-anwu màlàmàlà, gịnị ka ọ bụ?
examples.english: That thing is dazzling, what is it?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ede ìdùàzị̀, ọ bụghị abụ.
examples.english: He writes prose, not poetry.

examples.igbo: Ìdùàzị̀ a dị mfe nghọta karịa abụ.
examples.english: This prose is easier to understand than poetry.

examples.igbo: Ndị ògbọ anyị na-ezukọta kwa ọnwa.
examples.english: Our age-set members meet every month.

examples.igbo: Ògbọ ya na ògbọ gị bụ otu?
examples.english: Is his age-set the same as yours?

examples.igbo: Onye nkuzi na-akụzi anyị mgbakọ na mwepụ.
examples.english: The teacher teaches us mathematics.

examples.igbo: Kụziere ụmụaka otú e si asụ Igbo.
examples.english: Teach the children how to speak Igbo.

examples.igbo: Nwanne nwaanyị m bi n'Enugwu.
examples.english: My sister lives in Enugu.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ nwanne nwaanyị gị n'ahịa?
examples.english: Did you see your sister at the market?

examples.igbo: Mma ahụ tara nchārā n'ihi mmiri.
examples.english: That knife rusted because of water.

examples.igbo: Ígwè na-ata nchārā ma ọ nọọ n'ime mmiri.
examples.english: Iron rusts if it stays in water.

gloss: bride-wealth; deposit paid to wife's family which is refunded in the event of a divorce and remarriage

examples.igbo: E nyere ezinụlọ nwunye ya ngò.
examples.english: They gave bride-wealth to his wife's family.

examples.igbo: Ha kwụrụ ngò tupu ha akpọbata nwunye.
examples.english: They paid the bride-wealth before bringing in the wife.

gloss: cover up; shut up; shut; cover

examples.igbo: O kpùchitere ite nri ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: She covered the pot of food well.

examples.igbo: Kpụchita ọnụ ụzọ ahụ, ka ikuku ghara ịbata.
examples.english: Shut that door so the air doesn't come in.

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ na-agà mbọ ya n'ihu nwanne ya.
examples.english: That child is scratching his sibling's face with his nails.

examples.igbo: Gàa mbọ ya n'azụ.
examples.english: Scratch his back with your nails.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-agbapụ ụta n'ala.
examples.english: He is spitting saliva on the ground.

examples.igbo: Gbapụ ụta ahụ n'ala.
examples.english: Spit that saliva on the ground.

examples.igbo: Ụzọ̀ọma dị n'ebe ahụ.
examples.english: There is a good road there.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-aga n'ụzọ̀ọma a?
examples.english: Will you go on this good road?

examples.igbo: Ọ gbara òbàlà n'imi mgbe ọ dara.
examples.english: He bled from the nose when he fell.

examples.igbo: Ị na-agba òbàlà n'aka?
examples.english: Are you bleeding on your hand?

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ gbepụtara n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: The child crawled out of the room.

examples.igbo: Gbepụta n'okpuru àkwà ahụ.
examples.english: Crawl out from under that bed.

examples.igbo: Ànì ogwē akā ya merụrụ ahụ.
examples.english: His forearm got injured.

examples.igbo: Ànì ogwē akā gị ọ na-egbu mgbu?
examples.english: Does your forearm hurt?

gloss: approach playfully; be playful to someone or something who is playful to you

examples.igbo: Ọ na-agwūsò egwu n'ebe nwanne ya nọ.
examples.english: She is playful toward her sibling.

examples.igbo: Gwūsò egwu nwa ahụ, ọ na-atọ ya ụtọ.
examples.english: Be playful to that child; he enjoys it.

examples.igbo: Òwu akpū na-eto n'ubi anyị.
examples.english: Kapok grows in our farm.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ òwu akpū n'ime ohia?
examples.english: Did you see kapok in the bush?

gloss: lift down and out (e.g. pot from the cooking tripod)

examples.igbo: Biko rọpụta ite ahụ n'elu ọkụ.
examples.english: Please take that pot down from the fire.

examples.igbo: Ị rọpụtara ite osikapa tupu ọ gbawa?
examples.english: Did you take down the pot of rice before it boiled over?

examples.igbo: Nnụnụ ahụ fedara n'ala ma gbapụ ọzọ.
examples.english: That bird flew down to the ground and flew away again.

examples.igbo: Feda n'ala ka anyị hụ nku gị.
examples.english: Fly down so we can see your wings.

examples.igbo: Dọkịta tụtere nwata ahụ ndụ mgbe ọ dara.
examples.english: The doctor revived the child when he collapsed.

examples.igbo: Ọ dị mkpa ịtụte ndụ onye fọrọ nke nta ka ọ nwụọ.
examples.english: It is important to resuscitate someone who almost died.

note: The phrase tụte ndụ is correct in sense, but I would double-check the past form.

examples.igbo: Olu ya na-egbu mgbu mgbe ọ na-ehi ụra.
examples.english: His neck hurts when he is sleeping.

examples.igbo: Olu gị ọ na-egbu mgbu n'ụtụtụ a?
examples.english: Does your neck hurt this morning?

examples.igbo: Jide osisi ndị ahụ gbakọta ọnụ.
examples.english: Hold those sticks together.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-ejide ha niile gbakọta ọnụ?
examples.english: Will you hold them all together?

examples.igbo: Anyị na-agba azị efifie n'elekere abụọ.
examples.english: We take lunch at two o'clock.

examples.igbo: Gbaa azị efifie tupu ị laa ọrụ.
examples.english: Take lunch before you leave work.

note: I am not fully certain of this idiom; the examples follow the given gloss.

examples.igbo: Okwu ya wutere m nke ukwuu.
examples.english: His words hurt me greatly.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji wute nwanne gị?
examples.english: Why did you sadden your sibling?

examples.igbo: Yochapụ ntụ ahụ n'ime ọka nke ọma.
examples.english: Sift out that chaff from the corn well.

examples.igbo: O yochapụrụ ájá niile n'ime agwa.
examples.english: She sifted out all the sand from the beans.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-aṅụ ala efi ọhụrụ n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: Children drink fresh cow milk in the morning.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara ala efi na ahịa?
examples.english: Did you buy cow milk at the market?

note: Standard Igbo commonly says mmiri ara ehi; I followed the headword ala efī.

gloss: swelling (usually around the armpit, groin, upper thigh)

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ nwere azị̀zaā n'apata ụkwụ ya.
examples.english: That child has a swelling on his thigh.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ azị̀zaā ahụ dị n'okpuru aka ya?
examples.english: Did you see that swelling under his arm?

examples.igbo: Dee ahà gị n'akwụkwọ a.
examples.english: Write your name in this book.

examples.igbo: Ọ dere ahà ya n'akwụkwọ tupu ọ pụọ.
examples.english: He wrote his name in the book before leaving.

examples.igbo: Nwùchie anya gị, anyị ga-ekpe ekpere.
examples.english: Close your eyes, we will pray.

examples.igbo: Nwatakịrị ahụ nwùchiri anya ya mgbe ọ na-ehi ụra.
examples.english: That child closed his eyes while sleeping.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-alụsi ike n'ubi ya.
examples.english: He works hard on his farm.

examples.igbo: Anyị lụsiri ike rụchaa ọrụ ahụ tupu abalị.
examples.english: We worked hard and finished that work before night.

examples.igbo: Onye ahụ bụ mmadụ ọjọọ, ọ na-akparị ụmụaka.
examples.english: That person is a bad person; he maltreats children.

examples.igbo: Ihe ọjọọ mere n'ụlọ akwụkwọ taa?
examples.english: Did something bad happen at school today?

gloss: be native or home-born, indigenous (literally grow, sprout in the soil)

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ onye pụtara n'ànì n'obodo a, ọ bụghị ọbịa.
examples.english: He is a native of this town, not a visitor.

examples.igbo: Ị bụ onye pụtara n'ànì n'obodo a?
examples.english: Are you a native of this town?

gloss: act as regent; administer during interregnum

examples.igbo: Onye nọ n'oche eze na-eche ǹdò ugbu a.
examples.english: The one on the throne is acting as regent now.

examples.igbo: Ha mere ya onye na-eche ǹdò ruo mgbe eze ọhụrụ ga-abịa.
examples.english: They made him regent until a new king comes.

gloss: breathe out; scoop out with a spoon

examples.igbo: Kupùa ume gị nwayọọ tupu i kwuo okwu.
examples.english: Breathe out slowly before you speak.

examples.igbo: O ji ngaji kupụta ofe ahụ.
examples.english: She scooped out that soup with a spoon.

examples.igbo: Anyanwụ na-agbu màlàmàlà n'elu mmiri.
examples.english: The sun glitters on the water.

examples.igbo: Lee ka kpakpando na-agbu màlàmàlà n'abalị!
examples.english: Look how the stars glitter at night!

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ ịrịba ama na mmiri ga-ezo.
examples.english: It is a sign that it will rain.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ịrịba ama ahụ n'ọnụ ụzọ?
examples.english: Did you see that sign at the door?

examples.igbo: O hịgharịrị osisi ahụ ruo mgbe ọ gbajiri.
examples.english: He twisted that stick until it broke.

examples.igbo: Hịgharịa ihe ahụ n'aka gị ka m hụ ya.
examples.english: Turn that thing in your hand so I can see it.

examples.igbo: Achọtara m akpa m n'okpuru akwa.
examples.english: I found my bag under the bed.

examples.igbo: Ị chọtara ụlọ ọgwụ ahụ?
examples.english: Did you find that hospital?

examples.igbo: Chachanye osikapa ahụ n'ite.
examples.english: Wash that rice into the pot.

examples.igbo: Ị chachanyerela ọka ahụ n'ite?
examples.english: Have you washed that corn into the pot?

gloss: make to long after unnecessarily(especially food); be attractive(especially in a useable way)

examples.igbo: Anụ ahụ na-adọ àkpịrị̄ n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: That meat is enticing in the market today.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-adọ gị àkpịrị̄, ị zụta ya?
examples.english: Does it make you long for it, will you buy it?

note: Uncertain of the exact idiomatic use of dọ àkpịrị̄.

gloss: trial; temptation (from -dàma fall up and down, here and there)

examples.igbo: Ọ dara n'ndàma ndàmi nke ego.
examples.english: He fell into the temptation of money.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-ada n'ndàma ndàmi ahụ?
examples.english: Will you fall into that temptation?

examples.igbo: Ifufe na-eku nke ọma n'abalị a.
examples.english: The wind is blowing well tonight.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ifufe ji a-eku ike taa?
examples.english: Why is the wind blowing hard today?

examples.igbo: Ugòlo òmà nọ n'elu osisi ahụ.
examples.english: The pied crow is on that tree.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ugòlo òmà n'ubi?
examples.english: Did you see a pied crow in the farm?

examples.igbo: O nwere obiì ònyìnye n'ebe ụmụaka nọ.
examples.english: He has a generous mind toward children.

examples.igbo: Obiì ònyìnye ya pụtara ìhè mgbe o kesara nri.
examples.english: His generous disposition showed when he shared the food.

gloss: (of animals) wander about in farm, forest, etc., in search of food

examples.igbo: Ewu na-akpa nni n'ubi anyị.
examples.english: The goat is wandering our farm in search of food.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ọkụkọ ka ọ na-akpa nni n'ọhịa?
examples.english: Did you see the chicken wandering the bush for food?

examples.igbo: O yiri mgbanaka ọla edo n'aka.
examples.english: She wore a gold ring on her hand.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara mgbanaka maka agbamakwụkwọ?
examples.english: Did you buy a ring for the wedding?

gloss: woman of great influence; a woman who does wonders

examples.igbo: Nwanyị ahụ bụ agbàrànwaànyị̀ n'obodo anyị.
examples.english: That woman is a woman of great influence in our town.

examples.igbo: Ì maara na nne ya bụ agbàrànwaànyị̀ mgbe ọ dị ndụ?
examples.english: Did you know that her mother was a woman of great influence when she was alive?

note: The compound is uncommon; spelling and tone pattern vary in usage.

examples.igbo: Ezé ya na-acha ọcha nke ọma.
examples.english: Her teeth are very white.

examples.igbo: Saa ezé gị tupu i laa ụra.
examples.english: Brush your teeth before you go to bed.

examples.igbo: Anyị ga-aga ahịa ta à nị.
examples.english: We will go to the market today.

examples.igbo: Ta à nị ka ọ bịara?
examples.english: Was it today that he came?

note: The spelling of this time word varies in modern writing.

examples.igbo: Ose ndị a chakpọrọ nke ọma.
examples.english: These peppers are fully ripe.

examples.igbo: Ube a chakpọọla, ka ọ dị?
examples.english: Has this pear ripened fully, or not?

examples.igbo: Nwa a bụ ife ònyìnyò nna ya.
examples.english: This child is the very image of his father.

examples.igbo: Ì hụrụ ife ònyìnyò ya n'ime mmiri?
examples.english: Did you see its reflection in the water?

gloss: settlement of Nri, founded by Nri son of Èrì, and its people; (more loosely) people who claim some kind of relationship with Nri
