examples.english: He is a person of Nri; his mother comes from there.

examples.igbo: Ndị Ǹrì na-azụ ahịa n'obodo anyị.
examples.english: The Nri people trade in our town.

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ na-eme kwùlìkwùlì ná nzụkọ.
examples.english: That man behaves like a harmless madman at the meeting.

examples.igbo: Emeela kwùlìkwùlì n'ebe a!
examples.english: Don't behave like a madman here!

examples.igbo: Anyị nwere aṅụ̀rị mgbe nwa anyị lọtara.
examples.english: We rejoiced when our child came home.

examples.igbo: Nwee aṅụ̀rị, ihe ọma abịala!
examples.english: Rejoice, good things have come!

examples.igbo: Kpụdèbe nso ka m gwa gị okwu.
examples.english: Come near so I can tell you something.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka ahụ kpụdebere nso ka ha hụ anụ ahụ.
examples.english: The children drew near to see the animal.

note: Inflected forms of this stem are not fully standardized.

examples.igbo: Ìmìlìkiti mmadụ bịara oriri ahụ.
examples.english: Many people came to that feast.

examples.igbo: Ìmìlìkiti mmadụ ka ọ kpọrọ?
examples.english: Did he invite many people?

examples.igbo: Ụkwụ m na-agbu m mgbụ taa.
examples.english: My leg is aching today.

examples.igbo: Gịnị na-agbu gị mgbụ n'aka?
examples.english: What is hurting you in the hand?

note: The tone marks on m̄gbū in the entry are unusual; I wrote mgbụ plainly in the sentences.

gloss: (also agbàlà nwaànyì) woman of great influence or of strong, stout build

examples.igbo: Nne ya bụ agbàlà n'ala a.
examples.english: Her mother is a woman of influence in this land.

examples.igbo: Ị maara na ọ bụ agbàlà n'obodo a?
examples.english: Did you know that she is a woman of standing in this town?

gloss: new testament; the second part of the bible

examples.igbo: Anyị na-agụ àgbaọhụ̀rụ n'ụlọ akwụkwọ Sọnde.
examples.english: We read the New Testament in Sunday school.

examples.igbo: Ị gụọla àgbaọhụ̀rụ niile?
examples.english: Have you read the whole New Testament?

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka chọtara nkekele mbè n'akụkụ osimiri.
examples.english: The children found a tortoise shell by the river.

examples.igbo: Nkekele mbè a siri ike, ọ gbasaghị.
examples.english: This tortoise shell is hard, it did not break.

examples.igbo: Onyeisi ahụ dị èberè n'ebe ndị ọrụ ya nọ.
examples.english: That boss is kind-hearted towards his workers.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụrụ na ị dị èberè, gbaghara ya.
examples.english: If you are merciful, forgive him.

examples.igbo: Ha na-agbu akwụ n'ubi taa.
examples.english: They are cutting palm fruit on the farm today.

examples.igbo: Gbuo akwụ ndị a tupu abalị eruo.
examples.english: Cut these palm fruits before night falls.

examples.igbo: Ọ kwuru okwu ogologo n'ọgbakọ.
examples.english: He spoke a long speech at the meeting.

examples.igbo: Kwu ngwa ngwa, anyị na-aga ugbu a.
examples.english: Speak quickly, we are leaving right now.

note: The imperative kwu is common in speech, but many speakers would say kwuo here.

gloss: very large pot which can hold some 40 gallons of wine for feasting

examples.igbo: Ha jupụtara ìtè Agbāja na mmanya maka oriri.
examples.english: They filled the great pot with wine for the feast.

examples.igbo: Ị hụla ìtè Agbāja e ji mee emume a?
examples.english: Have you seen the great pot used for this ceremony?

examples.igbo: Ọ zụtara ànùnụ ngwe n'ahịa ụtụtụ a.
examples.english: She bought vegetables at the market this morning.

examples.igbo: Nne, tinye ànùnụ ngwe na ofe ahụ.
examples.english: Mother, put some vegetables in that soup.

examples.igbo: M tụkwàsị̀rị̀ obì na nwanne m.
examples.english: I relied on my brother.

examples.igbo: Ị na-atụkwàsị̀ obì na ya?
examples.english: Do you rely on him?

gloss: be far away, at a distance; stay for long; lasting

examples.igbo: Ụlọ ya notèrè akā n'ebe a.
examples.english: His house is far from here.

examples.igbo: Nọtè akā n'ụlọ, m ga-abịa.
examples.english: Stay long at home, I will come.

examples.igbo: Uwe m kọrọ akọ n'anyanwụ.
examples.english: My clothes dried in the sun.

examples.igbo: Kọọ akọ uwe gị tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Dry your clothes before you go out.

examples.igbo: O nyere m otu paụnd.
examples.english: He gave me one pound.

examples.igbo: Ego paụnd ole ka ị nwere?
examples.english: How many pounds do you have?

gloss: to hand something or someone over to somebody or something;

examples.igbo: O hafèrè m akwụkwọ ahụ.
examples.english: He handed the book over to me.

examples.igbo: Hafè ya n'aka onye uwe ojii.
examples.english: Hand him over to the police.

examples.igbo: O zụsịrị ndị ọrụ ya.
examples.english: He finished training his workers.

examples.igbo: Zụsịa ubi gị tupu ọ dịọ.
examples.english: Finish tending your farm before it gets dark.

examples.igbo: Nwanne m dịfùrù.
examples.english: My brother is well.

examples.igbo: Ị dịfùrù?
examples.english: Are you well?

gloss: the shrine of Ànì owned by the head of a compound, kept in front of his house

examples.igbo: Ànị ēzi dị n'ihu ụlọ onye isi.
examples.english: The Ani ezi is in front of the head's house.

examples.igbo: Ị hụla Ànị ēzi?
examples.english: Have you seen Ani ezi?

note: Cultural term; sense is specific to a shrine.

gloss: insert something into covering or mass (e.g. sword passed through belt, feather in hat or hair)

examples.igbo: O tùrù mma ya n'úkwù.
examples.english: He inserted his knife in his belt.

examples.igbo: Tù úkwù n'isi gị.
examples.english: Insert a feather in your hair.

examples.igbo: O nyere eze ifè nrù.
examples.english: He gave the king tribute.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akwụ ifè nrù?
examples.english: Are you paying tribute?

gloss: throw and kill; stone to death

examples.igbo: Ha tụgburu agwọ ahụ ji nkume n'ubi.
examples.english: They stoned that snake to death in the farm.

examples.igbo: Olee mgbe i tụgburu nnụnụ ji okwute?
examples.english: When did you stone a bird to death?

gloss: lock using a key or bolt

examples.igbo: O tụchiri ụzọ ụlọ ya tupu ọ pụọ.
examples.english: He locked his door before going out.

examples.igbo: Tụchie ụzọ ahụ ozugbo!
examples.english: Lock that door at once!

examples.igbo: Anyị jidere òbò ọdàa abụọ n'osimiri.
examples.english: We caught two Mormyrus rume in the river.

examples.igbo: Ị hụtụla òbò ọdàa n'ahịa?
examples.english: Have you seen Mormyrus rume in the market?

note: The fish name is specialized; examples are plausible but not certain of local usage.

examples.igbo: Akwa m dọwara n'oge ịsa ya.
examples.english: My cloth tore while washing it.

examples.igbo: Dọwaa akwa ochie ahụ n'ụzọ abụọ.
examples.english: Tear that old cloth into two.

examples.igbo: Ọ gabulu n'iru ibu ya.
examples.english: He went ahead with his load.

examples.igbo: Gabulu n'iru ibu a, anyị na-abịa.
examples.english: Go ahead with this load, we are coming.

note: The phrase is uncommon; the examples are plausible.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akpọ ya ànyaā mgbe ọ na-ewe iwe.
examples.english: She calls him ànyaā when she is angry.

examples.igbo: Ànyaā, gịnị ka ị chọrọ?
examples.english: Hey, what do you want?

note: The term is an address form; usage varies.

examples.igbo: Mama zụtara ofe Ìgbò n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: Mama bought Igbo palm-oil in the market today.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eji ofe Ìgbò esi nri?
examples.english: Do you use Igbo palm-oil to cook food?

note: Assuming ofe Ìgbò is a palm-oil variety.

gloss: a speech whereby the attributes are used to replace names; metonymy

examples.igbo: Ọkà okwu ji ahọ̀ọnọ̀chī kọwaa dike.
examples.english: The speaker used metonymy to describe the hero.

examples.igbo: Ị ma ihe ahọ̀ọnọ̀chī pụtara?
examples.english: Do you know what metonymy means?

note: A literary term; examples are limited to discussion of the term.

examples.igbo: Kpakpando na-egbuke egbuke n'abalị.
examples.english: Stars glitter at night.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ọla ahụ ji egbuke egbuke?
examples.english: Why does that jewelry glitter?

examples.igbo: Nne m kpachara ji tupu ọ sie ofe.
examples.english: My mother scraped yam before cooking soup.

examples.igbo: Kpachaa ji ndị a, anyị ga-esi nri.
examples.english: Scrape these yams, we will cook.

examples.igbo: O nyere onye uwe ojii n gàlì ka ọ hapụ ya.
examples.english: He gave the policeman a bribe to let him go.

examples.igbo: Ị na-enye ndị uwe ojii n gàlì?
examples.english: Are you bribing the police?

note: Uncertain about the exact form 'n gàlì'.

examples.igbo: Nnụnụ ahụ fenyere elu ozugbo.
examples.english: That bird flew up immediately.

examples.igbo: Fenienu elu, ụmụ nnụnụ!
examples.english: Fly up, birds!

note: Verb inflection may vary; 'feni' is assumed correct.

examples.igbo: O tere mmanụ n'ahụ nwa ya.
examples.english: She rubbed oil on her child's body.

examples.igbo: Tee mmanụ n'ahụ gị tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Rub oil on your body before you go out.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ ya bụ ọnụ na-ekwulụ nke obodo anyị.
examples.english: He is the spokesman of our town.

examples.igbo: Ị bụ ọnụ na-ekwulụ nke ezinụlọ a?
examples.english: Are you the spokesman of this family?

examples.igbo: Onye ònùmà na-ewe iwe ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: A hot-tempered person gets angry quickly.

examples.igbo: Bịa, onye ònùmà, jide onwe gị.
examples.english: Come, hot-tempered one, control yourself.

gloss: wizard; kind of male witch capable of travelling where it wishes unseen by day. Fewer in number than the ordinary witch, but capable of greater damage once offended (compare Yoruba ọsò)

examples.igbo: Ògbòmà ahụ na-efe efe n'ehihie.
examples.english: That ògbòmà flies during the day.

examples.igbo: Ị maara na ọ bụ ògbòmà?
examples.english: Do you know that he is an ògbòmà?

gloss: put aside; take out of the way; move aside (of light things)

examples.igbo: Wèrụka akwụkwọ ndị a n'ụzọ.
examples.english: Move these papers out of the way.

examples.igbo: Ị wèrụkala ihe ndị ahụ?
examples.english: Have you moved those things aside?

note: Verb form 'wèrụka' assumed correct.

examples.igbo: Nne m zụtara àchìchà n'ahịa.
examples.english: My mother bought biscuits at the market.

examples.igbo: Nye m àchìchà abụọ.
examples.english: Give me two biscuits.

gloss: panacea; medicine capable of curing all diseases (literally curer of 400 diseases)

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ ògwọ ǹnù ọyà, ọ na-agwọ ọrịa niile.
examples.english: It is a panacea, it cures all diseases.

examples.igbo: Ị chere na ògwọ ǹnù ọyà dị?
examples.english: Do you think a panacea exists?

examples.igbo: O cheere nri n'ihu ndị ọbịa.
examples.english: She placed food before the guests.

examples.igbo: Chee mmiri n'ihu ya ozugbo.
examples.english: Place water before him immediately.

note: Used standard spelling n'ihu for the entry's n'iru.

examples.igbo: O lọtara m maka nzukọ echi.
examples.english: He reminded me about tomorrow's meeting.

examples.igbo: Biko lọtalụ m ihe m ga-eme.
examples.english: Please remind me what I will do.

examples.igbo: Tachi obi, ihe ga-adị mma.
examples.english: Be firm, things will be well.

examples.igbo: O tachiri obi ruo ọgwụgwụ.
examples.english: He endured to the end.

gloss: seize by the throat; choke; throttle

examples.igbo: O tọdọrọ ya n'olu n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: He seized him by the throat on the road.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka ọ tọdo gị n'olu.
examples.english: Don't let him throttle you.

examples.igbo: Ọ gbara akaebe n'ụlọ ikpe.
examples.english: He bore witness in court.

examples.igbo: Gbaa akaebe maka nwanne gị.
examples.english: Stand surety for your brother.

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ bụ ọgbu anụ n'obodo.
examples.english: That man is an animal-killer in the town.

examples.igbo: Ògbu anụ ahụ gburu atụrụ anyị.
examples.english: That animal-killer killed our sheep.

examples.igbo: Ume kụpụrụ ya mgbe ọ nọ n'ọrụ.
examples.english: He fainted while at work.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka ume kụpụ gị.
examples.english: Don't let yourself faint.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụna mmiri zoro, anyị ga-aga ahịa.
examples.english: Even if it rains, we will go to market.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụna ị dara, gbalịa ọzọ.
examples.english: Even if you fail, try again.

gloss: different; separate; not the same as another

examples.igbo: Uwe m na uwe ya dị iche.
examples.english: My cloth and his are different.

examples.igbo: Iche dị n'etiti ha abụọ.
examples.english: There is a difference between the two.

examples.igbo: Nnụnụ ahụ fegoro elu n'elu osisi.
examples.english: That bird flew up onto the tree.

examples.igbo: Fego elu ka anyị hụ gị.
examples.english: Fly up so we can see you.

gloss: drink again, in addition, the remainder

examples.igbo: Ọ lakwuru mmiri fọdụrụ n'ite osi.
examples.english: She drank the remaining water in the cooking pot.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-alakwu mmiri ahụ fọdụrụ n'ite?
examples.english: Will you drink the rest of that water in the pot?

examples.igbo: Nwa m nwere ọnụ ūtọ, ọ na-eri swiiti.
examples.english: My child has a sweet tooth, he eats sweets.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere ọnụ ūtọ ma ọ bụ na ị nweghị?
examples.english: Do you have a sweet tooth or not?

examples.igbo: Nne ahụ kùrù nwa ya n'aka.
examples.english: That mother held her baby in her arms.

examples.igbo: Kùọ nwa ahụ n'aka, ọ na-ebe akwa.
examples.english: Hold that baby in your arms, he is crying.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-eme òyịyọ n'ihi agụụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: He is begging because of hunger in the market.

examples.igbo: Kwụsị òyịyọ, gaa rụọ ọrụ.
examples.english: Stop begging, go and work.

examples.igbo: Ònyụnyụ oriọna ahụ mere ka ụlọ bụrụ ọchịchịrị.
examples.english: The extinguishing of that lamp made the house dark.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ònyụnyụ oriọna ahụ n'abalị?
examples.english: Did you see the extinguishing of that lamp at night?

examples.igbo: Ha kèrè ada ha nye ezinụlọ ahụ.
examples.english: They gave their daughter in marriage to that family.

examples.igbo: Onye ka ị kèrè ada gị nye?
examples.english: Whom did you give your daughter to in marriage?

examples.igbo: Onye uwe ojii ahụ bu egbè n'aka.
examples.english: That policeman carried a gun in his hand.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere egbè n'ụlọ gị ugbu a?
examples.english: Do you have a gun in your house now?

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka ahụ na-akpasu nne ha iwe.
examples.english: Those children are provoking their mother.

examples.igbo: Kpasula nwanne gị iwe n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: Don't provoke your sibling at school.

examples.igbo: Ikpèlè m na-egbu mgbu mgbe m na-aga.
examples.english: My knee aches when I walk.

examples.igbo: Olee ebe ikpèlè gị merụrụ ahụ?
examples.english: Where did your knee get injured?

examples.igbo: Onye isi nyere anyị ikike ịbanye n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: The principal authorized us to enter the school.

examples.igbo: Ị nyere ya ikike ịkwọ ụgbọala?
examples.english: Did you authorize him to drive?

examples.igbo: Ọ dụrụ ubìlì mgbe ọ risịrị nri.
examples.english: He belched after he ate.

examples.igbo: Ị na-adụ ubìlì mgbe ọ bụla ị rie?
examples.english: Do you belch whenever you eat?

examples.igbo: Ìgbàdikē bụ egwu a na-agba n'ememme.
examples.english: Igbadike is a dance performed at festivals.

examples.igbo: Ị hụtụla ìgbàdikē n'ememme obodo?
examples.english: Have you seen Igbadike at the town festival?

examples.igbo: Chìfìa ájá ahụ n'ụkwụ gị.
examples.english: Scrub that sand off your feet.

examples.igbo: Nne na-achìfìa unyi n'aka nwa ya.
examples.english: The mother is scrubbing dirt off her child's hand.

gloss: the most elderly and most venerated form of the incarnate dead, of Igala origin (Igala ègwùgwù, = mmụọ ogonogo)

examples.igbo: Egwugwu bụ mmụọ ndị nna ochie kacha asọpụrụ.
examples.english: Egwugwu is the most revered ancestral spirit.

examples.igbo: Ị na-asọpụrụ egwugwu n'ememme obodo?
examples.english: Do you respect egwugwu at the town festival?

examples.igbo: Ǹsèli àzù na-eguzo n'akụkụ mmiri.
examples.english: The heron stands by the water.

examples.igbo: Ahụrụ m ǹsèli àzù ka ọ na-eri azụ.
examples.english: I saw a heron eating fish.

gloss: praying mantis (literally the one offering fight)

examples.igbo: Òche ògù nọ n'akwụkwọ osisi.
examples.english: The praying mantis is on the leaf.

examples.igbo: Nwa m jidere òche ògù n'aka.
examples.english: My child caught a praying mantis.

examples.igbo: N'ụtụtù ọma, anyị gara ubi.
examples.english: In the fine morning, we went to the farm.

examples.igbo: Ụtụtù ọma taa dị mma maka njem.
examples.english: Today's fine morning is good for a journey.

gloss: king of the birds, the eagle

examples.igbo: Ezè nnùnù na-efe elu igwe.
examples.english: The eagle flies high in the sky.

examples.igbo: Ezè nnùnù jidere ọkụkọ n'ubi.
examples.english: The eagle caught a chicken in the farm.

examples.igbo: Mgbanwè dị na ndụ mmadụ.
examples.english: Change is in human life.

examples.igbo: Mgbanwè ihu igwe na-emetụta ọrụ ugbo.
examples.english: Climate change affects farming.

gloss: a good for nothing; an irresponsible person

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ bụ òseēkā, ọ naghị arụ ọrụ.
examples.english: That man is a good-for-nothing; he does not work.

examples.igbo: Òseēkā anaghị ezu ụgwọ ụlọ ya.
examples.english: A good-for-nothing does not pay his house rent.

gloss: tsetse fly; blood sucking fly that transmits sleeping sickness

examples.igbo: Òdùdù tara ehi ahụ.
examples.english: A tsetse fly bit that cow.

examples.igbo: Gbuo òdùdù tupu ọ taa ehi.
examples.english: Kill the tsetse fly before it bites the cow.

examples.igbo: Nne m na-akwọ akpụ n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: My mother grates cassava in the morning.

examples.igbo: Kwọọ akpụ a ka anyị mee gari.
examples.english: Grate this cassava so we can make gari.

examples.igbo: O ji ùkpà rịgoro n'osisi.
examples.english: He used a climbing rope to climb the tree.

examples.igbo: Were ùkpà a rịa n'elu ugwu.
examples.english: Use this climbing rope to climb up the hill.

examples.igbo: Onye òtù Chukwu na-aga chọọchị ụbọchị Sọnde.
examples.english: A Christian goes to church on Sundays.

examples.igbo: Ị bụ onye òtù Chukwu?
examples.english: Are you a Christian?

examples.igbo: O nyere m kaadị ya.
examples.english: He gave me his card.

examples.igbo: Tinye kaadị a n'ime envelopu.
examples.english: Put this card inside the envelope.

examples.igbo: O kwachara ji n'ubi.
examples.english: He cut off yam roots on the farm.

examples.igbo: Kwacha ji ndị a ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Cut off the roots of these yams quickly.

gloss: kernels of unripe palm fruits (usually white)

examples.igbo: Nwata na-ata akụ ùtùtọlō.
examples.english: The child is chewing kernels of unripe palm fruits.

examples.igbo: Were akụ ùtùtọlō sie ofe.
examples.english: Use kernels of unripe palm fruits to cook soup.

gloss: to give thanks usually to God; to offer something in thanksgiving

examples.igbo: Anyị na-atụ mmām̄m̄ā nye Chukwu.
examples.english: We give thanks to God.

examples.igbo: Tụọ mmām̄m̄ā maka ihe ọma ahụ.
examples.english: Give thanks for that good thing.

examples.igbo: Ọ zụtara akwụkwọ ọfụlū n'ahịa.
examples.english: She bought a new book in the market.

examples.igbo: Akụkọ a dị n'akwụkwọ ọfụlū m.
examples.english: This story is in my new book.

examples.igbo: Ji anyị kụrụ n'ubi retọ̀la ugbu a.
examples.english: The yam we planted in the farm has become very rotten now.

examples.igbo: Tụfuo azụ retọ̀la ahụ tupu ọ kpata ọrịa.
examples.english: Throw away that rotten fish before it causes sickness.

examples.igbo: Anyị lọtara n'ètitī àbànì n'abalị ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: We returned at midnight last night.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-ala n'ètitī àbànì ma ọ bụ n'ụtụtụ?
examples.english: Will you go home at midnight or in the morning?

gloss: make a palm branch booth on a farm

examples.igbo: Ndị ọrụ na-eze ọdū n'ubi ji anyị.
examples.english: The workers are making palm branch booths on our yam farm.

examples.igbo: Zee ọdū ebe a ka anyị zuru ike.
examples.english: Make a palm booth here so we can rest.

gloss: pressure; need; difficulty; necessity; something pressing

examples.igbo: Mkpà ego na-enye ya nsogbu n'oge a.
examples.english: Financial pressure is troubling him at this time.

examples.igbo: Gịnị bụ mkpà gị ugbu a?
examples.english: What is your pressing need now?

examples.igbo: Ntụhị̀ eriri a siri ike nke ukwuu.
examples.english: The twist of this rope is very strong.

examples.igbo: Kee eriri ndị a ka ntụhị̀ ha sie ike.
examples.english: Tie these ropes so that their intertwining is strong.

examples.igbo: Ọ zụtara ùde oyìbo n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: She bought factory-prepared pomade at the market today.

examples.igbo: Ị na-etinye ùde oyìbo n'isi nwa gị?
examples.english: Do you apply factory-prepared pomade on your child's head?

examples.igbo: Anyị riri òpịrìma eghe n'ụtụtụ taa.
examples.english: We ate roasted plantain this morning.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara òpịrìma ole n'ahịa taa?
examples.english: How many plantains did you buy at the market today?

examples.igbo: Papa m na-asụ ọfịa n'ubi ọka.
examples.english: My father is cutting bush in the corn farm.

examples.igbo: Sụọ ọfịa tupu ị kụọ ji ọhụrụ.
examples.english: Cut the bush before you plant new yams.

examples.igbo: Òduduū nke ụtụtụ na-ama m ahụ.
examples.english: The morning damp/cold makes me feel cold.

examples.igbo: Ụlọ a jupụtara n'òduduū n'abalị niile.
examples.english: This house is filled with dampness all night.

gloss: in the twinkling of an eye; instantaneously; immediately; in a second

examples.igbo: O zuru ohi ahụ n'òfu ntabì anyā.
examples.english: He stole that in the twinkling of an eye.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eme ya n'òfu ntabì anyā?
examples.english: Will you do it in a second?

examples.igbo: Ọ dànyere n'okpuru ọchịchị eze.
examples.english: He submitted to the king's authority.

examples.igbo: Dànye n'aka ya, ọ gaghị eme gị ihe ọjọọ.
examples.english: Submit to him; he will not harm you.

examples.igbo: O lọjiri ọkụkọ ahụ olu.
examples.english: He broke that chicken's neck.

examples.igbo: A na-alọji ọkụkọ olu tupu esi ya?
examples.english: Do they break a chicken's neck before cooking it?

note: Entry shows 'onu'; standard Igbo for neck is 'olu'.

examples.igbo: O sechara mmanụ n'elu ofe ahụ.
examples.english: She skimmed the oil off the top of that soup.

examples.igbo: Secha mmanụ ahụ n'elu mmiri.
examples.english: Skim that oil off the water.

examples.igbo: O dụrụ m aka n'azụ.
examples.english: He poked me in the back.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji dụ m aka n'anya?
examples.english: Why did you poke me in the eye?

examples.igbo: O kpọbàtara anyị n'ụlọ ya.
examples.english: He welcomed us into his house.

examples.igbo: Kpọbàta ya n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: Call him into the house.

gloss: stay to block someone or something

examples.igbo: Nọ̀chì ha n'ọnụ ụzọ mere anyị egbu oge.
examples.english: Their blocking at the door made us late.

examples.igbo: Nọ̀chì n'okporo ụzọ na-egbochi ụgbọala ịgafe.
examples.english: Blocking on the road prevents vehicles from passing.

gloss: tree whose seed is used in making soup (Afzelia africana)

examples.igbo: Akpàlataā na-eto n'ime ọhịa.
examples.english: The akpalata tree grows in the forest.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-eji mkpụrụ akpàlataā eme ofe.
examples.english: We use akpalata seeds to make soup.

examples.igbo: Okwu ya na nke m dàkọrọ ọnū.
examples.english: His words and mine coincided.

examples.igbo: Ka anyị dàkọ ọnū n'okwu a.
examples.english: Let us be in harmony on this matter.

examples.igbo: Uwe ya na akpụkpọ ụkwụ ya dàkọrọ.
examples.english: Her dress and shoes matched.

examples.igbo: Ọ dịghị mma na okwu gị na omume gị adàkọghị.
examples.english: It is not good that your words and actions do not match.

gloss: be seated on flat surface (e.g. floor) and unable to stand

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ gwọlụrụ n'ala, o nweghị ike ibili.
examples.english: That child sat on the floor, unable to stand.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji gwọlụ n'ala, ị pụghị ibili?
examples.english: Why are you sitting on the floor, unable to stand?

examples.igbo: Ọ sùnyere osisi ahụ n’ala.
examples.english: He thrust that stick into the ground.

examples.igbo: Sùnye aka gị n’ime mmiri.
examples.english: Plunge your hand into the water.

examples.igbo: Òsefòtō ahụ sere anyị foto n’ahịa.
examples.english: That photographer took our photo at the market.

examples.igbo: Kpọọ òsefòtō ka o sere anyị foto.
examples.english: Call a photographer to take our photo.

examples.igbo: Ndùdùgandù a na-azụ ụmụaka n’ụzọ ọhụrụ.
examples.english: This generation raises children in a new way.

examples.igbo: Ndùdùgandù gị ọ na-akwanyere ndị okenye ùgwù?
examples.english: Does your generation respect elders?

note: I am not fully certain of this rare compound; I used it in the sense of 'generation'.

examples.igbo: Bọọlụ ahụ dàchighara azụ mgbe ọ kụrụ mgbidi.
examples.english: The ball rebounded back when it hit the wall.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere o ji dàchigha azụ n’okwukwe ya?
examples.english: Why did he backslide in his faith?

note: The phrase has several senses; the second example uses the 'backslide' sense.

examples.igbo: E nwere oghēle ọrụ n’ụlọ ọrụ ahụ.
examples.english: There is a job opportunity in that company.

examples.igbo: Oghēle a abụghị nke onye ọ bụla.
examples.english: This opportunity is not for everyone.

examples.igbo: O kpojuru ite ahụ mmiri.
examples.english: He filled that pot with water.

examples.igbo: Kpojuo ụgbọ ahụ mmanụ.
examples.english: Fill that vehicle with fuel.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-alụ afọ taa.
examples.english: That child has stomach-ache today.

examples.igbo: Ị na-alụ afọ mgbe i riri oke nri?
examples.english: Do you have stomach-ache when you eat too much?

note: I am not fully certain of this expression's everyday use, but the sentences follow the given meaning.

gloss: butt, knock with head (like fighting man)

examples.igbo: Ewu ahụ tiri isi n’ọnụ ụzọ.
examples.english: That goat butted the door with its head.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji eti isi nwa ahụ?
examples.english: Why did you butt that child with your head?

examples.igbo: Anyị zara osisi ndị ahụ n'ubi ọhụrụ.
examples.english: We transplanted those plants to a new farm.

examples.igbo: Zaa mkpụrụ osisi a n'ala ahụ.
examples.english: Transplant this seedling to that land.

note: The transplant sense of za is less common but attested.

examples.igbo: Ishishìugwù bụ akụkụ dị n'ahụ nwanyị.
examples.english: The clitoris is a part in a woman's body.

examples.igbo: Dọkịta nyochara ishishìugwù ya n'ụlọ ọgwụ.
examples.english: The doctor examined her clitoris in the hospital.

examples.igbo: Ha kwusara akụkọ ahụ n'obodo.
examples.english: They spread that news in the town.

examples.igbo: Kwusaa ya n'ọma ahịa.
examples.english: Spread it in the market.

examples.igbo: Unere a chaṅụrụ, ọ dịghị mma.
examples.english: This banana is overripe, it is not good.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụrụ na ọ chaṅụ, ụmụaka agaghị eri ya.
examples.english: If it is overripe, children will not eat it.

gloss: sweep something over something (e.g. vomit) so as to cover it completely

examples.igbo: O jiri ájá zachi ọgbụgbọ ahụ.
examples.english: He used sand to cover the vomit completely.

examples.igbo: Zachi ya ájá tupu mmiri abịa.
examples.english: Cover it with sand before the rain comes.

note: The verb zàchi is uncommon; these sentences follow the given sense.

examples.igbo: Wave nke osimiri ahụ tiri ụgbọ mmiri anyị.
examples.english: The wave of that sea hit our boat.

examples.igbo: Lee wave ahụ ka ọ na-akụ n'ụsọ osimiri.
examples.english: Look at that wave as it hits the shore.

note: Wave is an English loanword; usage may vary, and standard Igbo often uses ebili mmiri.

examples.igbo: Òne mgbè ị ga-aga ahịa?
examples.english: When will you go to the market?

examples.igbo: Òne mgbè ka anyị ga-ezute?
examples.english: When shall we meet?

gloss: use a malleable material to create something; mold; sculpt;

examples.igbo: O kpụrụ ite site n'ụrọ.
examples.english: He molded a pot from clay.

examples.igbo: Kpụọ nnụnụ na ụrọ.
examples.english: Mold a bird in clay.

gloss: be proud, arrogant, pompous, aloof, haughty

examples.igbo: O na-apàko n'ihi ego ya.
examples.english: He is arrogant because of his money.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji apàko?
examples.english: Why are you arrogant?

examples.igbo: O na-anyọ ụkọlọ n'oge ọrụ.
examples.english: He is lazy during work.

examples.igbo: Anyọla ụkọlọ, rụọ ọrụ gị.
examples.english: Don't be lazy, do your work.

examples.igbo: Nna m rụrụ ụkpà n'azụ ụlọ.
examples.english: My father built a hut behind the house.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ụkpà dị n'akụkụ ọhịa?
examples.english: Did you see the hut by the forest?

gloss: go out; go for a stroll

examples.igbo: Anyị na-apụ ìlo mgbe anyị rụchara ọrụ.
examples.english: We go out for a stroll after we finish work.

examples.igbo: Pụọ ìlo, ụmụaka na-egwu egwu.
examples.english: Go outside, the children are playing.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-ebi na mbara ala a.
examples.english: We live on this planet.

examples.igbo: Ị maara ihe dị na mbara ala ndị ọzọ?
examples.english: Do you know what is on other planets?

examples.igbo: Kwà mgbèdè, anyị na-eri nri abalị.
examples.english: Every evening, we eat dinner.

examples.igbo: Ị na-agụ akwụkwọ kwà mgbèdè?
examples.english: Do you read every evening?

gloss: miss a step; step into a wrong place or spot; misstep

examples.igbo: O zọhiè ụkwụ̄ wee daa n'ala.
examples.english: He missed a step and fell down.

examples.igbo: Ị zọhiè ụkwụ̄ n'ebe ahụ?
examples.english: Did you misstep there?

examples.igbo: Èbùnù ahụ na-ata ahịhịa n'ubi.
examples.english: That ram is grazing in the farm.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ere èbùnù gị n'ahịa?
examples.english: Are you selling your ram at the market?

examples.igbo: Sùlu òfu ibe nnī tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Take a piece of food before you leave.

examples.igbo: Sùlu òfu ibe nnī, nwa m.
examples.english: Take a piece of food, my child.

note: The headword is an imperative phrase, so both examples are commands; the phrase is used as given.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-atụtụkọ akwụkwọ n'ubi.
examples.english: We gather leaves in the farm.

examples.igbo: Tụtụkọnụ mkpụrụ ndị ahụ tupu mmiri ezo.
examples.english: Gather those seeds before it rains.

gloss: pluck, remove (grains of maize or ripe palm-fruits from cob or bunch respectively)

examples.igbo: O na-anwosị ọka n'ọkpụ.
examples.english: She is plucking maize from the cob.

examples.igbo: Nwosịa nkwụ ndị ahụ tupu anyị ahapụ ubi.
examples.english: Pluck those palm fruits before we leave the farm.

gloss: grub such as found in compost heap or decaying palm tree

examples.igbo: Àkpa dị n'ime ahịhịa rere ure.
examples.english: A grub is in the rotten grass.

examples.igbo: Ị hụtụla àkpa n'ọkpụ nkwụ?
examples.english: Have you seen a grub in a palm stump?

gloss: have a wear(shoe or cloth) on

examples.igbo: O sụrụ akpụkpọ ụkwụ ọhụrụ taa.
examples.english: He wore new shoes today.

examples.igbo: Sụọ akpụkpọ ụkwụ gị, anyị na-apụ.
examples.english: Put on your shoes, we are leaving.

examples.igbo: Òòbò ifē dị n'azụ ụlọ ahụ.
examples.english: There is a heap of something behind that house.

examples.igbo: O kụkọtara ihe ndị ahụ n'òòbò ifē.
examples.english: He gathered those things into a heap.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ kụrụ ànì isī ya n'ala.
examples.english: That child hit his skull on the ground.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ànì isī mmadụ n'ebe ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see a human skull there?

examples.igbo: O zere ndò n'okpuru osisi ahụ.
examples.english: He took shelter in the shade under that tree.

examples.igbo: Zee ndò n'okpuru ụlọ, anyanwụ na-ekpo ọkụ.
examples.english: Take shelter under the house, the sun is hot.

examples.igbo: O mụrụ nwa nwoke n'ụlọ ọgwụ.
examples.english: She gave birth to a boy in the hospital.

examples.igbo: Ị mụrụ nwa gị mgbe ole?
examples.english: When did you give birth to your child?

examples.igbo: O dọwara ụnò anwū n'elu akwa.
examples.english: He hung the mosquito net over the bed.

examples.igbo: Ụnò anwū adịghị, anwụ tara anyị.
examples.english: The mosquito net is not there, mosquitoes bit us.

examples.igbo: O jikwara uwe ya nke ọma.
examples.english: He dressed his clothes well.

examples.igbo: Jikwaa onwe gị ngwa ngwa, anyị na-apụ.
examples.english: Get yourself ready quickly, we are leaving.

examples.igbo: O mezuru ọrụ ahụ taa.
examples.english: He completed that work today.

examples.igbo: Mezue ihe niile tupu anyị apụ.
examples.english: Complete everything before we leave.

examples.igbo: O gbatịrị àrụ ya n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: He stretched his body in the morning.

examples.igbo: Gbatịa àrụ gị tupu ị gbaa ọsọ.
examples.english: Stretch your body before you run.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ yi uwe ngịlịga gaa akwụkwọ.
examples.english: That child wore ragged clothes to school.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ iyi uwe ngịlịga n'ahịa?
examples.english: Do you want to wear ragged clothes to the market?

gloss: praise-name for someone who has taken highest title

examples.igbo: E nyere ya aha Igwē nā-ezùlu òrà mgbe o mechara emume ahụ.
examples.english: He was given the name Igwē nā-ezùlu òrà after he completed that ceremony.

examples.igbo: Ì bụ Igwē nā-ezùlu òrà nke obodo a?
examples.english: Are you the Igwē nā-ezùlu òrà of this town?

examples.igbo: Àhụ ya dị ọcha mgbe ọ si n'ọdọ mmiri pụta.
examples.english: His body was clean when he came out of the river.

examples.igbo: Olee ebe àhụ na-egbu ya?
examples.english: Where is his body aching?

gloss: hold someone responsible; hold on to

examples.igbo: Gado akā na ya maka ihe ahụ.
examples.english: Hold him responsible for that thing.

examples.igbo: Ị gado akā na eriri ahụ?
examples.english: Are you holding on to that rope?

note: The phrase is not common in all dialects; both senses are shown.

examples.igbo: Ji ahụ luru èlù mgbe e siri ya.
examples.english: The yam became soft when it was cooked.

examples.igbo: Sie ya ka ọ lù èlù.
examples.english: Cook it so that it becomes soft.

note: The past form luru èlù may vary by speaker.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-akwụ ụgbà n'ama.
examples.english: The children are doing somersaults in the compound.

examples.igbo: Kwụọ ụgbà otu ugboro ka anyị hụ.
examples.english: Do a somersault once so we can see.

examples.igbo: Akpù onū na-etolite n'olu ya.
examples.english: A goitre is growing on his neck.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-aga ụlọ ọgwụ maka akpù onū?
examples.english: Is he going to the hospital because of goitre?

examples.igbo: Kpamkpamkpam, onye ahụ kụrụ aka n'ọnụ ụzọ.
examples.english: Knock knock knock, the person knocked on the door.

examples.igbo: Anụrụ m kpamkpamkpam n'abalị.
examples.english: I heard a knock-knock at night.

examples.igbo: Nwantàkịrị ahụ na-ebe akwa.
examples.english: That small child is crying.

examples.igbo: Onye na-elekọta nwantàkịrị a?
examples.english: Who is caring for this small child?

examples.igbo: Ọ̀gbatùmtùm ya na-ada ụda n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: His motorcycle is making noise on the road.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eji ọ̀gbatùmtùm aga ọrụ?
examples.english: Do you use a motorcycle to go to work?

examples.igbo: Ha busàrà nkume ndị ahụ n'ala.
examples.english: They scattered those stones on the ground.

examples.igbo: Bụsà ji ndị a n'ọba.
examples.english: Scatter these yams in the barn.

gloss: make low groan; grunt (e.g. as seriously ill person, animals)

examples.igbo: Onye ọrịa ahụ na-asù udè n'abalị.
examples.english: That sick person groans at night.

examples.igbo: Ewu ahụ sùrù udè mgbe anyị jidere ya.
examples.english: The goat grunted when we held it.

examples.igbo: O nyere m otu oko ọkà.
examples.english: He gave me one ear of corn.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara m oko ọkà ole n'ahịa?
examples.english: How many ears of corn did you buy for me at the market?

examples.igbo: Ha bụrụ abù mgbasà mgbe oriri gwusịrị.
examples.english: They sang the dismissal song when the feast ended.

examples.igbo: Bụrụ abù mgbasà ka ụmụaka laa.
examples.english: Sing the dismissal song so the children can go home.

examples.igbo: O sechara mmanụ n'elu ofe ahụ.
examples.english: She skimmed the oil from the top of that soup.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-esecha abụba n'ahụ ya ugbu a.
examples.english: She is slimming down now.

examples.igbo: O kpọrọ okpùlùkpu òkwè n'ememme.
examples.english: He played the stringed instrument at the festival.

examples.igbo: Ị maara ịkpọ okpùlùkpu òkwè?
examples.english: Do you know how to play the stringed instrument?

examples.igbo: O gosiri nchèghalị mgbe anyị tara ya ahụhụ.
examples.english: He showed repentance when we punished him.

examples.igbo: Nchèghalị ya mere ka anyị gbaghara ya.
examples.english: His repentance made us forgive him.

gloss: drought; extended dry season; severe dry season; long period without rain

examples.igbo: Mkpọ ānwụ bibiri ihe ọkụkụ anyị.
examples.english: Drought destroyed our crops.

examples.igbo: Osimiri na-akpọ nkụ n'oge mkpọ ānwụ.
examples.english: Rivers dry up during drought.

examples.igbo: Onye ikpe kèrè ikpe ahụ n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: The judge gave that judgement in the morning.

examples.igbo: Kèe ikpe ziri ezi, ọ bụghị ikpe aka ike.
examples.english: Give a just judgement, not an arbitrary judgement.

examples.igbo: Àluluū dị n'elu mmiri n'ụtụtụ taa.
examples.english: Mist is on the water this morning.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ àluluū n'elu ugwu ụnyaahụ?
examples.english: Did you see mist on the hill yesterday?

examples.igbo: Nne m kèwara achịcha ahụ ụzọ abụọ.
examples.english: My mother divided that bread into two.

examples.igbo: Kèwaa osikapa ahụ n'ime efere abụọ.
examples.english: Divide that rice into two plates.

examples.igbo: Àda nne nnē m na-ere azụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: My maternal aunt sells fish in the market.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eleta àda nne nnē gị taa?
examples.english: Will you visit your maternal aunt today?

note: The phrase is used as given; one might also say àda nne m.

examples.igbo: Nwanne m na-ejerube n'ahịa kwa ụbọchị.
examples.english: My brother goes round the market every day.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ ijerube n'ahịa obodo taa?
examples.english: Do you want to go round the town market today?

note: Inflected forms na-ejerube and ijerube are used; the stem is uncommon.

examples.igbo: Akpụkpọ ụkwụ m dọwara agbawa taa.
examples.english: My shoe tore today.

examples.igbo: Zụta akpụkpọ ụkwụ ọhụrụ maka nwa gị.
examples.english: Buy new shoes for your child.

examples.igbo: Ha gbakpọrọ ìzù megide onyeisi ha.
examples.english: They plotted secretly against their leader.

examples.igbo: Egbakpọla ìzù megide nwanne gị n'ụlọ.
examples.english: Do not plot secretly against your brother at home.

examples.igbo: Anyanwụ na-ada n'òdìdà anyanwū n'oge mgbede.
examples.english: The sun sets in the west in the evening.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ òdìdà anyanwū taa n'akụkụ osimiri?
examples.english: Did you see the sunset today by the river?

examples.igbo: Àbànì dì egwù wakporo obodo anyị n'abalị.
examples.english: Bandits attacked our town at night.

examples.igbo: Ndị uwe ojii jidere àbànì dì egwù ahụ?
examples.english: Did the police catch that bandit?

examples.igbo: Bìlìbìlì dị n'elu igwe n'ụtụtụ taa.
examples.english: There is cloudiness in the sky this morning.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ahụ bìlìbìlì n'elu mmiri ugbu a?
examples.english: Do you see cloudiness on the water now?

note: Bìlìbìlì is uncommon; the examples keep the cloudiness/dimness sense.

examples.igbo: M zụtara òkpa ìkele n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: I bought groundnut in the market today.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ere òkpa ìkele n'ụlọ gị?
examples.english: Do you sell groundnut in your house?

examples.igbo: Ha lụrụ ògù ikpe ōmụma megide nwa agbọghọ ahụ.
examples.english: They fought an unjust fight against that girl.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji lụọ ògù ikpe ōmụma?
examples.english: Why did you fight an unjust fight?

examples.igbo: Etinyela aka n'ùwa ōnye òzọ.
examples.english: Don't interfere in another person's business.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-etinye aka n'ùwa ōnye òzọ mgbe niile.
examples.english: He always interferes in other people's business.

examples.igbo: Anyị riri urù n'ahịa ahụ.
examples.english: We made a profit in that market.

examples.igbo: Ì riri urù n'ahịa taa?
examples.english: Did you make a profit in the market today?

examples.igbo: Ha chetèrè akā ruo mgbe chi bọrọ.
examples.english: They waited for a long time until dawn.

examples.igbo: Chetè akā tupu i laa.
examples.english: Wait for a long time before you leave.

examples.igbo: Nwa ọhụrụ na-ebe akwa n'ihi agụụ.
examples.english: The baby is crying because of hunger.

examples.igbo: Kwụsị ịbe akwa, nne gị nọ ebe a.
examples.english: Stop crying, your mother is here.

examples.igbo: Ihe ahụ dara n'ụkwụ m.
examples.english: That thing happened in my presence.

examples.igbo: Ọ dara n'ụkwụ gị?
examples.english: Did it happen in your presence?

gloss: I am going to sow pepper seeds (broadcast)

examples.igbo: Anà m èje ịghā osè n'ubi taa.
examples.english: I am going to sow pepper seeds in the farm today.

examples.igbo: Anà m èje ịghā osè, ị na-abịa?
examples.english: I am going to sow pepper seeds, are you coming?

examples.igbo: Ọ machasịlị ụzọ ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: He knows that road well.

examples.igbo: Ị machasịlị obodo anyị?
examples.english: Do you know our town well?

examples.igbo: O kụrụ mkpụrụ ọka n'ubi.
examples.english: He planted maize seeds in the farm.

examples.igbo: Kụọ mkpụrụ osisi n'ogige.
examples.english: Plant fruit seeds in the garden.

gloss: be zealous, enthusiastic; agitate; anger; enrage

examples.igbo: Ọ nụrụ ọkụ n'obì ịmụ ihe ọhụrụ.
examples.english: He was eager to learn something new.

examples.igbo: Ha nụrụ ọkụ n'obì mgbe e zuru ego ha.
examples.english: They were enraged when their money was stolen.

examples.igbo: Ùme òmùmù na-ewute nne ya.
examples.english: The frequent loss of newborns saddens her mother.

examples.igbo: Gịnị na-akpata ùme òmùmù n'ezinụlọ a?
examples.english: What causes frequent loss of newborns in this family?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ele ọbị̀à anya mgbe ọ bụla.
examples.english: He entertains visitors whenever.

examples.igbo: Lee anyị ọbị̀à anya taa.
examples.english: Entertain us today.

examples.igbo: Gogògo dị n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: Gogogo is in the market today.

examples.igbo: Anyị zụtara gogògo abụọ.
examples.english: We bought two gogogo.

examples.igbo: Ọ gbakwutere m n'ọsọ.
examples.english: He ran towards me.

examples.igbo: Gbakwute ụlọ ahụ ngwa ngwa!
examples.english: Run towards that house quickly!

gloss: extreme part of a surface or an item; extreme or end

examples.igbo: O guzoro n'isiisi tebụl.
examples.english: He stood at the edge of the table.

examples.igbo: Gaa ruo n'isiisi okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: Go to the end of the road.

gloss: fear; be afraid; be cowardly, timid (less common than -tụ egwù)

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-ajọ ụjọ n'abalị.
examples.english: Children are afraid at night.

examples.igbo: Ajọla ụjọ, anyị nọ ebe a.
examples.english: Don't be afraid, we are here.

examples.igbo: Njìkọ aka anyị mere ka anyị nwee ike.
examples.english: Our joining hands made us strong.

examples.igbo: Njìkọ nke ndị otu ahụ dị mkpa.
examples.english: The joining of that group is important.

examples.igbo: Afànnà ya bụ Okeke.
examples.english: His surname is Okeke.

examples.igbo: Kedu afànnà gị?
examples.english: What is your surname?

examples.igbo: O dere akàrà ajụ̀jụ n'ikpeazụ ahịrịokwu.
examples.english: He wrote a question mark at the end of the sentence.

examples.igbo: Akàrà ajụ̀jụ na-egosi na ọ bụ ajụjụ.
examples.english: A question mark shows that it is a question.

examples.igbo: Nkịta ahụ na-eyi ụmụaka egwù.
examples.english: That dog frightens the children.

examples.igbo: Gịnị na-eyi gị egwù?
examples.english: What frightens you?

examples.igbo: Ịnyịnya ibu na-ebu osisi n'ọhịa.
examples.english: The donkey carries wood in the forest.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ịnyịnya ibu n'ụzọ ahịa?
examples.english: Did you see the donkey on the market road?

note: Ass taken as donkey; standard spelling ịnyịnya ibu.

examples.igbo: O nọ na-asụ udè n'ihi mgbu.
examples.english: He was groaning because of pain.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji asụ udè?
examples.english: Why are you groaning?

examples.igbo: Ànìegbòka bụ nwa nwanne m.
examples.english: Aniegbo is my cousin.

examples.igbo: Ànìegbòka, bịa rie nri.
examples.english: Aniegbo, come and eat.

examples.igbo: O kewara anụ ahụ nkerì.
examples.english: He divided the meat into bits.

examples.igbo: Kee ji a nkerì tupu ị sie ya.
examples.english: Cut this yam into bits before you cook it.

examples.igbo: Kwụpụ mkpuchi karama ahụ.
examples.english: Uncork that bottle.

examples.igbo: O kwụpụrụ mkpuchi karama mmiri ahụ.
examples.english: He uncorked the bottle of water.

examples.igbo: O tapuru akị.
examples.english: He bit open a palm nut.

examples.igbo: Tapuo mkpụrụ ahụ ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Bite that seed open quickly.

gloss: Awka; name of a place in Igbo land

examples.igbo: Ọka bụ obodo dị na Anambra.
examples.english: Awka is a town in Anambra.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-aga Ọka echi.
examples.english: We are going to Awka tomorrow.

examples.igbo: Welie aka gị elu ma ọ bụrụ na ị maara azịza.
examples.english: Raise your hand if you know the answer.

examples.igbo: Ọ weliri aka ya zaa ajụjụ ahụ.
examples.english: He raised his hand and answered the question.

examples.igbo: Ọ dàjụrụ obì nna ya.
examples.english: He appeased his father.

examples.igbo: Dàjụ obì nne gị tupu ị laa.
examples.english: Appease your mother before you go.

examples.igbo: O jiri osisi tinyụ ọkụ.
examples.english: He used a stick to beat out the fire.

examples.igbo: Tinyụ ọkụ ahụ tupu o gbasaa.
examples.english: Beat out that fire before it spreads.

gloss: push out; sail, push off (a boat); set off (in vehicle)

examples.igbo: Ha nupụrụ ụgbọ mmiri n'ọdụ.
examples.english: They pushed off the boat from the shore.

examples.igbo: Ole mgbe ị ga-anupụ?
examples.english: When will you set off?

gloss: feast for a child (e.g. outing, christening, etc.) ( -ŋù 1. rejoice)

examples.igbo: Ha mere aŋùlị nnwā n'ụbọchị Sọnde.
examples.english: They held a child's feast on Sunday.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-abịa aŋùlị nnwā anyị?
examples.english: Will you come to our child's feast?

examples.igbo: Òli ǹzèlè ahụ bụ onye obiọma.
examples.english: That chief is a kind person.

examples.igbo: Òli ǹzèlè, bịanụ n'ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: Chief, come to our house.

examples.igbo: Anyị gbara anyàsì n'elekere asaa.
examples.english: We took supper at seven.

examples.igbo: Ị gbara anyàsì?
examples.english: Have you taken supper?

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-agbaghalị n'okporo ámá.
examples.english: Children are running about in the street.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji agbaghalị n'efu?
examples.english: Why are you running about in vain?

examples.igbo: O ji okwu ọjọọ sa nwa ya isī.
examples.english: He brainwashed his child with bad words.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka ha saa gị isī.
examples.english: Don't let them brainwash you.

examples.igbo: Onye nche kụrụ ọgẹnẹ ụtụtụ taa.
examples.english: The guard struck the gong this morning.

examples.igbo: Kụọ ọgẹnẹ ka ndị obodo zukọta.
examples.english: Strike the gong so that the villagers gather.

note: The tone marks on ọgẹnẹ are uncertain; the word and the sense (metal gong) are clear.

examples.igbo: O tụkọnyesịrị ahịhịa ndị ahụ n'ọkụ.
examples.english: He gathered the grass and threw it into the fire.

examples.igbo: Tụkọnyesịa mkpụrụ ndị a n'ite.
examples.english: Gather these seeds together and throw them into the pot.

note: Inflected forms (tụkọnyesịrị, tụkọnyesịa) are the expected ones, but the stem is uncommon.

gloss: seize for debt; seize wrongly for debt

examples.igbo: Ha wefiri ewu ya maka ụgwọ o ji.
examples.english: They seized his goat for the debt he owed.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji wefie ụgwọ ya?
examples.english: Why did you seize his goods for the debt?

note: Past form wefiri follows the -fie pattern.

gloss: (literally wine that enters the eyes - mostly used in Bible)

examples.igbo: Akwụkwọ Nsọ na-ekwu maka mmanya na-abà n'anya.
examples.english: The Bible speaks about wine that goes into the eyes.

examples.igbo: Ị ma ihe mmanya na-abà n'anya pụtara?
examples.english: Do you know what 'wine that enters the eyes' means?

note: The phrase is a set Biblical expression rather than everyday speech, so the examples are built around that usage.

gloss: be soft (as ripe fruit); be soft and wet, soggy (as muddy ground, wet clothes); dissolve in water (compare -di-dè)

examples.igbo: Mangoro ndị a na-adè ugbu a.
examples.english: These mangoes are getting soft now.

examples.igbo: Akwa ahụ dere mmiri, o kpọrọ nkụ ọzọ?
examples.english: That cloth is soggy with water; has it dried again?

note: The sense (be soft, soggy) is clear, but I am not fully sure of the inflected forms dere / na-adè, and -dè is easily confused with dè 'write'.

examples.igbo: Mmanya ahụ tara ụka.
examples.english: That palm wine is sour.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ofe a ji ata ụka?
examples.english: Why does this soup taste sour?

note: ụka 'sourness' appears in the collocation ịta ụka; tone marks are not given in the entry.

examples.igbo: O chekwatara ego maka agụmakwụkwọ ụmụ ya.
examples.english: He saved money for his children's education.

examples.igbo: Ị na-echekwata ego ole n'ọnwa?
examples.english: How much do you save in a month?

examples.igbo: Anyị zutere ya n'isi ọzara.
examples.english: We met him at the edge of the grassland.

examples.igbo: Ewu na-ata ahịhịa n'isi ọzara.
examples.english: The goat grazes at the edge of the grassland.

note: The entry gives tones òzàlà; I write ọzara without tone marks.

examples.igbo: Mbè na-eje nwayọ nwayọ.
examples.english: The tortoise walks slowly.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka ahụ jidere mbè n'ọhịa.
examples.english: Those children caught a tortoise in the bush.

gloss: fold hands; clasp hands between knees; sit with one's hands in one's lap; sit idle

examples.igbo: Ọ nọdụrụ fànye aka n'ụkwụ, ọ dịghị arụ ọrụ.
examples.english: He sat with hands clasped between knees, not working.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji fànye aka n'ụkwụ? Bilie!
examples.english: Why are you sitting idle? Get up!

examples.igbo: Pùni, anyị na-aga ugbo.
examples.english: Rise up, we are going to the farm.

examples.igbo: Anyanwụ na-apùni n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: The sun is rising in the morning.

examples.igbo: Ọ gbara asọ n'ala.
examples.english: He spat on the ground.

examples.igbo: Gbaa asọ n'èzí, ọ bụghị n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: Spit outside, not inside the house.

gloss: area raised or demarcated within the òbi to keep ritual objects

examples.igbo: O tinyere ọgwụ n'iru ùkpò.
examples.english: He put the medicine in the iru ùkpò.

examples.igbo: Ị ma ebe iru ùkpò dị?
examples.english: Do you know where the iru ùkpò is?

note: The term is culturally specific; sentences are plausible but might vary by dialect.

examples.igbo: Nna m gbara àfù ọnū mgbe ọ dị obere.
examples.english: My father grew a beard when he was young.

examples.igbo: Ị na-agba àfù ọnū? Ị bụ okenye ugbua.
examples.english: Are you growing a beard? You are an adult now.

gloss: a road barricade put in place to prevent crossing; a roadblock

examples.igbo: Ndị uwe ojii gbara òkwelagha n'ụzọ.
examples.english: The police set up a roadblock on the road.

examples.igbo: Òkwelagha dị n'ụzọ a?
examples.english: Is there a roadblock on this road?

examples.igbo: Nne m na-aga ùsokwū mgbe ọ bụla.
examples.english: My mother goes to the woman's house every time.

examples.igbo: Gaa n'ùsokwū, ị ga-ahụ ndị inyom.
examples.english: Go to the woman's house, you will see the women.

note: The word may be less common in some areas; sentences are based on the given meaning.

gloss: rod of wood; stalk of plant; stem of young tree of sapling

examples.igbo: Okpòlò osisi ahụ toro ogologo.
examples.english: That sapling grew tall.

examples.igbo: Were okpòlò osisi kwụchie ụzọ.
examples.english: Use a wooden rod to bar the road.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ekwu okwu n'olu dara ụda.
examples.english: He is speaking in a loud voice.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ị na-ekwu okwu n'oge nri?
examples.english: Why are you speaking during the meal?

examples.igbo: Ha bere àlìlì maka nna ha nwụrụ.
examples.english: They mourned for their late father.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ị na-ebe àlìlì? Ọ dịghị ihe ọjọọ mere.
examples.english: Why are you lamenting? Nothing bad happened.

examples.igbo: O zoro ife nzuzo ya n'ime akpa.
examples.english: He hid his secret thing inside the bag.

examples.igbo: Gịnị bụ ife nzuzo ị na-ekwu?
examples.english: What is the secret thing you are talking about?

note: Headword ife is dialectal; standard Igbo is ihe nzuzo.

examples.igbo: Ndị uwe ojii jidere ya na ìgbo.
examples.english: The police caught him with marijuana.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ere ìgbo n'ahịa?
examples.english: Are you selling marijuana in the market?

examples.igbo: Nne m na-asụ nrī n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: My mother pounds food in the morning.

examples.igbo: Sụọ nrī ahụ ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Pound that food quickly.

examples.igbo: Nwa agbọghọ ahụ nwere ifele.
examples.english: That girl is shy.

examples.igbo: Nwee ifele n'ihu ndị ọbịa.
examples.english: Be reserved in front of guests.

examples.igbo: Ha tụrụ ụlọ akịlịka n'ime obodo.
examples.english: They built a grass-roofed house in the village.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-atụ ụlọ akịlịka n'afọ a?
examples.english: Will you build a grass-roofed house this year?

note: Headword uses dialectal unò; standard Igbo is ụlọ.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ese anwụ̀rụ̀ n'ụlọ.
examples.english: He smokes tobacco in the house.

examples.igbo: Esekwala anwụ̀rụ̀ ebe a.
examples.english: Don't smoke tobacco here.

gloss: to abide; stay; be with with someone

examples.igbo: Ọ nọ̀nyèrè anyị n'ụlọ.
examples.english: He stayed with us at home.

examples.igbo: Nọ̀nyèrè m ebe a.
examples.english: Stay with me here.

examples.igbo: Ọ chìchapụrụ m anya.
examples.english: He stared at me.

examples.igbo: Chìchapụla m anya otú ahụ.
examples.english: Don't glare at me like that.

examples.igbo: Osisi ahụ ra ìfulū.
examples.english: That tree blossomed.

examples.igbo: Osisi ndị a na-ara ìfulū n'oge ọkọchị?
examples.english: Do these trees blossom in the dry season?

note: The word ìfulū is used here in the sense of blossom or flower.

gloss: cease to expect; give up hope (literally remove mind)

examples.igbo: Ọ wèpụrụ uchè na nne ya ga-alọta.
examples.english: He gave up hope that his mother would return.

examples.igbo: Ị wèpụrụ uchè na ọ ga-abịa?
examples.english: Have you given up hope that he will come?

examples.igbo: O nyere nwa ya otu ǹju ọnū osikapa.
examples.english: She gave her child one mouthful of rice.

examples.igbo: Nye m otu ǹju ọnū ofe.
examples.english: Give me one mouthful of soup.

examples.igbo: Anyị gbakọbara ọnụ n'ụlọ nzukọ.
examples.english: We assembled in the meeting hall.

examples.igbo: Gbakọba ọnụ ebe a tupu anyị apụ.
examples.english: Assemble here before we leave.

examples.igbo: Ntilì nke ite ahụ wutere nne m.
examples.english: The breaking of that pot pained my mother.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ntilì nke iko ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see the breaking of that cup?

note: Sense is 'breaking into pieces'; sentences are grammatical but I would phrase them differently.

examples.igbo: O ji mma kwacha àkwacha n'osisi ahụ.
examples.english: He used a knife to chip pieces off that wood.

examples.igbo: Kwacha àkwacha ntakịrị n'osisi a.
examples.english: Chip a little off this wood.

gloss: title; holder of Ògbu āgụ title

examples.igbo: Nna ya bụ Ògbu āgụ n'obodo anyị.
examples.english: His father is the Ògbu āgụ in our town.

examples.igbo: Ị maara onye bụ Ògbu āgụ ebe a?
examples.english: Do you know who is the Ògbu āgụ here?

examples.igbo: Ọkụkọ ahụ bùrụ ụmụ ya n'ime akwa.
examples.english: That hen pecked the eggshells open for her chicks.

examples.igbo: Ọkụkọ gị ọ bùrụla ụmụ ya?
examples.english: Has your hen pecked the shells open for her chicks?

note: The compound -bù ụmù is not one I know well; the sentences are my best guess and may not match usage.

examples.igbo: Ọ gbaghaara m okwu n'ihu mmadụ.
examples.english: He contradicted me in front of people.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji agbagha m okwu?
examples.english: Why are you contradicting me?

examples.igbo: Anyị jìkọtara aka n'ọrụ ubi.
examples.english: We joined hands in the farm work.

examples.igbo: Jìkọta osisi abụọ a ọnụ.
examples.english: Join these two sticks together.

examples.igbo: Ọ kwachara agbụ osisi ahụ.
examples.english: He scraped off the bark of that tree.

examples.igbo: Kwacha ya nke ọma tupu ị tee ya mmanụ.
examples.english: Scrape it well before you apply oil to it.

examples.igbo: Ọdị̀nakachūkwū, anyị ga-eme nke ọma.
examples.english: It is in God's hands, we will do well.

examples.igbo: Ị kwenyere na ọdị̀nakachūkwū?
examples.english: Do you believe it is in God's hands?

note: Fixed expression; examples treat it as a quoted phrase.

examples.igbo: Ọ kwụsiri ike n'okwu ya.
examples.english: He stood firm on his word.

examples.igbo: Kwụsie ike mgbe ihe siri ike.
examples.english: Stand firm when things are hard.

gloss: stretch oneself (as sometimes done when yawning or during exhaustion or idleness)

examples.igbo: Mgbe ọ tetara, ọ sere ụtịrị̄.
examples.english: When he woke up, he stretched himself.

examples.igbo: Sè ụtịrị̄ tupu ị bido ọrụ.
examples.english: Stretch yourself before you start work.

note: The phrase is specialized; I believe the inflections are correct.

examples.igbo: Edensìbịa akwụkwọ a dị n'ikpeazụ.
examples.english: The bibliography of this book is at the end.

examples.igbo: Ọ tinyere edensìbịa na akwụkwọ ya.
examples.english: He included a bibliography in his book.

examples.igbo: Ọ yikasịrị afọ ya na mma.
examples.english: He cut his stomach open with a knife.

examples.igbo: Yikasịla aka gị na mma ahụ!
examples.english: Don't cut your hand open with that knife!

note: Rare verb; examples use a body-part object rather than a bare reflexive.

examples.igbo: Ọ rìnyere anyị ego ahụ.
examples.english: He handed over that money to us.

examples.igbo: Rìnye ya akwụkwọ a tupu ọ pụọ.
examples.english: Hand this book over to him before he leaves.

examples.igbo: Osisi ahụ na-ese n'elu mmiri.
examples.english: That wood floats on water.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ka akwa ahụ sere n'elu mmiri?
examples.english: Did you see how that cloth floated on water?

examples.igbo: Ònìnì nna ya ga-ewe ụbọchị atọ.
examples.english: His father's burial will take three days.

examples.igbo: Anyị gara ònìnì nwanne ya nwanyị.
examples.english: We went to her sister's burial.

gloss: praise someone and remind him of what his forefathers did, sometimes to encourage him to undertake new enterprises; chant praise-poetry

examples.igbo: Ha tiri ya mkpùkpò n'ụlọ ọha.
examples.english: They chanted praise-poetry for him in the village square.

examples.igbo: Tie nwa gị mkpùkpò ka o nwee obi ike.
examples.english: Chant praise-poetry for your child so he may have courage.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-agha mkpụlū n'ubi ya.
examples.english: He is broadcasting seeds in his farm.

examples.igbo: Ghaa mkpụlū tupu mmiri ezie.
examples.english: Broadcast the seeds before the rain falls.

gloss: change into a better, newer or advanced version; shed (skin or leaves); metamorphose

examples.igbo: Osisi na-enwe nwò akwụkwọ n'oge ọkọchị.
examples.english: Trees undergo leaf shedding in the dry season.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ nwò agwọ n'ọhịa?
examples.english: Did you see a snake's slough in the bush?

examples.igbo: O runatara iji bulie nwa ya.
examples.english: She stooped down a bit to lift her child.

examples.igbo: Runata ntakịrị ka anyị hụ ihe ahụ.
examples.english: Stoop down a bit so we can see that thing.

examples.igbo: Size akpụkpọ ụkwụ m bụ isii.
examples.english: My shoe size is six.

examples.igbo: Kedu size uwe ị chọrọ?
examples.english: What size dress do you want?

gloss: blacksmith's hammer (the biggest of all the blacksmith's hammers). This tool is ceremonially the most important item for an apprentice who has just completed his period of apprenticeship and is going to set up as a master blacksmith, in that it is symbolic of his master's status. On the day of the celebration of his freedom, which features much feasting, the otùtù is set on a stool in the middle of the gathering of master smiths who were invited to the occasion. Shortly before the celebration is over the young master is called to the middle. The master holds out the otùtù towards the young master as one who is handing to another a staff of office. The master recites some blessings and incantations, at the end of which he hands the otùtù to the young master. An apprentice who has completed his course but who has not completed his obligations (usually monetary) is not given the otùtù and his freedom is not celebrated. The apprentice can leave his master for some period in search of money. He sometimes has to secure a temporary job, like farm labour, to get the required money, both for his training fees and for the celebration expenses. He then comes back to do the freedom celebration. To every master smith the otùtù is the most important item in his tools, for though it is rarely used because of its weight, the blacksmith, particularly the non-Christian one, kills cocks on top of his otùtù from time to time and on special occasions, letting the blood pour over the otùtù. Afterwards some down is scattered on top of the wet blood, which sticks it firmly to the otùtù
