examples.english: They are rubbing grains off maize cobs in her mother's house.

examples.igbo: Gbasịa ògbàdụ ndị a ka anyị sie ọka.
examples.english: Rub grains off these cobs so we can cook corn.

examples.igbo: O kwụbara akwà ya n'elu eriri.
examples.english: She hung her cloth on the line.

examples.igbo: Kwụbaa akwà ahụ tupu mmiri ezoo.
examples.english: Hang up that cloth before the rain falls.

examples.igbo: Nchekwata ego ya dị ntakịrị.
examples.english: His money savings are small.

examples.igbo: Ị na-edebe nchekwata gị n'ụlọ akụ?
examples.english: Are you keeping your savings in the bank?

gloss: scatter (with some care); spread out (e.g. grains in sun, partly burnt firewood)

examples.igbo: Anyị na-akpasà ọka n'anyanwụ.
examples.english: We are spreading maize in the sun.

examples.igbo: Kpasàa mkpụrụ osisi ndị ahụ n'ala.
examples.english: Spread those seeds on the ground.

examples.igbo: Mkpụrụ ọka anyị kụrụ gbapụtara taa.
examples.english: The maize seeds we planted broke ground today.

examples.igbo: Olee mgbe mkpụrụ ahụ ga-agbapute?
examples.english: When will that seed break ground?

examples.igbo: Anyị na-amịkpọ azụ n'ọkụ.
examples.english: We are drying fish over the fire.

examples.igbo: Mịkpọa azụ ndị a nke ọma.
examples.english: Dry these fish well.

examples.igbo: Anyị kụrụ ụlọikwuu n'ọma ahịa taa.
examples.english: We pitched a tent at the market today.

examples.igbo: Ụlọikwuu a ọ na-eche anyị mmiri?
examples.english: Does this tent keep the rain off us?

note: Headword appears as ụnò ikwuù; examples use the standard modern form ụlọikwuu.

examples.igbo: O ligburu nwanne ya ego n'ụzọ aghụghọ.
examples.english: He defrauded his brother of money deceitfully.

examples.igbo: Eligbula mmadụ ego n'ụzọ aghụghọ.
examples.english: Do not defraud people of money deceitfully.

gloss: watchnight service (e.g. that held on eve of Christmas, New Year, etc.)

examples.igbo: Anyị gara ụkā nche n'abalị ekeresimesi.
examples.english: We went to the watchnight service on Christmas night.

examples.igbo: Ụkā nche afọ ọhụrụ ga-amalite elekere itoolu?
examples.english: Will the New Year watchnight service start at nine?

examples.igbo: Ọ fụrụ ọbara n'egedege ihu ya.
examples.english: Blood was on his forehead.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ ọ nwere egedege ihu sara mbara?
examples.english: Does that child have a wide forehead?

note: Examples use the standard form egedege ihu for the given headword spelling.

examples.igbo: Chiēmēēlā, anyị rụchara ọrụ ugbo taa.
examples.english: God has done well, we finished the farm work today.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ekele Chiēmēēlā maka nwa ọhụrụ a?
examples.english: Are you thanking God-has-done-well for this newborn?

examples.igbo: O mere mmebī īwu n'ihi na o zuru ego.
examples.english: He committed a crime because he stole money.

examples.igbo: Mmebī īwu ọ bụla na-eweta ntaramahụhụ?
examples.english: Does every crime bring punishment?

examples.igbo: Efìfìè naàbò, anyị na-ezu ike n'okpuru osisi.
examples.english: At noonday, we rest under a tree.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ekpo ọkụ nke ukwuu n'efìfìè naàbò.
examples.english: It is very hot at noonday.

examples.igbo: Dọkịta gbara ntì ya wee hụ ihe.
examples.english: The doctor probed his ear and saw something.

examples.igbo: Jiri nwayọ gbaa ntì nwa ahụ.
examples.english: Gently probe that child's ear.

examples.igbo: Nta egō mere ka ọ hapụ ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: Striving for money made him leave school.

examples.igbo: Ị na-achụ nta egō n'oge niile?
examples.english: Are you pursuing money all the time?

gloss: call up and out; escort up and out

examples.igbo: Ọ kpọgopụtara ndị ọbịa n'ụlọ n'ụtụtụ taa.
examples.english: He called the guests up out of the house this morning.

examples.igbo: Kpọgopụta ụmụaka ahụ n'ime olulu ugbu a.
examples.english: Call those children up out of the pit now.

note: The verb stem is uncommon; examples follow the given sense of calling someone up and out.

examples.igbo: Ọrụ ubi na-afịa n'oge ọkọchị nke ukwuu.
examples.english: Farm work is very difficult in the dry season.

examples.igbo: Njem ahụ ọ fịara gị?
examples.english: Was that journey difficult for you?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-enwe àrụ alō n'ụtụtụ mgbe ọ bụla.
examples.english: He has sluggishness every morning.

examples.igbo: Wepụ àrụ alō, rụọ ọrụ n'ubi taa.
examples.english: Remove sloth and work on the farm today.

note: The noun phrase is not very common in everyday speech, but the examples follow the given sense.

gloss: run after someone or something in order to reach or chase them away

examples.igbo: Ndị uwe ojii chụrụ ọsọ jide onye ohi ahụ.
examples.english: The police ran after and caught that thief.

examples.igbo: Chụọ ọsọ chụpụ ewu n'ubi taa.
examples.english: Run after and chase the goat out of the farm today.

gloss: any rash caused by perspiration; dermatitis; eczema; uticaria; swollen patches due to sensitivity to some particular food, serum, drug, etc. ( -fù 1. swell)

examples.igbo: Afùfù pụtara n'ahụ ya mgbe ọ gbara ọsọ.
examples.english: A rash appeared on his body when he ran.

examples.igbo: Ọ nwere afùfù n'aka mgbe o riri azụ?
examples.english: Did she have a rash on her hand when she ate fish?

examples.igbo: Ọ kpachara anya mebie ihe ahụ.
examples.english: He deliberately broke that thing.

examples.igbo: Ị kpachara anya zọọ m ụkwụ?
examples.english: Did you intentionally step on my foot?

note: The phrase often means 'be careful'; the examples follow the given sense 'do something on purpose'.

gloss: mourning song; Songs of Solomon; lamentation

examples.igbo: Ha bụrụ abụ̀akwā n'olili nwoke ahụ.
examples.english: They sang a mourning song at that man's funeral.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji bụọ abụ̀akwā?
examples.english: Why did you sing a mourning song?

examples.igbo: Ifufe kwàkpọrọ nnukwu osisi n'ubi anyị.
examples.english: Wind pushed down a big tree on our farm.

examples.igbo: Biko kwàkpọọ ya n'ala ugbu a.
examples.english: Please push him down now.

note: The verb is clear, but the tone-marked spelling and inflection vary; examples use the given sense.

examples.igbo: Owùmaàgànà na-agbanwe àgwà ya n'elu osisi.
examples.english: A chameleon changes its color on a tree.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ owùmaàgànà n'elu osisi taa?
examples.english: Did you see a chameleon on a tree today?

examples.igbo: Anyị nụrụ òbụba alaka n'ubi n'abalị.
examples.english: We heard the breaking of a branch on the farm at night.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara òbụba iko ahụ n'ụtụtụ?
examples.english: What caused the breaking of that glass in the morning?

note: The noun is somewhat uncommon; examples follow the given sense of 'breaking'.

examples.igbo: Nwa ehi a ma àbụ̀bà nke ukwuu.
examples.english: This calf is very fat/plump.

examples.igbo: Efi gị ọ̀ ma àbụ̀bà n'ezie?
examples.english: Is your cow really fat/plump?

gloss: cover; use one thing to cover up another

examples.igbo: Kpùdo ite nri ahụ ka ihe ghara ịdaba na ya.
examples.english: Cover that pot of food so things do not fall into it.

examples.igbo: Ọ ji akwa ọcha kpùdo efere ahụ.
examples.english: She covered that plate with a white cloth.

gloss: (colloquial) stretchy and chewy edibles, especially meat and chewing gum

examples.igbo: Anụ ehi a dị ǹtàǹta nke ukwuu.
examples.english: This beef is very chewy/stretchy.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ata ǹtàǹta mgbe ọ na-eje ije.
examples.english: He chews gum while walking.

examples.igbo: Nna m na-agba ịnyịnya n'ugbo kwa ụbọchị.
examples.english: My father rides a horse on the farm every day.

examples.igbo: Ị na-agba ịnyịnya n'okporo ụzọ a?
examples.english: Are you riding a horse on this road?

examples.igbo: Ha doro alụsị ọhụrụ n'obi ezinụlọ ha.
examples.english: They erected a new shrine in their family compound.

examples.igbo: Doo alụsị ahụ n'akụkụ ụlọ nna gị.
examples.english: Erect that shrine beside your father's house.

examples.igbo: Anyị ji ụkwụ enū gaa Enugu n'izu gara aga.
examples.english: We went to Enugu by land last week.

examples.igbo: Ụkwụ enū ka ọ na-aga, ọ bụghị ụgbọelu.
examples.english: He travels by land, not by air.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-erite ego n'ọrụ ugbo ya.
examples.english: He earns money from his farming.

examples.igbo: Ị ritere ego ole n'izu a?
examples.english: How much did you earn this week?

examples.igbo: Mama na-akwadebe nri abalị maka anyị.
examples.english: Mother is preparing dinner for us.

examples.igbo: Kwadebe onwe gị maka njem ahụ.
examples.english: Prepare yourself for that journey.

examples.igbo: Oké mmiri dakwàsàrị anyị n'ụzọ.
examples.english: The heavy rain fell upon us on the road.

examples.igbo: Onye ka ọrụ a dakwàsàrị?
examples.english: On whom did this work fall upon?

examples.igbo: Ịgāniiru nke obodo a dị mma.
examples.english: The progress of this town is good.

examples.igbo: Kedu ihe na-egbochi ịgāniiru gị?
examples.english: What is hindering your progress?

gloss: express grief, regret or disappointment about something; lament

examples.igbo: Nne ya beere àrị̀rị̀ mgbe nwa ya dara.
examples.english: His mother lamented when her child fell.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji be àrị̀rị̀?
examples.english: Why are you lamenting?

examples.igbo: Anyị gafere ụlọ ya n'ụzọ.
examples.english: We missed his house on the way.

examples.igbo: Ị gafere ule ahụ?
examples.english: Did you miss that exam?

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ gbà ọ̀tọ n'ụlọ.
examples.english: That child is naked in the house.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji gbà ọ̀tọ?
examples.english: Why are you naked?

gloss: be tight (e.g. as undersized shirt, etc.)

examples.igbo: Uwe ahụ mere ntado.
examples.english: That shirt is tight.

examples.igbo: Uwe a ọ̀ na-eme ntado?
examples.english: Is this dress tight?

examples.igbo: Wèpù obì gị n'ihe ahụ.
examples.english: Dismiss your mind from that thing.

examples.igbo: Ọ wepụrụ obì ya n'ihe ahụ.
examples.english: He dismissed his mind from that matter.

gloss: cry bitterly (literally blind oneself with tears)

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ kwakpọsịrị anya mgbe e merụrụ ya ahụ.
examples.english: That child cried bitterly when he was hurt.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji kwakpọsị anya?
examples.english: Why are you crying bitterly?

gloss: (literally head and tail) substance, meaning (especially of speech)

examples.igbo: Okwu ya enweghị isi na ọdù.
examples.english: His speech has no substance.

examples.igbo: Gịnị bụ isi na ọdù okwu a?
examples.english: What is the substance of this speech?

examples.igbo: Ụgbọ enū na-efe n'elu igwe.
examples.english: The aeroplane flies in the sky.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-aba ụgbọ enū?
examples.english: Will you board the aeroplane?

examples.igbo: Àkpàkwùlù m na-egbu mgbu kemgbe ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: My stomach has been aching since yesterday.

examples.igbo: Biko, gwa dọkịta na àkpàkwùlù gị na-egbu gị.
examples.english: Please, tell the doctor that your stomach is aching.

note: Rare/dialectal word for stomach; sentences are idiomatic but the word is far less common than afọ.

gloss: large ape, especially chimpanzee, gorilla [N.B. neither of the great apes has been recorded in Igbo territory in centuries, making it difficult to know the referent of this word]

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka ahụ hụrụ ọzò na telivishọn.
examples.english: Those children saw an ape on television.

examples.igbo: Ị hụtụla ọzò na ndụ gị?
examples.english: Have you ever seen an ape in your life?

note: The referent of ọzò (great ape) is uncertain, as the dictionary itself notes; these sentences are grammatical but I cannot vouch for the sense.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-akọpu ahụ ya n'ihi ọkọ.
examples.english: The child is scratching his body because of the itching.

examples.igbo: O kwesịghị ịkọpu ahụ ya otú ahụ.
examples.english: He should not scratch his body like that.

note: Inflected as na-akọpu / ịkọpu; the verb itself is uncommon and I would phrase the second sentence differently.

gloss: move, move (something) about; remove; change the position (of something)

examples.igbo: Biko weghalịa oche ahụ n'akụkụ.
examples.english: Please move that chair aside.

examples.igbo: O weghalịrị igbe ya gaa n'ọnụ ụzọ.
examples.english: He moved his box over to the doorway.

note: weghalịa / weghalịrị inflections are sound, but the more usual verb would be wegharị/weghachi.

gloss: cover (so as to prevent looking in or attack)

examples.igbo: O ji akwa gbochie windo ahụ.
examples.english: She covered the window with cloth.

examples.igbo: Gbochie olulu ahụ tupu mmiri abịa.
examples.english: Cover that hole before the rain comes.

note: gbochi / gbochie forms are correct; the sense of blocking view or entry is preserved.

examples.igbo: Ajù nà-èbu m, ka m nọdụ ala ntakịrị.
examples.english: I am dizzy, let me sit down a little.

examples.igbo: Ajù ọ̀ nà-èbu gị ugbua?
examples.english: Are you dizzy now?

note: Kept the phrase as given (ajù nà-èbu); the question form with gị is a normal transformation but I would confirm the tone on ọ̀.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka ahụ na-amịghalị n'okporo ámá.
examples.english: Those children are loitering about on the street.

examples.igbo: Onye ohi ahụ mịghalịrị n'azụ ụlọ.
examples.english: That thief crept stealthily behind the house.

note: na-amịghalị / mịghalịrị inflections; the 'walk stealthily' sense is the one I am least sure of.

examples.igbo: Nkịta ahụ chụrụ ọsọ ewu n'ubi.
examples.english: The dog chased the goat on the farm.

examples.igbo: Ndị uwe ojii chụrụ ọsọ onye ohi n'okporo ámá.
examples.english: The police chased the thief along the street.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-etinye efùrù n'ofe ka ọ see ísì ọma.
examples.english: We put African nutmeg in the soup so it smells good.

examples.igbo: Zụta efùrù abụọ n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: Buy two African nutmegs at the market today.

note: Tone marks follow the entry; efùrù is the usual word for this spice in cooking.

examples.igbo: Nne m na-akpọ m mgbe ọ bụla.
examples.english: My mother calls me every time.

examples.igbo: Kpọọ ya ka ọ bịa ebe a.
examples.english: Call him to come here.

examples.igbo: Puku ndi mmadụ bịara ahịa taa.
examples.english: Thousands of people came to the market today.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ puku ndi mmadụ n'ebe ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see thousands of people there?

examples.igbo: Anyị na-akpa ǹjàkìlì mgbe anyị zutere.
examples.english: We engage in friendly joking when we meet.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ ǹjàkìlì ka ị na-eme?
examples.english: Is it friendly joking you are doing?

examples.igbo: O ketara ekpē nna ya n'afọ gara aga.
examples.english: He inherited his father's inheritance last year.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eketa ekpē ahụ niile mgbe nna gị nwụrụ?
examples.english: Will you inherit all that inheritance when your father dies?

examples.igbo: Òdụdụ agịga na-egbu mgbu n'aka m.
examples.english: The pricking of a needle hurts in my hand.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eji òdụdụ akwa akwa mgbe niile?
examples.english: Do you always use sewing to sew cloth?

examples.igbo: Ndị obodo na-efe Èdò kwa ụbọchị.
examples.english: The people of the village worship Èdò every day.

examples.igbo: Èdò bụ chi ha n'ezie ka ha na-ekwu?
examples.english: Is Èdò really their deity as they say?

examples.igbo: O kpasàpùrù ọnụ ya n'ebe ahụ.
examples.english: He spread his mouth wide open there.

examples.igbo: Kpasàpù ụzọ ahụ ka anyị banye.
examples.english: Spread that door wide open so we can enter.

examples.igbo: Mwewụsa iwē ya mere ka anyị ghara ịga.
examples.english: His provoking anger made us not go.

examples.igbo: Ị na-achọ mwewụsa iwē m n'efu?
examples.english: Are you trying to provoke my anger for nothing?

examples.igbo: Ahụrụ m ya sọ oyī nke ukwuu.
examples.english: I felt great disgust for it.

examples.igbo: Nri a na-asọ oyī n'ezie ka ị na-ekwu?
examples.english: Is this food really yucky as you say?

examples.igbo: Ha na-emegbu ụmụaka n'ahịa mgbe niile.
examples.english: They oppress children in the market all the time.

examples.igbo: Emegbula nwanne gị n'ụlọ akwụkwọ ọ bụla.
examples.english: Don't maltreat your sibling in any school.

examples.igbo: M ga-akụgwa gị ọkpọ ahụ i kụrụ nwanne m.
examples.english: I will avenge the blow you gave my brother on you.

examples.igbo: Ọ kụgwaara m ọkpọ ahụ m kụrụ ya.
examples.english: He repaid me the blow I gave him.

note: Tentative on exact inflection of -kụgwa; sense is revenge/repay a blow.

examples.igbo: Echegbula onwe gị banyere ego ahụ.
examples.english: Don't worry yourself about that money.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-echegbu onwe ya maka ule na-abịa.
examples.english: She is anxious about the coming exam.

examples.igbo: Ọ nyedoro ụgbọala ya n'akụkụ ụlọ ahụ.
examples.english: He parked his car beside that house.

examples.igbo: Nyedo ụgbọala ebe a, biko.
examples.english: Park the car here, please.

examples.igbo: Azụrụ m azụ n'ahịa ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: I bought fish in the market yesterday.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-azụ akwa ọhụrụ maka emume?
examples.english: Will you buy new clothes for the ceremony?

examples.igbo: Ọ bu ponì mmānụ n'ụgbọala ya.
examples.english: He carried a cask of palm oil in his vehicle.

examples.igbo: Ponì mmānụ ahụ dị oke ọnụ.
examples.english: That cask of palm oil is very expensive.

note: Assumes ponì mmānụ is a cask/puncheon of palm oil.

examples.igbo: Anyị gwụsịrị ọrụ ubi taa.
examples.english: We finished the farm work today.

examples.igbo: Gwụsịa nri gị tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Finish your food before you leave.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka mebiri ihe egwuregwu ahụ.
examples.english: The children damaged that toy.

examples.igbo: Mebila akwụkwọ m, biko.
examples.english: Don't spoil my book, please.

examples.igbo: Nwojiri m otu ibe achịcha.
examples.english: I broke off a piece of bread.

examples.igbo: Nwojiri ya obere ihe tinye n'ọnụ nwa.
examples.english: Break off a little and put it in the baby's mouth.

note: Uncertain about the exact inflection and idiomatic use of -nwoji.

examples.igbo: Agwọ na-alị alị n'ime ahịhịa.
examples.english: A snake is creeping in the grass.

examples.igbo: Ahụhụ na-alị alị n'ala ebe a.
examples.english: Insects are creeping on the ground here.

examples.igbo: Ndị obodo na-eme òwụwa jī n'ọnwa Ọgọọst.
examples.english: The villagers celebrate the new yam festival in August.

examples.igbo: Òwụwa jī bụ nnukwu emume n'ala Igbo.
examples.english: The new yam festival is a big celebration in Igboland.

gloss: at home; in the house; within (the house)

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka nọ n'ụnò na-egwuri egwu n'ụtụtụ a.
examples.english: The children are at home playing this morning.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-anọ n'ụnò taa ma ọ bụ na ị ga-aga ahịa?
examples.english: Will you stay at home today or go to market?

examples.igbo: Onye ọkụ ahụ kpụrụ mmà siri ike.
examples.english: That blacksmith made a strong cutlass.

examples.igbo: Ị kpụrụ mmà a maka ọrụ ugbo?
examples.english: Did you make this cutlass for farm work?

examples.igbo: Nne m gbọkàpụrụ anụ ọkụkọ ahụ.
examples.english: My mother cut up that chicken meat.

examples.igbo: Gbọkàpụ anụ ahụ ngwa ngwa tupu ọ sie.
examples.english: Cut up that meat quickly before it cooks.

note: Past form gbọkàpụrụ is assumed.

examples.igbo: Ọ gara ùfèsi ịzụ ahịa n'afọ gara aga.
examples.english: He went abroad to trade last year.

examples.igbo: Ị na-aga ùfèsi n'afọ a ma ọ bụ n'afọ ọzọ?
examples.english: Are you going abroad this year or next year?

examples.igbo: Ọ tigọrọ osisi ahụ n'iti ya ihe.
examples.english: He bent that stick by beating it.

examples.igbo: Gịnị tigọrọ ihu ya n'ihe mberede ahụ?
examples.english: What disfigured his face in that accident?

note: Inflected form tigọrọ is assumed.

examples.igbo: Akwụkwọ ahụ dọrì adọ mgbe ọ dara n'elu mmiri.
examples.english: The paper tore into pieces when it fell on water.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere uwe gị ji dọrì adọ?
examples.english: Why are your clothes torn into pieces?

note: Used in the idiom dọrì adọ 'tear into pieces'.

examples.igbo: Ndị obodo ahụ nụrụ agha megide ndị agbata obi ha.
examples.english: The people of that town fought a war against their neighbours.

examples.igbo: Anyị ga-anụ agha ma ha wakpo anyị?
examples.english: Will we fight a war if they attack us?

note: Sense of -nụ agha is uncommon; examples follow the given meaning.

examples.igbo: O yiri òkpu ọhụrụ ọ zụtara n'ahịa.
examples.english: He wore a new hat he bought at the market.

examples.igbo: Òkpu a bụ nke gị ka ọ bụ nke m?
examples.english: Is this cap yours or mine?

examples.igbo: Anyị na-azụ òke oyìbo n'ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: We rear guinea-pigs in our house.

examples.igbo: Ị hụla òke oyìbo na-ata ahịhịa n'ubi?
examples.english: Have you seen a guinea-pig eating grass in the farm?

gloss: wash breasts, especially of a newly delivered mother, to induce breast milk

examples.igbo: Nne ọhụrụ ahụ sara ala ya iji nweta mmiri ara.
examples.english: The new mother washed her breasts to get breast milk.

examples.igbo: Sa ala gị tupu ị nye nwa ara.
examples.english: Wash your breasts before you breastfeed the baby.

note: ala 'breasts' is the sense given.

examples.igbo: O ji mụrị kelee ndị ọbịa.
examples.english: She greeted the guests with a smile.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ mụrị ya mgbe o bịara?
examples.english: Did you see her smile when she came?

examples.igbo: Mfefè ụgbọ elu ahụ gafee osimiri dị egwu.
examples.english: That plane's flying across the river was scary.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ mfefè nnụnụ n'elu ụlọ anyị?
examples.english: Did you see the birds flying across over our house?

examples.igbo: Anyị lere ihoònyòònyoò banyere oriri ahụ.
examples.english: We watched a video about that feast.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere ihoònyòònyoò nke egwuregwu ahụ?
examples.english: Do you have the video of that match?

note: Headword spelling is unusual; assumed to mean video.

examples.igbo: Igodo ụlọ anyị tara nchāla.
examples.english: Our house key is rusty.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ na ígwè ahụ tara nchāla?
examples.english: Did you see that the metal is rusty?

gloss: pack up Ọ kwàlù ife yā wèe naa He packed up and went home

examples.igbo: O kwàlù ihe ya wee laa.
examples.english: He packed up his things and went home.

examples.igbo: Kwàlụ akpa gị, anyị na-apụ.
examples.english: Pack up your bag, we are leaving.

examples.igbo: Nne m tinyere mị azụ̀ na ofe.
examples.english: My mother put dry fish in the soup.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ mị azụ̀ ka anyị sie ofe?
examples.english: Do you want dry fish so we can cook soup?

examples.igbo: Ndị ìsì na-eji mkpisi aka aga ije.
examples.english: Blind people use walking sticks to walk.

examples.igbo: Ị na-enyere ndị ìsì aka n'okporo ụzọ?
examples.english: Do you help blind people on the road?

examples.igbo: Anyị dọnòrube n'ụlọ wee kparịta ụka.
examples.english: We sat around at home and chatted.

examples.igbo: Ha na-adọnòrube n'okpuru osisi kama ịrụ ọrụ.
examples.english: They sit around under the tree instead of working.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-akwụ ụgwọ ụlọ ọnwa kwùlu ọnwā.
examples.english: We pay house rent month after month.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-arụ ọrụ ọnwa kwùlu ọnwā n'enweghị ezumike?
examples.english: Does he work month after month without rest?

gloss: at one time; once upon a time; once

examples.igbo: Òfu ogè ka m gara ahịa ahụ.
examples.english: I went to that market once.

examples.igbo: Ị gara ebe ahụ òfu ogè?
examples.english: Did you go there once?

examples.igbo: Òka elùlò ahụ nyere m ndụmọdụ bara uru.
examples.english: That counsellor gave me useful advice.

examples.igbo: Ì na-ajụ òka elùlò tupu i mee mkpebi?
examples.english: Do you ask the counsellor before you make a decision?

examples.igbo: Enyò anyā m dara ada n'ahịa.
examples.english: My spectacles fell at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ènyò anyā nna gị?
examples.english: Did you see your father's spectacles?

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ na-abọsà ntụ n'ikuku.
examples.english: That child is scattering ash in the air.

examples.igbo: Bọsà ọka ahụ n'ala ka ọkụkọ taa ya.
examples.english: Scatter that corn on the ground so the chickens eat it.

note: Inflection of bọsà is given in a common but not fully certain form.

examples.igbo: Ndezù akwụkwọ a dị mma karịa nke mbụ.
examples.english: The revised edition of this book is better than the first.

examples.igbo: Ị gụọla ndezù edemede m?
examples.english: Have you read the revision of my essay?

examples.igbo: Ònyê nò ebe afù? ka ọ jụrụ tupu o mepe ụzọ.
examples.english: Who is there? he asked before opening the door.

examples.igbo: Ajụrụ m, Ònyê nò ebe afù? mgbe m nụrụ mkpọtụ.
examples.english: I asked, Who is there? when I heard a noise.

examples.igbo: Mmili osisi na-agbapụta n'osisi ahụ.
examples.english: Sap is flowing from that tree.

examples.igbo: E ji mmili osisi eme ọgwụ?
examples.english: Is sap used to make medicine?

note: Mmili is a dialectal form; standard Igbo commonly has mmiri osisi.

examples.igbo: Mmiri na-arùfèga n'ala ebe ahụ.
examples.english: Water is flowing over the ground there.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka mmiri rùfèga n'ụlọ.
examples.english: Don't let water flow over into the house.

note: The verb stem is used in continuous and after ka; inflectional forms vary.

gloss: small private room where family head holds private discussions (= ụnò ọbā)

examples.igbo: Papa m na-anọ n'ụnò ime ụnò na-ekwu okwu ezinụlọ.
examples.english: My father stays in the private inner room discussing family matters.

examples.igbo: Ònye nọ n'ụnò ime ụnò?
examples.english: Who is in the private inner room?

note: Ụnò is a dialectal variant of ụlọ.

examples.igbo: Onye ikpē ahụ na-ekpe ikpe ziri ezi.
examples.english: That judge judges fairly.

examples.igbo: Ònye bụ onye ikpē n'okwu a?
examples.english: Who is the judge in this case?

examples.igbo: O sịrị òsiālị n'ụlọ ikpe.
examples.english: He bore witness in court.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-asị òsiālị echi?
examples.english: Will you bear witness tomorrow?

note: The phrase is less common than gbaa akaebe, but the forms given are plausible.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ejedide n'ọrụ ugbo ya kwa ụbọchị.
examples.english: He keeps going on with his farm work every day.

examples.igbo: Jedide n'ihu, anyị fọrọ obere.
examples.english: Keep going on, we are almost there.

note: The verb stem is uncommon; I used it in the sense of continuing or keeping on.

examples.igbo: Ndị mmadụ guzoro n'nsò n'ihu ụlọ ahịa.
examples.english: People stood in a queue in front of the shop.

examples.igbo: Guzo n'nsò ka e nye gị nri.
examples.english: Stand in the queue so they give you food.

note: Nsò is not the most common word for queue, but I used it as given.

gloss: a system of government where leadership is transferred from one generation to another

examples.igbo: N'obodo ha, ọ̀chịchị ezèchihachìbèrè ka e ji ahọpụta eze.
examples.english: In their town, they use a hereditary system to choose the king.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ ọ̀chịchị ezèchihachìbèrè mere nwa ya ji bụrụ eze?
examples.english: Is it the hereditary system that made his son become king?

note: Specialized term; the examples show hereditary succession.

gloss: round shape (circular, not spherical); surrounding parts

examples.igbo: Tebụl ahụ dị òkìlìkili, ọ bụghị akụkụ anọ.
examples.english: That table is round, not four-cornered.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka gbara òkìlìkili gburugburu onye nkụzi.
examples.english: The children formed a circle around the teacher.

note: Òkìlìkili is used for a circular shape or surrounding arrangement.

examples.igbo: Enwere m nchèkwube n'ebe ya nọ.
examples.english: I have confidence in him.

examples.igbo: Nwee nchèkwube na ọ ga-abịa.
examples.english: Have confidence that he will come.

gloss: saving money on daily or monthly basis; to save either daily, weekly or monthly with an agreed person who also keeps money for other people to be shared on an agreed date

examples.igbo: Ọ na-atụ isūsū kwa ụbọchị n'aka nwanne ya.
examples.english: He saves daily in esusu with his brother.

examples.igbo: Tụọ isūsū ka ị zụta ọka.
examples.english: Save in esusu so that you buy maize.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ekene ndị ọbịa mgbe ha bịara.
examples.english: He greets visitors when they come.

examples.igbo: Kene Chineke maka nri a.
examples.english: Thank God for this food.

note: The stem covers both greeting and thanking.

gloss: father-in-law; any male relative by marriage

examples.igbo: Ọgọ nwoke m bịara ile anyị ọbịa.
examples.english: My father-in-law came to visit us.

examples.igbo: Ị hụla ọgọ nwoke gị taa?
examples.english: Have you seen your father-in-law today?

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-emeta ụda olu nne ya nke ọma.
examples.english: That child imitates his mother's voice correctly.

examples.igbo: Meta ya kpọmkwem otu a.
examples.english: Imitate it exactly like this.

note: The stem means to imitate exactly or be exact.

gloss: be punctual; do something in good time

examples.igbo: Ada na-eme n'oge n'ọrụ ya.
examples.english: Ada is punctual at her work.

examples.igbo: Mee n'oge, ka ị ghara igbu oge.
examples.english: Be punctual so you don't waste time.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-eme mgbanu mgbe ọ na-aga ahịa.
examples.english: He is in a hurry when going to market.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji eme mgbanu?
examples.english: Why are you in a hurry?

examples.igbo: Ahụ m na-elo ilo mgbe ọ na-ezo.
examples.english: My body aches when it rains.

examples.igbo: Gịnị na-elo gị ilo?
examples.english: What is aching you?

examples.igbo: Kwanị ọkụ ahụ ka ọ na-enwu.
examples.english: Fan that fire so it blazes.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akwanị ọkụ?
examples.english: Are you fanning the fire?

examples.igbo: Dọkịta gwara ya yatọ ọnụ.
examples.english: The doctor told him to open his mouth.

examples.igbo: Yatọ ọnụ ka m hụ eze gị.
examples.english: Open your mouth so I can see your teeth.

examples.igbo: O kwenyere na ọ ga-ahụ ya n'ụwa ọzọ.
examples.english: He believes he will see him in the world to come.

examples.igbo: Ị chere na anyị ga-ezute n'ụwa ọzọ?
examples.english: Do you think we shall meet in the world to come?

examples.igbo: Ha gụrụ nwa ha aha Chidi.
examples.english: They named their child Chidi.

examples.igbo: Ị gụrụ nwa gị aha gịnị?
examples.english: What did you name your child?

gloss: flare up; blaze; force away by heat

examples.igbo: Ọkụ na-achani n'ọhịa.
examples.english: Fire is blazing in the bush.

examples.igbo: Anwụ na-achani anyị n'ọhịa.
examples.english: The sun is driving us from the farm with heat.

note: Not fully certain of the inflection and transitive use of -chani.

gloss: charge, price more than right price

examples.igbo: O rụrụ m ụma n'ahịa.
examples.english: He overcharged me at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị na-arụ m ụma?
examples.english: Are you overcharging me?

gloss: example; sample (also used as female name)

examples.igbo: Nke a bụ ife atụ maka ụmụ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: This is an example for students.

examples.igbo: Nye m ife atụ ọzọ.
examples.english: Give me another example.

gloss: extinguish; put off fire or light

examples.igbo: Menyụọ oriọna ahụ tupu ị lakpuo ụra.
examples.english: Put off that lamp before you sleep.

examples.igbo: Ònye menyụrụ ọkụ n'ụlọ akwụkwọ?
examples.english: Who put off the light in the school?

examples.igbo: O ji ǹdele igwè na-alụ ọgụ n'okporo ámá.
examples.english: He uses an iron rod to fight in the street.

examples.igbo: Ndị uwe ojii wepụrụ ǹdele igwè n'aka ya.
examples.english: The police took the iron rod from his hand.

examples.igbo: Ụkwụ ya turu ụkpò mgbe o jere ogologo njem.
examples.english: His foot blistered when he went on a long journey.

examples.igbo: Ọkụ ahụ turu m ụkpò n'aka.
examples.english: The fire blistered my hand.

note: Not fully certain of the inflection of -tu in this sense.

examples.igbo: Anyị ji ụgbọ àmàlà gafee osimiri ahụ.
examples.english: We used a canoe to cross that river.

examples.igbo: Ònye na-akwọ ụgbọ àmàlà ahụ?
examples.english: Who is paddling that canoe?

examples.igbo: Pòtòkiri dị na Europe.
examples.english: Portugal is in Europe.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-asụ asụsụ Pòtòkiri nke ọma.
examples.english: He speaks Portuguese well.

examples.igbo: Onye nkuzi dọrọ ụmụ akwụkwọ ntì banyere ịgbachi nkịtị.
examples.english: The teacher warned the students about keeping quiet.

examples.igbo: Dọọ nwa gị ntì ka ọ ghara ịgba ọsọ n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: Warn your child not to run on the road.

examples.igbo: Ụkà Anglịkan nwere ọtụtụ ụlọ ụka n'Naịjirịa.
examples.english: The Anglican Church has many churches in Nigeria.

examples.igbo: Anyị gara Ụkà Anglịkan ụtụtụ Sọnde.
examples.english: We went to the Anglican Church on Sunday morning.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-edina n'àba mgbe ọ na-ehi ụra.
examples.english: He sleeps on his back when sleeping.

examples.igbo: Dina n'àba ka m nyochaa azụ gị.
examples.english: Lie on your back so I can examine your back.

gloss: prepare land for planting by propitiating the spirits (or gods) concerned

examples.igbo: Ndị okenye fere ànì tupu ha akọọ ihe.
examples.english: The elders appeased the land before they sowed.

examples.igbo: Ị fere ànì tupu ịkọ ọka?
examples.english: Did you appease the land before planting corn?

note: The ritual sense is specialized, but the examples are phrased idiomatically.

examples.igbo: Anwụrụ ọkụ na-emerụ òkùkù ume.
examples.english: Smoke harms the lungs.

examples.igbo: Dọkịta na-ele òkùkù ume ya anya.
examples.english: The doctor is examining his lungs.

examples.igbo: Ezi okwū na-ewute ndị na-agha ụgha.
examples.english: The truth pains those who lie.

examples.igbo: Gwa m ezi okwū, ị hụrụ ya?
examples.english: Tell me the truth, did you see him?

examples.igbo: Onye dibịa dọrọ ǹkì n'ihu nwa ya.
examples.english: The traditional doctor cut marks on his child's face.

examples.igbo: Ị na-adọ ǹkì n'aka gị?
examples.english: Are you cutting marks on your hand?

examples.igbo: Ọkụ ụgbọala ahụ gbụrụ àmụ̀mà n'abalị.
examples.english: That car light flashed at night.

examples.igbo: Gịnị gbụrụ àmụ̀mà n'elu igwe n'abalị?
examples.english: What flashed in the sky at night?

note: The verb gbū with àmụ̀mà is somewhat specialized; sentences are idiomatic but the construction may vary by dialect.

examples.igbo: Onye isi kèrè okwu n'etiti ụmụaka.
examples.english: The head settled the dispute among the children.

examples.igbo: Kee okwu a ngwa ngwa tupu anyị laa.
examples.english: Settle this dispute quickly before we go.

examples.igbo: Ọnwụ ikē gburu nna ya n'abalị.
examples.english: Sudden death killed his father at night.

examples.igbo: Ị na-atụ egwu ọnwụ ikē nke ukwuu?
examples.english: Are you very afraid of sudden death?

gloss: source of a stream or river

examples.igbo: Anyị ruru n'isi mmīli n'ụtụtụ a.
examples.english: We reached the source of the stream this morning.

examples.igbo: Olee ebe isi mmīli a dị?
examples.english: Where is the source of this stream?

gloss: Good morning (literally have you come out of the sleeping-room?

examples.igbo: Ì pùtago ūla, nne m, ọ dị mma?
examples.english: Good morning, my mother, is it well?

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-ekele gị, Ì pùtago ūla.
examples.english: The children greet you, good morning.

examples.igbo: Akpọkọta ahụ buru ibu nke ukwuu.
examples.english: That gathering was very large.

examples.igbo: Anyị nọ na akpọkọta n'abalị ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: We were at a gathering last night.

examples.igbo: Ọ nyòrọ enyò na m, ọ hụghị ihe.
examples.english: He looked twice at me, he saw nothing.

examples.igbo: Nyọọ enyò na akpa gị tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Look twice in your bag before you leave.

note: The phrase nyò enyò is idiomatic but its usage can be subtle; sentences are likely correct but may vary in register.

examples.igbo: O mejuru ite ahụ mmiri n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: He filled that pot with water this morning.

examples.igbo: Mejuo iko m mmiri ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Fill my cup with water quickly.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akọ mkpòlị nye nwanne ya.
examples.english: He reproaches his brother.

examples.igbo: Akọla mkpòlị nye nne gị.
examples.english: Don't reproach your mother.

examples.igbo: Ghèe ụzọ ahụ, ọ na-ekpo ọkụ.
examples.english: Open the door, it is hot.

examples.igbo: Ụzọ ahụ ọ ghèrè oghe?
examples.english: Is the door open?

note: The verb stem ghè is used with the meaning 'open' and 'be open'; the imperative and stative forms are given as ghèe and ghèrè oghe.

gloss: enemy; person bearing malice towards one

examples.igbo: Onye ilō m bịara n'ụlọ m.
examples.english: My enemy came to my house.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji bụrụ onye ilō m?
examples.english: Why have you become my enemy?

gloss: a legume which is often fried in a pot without oil and eaten with palm kernel

examples.igbo: Mama m na-eghe ụ̀zàakị̄ n'ite.
examples.english: My mother fries ụ̀zàakị̄ in a pot.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eri ụ̀zàakị̄ na akị?
examples.english: Do you eat ụ̀zàakị̄ with palm kernel?

note: The verb eghe is used for frying; the legume is typically fried without oil.

gloss: arrive at a settlement or conclusion

examples.igbo: Anyị luru ànì n'okwu ahụ.
examples.english: We settled that matter.

examples.igbo: O kwesịrị ka anyị luo ànì tupu anyị laa.
examples.english: We should conclude before we leave.

examples.igbo: Òmù osimiri ahụ dị ike.
examples.english: The current of that river is strong.

examples.igbo: Òmù mmiri ahụ ọ kwuru ụgbọ mmiri ahụ?
examples.english: Did the current carry the canoe?

examples.igbo: Ọ mara ahụ n'ọrụ ahụ.
examples.english: He became accustomed to that work.

examples.igbo: Ị marala ahụ n'oge ọkọchị?
examples.english: Have you become accustomed to the dry season?

note: The phrase ma āhụ means to become used to or fond of something.

gloss: backwards and forwards; up and down; to and fro

examples.igbo: Ọ na-agagharị iru nà àzụ n'ọnụ ụzọ.
examples.english: He walks to and fro at the door.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji aga iru nà àzụ?
examples.english: Why are you going to and fro?

gloss: Igbo name (versus ahà Oyìbo, English name)

examples.igbo: Aha Igbo m bụ Chukwuemeka.
examples.english: My Igbo name is Chukwuemeka.

examples.igbo: Ị maara aha Igbo ya?
examples.english: Do you know his Igbo name?

gloss: be surrounded by anxious, pushing crowd trying to get water (of tap)

examples.igbo: Pọmpù ahụ kwòrò ụmụ nwanyị na-achọ mmiri.
examples.english: The tap was surrounded by women seeking water.

examples.igbo: Pọmpù ọhụrụ ahụ ọ kwòrọla ndị mmadụ?
examples.english: Has the new tap become crowded with people?

note: The sense of -kwò here is specific to a tap being surrounded by a pushing crowd; I am not fully certain of the natural inflection.

examples.igbo: Anyị bọ̀rọ̀ ọ̀rà n'ụlọ nwanne m.
examples.english: We stayed overnight at my brother's house.

examples.igbo: Nri a bọ̀rọ̀ ọ̀rà, erila ya.
examples.english: This food has gone stale, don't eat it.

note: The stale-food sense is less certain.

examples.igbo: Oge nteta m bụ elekere ise.
examples.english: My waking-up time is five o'clock.

examples.igbo: Olee oge nteta gị?
examples.english: What is your waking-up time?

examples.igbo: Ùdo dị n'ezinụlọ anyị.
examples.english: There is peace in our family.

examples.igbo: Gịnị na-eweta ùdo n'obodo a?
examples.english: What brings peace in this town?

examples.english: Touch this cloth, you will feel its softness.

examples.english: Pray to God.

gloss: intrude; force in between tight space; insert

examples.igbo: Òkwutē ùwà tụùwà, chebe anyị n'oké mmiri.
examples.english: Rock of Ages, protect us in the great flood.

note: The phrase is a religious title, so the examples are naturally church-related.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-aga ịkụ nkụ n'àbọ.
examples.english: He goes to fetch firewood in the forest.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka, unu abanyela n'àbọ.
examples.english: Children, do not enter the forest.

examples.igbo: O nyere nwa ya onono mmiri.
examples.english: She gave her child a bottle of water.

examples.igbo: Onono a dara n'ala, ọ gbajiri?
examples.english: This bottle fell down, did it break?

examples.igbo: Iru ya chaghalịrị mgbe ọ nụrụ akụkọ ahụ.
examples.english: His face changed expression when he heard the news.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere iru gị jiri chaghalịa?
examples.english: Why did your face change expression?

note: The verb is usually used with iru; the inflected forms here are sound but the second sentence could also be phrased with chaghalịrị.

gloss: tear to pieces; to torn to pieces

examples.igbo: Nkịta dọkasịrị akpa m.
examples.english: The dog tore my bag to pieces.

examples.igbo: Ònye dọkasịrị akwụkwọ ahụ?
examples.english: Who tore that paper to pieces?

examples.igbo: Anyị jidere ìpo abụọ n'osimiri.
examples.english: We caught two ìpo fish in the river.

examples.igbo: Ìpo a dị ọhụrụ?
examples.english: Is this ìpo fresh?

note: Ìpo refers to a specific river fish; the examples keep it in a market/river context.

gloss: unpack items from something like bag, sack, box, trunk of a car

examples.igbo: O kwàsịrị akpa ya wee chọta akwụkwọ ahụ.
examples.english: He unpacked his bag and found the paper.

examples.igbo: Ị kwàsịrị igbe ahụ?
examples.english: Have you unpacked that box?

note: The verb is not common in everyday conversation, but the inflected forms fit the meaning 'unpack items'.

gloss: male name (literally pillar that holds the land)

examples.igbo: Aha nwa okorobịa ahụ bụ Ìdebūànì.
examples.english: The young man's name is Idebuani.

examples.igbo: Ìdebūànì, jide nkata ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: Idebuani, hold that basket well.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-aga n'ǹgòǹgò mgbe ọ na-achọ ụra.
examples.english: The child staggers when he is sleepy.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji na-aga n'ǹgòǹgò?
examples.english: Why are you staggering?

gloss: burst out crying after suppressed sobbing

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ mìkpọrọ mgbe e tiri ya ihe.
examples.english: The child burst out crying after holding back when he was beaten.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji mìkpọrọ?
examples.english: Why did you burst out crying after holding back?

examples.igbo: Ụgbọala a na-ebu ọnū.
examples.english: This car is fast.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ebu ọnū karịa nwanne ya.
examples.english: He is faster than his brother.

examples.igbo: Ọ fàbàrị n'ime ụgbọala ahụ.
examples.english: He squeezed into that vehicle.

examples.igbo: Fàbà n'ọnụ ụzọ ahụ ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Squeeze into that doorway quickly.

examples.igbo: Nnụnụ ahụ na-efefèga n'elu osimiri.
examples.english: The bird is flying across the river.

examples.igbo: Ụgbọelu ahụ fefèga n'elu ugwu ndị ahụ.
examples.english: The plane flew across over those mountains.

gloss: kind of native medicine prepared and stored in a bottle with palm-kernel oil, used for curing convulsions, poisoning

examples.igbo: E tinyere ọgwū ūde n'ime karama.
examples.english: The ọgwū ūde was put inside a bottle.

examples.igbo: Ọgwū ūde na-agwọ nsị?
examples.english: Does ọgwū ūde cure poisoning?

gloss: a masquerade with porcupine quills on the body

examples.igbo: Mmụọ ebì ogwū pụtara n'ọhịa.
examples.english: The porcupine-quill masquerade appeared in the village square.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-atụ egwu mmụọ ebì ogwū.
examples.english: Children are afraid of the porcupine-quill masquerade.

examples.igbo: A kpọrọ ya àda òrà n'obodo.
examples.english: She was called àda òrà in the town.

examples.igbo: Àda òrà na-elekọta ụmụaka niile.
examples.english: The daughter of all cares for all the children.

examples.igbo: O zụpụ̀tara ụmụ ya n'ụzọ ziri ezi.
examples.english: She trained her children in the right way.

examples.igbo: Ị zụpụ̀tara nwa gị ruo mgbe ọ gụsịrị akwụkwọ?
examples.english: Did you train your child until he finished school?

examples.igbo: O kere ego ahụ nkerà hà nhata.
examples.english: He divided that money into equal parts.

examples.igbo: Nkerà achịcha a hà nhata n'etiti ụmụaka?
examples.english: Is this sharing of the bread equal among the children?

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-agwu egwu n'ogige ahụ.
examples.english: The children are playing in that field.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-agwu egwu na nnọkọ ahụ?
examples.english: Will you play at that gathering?

examples.igbo: Anyị ji mgbòlòdị sie ofe.
examples.english: We used waterleaf to cook the soup.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara mgbòlòdị n'ahịa taa?
examples.english: Did you buy waterleaf at the market today?

gloss: take honey from the comb (after driving away the bees)

examples.igbo: O rara anwū n'ụlọ aṅụ.
examples.english: He took honey from the beehive.

examples.igbo: Ndị ọrụ na-ara anwū ugbu a?
examples.english: Are the workers taking honey now?

gloss: cloth, garment, robe set aside and devoted to wearing to divine service; Sunday best

examples.igbo: O yiri àfè ụkà ya gaa chọọchị.
examples.english: He wore his Sunday best to church.

examples.igbo: Yiri àfè ụkà gị taa.
examples.english: Wear your Sunday best today.

examples.igbo: Nye m ife ōŋụŋụ.
examples.english: Give me something to drink.

examples.igbo: O nyere anyị ife ōŋụŋụ mgbe anyị bịara.
examples.english: He gave us something to drink when we arrived.

headword: o mēekwe m (= o mā ekwe m)

examples.igbo: O mēekwe m ịga ahịa taa.
examples.english: I cannot go to the market today.

examples.igbo: O mēekwe gị ịbịa echi?
examples.english: Can you not come tomorrow?

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-agbu nchà n'ahụ ya.
examples.english: That child is soaping his body.

examples.igbo: Gbuo nchà tupu ị banye n'ime mmiri.
examples.english: Soap yourself before you get into the water.

examples.igbo: Ndị jī egbè èje orī wakporo ụlọ anyị n'abalị.
examples.english: Armed robbers attacked our house at night.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ndị jī egbè èje orī n'ụzọ?
examples.english: Did you see armed robbers on the road?

gloss: pot; clay pot; a one or two armed pot with a wide mouth, narrow neck and a big protruded spherical body mostly used for storing water

examples.igbo: Nne m zụtara ùdù ọhụrụ n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: My mother bought a new pot in the market today.

examples.igbo: Juru ùdù mmiri ka anyị ṅụọ taa.
examples.english: Fill the pot with water so we can drink today.

examples.igbo: Anyanwụ na-enwu enwu nke ukwuu taa.
examples.english: The sun is shining very brightly today.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ahụ ka ọkụ ahụ si enwu enwu?
examples.english: Do you see how that fire blazes?

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ dara ogbù, o nweghị ike ikwu okwu.
examples.english: That child is dumb; he cannot speak.

examples.igbo: Ị ma onye dara ogbù n'ụlọ akwụkwọ a?
examples.english: Do you know who is dumb in this school?

note: The verb phrase is understood, though other expressions for mute also exist.

examples.igbo: Enwe uchè ya mere ka ọ daa n'ule.
examples.english: His foolishness made him fail the exam.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akpọ enwe uchè ka ọ bụ amamihe?
examples.english: Do you call foolishness wisdom?

gloss: S. clarias, S. sorex, S. eupterus, S. ocellifer, S. gobroni, S. nigrita

examples.igbo: Òkpọ mmānụ bụ azụ a na-ahụ n'osimiri anyị.
examples.english: Catfish is a fish found in our river.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-azụta òkpọ mmānụ maka ofe taa?
examples.english: Will you buy catfish for soup today?

gloss: full strength; one's best or utmost

examples.igbo: O jiri òkò ya niile kụọ ihe ahụ.
examples.english: He used his full strength to hit that thing.

examples.igbo: Tinye òkò gị niile n'asọmpi a.
examples.english: Put your utmost into this competition.

examples.igbo: Echezọ m aha nwata ahụ taa.
examples.english: I forgot that child's name today.

examples.igbo: Echezọla ịzụta nri maka ụmụaka taa.
examples.english: Don't forget to buy food for the children today.

note: The verb form given is understood, though chefuo is also common.

gloss: undo the lock of (something), typically with a key; unlock

examples.igbo: O gbaghere ụzọ ụlọ akwụkwọ taa.
examples.english: He unlocked the school door today.

examples.igbo: Gbaghee igbe ahụ ka m hụ akwụkwọ dị n'ime.
examples.english: Unlock that box so I can see the book inside.

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ nedụrụ jụụ mgbe nne ya na-ekwu.
examples.english: The child kept quiet while his mother was talking.

examples.igbo: Nedụnụ, anyị na-anụ olu nne gị.
examples.english: Keep quiet, we are hearing your mother's voice.

note: The inflected forms are given as understood; usage can vary by dialect.

examples.igbo: Nwa agbọghọ ahụ nwere akpụkpọ ọcha.
examples.english: That girl has a fair complexion.

examples.igbo: Akpụkpọ ya ọ dị ọcha n'ezie?
examples.english: Is her skin really fair?

examples.igbo: O na-akèwò m òkè n'oge oriri.
examples.english: He denies me a share during feasts.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akèwò nwanne gị òkè mgbe ọ bụla?
examples.english: Do you deny your sibling a share every time?

note: The form na-akèwò is used for the verb stem; tone and inflection may vary.

examples.igbo: Nkịta ahụ gbọrọ ụja n'abalị niile.
examples.english: That dog barked all night.

examples.igbo: Ị nụrụ ọdụm ka ọ na-agbọ ụja n'abalị?
examples.english: Did you hear the lion roaring at night?

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka ahụ na-akpọlị oghū n'ama n'ehihie.
examples.english: Those children are playing in the compound in the afternoon.

examples.igbo: Bịa kpọlị oghū na anyị n'ama ugbu a.
examples.english: Come and play with us in the compound now.

note: The phrase is somewhat dialectal or less common; inflection may vary.

examples.igbo: O fàrà ego n'ime akpa ya.
examples.english: He stuffed money inside his pocket.

examples.igbo: Fàa akwụkwọ ndị a n'igbe ozugbo.
examples.english: Stuff these papers in the box immediately.

note: Past and imperative forms fàrà/fàa are my best reconstruction.

examples.igbo: O sụrụ ugbō n'ụtụtụ tupu anwụ awapụta.
examples.english: He weeded the farm in the morning before the sun came out.

examples.igbo: Sụọ ugbō n'ubi gị tupu mmiri ezoo.
examples.english: Weed the farm in your farm before it rains.

examples.igbo: Ígwé ojii gbara n'eluigwe n'ehihie a.
examples.english: Clouds gathered in the sky this afternoon.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ígwé ojii ahụ n'elu ugwu?
examples.english: Did you see that cloud on the mountain?

examples.igbo: O nyere m penì abụọ n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: He gave me two pennies in the morning.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere penì n'akpa gị?
examples.english: Do you have a penny in your pocket?

examples.igbo: Mkpọcha ahịhịa na-emerụ ala n'oge ọkọchị.
examples.english: Burning of grass damages the land in dry season.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ahụ mkpọcha ọkụ n'ime ọhịa?
examples.english: Do you see the burning fire in the forest?

note: The sense of mkpọcha as 'burning' is not fully certain; examples are plausible.

examples.igbo: O jiri ubè maa ehi n'ọhịa.
examples.english: He used a spear to pierce the cow in the forest.

examples.igbo: Maa ubè n'ahụ ehi ahụ!
examples.english: Pierce that cow with a spear!

note: Tone and verb inflection for ma ubè may vary.

examples.igbo: Ọ gbụrụ ikpèrè n'ala.
examples.english: He knelt on the ground.

examples.igbo: Gbụọ ikpèrè n'ala, ka anyị kpee ekpere.
examples.english: Kneel down so we can pray.

note: The verb is often written gbụ; used as given.

examples.igbo: Dọkịta bepụrụ alọ nwa ọhụrụ ahụ.
examples.english: The doctor cut the newborn's umbilical cord.

examples.igbo: Kpachara anya na alọ nwa ahụ.
examples.english: Be careful with that baby's umbilical cord.

examples.igbo: Osisi a dị oké.
examples.english: This tree is thick.

examples.igbo: Oké eriri a agaghị adị mfe ịdọka.
examples.english: This thick rope will not be easy to break.

examples.igbo: O nyere nwunye ya ọla.
examples.english: He gave his wife jewelry.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara ọla ọhụrụ?
examples.english: Did you buy new jewelry?

examples.igbo: Ọ nwụrụ n'ihi kpagbu nri.
examples.english: He died from choking on food.

examples.igbo: Kpagbu nri na-atụ ụmụaka egwu.
examples.english: Choking on food frightens children.

note: Treated as the noun 'choking'; if it is a verb form, the examples would differ.

examples.igbo: Anụ ahụ kpàgburu nwa ahụ.
examples.english: The meat choked that child.

examples.igbo: Kwụsị iri ngwa ngwa, ọ ga-akpàgbu gị.
examples.english: Stop eating fast; it will choke you.

note: Inflected forms from the verb stem -kpàgbu.

examples.igbo: Ọ gwòrọ osisi ahụ n'ime obere iberibe.
examples.english: He broke that wood into small pieces.

examples.igbo: Gwòo osisi ahụ, anyị ga-esi nri.
examples.english: Break that wood into pieces; we will cook.

note: Inflected forms from the verb stem -gwò.

gloss: chew, gnaw everything or the whole of the object (of ants, rats, etc.)

examples.igbo: Oke na-atagbado akpa ahụ.
examples.english: The rat is gnawing that bag.

examples.igbo: Ndanda na-atagbado achicha ahụ?
examples.english: Are ants gnawing that bread?

note: Inflected forms from the verb stem -tagbàdo.

examples.igbo: Uwe ya na-acha iriīrē.
examples.english: Her dress is pink.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara akwa iriīrē?
examples.english: Did you buy pink cloth?

note: The colour term is used as given.

examples.igbo: Ụdị azụ̀ a dị ọnụ ahịa n'ahịa.
examples.english: This type of fish is expensive in the market.

examples.igbo: Olee ụdị osikapa ị na-ere?
examples.english: What type of rice do you sell?

examples.igbo: Àtùtù osisi na-arapara n'aka nwatakịrị mgbe ọ na-egwu egwu.
examples.english: Tree sap sticks to a child's hand when he plays.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eji àtùtù osisi eme ọgwụ?
examples.english: Do you use tree sap to make medicine?

note: The phrase is somewhat specialized, but the sentences use it in the sap sense.

examples.igbo: Anyị riri nni anyàsì tupu anyị lakpuo ụra.
examples.english: We ate supper before we slept.

examples.igbo: Nni anyàsì adịla njikere maka anyị?
examples.english: Is supper ready for us?

examples.igbo: Pusi ahụ na-acha ọcha nke ukwuu.
examples.english: That cat is very white.

examples.igbo: Ị na-enye pusi nri kwa ụtụtụ?
examples.english: Do you feed the cat every morning?

examples.igbo: Esuso toro n'ụkwụ ya nke ukwuu.
examples.english: A boil grew badly on his foot.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ete ọgwụ n'esuso ahụ kwa ụtụtụ?
examples.english: Are you applying medicine to that boil every morning?

examples.igbo: Mgbụ ākwụkwọ juru n'ụzọ n'ogige anyị.
examples.english: Shed leaves filled the path in our compound.

examples.igbo: Ị zọrọ mgbụ ākwụkwọ niile n'ogige?
examples.english: Did you sweep all the shed leaves in the compound?

note: The phrase is uncommon; I used it as given for shed/dry leaves.

gloss: Igbo name (versus afà Oyìbo, European name)

examples.igbo: Afā Ìgbò nwata a bụ Chukwuemeka.
examples.english: This child's Igbo name is Chukwuemeka.

examples.igbo: Ị ma afā Ìgbò nne gị?
examples.english: Do you know your mother's Igbo name?

gloss: pull down the lower eyelids and widening the eyes as a form of mockery to imply 'serves you right'

examples.igbo: O bọọ ntọ̀ọọ̄ n'anya ya mgbe m dara ule.
examples.english: He pulled down his eyelid at me when I failed the exam.

examples.igbo: Ị na-abọ ntọ̀ọọ̄ n'anya gị mgbe mmadụ dara?
examples.english: Do you pull down your eyelid when someone fails?

note: The gesture phrase is rare; the wording follows the given sense.

examples.igbo: Ha kọọrọ nwanne m ọgwụ n'ihi ego.
examples.english: They practiced sorcery against my brother because of money.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ ịkọ m ọgwụ n'ihi gịnị?
examples.english: Why do you want to practice sorcery against me?

note: The verb phrase is restricted; I used the expected inflected forms.

examples.igbo: Nna m lụrụ ụnò ọhụrụ n'afọ gara aga.
examples.english: My father built a new house last year.

examples.igbo: Olee mgbe ị ga-alụ ụnò gị?
examples.english: When will you build your house?

note: Standard Igbo more commonly uses ụlọ; I used ụnò as given.

examples.igbo: Ahịhịa na-agbebà n'ubi ọka anyị.
examples.english: Weeds are creeping into our corn farm.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka ewu gbebà n'ogige akwụkwọ ndụ gị.
examples.english: Don't let the goat encroach into your vegetable garden.

examples.igbo: Akwụkọ mmiri ahụ gbazere n'anwụ.
examples.english: The ice melted in the sun.

examples.igbo: Kpoo mmanụ ahụ ka ọ gbazè.
examples.english: Heat that oil so that it melts.

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ na-atụfu mkpomkpo n'okporo ámá.
examples.english: That child is dumping rubbish on the road.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji tụfu mkpomkpo n'azụ ụlọ?
examples.english: Why did you throw rubbish behind the house?

gloss: be clear, settled, shady; settle, become clear (of liquids)

examples.igbo: Mmiri ahụ adọla, ị pụrụ ịṅụ ya.
examples.english: The water has settled, you can drink it.

examples.igbo: Kwe ka mmiri ahụ dòọ tupu i ṅụọ ya.
examples.english: Let the water settle before you drink it.

gloss: construct an akwalī to increase fruitfulness

examples.igbo: Ndị ọrụ ugbo ahụ tiri akwalī n'ubi ha.
examples.english: Those farmers made an akwalī in their farm.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eti akwalī n'ubi gị tupu ị kụọ ihe?
examples.english: Will you make an akwalī in your farm before you plant?

note: The practice behind 'akwalī' is not well known to me, so the sentences may not match how speakers actually phrase it.

gloss: small fish with fins, caught when the Niger falls (November)

examples.igbo: Ndị ọkụ azụ na-egbu ifùlù n'ọnwa Nọvemba.
examples.english: Fishermen catch ifùlù in November.

examples.igbo: Nne m ghere ifùlù maka nri abalị.
examples.english: My mother fried ifùlù for dinner.

examples.igbo: Ndị obodo ahụ kobere eze ha èbùbè.
examples.english: The people of that town honoured their king.

examples.igbo: O kwesịrị ka anyị kobe nne anyị èbùbè.
examples.english: It is right that we honour our mother.

gloss: take or lift up hands together

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka ahụ chịliri aka ọnụ n'okporo ámá.
examples.english: The children held hands together on the road.

examples.igbo: Ọ chịliri aka abụọ nara ego ahụ.
examples.english: She cupped her two hands and took the money.

gloss: change (usually for worse); turn; alter; turn round

examples.igbo: Ghaa n'aka ekpe mgbe i ruru ebe ahụ.
examples.english: Turn left when you reach that place.

examples.igbo: Ụzọ ahụ na-agha n'akụkụ ugwu.
examples.english: The road turns towards the hillside.

gloss: skirt; native skirt worn as underwear

examples.igbo: Ọ zụtara mbè n'ukwù ọhụrụ n'ahịa Eke.
examples.english: She bought a new skirt at Eke market.

examples.igbo: Sakwaa mbè n'ukwù gị, ọ ruru unyi.
examples.english: Wash your skirt, it is dirty.

examples.igbo: Nne m zụtara ntī oke n’ahịa.
examples.english: My mother bought ntī oke at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị na-esi ntī oke ofe?
examples.english: Do you cook ntī oke soup?

examples.igbo: Ọ tụbara mgbụgbō ākwa n’ala.
examples.english: He threw an eggshell on the ground.

examples.igbo: Gbakọta mgbụgbō ākwa niile tupu ị kpochaa ụlọ.
examples.english: Gather all the eggshells before you sweep the house.

examples.igbo: Onye dibịa tụrụ ya ǹkì n’ihu.
examples.english: The native doctor tattooed marks on his face.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-atụ ǹkì n’aka gị?
examples.english: Will you tattoo marks on your hand?

examples.igbo: Ndùdùgandū ǹke ītọ bi n’ụlọ a.
examples.english: The third generation lives in this house.

examples.igbo: Ị bụ ndùdùgandū ǹke ītọ n’ezinụlọ anyị?
examples.english: Are you the third generation in our family?

examples.igbo: Anyị jidere otu ònìinu n’osimiri.
examples.english: We caught one ònìinu in the river.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ònìinu n’ahịa taa?
examples.english: Did you see ònìinu at the market today?

examples.igbo: Ọ bìàjuru akpa ya n’akwụkwọ.
examples.english: He filled his bag with books by squeezing them in.

examples.igbo: Bìàjuo ite ahụ n’osikapa.
examples.english: Fill that pot with rice by squeezing it in.

examples.igbo: Ọ zere ume mgbe ọ nụrụ akụkọ ahụ.
examples.english: He sighed when he heard that news.

examples.igbo: Ị zere ume n’ihi ọrụ a?
examples.english: Did you sigh because of this work?

examples.igbo: O kpàrù nkàtà n’ụlọ.
examples.english: He wove a basket in the house.

examples.igbo: Kpàa nkàtà maka ahịa echi.
examples.english: Weave a basket for tomorrow's market.

gloss: spy; scout; private detective (from -ta nke eavesdrop)

examples.igbo: Òtanke ahụ na-eso ndị ohi n'ahịa.
examples.english: That spy follows thieves in the market.

examples.igbo: Ì bụ òtanke ha zitere anyị?
examples.english: Are you the spy they sent to us?

examples.igbo: O pìgburu ọkụkọ ahụ n'aka ya.
examples.english: He killed the chicken by squeezing it in his hand.

examples.igbo: E kwesịghị ipìgbu ụmụ ọkụkọ.
examples.english: One should not squeeze chicks to death.

gloss: name of one of the founding fathers of one of the nine quarters of Onitsha; hence Umùdeì, a village in Onitsha founded by him

examples.igbo: Deì bụ otu n'ime ndị malitere Onitsha.
examples.english: Dei is one of the people who founded Onitsha.

examples.igbo: Ụmụ Deì bi n'Umùdeì.
examples.english: Dei's children live in Umudei.

note: Proper historical name; examples are necessarily historical.

examples.igbo: O ji mpekarị ego zụta akwụkwọ ahụ.
examples.english: He used less money to buy that book.

examples.igbo: Mpekarị ụmụaka bịara taa.
examples.english: Fewer children came today.

examples.igbo: Ụmù azì na-egwu egwu n'ogige.
examples.english: Young children are playing in the field.

examples.igbo: Ì na-elekọta ụmù azì ndị ahụ?
examples.english: Are you looking after those young children?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-eme òtịtị mgbe ọ tetara n'ụra.
examples.english: He stretches when he wakes from sleep.

examples.igbo: Òtịtị dị mma maka ahụ́ mmadụ.
examples.english: Stretching is good for the human body.

examples.igbo: O kwụrụ ùdò n'osisi mango.
examples.english: He hanged himself on a mango tree.

examples.igbo: O kwụrụ ùdò n'abalị?
examples.english: Did he hang himself at night?

gloss: freeborn children; children of a king or chief

examples.igbo: Ụmùdeì na-akwanyere ndị okenye ùgwù.
examples.english: Freeborn children respect elders.

examples.igbo: Ụmùdeì bụ ụmụ eze na ndị isi.
examples.english: Freeborn children are children of kings and chiefs.

note: Rare status term; the examples show the likely sense but I am not fully certain of current idiomatic usage.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-adọ nsogbu n'obodo a.
examples.english: He causes trouble in this town.

examples.igbo: Dọọ m nsogbu ọzọ, ị ga-ahụ ihe.
examples.english: Cause me trouble again, and you will see.

examples.igbo: Ǹkù nnụnụ ahụ gbajiri, ọ naghịzi efe efe.
examples.english: That bird's wing is broken, it can no longer fly.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ǹkù ọkụkọ a ji dị mkpụmkpụ?
examples.english: Why are this chicken's wings so short?

examples.igbo: Ha doro ajā gburugburu ụlọ ahụ.
examples.english: They built a wall around that house.

examples.igbo: Doo ajā n'ebe ahụ tupu mmiri abịa.
examples.english: Build a wall there before the rain comes.

gloss: foul; defile; be defiled, polluted (as when water containing sediment, standing in a jar, is stirred, or when the water of the stream is polluted by the activities of fish)

examples.igbo: Mmiri dị n'ite ahụ gbalụ, ọ dịghị mma.
examples.english: The water in that pot is fouled, it is not good.

examples.igbo: Gịnị gbalu mmiri ọṅụṅụ anyị?
examples.english: What fouled our drinking water?

note: Inflected forms of -gbalù vary; past/stative 'gbalu' is used here.

gloss: title entitling holder to be called ǹzè; title of high degree, and much coveted, conferring on the owner privileges and honour as a sacrosanct being

examples.igbo: O nwere ọzō, ya mere a na-akpọ ya ǹzè.
examples.english: He holds a title, that is why he is called ǹzè.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ ịnweta ọzō dịka nna gị?
examples.english: Do you want to take a title like your father?

gloss: to slander; to speak evil of someone or something

examples.igbo: O kwutọrọ nwanne ya n'ihu ọha.
examples.english: He slandered his brother in public.

examples.igbo: Kwụsị ịkwutọ ndị agbata obi gị.
examples.english: Stop slandering your neighbours.

gloss: stubbornness; habitual disobedience (usually of young person)

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ nwere mkpọchi ǹtì, ọ naghị anụ ihe a na-agwa ya.
examples.english: That child is stubborn, he does not listen to what he is told.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji nwee mkpọchi ǹtì?
examples.english: Why are you so stubborn?

examples.igbo: O dọliri ákwà ahụ elu n'elu ụlọ.
examples.english: He drew that cloth up onto the roof.

examples.igbo: Dọli igbe ahụ elu, mmiri na-abịa.
examples.english: Draw that box up, the rain is coming.

note: The exact sense of dọ̀li is unclear; examples assume 'draw/pull up' and may not match the intended meaning.

examples.igbo: O riri nrā nnukwu maka izu ohi.
examples.english: He paid a heavy fine for stealing.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eri nrā ma i mebie iwu?
examples.english: Will you pay a fine if you break the rule?

note: Assumes nrā is the fine paid or incurred; the idiom ri nrā is used as given.

examples.igbo: Ọ kwugidere okwu ya n'ihu ọha.
examples.english: He continued his speech in public.

examples.igbo: Kwugide, anyị na-ege gị ntị.
examples.english: Continue speaking, we are listening to you.

examples.igbo: O yiri àfè ọhụrụ gaa ahịa.
examples.english: She wore a new cloth and went to the market.

examples.igbo: Yiri àfè gị ngwa ngwa, anyị na-aga ahịa.
examples.english: Wear your cloth quickly, we are going to the market.

examples.igbo: Ọ gbatịrị akwa ahụ n'ala ụlọ.
examples.english: He unrolled that cloth on the floor of the house.

examples.igbo: Gbatịa akwa ahụ n'ala ụlọ.
examples.english: Unroll that cloth on the floor of the house.

gloss: (-a after a ị ụ; -e after e i u; -ọ after ọ; -o after o) completive or open vowel suffix, used with most verbs in the imperative, the subjunctive, and the sequential forms Lùa ọlū Do the work: Kà ànyị jee Let us go ... ò wèe nalue ụnò wèe fụ yā ... and then he got home and found it

examples.igbo: Lùa ọlū gị, rie nri gị.
examples.english: Do your work, eat your food.

examples.igbo: Ọ wèe zụọ azụ, wèe too ya.
examples.english: He then bought fish and then roasted it.

note: The headword is a grammatical suffix; examples show it in imperative and sequential verb forms.

gloss: dry land (as opposed to water); high land between Asaba and Agbor

examples.igbo: Ụgbọ mmiri ahụ ruru n'enu ànì.
examples.english: The boat reached dry land.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ enu ànì n'akụkụ osimiri?
examples.english: Did you see dry land by the river?

examples.igbo: E ji nzu oyìbo na-ede ihe n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: Chalk is used to write things in school.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara nzu oyìbo n'ahịa?
examples.english: Did you buy chalk at the market?

examples.igbo: Ọ mere òmùme ọma nye nne ya.
examples.english: He did a good deed for his mother.

examples.igbo: Kà anyị na-eme òmùme ọma.
examples.english: Let us do good deeds.

examples.igbo: Nkịta ahụ yigburu ọkụkọ m.
examples.english: That dog turned upon and killed my chicken.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eyigbu ya ma ọ bịa nso?
examples.english: Will you turn upon and kill it if it comes close?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ege ntị na redio.
examples.english: He is listening to the radio.

examples.igbo: Gee ntị n'ihe onye nkụzi na-ekwu.
examples.english: Listen to what the teacher is saying.

gloss: rub, pluck off grains from cob, etc.

examples.igbo: Ọ kpọsịrị ọka niile n'ọkpụ.
examples.english: He plucked all the corn off the cob.

examples.igbo: Kpọsịa ọka ahụ n'ọkpụ tupu ị see ya.
examples.english: Pluck that corn off the cob before you cook it.

examples.igbo: Ọ kpụgọrọ mmiri n'olulu n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: He drew water from the well in the morning.

examples.igbo: Kpụgo mmiri ahụ n'olulu taa.
examples.english: Draw that water from the well today.

examples.igbo: Anụ a tìrì àtì, ọ dịghị mfe ata.
examples.english: This meat is tough; it is not easy to chew.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ osisi tìrì àtì n'ọhịa?
examples.english: Did you see a hard tree in the bush?

note: The verb phrase is not common in everyday speech; examples use its inflected form.

examples.igbo: Agwọ ahụ dị ogologo ma dị egwu.
examples.english: That snake is long and scary.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ agwọ n'ubi taa?
examples.english: Did you see a snake in the farm today?

examples.igbo: Ndị inyom na-akwe akwà n'ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: The women weave cloth in our house.

examples.igbo: Kwe akwà a ngwa ngwa, anyị ga-ere ya.
examples.english: Weave this cloth quickly; we will sell it.

gloss: be too much; surpass expected quantity or size

examples.igbo: Ahịhịa fere okè n'ubi a.
examples.english: The weeds are too much in this farm.

examples.igbo: Mmiri fere okè n'ite ahụ, wụpụ ya.
examples.english: The water is too much in that pot; pour some out.

note: Inflected forms of fè okè are given; the phrase is idiomatic but tone marking on fere may vary.

examples.igbo: Abù m onye Ìgbò, aha m bụ Chidi.
examples.english: I am an Igbo person; my name is Chidi.

examples.igbo: Abù m onye Ìgbò, ị bụkwa onye Ìgbò?
examples.english: I am an Igbo person; are you also an Igbo person?

examples.igbo: Ọkpụkpụ nkịtā na-eto n'ọhịa anyị.
examples.english: The ọkpụkpụ nkịtā tree grows in our bush.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-eji ọkpụkpụ nkịtā agwọ ọrịa.
examples.english: We use ọkpụkpụ nkịtā to treat illness.

note: The tree is chiefly known by its botanical name; example usage is plausible but not everyday.

examples.igbo: Ànì mmarùbe mere n'abalị, ụlọ dara.
examples.english: An earthquake happened at night, and a house collapsed.

examples.igbo: Ị nụtụla banyere ànì mmarùbe n'ala anyị?
examples.english: Have you heard about the earthquake in our land?

examples.igbo: Mkpụlụ mmadù bịara nzukọ ahụ.
examples.english: Few people came to that meeting.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ naanị mkpụlụ mmadù ka anyị hụrụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: It was only a few people that we saw at the market.

gloss: long, narrow calabash for carrying water or wine; calabash

examples.igbo: Mama bu agbè mmiri n'isi.
examples.english: Mother carried a calabash of water on her head.

examples.igbo: Juru agbè a mmiri, ọ ga-ezu anyị.
examples.english: Fill this calabash with water; it will be enough for us.

examples.igbo: O kàgharị̄rị̄ oche ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: He re-fixed that chair well.

examples.igbo: Ị kàgharị̄rị̄ egwuregwu ahụ?
examples.english: Did you postpone that match?

note: Unsure of exact inflection of kàgharị̄; both senses covered.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-emegheli n'èzí.
examples.english: Children are fooling about outside.

examples.igbo: Emeghela, rụọ ọrụ gị.
examples.english: Don't fool about, do your work.

examples.igbo: Òsụsụ osikapa na-ewe oge.
examples.english: Pounding rice takes time.

examples.igbo: Mee òsụsụ ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Do the pounding quickly.

examples.igbo: O kèrè achịcha ahụ ìbùọ.
examples.english: He divided that bread into two.

examples.igbo: Kee ya ìbùọ.
examples.english: Divide it into two.

examples.igbo: O gwùrù n'osimiri.
examples.english: He swam in the river.

examples.igbo: Ị gwùrù n'osimiri?
examples.english: Did you swim in the river?

examples.igbo: Ǹdù na-eri anụ ahụ.
examples.english: Maggots are eating the meat.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ǹdù n'ime ya?
examples.english: Did you see maggots in it?

gloss: secret place worshipped by Ọnịcha people

examples.igbo: Ànị Ònìchà bụ ebe nsọ.
examples.english: Ànị Ònìchà is a sacred place.

examples.igbo: Ndị Ònìchà na-efe ànị Ònìchà?
examples.english: Do the Ọnịcha people worship Ànị Ònìchà?

note: Cultural term; unsure if 'efe' is the right verb for worshiping a place.

examples.igbo: O kweere akwà ahụ.
examples.english: He wove that cloth.

examples.igbo: Kweere akwà ahụ ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Weave that cloth quickly.

gloss: force to drink water (e.g. primitive way of feeding baby); force to drink water by pushing the victim under water

examples.igbo: O gbara nwa ahụ mmilī.
examples.english: He forced that child to drink water.

examples.igbo: Gbaa ya mmilī.
examples.english: Force him to drink water.

examples.igbo: O lipùrù nri ahụ niile.
examples.english: He devoured all that food.

examples.igbo: Lipu ya ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Devour it quickly.

gloss: take the whole number for oneself

examples.igbo: Ada chịkọlụrụ ego ahụ niile.
examples.english: Ada took all the money for herself.

examples.igbo: Ì chịkọlụrụ ụmụnne gị anụ ahụ niile?
examples.english: Did you take all the meat from your siblings?

note: Sense of -chịkọlụ is not fully clear to me; examples are plausible but I would not vouch for the exact usage.

examples.igbo: O ji mpòmà gbue osisi ahụ.
examples.english: He used a matchet to cut down that tree.

examples.igbo: Zụta mpòmà ọhụrụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: Buy a new matchet at the market.

examples.igbo: Onye chọrọ iza ajụjụ wèni aka elu.
examples.english: Whoever wants to answer the question should raise a hand.

examples.igbo: Wèni aka gị elu ka m hụ gị.
examples.english: Raise your hand so that I can see you.

gloss: write in(to); enter by writing; include

examples.igbo: Denye aha gị n'akwụkwọ a.
examples.english: Write your name in this book.

examples.igbo: O denyere m aha n'ndepụta ahụ.
examples.english: She included my name in that list.

examples.igbo: M ga-akpa mmanụ n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: I will buy oil at the market today.

examples.igbo: Kpaa mmanụ ntakịrị ka anyị sie nri.
examples.english: Buy a little oil so that we can cook.

examples.igbo: Pịa utùegbè égbè a.
examples.english: Press the trigger of this gun.

examples.igbo: Utùegbè égbè ahụ adịghị arụ ọrụ.
examples.english: The trigger of that gun is not working.

gloss: be old by year; clock an age

examples.igbo: Nna m gbàrị afọ iri isii.
examples.english: My father has clocked sixty years.

examples.igbo: Nwanne gị ọ gbàrị afọ iri abụọ?
examples.english: Has your sibling clocked twenty years?

examples.igbo: N'oke efifie naabo, anyanwụ na-ekpo ọkụ nke ukwuu.
examples.english: At midday the sun is very hot.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-abịa tupu oke efifie naabo?
examples.english: Will you come before midday?

gloss: the side part of a street dedicated to pedestrians; sidewalk

examples.igbo: Anyị jere ije n'ụzụ̀ụkwū.
examples.english: We walked on the sidewalk.

examples.igbo: Zọrọ ụkwụ n'ụzụ̀ụkwū, ọ bụghị n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: Walk on the sidewalk, not in the road.

gloss: (slang) food prepared by mashing together different kinds of

examples.igbo: Nne m gwọrọ ji na akpụ mee ǹgwòlù ǹgwọlụ.
examples.english: My mother mashed cassava and cocoyam to make ngwolu ngwolu.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eri ǹgwòlù ǹgwọlụ taa?
examples.english: Will you eat ngwolu ngwolu today?

note: Slang term not fully familiar; examples are tentative.

gloss: large earthenware pot used for storing water

examples.igbo: Ùdụ ahụ juru eju mmiri.
examples.english: That large pot is full of water.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eji ùdụ a weta mmiri?
examples.english: Will you use this large pot to bring water?

examples.igbo: O gbara akpụkpọ ewu ahụ n'ọhịa.
examples.english: He flayed that goat in the field.

examples.igbo: Gbaa akpụkpọ ewu a ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Flay this goat quickly.

examples.igbo: Osisi a na-asọpị n'ọnụ.
examples.english: This stick tapers at the tip.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ka osisi ahụ si asọpị n'ọnụ?
examples.english: Did you see how that stick tapers at the tip?

examples.igbo: Ha lefuru ya n'ohu n'oge ochie.
examples.english: They sold him into slavery in olden times.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-alefu mmadụ n'ohu?
examples.english: Will you sell a person into slavery?

examples.igbo: Ha bītèrè aka n'obodo ọzọ.
examples.english: They live far away in another town.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-abītè aka, anyị anaghị ahụ ha.
examples.english: We live far away; we do not see them.

note: Phrase and inflection uncertain.

examples.igbo: Ụlọ ahụ dàchàrà kpamkpam n'oké ifufe.
examples.english: That house collapsed completely in the strong wind.

examples.igbo: Atụmatụ gị ọ dàchàrà?
examples.english: Did your plan fail completely?

gloss: (literally European money) name given to the present currency when it existed side by side with cowrie currency

examples.igbo: Nna ochie m na-eji ego oyìbo azụ ihe.
examples.english: My grandfather used European money to buy things.

examples.igbo: Mgbe ahụ, ego oyìbo na mkpụrụ ego dịkọtara.
examples.english: Then, European money and cowries existed together.

examples.igbo: Agụū mmīli na-agụ m mgbe ọ na-ekpo ọkụ.
examples.english: I am thirsty when it is hot.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere agụū mmīli?
examples.english: Are you thirsty?

examples.igbo: O nwere isi ọma n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: He had good luck in the market today.

examples.igbo: Isi ọma ga-eso gị n'ụzọ.
examples.english: Good luck will follow you on the journey.

examples.igbo: Ùfù na-eri ọkụkọ n'ụlọ anyị n'abalị.
examples.english: A mongoose eats chickens in our house at night.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ùfù n'okporo ụzọ?
examples.english: Did you see a mongoose on the road?

gloss: traditional marriage rite of the Igbo people; wine carrying

examples.igbo: Ha gbara nkwụ n'ụlọ nne ya.
examples.english: They performed the wine-carrying rite at her mother's house.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-agba nkwụ tupu agbamakwụkwọ?
examples.english: Will you do the wine-carrying before the wedding?

examples.igbo: Ọ dàjùlù àdàjụ n'ụlọ akwụkwọ taa.
examples.english: It is very quiet at school today.

examples.igbo: Ọ dàjùlù àdàjụ n'ahịa taa?
examples.english: Is it very quiet in the market today?

examples.igbo: Òkpụkpọ nkụ mebiri ihe ubi anyị n'afọ a.
examples.english: Drought spoiled our crops this year.

examples.igbo: Òkpụkpọ nkụ na-eweta ụnwụ nri?
examples.english: Does drought cause famine?

examples.igbo: Nri a gbara ụka n'ọnụ m.
examples.english: This food tastes sour in my mouth.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụrụ na mmanya gbara ụka, awụpụla ya.
examples.english: If the drink is sour, pour it away.

examples.igbo: O fùnyere ume n'ime bọọlụ nke ọma.
examples.english: He inflated the ball well.

examples.igbo: Fùnye ume n'ime taya ụgbọala tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Inflate the car tyre before you leave.

examples.igbo: Anwụ ntà tara m n'abalị niile.
examples.english: Mosquitoes bit me all night.

examples.igbo: Gbuo anwụ ntà ndị ahụ tupu ha ata gị.
examples.english: Kill those mosquitoes before they bite you.

gloss: accreditation; recognition given to (mostly educational) institutions for maintaining the required standard

examples.igbo: Mahadum ahụ nwetara nzèrèntozù n'afọ a.
examples.english: That university received accreditation this year.

examples.igbo: Ụlọ akwụkwọ ahụ nwetara nzèrèntozù?
examples.english: Did the school receive accreditation?

gloss: stretch; pull or stretch to make long

examples.igbo: Sètị̀ eriri ahụ ka ọ dị ogologo.
examples.english: Stretch that rope so it is long.

examples.igbo: O sètị̀rị̀ akwa ahụ ruo n'ala.
examples.english: She stretched the cloth down to the ground.

examples.igbo: O chụgọrọ ehi ahụ n'elu ugwu.
examples.english: He drove the cow up the hill.

examples.igbo: Chụgo ewu ndị a banye n'ogige.
examples.english: Drive these goats up into the pen.

examples.igbo: Mbèbèlè anyā ya na-egbu mgbu.
examples.english: His eyelid is hurting.

examples.igbo: Kpuchie mbèbèlè anyā gị, zuru ike ntakịrị.
examples.english: Close your eyelids and rest a little.

examples.igbo: A fụrụ m efè ịga ahịa taa.
examples.english: I found time to go to the market today.

examples.igbo: Olee mgbe ị ga-afụ efè ịbịa ile anyị?
examples.english: When will you find time to come and see us?

examples.igbo: Òŋiŋe n'elu mmiri ahụ siri ike.
examples.english: Stepping over that stream was difficult.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-atụ egwu òŋiŋe n'elu mgbidi ahụ.
examples.english: He is afraid of stepping over that wall.

examples.igbo: Ha kpara okè n'etiti ubi abụọ ahụ.
examples.english: They made a boundary between the two farms.

examples.igbo: Kpaa okè n'ala gị tupu mmiri abịa.
examples.english: Make a boundary on your land before the rain comes.

gloss: shine; burn; be clean, pure, bright; flare; blaze

examples.igbo: Ọkụ ahụ na-enwu n'ọhịa.
examples.english: That fire is blazing in the bush.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere anyanwụ ji enwu ọcha taa?
examples.english: Why is the sun shining brightly today?

examples.igbo: O gbupụrụ alaka osisi ahụ.
examples.english: He cut off the branch of that tree.

examples.igbo: Gbupụ eriri a tupu ọ gbawaa.
