examples.english: Cut off this rope before it tears.

examples.igbo: Ọtụtụ ndị Hausa na-ekpe Ụkāàlakụ̀bā.
examples.english: Many Hausa people practice Islam.

examples.igbo: Ụkāàlakụ̀bā bụ okpukpe a na-akụzi n'ụlọ akwụkwọ ụfọdụ.
examples.english: Islam is a religion taught in some schools.

examples.igbo: O buru ǹche ānwụ gaa ahịa.
examples.english: She took a sunshade to the market.

examples.igbo: Ǹche ānwụ a adịghị arụ ọrụ.
examples.english: This sunshade does not work.

examples.igbo: Onye mmùta ahụ na-agụ akwụkwọ nke ọma.
examples.english: That pupil studies well.

examples.igbo: Ị bụ onye mmùta ma ọ bụ onye nkuzi?
examples.english: Are you a pupil or a teacher?

examples.igbo: Afọ ya tepùbèrè n'ihi oke nri.
examples.english: His stomach is bulging because of too much food.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere afọ gị ji tepùbe?
examples.english: Why is your stomach bulging?

examples.igbo: Nne m na-akọ akụkọ mgbe anyị riri nri.
examples.english: My mother tells stories when we finish eating.

examples.igbo: Kọọ m akụkọ gbasara njem gị.
examples.english: Tell me a story about your journey.

examples.igbo: Ǹke ōbụnà ka ị họrọ, ọ dị mma.
examples.english: Whichever you choose is fine.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-ewere ǹke ōbụnà?
examples.english: Will you take either one?

examples.igbo: Ewu nyiè ahụ amụọla nwa.
examples.english: That female goat has given birth.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara ewu nyiè?
examples.english: Did you buy a female goat?

gloss: arụsị of the second Igbo market day

examples.igbo: Ndị obodo ahụ na-efe Orìè n'ụbọchị ahịa.
examples.english: The people of that town worship Orìè on market day.

examples.igbo: Ị na-efe arụsị Orìè?
examples.english: Do you worship the deity Orìè?

gloss: be dry Wètalụ m  òfu oko ọkā kpọ lụ akpọ Bring me a dry ear of corn

examples.igbo: Ọka anyị tinyere n'èzí kpọrọ akpọ.
examples.english: The corn we put outside is dry.

examples.igbo: Uwe m kpọrọ akpọ?
examples.english: Are my clothes dry?

gloss: irredeemable; that which can never be completely repaid; debt

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ akwụ cha anyị ji ya.
examples.english: It is an irredeemable debt we owe him.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ akwụ cha ka ọ bụ?
examples.english: Is it an irredeemable debt?

gloss: grief; deep sorrow; heartache; great unhappiness caused by the death of a loved one;

examples.igbo: Àrị̀rị̀ gburu ya mgbe nne ya nwụrụ.
examples.english: Grief killed him when his mother died.

examples.igbo: Wepụ àrị̀rị̀ n'obi gị.
examples.english: Remove grief from your heart.

examples.igbo: Ọ zìchàrà imi ya n’akwa.
examples.english: He blew his nose on the cloth.

examples.igbo: Ị zìchàrà imi gị tupu ị bata?
examples.english: Did you blow your nose before you came in?

examples.igbo: Ọ zèrè nri ahụ n’ihi ísì ya.
examples.english: He loathed that food because of its smell.

examples.igbo: Ị na-azè ọrụ ugbo kpamkpam?
examples.english: Do you abhor farm work completely?

examples.igbo: Pìnye aka gị n’ime akpa ahụ.
examples.english: Squeeze your hand into that bag.

examples.igbo: Nwata pìnyere mkpịsị aka ya n’ime oghere.
examples.english: The child squeezed his finger into the hole.

examples.igbo: Ụkwụ m na-arìnyị m mgbe m na-aga ahịa.
examples.english: My leg hurts me when I go to market.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-arìnyị gị ebe a?
examples.english: Does it hurt you here?

examples.igbo: Biko gadòbe n’akụkụ m.
examples.english: Please move nearer to me.

examples.igbo: Ọ gadòbèrè aka n’ọkụ.
examples.english: He moved his hand nearer the fire.

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ nwere ǹzịza n’olu.
examples.english: That child has a swelling on the neck.

examples.igbo: Ǹzịza a na-egbu gị mgbu?
examples.english: Is this swelling paining you?

examples.igbo: Ọnya ahụ luru arụrụ n’ihi unyi.
examples.english: The wound bred worms because of dirt.

examples.igbo: Anụ ahụ ga-elu arụrụ ma ọ nọghị n’friji.
examples.english: The meat will breed worms if it is not in the fridge.

gloss: molar teeth; part of the jaw where they are situated

examples.igbo: Agbùlùgada m na-egbu m mgbu mgbe m na-ata ihe.
examples.english: My molars hurt when I chew.

examples.igbo: Were agbùlùgada taa anụ ahụ.
examples.english: Use your molars to chew that meat.

examples.igbo: Ọ rèpụrụ n’ọnụ ụlọ n’abalị.
examples.english: He crept out of the room at night.

examples.igbo: Rèpụ n’ụlọ tupu onye ọ bụla ehiwe.
examples.english: Creep out of the house before anyone wakes.

examples.igbo: Anyị ji akwụkwọ ōbodòlòbo ekpuchi nri.
examples.english: We used broad leaves to cover the food.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ere akwụkwọ ōbodòlòbo n’ahịa?
examples.english: Is she selling broad leaves in the market?

examples.igbo: Ndị njem ahụ mara ụlọikwuu n'akụkụ osimiri.
examples.english: The travelers camped by the river.

examples.igbo: Mara ụlọikwuu n'okpuru osisi a.
examples.english: Camp under this tree.

gloss: break up land by digging; divide land for planting; dig ground

examples.igbo: O wara ànì n'ubi ya taa.
examples.english: He broke up land in his farm today.

examples.igbo: Waa ànì a tupu ị kụọ ọka.
examples.english: Break up this land before you plant maize.

gloss: plaster a house; rub, smooth, wet walls of a mud house

examples.igbo: O tere ụnò ya ụrọ ọhụrụ.
examples.english: He plastered his house with new clay.

examples.igbo: Tee ụnò ahụ tupu ọ kpọọ nkụ.
examples.english: Plaster that house before it dries.

examples.igbo: Okpòlò ọka ahụ toro ogologo.
examples.english: That maize stalk grew tall.

examples.igbo: Gbutu okpòlò ahụ tupu ọ daa n'ala.
examples.english: Cut that stalk before it falls to the ground.

examples.igbo: Nne ya nwere ùgwù n'obodo a.
examples.english: His mother has respect in this town.

examples.igbo: Ị na-enye ndị okenye ùgwù?
examples.english: Do you give elders respect?

examples.igbo: E nwere ònunu n'ọdụ ụgbọ ahụ.
examples.english: There is pushing at that bus stop.

examples.igbo: Ònunu ahụ na-ewe gị iwe?
examples.english: Does that pushing annoy you?

examples.igbo: O bụrụ àbù n'ubi ya n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: He rooted up cassava in his farm in the morning.

examples.igbo: Ị bụrụ àbù n'ubi gị?
examples.english: Did you root up cassava in your farm?

examples.igbo: Nye ụmụaka nri n'òfu n'òfu.
examples.english: Give the children food one by one.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akpọ ha n'òfu n'òfu?
examples.english: Are you calling them one by one?

examples.igbo: Afụfụ mmụọ na-eche ndị na-eme ajọ ihe.
examples.english: Punishment in the underworld awaits those who do evil.

examples.igbo: Ị na-atụ egwu afụfụ mmụọ?
examples.english: Do you fear punishment in the underworld?

examples.igbo: O lịtara n'ùkwù nna ya ụlọ ahụ.
examples.english: He inherited that house from his father.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-alita n'ùkwù nne gị ala ahụ?
examples.english: Will you inherit that land from your mother?

examples.igbo: Nwa nwoke ahụ nwere nkà n'ịkpụ ihe.
examples.english: That boy has skill in carving.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-akụziri m nkà ịkpa akwà?
examples.english: Will you teach me the skill of weaving cloth?

examples.igbo: Nnụnụ ahụ bègō n'elu osisi.
examples.english: The bird perched on top of the tree.

examples.igbo: Ebee ka ọkụkọ bègō n'abalị?
examples.english: Where did the chicken perch at night?

note: Used as a verb meaning 'perch'.

examples.igbo: O yiri àfè mmīli n'ihi mmiri ozuzo.
examples.english: He wore a raincoat because of the rain.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere àfè mmīli m ga-eji?
examples.english: Do you have a raincoat I can use?

gloss: grub usually found in a decaying compost heap

examples.igbo: Àkpa āgbụgbō na-ebi n'ime ebe ahịhịa rere.
examples.english: Grubs live in a decaying compost heap.

examples.igbo: Chịkọta àkpa āgbụgbō ndị a tupu ọkụkọ rie ha.
examples.english: Gather these grubs before the chickens eat them.

note: Used for the grub found in decaying vegetation.

examples.igbo: Ndị obodo jìkọtara ọnụ iwu ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: The villagers joined together to build a school.

examples.igbo: Jìkọta ọnụ ka anyị wee nụ ihe niile.
examples.english: Join together so we can hear everything.

examples.igbo: O ji aka gàdo eriri ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: He held the rope firmly with his hand.

examples.igbo: Gàdo osisi ahụ aka abụọ ka ị ghara ịda.
examples.english: Hold that tree firmly with both hands so you don't fall.

note: Used for holding firm with hands or claws.

examples.igbo: O wụchapụtara efere ndị ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: She washed those plates thoroughly.

examples.igbo: Wụchapụta akwa gị tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Wash your clothes thoroughly before you leave.

examples.igbo: Ọ sekpụrụ n'ala kpee ekpere.
examples.english: He knelt on the ground and prayed.

examples.igbo: Sekpù ebe ahụ wee kpee ekpere.
examples.english: Kneel there and pray.

examples.igbo: Nne m na-akpa akwà n'ụlọ.
examples.english: My mother weaves cloth at home.

examples.igbo: Ị maara ịkpa akwà dị ka nne gị?
examples.english: Do you know how to weave cloth like your mother?

examples.igbo: Bịakèta ebe a, ka m hụ gị.
examples.english: Come nearer here, let me see you.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ bịakètara nne ya n'akụkụ.
examples.english: That child came nearer to his mother's side.

examples.igbo: O rọrọ atụmatụ maka ego ahụ.
examples.english: She formulated a plan for that money.

examples.igbo: Rọọ atụmatụ maka njem anyị.
examples.english: Formulate a plan for our journey.

gloss: serve; wait upon; pay tribute; worship

examples.igbo: O na-efe nne ya nrù n'ụlọ ọgwụ.
examples.english: She is serving her mother in the hospital.

examples.igbo: Fee ya nrù nke ọma.
examples.english: Serve him well.

gloss: knead pounded food in plate, mortar, etc.

examples.igbo: O raara nni ahụ n'efere.
examples.english: She kneaded that food in the plate.

examples.igbo: Raa nni ahụ ka anyị rie.
examples.english: Knead that food so we may eat.

examples.igbo: Anyị bidoro ịkọ ugbo n'ùhuruchī.
examples.english: We started farming at dawn.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ebili n'ùhuruchī?
examples.english: Do you wake up at dawn?

examples.igbo: O nekwàsịrị anya n'ụmụaka ahụ.
examples.english: She looked upon those children.

examples.igbo: Nekwàsị anya n'ihe m dere.
examples.english: Look again at what I wrote.

examples.igbo: Ha na-ero uro n'etiti onwe ha.
examples.english: They are at enmity among themselves.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ero uro megide m?
examples.english: Are you at enmity against me?

examples.igbo: Anyị zụtara ìgbènù n'ahịa.
examples.english: We bought ìgbènù at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ìgbènù n'ahịa?
examples.english: Did you see ìgbènù at the market?

gloss: be rooted in; be connected with a place by birth

examples.igbo: O gbanyere mkpòlògwù n'obodo nna ya.
examples.english: He is rooted in his father's town.

examples.igbo: Ị gbanyere mkpòlògwù n'obodo gị?
examples.english: Are you rooted in your town?

gloss: any type of masquerade with horned head (For other types of masquerade, see àkàtaàkà, àtùmà, ìgbàdikē, ùlàgà)

examples.igbo: Òdogwu mmūọ pụtara n'ama.
examples.english: The horned masquerade appeared in the village square.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ òdogwu mmūọ n'emume ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see the horned masquerade at that festival?

gloss: live for a long time in one place and become accustomed to it

examples.igbo: Ọ bimalụrụ n'obodo a ruo ọtụtụ afọ.
examples.english: He has lived long in this town for many years.

examples.igbo: Ị bimalụrụ n'ebe a ugbu a?
examples.english: Have you become accustomed to this place now?

note: The verb -bimalụ is not common in everyday speech; the inflected forms used here are plausible but may vary by dialect.

examples.igbo: Anyị nwere ùle n'ụlọ akwụkwọ echi.
examples.english: We have an exam at school tomorrow.

examples.igbo: Ị gafere ùle ahụ nke ọma?
examples.english: Did you pass that exam well?

examples.igbo: M hụrụ ya ìnyègè n'ọchịchịrị abalị.
examples.english: I saw him faintly in the night darkness.

examples.igbo: Ì hụrụ ụlọ ahụ ìnyègè n'okporo ụzọ?
examples.english: Did you see that house faintly from the road?

note: The phrase hụ ìnyègè is somewhat idiomatic; the sentences are sound but one might phrase the second differently.

gloss: prod a part of the body in a way that causes laughter; tickle

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ yị̀rị nne ya ǹtatàrabụ̀.
examples.english: That child tickled his mother.

examples.igbo: Ị yị̀rị ya ǹtatàrabụ̀ n'apata?
examples.english: Did you tickle him on the thigh?

note: The verb yị̀ with ǹtatàrabụ̀ is understood here as tickle; the inflected form yị̀rị is likely correct but not certain.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-egwu n'ànì apìtì n'akụkụ osimiri.
examples.english: Children are playing in the swamp by the river.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ànì apìtì n'azụ ụlọ anyị?
examples.english: Did you see the swamp behind our house?

examples.igbo: Ọ nalụrụ ego ahụ n'aka nwanne ya.
examples.english: He received that money from his brother.

examples.igbo: Nalụ ego gị tupu ị pụọ n'ụlọ.
examples.english: Take your money before you leave the house.

note: The verb stem -nalụ is less common than nata/nara in some areas; the sentences follow the given stem.

gloss: white ant (the type that lives in the ground) (literally palmnut of the ground)

examples.igbo: Akwụ ànì na-ata osisi anyị n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: White ants are eating our wood in the house.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ akwụ ànì n'ala ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see white ants in that land?

examples.igbo: Igwu isī dị n'isi nwa ahụ.
examples.english: Head lice are on that child's head.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ igwu isī n'isi ya?
examples.english: Did you see head lice on his head?

note: Igwu isī is the usual term for head louse/lice; the plural use is acceptable in context.

examples.igbo: O na-akpa ụkpa na ụmụ klas ya.
examples.english: He socializes with his classmates.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akpa ụkpa na ndị agbata obi gị?
examples.english: Do you socialize with your neighbors?

examples.igbo: Jesiri ijè ike ka anyị ruo ahịa n'oge.
examples.english: Go fast so that we reach the market in time.

examples.igbo: Ọ jesiri ijè ike wee gafee anyị niile.
examples.english: He went fast and passed all of us.

note: The stem -jesi is inflected here as jesiri; the sense 'go fast' is kept throughout.

gloss: across the stream, river, etc.; the other side of the river, stream, etc.

examples.igbo: Ụlọ ha dị ùfèsi mmīli.
examples.english: Their house is on the other side of the stream.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-aga ùfèsi mmīli taata?
examples.english: Will you go across the stream today?

note: Kept the locative sense 'the other side of the river/stream'.

examples.igbo: Nkịta gàrị m̀bọ n'ọnụ ụzọ.
examples.english: The dog scratched at the door.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji agà m̀bọ n'azụ m?
examples.english: Why are you scratching my back?

note: Inflected as gàrị m̀bọ (past) and agà m̀bọ (progressive).

examples.igbo: Ọ kọọrọ ụmụaka akụkọ banyere anụ ọhịa.
examples.english: She told the children a story about wild animals.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ ịnụ akụkọ ọzọ?
examples.english: Do you want to hear another story?

examples.igbo: Anyị kụrụ ọkà n'ubi a.
examples.english: We planted maize in this farm.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara ọkà ole n'ahịa taa?
examples.english: How much maize did you buy at the market today?

examples.igbo: Nwabụēzè bụ aha e ji akpọ nwa eze.
examples.english: Nwabueze is the name used to call a king's child.

examples.igbo: Kedu ihe mere ha ji akpọ nwa ya Nwabụēzè?
examples.english: Why do they call their child Nwabueze?

note: The headword looks like a personal name with unusual tone marks; I treated it as a name meaning 'a child who is king'.

gloss: draw or pull near or nearer, close or closer; shift close or near;

examples.igbo: Kpụdèbè ǹso ka m gwa gị ihe.
examples.english: Move close so that I tell you something.

examples.igbo: Ọ kpụdèbèrè ǹso n'ọnụ ọkụ.
examples.english: He moved close to the fire.

note: The verb is inflected as kpụdèbèrè in the past-tense sentence.

gloss: greeting to a person travelling (literally return early!)

examples.igbo: Nògboo, ka ị mee njem gị nke ọma.
examples.english: Nògboo — may your journey go well.

examples.igbo: Ha sịrị ya nògboo mgbe ọ na-apụ n'ụlọ.
examples.english: They said nògboo to him as he was leaving the house.

note: Kept it as the farewell said to a traveller, meaning roughly 'return early'.

gloss: cutting, clearing of bush preparatory to farming

examples.igbo: Ha malitere òsụsụ ànì n'ubi ọhụrụ ahụ.
examples.english: They started clearing the bush on that new farm.

examples.igbo: Olee mgbe anyị ga-eme òsụsụ ànì?
examples.english: When will we do the bush clearing?

examples.igbo: O fotara afà m n'ụlọ ahịa.
examples.english: He mentioned my name at the market.

examples.igbo: Biko fota afà ya n'akwụkwọ a.
examples.english: Please mention her name in this book.

gloss: part (antagonists); arbitrate and make peace; settle the dispute;

examples.igbo: Ndị okenye gboro ọgụ ụmụaka ahụ.
examples.english: The elders settled those children's fight.

examples.igbo: Gboo ọgụ ha tupu ọ gaa n'ihu.
examples.english: Settle their fight before it goes further.

examples.igbo: Okwu alū ka o kwuru n'ụlọ ekpere.
examples.english: It was an abominable word he spoke in the church.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ekwu okwu alū n'ihu ụmụaka?
examples.english: Are you saying abominable words in front of children?

examples.igbo: Oke ufèlè kwaturu osisi n'ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: A great wind uprooted a tree in our compound.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ oke ufèlè n'ụtụtụ ụnyaahụ?
examples.english: Did you see the great wind yesterday morning?

examples.igbo: Ha hụrụ ònwe fā n'ime enyo.
examples.english: They saw themselves in the mirror.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ ònwe fā kwuru okwu ahụ?
examples.english: Was it themselves who said that word?

examples.igbo: Akpa a bụ ife nkịtị n'ahịa.
examples.english: This bag is a worthless thing in the market.

examples.igbo: Ị na-azụ ife nkịtị n'ahịa?
examples.english: Are you buying worthless things in the market?

examples.igbo: O nyere nwa ahụ otu ǹju ōnụ osikapa.
examples.english: She gave the child one mouthful of rice.

examples.igbo: Were ǹju ōnụ tupu ị gaa ọrụ.
examples.english: Take a mouthful before you go to work.

examples.igbo: Mwuta juru obi ya mgbe nwa ya furu.
examples.english: Grief filled her heart when her child got lost.

examples.igbo: Gịnị na-akpata mwuta a n'obi gị?
examples.english: What is causing this grief in your heart?

examples.igbo: O gọrọ agọ na ya zuru ego ahụ.
examples.english: He denied that he stole that money.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji gọọ agọ?
examples.english: Why did you deny?

examples.igbo: O gwaziri ntụ na mmiri nke ọma.
examples.english: He mixed ash and water properly.

examples.igbo: Gwazie ọgwụ ahụ tupu ị nye ya.
examples.english: Mix that medicine properly before you give it to him.

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ na-akpọ òmìmì akwā n'ihi agụụ.
examples.english: The child is sobbing because of hunger.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akpọ òmìmì akwā?
examples.english: Are you sobbing?

examples.igbo: Ọ dị ùfụ nye m ịnọ ebe a.
examples.english: It is painful for me to stay here.

examples.igbo: Ọ dị ùfụ na ọ dara ule?
examples.english: Is it distressing that he failed the exam?

examples.igbo: Okenye ahụ gbàbara ute n'ala.
examples.english: The elder spread a mat on the ground.

examples.igbo: Gbàbaa akwa ahụ n'ala ka anyị nọdụ.
examples.english: Spread that cloth on the ground so we can sit.

examples.igbo: Mkparịta ụka ahụ gbadùbara ya uche.
examples.english: That discussion dulled his mind.

examples.igbo: Gịnị gbadùbara gị uche taa?
examples.english: What dulled your mind today?

note: The word gbadùba is rare; the examples are plausible but I am not fully certain of its idiomatic use.

examples.igbo: Onye nnụsọ ògù ya bịara n'ụlọ ya.
examples.english: His enemy came to his house.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eme enyi gị ka onye nnụsọ ògù?
examples.english: Are you treating your friend like an enemy?

examples.igbo: Teji na-acha ọcha dị n'ụlọ ahụ.
examples.english: The white paint is in that house.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara teji maka ịcha ụlọ?
examples.english: Did you buy paint for painting the house?

note: Teji can be noun or verb; I have used it as a noun for 'paint', which is common, but the tone and exact usage may vary.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-agbalị ịrụ ọrụ ahụ.
examples.english: He is trying to do that work.

examples.igbo: Gịnị ka ị na-agbalị ime?
examples.english: What are you trying to do?

examples.igbo: O nwere obì ọcha.
examples.english: He has a pure heart.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere obì ọcha?
examples.english: Do you have a pure heart?

examples.igbo: Ụkọlọ na-egbochi ya ịga ọrụ.
examples.english: Laziness prevents him from going to work.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara ụkọlọ a?
examples.english: What caused this laziness?

examples.igbo: O lara oke mmānya n'ụlọ oriri.
examples.english: He drank to excess at the party.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji laa oke mmānya?
examples.english: Why did you get drunk?

note: The verb 'la' in this phrase is not the standard modern form; the usual expression is 'ṅụbiga mmanya ókè'. The examples use the given form, but I am unsure it is idiomatic.

examples.igbo: Ndị agha wabàra n'obodo anyị n'abalị.
examples.english: The soldiers invaded our town at night.

examples.igbo: Wabà n'ime ụlọ, mmiri na-ezo!
examples.english: Rush into the house, it's raining!

examples.igbo: Ihe ọjọọ dapụtara n'ụtụtụ a.
examples.english: Something bad happened this morning.

examples.igbo: Gịnị dapụtara n'oge ọrụ?
examples.english: What happened during work?

examples.igbo: O kuchiri nwunye nwanne ya nwụrụ anwụ.
examples.english: He took the wife of his late brother.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-akuchi nwunye nwanne gị?
examples.english: Will you take your late brother's wife?

examples.igbo: Anyanwụ nwuchitere m anya n'ehihie.
examples.english: The sun dazzled my eyes at noon.

examples.igbo: Ọkụ ahụ nwuchitere anya gị?
examples.english: Did that light dazzle your eyes?

gloss: have sexual intercourse (of woman); be promiscuous, sexually loose (of woman)

examples.igbo: Nwanyị ahụ lara di n'abalị gara aga.
examples.english: That woman had sexual intercourse last night.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ala di n'ebe ọ bụla?
examples.english: Is she promiscuous everywhere?

examples.igbo: O fichasịrị tebụl ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: She wiped the table thoroughly.

examples.igbo: Fichasịa efere ndị ahụ ugbu a.
examples.english: Wipe those plates thoroughly now.

gloss: have or carry (things not naturally in the mouth) in the mouth

examples.igbo: Nkịta kpụrụ ọkpụkpụ n'ọnụ ya.
examples.english: The dog carried a bone in its mouth.

examples.igbo: Gịnị ka ị na-akpụ n'ọnụ?
examples.english: What are you carrying in your mouth?

gloss: advise; counsel; deliberate on and give advice or offer suggestion

examples.igbo: O tụrụ m alò ka m gaa ahịa.
examples.english: He advised me to go to the market.

examples.igbo: Tụọ nwanne gị alò tupu ọ gaa ọrụ.
examples.english: Advise your brother before he goes to work.

examples.igbo: O napụtara akwụkwọ ahụ n'aka m.
examples.english: He snatched the book from my hand.

examples.igbo: Napụta nwa ahụ n'ime mmiri!
examples.english: Snatch that child out of the water!

examples.igbo: O pụrụ òkò ibute igbe ahụ.
examples.english: He was able to carry that box.

examples.igbo: Ị pụrụ òkò ịzụta akwụkwọ ahụ?
examples.english: Are you able to buy that book?

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ na-adọkali akwa m.
examples.english: That child is tearing my cloth in pieces.

examples.igbo: Dọkalia akwụkwọ a ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Tear this paper in pieces quickly.

note: Verb form uncertain; used continuous and imperative.

examples.igbo: Ndị uwe ojii jidere akâ mèlù n'ahịa.
examples.english: The police seized illicit gin at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ere akâ mèlù n'ụlọ gị?
examples.english: Are you selling illicit gin in your house?

examples.igbo: Anyị ruru n'ụlọ n'àbànì.
examples.english: We arrived home at midnight.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-aga ahịa n'àbànì?
examples.english: Does she go to the market at night?

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-eme nṅòmī nke nwanne ya.
examples.english: That child emulates his brother.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eme nṅòmī nke onye?
examples.english: Whom are you emulating?

note: The noun is abstract; examples show it in ordinary school/home context.

examples.igbo: Ọ kpọrọ m na ètitī ūchichì.
examples.english: He called me at midnight.

examples.igbo: Ị na-aga n'ètitī ūchichì?
examples.english: Are you traveling at midnight?

examples.igbo: O ji igwù kechie ụlọ ahụ.
examples.english: He used palm fronds to thatch that house.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ igwù maka ịkpa ụlọ?
examples.english: Do you want palm fronds for thatching?

gloss: fruit of a type of palm, easy to break

examples.igbo: Akwū ōsụkwū na-agbaji ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: The osukwu fruit breaks easily.

examples.igbo: Ị hụla akwū ōsụkwū n'osisi ahụ?
examples.english: Have you seen osukwu fruit on that tree?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-agba ògù nwanne ya n'okwu ahụ.
examples.english: He sided with his brother in that matter.

examples.igbo: Agbala ògù onye ọjọọ!
examples.english: Don't side with a bad person!

examples.igbo: Kpùchie ọnụ gị, anyị na-anụ ihe.
examples.english: Shut your mouth, we are listening.

examples.igbo: Ọ kpùchiri ọnụ ya ozugbo.
examples.english: He shut his mouth immediately.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-aga semēǹsị̀ na Sọnde.
examples.english: We go to the Anglican church on Sunday.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ onye semēǹsị̀?
examples.english: Is he an Anglican?

gloss: break by throwing; throw and break, damage (e.g. egg, eyes)

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ tụkpọrọ àkwá na mgbidi.
examples.english: That child threw an egg against the wall and broke it.

examples.igbo: Ị tụkpọrọ àkwá ahụ n'ala?
examples.english: Did you throw that egg on the ground and break it?

examples.igbo: Degọ̀ aha akwụkwọ ahụ.
examples.english: Italicise the title of that book.

examples.igbo: O degọrọ okwu ahụ n'akwụkwọ.
examples.english: He italicised that word in the book.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka ahụ nọkọrọ n'okpuru osisi.
examples.english: Those children sat together under the tree.

examples.igbo: Nọkọnụ n'ebe a, ụmụaka.
examples.english: Sit together here, children.

gloss: think; think deeply on an abstract problem; ponder; meditate

examples.igbo: Ọ na-eche echìchè banyere ọdịnihu ya.
examples.english: He is pondering about his future.

examples.igbo: Chee echìchè tupu i kwuo okwu.
examples.english: Think deeply before you speak.

gloss: make boundary; move (objects) aside to show demarcation

examples.igbo: O kpara okè n'ala anyị.
examples.english: He made a boundary on our land.

examples.igbo: Kpaa okè n'etiti ubi abụọ a.
examples.english: Make a boundary between these two farms.

examples.igbo: Anyị zụrụ akwụkwọ nnī n'ahịa.
examples.english: We bought vegetables at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eri akwụkwọ nnī n'ụlọ?
examples.english: Do you eat vegetables at home?

examples.igbo: Anyị hụrụ ìpètè arịlị n'osimiri.
examples.english: We saw Citharinus distichoides in the river.

examples.igbo: Ị jidere ìpètè arịlị abụọ n'osimiri?
examples.english: Did you catch two Citharinus distichoides in the river?

examples.igbo: Nwa ọhụrụ ahụ nwere òpùnè isi āzụ.
examples.english: That baby has a posterior fontanelle.

examples.igbo: Lere òpùnè isi āzụ nwa ahụ.
examples.english: Examine the baby's posterior fontanelle.

gloss: construct framework of roof before thatching or fixing the sheets

examples.igbo: Ndị ọrụ na-adụmi ụnò ụlọ ahụ.
examples.english: The workers are constructing the roof framework of that house.

examples.igbo: Dụmi ụnò ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: Construct that roof framework well.

examples.igbo: Anyị zụrụ mkpụlụ jī n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: We bought seed-yams at the market today.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-akụ mkpụlụ jī n'ubi a?
examples.english: Will you plant seed-yams in this farm?

examples.igbo: Ọ nọrọ n'ebe ahụ ọnwa ndozù.
examples.english: He stayed there a full month.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-anọ ebe a ọnwa ndozù?
examples.english: Will you stay here a full month?

note: The compound is uncommon; it is used here as an adverbial of duration.

examples.igbo: Akụkọ ọ na-akọ na-akpa anyị amụ.
examples.english: The stories he tells amuse us.

examples.igbo: Kpa anyị amụ ntakịrị.
examples.english: Amuse us a little.

note: Usually heard as na-akpa amụ; the transitive use with a personal object is slightly rarer.

gloss: shine, glitter, very brightly; be very white

examples.igbo: Uwe ya na-acha ọcha nwụ gbàà.
examples.english: Her dress is dazzlingly white.

examples.igbo: Anyanwụ na-enwu gbàà taa.
examples.english: The sun is shining very brightly today.

note: Both are idiomatic, but the choice between na-enwu and na-acha nwụ gbàà varies by speaker and region.

examples.igbo: Tinyekwu nnu n'ofe a.
examples.english: Add more salt to this soup.

examples.igbo: O tinyekwuru osikapa n'efere m.
examples.english: She added more rice to my plate.

examples.igbo: O zụtara m̀gbiisìọ̄mā n'ahịa.
examples.english: She bought perfume at the market.

examples.igbo: M̀gbiisìọ̄mā a na-esi ísì ọma.
examples.english: This perfume smells nice.

note: The tone marking of the headword is unusual in everyday writing; the word itself is standard.

examples.igbo: O kụjiri ọjị kelee ọbịa.
examples.english: He broke the kola nut into parts to greet the guest.

examples.igbo: Ị kụjiri achịcha ahụ?
examples.english: Did you break that bread into parts?

note: The stem is most often heard with kola or bread; the past form kụjiri is given as typical.

examples.igbo: Ụlọ m dị ọcha karịa nke ya.
examples.english: My room is cleaner than his.

examples.igbo: Bata n'ụlọ m ka anyị kparịta.
examples.english: Come into my room so we can talk.

note: Alone, ụlọ usually means 'house'; the 'room' sense is clear here from the possessive and the prepositional phrase.

examples.igbo: Ọdù ụkwū m na-egbu mgbu.
examples.english: My little toe is hurting.

examples.igbo: Lelee ọdù ụkwū nwa ahụ.
examples.english: Look at that child's little toe.

gloss: pinch (bits of food, meat, etc., usually by children)

examples.igbo: O sara ùsà anụ n'efere.
examples.english: He pinched bits of meat from the plate.

examples.igbo: Kwụsị ịsa ùsà anụ ahụ!
examples.english: Stop pinching bits of that meat!

note: The expression is chiefly used of children stealing pinches of food; both sentences keep that sense.

examples.igbo: Iru mmà a dị nkọ.
examples.english: The edge of this knife is sharp.

examples.igbo: Iru mmà gị ọ dị nkọ?
examples.english: Is the edge of your knife sharp?

gloss: lead or guide on a journey or path

examples.igbo: Nna m duuru anyị ijè gaa Owere.
examples.english: My father led us on a journey to Owerri.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-edu anyị ijè gaa Enugwu?
examples.english: Will you guide us on the journey to Enugu?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-eli ụgwọ ọrụ ya kwa ọnwa.
examples.english: He receives his wages every month.

examples.igbo: Ị liri ụgwọ ọrụ gị n'ọnwa a?
examples.english: Did you receive your wages this month?

note: The verb li with ụgwọ is less common than nara in some areas; the sentences are sound.

gloss: the last time; at the end of the time; at the end of the world

examples.igbo: Oge ikpeazụ anyị hụrụ ya bụ n'afọ gara aga.
examples.english: The last time we saw him was last year.

examples.igbo: Ole mgbe bụ oge ikpeazụ ị bịara ebe a?
examples.english: When was the last time you came here?

gloss: a cloth worn by women during their first pregnancy; maternity dress

examples.igbo: Ọ na-eyi àgbàlè n'ihi afọ ime mbụ ya.
examples.english: She wears a maternity dress because of her first pregnancy.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara nwanne gị àgbàlè ọhụrụ?
examples.english: Did you buy your sister a new maternity dress?

note: Àgbàlè is a regional word; the usage is right but not heard everywhere.

examples.igbo: Okoti akpo na-agba ọsọ n'elu mgbidi.
examples.english: The male lizard is running on the wall.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ okoti akpo n'ogige ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see the male lizard in that garden?

note: Okoti akpo is a local name for the male lizard; spelling varies.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-asọ ọsụsọ n'ihi ọrụ ike.
examples.english: He is sweating because of hard work.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji asọ ọsụsọ?
examples.english: Why are you sweating?

gloss: fit; suit; suppose to, especially as high time

examples.igbo: Oge tosiri ka anyị lawa.
examples.english: It is high time we went home.

examples.igbo: Uwe a tosiri gị nke ọma.
examples.english: This dress fits you well.

note: The word is felt as slightly old-fashioned; a speaker might say dabara for 'fit'.

examples.igbo: Ha lere ọkụkọ ha ọkụshọm n'ahịa.
examples.english: They sold their fowls by auction at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị lere ụgbọ ala gị ọkụshọm?
examples.english: Did you sell your car by auction?

note: The headword's loanword (given as ọkshòm) is garbled; I used ọkụshọm, but the exact form of 'auction' varies and the verb -le here may be dialectal.

gloss: cut face or body mark; tattoo

examples.igbo: Nna ya tụrụ nkì n'ihu ya mgbe ọ dị obere.
examples.english: His father cut face marks on him when he was small.

examples.igbo: E tụrụ ya nkì n'ihu?
examples.english: Was he given face marks?

note: The practice is now rare, so the wording is heard mostly from older speakers.

gloss: a small high-pitched drum used with òkàǹgà

examples.igbo: Òkekele na-ada ụda dị elu n'egwu ọdịnala.
examples.english: The okekele drum makes a high-pitched sound in traditional music.

examples.igbo: Ị na-anụ ụda òkekele na òkàǹgà?
examples.english: Do you hear the sound of the okekele and the okanga?

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ bēkùrù nne ya ka o zụta ya achịcha.
examples.english: That child implored his mother to buy him bread.

examples.igbo: Bēkù ya ka o nyere gị aka.
examples.english: Implore him to help you.

examples.igbo: O fòchara ahịhịa n'ubi ya.
examples.english: He cleared the weeds in his farm.

examples.igbo: Fòcha ebe a tupu ị kụọ osisi.
examples.english: Clear this place before you plant a tree.

examples.igbo: Ndị okenye zùrù ìzù n'abalị ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: The elders held a meeting last night.

examples.igbo: Zùọ ìzù tupu anyị ekpebi ihe.
examples.english: Hold a meeting before we decide.

examples.igbo: O fàpụrụ ibé nkụ ahụ ka ibu ahụ dị mfe.
examples.english: He removed some of the firewood so the load became light.

examples.igbo: Fàpù ihe ndị a n'ụgbọ ka ọ ghara ịdị arọ.
examples.english: Remove these things from the vehicle so it won't be heavy.

examples.igbo: O mụpụtara nwa nwoke n'ụlọ ọgwụ.
examples.english: She gave birth to a boy in the hospital.

examples.igbo: Mụpụta ezigbo ihe n'ọrụ gị.
examples.english: Bring forth good things in your work.

gloss: to wander about from place to place; roam; walk around

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ na-agagharị n'ahịa.
examples.english: That child roams about the market.

examples.igbo: Gagharịa n'obodo a niile, ị ga-ahụ ya.
examples.english: Roam around this whole town, and you will see it.

gloss: Drop a child or thing carefully

examples.igbo: O kùsara nwa ya n'ala nwayọọ.
examples.english: She carefully dropped her child on the ground.

examples.igbo: Kùsa akpa ahụ n'oche ka ọ ghara ịda.
examples.english: Drop that bag carefully on the chair so it doesn't fall.

examples.igbo: Òhoò! Ị bịara ebe a?
examples.english: Oho! You came here?

examples.igbo: Òhoò! Ihe a tụrụ m n'anya.
examples.english: Oho! This surprised me.

examples.igbo: O pụrụ n'orù mgbe agha biri.
examples.english: He got free from slavery when the war ended.

examples.igbo: Ị pụrụ n'orù, ị chọrọ ihu ezinụlọ gị?
examples.english: You got free from slavery, do you want to see your family?

note: Uncertain if 'pụ n'orù' is the usual expression for freedom from slavery; more common might be 'pụ n'ohu'.

examples.igbo: Aja ūke na-acha ọbara ọbara n'ubi anyị.
examples.english: Red soil is red in our farm.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eji aja ūke arụ ụlọ?
examples.english: Are you using red soil to build a house?

note: Uncertain if 'aja ūke' is the common term for red soil; may be dialectal.

examples.igbo: O bị̀ànyè aka ya n'elu akwụkwọ.
examples.english: He imprinted his hand on the paper.

examples.igbo: Bị̀ànyè akara gị ebe a ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Imprint your mark here quickly.

note: Uncertain if 'bị̀ànyè' is the standard verb for 'imprint'; possibly a variant or specialized term.

gloss: pretend to be mad (in order to cheat or trick)

examples.igbo: O pụrụ ala aghùghò ka o zuo ego.
examples.english: He pretended to be mad so he could steal money.

examples.igbo: Ị na-apụ ala aghùghò, gịnị mere?
examples.english: You are pretending to be mad, why?

note: Uncertain if 'pụ ala aghùghò' is the exact idiom; may vary by dialect.

gloss: break something, especially in the form of a shaft or stick, by hitting it;

examples.igbo: O kụjiri osisi ahụ n'ala ike.
examples.english: He broke that stick on the ground with force.

examples.igbo: Kụji mkpanaka ahụ, ọ gaghị eji arụ ọrụ.
examples.english: Break that stick, it will not be used for work.

examples.igbo: Nchègbū na-egbu ya kwa ụbọchị ugbu a.
examples.english: Worry is killing him every day now.

examples.igbo: Gịnị na-akpata nchègbū a n'obi gị?
examples.english: What is causing this worry in your heart?

examples.igbo: O kèmùrù anụ ahụ n'ime efere.
examples.english: He divided the meat into small pieces in a plate.

examples.igbo: Kèmù ya ntakịrị ntakịrị maka ụmụaka.
examples.english: Divide it into small pieces for the children.

examples.igbo: O wakpòrò ya na mmiri ozugbo.
examples.english: He submerged it in water immediately.

examples.igbo: Wakpò ụgbọ mmiri ahụ na mmiri nke ọma.
examples.english: Submerge that boat in water well.

examples.igbo: Ụmụ nnụnụ fekwuru n'osisi ọzọ n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: The birds flew to another tree in the morning.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-efekwu n'ebe ahụ elekere abụọ?
examples.english: Will you fly to that place at two o'clock?

examples.igbo: Anyị zùkọtara n'otu ebe n'ahịa ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: We met together at one place in the market yesterday.

examples.igbo: Zùkọta ụmụ akwụkwọ ahụ n'ihu ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: Assemble those students in front of the school.

gloss: malaria; jaundice without yellow coloration of eyeballs and fingernails

examples.igbo: Ịbà ojiī na-ata nwa m ahụ.
examples.english: My child is suffering from malaria.

examples.igbo: Ị na-aṅụ ọgwụ ịbà ojiī?
examples.english: Are you taking malaria medicine?

note: Tone on ojiī retained from headword.

examples.igbo: Ezi okènyè ahụ na-eje ije nwayọọ.
examples.english: That aged person walks slowly.

examples.igbo: Ị na-enye ezi okènyè nri?
examples.english: Do you give the aged person food?

examples.igbo: Lakpu n'àkwà, echi ị ga-aga ahịa.
examples.english: Go to bed; tomorrow you will go to market.

examples.igbo: Nwa m lakpuru n'àkwà n'elekere asatọ.
examples.english: My child went to bed at eight o'clock.

note: Past form lakpuru used.

examples.igbo: Obi mkpụ dị n'ime ụlọ mkpụ.
examples.english: The queen termite is inside the termite mound.

examples.igbo: Ndị ọrụ mkpụ na-eche obi mkpụ nche.
examples.english: The worker termites guard the queen termite.

examples.igbo: Ofe a gbara ghòlòghòlò, tinye ntụ ọka.
examples.english: This soup is watery; add flour.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-agba ghòlòghòlò ka mmiri.
examples.english: It is watery like water.

gloss: walk in single file; follow immediately behind each other; follow immediately behind or after companions

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka sòchìrì ibe ha n'àzụ n'ụzọ.
examples.english: The children followed one another in single file on the road.

examples.igbo: Sòchie ibe gị n'àzụ mgbe unu na-aga.
examples.english: Follow your companion behind when you go.

examples.igbo: Anyị zụtara ife ibī ụnò ọhụrụ.
examples.english: We bought new furniture.

examples.igbo: Ife ibī ụnò dị n'ime ụlọ ahụ dị oke ọnụ.
examples.english: The furniture in that room is expensive.

gloss: indigo; plant (Randia malleifera Benth. and Hook.f. and/or R. maculata DC) whose juice, obtained on grinding the fruit, turns black on drying. Used traditionally by women for body designs to enhance their beauty. Also marked on the lower eye-lid of patient attacked by measles, influenza, smallpox, as prevention and/or cure

examples.igbo: Ùlì na-acha ojii ma ọ kpọọ nkụ.
examples.english: Indigo turns black when it dries.

examples.igbo: Ụmụagbọghọ na-ete ùlì n'ahụ ha.
examples.english: Young women apply indigo to their bodies.

examples.igbo: Kpụ̀go mmiri ahụ n'olulu mmiri.
examples.english: Draw that water from the well.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akpụ̀go mmiri n'olulu mmiri kwa ụtụtụ.
examples.english: She draws water from the well every morning.

examples.igbo: Ọ kara ihe isi ike ahụ.
examples.english: He endured that hardship.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-aka ahụhụ a ruo ọgwụgwụ?
examples.english: Will you endure this suffering to the end?

note: Endure sense of ka used; tone not marked.

gloss: make trail especially with the feet

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka kpụrụ ụ̀kpụ̀rụ̀ n'ájá.
examples.english: The children made footprints in the sand.

examples.igbo: Kpụrụ ụ̀kpụ̀rụ̀ n'ụzọ ka anyị soro.
examples.english: Make a trail on the path so we can follow.

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ tiri mkpu mgbe ọ hụrụ agwọ.
examples.english: That child shouted when he saw a snake.

examples.igbo: Tie mkpu! Ndị ohi abịala.
examples.english: Shout! Thieves have come.

gloss: an indecisive person trying out several things

examples.igbo: Nwoke a bụ agarachaa, ọ naghị arụ otu ọrụ.
examples.english: This man is a flitter, he does not do one job.

examples.igbo: Ị bụ agarachaa; gịnị mere ị naghị anọ n'otu ebe?
examples.english: You are a flitter; why don't you stay in one place?

examples.igbo: Nne m jiri ọdū kwọọ ji.
examples.english: My mother used a pestle to pound yam.

examples.igbo: Buru ọdū, anyị ga-akwọ ọka.
examples.english: Carry the pestle, we will pound corn.

examples.igbo: Anyị gara ose òkwòọdū ịzụ azụ.
examples.english: We went to the bank of River Niger to buy fish.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-egwu egwu n'ose òkwòọdū.
examples.english: Children are playing at the bank of River Niger.

gloss: remove with difficulty from a crowded place; squeeze out

examples.igbo: O ji ike fapụsị n'ime igwe mmadụ.
examples.english: He struggled to squeeze out from the crowd.

examples.igbo: Fapụsịa akpa gị n'ime igwe mmadụ.
examples.english: Squeeze your bag out from the crowd.

examples.igbo: O na-akpụchigha ehi n'ogige.
examples.english: He is leading cattle back to the pen.

examples.igbo: Kpụchighaa ewu gị n'ubi.
examples.english: Lead your goat back from the farm.

gloss: habitual unwillingness to spend or give; stinginess; miserliness

examples.igbo: Akantachị ya na-egbochi ya inye ndị ogbenye ego.
examples.english: His stinginess prevents him from giving money to the poor.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ akantachị mere o ji jụ inye nwa ya ego?
examples.english: Is it stinginess that made him refuse to give his child money?

gloss: change for worse; be polluted, fouled, defiled

examples.igbo: Mmiri ahụ gbalụrụ àgbalụ, ọ dịghị mma ịṅụ.
examples.english: That water became polluted, it is not good to drink.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka mmiri gbalụ àgbalụ.
examples.english: Don't let water become polluted.

examples.igbo: Anyị zụtara azụ n'otu òkwòọdū.
examples.english: We bought fish at Onitsha waterside.

examples.igbo: Otu òkwòọdū na-ejupụta ndị ahịa n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: Onitsha waterside fills with traders in the morning.

examples.igbo: Ọ maara ehi ubè n'afọ.
examples.english: He pierced the cow in the belly with a spear.

examples.igbo: Ha na-ama azụ ubè n'osimiri.
examples.english: They are spearing fish in the river.

note: The verb -ma with ubè is not common in everyday speech; examples are constructed to show the sense given.

examples.igbo: Nwanne m nwanyị lụrụ di n'ọnwa gara aga.
examples.english: My sister got married last month.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-alụ di mgbe ị gụsịrị akwụkwọ?
examples.english: Will you get married after you finish school?

examples.igbo: Ndị uwe ojii pịasàrị igwe mmadụ ahụ.
examples.english: The police flogged and scattered that crowd.

examples.igbo: Ọkụkọ pịasàrị ọka anyị wụsara n'ala.
examples.english: The chickens scattered the corn we poured on the ground.

note: The exact range of pịasà is uncertain; the second sentence uses it in the simple 'scatter' sense.

examples.igbo: Ùbu osikapa ahụ gwụrụ m ike.
examples.english: The carrying of that rice tired me.

examples.igbo: Ùbu mmiri n'isi abụghị ọrụ dị mfe.
examples.english: Carrying water on the head is not easy work.

examples.igbo: Ndị ọrụ naara ụgwọ ha taa.
examples.english: The workers received their wages today.

examples.igbo: Ị naara ụgwọ ọnwa a?
examples.english: Did you receive this month's salary?

note: The verb form naara is used here for receiving wages, as indicated by the entry.

gloss: middle of path or road; main road; permanent path

examples.igbo: Anyị zutere ya n'ọkpụ ezi ụzọ.
examples.english: We met him in the middle of the main road.

examples.igbo: Ọkpụ ezi ụzọ a na-aga ahịa.
examples.english: This main road leads to the market.

examples.igbo: Ọ tiri ya aka n'òkpùn'okwò.
examples.english: He hit him on the back of the head.

examples.igbo: Òkpùn'okwò ya dị okirikiri.
examples.english: The back of his head is round.

examples.igbo: Nwa ọhụrụ lomìrì ọgwụ ahụ.
examples.english: The baby swallowed the medicine completely.

examples.igbo: Lomì mmiri ahụ niile.
examples.english: Swallow all that water.

examples.igbo: Eze nkwọ na-enye ya nsogbu.
examples.english: Tooth loss is giving him trouble.

examples.igbo: Eze nkwọ mere ka ọ ghara ịta ọka.
examples.english: Tooth loss made him unable to chew corn.

examples.igbo: Nna m jidere ìkpoòkpo àgù abụọ n'ọdọ mmiri.
examples.english: My father caught two tilapia in the lake.

examples.igbo: Ị hụla ìkpoòkpo àgù n'ahịa taa?
examples.english: Have you seen tilapia in the market today?

note: The fish name is uncommon; sentences are idiomatic but the exact species reference may vary by area.

examples.igbo: Anwụlù juru n'ime ụlọ ebe anyị na-esi nri.
examples.english: Smoke filled the room where we cook.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ahụ anwụlù na-esi n'elu ụlọ ahụ?
examples.english: Do you see the smoke rising from that house?

note: Anwụrụ ọkụ is the more usual modern form; anwụlù is understood but sounds regional.

gloss: say the opposite of what one said before

examples.igbo: Ọ kwughalịrị okwu ọ kwuru ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: He said the opposite of what he said yesterday.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji na-akwughalị okwu gị?
examples.english: Why do you keep contradicting what you said?

note: The verb is rare; the inflected forms used here follow regular patterns but a speaker might prefer ikwughachi.

gloss: rub on pomade, grease, ointment, cream

examples.igbo: Nne m na-akpa ùde n'ahụ nwa ọhụrụ.
examples.english: My mother rubs pomade on the baby's body.

examples.igbo: Kpaa ùde n'ahụ gị tupu i pụọ.
examples.english: Rub pomade on your body before you go out.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-agwu egwu n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: The children are playing in the house.

examples.igbo: Bịa gwuo egwu anyị n'èzí.
examples.english: Come and play with us outside.

note: Given only 'play', the sentences show playful activity; the same expression can also mean playing music.

examples.igbo: Nna m nwere ume nke ukwuu.
examples.english: My father is very strong.

examples.igbo: Ị nweghị ume ibuli igbe a?
examples.english: Don't you have the strength to lift this box?

examples.igbo: Ntùtù anyā ya dị ogologo ma dịkwa ojii.
examples.english: Her eyelashes are long and black.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ntùtù anyā nwa ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see that child's eyelashes?

examples.igbo: Ha kwụgbụrụ onye ohi ahụ n'osisi.
examples.english: They hanged the thief on a tree.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ha ji kwụgbu ya?
examples.english: Why did they hang him?

note: The verb is uncommon in everyday speech; forms are regular but a speaker might phrase it periphrastically.

gloss: cause someone to spend all he has; squander profit

examples.igbo: Azụmahịa ahụ rịdara ya ihe niile o nwere.
examples.english: That business made him spend everything he had.

examples.igbo: O ji ọkụ ọwā gaa n'ọhịa n'abalị.
examples.english: He took a torch to the farm at night.

examples.igbo: Gbaa ọkụ ọwā ka anyị hụ ụzọ.
examples.english: Light the torch so we can see the road.

examples.igbo: Akwụkwo ahụ tadiri n'ahụ nwata ahụ.
examples.english: That cloth stuck to the child's body.

examples.igbo: Mmanụ ga-atadide n'aka gị.
examples.english: Oil will stick to your hand.

examples.igbo: Nnụnụ na-efe efe n'eluigwe.
examples.english: The bird is flying in the sky.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ nnụnụ ahụ n'elu ụlọ?
examples.english: Did you see that bird on the roof?

examples.igbo: Ndị ọrụ tọsịsịrị ụlọ ahụ.
examples.english: The workers unroofed that house.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-atọsịsị ụlọ ochie ahụ.
examples.english: We are unroofing that old house.

examples.igbo: O rànyere aka ya n'ime mmiri.
examples.english: He lowered his hand into the water.

examples.igbo: Rànye ya n'ime ite ahụ.
examples.english: Lower it into that pot.

examples.igbo: Debe uche gị n'ihe m na-agwa gị.
examples.english: Think about what I am telling you.

examples.igbo: O debeghị uche na nke ahụ.
examples.english: He didn't think about that.

examples.igbo: Eteke uvīe dị n'ime mmiri ahụ.
examples.english: The eteke uvīe fish is in that water.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ eteke uvīe n'ahịa?
examples.english: Did you see eteke uvīe in the market?

note: Specific fish name; usage is plausible but not common in everyday speech.

examples.igbo: Onye na-ebinye ego ahụ bịara n'ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: That money-lender came to our house.

examples.igbo: Ị gbaziri ego n'aka onye na-ebinye ego?
examples.english: Did you borrow money from a money-lender?

examples.igbo: N'oge ọkọchì, mmiri na-adịghị.
examples.english: In the dry season, there is no water.

examples.igbo: Mgbè ọkọchì bịara, osisi akpọnwụọ.
examples.english: When dry season came, the trees dried up.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-ebi n'ùdo n'obodo a.
examples.english: We live in peace in this town.

examples.igbo: Bịa biri n'ùdo na ezinụlọ gị.
examples.english: Come and live in peace with your family.

examples.igbo: Nkịta na-asa mmiri n'ite.
examples.english: The dog is lapping water in the pot.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-asa mmiri ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: It laps water quickly.

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ na-apàkò mpàkō n'ihu ndị ọbịa.
examples.english: That man is arrogant in front of guests.

examples.igbo: Ị na-apàkò mpàkō n'ebe ndị enyi gị nọ?
examples.english: Are you being arrogant among your friends?

gloss: life imprisonment (literally imprisonment of grains of maize; from idea that each year was represented by a single grain of maize)

examples.igbo: Ọ na-anọ n'ụlọ mkpọrọ na ǹga mkpụlụ ọkà.
examples.english: He is in prison serving life imprisonment.

examples.igbo: Ikpe ǹga mkpụlụ ọkà ka ụlọ ikpe nyere ya.
examples.english: The court gave him a life imprisonment sentence.

examples.igbo: O dọsàrà akwa ahụ n'ime abụọ.
examples.english: She tore the cloth into two.

examples.igbo: Dọsàa anụ ahụ tupu ị tinye ya n'ofe.
examples.english: Pull the meat apart before you put it in the soup.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-alụ ajọ ọlụ n'ọrụ ugbo ya.
examples.english: He does his farm work badly.

examples.igbo: Unu alụla ajọ ọlụ n'ebe a.
examples.english: Don't do work badly here.

examples.igbo: Oka n'ubi anyị achaala acha ugbu a.
examples.english: The maize in our farm is ripe now.

examples.igbo: Oge unere n'ubi anyị cha acha erugo.
examples.english: The time for bananas in our farm to ripen has come.

gloss: finish work or a piece of work, finish constructing

examples.igbo: Anyị rụchara ụlọ ahụ tupu udummiri abịa.
examples.english: We finished building that house before the rain came.

examples.igbo: Rụchaa ọrụ gị tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Finish your work before you leave.

gloss: feast for sacrificing to the ancestors

examples.igbo: E mere àlòmmụō n'ụlọ eze n'abalị ahụ.
examples.english: They held an àlòmmụō feast in the king's house that night.

examples.igbo: Ndi obodo na-eme àlòmmụō kwa afọ.
examples.english: The villagers hold an àlòmmụō every year.

examples.igbo: Ọ tabèrè achịcha ahụ otu ibe.
examples.english: He bit off a piece of the bread.

examples.igbo: Tabee anụ ahụ ntakịrị.
examples.english: Bite off a little of the meat.

note: Verb stem used with -rV past and imperative; forms vary by dialect.

examples.igbo: Ọkụkọ ahụ na-eti ǹkù.
examples.english: The chicken is flapping its wings.

examples.igbo: Nnụnụ ahụ tiri ǹkù wee fepụ.
examples.english: The bird flapped its wings and flew away.

examples.igbo: Ọ gụdàrà akwụkwọ ahụ niile n'otu abalị.
examples.english: He read through the whole book in one night.

examples.igbo: Gụdàa akwụkwọ ahụ tupu i gaa ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: Read through the book before you go to school.

examples.igbo: Osisi ahụ dàkpudoro ụlọ anyị n'abalị.
examples.english: That tree fell upon our house at night.

examples.igbo: Lezienụ anya ka mgbidi ghara ịdàkpudo unu.
examples.english: Be careful so the wall does not fall upon you.

gloss: appear rusty; be in a rusty state

examples.igbo: Mma ahụ gbara nchārā n'ihi mmiri.
examples.english: The knife is rusty because of water.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ígwè ahụ ji gbaa nchārā?
examples.english: Why is that metal rusty?

examples.igbo: Ọ wụpụrụ mmiri ruru unyi ahụ n'ala.
examples.english: She poured the dirty water on the ground.

examples.igbo: Wụpụ mmiri ahụ n'ime ọdọ.
examples.english: Pour that water into the ditch.

gloss: make bad or disagreeable friendship (e.g. as when a person is intimate with another person whose morality and ways are bad or questionable); walk with criminals or suspects; keep bad company

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akpa ajọ ụkpa n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: He keeps bad company at school.

examples.igbo: Kpachara anya ka ị ghara ịkpa ajọ ụkpa.
examples.english: Be careful so that you do not keep bad company.

examples.igbo: Nne m sùlùrù ìchàfù n'isi.
examples.english: My mother put on a headtie.

examples.igbo: Sùlụ ìchàfù n'isi gị tupu anyị apụọ.
examples.english: Put your headtie on before we leave.

note: The -rV past form sùlùrù varies; some speakers say sùrù.

examples.igbo: Ndị àgàfù zuru ego anyị niile.
examples.english: Bandits stole all our money.

examples.igbo: E jidere àgàfù ahụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: That bandit was caught at the market.

examples.igbo: Ákwà ahụ mere kpukpulukpu mgbe ọ kpọrọ nkụ.
examples.english: The cloth became stiff when it dried.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ji ahụ ji mee kpukpulukpu?
examples.english: Why has that yam become stiff?

note: The compound is idiomatic but the exact verb form (mere vs mechara) may be phrased differently by some speakers.

examples.igbo: Ikwu nà ànyị bịara ọzụkọ taa.
examples.english: Our people came to the meeting today.

examples.igbo: Ebee ka ikwu nà ànyị nọ ugbu a?
examples.english: Where are our people now?

gloss: money or kind paid as tax, collection, rent, fare

examples.igbo: Anyị na-akwụ ùtụ ụlọ kwa ọnwa.
examples.english: We pay house rent every month.

examples.igbo: Ị kwụrụ ùtụ ụgbọ ala taa?
examples.english: Did you pay the vehicle fare today?

examples.igbo: O tinyere nsulu n'ofe.
examples.english: He dipped the sop into the soup.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-enye m nsulu ka m rie?
examples.english: Will you give me a sop to eat?

examples.igbo: Ọ liri àkù nna ya.
examples.english: He inherited his father's wealth.

examples.igbo: Ị liri àkù nne gị?
examples.english: Did you inherit your mother's wealth?

gloss: shredded cassava; raw or pounded fufu; archaic name loosely used for cassava generally

examples.igbo: Mama na-egwe akpụ ǹkòlò n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: Mother is grating cassava in the morning.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-egwe akpụ ǹkòlò taa?
examples.english: Will you grate cassava today?

gloss: guide or lead out; bring someone or an animal out

examples.igbo: Dupụ̀ta ehi ahụ n'ụlọ ehi.
examples.english: Lead that cow out of the cowshed.

examples.igbo: O dupụtara anyị n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: He led us out onto the road.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akụ ùbọ ọnū na oriri.
examples.english: He plays the mouth-organ at feasts.

examples.igbo: Ị pụrụ ịkụ ùbọ ọnū?
examples.english: Can you play the mouth-organ?

examples.igbo: Ògwụgwụ akụkọ ahụ dị mma.
examples.english: The ending of that story is good.

examples.igbo: Kedu mgbe ògwụgwụ ọrụ a ga-abịa?
examples.english: When will the end of this work come?

examples.igbo: Ọ dụ̀rụ̀ m ọdụ̄ ịzụta akwụkwọ.
examples.english: He advised me to buy books.

examples.igbo: Dụ̀ m ọdụ̄ gbasara ụlọ.
examples.english: Advise me concerning the house.

gloss: hang something on; spread out to dry; confer, bestow

examples.igbo: O kobere akwa ya n'elu eriri.
examples.english: She spread her cloth on the line.

examples.igbo: Kobe uwe ndị ahụ n'ala.
examples.english: Spread those clothes on the ground.

gloss: laughter; mockery (-chì make sound with effort)

examples.igbo: Ọchị ya na-ada n'ụlọ.
examples.english: His laughter echoes in the house.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ ọchị ka ọ na-achị m?
examples.english: Is it mockery he is laughing at me?

examples.igbo: Osisi anyikē ahụ gbajiri.
examples.english: That axe handle broke.

examples.igbo: Were osisi anyikē ọhụrụ dochie nke a.
examples.english: Replace this with a new axe handle.

gloss: break (something into tiny pieces, especially using the finger nails)

examples.igbo: O tụbiri akwụkwọ ahụ n'ime obere iberibe.
examples.english: She broke the paper into tiny pieces.

examples.igbo: Tụbie ahịhịa ndị ahụ tupu ịkụ ha.
examples.english: Break those weeds into tiny pieces before burning them.

gloss: burn; set fire to; burn off with fire

examples.igbo: Ha kpọrọ ọkụ n'ubi ahụ.
examples.english: They set fire to that farm.

examples.igbo: Kpọọ ọkụ n'ahịhịa a.
examples.english: Burn off these weeds.

examples.igbo: O ṅụrụ iyī na ya agaghị ezu ohi.
examples.english: He swore an oath that he would not steal.

examples.igbo: ṅụọ iyī tupu ị banye n'ọrụ.
examples.english: Swear an oath before you start work.

examples.igbo: O gburu ikpèlè ụkwū n'ihu eze.
examples.english: He knelt before the king.

examples.igbo: Gbuo ikpèlè ụkwū n'ala.
examples.english: Kneel on the ground.

examples.igbo: O gbadara n'ugwu ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: He ran down the hill quickly.

examples.igbo: Gbadà n'ebe a.
examples.english: Descend here.

examples.igbo: O gwuru ọbù n'ime ọhịa.
examples.english: He dug a pit-trap in the forest.

examples.igbo: Anụmanụ dara n'ọbù ahụ.
examples.english: An animal fell into that pit-trap.

gloss: a nurse who is practicing without a license; a quack nurse

examples.igbo: Nọọ̄sụ elizā ahụ na-agwọ ndị ọrịa n'ụlọ ya.
examples.english: That quack nurse treats patients in her house.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-ekwe ka nọọ̄sụ elizā gbaa gị ọgwụ?
examples.english: Will you let a quack nurse inject you?

note: The term is colloquial and not common in formal writing.

gloss: cook very soft (especially of carbohydrate food)

examples.igbo: Nne m ghèdèrè ji maka nwa ọhụrụ.
examples.english: My mother cooked yam very soft for the baby.

examples.igbo: Ị ghèdèrè ji a nke ọma?
examples.english: Did you cook this yam very soft?

gloss: pack up; pack together Ànyị nà-àkwakọ ife ānyị ọnụ We are bringing our belongings together

examples.igbo: Ànyị nà-àkwakọ ife ānyị ọnụ.
examples.english: We are packing our belongings together.

examples.igbo: Kwakọọ akwụkwọ gị ọnụ tupu anyị apụ.
examples.english: Pack your books together before we leave.

examples.igbo: Gịlịgịlị nwa ahụ na-eme ka ọ dị ka ọ na-arịa ọrịa.
examples.english: The child's thinness makes him look sick.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara gịlịgịlị a n'ahụ gị?
examples.english: What caused this thinness on your body?

examples.igbo: O kwedoro aka n'aka nwatakịrị ahụ.
examples.english: He laid hold of that child's hand.

examples.igbo: Kwedo aka n'osisi ahụ ka ị ghara ịda.
examples.english: Hold on to that tree so you don't fall.

examples.igbo: M tinyere osè ọcha n'ofe.
examples.english: I put red pepper in the soup.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara osè ọcha n'ahịa?
examples.english: Did you buy red pepper at the market?

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ dara n'ala mgbe ọ na-agba ọsọ.
examples.english: That child fell down while running.

examples.igbo: Lezie anya ka ị ghara ịda n'ala.
examples.english: Be careful so you don't fall down.

gloss: flip/open the leaves of a book (looking for a particular page or chapter)

examples.igbo: O sàrà akwụkwọ ahụ chọọ ibe ahụ.
examples.english: He flipped through the book looking for that page.

examples.igbo: Saa akwụkwọ ahụ ka anyị hụ ihe dị na ya.
examples.english: Flip the book so we can see what is in it.

gloss: swell; rise; puff out; increase in bulk (as dough)

examples.igbo: Ntụ ọka ahụ rịlịrị n'ike.
examples.english: The dough rose greatly.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-arịlị ka ntụ ọka na-eto.
examples.english: It is puffing up like rising dough.

gloss: puffer-fish with very poisonous gall (Tetraodon fahaka)

examples.igbo: Ọkpìjò nwere nnukwu ose na-egbu mmadụ.
examples.english: The puffer fish has a very poisonous gall that kills.

examples.igbo: Ndị ọkụ azụ jidere ọkpìjò n'osimiri.
examples.english: Fishermen caught a puffer fish in the river.

examples.igbo: Fùnyụ oriọna ahụ tupu ị lakpuo.
examples.english: Blow out that lamp before you sleep.

examples.igbo: Ọ fùnyụrụ oriọna ahụ mgbe ọ nụrụ mkpọtụ.
examples.english: She blew out the lamp when she heard a noise.

examples.igbo: Èbeē zi ka ị na-aga ugbu a?
examples.english: Where else are you going now?

examples.igbo: Ọ jụrụ ebe a, èbeē zi ka ọ ga-aga?
examples.english: He refused here, where else will he go?

note: Both examples are questions because the headword is an interrogative phrase.

examples.igbo: Ajù na-ebu m mgbe m biliri n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: I feel dizzy when I stand up in the morning.

examples.igbo: Ajù na-ebu gị mgbe ị nọ n'ụgbọ?
examples.english: Do you feel dizzy when you are in a vehicle?

examples.igbo: Dolu ànì akpa ahụ, ọ dị arọ.
examples.english: Put down that bag, it is heavy.

examples.igbo: Ọ dolu ànì ego ahụ ma pụọ.
examples.english: He put down that money and left.

gloss: spill Ọ kwāfùlù mmiliì He spilt the water, or He poured away the water

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ kwafùlù mmiri n'ala ozugbo.
examples.english: That child spilt water on the ground at once.

examples.igbo: Kwafù mmiri ahụ n'ime ọdọ.
examples.english: Pour away that water into the ditch.

examples.igbo: Nna m na-akọ ugbo ji n'azụ ụlọ.
examples.english: My father farms yam behind the house.

examples.igbo: Kọọ ugbo gị tupu mmiri ezoo.
examples.english: Cultivate your farm before the rain falls.

gloss: be thoroughly clean; wash, rinse out; absolve

examples.igbo: Ọ nwuchapụrụ efere ndị ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: She washed those plates thoroughly.

examples.igbo: Sachaa ite ahụ ka ọ nwuchapụ.
examples.english: Wash that pot so it is thoroughly clean.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ kalịrị ndị ọzọ n'ịgụ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: That child surpassed the others in reading.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akalị m n'ịrụ ọrụ ugbu a?
examples.english: Are you surpassing me in work now?

gloss: take out, remove one's tooth; lose one's tooth

examples.igbo: Dọkịta fòrò ezē ahụ na-egbu m mgbu.
examples.english: The doctor removed that tooth that was paining me.

examples.igbo: Foo ezē ahụ tupu ọ kpasuo gị nsogbu.
examples.english: Remove that tooth before it troubles you.

examples.igbo: Pịa utù egbè ka mgbọ pụta.
examples.english: Press the trigger so the bullet comes out.

examples.igbo: Ọ jidere utù egbè mana o gbaghị ya.
examples.english: He held the trigger but did not shoot it.

examples.igbo: Ọ gwuferè osimiri ahụ n'ụtụtụ taa.
examples.english: He swam across that river this morning.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-agwufe osimiri a n'onwe gị?
examples.english: Will you swim across this river by yourself?

note: Tone marking of the inflected form gwuferè is uncertain.

examples.igbo: Nwoke a na-atụ àkpànì n'okwu ọ bụla.
examples.english: This man is pugnacious in every speech.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji atụ àkpànì n'ụlọ a?
examples.english: Why are you so bellicose in this house?

examples.igbo: O ji osisi kpani igbe ahụ dị arọ.
examples.english: He used a stick to lift that heavy box.

examples.igbo: Kpani ya elu ka anyị hụ ihe n'okpuru ya.
examples.english: Lift it up so we can see what is under it.

gloss: someone who gives evidence of harm done by sorcery

examples.igbo: Onye ịtà ahụ kwuru na nwoke a kpara ya n'ọgwụ.
examples.english: That informant said that this man used sorcery on him.

examples.igbo: Ị bụ onye ịtà n'okwu a?
examples.english: Are you the one giving evidence in this matter?

note: Rare term; the exact construction used by speakers of this word is not fully clear to me.

examples.igbo: Afà oyìbo ya bụ John.
examples.english: His English name is John.

examples.igbo: Ị ma afà oyìbo ya?
examples.english: Do you know her English name?

note: Kept the headword spelling afà oyìbo; the more usual modern form is aha ọyịbo.

gloss: grope; grabble; scrabble; touch lightly, at quick intervals, in order to feel something when searching;

examples.igbo: O dịdà aka n'akpa ya chọta ego.
examples.english: He groped in his bag and found money.

examples.igbo: Dịdà aka n'ime igbe ahụ, ị ga-ahụ mkpịsị ugodi.
examples.english: Grope inside that box and you will find the key.

gloss: untie to open (sometimes used for a parcel without knots)

examples.igbo: O tọhere ngwugwu ahụ ozugbo.
examples.english: He untied the parcel at once.

examples.igbo: Tọhee akwụkwọ a ka anyị hụ ihe dị n'ime.
examples.english: Untie this parcel so we can see what is inside.

examples.igbo: Ọ wọrọ nwa ya nri n'abalị ahụ.
examples.english: She denied her child food that night.

examples.igbo: Ekwela iwọ nwa gị nri.
examples.english: Don't deny your child food.

note: The headword is written with nni; the standard spelling used here is nri.

examples.igbo: Ọ zụtara ọgụ ìbùa nwa ọkụkọ n'ahịa.
examples.english: She bought forty chicks at the market.

examples.igbo: Ọgụ ìbùa mmadụ bịara nzụkọ ahụ.
examples.english: Forty people came to that meeting.

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ tụrụ ibù nnọọ.
examples.english: That man is very stout.

examples.igbo: Ọ dị gị ka ọ tụrụ ibù karịa mbụ?
examples.english: Does it seem to you that he is stouter than before?

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ nọ n'ime ụlọ ugbua.
examples.english: That child is inside the house now.

examples.igbo: Ọ dị ihe n'ime akpa gị?
examples.english: Is there something inside your bag?

examples.igbo: Ezè alụsị na-elekọta ụlọ arụsị.
examples.english: The priest takes care of the shrine.

examples.igbo: Ònye bụ ezè alụsị n'obodo a?
examples.english: Who is the priest in this town?

examples.igbo: Tụnye nkụ ndị a n'ọkụ ozugbo.
examples.english: Throw these pieces of firewood into the fire at once.

examples.igbo: O tụnyere ego n'ime akpa m.
examples.english: He threw money into my bag.

examples.igbo: Ọ nọrọ n'ụlọ ọgwụ mgbà arò.
examples.english: He was in the hospital a year ago.

examples.igbo: Mgbà arò ka anyị rụrụ ụlọ a?
examples.english: Was it a year ago that we built this house?

examples.igbo: Onye ọrụ anyị na-akpụ mmà n'ụlọ ọrụ.
examples.english: Our worker makes knives in the workshop.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akpụ mmà ole n'ụbọchị?
examples.english: How many knives do you make a day?

examples.igbo: Onye ọchịchị na-emegbu ndị obodo nke ukwuu.
examples.english: The leader oppresses the townspeople greatly.

examples.igbo: Emegbula nwanne gị n'ihi ego.
examples.english: Don't ill-treat your sibling because of money.

examples.igbo: Quotient nke iri na abụọ na atọ bụ anọ.
examples.english: The quotient of twelve and three is four.

examples.igbo: Gịnị bụ quotient nke iri abụọ na ise?
examples.english: What is the quotient of twenty and five?

note: Quotient is an English loan used in Igbo mathematics; ọnụọgụ nke nkewa is also possible.

gloss: move; root up; cast out; root out

examples.igbo: Onye ọrụ ropụrụ osisi ahụ n'ala.
examples.english: The worker uprooted that tree from the ground.

examples.igbo: Ropụ ahịhịa ndị a tupu ị kụọ ihe.
examples.english: Remove these weeds before you plant.

examples.igbo: Ala ebe a dị chìm nke ukwuu.
examples.english: The ground here is very firm.

examples.igbo: Jide osisi ahụ ka ọ dị chìm.
examples.english: Hold that stick so it is firm.

examples.igbo: Ụmụ Ònìchà Ebo na-akọ ugbo.
examples.english: The people of Onitsha Ebo farm.

examples.igbo: Ị ma ebe Ònìchà Ebo dị?
examples.english: Do you know where Onitsha Ebo is?

gloss: listen carelessly; pretend not to hear; be obstinate (literally close ear)

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-akpà ntì mgbe m na-akpọ ya.
examples.english: That child pretends not to hear when I call him.

examples.igbo: Akwụsịla ịkpà ntì, gee m ntị!
examples.english: Stop pretending not to hear, listen to me!

examples.igbo: Aka m'kà aka yā n'ọrụ ugbo.
examples.english: I am stronger than he in farm work.

examples.igbo: O kwuru na aka m'kà aka yā?
examples.english: Did he say that I am stronger than he?

gloss: compress hard (e.g. the throat); choke; press firmly against

examples.igbo: Nri ahụ rìrì m akpịrị.
examples.english: That food choked my throat.

examples.igbo: Rì ya n'ala ka ọ ghara ịgbapụ.
examples.english: Press him firmly to the ground so he doesn't escape.

gloss: a piece of land where crops are planted; a farmland

examples.igbo: Ubì m dị n'akụkụ osimiri.
examples.english: My farmland is by the river.

examples.igbo: Gaa n'ubì kpọta akwụkwọ ndụ.
examples.english: Go to the farmland and fetch vegetables.

examples.igbo: O lichapụrụ nri ahụ niile.
examples.english: He ate up all that food.

examples.igbo: Lichapụ nri gị!
examples.english: Eat up your food!

examples.igbo: O nyere ya che m̄gbā n'ọhịa.
examples.english: He gave him a wrestling challenge in the field.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-anabata che m̄gbā ya?
examples.english: Will you accept his wrestling challenge?

examples.igbo: Mangòlò a chara acha.
examples.english: This mango is ripe.

examples.igbo: Zụta mangòlò atọ n'ahịa.
examples.english: Buy three mangoes at the market.

gloss: be beaten by rain to the skin (of humans); be beaten soggy by rain (of articles)

examples.igbo: Mmiri madèrè anyị n'ụzọ.
examples.english: Rain beat us to the skin on the way.

examples.igbo: Lezie anya ka mmiri madèrè gị.
examples.english: Be careful lest the rain beats you.

gloss: draw blood with horn or horn-shaped calabash from any part of the body to relieve pain, swelling, congestion; get rid of impure or stagnant blood

examples.igbo: O gburu ya ọchi n'isi.
examples.english: He drew blood from his head with a horn.

examples.igbo: Ị gburu ọchi n'ụkwụ gị?
examples.english: Did you draw blood from your leg with a horn?

examples.igbo: Chịnị ihe ndị a niile elu.
examples.english: Lift up all these things.

examples.igbo: O na-achịni nkata ndị ahụ elu.
examples.english: He is lifting those baskets up.

examples.igbo: O gbapụrụ afọ nwoke ahụ n'ihu ọha.
examples.english: He exposed that man publicly.

examples.igbo: Gbapụ afọ ya ka ndị mmadụ mara ihe o mere.
examples.english: Expose him so people know what he did.

gloss: collect decayed compost for application to the crops

examples.igbo: O kpọrọ àgbụgbọ kpochaa ubi ya.
examples.english: He collected compost and applied it to his farm.

examples.igbo: Kpọọ àgbụgbọ kpocha ubi gị tupu ị kụọ ihe.
examples.english: Collect compost and apply it to your farm before you plant.

examples.igbo: Ofe ahụ na-akò èkò n'ite.
examples.english: The soup is bubbling in the pot.

examples.igbo: Azụ ahụ na-akò èkò n'ala.
examples.english: The fish is writhing on the ground.

examples.igbo: Onye mmānụ ahụ na-ere mmanụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: That oil-seller sells oil in the market.

examples.igbo: Gaa n'aka onye mmānụ zụta mmanụ.
examples.english: Go to the oil-seller and buy oil.

examples.igbo: Uwe ahụ kpọrọ nkụ kọrọkọrọ.
examples.english: The cloth is bone-dry.

examples.igbo: Ala ahụ kpọrọ nkụ kọrọkọrọ n'oge ọkọchị.
examples.english: The land is completely dry in the dry season.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-eji ǹtụtū na-akwa akwa.
examples.english: She uses a needle to sew cloth.

examples.igbo: Nye m ǹtụtū ahụ dị n'elu oche.
examples.english: Give me that needle on the chair.

examples.igbo: Ndị ohi wakwàsịrị ụlọ ya n'abalị.
examples.english: Thieves attacked his house at night.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji awakwàsị nwa ahụ?
examples.english: Why are you attacking that child?

gloss: 'tall ghost', the most elderly and venerated form of the incarnate dead (= egwugwu)

examples.igbo: Mmụọ ogonogo pụtara n'ọhịa n'abalị.
examples.english: The tall ghost appeared in the field at night.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-atụ egwu mmụọ ogonogo.
examples.english: Children are afraid of the tall ghost.

examples.igbo: Onye nligbu ahụ napụrụ nne m ego n'ahịa.
examples.english: That rogue snatched my mother's money at the market.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji akpọ nwanne gị onye nligbu?
examples.english: Why do you call your brother a cheat?

note: Onye nligbu is somewhat uncommon but the sense is clear.

examples.igbo: Mmanụ ahụ na-anya n'aka m nke ukwuu.
examples.english: That oil is very sticky on my hand.

examples.igbo: Ghee aka gị, ọ na-anya ebe ahụ.
examples.english: Wash your hands, it is sticky there.

examples.igbo: M debere ego m n'ụlọ akụ n'ụtụtụ a.
examples.english: I deposited my money in the bank this morning.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-aga ụlọ akụ tupu ahịa mechie?
examples.english: Will you go to the bank before the market closes?

note: Standard modern orthography is ụlọ akụ.

examples.igbo: Ọ kpọrọ ụmụaka naātọ n'ụlọ ya.
examples.english: He invited three children to his house.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara azụ naātọ n'ahịa taa?
examples.english: Did you buy three fish at the market today?

note: Qualifying form; standard Igbo would usually use atọ after the noun.

examples.igbo: M na-ekele gị maka enyemaka gị.
examples.english: I thank you for your help.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ekele ya mgbe ọ nyere gị ego?
examples.english: Do you thank him when he gives you money?

examples.igbo: Ehi ahụ na-ata ụza n'okpuru osisi.
examples.english: That cow is chewing the cud under the tree.

examples.igbo: Ị hụla ehi ka ọ na-ata ụza?
examples.english: Have you seen a cow chewing the cud?

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-aṅụ mmiri ara ehi n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: The children drink cow's milk in the morning.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara mmiri ara ehi n'ahịa taa?
examples.english: Did you buy cow's milk at the market today?

note: Given in standard modern orthography as mmiri ara ehi.

gloss: the ram of the Idemìli god (This ram lives mainly in the Idemìli god’s shrine and its surroundings. But it also roams about the village from compound to compound. The ram must not be beaten or killed by anybody, as it is believed that anyone who does this will automatically be visited and killed by the god.)

examples.igbo: Èbùnu Idemīli na-agagharị n'ime obodo anyị.
examples.english: The Idemili ram roams about our village.

examples.igbo: Emegbula èbùnu Idemīli, ọ bụ nke chi.
examples.english: Don't beat the Idemili ram; it belongs to the god.

examples.igbo: Mgbalị anyị niile lara n'iyì n'ọrụ a.
examples.english: All our effort in this work was useless.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere okwu gị ji ala n'iyì?
examples.english: Why is your speech useless?

note: Inflected as lara/ala; the sense is to be wasted or useless.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka gbalụrụ mmilī anyị n'ọdọ.
examples.english: The children defiled our water in the stream.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka ehi gbalụ mmilī ị na-aṅụ.
examples.english: Don't let the cows defile the water you drink.

note: gbalụ mmilī is idiomatic enough, but the past form gbalụrụ varies by dialect.

examples.igbo: Ọ zụtara òfu jī atọ n'ahịa.
examples.english: He bought three seed yams at the market.

examples.igbo: Òfu jī ole ka ị kụrụ n'ugbo gị?
examples.english: How many seed yams did you plant in your farm?

examples.igbo: Ògbunamkpọ gburu ọkụkọ anyị niile n'izu gara aga.
examples.english: Fowl disease killed all our chickens last week.

examples.igbo: Kpachara anya ka ògbunamkpọ ghara ibute ọkụkọ gị.
examples.english: Be careful so that fowl disease does not infect your chickens.

note: The name of the disease is uncommon; the sentences are ordinary farm talk.

examples.igbo: Osisi mango ahụ kpọrọ ìgùgù n'ọnwa a.
examples.english: That mango tree blossomed this month.

examples.igbo: Ole mgbe osisi pear gị ga-akpọ ìgùgù?
examples.english: When will your pear tree blossom?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-atụtụ aka ntụtụ n'ahịa ọ bụla.
examples.english: He pilfers in every market.

examples.igbo: Kwụsị ịtụtụ aka ntụtụ, ọ bụ ihe ọjọọ.
examples.english: Stop pilfering; it is a bad thing.

note: The verb form atụtụ aka ntụtụ is common, but usage varies.

examples.igbo: Nwaanyị ahụ gara gụta ọkụ n'ụlọ onye agbata obi.
examples.english: That woman went to fetch fire from the neighbour's house.

examples.igbo: Gaa gụta ọkụ ka anyị sie nri abalị.
examples.english: Go and fetch fire so that we can cook supper.

gloss: small bird which nods its head

examples.igbo: Ahụrụ m ǹkenū ka ọ na-eguzo n'elu okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: I saw a ǹkenū standing on the roadside.

examples.igbo: I hụla ǹkenū n'ogige anyị?
examples.english: Have you seen a ǹkenū in our compound?

note: The bird name is rare; the sentences are plain everyday speech.

examples.igbo: Kwakọọ akwụkwọ gị niile n'akpa.
examples.english: Pack all your books into the bag.

examples.igbo: Anyị kwakọrọ ngwongwo anyị banye n'ụgbọala.
examples.english: We packed our things into the car.

examples.igbo: Ha kwụrụ òkwụkwụ ngò tupu agbamakwụkwọ ahụ.
examples.english: They paid the bride-price before that wedding.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ ezinụlọ nwoke na-akwụ òkwụkwụ ngò.
examples.english: It is the man's family that pays the bride-price.

note: The term òkwụkwụ ngò refers to a bride-price payment, but the exact instalment it names varies by area.

gloss: a sleepover at a presumed sexual partner's

examples.igbo: Ọ na-aga m̀bọ̀m̀chi n'ụlọ enyi ya nwoke.
examples.english: She goes for a sleepover at her boyfriend's house.

examples.igbo: M̀bọ̀m̀chi abụghị ihe ọma maka nwa akwụkwọ.
examples.english: A sleepover at a lover's place is not good for a student.

gloss: be fat, plump; have stout build (of human being only)

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ gbara agịdịgị.
examples.english: That child is plump.

examples.igbo: Ị gbara agịdịgị mgbe ị dị afọ iri?
examples.english: Were you plump when you were ten?

examples.igbo: Ọ rulu ànì were akwụkwọ ahụ.
examples.english: He stooped down and took that book.

examples.igbo: Rulu ànì ka ị hụ nwa ahụ.
examples.english: Stoop down so that you can see the child.

examples.igbo: Nke itọ bụ nke m.
examples.english: The third one is mine.

examples.igbo: Olee ǹke ītọ n'usoro ahụ?
examples.english: Where is the third one in that line?

examples.igbo: O mere ya mmā mma.
examples.english: He did it well.

examples.igbo: Mee ọrụ gị mmā mma.
examples.english: Do your work well.

gloss: release; untie; loose; absolve; release from bondage, fetters

examples.igbo: Tọpụ̀ eriri ahụ.
examples.english: Untie that rope.

examples.igbo: Ha tọpụ̀rụ ya n'agbụ.
examples.english: They released him from chains.

examples.igbo: Osisị ogwū ahụ dị n'azụ ụlọ.
examples.english: That thorny tree is behind the house.

examples.igbo: Gbụọ osisị ogwū ahụ.
examples.english: Cut down that thorny tree.

gloss: bad death, i.e. a premature death by accident, suicide, certain diseases or childbirth, which causes one to become ekwensu

examples.igbo: Ọ nwụrụ ọnwụ ọjọō n'ihe mberede.
examples.english: He died a bad death in an accident.

examples.igbo: Ndị mmadụ na-atụ egwu ọnwụ ọjọō.
examples.english: People fear a bad death.

examples.igbo: Ọ bọrọ èzi taa.
examples.english: He weeded the compound today.

examples.igbo: Bọọ èzi tupu anyanwụ awapụta.
