examples.english: Weed the compound before the sun comes out.

examples.igbo: Ònòkò ọkū ahụ ka na-ekpo ọkụ.
examples.english: That half-burnt piece of wood is still hot.

examples.igbo: Were ònòkò ọkū sie ofe.
examples.english: Use the half-burnt piece of wood to cook soup.

gloss: keep oneself awake by using kolanuts, etc.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-egwọ ụrā ya ji ọjị mgbe ọ na-akwọ ụgbọ abalị.
examples.english: He keeps himself awake with kola nut when he drives at night.

examples.igbo: Gwọọ ụrā gị ji ọjị, anyị ga-aga njem abalị taa.
examples.english: Keep yourself awake with kola nut, we are travelling by night today.

examples.igbo: Pastọ bìkwàsịrị aka n'isi nwa ahụ wee kpee ekpere.
examples.english: The pastor laid hands on the child's head and prayed.

examples.igbo: Bìkwàsị aka n'isi ya kpee ekpere maka ọrịa ya.
examples.english: Lay hands on his head and pray for his sickness.

examples.igbo: O ji mma chàa akwụkwọ ahụ ka ọ dị obere.
examples.english: She cut that paper with a knife to make it smaller.

examples.igbo: Chàa akwụkwọ a ntakịrị tupu i tinye ya n'akpa.
examples.english: Cut this paper a little before you put it in the bag.

examples.igbo: Ọ nyere ụsaà na ọ rịara ọrịa, ma ọ bụghị eziokwu.
examples.english: He gave the excuse that he was sick, but it was not true.

examples.igbo: Ị na-enye ụsaà ọzọ maka abịaghị n'oge?
examples.english: Are you giving another excuse for coming late?

examples.igbo: Nni jī na ofe akwụ bụ nri anyị riri taa.
examples.english: Pounded yam and vegetable soup is the food we ate today.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eri nni jī ka ọ bụ fufu?
examples.english: Will you eat pounded yam or fufu?

examples.igbo: Ha kpafèrè osimiri ahụ n'ụgbọ nta.
examples.english: They paddled across that river in a small boat.

examples.igbo: Kpafèe anyị gafee mmiri a ka anyị ruo ahịa.
examples.english: Ferry us across this water so we can reach the market.

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ nwere otu ụkwụ òlọgbà kemgbe a mụrụ ya.
examples.english: That child has had one crooked leg since birth.

examples.igbo: Ụkwụ òlọgbà ya na-eme ka ọ na-eje ije nwayọọ.
examples.english: His K-leg makes him walk slowly.

examples.igbo: Gbàkọọ shuga n'ime tii ahụ tupu ọ jụọ oyi.
examples.english: Add sugar to that tea before it gets cold.

examples.igbo: O gbàkọrọ ego ya na nke nwanne ya zụta bọs.
examples.english: He added his money to his brother's and they bought a bus.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-aghọ aghụghọ ka ọ ghara ịrụ ọrụ n'ubi.
examples.english: He is crafty so that he will not work on the farm.

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ ghọrọ aghụghọ n'ahịa, ọ dịghị onye tụkwasịrị ya obi.
examples.english: That man became cunning in the market; nobody trusted him.

examples.igbo: Ehi ahụ bere ọnwụ tupu ọ daa.
examples.english: That cow cried in death-agony before it fell.

examples.igbo: Ị nụrụ ka atụrụ ahụ na-ebe ọnwụ?
examples.english: Did you hear that sheep crying in death-agony?

note: Sense is clear; the verb be ọnwụ is uncommon in everyday speech, so phrasing may vary by dialect.

examples.igbo: Chube m nnu n'ụlọ nwanne gị nwanyị.
examples.english: Go and fetch me salt from your sister's house.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-achube mmiri maka nne ya.
examples.english: She goes to fetch water for her mother.

examples.igbo: Anyị nọ na-ele òfufe ụgbọelu ahụ.
examples.english: We were watching the flight of that aeroplane.

examples.igbo: Òfufe ijiji adịghị ewe ogologo oge.
examples.english: A fly's flight does not take long.

examples.igbo: Kwàghe ụzọ ahụ ka m banye.
examples.english: Push that door open so I can come in.

examples.igbo: O ji iwe kwàghee ọnụ ụzọ.
examples.english: He angrily pushed the door open.

note: Vowel harmony in the suffix (kwàghere/kwàghee) varies; both are heard.

gloss: "hiss"; sound (of contempt) made by sucking teeth

examples.igbo: O sọrọ ọsò mgbe ọ nụrụ okwu ahụ.
examples.english: She hissed when she heard that remark.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji asọ m ọsò?
examples.english: Why are you hissing at me?

note: The verb is usually ịsọ ọsọ; the noun ọsò alone is the hiss itself.

gloss: beads worn round waist by women for ornament (Hausa jìgìdaa)

examples.igbo: Nwanyị ahụ kechiri jìgìda n'úkwù ya.
examples.english: That woman tied jìgìda beads round her waist.

examples.igbo: Jìgìda a dị oke ọnụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: These jìgìda beads are very expensive in the market.

note: A borrowed noun; usage as a plain noun is safest, though the hyphen in the entry suggests verbal use.

gloss: glare; look at someone in a way showing anger, mostly as a sign of warning

examples.igbo: Ọ hùrụ m anya mgbe m gbara ya ajụjụ.
examples.english: He glared at me when I asked him a question.

examples.igbo: Kwụsị ịhù m anya otú ahụ.
examples.english: Stop glaring at me like that.

note: Often rendered as ile anya hù anya; the verb hù anya is the core sense.

examples.igbo: Ego nwunye nwa agbọghọ ahụ dị oke ọnụ.
examples.english: That girl's bride-price is very high.

examples.igbo: Ha kwụrụ ego nwunye tupu ha alụọ.
examples.english: They paid the bride-price before they married.

gloss: take or bestow a title, especially traditional

examples.igbo: Ha chiri nwoke ahụ echichi n'ọha.
examples.english: They bestowed a title on that man in public.

examples.igbo: Ndị okenye na-achi echichi n'oge emume.
examples.english: Elders bestow titles during festivals.

note: The verb form chi/cha echichi varies; chiri and na-achi are both current.

examples.igbo: Kèwà achịcha a ụzọ abụọ ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Divide this bread into two parts quickly.

examples.igbo: Ònye kèwàrà ego ahụ n'etiti ụmụaka?
examples.english: Who divided that money among the children?

gloss: the fifth letter of the Igbo language alphabet; the second vowel of the Igbo language alphabet

examples.igbo: E bụ ụdaume nke abụọ n'asụsụ Igbo.
examples.english: E is the second vowel in the Igbo language.

examples.igbo: Dee mkpụrụ akwụkwọ 'e' n'akwụkwọ gị.
examples.english: Write the letter 'e' in your book.

note: The word is a letter name; examples necessarily concern the alphabet.

examples.igbo: Ọ zụtara àbùa ọkpa n'ahịa ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: She bought two fowls at the market yesterday.

examples.igbo: Ì nwere naanị àbùa akwụkwọ n'ụlọ?
examples.english: Do you have only two books at home?

examples.igbo: Bịa hụ m èkpe ọbụna ị nwere oge.
examples.english: Come see me whenever you have time.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-abụ abụ èkpe ọbụna obi dị ya mma.
examples.english: He sings whenever he is happy.

examples.igbo: Ọka aka ya nwojipụrụ mgbe ọ dara.
examples.english: His finger went out of joint when he fell.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara na mkpịsị ụkwụ gị nwojipụrụ?
examples.english: Why is your toe out of joint?

examples.igbo: Anyị nọrọ n'ife izè ǹdò ruo mgbe mmiri kwụsịrị.
examples.english: We stayed in the shelter until the rain stopped.

examples.igbo: Chọta ife izè ǹdò tupu mmiri amalite.
examples.english: Find shelter before the rain starts.

gloss: slip off; be out of joint

examples.igbo: Akpụkpọ ụkwụ m gbụchapụrụ n'ụzọ.
examples.english: My shoe slipped off on the road.

examples.igbo: Olee ebe mgbanaka gị gbụchapụrụ n'aka?
examples.english: Where did your ring slip off your finger?

examples.igbo: Ọ sịrị ụkwụ ya n'ájá n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: He marked his footprint in the sand in the morning.

examples.igbo: Sị ụkwụ gị n'ala ka m hụ ya.
examples.english: Mark your footprint on the ground so I can see it.

examples.igbo: Kpụchi ọnụ gị ka anyị nụ ihe ọ na-ekwu.
examples.english: Shut your mouth so we can hear what he is saying.

examples.igbo: Ọ kpụchiri ọnụ ya mgbe onye nkuzi batara.
examples.english: He shut his mouth when the teacher entered.

examples.igbo: Obi nwere aka ntachi, ọ naghị enye mmadụ ihe.
examples.english: Obi is stingy; he doesn't give people things.

examples.igbo: Ị na-enwe aka ntachi, gịnị mere ị jụrụ inye ya ego?
examples.english: You are being stingy; why did you refuse to give him money?

examples.igbo: Ndị okenye na-agbò ògù n'ime obodo.
examples.english: The elders arbitrate disputes in the town.

examples.igbo: Gbòọ ògù n'etiti ụmụaka abụọ a.
examples.english: Settle the dispute between these two children.

examples.igbo: Ewu-elī-òkụkò-atù na-eto n'akụkụ ụzọ ahụ.
examples.english: The ewu-elī-òkụkò-atù plant grows by that road.

examples.igbo: Ị maara na ewu-elī-òkụkò-atù na-egbu anụmanụ?
examples.english: Do you know that ewu-elī-òkụkò-atù kills animals?

examples.igbo: Nna m na-akpụ ụ̀zụ̀ n'ụlọ ọrụ.
examples.english: My father does metalwork in the workshop.

examples.igbo: Kpụọ ụ̀zụ̀ a ka ọ bụrụ mma.
examples.english: Forge this metal into a knife.

examples.igbo: Òtụkpà ụlọ ahụ dapụrụ n'oge mmiri.
examples.english: The grass ridging on that house fell in the rainy season.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-arụ òtụkpà ọhụrụ n'elu ụlọ.
examples.english: We are making a new grass ridging on the roof.

examples.igbo: Òkwa òjà ahụ na-afụ ọjà n'ememme obodo.
examples.english: That piper plays the flute at the town festival.

examples.igbo: Òkwa òjà, kụọ ọjà ka anyị bụọ egwu.
examples.english: Piper, play the flute so we can dance.

examples.igbo: Ọbọgwụ na-egwu mmiri n'ọdọ mmiri.
examples.english: The duck is swimming in the pond.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ọbọgwụ ndị ahụ n'ụlọ ọkụkọ?
examples.english: Did you see those ducks in the poultry house?

examples.igbo: Ha na-ere ahịa n'ebe dị iche iche.
examples.english: They sell goods in different places.

examples.igbo: Gaa ebe dị iche iche chọta ọrụ.
examples.english: Go to various places and find work.

gloss: to rule by force and intimidation

examples.igbo: Onyeisi ahụ na-achịgbu ndị ọrụ ya.
examples.english: That boss rules his workers by force.

examples.igbo: Ha chịgburu obodo ahụ ruo ọtụtụ afọ.
examples.english: They ruled that town by force for many years.

examples.igbo: Mkpọtụ ahụ kụjara nwa m n'abalị.
examples.english: The noise startled my child at night.

examples.igbo: Ị na-achọ ịkụja m n'ụzọ a?
examples.english: Are you trying to startle me this way?

examples.igbo: Okwu ahụ bamiri n'obi m nke ukwuu.
examples.english: That word sank deep into my heart.

examples.igbo: Mma ahụ ọ bamiri n'ime osisi a?
examples.english: Did that knife go deep into this wood?

note: bami is uncommon; examples use the inflected form bamiri.

examples.igbo: Onye dibị gburu nwa ya ichi n'ihu.
examples.english: The dibia cut ichi marks on his child's face.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-agbu nwa gị ichi taa?
examples.english: Will you cut ichi marks on your child today?

gloss: bring out with an instrument; to pick out, expose, bring out by scraping

examples.igbo: O jiri mkpịsị kpachapụta nkume n'ala.
examples.english: He used a stick to scrape out a stone from the ground.

examples.igbo: Jiri ngaji kpachapụta ya n'ite.
examples.english: Use a spoon to bring it out of the pot.

gloss: present kola nut; serve an edible to a visitor

examples.igbo: O cheere anyị ọjị n'ụtụtụ a.
examples.english: He presented kola nut to us this morning.

examples.igbo: Biko chee ọjị nye ọbịa ahụ nọ n'ụlọ.
examples.english: Please present kola nut to that visitor in the house.

examples.igbo: O kworo nwa ya n'azụ ụtụtụ a.
examples.english: She carried her child on her back this morning.

examples.igbo: Kworo nwa gị n'azụ mgbe ọ na-ebe akwa.
examples.english: Carry your child on your back when she cries.

gloss: sacrifice to ground, regarded as deity

examples.igbo: Onye isi ezinụlọ ruru ànì tupu ọ gaa njem.
examples.english: The head of the family sacrificed to the ground before traveling.

examples.igbo: Ị ruru ànì n'ụtụtụ a?
examples.english: Did you sacrifice to the ground this morning?

gloss: patronize; first to patronize; be patronized

examples.igbo: Onye ahịa gbara akaahịā n'ụlọ m.
examples.english: The customer patronized my shop.

examples.igbo: Biko gbaa akaahịā n'ụlọ ahịa m.
examples.english: Please patronize my shop.

note: The idiom gba akaahịā is less common; examples follow the given sense.

examples.igbo: Nna m ji mkpà n'aka aga ije.
examples.english: My father uses a walking stick to walk.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara mkpà n'aka ọhụrụ?
examples.english: Did you buy a new walking stick?

gloss: make sound like vehicle or machine

examples.igbo: Ụgbọ ala ahụ na-asụ àsù n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: That car is making a humming sound on the road.

examples.igbo: Gịnị na-asụ àsù n'èzí n'abalị a?
examples.english: What is making that sound outside tonight?

examples.igbo: Mgbe chi abòọ, anyị ga-aga ubi.
examples.english: When day breaks, we will go to the farm.

examples.igbo: Gịnị ka ị na-eme mgbe chi abòọ?
examples.english: What do you do when day breaks?

examples.igbo: Ògèdè oyìbo abụọ na-eto n'ogige anyị.
examples.english: Two pawpaw trees grow in our garden.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ògèdè oyìbo ahụ na ahịa?
examples.english: Did you see that pawpaw in the market?

gloss: reduce; make lower the sound or volume of an electronic device

examples.igbo: Biko gbadàtà ụda redio ahụ ntakịrị.
examples.english: Please reduce the volume of that radio a little.

examples.igbo: Ị gbadàtàla ụda ekwentị gị taa?
examples.english: Have you lowered your phone volume today?

examples.igbo: Ndị omeiwu na-ewu ìwu ọhụrụ ugbu a.
examples.english: Lawmakers are making a new law now.

examples.igbo: Gọọmenti wuru ìwu maka ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: The government made a law for schools.

gloss: smoke; visible carbon suspended in the air, commonly from burning

examples.igbo: Anwụrụ̀ na-esi na ọkụ ahụ apụta.
examples.english: Smoke is coming out of that fire.

examples.igbo: Ị na-anụ anwụrụ̀ nke ọkụ nkụ?
examples.english: Do you smell the smoke of firewood?

examples.igbo: O gbudoro ogwe ahụ n'ime ala.
examples.english: He fixed that post firmly into the ground.

examples.igbo: Gbudo osisi ahụ n'akụkụ ụzọ maka m.
examples.english: Cut and place that stick by the road for me.

examples.igbo: M na-aga Otu ìkwọ ịzụta akwa.
examples.english: I am going to Onitsha main market to buy cloth.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-aga Otu ìkwọ taa maka akwa?
examples.english: Will you go to Onitsha main market today for cloth?

examples.igbo: Ọ lòpụtara ka anyị zụta ngwa ọhụrụ.
examples.english: He suggested that we buy new tools.

examples.igbo: Biko lòpùta ihe anyị ga-eme echi.
examples.english: Please suggest what we will do tomorrow.

examples.igbo: M na-ayòta ọka tupu m esi ya.
examples.english: I sieve the corn before I cook it.

examples.igbo: Yòta ájá n'ime ntụ ọka ahụ.
examples.english: Sieve out sand from that flour.

examples.igbo: Agụụ na-agụ m, ka m rie nri.
examples.english: I am hungry, let me eat food.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-agụ agụụ maka akwụkwọ ọhụrụ?
examples.english: Is he eager for a new book?

examples.igbo: Ha na-eme òkpụkpa ànì n'etiti ubi abụọ.
examples.english: They are making a boundary between two farms.

examples.igbo: Kedu mgbe anyị ga-eme òkpụkpa ànì?
examples.english: When will we make the boundary?

gloss: cloth, garment, robe set aside and devoted to wearing to divine service; Sunday best

examples.igbo: O yiri efè ụkà ya gaa chọọchị.
examples.english: He wore his Sunday best to church.

examples.igbo: Ị kwadebere efè ụkà gị maka ụka echi?
examples.english: Have you prepared your Sunday best for tomorrow's service?

examples.igbo: Nligbu adịghị mma n'ahịa.
examples.english: Cheating is not good in the market.

examples.igbo: Emela nligbu n'ahịa.
examples.english: Don't do fraud in the market.

examples.igbo: Ife nnwùta ahụ bụ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: That borrowed thing is a book.

examples.igbo: Weghachite ife nnwùta gị taa.
examples.english: Return your borrowed thing today.

note: 'ife' is dialectal for standard 'ihe'; the compound sense is clear but the form is not standard modern Igbo.

gloss: base of a pillar of house; pillar of house

examples.igbo: Ukwù isò ụlọ ahụ siri ike.
examples.english: The base of that house's pillar is strong.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ukwù isò ụlọ ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see the base of that house's pillar?

examples.igbo: Mmiri oyi tụnyere ya ndụ.
examples.english: Cold water revived him.

examples.igbo: Tụnye nwa ahụ ndụ.
examples.english: Revive that child.

examples.igbo: O mekwara ya ọzọ.
examples.english: He did it again.

examples.igbo: Mekwa ya ọzọ.
examples.english: Do it again.

examples.igbo: O na-akpagozi ụmụaka ihe ọmụmụ.
examples.english: He teaches children a lesson.

examples.igbo: Kpagozi m otu e si esi nri.
examples.english: Teach me how to cook.

gloss: tap or stream where there is a rush of people wishing to fetch water

examples.igbo: Ụmụ nwanyị na-agba ọsọ gaa mmili nā-ekwō èkwò.
examples.english: Women rush to the busy water point.

examples.igbo: Kedu ebe mmili nā-ekwō èkwò dị?
examples.english: Where is the busy water point?

note: Rare/dialectal phrase; 'mmili' is dialectal for standard 'mmiri', and the exact sense is uncertain.

examples.igbo: O zachapụrụ ájá n'ụlọ.
examples.english: She swept out sand from the house.

examples.igbo: Zachapụ ihe n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: Sweep out things from the room.

examples.igbo: Nne m gbachiri ụzọ ụlọ tupu anyị lakpuo.
examples.english: My mother locked the door of the house before we slept.

examples.igbo: Gbachie ọnụ ụzọ ahụ ngwa ngwa, mmiri na-ezo!
examples.english: Lock that door quickly, it is raining!

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ere ahịa ya n'akụkụ okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: She sells her goods by the roadside.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-ere ahịa gị taa?
examples.english: Will you sell your goods today?

examples.igbo: Anyị nọ na-akpa nkàta mgbe ọ bịara.
examples.english: We were chatting when he arrived.

examples.igbo: Gịnị ka unu na-akpa nkàta?
examples.english: What are you chatting about?

examples.igbo: Egwuregwu a na-ara m àrà.
examples.english: This game bores me.

examples.igbo: Akụkọ ya rara anyị àrà nke ukwuu.
examples.english: His story bored us a lot.

note: The verb stem and its tones are known, but 'ra àrà' is often heard as 'gwụ àrà'; the inflection used here is my best reading.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ tipịara efere ahụ n'ala.
examples.english: That child smashed the plate on the ground.

examples.igbo: Kpachara anya, ị ga-atipịa ite ahụ.
examples.english: Be careful, you will smash that pot.

examples.igbo: Chibụīkē bụ nwanne m nwoke.
examples.english: Chibuike is my brother.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ Chibụīkē n'ahịa taa?
examples.english: Did you see Chibuike at the market today?

examples.igbo: O siiri ọnyà n'ụzọ òké.
examples.english: He set a trap on the rat's path.

examples.igbo: Ndị dinta na-esi ọnyà n'ọhịa.
examples.english: Hunters set traps in the bush.

examples.igbo: O gbara ọkìkà n'aka ya.
examples.english: He had a tattoo drawn on his hand.

examples.igbo: Ọkìkà ahụ dị ya mma nke ukwuu.
examples.english: That tattoo suits him very well.

examples.igbo: Nne ya na-ele òpùnè isī nwa ahụ anya.
examples.english: Her mother watches the baby's fontanelle.

examples.igbo: Emetụla òpùnè isī nwa ọhụrụ aka.
examples.english: Do not touch the newborn's fontanelle.

examples.igbo: Deème, nne m, maka nri a.
examples.english: Thank you, my mother, for this food.

examples.igbo: Deème, were ego a zụta mkpụrụ.
examples.english: Thank you, take this money and buy seeds.

note: Deème is an interjection of thanks; second sentence adds a command.

examples.igbo: Enyi mbà bụ aha e ji akpọ Ndị Igbo.
examples.english: Elephant people is a name used to call the Igbo.

examples.igbo: Ndị enyi mbà bi n’ala Igbo.
examples.english: The Elephant people live in Igboland.

note: Ethnographic term; examples are explanatory rather than everyday conversation.

gloss: fall upon (of thing) Ọ dākwàsì nénu ọche  It fell on the chair Ọ nọ kwàsì nénu ikpo akwụ  She sits on the heap of palmnuts O biìkwàsì yà aka He lays his hands on him

examples.igbo: Nkume dākwàsịrị n’ụkwụ nwa m.
examples.english: A stone fell on my child's leg.

examples.igbo: Gịnị dākwàsịrị n’elu tebụl?
examples.english: What fell on the table?

note: Verb stem -dakwàsị; past forms used.

examples.igbo: Ọ kwàtùrù oche ahụ n’ala.
examples.english: He knocked that chair down.

examples.igbo: Kwàtuo osisi ahụ ka ọ daa.
examples.english: Push that tree down so it falls.

note: Verb stem -kwàtù; imperative used in second sentence.

examples.igbo: Mbikọ anyị n’otu ụlọ dị mma.
examples.english: Our living together in one house is good.

examples.igbo: Ị na-enwe mmasị na mbikọ anyị?
examples.english: Do you enjoy our living together?

examples.igbo: Ụlọ nụfù bụ nke m.
examples.english: That house yonder is mine.

examples.igbo: Lee nwa nụfù n’okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: Look at that child yonder on the road.

examples.igbo: Anyị riri nni ūchichì taa.
examples.english: We ate late supper today.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eri nni ūchichì taa?
examples.english: Will you eat late supper today?

gloss: cover, especially as a form of protection; conceal

examples.igbo: Nne kpùchiri nwa ya na akwa.
examples.english: Mother covered her child with cloth.

examples.igbo: Kpùchie ite nri ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: Cover that pot of food well.

note: Verb kpùchi; second sentence is imperative.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-ejọ egwu nkịta.
examples.english: That child fears dogs.

examples.igbo: Anyị anaghị ejọ egwu mmiri ozuzo.
examples.english: We do not fear rain.

note: Uses the collocation jọ egwu 'fear'.

gloss: cut off with knife or matchet; cut across

examples.igbo: O jiri mma gbuji ji ahụ.
examples.english: He used a knife to cut off that yam.

examples.igbo: Gbuji ahịhịa n’akụkụ ụzọ.
examples.english: Cut off the grass by the roadside.

note: Verb gbuji; imperative used in second sentence.

examples.igbo: Nri ahụ dịlịlị n'efere.
examples.english: That food remains in the plate.

examples.igbo: Ọ dịlịlị n'ụlọ ruo mgbe anyị lọtara.
examples.english: He remained in the house until we returned.

examples.igbo: Lalụ mmiri tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Drink some water before you go.

examples.igbo: Ọ lalụrụ mmanya ntakịrị.
examples.english: He drank a little wine.

examples.igbo: Àkpịlī m na-egbu mgbu.
examples.english: My throat hurts.

examples.igbo: Kwe ka m hụ àkpịlī gị.
examples.english: Let me see your throat.

gloss: go out; go for a stroll;

examples.igbo: Anyị pụrụ īrō n'uhuruchi.
examples.english: We went for a stroll in the evening.

examples.igbo: Pụọ īrō tupu ọ daa.
examples.english: Go for a stroll before it gets dark.

examples.igbo: O kwùchikpọrọ nwa ahụ akwa.
examples.english: She covered the baby with cloth.

examples.igbo: Kwùchikpọọ nwa ahụ akwa ka oyi ghara ịtụ ya.
examples.english: Cover the baby with cloth so cold will not catch him.

examples.igbo: Anyị ṅụrụ mmanya ògòlò n'ụlọ ọbịa.
examples.english: We drank raffia palm wine at the guest house.

examples.igbo: Mmanya ògòlò dị ụtọ karịa mmanya ọzọ.
examples.english: Raffia palm wine is sweeter than other wine.

examples.igbo: Dọọ mmiri ahụ n'olulu.
examples.english: Draw that water from the well.

examples.igbo: O dọrọ ụkwụ nne ya.
examples.english: He pulled his mother's leg.

gloss: word used by children when trying to count stars at night; each number is preceded by this word, and they try to count as far as possible on one breath

examples.igbo: Kìlịkìlịkìlị otu, kìlịkìlịkìlị abụọ, kìlịkìlịkìlị atọ.
examples.english: Kilikilikili one, kilikilikili two, kilikilikili three.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-agụ kìlịkìlịkìlị ka anyị na-agụ kpakpando.
examples.english: We count kilikilikili as we count stars.

examples.igbo: Elu igwe gbàchiri taa.
examples.english: The sky is cloudy today.

examples.igbo: Lee, elu igwe gbàchiri, ọ ga-ezo.
examples.english: Look, the sky is cloudy, it will rain.

examples.igbo: Nne ya kpọnabara ụmụ ya n'ụlọ mgbe abalị dara.
examples.english: Her mother called her children home when night fell.

examples.igbo: Kpọnaba nwa gị n'ụlọ tupu ọchịchịrị.
examples.english: Call your child home before it gets dark.

note: Verb stem; inflected forms (kpọnabara, kpọnaba) are my best reading of the entry.

examples.igbo: Ọ kudàrà ume mgbe ọ nụrụ akụkọ ọma ahụ.
examples.english: He breathed easy when he heard that good news.

examples.igbo: Kudà ume, anyị erugo ụlọ.
examples.english: Breathe easy, we have reached home.

note: Treated as a verb meaning to exhale/breathe easy; tonal inflection uncertain.

examples.igbo: E nwere òkìkà n'ụlọ ha ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: There was a ceremony at their house yesterday.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-aga òkìkà ahụ echi?
examples.english: Will you go to that ceremony tomorrow?

examples.igbo: Obi dị m ụtọ ịhụ gị ọzọ.
examples.english: I am happy to see you again.

examples.igbo: Obi ọ dị gị ụtọ na anyị ga-aga ahịa?
examples.english: Are you happy that we are going to the market?

gloss: squeeze self into (somewhere) through small opening or doorway

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka pionyere n'ime ụgbọ ala ahụ.
examples.english: The children squeezed themselves into that car.

examples.igbo: Pionye n'ime obere ọnụ ụzọ ahụ.
examples.english: Squeeze yourself through that small doorway.

note: Verb stem; past form pionyere and imperative pionye are my reconstruction.

examples.igbo: Mmiri na-asọ n'ọnụ ìlòlò ahụ.
examples.english: Water is flowing in that gutter.

examples.igbo: Mechie ọnụ ìlòlò ahụ ka ahịhịa ghara ịba n'ime.
examples.english: Cover that drain so weeds don't get inside.

note: Spelling kept as given; written elsewhere as ọnụ ilolo.

examples.igbo: Budata akpa ahụ n'elu osisi.
examples.english: Bring down that bag from the tree.

examples.igbo: Onyeisi budara ya ala n'ihu ọha.
examples.english: The boss humbled him in public.

note: Verb stem; covers both the physical 'bring down' and the 'humble' sense.

examples.igbo: Ahịhịa bùka n'ubi anyị n'afọ a.
examples.english: Weeds are plenty in our farm this year.

examples.igbo: Ọ bùka ndị bịara oriri ahụ?
examples.english: Were the people who came to that feast many?

note: 'bùka' as a quantifier of abundance; usage varies by dialect.

examples.igbo: Ntelà okporo ụzọ ahụ were ọtụtụ ụbọchị.
examples.english: The levelling of that road took many days.

examples.igbo: Ha na-arụ ntelà ala ebe a.
examples.english: They are doing land levelling here.

note: Sense 'levelling' is clear but the word is not common in everyday speech; examples are plausible rather than attested.

examples.igbo: Afọ tepụbèrè ya mgbe ọ riri oke nri.
examples.english: His abdomen bulged after he ate too much.

examples.igbo: Afọ na-ete nwa ahụ pụbè, ọ dịkwa ka ọ na-arịa ọrịa.
examples.english: The child's abdomen keeps bulging and he seems to be sick.

note: Verb stem; inflected forms tepụbèrè / na-ete ... pụbè are reconstructed.

examples.igbo: Bìni n’ala, anyị agaa ugbo.
examples.english: Get up from the ground, let's go to the farm.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-abìni n’ụra mgbe ole?
examples.english: When will you get up from sleep?

note: Standard Igbo often uses 'bilie' for 'get up'; 'bìni' is used here as given.

examples.igbo: Ọ sibịara n’ahịa.
examples.english: He came from the market.

examples.igbo: Olee ebe i sibịara?
examples.english: Where did you come from?

gloss: get married to a woman; marry (man to a woman)

examples.igbo: Ọ lụrụ nwunye ya n’afọ gara aga.
examples.english: He married his wife last year.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-alụ nwunye mgbe ole?
examples.english: When will you marry a wife?

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ nụpụrụ isi nye nne ya.
examples.english: That child disobeyed his mother.

examples.igbo: Ị na-anụpụ isi nye ndị mụrụ gị.
examples.english: You are disobeying your parents.

gloss: be fair in complexion; light skinned

examples.igbo: Nwa agbọghọ ahụ na-acha ọchā.
examples.english: That girl is light-skinned.

examples.igbo: Nwa gị na-acha ọchā?
examples.english: Is your child light-skinned?

examples.igbo: Ite a nwere ike ichedo mmiri.
examples.english: This pot can hold water.

examples.igbo: Akpa a nwere ike ichedo mmiri?
examples.english: Can this bag hold water?

note: 'Chedo mmiri' is used as given; some speakers may prefer another verb for holding water.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-enwe ngwùli n’èzí.
examples.english: The children are having fun outside.

examples.igbo: Ngwùli anyị mere taa tọrọ ụtọ.
examples.english: The fun we had today was enjoyable.

examples.igbo: O kwùkwùrù aka ya n’iwe.
examples.english: He clenched his fist in anger.

examples.igbo: Kwùkwù aka gị wee jide eriri ahụ.
examples.english: Clench your hand and hold that rope.

examples.igbo: Ebe obibi ha dị nso n’osimiri.
examples.english: Their dwelling place is near the river.

examples.igbo: Anyị chọrọ ebe obibi ọhụrụ.
examples.english: We are looking for a new dwelling place.

gloss: plant resembling aŋā, used for its fibres

examples.igbo: Àbù na-eto n'akụkụ ụlọ anyị nke ọma.
examples.english: Àbù grows well beside our house.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akpa ụdọ site n'àbù maka m?
examples.english: Do you weave rope from àbù for me?

note: The plant àbù is not common in everyday speech; sentences are plausible but I am not fully certain of idiomatic usage.

gloss: be the head (first and foremost, before being anything else)

examples.igbo: Ọ bụgodu isi n'ezinụlọ anyị nke ukwuu.
examples.english: He is truly the head in our family.

examples.igbo: Ị bụgodu isi n'ọrụ a n'ezie?
examples.english: Are you really the head in this work?

note: The phrase is somewhat formal; I am not fully certain of all contexts.

examples.igbo: Ọ zara azìza nke ọma n'oge.
examples.english: He answered the query well in time.

examples.igbo: Biko za azìza ajụjụ m nke ọma.
examples.english: Please answer my query well.

examples.igbo: O tìkọrọ osisi abụọ ọnụ n'ubi.
examples.english: He put two sticks together in the farm.

examples.igbo: Tìkọ mkpịsị aka gị ọnụ wee hụ.
examples.english: Put your fingers together and see.

examples.igbo: O sere ife ahụ na igwe foto.
examples.english: He photographed that object with a camera.

examples.igbo: Ihe ahụ sere na enyo nke ọma.
examples.english: That object reflected well in the mirror.

note: The verb -sèlụ has two senses; I have illustrated both. I am not fully certain of the exact tone patterns in all inflections.

examples.igbo: Ọkwùlù na-eto n'ubi anyị nke ọma.
examples.english: Okra grows well in our farm.

examples.igbo: Ị na-esi ọkwùlù ofe mgbe ụfọdụ?
examples.english: Do you sometimes cook okra soup?

gloss: act together; have intercourse with; fraternise with

examples.igbo: Ha na-emekọ ihe ọnụ n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: They do things together at school.

examples.igbo: Biko mekọọ ya ihe n'udo mgbe niile.
examples.english: Please always associate with him in peace.

examples.igbo: O nyere anyị ogbe nke osisi ahụ.
examples.english: He gave us a sample of that plant.

examples.igbo: Ogbe a ọ dị mma maka nnwale?
examples.english: Is this sample good for testing?

examples.igbo: O rechara ahịa ya niile n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: He sold all his goods completely in the morning.

examples.igbo: Recha ngwa ahịa gị tupu ọ chịa.
examples.english: Finish selling your goods before it gets dark.

examples.igbo: Igwe ojii lùchìrì anyanwụ n'ehihie taa.
examples.english: Clouds obscured the sun this afternoon.

examples.igbo: Igwe ojii ọ na-alùchì anyanwụ ugbu a?
examples.english: Are clouds obscuring the sun now?

note: The verb is not common; I am unsure of the exact past tense form and tone.

examples.igbo: O kpèchalụrụ osisi ahụ maka akpụkpọ ya.
examples.english: He stripped that tree for its bark.

examples.igbo: Kpèchalụ osisi a, were akpụkpọ ya.
examples.english: Strip this tree and take its bark.

note: Verb inflection kpèchalụrụ is plausible but not certain.

examples.igbo: Nne m na-eji ǹkwọ òsè egwe ose.
examples.english: My mother uses a pepper grinder to grind pepper.

examples.igbo: Ebee ka ǹkwọ òsè dị?
examples.english: Where is the pepper grinder?

gloss: sift (to separate chaff or foreign body)

examples.igbo: O yòchara ọka ahụ wepụ ihe ndị ọzọ.
examples.english: She sifted that corn and removed other things.

examples.igbo: Yòcha ọka a tupu ị kwo ya.
examples.english: Sift this corn before you cook it.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ bụ mkpìlìsì, o nweghị ike iru na tebụl.
examples.english: That child is short; he cannot reach the table.

examples.igbo: Mkpìlìsì osisi dara n'ala.
examples.english: A broken piece of wood fell on the ground.

note: Unsure whether mkpìlìsì is commonly used this way in ordinary speech.

gloss: rekindle fire by blowing air to it

examples.igbo: O fụ̀nwuru ọkụ̄ ka ọ na-enwu ọzọ.
examples.english: He blew the fire to make it burn again.

examples.igbo: Fụ̀nwu ọkụ̄ ahụ, ọ na-emenwu.
examples.english: Blow that fire; it is going out.

note: The inflected form fụ̀nwuru is plausible but not certain.

examples.igbo: Òli ahụ riri nnukwu nri.
examples.english: That eater ate a big meal.

examples.igbo: Ị bụ òli ukwu?
examples.english: Are you a big eater?

examples.igbo: O fùnwuru ọkụ were sie nri.
examples.english: He lit the fire by blowing and cooked food.

examples.igbo: Fùnwu ọkụ, anyị ga-esi nri.
examples.english: Light the fire by blowing; we will cook.

note: The inflected form fùnwuru is plausible but not certain.

gloss: collect and throw away [refuse, clothes, books etc.];

examples.igbo: O kpopụ̀rụ ahịhịa ndị ahụ.
examples.english: He collected and threw away that refuse.

examples.igbo: Kpopụ̀ ihe ndị a niile.
examples.english: Throw away all these things.

note: The past form kpopụ̀rụ is plausible but not certain.

examples.igbo: Nzò ụkwū ya dị n'aja.
examples.english: His footprint is in the sand.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ nzò ụkwū n'ụzọ?
examples.english: Did you see a footprint on the road?

examples.igbo: Ọ bu isi ūtabà n'aka.
examples.english: He carried a head of tobacco in his hand.

examples.igbo: Isi ūtabà a dị oke ọnụ.
examples.english: This head of tobacco is very expensive.

gloss: to move or shake; to make something or somebody move or shake

examples.igbo: Ifufe na-megharị akwụkwọ osisi.
examples.english: The wind shakes the leaves.

examples.igbo: Megharịa oche ahụ ntakịrị.
examples.english: Move that chair a little.

examples.igbo: Ọ kpùrù mmụọ n'emume.
examples.english: He put on a mask at the festival.

examples.igbo: Ha na-ekpu mmụọ n'oge egwuregwu.
examples.english: They put on masks during the play.

gloss: (harmonizes with vowel of verb root) (marks infinitive)

examples.igbo: Ọ chọrọ ịzụ akwa.
examples.english: He wants to buy cloth.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ ịga ahịa?
examples.english: Do you want to go to the market?

examples.igbo: Achọpụtara m ego ahụ n'akpa.
examples.english: I found that money in the bag.

examples.igbo: Chọpụta ebe ọ nọ!
examples.english: Find out where he is!

gloss: building with corrugated iron roofing, 'zinc house'

examples.igbo: Ụnò gbamgbam ya na-egbuke egbuke.
examples.english: His zinc house is shining.

examples.igbo: Anyị rụrụ ụnò gbamgbam ọhụrụ.
examples.english: We built a new zinc house.

examples.igbo: Biko fụtalụ m ebe ọ gara.
examples.english: Please find out for me where he went.

examples.igbo: Ha fụtalụrụ m onye zuru ego ahụ.
examples.english: They found out for me who stole the money.

note: The applicative form -fụtalụ is less common; the inflections may vary by dialect.

gloss: cake made of beans (derived from Yoruba àkàrà)

examples.igbo: Mama na-ere àkàlà n'ahịa.
examples.english: Mama sells bean cakes in the market.

examples.igbo: Àkàlà a na-atọ ụtọ.
examples.english: This bean cake is sweet.

examples.igbo: Osisi ahụ dàkwepụrụ.
examples.english: That stick snapped.

examples.igbo: Ọ dàkwepụrụ eriri ahụ.
examples.english: He snapped the rope.

examples.igbo: Kèdụ ogè ị ga-abịa n'ụlọ anyị?
examples.english: When will you come to our house?

examples.igbo: Gwa m kèdụ ogè ụgbọ ga-abịa.
examples.english: Tell me when the car will come.

examples.igbo: Nne m sara afele ndị ahụ.
examples.english: My mother washed those plates.

examples.igbo: Biko wetara m afele ọzọ.
examples.english: Please bring me another plate.

examples.igbo: Atuma mmanya ahụ dị n'akụkụ ụlọ.
examples.english: That palm wine keg is beside the house.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ atuma mmanya ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see that palm wine keg?

examples.igbo: O na-eje ijè kwa ụtụtụ.
examples.english: He goes on a walk every morning.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eje ijè taa?
examples.english: Will you go on a journey today?

examples.igbo: O nyere ya efè ka o kwuo okwu.
examples.english: He gave him a chance to speak.

examples.igbo: Biko nye m efè!
examples.english: Please give me a chance!

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-atachi mgbe niile.
examples.english: That child is always obstinate.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji atachi?
examples.english: Why are you obstinate?

examples.igbo: Ekelebe jidere onye ohi n'abalị.
examples.english: The police arrested the thief at night.

examples.igbo: Ị kpọrọ ekelebe?
examples.english: Did you call the police?

gloss: put (in or out); take out from; put, squeeze, insert into (bag, pocket, etc.)

examples.igbo: Fọọ ego n'akpa gị.
examples.english: Put money in your pocket.

examples.igbo: O fọrọ mkpụrụ n'ime ala.
examples.english: He put the seed in the ground.

gloss: nail; drive a peg or skewer

examples.igbo: O kpọnyere ntu n'ime mgbidi.
examples.english: He nailed a nail into the wall.

examples.igbo: Kpọnye osisi ahụ n'ala.
examples.english: Nail that wood to the ground.

gloss: be in harmony with (literally sound together or fall together)

examples.igbo: Olu ha dàkọlịtara nke ọma.
examples.english: Their voices were in harmony well.

examples.igbo: Okwu ha abụọ dàkọlịtara?
examples.english: Do their two words agree?

examples.igbo: Ọ kụpụrụ aka n'ọrụ ugbo ya.
examples.english: He gave up his farm work.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji kụpụ aka n'ọsọ ahụ?
examples.english: Why did you give up in that race?

examples.igbo: Mechi anyā gị bido ikpe ekpere.
examples.english: Close your eyes and start praying.

examples.igbo: Nwa ọhụrụ ahụ mechiri anyā hie ụra.
examples.english: That baby closed its eyes and slept.

examples.igbo: Ndị obodo na-agọ alūsi n'ọhịa.
examples.english: The villagers worship a spirit in the forest.

examples.igbo: Ị na-agọ alūsi kama ịgọ Chineke?
examples.english: Are you worshipping a spirit instead of God?

examples.igbo: Gàkwu ebe ahụ ugbua.
examples.english: Go to that place now.

examples.igbo: Ọ gàkwuru nne ya n'ụlọ ọgwụ.
examples.english: He went to his mother at the hospital.

examples.igbo: Emēnjọ ya doro anya n'ụlọ ikpe.
examples.english: His innocence was clear in court.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ekwu na emēnjọ gị bụ ihe mere o ji hapụ gị?
examples.english: Are you saying your innocence is why he let you go?

examples.igbo: Ọ nọ n'ahịa ugbua.
examples.english: He is at the market now.

examples.igbo: Ị nọ n'ụlọ?
examples.english: Are you at home?

gloss: carve, shape image an to represent a god or deity

examples.igbo: Ọ pịrị arūsị̄ n'osisi.
examples.english: He carved a deity image in wood.

examples.igbo: Pịa arūsị̄ ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: Carve that deity image well.

examples.igbo: Ọ wabàtara n'ụlọ mgbe mmiri malitere.
examples.english: He rushed inside when it started raining.

examples.igbo: Wabàta n'ụlọ ngwa ngwa!
examples.english: Rush inside quickly!

gloss: open; open wide (e.g. hand, mouth, book, but not door)

examples.igbo: Sàghe aka gị ka m hụ ihe dị n'ime.
examples.english: Open your hand so I can see what is inside.

examples.igbo: Ọ sàghere ọnụ ya were tie mkpu.
examples.english: He opened his mouth wide and shouted.

examples.igbo: Ọ gbara òkpoòfùfù n'ọrụ ubi.
examples.english: He perspired at farm work.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji agba òkpoòfùfù?
examples.english: Why are you perspiring?

examples.igbo: Ọ gbusịsịrị ahụhụ niile dị n'ubi ya.
examples.english: He annihilated all the insects in his farm.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-agbusịsị oke ndị a niile?
examples.english: Will you annihilate all these rats?

note: The stem -gbusịsị is rare; I inflected it as gbusịsịrị / ga-agbusịsị, which is my best reading of its conjugation.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-akpori ndụ n'ogige egwuregwu.
examples.english: The children are having fun in the playground.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akpori ndụ mgbe ọ bụla ị bịara ebe a?
examples.english: Do you have fun every time you come here?

note: Treated kpori ndụ as a fixed expression taking the -na- habitual prefix.

examples.igbo: O kwụzùrù ụgwọ ụlọ ya niile.
examples.english: He paid his house rent in full.

examples.igbo: Ị kwụzùrù ụgwọ akwụkwọ ụmụ gị?
examples.english: Did you complete the payment of your children's school fees?

note: Past form given as kwụzùrù; tones on the suffix are my best reconstruction.

gloss: re-wash; wash again Ọ gà-àsụnwù akwà ọ sùlù n’ùtụtù She will re-wash the cloth she washed in the morning

examples.igbo: Sụnwù aka gị ọzọ, ha ka ruru unyi.
examples.english: Wash your hands again, they are still dirty.

examples.igbo: Nne m sụnwùrù akwa ahụ n'ihi na ọ dịghị ọcha.
examples.english: My mother re-washed that cloth because it was not clean.

note: Kept the verb with what it usually takes in washing: hands and cloth.

examples.igbo: M zụtara òlòma oyìbo atọ n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: I bought three grapefruits at the market today.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ òlòma oyìbo ka ị chọrọ, ka ọ bụ oroma?
examples.english: Is it grapefruit you want, or orange?

examples.igbo: Ndanda na-arị àrị n'ala kichin.
examples.english: Ants are crawling on the kitchen floor.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ijiji ji arị àrị n'elu nri anyị?
examples.english: Why are flies crawling on our food?

note: Used the reduplicated na-arị àrị construction for insects moving about.

examples.igbo: Igwe ojii na-ara mmiri, anyị ga-agba ọsọ laa.
examples.english: The clouds are producing rain, we shall run home.

examples.igbo: Igwe na-ara mmiri n'abalị a?
examples.english: Is the sky producing rain tonight?

note: Subject kept as igwe (the sky/clouds), which is what properly 'produces' rain here.

examples.igbo: Ọbù ụkwụ ya gbara ọkụ n'ihi okporo ụzọ ahụ.
examples.english: The sole of his foot burned because of that road.

examples.igbo: Ọbù ụkwụ gị na-egbu gị mgbu?
examples.english: Does the sole of your foot hurt you?

examples.igbo: O gbatùrù mkpụrụ ube ahụ n'ala.
examples.english: He knocked that pear fruit down to the ground.

examples.igbo: Ị gbatùrù mkpụrụ ube ahụ niile?
examples.english: Did you knock down all those pear fruits?

note: Read gbatù as 'knock/kick down'; past form written gbatùrù.

gloss: set an example (to be followed by younger generations)

examples.igbo: Okenye ọ bụla kwesịrị ịtọ ụkpụlụ ọma nye ụmụaka.
examples.english: Every elder should set a good example for children.

examples.igbo: Ị na-atọ ụkpụlụ ọma nye ụmụ gị?
examples.english: Are you setting a good example for your children?

note: The verb is used here with the indirect object nye ụmụaka / nye ụmụ gị.

examples.igbo: N'abalị tara, m rọrọ nrọ ọjọọ.
examples.english: Last night, I had a bad dream.

examples.igbo: Ị rọrọ nrọ ọ bụla n'abalị tara?
examples.english: Did you have any dream last night?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-abịakarị n'ụlọ akwụkwọ n'oge.
examples.english: He always comes to school on time.

examples.igbo: Ị na-agakarị ahịa ụbọchị Satọde?
examples.english: Do you always go to the market on Saturdays?

note: The suffix -karị adds 'usually/often'; the gloss 'always' is broader, but the sentences show the habitual sense.

examples.igbo: N'Igbo, 'm' na 'n' bụ m̀kpọnimi.
examples.english: In Igbo, 'm' and 'n' are nasals.

examples.igbo: Kpọọ m̀kpọnimi ndị a nke ọma.
examples.english: Pronounce these nasals well.

note: The word is a technical term, so the examples are necessarily about language.

examples.igbo: Ọnwa zomì n'igwe ojii.
examples.english: The moon is hidden in the clouds.

examples.igbo: Ònye zomì n'ime ụlọ ahụ?
examples.english: Who is hidden in that room?

gloss: take far away; take far inside

examples.igbo: O wemìrì akpa ahụ n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: He took that bag far inside the house.

examples.igbo: Biko wemì osisi ahụ n'azụ ụlọ.
examples.english: Please take that stick far behind the house.

gloss: change form or appearance; transform; transfigure

examples.igbo: Igwe ojii ahụ nwòghàrị̀rị̀ ka ọ na-efe.
examples.english: That cloud changed form as it flew.

examples.igbo: Ihe ahụ nwòghàrị̀rị̀ ghọọ agwọ?
examples.english: Did that thing transform into a snake?

examples.igbo: Mama gwaziri osikapa na tomato n'ite.
examples.english: Mother mixed the rice and tomatoes properly in the pot.

examples.igbo: Ị gwaziri ofe ahụ nke ọma?
examples.english: Did you mix that soup well?

examples.igbo: Anụ m ùdà mgbọ n'ime ọhịa.
examples.english: I heard the sound of a gun in the forest.

examples.igbo: Ì nụrụ ùdà ụgbọ oloko?
examples.english: Did you hear the sound of the train?

gloss: persist; be obstinate in desperation or in last desperate effort (by sufferer) before or to prevent death

examples.igbo: Ọ na-asi ọnwụ na-arịọ mmiri.
examples.english: He desperately kept asking for water.

examples.igbo: Ha na-asi ọnwụ ịpụ n'ụlọ ahụ.
examples.english: They desperately persisted to leave that house.

note: The idiom is uncommon; the sentences show the desperate, last-effort sense.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-amalite ọrụ ugbu a.
examples.english: He is beginning work now.

examples.igbo: Ihe ọmụmụ na-amalite n'elekere asatọ.
examples.english: Class begins at eight o'clock.

gloss: put clothes on someone (compare -yi 1. wear clothes)

examples.igbo: Nne ya yibere ya uwe ọhụrụ.
examples.english: Her mother put new clothes on her.

examples.igbo: Yibe nwa gị uwe ọcha taa.
examples.english: Put white clothes on your child today.

examples.igbo: Ọka anyị pụrụ epụ n’ubi.
examples.english: Our maize sprouted in the farm.

examples.igbo: Osisi a na-apụ epụ n’oge mmiri.
examples.english: This tree sprouts in the rainy season.

examples.igbo: Akpa ọka a nyịrị arọ.
examples.english: This bag of maize is heavy.

examples.igbo: Nkụ a ọ nyịrị arọ?
examples.english: Is this firewood heavy?

examples.igbo: O zòkwàsịrị ụkwụ m n’ụzọ.
examples.english: He trod upon my foot on the road.

examples.igbo: Zòkwàsịa nwayọ, e nwere ụmụaka ebe a.
examples.english: Tread gently, there are children here.

examples.igbo: O lifọrọ nri n’efere.
examples.english: He ate and left some food in the plate.

examples.igbo: Lifọa ntakịrị maka nwanne gị.
examples.english: Leave a little for your sibling.

examples.igbo: Òkà ụtā ahụ gbara nnụnụ n’elu osisi.
examples.english: That archer shot a bird on the tree.

examples.igbo: Òkà ụtā ahụ ọ zụrụ ụta ọhụrụ?
examples.english: Did that archer buy a new bow?

gloss: to force way through small doorway, small opening in wall, thicket

examples.igbo: Ọ na-apio n’ọnụ ụzọ dị warara.
examples.english: He forces his way through the narrow doorway.

examples.igbo: Pio n’oghere ahụ, ọ dị warara.
examples.english: Force through that hole; it is narrow.

examples.igbo: O kpere m̄kpēsā banyere ego efu ya.
examples.english: He laid a complaint about his lost money.

examples.igbo: Kpee m̄kpēsā n’ụlọ ọrụ gị maka ụgwọ ọrụ.
examples.english: Lay a complaint at your office about salary.

gloss: (in Nri thought) the firmament and the earth, which together make up Ùwà, the visible world

examples.igbo: Igwē nà Ànì bụ ùwà anyị na-ahụ anya.
examples.english: The firmament and earth are the world we see.

examples.igbo: Ì maara ihe Igwē nà Ànì pụtara?
examples.english: Do you know what Igwe na Ani means?

examples.igbo: O jiri ọgbàlà kwọọ ụgbọ mmiri ya.
examples.english: He used a punting pole to punt his canoe.

examples.igbo: Ọgbàlà a ọ toro ogologo maka ụgbọ mmiri?
examples.english: Is this punting pole long enough for the canoe?

examples.igbo: Pastọ gọziri ụmụaka ahụ tupu ha alaa.
examples.english: The pastor blessed those children before they left.

examples.igbo: Gọzie nri a tupu anyị eri ya.
examples.english: Bless this food before we eat it.

examples.igbo: Ndị njem ahụ fọdụgara n'obodo dị iche iche.
examples.english: Those travelers remained in different towns.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere unu ji fọdụga n'ụlọ dị iche iche?
examples.english: Why did you remain in different houses?

note: The verb form fọdụgara is used; aspect choice may vary by dialect.

examples.igbo: Ọ bìfèrè n'obodo a, ọ ga-akwaga ebe ọzọ.
examples.english: He has lived too long in this town; he will move elsewhere.

examples.igbo: Anyị abìfèla n'ebe a okè, anyị ga-ala.
examples.english: We have lived too long here; we will go back.

note: The sense is clear, but the inflected forms of -bifè can vary.

examples.igbo: Gọọmenti kwara ụzọ ọhụrụ gaa obodo anyị.
examples.english: The government opened a new road to our town.

examples.igbo: Kwaa ụzọ maka ndị ọbịa ka ha banye.
examples.english: Clear the way for the guests to enter.

examples.igbo: Nna m ukwu bụ nnà milichukwu m.
examples.english: My uncle is my godfather.

examples.igbo: Ị họrọla nnà milichukwu maka nwa gị?
examples.english: Have you chosen a godfather for your child?

examples.igbo: Ndị mmadụ nọ n'ùfụ mgbe idei mmiri bịara.
examples.english: People were in distress when the flood came.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji nọ n'ùfụ?
examples.english: Why are you in distress?

gloss: association; team; group; a group of people focusing on a central topic; party; camp

examples.igbo: Òtù anyị na-ezukọ kwa Satọde.
examples.english: Our association meets every Saturday.

examples.igbo: Ị sonyeere òtù egwuregwu ọhụrụ?
examples.english: Did you join a new sports team?

examples.igbo: O ziri ibu ya n'isi mgbe o ruru n'ụlọ.
examples.english: He put down his load from his head when he reached home.

examples.igbo: Zie ibu gị, anyị eruoela.
examples.english: Put down your load; we have arrived.

examples.igbo: Uwe ya chàrà ọ̀bàraọ̀bàrà n'ụbọchị ahụ.
examples.english: Her dress was red that day.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ụgbọala chàrà ọ̀bàraọ̀bàrà n'okporo ụzọ?
examples.english: Did you see a red car on the road?

note: The color phrase is correct; the verb form chàrà may vary with context.

examples.igbo: Mkpa akū na-ewe oge n'ụlọ.
examples.english: Searching for kernels takes time at home.

examples.igbo: Bịa nyere m aka mkpa akū.
examples.english: Come help me search for kernels.

note: The phrase is understood as searching for kernels; context may affect phrasing.

examples.igbo: Nwa ọhụrụ na-efufe aka ya n'elu.
examples.english: The baby is waving its hand in the air.

examples.igbo: Ị na-efufe akwa ọcha ahụ n'ikuku?
examples.english: Are you waving that white cloth in the air?

examples.igbo: O nwere anya ukwu n'ahụ ego nwanne ya.
examples.english: He covets his brother's money.

examples.igbo: Enwela anya ukwu n'ahụ ihe onye ọzọ.
examples.english: Don't covet someone else's things.

examples.igbo: Osisi ahụ na-akwukwe n'ikuku nke ukwuu.
examples.english: That tree is shaking in the wind a lot.

examples.igbo: Kwukwee oche ahụ ka ọ kwụsị ịkwukwe.
examples.english: Shake that chair so it stops wobbling.

examples.igbo: Ahụrụ m fig na-eto eto n'ọhịa.
examples.english: I saw a growing fig in the bush.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eri fig nke ọhụrụ a?
examples.english: Are you eating this fresh fig?

gloss: a creeping plant whose yellow juice is used to decorate the body

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-ete ògàalụ n'ahụ ha.
examples.english: Children smear ògàalụ on their bodies.

examples.igbo: Ògàalụ na-akwụ n'osisi ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: Ògàalụ creeps on that tree well.

examples.igbo: Onye amụma ahụ na-ebu amụma banyere ọdịnihu.
examples.english: That prophet prophesies about the future.

examples.igbo: Buru amụma maka obodo a ugbu a.
examples.english: Prophesy about this town right now.

examples.igbo: O pịaziri ego ahụ niile n'oge ọ bụla.
examples.english: He reckoned up all that money at any time.

examples.igbo: Pịazie ụgwọ gị tupu ị pụọ n'ụlọ.
examples.english: Settle your debt before you leave the house.

examples.igbo: Nna m na-azọ ezè n'obodo anyị.
examples.english: My father is contesting for chieftaincy in our town.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-azọ ezè n'afọ a ọzọ?
examples.english: Will you contest for chieftaincy again this year?

examples.igbo: O ghalịrị àzụ mgbe ọ nụrụ olu nne ya.
examples.english: He turned round when he heard his mother's voice.

examples.igbo: Ghalịa àzụ, anyị echefuola ihe nke anyị.
examples.english: Turn round, we have forgotten our thing.

examples.igbo: Nchèzọ na-akpatakarị m nsogbu n'ọrụ.
examples.english: Forgetfulness often causes me trouble at work.

examples.igbo: Ị na-enwe nchèzọ ugbu a?
examples.english: Are you experiencing forgetfulness now?

gloss: curry leaves [Murraya koenigii or Bergera koenigii]

examples.igbo: M tinyere kọ̀rị na ofe ọkwa.
examples.english: I put curry leaves in the cocoyam soup.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara kọ̀rị n'ahịa?
examples.english: Did you buy curry leaves at the market?

examples.igbo: Ọ bara ọ̀gụ̀ n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: He launched a fight at the market today.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-aba ọ̀gụ̀ ọzọ?
examples.english: Will you launch a fight again?

gloss: day before yesterday (literally today is three)

examples.igbo: Ta à bù àtọ ka anyị gara ahịa.
examples.english: We went to the market the day before yesterday.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ya ta à bù àtọ?
examples.english: Did you see him the day before yesterday?

examples.igbo: Onye na-achụ nta na-agbe egbe n'ọhịa.
examples.english: The hunter stalks in the bush.

examples.igbo: Ndị ohi gbara egbe banye n'ụlọ.
examples.english: The thieves moved stealthily into the house.

examples.igbo: Ahịa taa dùrù-dù.
examples.english: The market is dull today.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji dù-dù otu a?
examples.english: Why are you in a dull state like this?

examples.igbo: O ji mgburu aga ije.
examples.english: He uses a walking stick to take a walk.

examples.igbo: Were mgburu gị bịa.
examples.english: Bring your walking stick.

examples.igbo: Ọ ràlụsịrị n'ọrụ ya.
examples.english: He left his job altogether.

examples.igbo: Ị ràlụsịrị n'ụlọ ha?
examples.english: Did you leave their house altogether?

examples.igbo: O kpụkọrọ akwụkwọ ya ọnụ.
examples.english: She packed her books together.

examples.igbo: Kpụkọọ uwe ndị a ọnụ.
examples.english: Pack these clothes closely together.

examples.igbo: Ha kpara oke ànì n'etiti ubi abụọ.
examples.english: They made a boundary between two farms.

examples.igbo: Ị kpara oke ànì gị na nke ya?
examples.english: Did you make a boundary between your land and his?

examples.english: The doctor examined the child's oral cavity.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ezi m àzụ akā n'okwu a?
examples.english: Are you being insincere with me in this matter?

note: Idiom; literal image may be unclear to some speakers.

examples.igbo: Ị na-achi mmụọ n'afọ a?

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ǹke anyị n'ahịa?
examples.english: Did you see ours in the market?

examples.igbo: Ị nụrụ na ọ lara mmụọ?

examples.english: The ember is hot, be careful.

examples.english: Motion your hand, we will hear everything.

examples.english: Pull it off before it catches you.

examples.english: This sheathed sword is heavy; will you carry it?

note: The word is uncommon; examples are plausible but I am not fully certain of its modern usage.

examples.english: Is the central room of this house where my mother stays?

note: The second sentence is idiomatic, but another phrasing could also work.

gloss: cross the feet or legs; throw one leg across the other

examples.english: Cross your legs on this chair.

examples.english: Did we make the division of that land fairly?

examples.english: How many people is that company employing this year?

gloss: pluck (unripe fruit); miscarry (especially of animals, but also of humans)

examples.english: Our cow miscarried before it could calve.

examples.igbo: Ị na-aga ahịa ụbọsị daa?
examples.english: Do you go to the market every day?

examples.english: Did you see that yellow maize in the market?

note: The word is a colour term used mainly with -cha or as a modifier; phrasing may vary by dialect.

examples.igbo: Ị bụ enyi m?
examples.english: Are you my friend?

gloss: fold; bend or arrange so that one side covers the other

examples.english: His words are full of bitterness.

examples.english: What is rolling inside the house?
