examples.english: We will not accept his invitation.

note: Uncertain whether -lite ùtà takes lite or lịta forms; examples follow the headword.

examples.igbo: O gụnwụrụ akwụkwọ ahụ.
examples.english: He read that book again.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-agụnwù ya?
examples.english: Will you read it again?

examples.igbo: Anyị hụrụ àkpà anwū n'elu osisi.
examples.english: We saw a bees' nest on the tree.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-atụ egwu àkpà anwū.
examples.english: The children are afraid of a bees' nest.

examples.igbo: Tụdàta m ụdọ ahụ.
examples.english: Throw the rope down to me.

examples.igbo: O tụdàtara anyị mkpụrụ osisi.
examples.english: He threw down fruit to us.

examples.igbo: Òpu ākpịlị dị ya n'olu.
examples.english: He has goitre on his neck.

examples.igbo: Dọkịta na-enyocha òpu ākpịlị n'olu ya.
examples.english: The doctor is examining the goitre on his neck.

gloss: deadly or terminal (disease); a disease without a cure

examples.igbo: Ọrịa m̀mènwụ na-egbu mmadụ.
examples.english: A terminal disease kills people.

examples.igbo: Dọkịta kwuru na ọrịa ya bụ m̀mènwụ.
examples.english: The doctor said his disease is terminal.

examples.igbo: Ǹsị ehi juru n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: Cow dung filled the road.

examples.igbo: O jiri ǹsị ehi na-akụ ihe ọkụkụ.
examples.english: He uses cow dung to fertilize crops.

examples.igbo: O kwubìdoro m okwu.
examples.english: He interrupted me.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-akwubìdo ya mgbe ọ na-ekwu.
examples.english: We interrupt him when he is talking.

gloss: something roundish and smooth, e.g. shot-putt

examples.igbo: O tụrụ mkpụlù n'egwuregwu ụmụaka.
examples.english: He threw the shot put in the children's game.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ ịtụ mkpụlù?
examples.english: Do you want to throw the shot put?

note: The word mkpụlù is less common; I used it for a round, smooth object like a shot put.

examples.igbo: O tinyere nnu ụtabà n'ime ofe.
examples.english: She put potash stone in the soup.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere nnu ụtabà n'ụlọ?
examples.english: Do you have potash stone at home?

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-atamu anụ.
examples.english: That child is biting the meat into small pieces.

examples.igbo: Tamuo mkpụrụ osisi ahụ tupu ịmụọ ya.
examples.english: Bite the fruit into small pieces before swallowing it.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-abịa mgbe niile.
examples.english: He comes every time.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eme ya mgbe niile?
examples.english: Do you do it every time?

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka ahụ guzoro n'ògbà.
examples.english: The children stood in a row.

examples.igbo: Kee ha n'ògbà abụọ.
examples.english: Arrange them in two rows.

examples.igbo: O nyere m àdù.
examples.english: He gave me bitter kola.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ata àdù?
examples.english: Do you chew bitter kola?

examples.igbo: O nwere ahụmahụ n'ọrụ ahụ.
examples.english: He has experience in that work.

examples.igbo: Ahụmahụ gị dị mkpa.
examples.english: Your experience is important.

examples.igbo: O setịwanyere eriri ahụ.
examples.english: He stretched the rope further.

examples.igbo: Setịwanye akwa ahụ ntakịrị.
examples.english: Stretch the cloth a little further.

examples.igbo: Onye okike kere ụwa.
examples.english: The creator made the world.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-ekele onye okike.
examples.english: We thank the creator.

examples.igbo: O sekpụrụ igbe ahụ elu.
examples.english: He lifted the box up.

examples.igbo: Sekpụniri ya elu.
examples.english: Lift it up.

note: The verb conjugation of sekpụni is uncertain; I used sekpụrụ and sekpụniri based on common patterns.

gloss: a noisy masquerade with a lot of items on its body

examples.igbo: Àjị̀kwụ̀ na-eme mkpọtụ n'ọ̀hịa taa.
examples.english: Àjị̀kwụ̀ is making noise in the square today.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ Àjị̀kwụ̀ mgbe ọ na-agafe?
examples.english: Did you see Àjị̀kwụ̀ when it was passing?

gloss: spike used for bringing boiled pieces of yam or meat out of the pot

examples.igbo: Jiri mkpịsị nnī wepụta ji dị n'ite.
examples.english: Use the yam spike to bring out the yam in the pot.

examples.igbo: Mkpịsị nnī a dị mkpụmkpụ, ọ gaghị eru anụ.
examples.english: This yam spike is short; it will not reach the meat.

examples.igbo: Osisi ahụ gbàrà ùfìè n'ụzọ anyị.
examples.english: That stick lay across our path.

examples.igbo: Gbàa ùfìè n'ọnụ ụzọ, onye ọ bụla agaghị abanye.
examples.english: Lie across the doorway; nobody will enter.

gloss: throw water over (as in taking a shower)

examples.igbo: Nne m kwọsàrà mmilī n'ahụ nwa ya.
examples.english: My mother poured water over her child's body.

examples.igbo: Kwọsaa mmilī n'ahụ gị tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Pour water over yourself before you go out.

gloss: join or hold together in order to become one mass; bind

examples.igbo: Anyị jìkọtara aka anyị ọnụ.
examples.english: We held our hands together.

examples.igbo: Jìkọta osisi ndị a ọnụ, ha ga-esi ike.
examples.english: Bind these sticks together; they will be strong.

examples.igbo: Ụkwụ m na-egbu mgbu n'ìkili ụkwū.
examples.english: My foot hurts at the heel.

examples.igbo: Ìkili ụkwū ya merụrụ ahụ mgbe ọ dara.
examples.english: His heel was injured when he fell.

examples.igbo: Nye m otu ibe òlòma.
examples.english: Give me one segment of orange.

examples.igbo: Ibe òlòma a dị ụtọ.
examples.english: This segment of orange is sweet.

gloss: desire something, especially edible, even though you are not hungry or in need of it

examples.igbo: Ọ na-asa ụ̀sà mgbe ọ hụrụ anụ.
examples.english: He craves meat when he sees it.

examples.igbo: Ị na-asa ụ̀sà maka achịcha?
examples.english: Are you craving bread?

examples.igbo: Mgbè anyị ruru, ọ na-ezo.
examples.english: When we arrived, it was raining.

examples.igbo: Mgbè ole ka ị ga-abịa?
examples.english: What time will you come?

gloss: form of praise for one who excels his colleagues; first among equals

examples.igbo: Chinedu bụ nwa kā ibè ya n'ịkụ osikapa.
examples.english: Chinedu is first among equals in pounding rice.

examples.igbo: Ònye bụ nwa kā ibè ya n'egwuregwu bọọlụ?
examples.english: Who is first among equals in football?

examples.igbo: Amāafịa ǹtùtọ ākpịlị na-egbu m mgbu.
examples.english: Sore throat is paining me.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere amāafịa ǹtùtọ ākpịlị?
examples.english: Do you have a sore throat?

examples.igbo: M na-akpa nkụ n'ọhịa.
examples.english: I am gathering firewood in the bush.

examples.igbo: Kpaa nkụ tupu ọ daa.
examples.english: Gather firewood before it gets dark.

examples.igbo: Ọ zàkpọrọ ájá n'ọnụ ụzọ.
examples.english: He swept dirt to the doorway.

examples.igbo: Zàkpò ájá ahụ n'ebe a.
examples.english: Sweep that dirt onto here.

note: Uncertain of exact sense; examples show sweeping onto a place.

examples.igbo: Ngwá egwu a na-ada ụda.
examples.english: This musical instrument sounds sweet.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akụ ngwá egwu?
examples.english: Do you play a musical instrument?

gloss: to have a say in something; have influence over something; be influential

examples.igbo: Nna m nwere àgbà n'okwu ezinụlọ.
examples.english: My father has a say in family matters.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere àgbà n'ihe a?
examples.english: Do you have a say in this?

examples.igbo: Nlò nke akwa a dị mma.
examples.english: The softness of this cloth is nice.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ nlò nke oche a?
examples.english: Did you feel the softness of this chair?

examples.igbo: Nwata na-aracha aka ya.
examples.english: The child is licking his hand.

examples.igbo: Racha efere gị.
examples.english: Lick your plate.

examples.igbo: Obere akwa gbatịrị n'ala.
examples.english: The small cloth spread out on the ground.

examples.igbo: Gbatị aka gị.
examples.english: Stretch your hand.

examples.igbo: M na-adụkọ akwa abụọ.
examples.english: I am sewing two cloths together.

examples.igbo: Dụkọ akwa ndị a ọnụ.
examples.english: Sew these cloths together.

gloss: stand; a position whereby a person or object has its base on the ground and top in the air or in a height

examples.igbo: Osisi ahụ kwụrụ ọtọ n'akụkụ ụzọ.
examples.english: That tree stood upright beside the road.

examples.igbo: Guzo ọtọ ebe ahụ, ka m hụ gị.
examples.english: Stand upright there so I can see you.

examples.igbo: Akpụ ụkwụ ya na-egbu ya mgbu mgbe o si n'ọrụ lọta.
examples.english: His thigh muscle pains him when he comes home from work.

examples.igbo: Bọọlụ na-eme ka akpụ ụkwụ gị sie ike.
examples.english: Football makes your thigh muscle strong.

gloss: a tree from where we get durable timber for wood work.

examples.igbo: Anyị ji osisi agba rụọ oche siri ike.
examples.english: We used agba wood to make a strong chair.

examples.igbo: Ebee ka agba ndị ahụ toro?
examples.english: Where did those agba trees grow?

note: Sense is clear; the tone marking of agba may vary locally.

gloss: be crooked, bent, winding, sinuous, tortuous Mkpịsị afù lò(lù) àlọ The spike is bent

examples.igbo: Osisi ahụ lọgọrọ n'akụkụ ụzọ.
examples.english: That tree is bent beside the road.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-alọgọ ma ị manye ya ike.
examples.english: It will bend if you force it.

note: Inflected forms lọgọrọ / ga-alọgọ follow the stem -lọgò, but tone on the suffix may differ.

gloss: expand; stretch to enlarge the gaps of a contracted or meshed material, especially a hard material like iron or wood

examples.igbo: O gbagara ígwè ahụ ka ọ baa n'oghere ahụ.
examples.english: He stretched the iron so it would fit into the hole.

examples.igbo: Gbaga ya ntakịrị ka osisi ahụ baa.
examples.english: Widen it a little so the wood fits in.

note: Sense is understood; a speaker might prefer gbapụta in some contexts.

examples.igbo: Anyị hụrụ mfịa arụ n'afọ gara aga.
examples.english: We experienced hardship last year.

examples.igbo: N'oge mfịa arụ, anyị na-eri ji na-edo.
examples.english: In times of want, we ate only cassava.

note: Both sentences are idiomatic; the exact tone pattern of mfịa arụ may vary.

gloss: cancel; indicate that what is written is no longer applicable, especially by drawing a line on it;

examples.igbo: O kàgburu aha ya na ndekọ ahụ.
examples.english: He cancelled his name in that register.

examples.igbo: Kàgbuo ọnụ ọgụgụ ahụ, o zighị ezi.
examples.english: Cancel that number, it is not correct.

note: The stem and meaning are sound; tone on the inflected form kàgburu may vary.

examples.igbo: Mmiri na-agbadata n'ǹdàlàgwùgwù ahụ mgbe ozuzo gasịrị.
examples.english: Water flows down into that valley after the rain.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ǹdàlàgwùgwù dị n'azụ ugwu ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see the valley behind that hill?

examples.igbo: Mkpùna na-egbu nna m mgbe ọ na-ebu ibu arọ.
examples.english: My father's hernia pains him when he carries a heavy load.

examples.igbo: Dọkịta gwọrọ mkpùna nwata ahụ n'ụlọ ọgwụ.
examples.english: The doctor treated that child's hernia at the hospital.

note: Sense is clear; mkpùna is often heard with slight tone variation.

examples.igbo: Nwanyị ahụ nwere ike ịmụkwo nwa.
examples.english: That woman may give birth prematurely.

examples.igbo: Ị na-atụ egwu ịmụkwo nwa?
examples.english: Are you afraid of giving birth prematurely?

note: Rare verb; used with infinitive.

examples.igbo: Nwa m na-amụ mgbàkwụnye n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: My child is learning about affixes at school.

examples.igbo: Ị maara ihe mgbàkwụnye pụtara?
examples.english: Do you know what an affix means?

examples.igbo: Anyị na-agọ Chineke n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: We worship God in the morning.

examples.igbo: Gọọ Chineke gị, kwesịkwa ntị n'okwu ya.
examples.english: Worship your God and obey his word.

gloss: to reset or fix a broken bone

examples.igbo: Dọkịta na-agba ọkpụkpụ nwa ahụ.
examples.english: The doctor is setting the child's bone.

examples.igbo: Gbaa ọkpụkpụ ya ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Reset his bone quickly.

examples.igbo: O jidere nwa ya n'ogwè akā.
examples.english: She held her child by the arm.

examples.igbo: Ogwè akā ya gbara ọkụ n'ọkụ ahụ.
examples.english: His arm was burnt in that fire.

gloss: draw in the mouth; pout; be envious

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-amì ọnụ mgbe a na-ata ya mba.
examples.english: The child pouts when he is scolded.

examples.igbo: Ị na-amì ọnụ maka ihe m nwere?
examples.english: Are you envious of what I have?

examples.igbo: Ụgwọ ụlọ akwụkwọ na-akpà anyị mkpà.
examples.english: School fees are causing us difficulty.

examples.igbo: Gịnị na-akpà gị mkpà ugbu a?
examples.english: What is pressing you now?

examples.igbo: O nwere ike ịlụkwa ụgbọala ahụ.
examples.english: He can repair that car.

examples.igbo: Lụkwaa ụlọ ahụ tupu mmiri abịa.
examples.english: Repair that house before the rain comes.

examples.igbo: Nchegbu ahụ na-achu m ụrā.
examples.english: That worry is causing me sleeplessness.

examples.igbo: Gịnị na-achu gị ụrā n'abalị a?
examples.english: What is causing you sleeplessness tonight?

gloss: to drive (a peg into the earth) Anà m èje ịkpọ  mkụkpọ n’okè mụ nà Ịbā I am going to put pegs along the boundary between Ịba and myself

examples.igbo: O kpọrọ mkpụkpọ n'ala.
examples.english: He drove a peg into the ground.

examples.igbo: Kpọọ mkpụkpọ ebe a iji gosi ókè.
examples.english: Drive a peg here to mark the boundary.

examples.igbo: Mmanụ ahụ larụrụ alarụ n'ite n'oge oyi.
examples.english: That oil congealed in the pot in the cold season.

examples.igbo: Mmanụ na-alarụ alarụ mgbe oyi na-atụ?
examples.english: Does oil congeal when it is cold?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-abịa ụlọ anyị ogè ǹcha.
examples.english: He comes to our house always.

examples.igbo: Ị na-aga ahịa ahụ ogè ǹcha?
examples.english: Do you go to that market always?

examples.igbo: Òzụzụ akwa dị oke ọnụ n'afọ a.
examples.english: Buying cloth is very expensive this year.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eme òzụzụ ma ọ bụ ire ere?
examples.english: Do you do buying or selling?

examples.igbo: O lụtara ọgụ maka nwanne ya nwoke.
examples.english: He fought for his brother.

examples.igbo: Lụta ọgụ maka ubi nna gị!
examples.english: Fight for your father's farm!

gloss: roadway; public path (less specific than okpolo īlo)

examples.igbo: Okpolo ụzò ahụ dị warara nke ukwuu.
examples.english: That roadway is very narrow.

examples.igbo: Ha na-arụ okpolo ụzọ ọhụrụ n'ime obodo?
examples.english: Are they building a new public path in the village?

gloss: shaky hand>> (e.g. some people cannot bear to inflict injury on other even in treatment, as in incision of abscess, injection, etc.)

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ nwere aka izizē, ọ naghị awa ọnya.
examples.english: That man has a shaky hand; he does not cut sores.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere aka izizē nke na ị pụghị ịgba ọgwụ?
examples.english: Do you have a shaky hand that you cannot give an injection?

examples.igbo: Nwanyị ahụ sụlụrụ ichafo ọhụrụ n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: That woman put on a new head-tie in the morning.

examples.igbo: Sụlụ ichafo gị tupu ị pụọ!
examples.english: Put on your head-tie before you go out!

examples.igbo: Nwa nnabè na-ada nke ọma na ndagwurugwu.
examples.english: The echo resounds well in the valley.

examples.igbo: Ị nụrụ nwa nnabè mgbe ị nọ n'okporo ụzọ?
examples.english: Did you hear the echo when you were on the road?

examples.igbo: Onye nkuzi kwara nzū n'ala tupu ọ kụzie ihe.
examples.english: The teacher marked the ground with chalk before teaching.

examples.igbo: Kaa nzū ebe a ka ụmụaka hụ ya!
examples.english: Mark chalk here so the children can see it!

gloss: perhaps; maybe; in case (literally one never knows)

examples.igbo: Adī àma āma ọ ga-abịa taa.
examples.english: Perhaps he will come today.

examples.igbo: Were mkpuchi, adī àma āma mmiri zoo.
examples.english: Take an umbrella, in case it rains.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-agaghalị n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: We are strolling in the market today.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji na-agaghalị n'ọhịa?
examples.english: Why are you wandering in the bush?

gloss: praying mantis (literally looking for a fight)

examples.igbo: Òchọògù nọ n'elu akwụkwọ osisi ahụ.
examples.english: A praying mantis is on the leaf of that tree.

examples.igbo: Ị hụla òchọògù n'ubi?
examples.english: Have you seen a praying mantis in the farm?

gloss: shift or move away, especially to create a gap or space

examples.igbo: Kpụmì ntakịrị ka m gafee.
examples.english: Move aside a little so I can pass.

examples.igbo: O kpụmịrị n'oche ya ka nwa ya nọdụ.
examples.english: He shifted on his seat so his child could sit.

examples.igbo: Ha na-akpokọ nkụ maka ọkụ.
examples.english: They are gathering firewood for the fire.

examples.igbo: Kpokọọ akwụkwọ gị niile.
examples.english: Gather all your books.

examples.igbo: O rịbara ama n'akpa ya iji mata ya.
examples.english: He marked his bag so as to identify it.

examples.igbo: Ị rịbara ama ebe ị kụrụ osisi?
examples.english: Did you mark where you planted the tree?

gloss: intestinal worm, very tiny; pinworm (literally ants of belly)

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ nwere arụrụ afō.
examples.english: That child has pinworm.

examples.igbo: Gịnị na-akpata arụrụ afō n'ụmụaka?
examples.english: What causes pinworm in children?

examples.igbo: Ezinụlọ ahụ rụrụ ụjụ ụbọchị asaa.
examples.english: That family mourned for seven days.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eru ụjụ maka nne gị?
examples.english: Are you grieving for your mother?

note: Tone marking on ụjụ̄ is uncertain; the verb form rụ ụjụ is what I have used.

examples.igbo: Ụgbọelu ahụ na-efefega elu obodo anyị.
examples.english: That airplane flies across over our town.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ụmụ nnụnụ na-efefega osimiri ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see the birds flying across that river?

gloss: name for a girl born into a wealthy family

examples.igbo: Aha nwa nwanyị ahụ bụ Òbìàgèèliàkù.
examples.english: That girl's name is Òbìàgèèliàkù.

examples.igbo: Òbìàgèèliàkù pụtara nwa a mụrụ n'ezinụlọ bara ọgaranya.
examples.english: Òbìàgèèliàkù means a child born into a wealthy family.

gloss: watery kind of soup very common among the Owere people

examples.igbo: Anyị riri ofe Òwèlè na fufu taa.
examples.english: We ate ofe Òwèlè with fufu today.

examples.igbo: Ị maara esi ofe Òwèlè?
examples.english: Do you know how to cook ofe Òwèlè?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ayatọ ọnụ mgbe ọ na-ekwu okwu.
examples.english: He is vulgar when he speaks.

examples.igbo: Ekwula okwu na-ayatọ ọnụ n'ihu ụmụaka.
examples.english: Don't speak vulgar words in front of children.

note: The verb form 'na-ayatọ ọnụ' is used, but I am not fully sure it is the most common way to express this sense.

examples.igbo: Agwọ ahụ gbefè n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: The snake crawled across the road.

examples.igbo: Nwa ọhụrụ na-agbefè n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: The baby is crawling around the room.

note: 'Gbefe' can mean crawl past or over; the second example is more 'crawl around' than 'past', but still illustrates the verb.

gloss: put aside; take out of the way

examples.igbo: Wèrụka akpa ahụ n'ùsọ.
examples.english: Put that bag aside.

examples.igbo: Ọ wèrụkara akwụkwọ ya n'ùsọ.
examples.english: He put his book aside.

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ na-eme isi ikē.
examples.english: That child is headstrong.

examples.igbo: Emela isi ikē n'ihu ndị okenye.
examples.english: Don't be headstrong in front of elders.

gloss: consider; take counsel; counsel; consult together; advise

examples.igbo: Anyị ralụrụ alò tupu anyị ekpebie.
examples.english: We took counsel before we decided.

examples.igbo: Ha na-aralụ alò banyere okwu ahụ.
examples.english: They are considering the matter.

gloss: to be a follower of African traditional religion

examples.igbo: Ọ na-efe arusị̄.
examples.english: He is a follower of African traditional religion.

examples.igbo: Ndị na-efe arusị̄ na-achụrụ arusị̄ àjà.
examples.english: Those who follow traditional religion sacrifice to idols.

note: The phrase is understood, but the second sentence is longer than ideal and the exact nuance of 'fe arusị̄' may vary.

examples.igbo: Bì akwụkwọ a maka m.
examples.english: Print this document for me.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-abì akwụkwọ n'ụlọ ọrụ.
examples.english: He prints documents at the office.

examples.igbo: Òŋụŋụ iyī na-ewe oge.
examples.english: Oath-taking takes time.

examples.igbo: Ha mere òŋụŋụ iyī n'ụlọ ikpe.
examples.english: They did oath-taking in the court.

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ toghàlụ uwe ya.
examples.english: That child has outgrown his clothes.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-atoghàlụ akpụkpọ ụkwụ ya ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: He outgrows his shoes quickly.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-abọsà ọka n'ubi tupu mmiri abịa.
examples.english: She is scattering maize in the farm before the rain comes.

examples.igbo: Bọsàa ọka ahụ n'ala ka ọ kpọọ nkụ.
examples.english: Scatter that maize on the ground so it dries.

examples.igbo: Ewu ahụ nwere mkpụlụ amù abụọ.
examples.english: That goat has two testicles.

examples.igbo: Ị hụla mkpụlụ amù ebule ahụ?
examples.english: Have you seen the ram's testicles?

examples.igbo: Òlaka mmanya ahụ na-abịa ebe a kwa ụbọchị.
examples.english: That drunkard comes here every day.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụghị òlaka mmanya; ọ na-aṅụ ntakịrị.
examples.english: He is not a drunkard; he drinks a little.

examples.igbo: Ọ nyere m aka ịkpofù ahịhịa n'ogige.
examples.english: She helped me to gather and throw away weeds in the garden.

examples.igbo: Kpofùa ihe mkpofu ahụ tupu mmiri abịa.
examples.english: Gather and throw away that refuse before the rain comes.

examples.igbo: Ọ kwuru okwu n'iru òrà n'ụlọ ahịa.
examples.english: He spoke in public at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-ekwu ya n'iru òrà n'ebe a?
examples.english: Will you say it publicly here?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-agwùsò nwa ya egwu n'ụlọ.
examples.english: She is playing with her child in the house.

examples.igbo: Gwùsò m egwu n'ebe a, biko.
examples.english: Play with me here, please.

examples.igbo: Nri ahụ zùrù ezù maka mmadụ niile.
examples.english: That food was sufficient for everybody.

examples.igbo: Ego a ezughị ezù ịzụta ọka?
examples.english: Is this money not enough to buy maize?

examples.igbo: Ọ tinyechara akwụkwọ ya niile n'akpa.
examples.english: She put all her books in the bag.

examples.igbo: Tinyecha akwụkwọ ndị a n'igbe ozugbo.
examples.english: Put all these books in the box at once.

examples.igbo: Ùgò mmā ahụ na-ere akị n'ahịa.
examples.english: That beautiful girl sells palm kernels at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị hụla ùgò mmā nọ n'ụlọ ahụ?
examples.english: Have you seen the beautiful girl in that house?

examples.igbo: Mmiri a jụrụ oyi nke ukwuu.
examples.english: This water is very cold.

examples.igbo: Nri a jụrụ oyi, tinye ya n'ọkụ.
examples.english: This food is cold, put it on the fire.

examples.igbo: Ụgbọ mmiri rutere n'ọdụ ụgbọ mmiri.
examples.english: The ship arrived at the port.

examples.igbo: Ndị ọrụ na-ebu ngwongwo n'ọdụ ụgbọ mmiri.
examples.english: Workers are carrying goods at the port.

examples.igbo: Efi Igbo dị ntakịrị ma sie ike.
examples.english: Dwarf cattle are small but strong.

examples.igbo: Onye ọrụ ugbo na-azụ efi Igbo n'ugbo ya.
examples.english: A farmer is rearing dwarf cattle on his farm.

gloss: cut, make, or have a significant mark on the body, especially tribal marks

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ dọrọ nkì n'ihu.
examples.english: That man has facial marks.

examples.igbo: Nna m dọrọ nkì n'aka nwa ya.
examples.english: My father made a mark on his child's hand.

examples.igbo: Anyị lịpụrụ n'ụgbọala na Aba.
examples.english: We alighted from the vehicle at Aba.

examples.igbo: Lịpụa n'ụgbọala tupu ọ gawa.
examples.english: Alight from the vehicle before it goes.

gloss: in circles Ọ nà-àgba kpelèkpelè It moves in circles

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-agba kpelèkpelè n'ama.
examples.english: The children are running in circles in the playground.

examples.igbo: Ụgbọala ahụ na-agba kpelèkpelè n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: That car is going in circles on the road.

examples.igbo: Anyị kwosịrị ugbene ọkụkọ ahụ.
examples.english: We plucked that fowl's feathers.

examples.igbo: Kwosịa ugbene ọkụkọ tupu ị sie ya.
examples.english: Pluck the fowl's feathers before you cook it.

examples.igbo: Iru anyanwụ na-achasi ike taa.
examples.english: The sun is shining brightly today.

examples.igbo: Anyị nọ n'okpuru osisi n'ihi iru anyanwụ.
examples.english: We are under the tree because of the sun.

examples.igbo: Ọ gbachara afele ya.
examples.english: He cleaned his plate.

examples.igbo: Gbachaa afele gị tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Clean your plate before you leave.

examples.igbo: Nwa m mụtara ngwaa taa.
examples.english: My child learned about verbs today.

examples.igbo: Onye nkuzi kọwara anyị ngwaa.
examples.english: The teacher explained verbs to us.

examples.igbo: Ha kwapụrụ ngwongwo niile n'ụlọ ahịa.
examples.english: They cleared all the goods out of the shop.

examples.igbo: Kwapụ ihe niile n'ụlọ tupu ndị ọbịa abịa.
examples.english: Clear everything in the house before the guests arrive.

gloss: be dedicated to a spirit by taking its name

examples.igbo: E zara nwa ahụ mmụọ osimiri, a na-akpọ ya Osimiri.
examples.english: That child was dedicated to the river spirit, she is called Osimiri.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-aza mmụọ nna gị?
examples.english: Will you be dedicated to your father's spirit?

note: The phrase is culturally specific; the second sentence is shorter and less explicit about taking the spirit's name.

examples.igbo: Atụmatụ anyị ghọrọ n'ihi enweghị ego.
examples.english: Our plan failed because of lack of money.

examples.igbo: Azụmahịa ya ọ̀ ghọrọ n'afọ a?
examples.english: Did his business fail this year?

note: The verb is less common in everyday speech; the intended sense is 'fail/go wrong'.

examples.igbo: Ha zụchara akwụkwọ nri niile n'ahịa.
examples.english: They bought up all the vegetables in the market.

examples.igbo: Zụchaa osikapa tupu ọnụ ahịa arịgo.
examples.english: Finish buying the rice before the price rises.

gloss: walk through a jam-packed (bush inclusive) space using random free spaces

examples.igbo: Ọ piogharịrị n'etiti ìgwè mmadụ ahụ.
examples.english: He walked through that crowd.

examples.igbo: Piogharịa n'ọhịa ahụ, anyị ga-erute ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Walk through that bush, we will arrive quickly.

note: The verb is somewhat specialized; the imperative form piogharịa is given as a plausible command form.

examples.igbo: O nyere nwa ya òdìdè ka ọ nọdụ.
examples.english: She gave her child a small stool to sit on.

examples.igbo: Bute òdìdè maka ọbịa ahụ.
examples.english: Bring a small stool for that guest.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-echekwa iwe megide nwanne ya.
examples.english: He bears malice against his brother.

examples.igbo: Echekwala iwe, gbaghara nwanne gị tupu ọ gaa.
examples.english: Do not bear malice, forgive your brother before he leaves.

examples.igbo: Akwụkwo osisi ahụ na-acha ògùlù n'oge ọkọchị.
examples.english: The leaves of that tree are yellow in the dry season.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ụgbọ ala na-acha ògùlù?
examples.english: Did you see a yellow car?

headword: ànì ọnà ọcha nà ọnā èdò

examples.igbo: Ndị njem ahụ chọrọ ànì ọnà ọcha nà ọnā èdò.
examples.english: Those travelers sought the land of gold and silver.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-aga ànì ọnà ọcha nà ọnā èdò?
examples.english: Will you go to the land of gold and silver?

note: This is a literary or biblical-sounding phrase; the examples are constructed to show the given meaning.

examples.igbo: Mbòcha mere ka ọ jụọ ọtụtụ ajụjụ.
examples.english: Curiosity made him ask many questions.

examples.igbo: Ejila mbòcha gị tinye aka n'ihe na-emetụtaghị gị.
examples.english: Don't use your curiosity to meddle in what doesn't concern you.

examples.igbo: O tinyere ntụ egbè n’ime egbe ya.
examples.english: He put gunpowder inside his gun.

examples.igbo: Ebee ka ha zụtara ntụ egbè?
examples.english: Where did they buy gunpowder?

examples.igbo: O gbanyere onì n’ubi ji ya.
examples.english: He drove a big stake into his yam farm.

examples.igbo: Olee ebe ị gbanyere onì?
examples.english: Where did you drive the stake?

note: The yam-stake term is less common; 'onì' is used here in its agricultural sense.

examples.igbo: O nwere obì ọjọō n’ebe nwanne ya nọ.
examples.english: He has ill-will toward his brother.

examples.igbo: Wepụ obì ọjọō n’obi gị.
examples.english: Remove malice from your heart.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-emegide nne ya mgbe niile.
examples.english: She always acts against her mother.

examples.igbo: Emegidela iwu obodo.
examples.english: Do not act against the law of the land.

examples.igbo: Ụkwụ ya tụnụdoro n’ụdọ.
examples.english: His foot got entangled in a rope.

examples.igbo: Ị tụnụdoro ụkwụ n’ụdọ?
examples.english: Did you entangle your foot in the rope?

note: The verb is less common; the inflected forms given are my best reconstruction.

examples.igbo: Ikeē Chukwu mere ka ọ gbakee.
examples.english: The power of God made him recover.

examples.igbo: Onye pụrụ imeri Ikeē Chukwu?
examples.english: Who can overcome the power of God?

examples.igbo: Ọgò nwaàyì m bịara n’ụlọ anyị ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: My mother-in-law came to our house yesterday.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-aga ileta ọgò nwaàyì gị?
examples.english: Will you go and visit your mother-in-law?

examples.igbo: Ọkụ sulere osisi ahụ.
examples.english: Fire burnt that wood.

examples.igbo: Ọkụ sulere ubi gị?
examples.english: Did fire burn your farm?

note: The verb '-sule' is not very common; I am reasonably but not fully certain of its inflection.

examples.igbo: O banyere n’okwu anyị n’etiti nzukọ.
examples.english: He joined our discussion during the meeting.

examples.igbo: Abanyela n’okwu ndị okenye.
examples.english: Do not intervene in elders’ discussion.

gloss: disgust; be ugly to; be ugly (e.g. faeces or jagged ulcer)

examples.igbo: Ọnyà ahụ na-asọ oyī.
examples.english: That sore is disgusting.

examples.igbo: Ihe ahụ ọ na-asọ oyī?
examples.english: Does that thing look disgusting?

gloss: to pray using the ọfọ, a symbol of authority or kingship among Igbo people

examples.igbo: Nna ochie gọrọ ọfọ maka udo obodo.
examples.english: The grandfather prayed with the ọfọ for the peace of the town.

examples.igbo: Gọọ ọfọ tupu ị banye n'ụlọ eze.
examples.english: Pray with the ọfọ before you enter the king's house.

note: The verb gọ with ọfọ is traditional; inflection gọrọ/gọọ is given as standard modern usage.

examples.igbo: Dàalụkwọ nù, ndị nọ n'ụlọ a.
examples.english: I greet you all, those in this house.

examples.igbo: Dàalụkwọ nù, unu abịala n'oge.
examples.english: I greet you all, you have come on time.

note: The entry is a fixed greeting phrase; examples keep it as a salutation.

gloss: camwood (dye-wood from the tree Baphia nitida Lodd. or

examples.igbo: O ji uhie tee akwa ọcha.
examples.english: She used camwood to dye the white cloth.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara uhie n'ahịa taa?
examples.english: Did you buy camwood at the market today?

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ nwa nke abụọ n'ezinụlọ anyị.
examples.english: She is the second child in our family.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-ewere nke abụọ?
examples.english: Will you take the second one?

note: Examples use the standard spelling nke abụọ for the entry's ǹke àbùa.

examples.igbo: Iru igwe taa dị ọcha.
examples.english: The sky is clear today.

examples.igbo: Lelee iru igwe tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Look at the sky before you go out.

examples.igbo: O nyere m aka na ntị banyere ụzọ.
examples.english: He gave me a warning about the road.

examples.igbo: Nụrụ aka na ntị ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: Listen to that warning well.

note: The standard modern form is aka na ntị; entry akanantị̀ is treated as a variant.

gloss: paying Anà m àbịa ịkwụ  onye ọ bụnà dịkà ọlụ yā sìlì dị I am coming to pay everyone according to his work Ibì egō adā àdị ọlọ  kà òkwụkwụ yā Borrowing money is not usually as difficult as repaying it

examples.igbo: Òkwụkwụ ụgwọ ụlọ na-ewe m oge.
examples.english: Paying the house rent takes my time.

examples.igbo: Òkwụkwụ ego ahụ dị mfe, ọ bụghị?
examples.english: The repayment of that money is easy, isn't it?

note: The noun òkwụkwụ is used here in the sense of paying or repaying.

examples.igbo: Hicha tebụl ahụ ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Wipe that table quickly.

examples.igbo: Ọ hichara efere niile n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: She wiped all the plates in the morning.

examples.igbo: Òzàlà tara nwa m n'ụkwụ n'ụtụtụ taa.
examples.english: A scorpion stung my child on the foot this morning.

examples.igbo: Lee òzàlà ka ọ na-aga n'okpuru nkume ahụ!
examples.english: Look at the scorpion going under that stone!

examples.igbo: Ụlọikpe mara ya ìkpe maka izu ohi.
examples.english: The court found him guilty of stealing.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji maa nwa gị ìkpe n'ihu mmadụ niile?
examples.english: Why did you condemn your child in front of everybody?

gloss: hunter (iv) snap (with sharp sound); spring up (as corn) with a popping sound, as when roasting

examples.igbo: Ògba nta gbara nnụnụ n'ọhịa taa.
examples.english: The hunter shot a bird in the bush today.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ògba nta n'ụzọ ahịa?
examples.english: Did you see the hunter on the market road?

examples.igbo: Àchì na-achì n'ime ahịhịa abalị niile.
examples.english: Crickets chirp in the grass all night.

examples.igbo: Gịnị na-achì n'akụkụ ụlọ ahụ?
examples.english: What is chirping beside that house?

note: I am not fully certain of the noun form àchì for cricket; the verb on-achì is well attested.

examples.igbo: Nna m kwọchara isi ugbu a.
examples.english: My father is bald now.

examples.igbo: Ị kwọchara isi dị ka nwanne gị nwoke?
examples.english: Are you bald like your brother?

note: The verb is usually heard with the perfect form kwọchara isi.

examples.igbo: O ji ntu dụgbuo osisi ahụ.
examples.english: He pierced that wood with an awl.

examples.igbo: Gịnị dụgburu bọọlụ anyị?
examples.english: What pierced our ball?

gloss: width; breadth; state or quality of being wide or broad

examples.igbo: Abadaba ụlọ a dị mita ise.
examples.english: The width of this house is five metres.

examples.igbo: Gịnị bụ abadaba ubi gị?
examples.english: What is the width of your farm?

examples.igbo: Ha na-adọ ǹdùdò banyere ego ahụ.
examples.english: They are arguing about that money.

examples.igbo: Gịnị ka unu na-adọ ǹdùdò?
examples.english: What are you arguing about?

examples.igbo: Ha tụkọtara ahịhịa ahụ n'otu ebe.
examples.english: They heaped the grass together in one place.

examples.igbo: Tụkọta osisi ndị ahụ ọnụ tupu abalị daa.
examples.english: Heap those sticks together before night falls.

gloss: wear, tie wrapper, be dressed in wrapper

examples.igbo: O mara ògòdò ọhụrụ gaa ahịa.
examples.english: She tied a new wrapper and went to the market.

examples.igbo: Mara ògòdò gị, anyị na-aga ahịa.
examples.english: Tie your wrapper, we are going to the market.

examples.igbo: Ụzọ ahụ na-agba ngìlìgò n'ime ọhịa.
examples.english: That road winds in the forest.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ụzọ a ji agba ngìlìgò?
examples.english: Why does this road wind?

examples.igbo: Nnyagò nke ụzọ ahụ na-egbu oge anyị.
examples.english: The crookedness of that road delays us.

examples.igbo: Lee nnyagò nke osisi a!
examples.english: Look at the crookedness of this tree!

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka gbago n'elu ugwu ahụ.
examples.english: The children ran up that hill.

examples.igbo: Gbago n'elu ụlọ were lee anya.
examples.english: Climb up on the roof and look.

examples.igbo: M zụtara ọ̀kọwookwū Igbo ọhụrụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: I bought a new Igbo dictionary at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere ọ̀kọwookwū Bekee?
examples.english: Do you have an English dictionary?

examples.igbo: Mmiri na-ezo ajō ọlụ n'abalị a.
examples.english: It rained very hard tonight.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji na-arụ ọrụ ajō ọlụ?
examples.english: Why do you work so hard?

gloss: the last time; at last; finally

examples.igbo: Ogē ìkpe āzụ anyị zutere bụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: The last time we met was at the market.

examples.igbo: Ogē ìkpe āzụ ị hụrụ ya bụ olee?
examples.english: When was the last time you saw him?

examples.igbo: Anyị na-agba ùtụtù tupu anyị aga ọrụ.
examples.english: We eat breakfast before we go to work.

examples.igbo: Gbaa ùtụtù ngwa ngwa, anyị na-apụ ugbua.
examples.english: Eat breakfast quickly, we are leaving now.

gloss: resemble in behaviour; behave in exactly the same way as another person

examples.igbo: Nwa a na-eli obì nna ya.
examples.english: This child behaves like his father.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eli obì nne gị?
examples.english: Do you behave like your mother?

examples.igbo: Oke ōlili na-egbu ya n'ụkwụ.
examples.english: Great pain is killing him in the leg.

examples.igbo: Ị na-enwe oke ōlili mgbe ị dara?
examples.english: Do you feel great pain when you fall?

gloss: twelfth month of the traditional Nri calender, devoted to rituals and offerings to the alūsị and to wrestling matches and dances before the temples

examples.igbo: N'Ọnwa Uzo Alūsị, ndị Nri na-achụ aja.
examples.english: In Ọnwa Uzo Alụsị, the Nri people offer sacrifice.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-aga egwu n'Ọnwa Uzo Alūsị?
examples.english: Will you go to the dance in Ọnwa Uzo Alụsị?

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ nwere isi awelē n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: That man was lucky at the market today.

examples.igbo: Nwee isi awelē n'ụzọ gị.
examples.english: Have good luck on your journey.

examples.igbo: N'oge ọkọchị, ala anyị na-aghọ àkọlọ.
examples.english: In the dry season, our land becomes dry.

examples.igbo: Ala ebe a bụ àkọlọ ma ọ bụ ala mmiri?
examples.english: Is this land dry land or wetland?

note: Àkọlọ is a rarer word for dry ground; the sentences are sound but a speaker might use 'ala kpọrọ nkụ' instead.

examples.igbo: Ha wulitere ndụmì ụlọ ahụ taa.
examples.english: They put up the roof framework of that house today.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ndụmì ụlọ ọhụrụ ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see the roof framework of that new house?

examples.igbo: Àrụ ōlulo gbụrụ m mgbe m rụchara ọrụ ugbo.
examples.english: Weariness overcame me after I finished the farm work.

examples.igbo: Ị na-enwe àrụ ōlulo mgbe ị lọtara n'ọrụ?
examples.english: Do you feel weariness when you come back from work?

gloss: pumpkin (Cucurbita pepo Linn. and C. maxima Duchesne)

examples.igbo: Mama m zụtara ụgbògùlù abụọ n'ahịa.
examples.english: My mother bought two pumpkins at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-esi ụgbògùlù a taa?
examples.english: Will you cook this pumpkin today?

gloss: dwell in a house till it is old

examples.igbo: Ha biri n'ụlọ ahụ, bikaa ya.
examples.english: They lived in that house until it grew old.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ ibika ụlọ a tupu ị kwaga?
examples.english: Do you want to live in this house till it is old before you move?

examples.english: Don't let that stick bend.

examples.english: Our teacher beats the ùdù pot while the children sing.

examples.igbo: Ndị nwoke ahụ sụrụ ùdù n'ememme ahụ.
examples.english: Those men beat the ùdù pot at that festival.

note: The verb for playing the ùdù pot is usually sụ ùdù; both sentences follow that usage.

examples.igbo: Ọ kpachibidoro ya n'ụlọ abalị ahụ.
examples.english: She locked him in the house that night.

examples.igbo: Kpachibido ụzọ ụlọ tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Lock the door of the house before you leave.

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ butere ògbakasị n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: That child caught chickenpox at school.

examples.igbo: Dọkịta kwuru na ọ bụ ògbakasị.
examples.english: The doctor said it was chickenpox.

examples.igbo: Afọ abụọ gara aga ka anyị lụrụ.
examples.english: We married two years ago.

examples.igbo: Ọnwa ole gara aga ka ọ bịara?
examples.english: How many months ago did he come?

examples.igbo: Akpụ mmiri na-agbazè n'anyanwụ.
examples.english: Ice melts in the sun.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-agbazè shuga n'ime tii?
examples.english: Will you dissolve sugar in the tea?

note: Both sentences use agbazè in the sense of melting/dissolving; the second is slightly less common but idiomatic.

gloss: be careful, warned, cautious, beware; take heed (literally clear way for sight)

examples.igbo: Kpachalụ anya n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: Be careful on the road.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akpachalụ anya mgbe ọ na-akwọ ụgbọala.
examples.english: He is careful when driving.

note: Kpachalụ anya is treated as the inflected form of the headword; the more common variant is kpachara anya.

examples.igbo: Netị anya n'ụzọ ka ị hụ ebe ị na-aga.
examples.english: Look ahead on the road so you see where you are going.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-enetị anya mgbe ọ na-akwọ ụgbọala.
examples.english: He looks ahead when he is driving.

examples.igbo: Nne m na-esi nni ògbàdụ n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: My mother cooks agidi in the morning.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eri nni ògbàdụ na ofe?
examples.english: Will you eat agidi with soup?

note: Nni ògbàdụ is a kind of agidi; the food is common in ordinary meals.

gloss: go astray; err; get lost when walking, travelling

examples.igbo: Nwatakịrị ahụ jefuru n'ahịa.
examples.english: That child got lost in the market.

examples.igbo: Ị jefuru n'ụzọ mgbe ị na-abịa?
examples.english: Did you get lost on the way when coming?

gloss: stay in expectation of someone or something; wait

examples.igbo: Che m obere oge.
examples.english: Wait for me a little while.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-eche ụgbọala n'ebe nkwụsị.
examples.english: We are waiting for the bus at the stop.

gloss: pass away; blow over as the wind

examples.igbo: Oke ifufe kùfèrè èkufè n'ime obodo.
examples.english: A strong wind blew over in the town.

examples.igbo: Nna nna ya kùfèrè èkufè n'afọ gara aga.
examples.english: His grandfather passed away last year.

note: The first sentence uses the wind sense; the second uses the euphemistic sense of passing away.

examples.igbo: Nnweju akā nri dị n'ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: There is enough food in our house.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere nnweju akā ego maka njem?
examples.english: Do you have enough money for the journey?

gloss: small private room (= ụnò ime ụnò)

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ehi ụra n'ụnò ọbā.
examples.english: He sleeps in the small private room.

examples.igbo: Nye m ụnò ọbā ka m gbanwee uwe.
examples.english: Give me the small private room so I can change clothes.

examples.igbo: Panite aka gị elu ka m hụ gị.
examples.english: Lift up your hand so I see you.

examples.igbo: O panitere igbe ahụ n'ala ozugbo.
examples.english: He lifted that box from the ground immediately.

note: Less common verb; examples use the literal sense 'lift up'.

examples.igbo: Nna m na-aga nta n'oké ọhịa.
examples.english: My father goes hunting in the big forest.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-aga nta n'oké ọhịa taa?
examples.english: Will you go hunting in the big forest today?

gloss: measure (a quantity, e.g. salt or beans with cup, etc.)

examples.igbo: Maa ọka ahụ n'ime iko a.
examples.english: Measure that corn into this cup.

examples.igbo: O jiri iko maa mmanụ ahụ.
examples.english: She used a cup to measure that oil.

note: Tone and inflection of -mà can vary; examples use the measure sense.

gloss: group of seven villages in Anambra Division which speak Igala as their first language

examples.igbo: Olumbànasā bụ obodo asaa dị n'Anambra.
examples.english: Olumbanasa is seven villages in Anambra.

examples.igbo: Ndị Olumbànasā na-asụ Igala dịka asụsụ mbụ ha.
examples.english: The Olumbanasa people speak Igala as their first language.

note: Proper place-name; examples follow the given description.

examples.igbo: Ọ tụrụ aka n'ejù isī ya.
examples.english: He touched the top of his skull.

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ nwere ọnya n'ejù isī ya.
examples.english: That child has a sore on the top of his skull.

examples.igbo: Nwanne m nọ na kọleèjì ugbu a.
examples.english: My sister is in college now.

examples.igbo: Kọleèjì ọhụrụ ahụ mepere n'isi obodo ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: That new college opened in the capital yesterday.

examples.igbo: O kọsara ndị uweojii mkpesa ya.
examples.english: He laid his complaint to the police.

examples.igbo: Biko kọsara anyị ihe merenụ nke ọma.
examples.english: Please tell us what happened clearly.

examples.english: There is a wasps' nest on that tree.

examples.igbo: Àkpa èbù ahụ dara n'ala na mberede.
examples.english: That wasps' nest fell to the ground suddenly.

examples.english: We hold this feast yearly.

examples.igbo: Kwà arò, ọ na-aga obodo nna ya.
examples.english: Every year, he goes to his father's village.

gloss: girl friend; woman friend; female friend

examples.igbo: Enyi nwaanyị m bịara n'ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: My female friend came to our house.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere enyi nwaanyị n'ebe a?
examples.english: Do you have a female friend here?

gloss: blow air, especially from the mouth, to remove dirt or chaff; blow off

examples.igbo: O fụ̀chàrà ájá n’anya nwa ya.
examples.english: She blew sand out of her child’s eye.

examples.igbo: Fụchaa ntụ ahụ n’elu tebụl tupu ị bịa.
examples.english: Blow the ash off the table before you come.

examples.igbo: Ọkà okwu ahụ kwuru ụkà banyere ụmụaka.
examples.english: That speaker gave a speech about children.

examples.igbo: Ị nụrụ ụkà ahụ e kwuru n’ụtụtụ?
examples.english: Did you hear the talk that was given in the morning?

examples.igbo: Okōkòòko! Ụkwụ m na-egbu m mgbu.
examples.english: Ouch! My leg is paining me.

examples.igbo: Okōkòòko! Gịnị mere i ji daa n’ala?
examples.english: Oh! Why did you fall down?

note: The exclamation is clear, but its tone marking varies in print.

examples.igbo: Kwụpụ̀ọ plọg ahụ n’oghere tupu ọkụ abịa.
examples.english: Unplug that plug from the socket before electricity comes.

examples.igbo: O kwụpụ̀rụ waya ahụ na igwe ahụ.
examples.english: He disconnected that wire from the machine.

examples.igbo: Etùm juru n’ikuku mgbe anyị na-aga ahịa.
examples.english: Dust filled the air when we were going to market.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ etùm ahụ na-ebili n’okporo ụzọ?
examples.english: Did you see that dust rising on the road?

gloss: steal fowls (habitually, mainly for eating) (literally draw and eat)

examples.english: Nwanna habitually steals fowls in this village.

examples.igbo: Kwụsị ịsèli òkụkù ndị agbata obi!
examples.english: Stop stealing the neighbors’ fowls!

examples.english: His great wisdom made him settle that quarrel.

examples.igbo: Ndị okenye na-eji oke àmàmife edozi okwu obodo.
examples.english: Elders use great wisdom to settle town matters.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akọfịa ahụ ya n'ihi ọnya ahụ.
examples.english: He is scratching his body because of the sore.

examples.igbo: Kọfịa akwụkwọ osisi ahụ n'ahụ osisi.
examples.english: Pick off that leaf from the tree.

examples.english: He caught a rat in a trap in my father's farm.

examples.igbo: Ị kọdoro azụ n'ụgbụ n'osimiri taa?
examples.english: Did you catch fish with a net in the river today?

examples.english: The breaking of that tree damaged our house.

examples.english: He snatched the book from my hand.

examples.igbo: Gachata ya n'aka nwata ahụ ozugbo!
examples.english: Snatch it from that child immediately!

examples.igbo: Ọ makọrọ akwa ahụ n'ime akpa.
examples.english: She compressed the cloth into the bag.

examples.igbo: Ị makọrọ mpempe akwụkwọ abụọ ahụ ọnụ?
examples.english: Did you press the two papers together?

examples.igbo: Onye òrà ahụ bịara n'ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: That visitor came to our house.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ onye òrà ahụ n'ọhịa?
examples.english: Did you see that stranger in the bush?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-esèlụ oche ahụ n'akụkụ ya.
examples.english: He pulls the chair to himself.

examples.igbo: Sèlụ eriri ahụ n'akụkụ gị.
examples.english: Pull the rope to yourself.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ ife èbùbè na ọ bịara n'oge.
examples.english: It is a wonder that he came on time.

examples.igbo: Ị hụtụla ife èbùbè dị otú a?
examples.english: Have you seen a wonder like this?

gloss: be dark; get dark; grow dark; have no lit vision due to absence of light, especially an environment

examples.english: When it got dark, we returned home.

examples.english: The house is dark because there is no light.

examples.english: Is water flowing into that hole?

examples.english: Did you see the soldier at the door?

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ǹkwọ ji dị n'ime mmiri?

examples.english: Snap off that branch before it falls.

note: The inflected form kpàjipụrụ is used; tone on the final syllable may vary by dialect.

gloss: fix gaze or point light continuously on something

examples.english: She fixed her gaze on the baby.

examples.igbo: Chàdo ọkụ ebe a ka m hụ ihe.
examples.english: Point the light here so I can see.

note: chàdo is uncommon; the examples show its sense of fixing gaze or directing light.

gloss: part of tree (split from the main body)

examples.english: He used a piece of wood to make a chair.

examples.igbo: Ebee ka ibe osisi a si pụta?
examples.english: Where did this piece of wood come from?

gloss: be forbidden, illegal, forbidden by law

examples.english: Hunting in this forest is forbidden.

examples.igbo: Ị ma na ọ dị n'ìwu ịkụ azụ n'osimiri a?
examples.english: Do you know it is illegal to fish in this river?

examples.igbo: Ị ga-agba mgba n'asọmpi echi?

examples.igbo: Ị mụrụ mbọ n'ahụ ya?

gloss: make low mud wall, usually on farm, to mark boundary and/or check erosion

examples.igbo: Ị tiri ekpè n'akụkụ ubi gị?

note: ekpè refers specifically to a low mud boundary or erosion-check wall on farmland.

examples.igbo: Pana ji ndị a n'ụlọ taa.
examples.english: Take these yams home today.

examples.igbo: Ònye sụgburu ọkụkọ m n'abalị ụnyaahụ?
examples.english: Who stabbed my chicken to death last night?

examples.english: People gathered at the market this morning.

examples.igbo: Gbakọọnụ n'okpuru osisi ahụ tupu mmiri ezoo.
examples.english: Gather under that tree before it starts raining.

gloss: untie; shake off; shake oneself free of

examples.english: The child shook himself free from his mother's hand.

examples.igbo: Rụpụ mmiri ahụ n'ahụ gị.
examples.english: Shake the water off your body.

examples.igbo: O kwuru okwu ògbòdì n'ihu ndị ọbịa.
examples.english: He spoke like a fool in front of the guests.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji akpọ m ògbòdì?

examples.english: There is no need to dispute this matter.

examples.igbo: Mmiri na-abụsa ntakịrị n'ụtụtụ taa.
examples.english: It is drizzling lightly this morning.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụsara mmiri ntakịrị n'abalị ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: It drizzled a little last night.

gloss: plan; two or more people thinking out how to approach something

examples.igbo: Ndị okenye gbara izu banyere oriri ahụ.
examples.english: The elders planned about that feast.

examples.igbo: Ò unu gbara izu maka njem ahụ?
examples.english: Have you planned about that journey?

gloss: Sarcophrynium spp.; of leaf with smooth surface much used in wrapping food and kola nuts

examples.english: My mother uses akwụkwọ ūma leaf to wrap kola nut.

examples.igbo: Ebee ka m ga-azụta akwụkwọ ūma?
examples.english: Where will I buy akwụkwọ ūma leaf?

examples.english: He put a new yam in place of that old one.

examples.igbo: Gịnị ka anyị ga-eji tinyechi osikapa ahụ?
examples.english: What shall we use to replace that rice?

examples.igbo: Ùgònàchọmmā bụ mmọnwụ a na-ahụ n'ememme.
examples.english: Ugonachomma is a masquerade seen at festivals.

examples.igbo: Ị hụla Ùgònàchọmmā ka ọ na-agba egwu?
examples.english: Have you seen Ugonachomma dancing?

examples.igbo: Okeòsìmìrì na-ebe n'akụkụ obodo anyị.
examples.english: The sea roars near our town.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-aga okeòsìmìrì ịzụ azụ echi?
examples.english: Will you go to the sea to buy fish tomorrow?

examples.igbo: Ọ dùgara nne ya gaa ahịa.
examples.english: She accompanied her mother to the market.

examples.igbo: Dùga nwanne gị gaa ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: Accompany your sibling to school.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-alụ àrụ ụkà mgbe ụmụaka na-eme mkpọtụ.
examples.english: He is self-controlled when children make noise.

examples.igbo: Lụọ àrụ ụkà, ewela iwe.
examples.english: Be self-controlled, don't be angry.

gloss: examination malpractice; expo; cheating in examination

examples.igbo: Ụmụ akwụkwọ na-eme m̀pụūlē n'ule.
examples.english: Students cheat in exams.

examples.igbo: Emeela m̀pụūlē n'ule gị.
examples.english: Don't cheat in your exam.

examples.igbo: Ụdà ọfīa na-eto n'oké ọhịa.
examples.english: The wild ụdà grows in the deep forest.

examples.igbo: Ị maara osisi ụdà ọfīa?
examples.english: Do you know the wild ụdà tree?

gloss: have distended abdomen like that of ascitic or overfed child

examples.english: The child's abdomen is distended after eating.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ahụ ka afọ ya tepùlù?
examples.english: Do you see how his abdomen is distended?

examples.igbo: Osisi kpọrọ nkụ na-ese n'elu mmiri.
examples.english: Dry wood floats on water.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ese n'elu mmiri ma ọ bụ na ọ na-emikpu?
examples.english: Does it float on water or sink?

examples.igbo: Isì ọma na-esi n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: A pleasant scent comes from inside the room.

examples.igbo: Ị na-anụ isì nri?
examples.english: Can you smell the aroma of food?

examples.igbo: Nwunye di m bụ ezigbo mmadụ.
examples.english: My co-wife is a good person.

examples.igbo: Nwunye di gị ọ na-akwado gị?
examples.english: Does your co-wife support you?

examples.igbo: Bịa kpụdèbè ǹso ka anyị kwurịta ihe ahụ.
examples.english: Come nearer so we can discuss that matter.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka kpụdèbèrè ǹso ebe nne ha nọ.
examples.english: The children drew near where their mother was.

note: The phrase is somewhat uncommon; I am fairly confident in the meaning, but the inflection may vary.

gloss: pounded palm nut fibre left after removal of kernels

examples.english: My mother removed the kernels from the pounded palm-nut fibre.

examples.english: The pounded palm-nut fibre remained under where palm nuts are cracked.

note: The term is specialised; the examples are plausible but I would check with a native speaker.

examples.igbo: Òdògwùmà na-egwu mmiri n'ọdọ mmiri.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka chụrụ òdògwùmà gaa n'ụlọ ọkụkọ.
examples.english: The children chased the duck to the chicken coop.

note: The word for duck varies by dialect; òdògwùmà is understood but ọbọgwụ is more common in some areas.

examples.igbo: Onye isi kụrụ ògenè, ụmụ akwụkwọ gbakọtara.
examples.english: The headteacher struck the gong, and the students gathered.

examples.english: Strike the gong so the workers come to the meeting.

examples.english: Where did you buy the sewing machine?

examples.english: Preservation of food is important in the dry season.

examples.igbo: E ji nnu eme nchebe azụ.
examples.english: Salt is used to preserve fish.

gloss: tall tree with bole up to 3-4' in diameter (Hannoa klaineana Pierre and Engl.). It is fast-growing; the wood is light and white and used for planks, canoes, etc. Medicinally the back is used for curing fevers (ịbà) by soaking pieces of it in water for some days and drinking the water, and by other ways of preparation

examples.igbo: Oghùlù toro ogologo n'akụkụ ubi anyị.
examples.english: The oghulu tree grew tall beside our farm.

examples.igbo: A na-eji osisi oghùlù arụ ụgbọ mmiri.

examples.english: Pasteurize that water before you drink it.

note: Verb formation is plausible; usage may be technical.
