examples.igbo: Ị ma ndịǹkè nya nke ọma?
examples.english: Do you know his own people well?

examples.igbo: O dọrọ mbọ n'aka nwanne ya.
examples.english: He scratched his brother's hand with nails.

examples.igbo: E dọla mbọ n'ihu nwa ahụ.
examples.english: Don't scratch that child's face with nails.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ejechi anya n'ọrụ ya.
examples.english: He is punctual at his work.

examples.igbo: Jechi anya, ma ọ bụghị anyị ga-ahapụ gị.
examples.english: Be punctual, otherwise we will leave you.

examples.igbo: Anyị zụtara gbiìgbiì abụọ n'ahịa.
examples.english: We bought two catfish at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ gbiìgbiì buru ibu n'osimiri?
examples.english: Did you see a big catfish in the river?

gloss: read more (of) Ọ chò ịmùkwù akwụkwọ She wants to study further

examples.igbo: Ọ chọrọ ịmụkwụ akwụkwọ n'ụlọ akwụkwọ ukwu.
examples.english: She wants to study further at the university.

examples.igbo: Mụkwụ akwụkwọ gị tupu ị gaa ahịa.
examples.english: Read more of your book before you go to the market.

gloss: slap the face with the open hand

examples.igbo: O mara ya ùla n'ihu mmadụ niile.
examples.english: He slapped him in front of everybody.

examples.igbo: A mara ya ùla n'ahịa.
examples.english: He was slapped at the market.

examples.igbo: Ngwa ahịa ndị a gbasàsịrị n'ahịa.
examples.english: These goods are scattered in the market.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ha ji gbasàsịrị n'ahịa?
examples.english: Why are they scattered in the market?

note: The inflected form gbasàsịrị is used for the stative/past sense.

examples.igbo: E ji òsè dọọ ibu ahụ n'elu ụlọ.
examples.english: They used a pulley to pull that load up to the roof.

examples.igbo: Òsè a adọghị arọ; dochie ya.
examples.english: This pulley is not pulling well; replace it.

gloss: swell and fill (a receptacle); heal up (of wound)

examples.igbo: Mmiri ozuzo rịchiri ite ahụ ruo ọnụ.
examples.english: Rainwater filled that pot to the brim.

examples.igbo: Ọnya n'ụkwụ ya ọ rịchiela?
examples.english: Has the wound on his leg healed?

examples.igbo: Ụbà o nwetara n'ahịa bụ otu puku naira.
examples.english: The commission he got at the market was one thousand naira.

examples.igbo: Ị na-enweta ụbà ole n'azụmahịa a?
examples.english: How much commission do you get in this business?

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka ahụ na-asụ Igbo nke ọma.
examples.english: Those children speak Igbo well.

examples.igbo: Biko sụọ Igbo ka m ghọta.
examples.english: Please speak Igbo so I understand.

examples.igbo: O bu ùkwù ọka n'isi.
examples.english: He carried a bundle of corn on his head.

examples.igbo: Gbakọta akwụkwọ ndị ahụ n'otu ùkwù.
examples.english: Gather those papers into one bundle.

gloss: White Guinea Yam (Dioscorea cayenensis rotundata Poir.), fat and of high quality; features in feasts

examples.igbo: Anyị ji ukòm mee oriri n'ụbọchị ọhụrụ.
examples.english: We used white Guinea yam for the feast on New Yam day.

examples.igbo: Ji ukòm a toro eto, ọ ga-atọ ụtọ.
examples.english: This white Guinea yam is mature, it will be tasty.

gloss: be at point of death; struggle with death

examples.igbo: Nna ya na-akwò ọnwụ n'ụlọ ọgwụ.
examples.english: His father is at the point of death in the hospital.

examples.igbo: Ha na-akwò ọnwụ tupu enyemaka abịa.
examples.english: They were struggling with death before help came.

gloss: energetically; with a lot of strength

examples.igbo: Ọ rụrụ ọrụ n'ubi ikiīkē.
examples.english: He worked on the farm energetically.

examples.igbo: Gbaa ọsọ ikiīkē ka ị nweta ihe nrite.
examples.english: Run with a lot of strength so you win the prize.

examples.igbo: Ọ tara ya n'otoko aka nri.
examples.english: He bit him on the right thigh.

examples.igbo: Otoko ya na-egbu mgbu mgbe o si ọrụ lọta.
examples.english: His thigh aches when he returns from work.

examples.igbo: O ziri nwanne ya n'anya ka ọ bịa ahịa.
examples.english: He convinced his brother to come to the market.

examples.igbo: Ị zịrị ya n'anya ka o kwenye?
examples.english: Did you convince him to agree?

note: Sense taken as 'persuade someone to accept something'; phrasing is idiomatic but the verb is uncommon in everyday speech.

examples.igbo: O zọrọ osisi mango n'akụkụ ụlọ.
examples.english: He transplanted a mango tree beside the house.

examples.igbo: Zọọ osisi a n'ebe ọhụrụ.
examples.english: Transplant this tree in a new spot.

note: Low-tone stem handled as 'zọrọ' / 'zọọ'; tone marking on the inflections may vary by speaker.

examples.igbo: Nkwụ Ògwùgwù na-eto n'akụkụ mmiri.
examples.english: The Ogwugwu palms grow beside the stream.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka anaghị egbu nkwụ Ògwùgwù.
examples.english: Children do not cut Ogwugwu palms.

note: A local, shrine-associated term; the examples are grammatical but I cannot confirm how speakers actually use the name.

examples.igbo: Akwa ahụ nyakụrụ n'ahụ ya n'ihi ọsụsụ.
examples.english: The cloth stuck to his body because of sweat.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-anyakụ n'aka nne ya.
examples.english: That child clings to his mother's hand.

gloss: use to; (a thing to a person experiencing) become familiar or conversant; become part of

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ mara ahụ n'ụlọ akwụkwọ ọhụrụ.
examples.english: The child has got used to the new school.

examples.igbo: Ị mara ahụ n'ọrụ a?
examples.english: Are you used to this work?

note: Written without a subject change; the expression is stative and often appears as 'ọ marala ahụ'.

gloss: dip food in soup or stew and eat

examples.igbo: Ọ na-asuli ji n'ofe ose.
examples.english: She dips yam in pepper soup and eats.

examples.igbo: Sulie achịcha gị n'ofe, ọ dị ụtọ.
examples.english: Dip your bread in the soup, it is tasty.

note: Imperative 'sulie' and habitual 'na-asuli' are the forms I would expect; tone marking on the stem varies.

examples.igbo: Ùbe n'osisi anyị ji eji ugbu a.
examples.english: The pears on our tree are ripe now.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ ùbe ji eji?
examples.english: Do you want ripe pears?

note: Uses the stative 'ji eji' as given; some speakers would say 'ùbe ndị a chara acha'.

examples.igbo: O nwụchiri anya wee malite ikpe ekpere.
examples.english: He shut his eyes and began to pray.

examples.igbo: Nwụchie anya gị, atụla egwu.
examples.english: Shut your eyes, do not be afraid.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-ekwu okwu mkpalị mgbe niile.
examples.english: That child always says insulting words.

examples.igbo: Ekwula okwu mkpalị mgbe ị na-ewe iwe.
examples.english: Don't say insulting words when you are angry.

gloss: pangolin, whose skin is used for medicine

examples.igbo: Akàbò bụ anụ ọhịa na-eri ndanda n'ọhịa.
examples.english: The pangolin is a wild animal that eats ants in the bush.

examples.igbo: Ị hụtụla akàbò n'ọhịa mgbe ọ bụla?
examples.english: Have you ever seen a pangolin in the bush?

gloss: to get or gather; amass; pile up

examples.igbo: Kpakọta akwụkwọ gị niile n'otu ebe.
examples.english: Gather all your books in one place.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akpakọta ego iji zụta ụgbọala.
examples.english: He is amassing money to buy a car.

examples.igbo: Nna m na-agba nta n'ọhịa.
examples.english: My father hunts in the bush.

examples.igbo: Gbaa nta taa ka anyị rie anụ.
examples.english: Hunt today so that we can eat meat.

examples.igbo: Ite ahụ juru eju mmiri.
examples.english: That pot is full of water.

examples.igbo: Jue eju iko ahụ na mmiri.
examples.english: Fill that cup with water.

note: Inflected forms are written without the dictionary tone marks; the sense is standard, but the imperative form may vary by speaker.

examples.igbo: Abụ olu ụtọ nke ukwe ahụ masịrị m.
examples.english: The melody of that song pleased me.

examples.igbo: Ị na-anụ abụ olu ụtọ si n'ụlọ ha?
examples.english: Do you hear the melody from their house?

examples.igbo: Mmụọ ikpo na-apụta n'oge emume obodo.
examples.english: The ikpo masquerade appears during the town festival.

examples.igbo: Ụmụntakịrị na-atụ egwu mmụọ ikpo n'abalị.
examples.english: Children are afraid of the ikpo masquerade at night.

gloss: instrument with cane handle and many cords, used for flogging or for killing flies

examples.igbo: O jiri ìbèlì chụpụ ijiji n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: She used an ibeli to chase flies in the house.

examples.igbo: Nye m ìbèlì ka m chụpụ ijiji.
examples.english: Give me an ibeli so I can chase flies.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-afùghalịba n'okporo ámá.
examples.english: He wanders about on the street.

examples.igbo: Kwụsị ịfùghalịba n'abalị.
examples.english: Stop wandering about at night.

note: The verb is rare and its inflected forms are not widely documented; the examples follow the given stem.

gloss: variety of ùbùlù whose leaves are used to cure malaria

examples.igbo: Ùbùlù inū bụ osisi e ji agwọ iba.
examples.english: Ubulu inu is a plant used to treat malaria.

examples.igbo: Nne m na-esi akwụkwọ ùbùlù inū gwọọ nwanne m.
examples.english: My mother boils ubulu inu leaves to treat my brother.

note: The plant name is given in the entry; botanical usage may vary locally.

examples.igbo: Ụmụazụ ya na-eso ya ebe ọ bụla.
examples.english: His disciples follow him everywhere.

examples.igbo: Ị bụ onye nkuzi ma ọ bụ otu n'ime ụmụazụ ya?
examples.english: Are you the teacher or one of his disciples?

examples.igbo: Onye mmānya ahụ na-ere mmanya ọcha.
examples.english: That palmwine seller sells fresh palmwine.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara mmanya n'aka onye mmānya?
examples.english: Did you buy wine from the palmwine seller?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-atụ ntụ mgbe ọ bụla.
examples.english: He lies every time.

examples.igbo: Atụla ntụ n'ihu nne gị!
examples.english: Don't lie before your mother!

examples.igbo: Ọ na-agbụ ọnụ mmiri mgbe ọ na-eri ose.
examples.english: He spits when he eats pepper.

examples.igbo: Gbụ ọnụ mmiri n'èzí, ọ bụghị n'ime ụlọ!
examples.english: Spit outside, not inside the house!

gloss: furnance; heap of coal, charcoal; fire

examples.igbo: Òòbo ọkū ahụ na-ekpo ọkụ nke ukwuu.
examples.english: That furnace is very hot.

examples.igbo: Ị na-etinye nkụ n'òòbo ọkū?
examples.english: Are you putting firewood in the furnace?

gloss: red clay used for building in upland areas (compare ụlō)

examples.igbo: Ha na-eji aja ụpà wuo ụlọ.
examples.english: They use red clay to build houses.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ aja ụpà n'ugwu ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see red clay on that hill?

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ gbara mmee n'ikpere.
examples.english: That child bled on the knee.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-agba mmee ma ị daa?
examples.english: Will you bleed if you fall?

examples.igbo: M̀gbogbo m bịara n'ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: My uncle came to our house.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akpọ m̀gbogbo gị?
examples.english: Are you calling your uncle?

examples.igbo: Wụ̀kọ mmiri abụọ a n'ite.
examples.english: Pour these two waters together into the pot.

examples.igbo: Ha wụkọrọ mmiri n'otu ite.
examples.english: They poured water together into one pot.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-akwụ ụkwalà ntìrịìrì nke ukwuu.
examples.english: That child is coughing whooping cough badly.

examples.igbo: Nwa ya ọ nwere ụkwalà ntìrịìrì?
examples.english: Does her child have whooping cough?

examples.igbo: Chekàta m n'ụlọ ahịa ruo oge.
examples.english: Wait for me at the market for a while.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-echekàta ruo mgbe m lọtara?
examples.english: Will you wait a long time until I return?

gloss: agidi; food prepared from maize by grinding, sifting, boiling until thick and stiff and sometimes wrapping in leaves for selling

examples.igbo: Mama na-ere nni ọkà n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: Mother is selling agidi in the market today.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-azụta nni ọkà n'ahịa taa?
examples.english: Will you buy agidi in the market today?

gloss: a person who plays guitar, guitarist

examples.igbo: Ọ̀kpụụbọ ahụ na-akpọ ụbọ n'ụlọ oriri.
examples.english: That guitarist plays guitar in a restaurant.

examples.igbo: Ị bụ ọ̀kpụụbọ nke ọma n'ezie?
examples.english: Are you really a good guitarist?

gloss: abyss; place at bottom of a cliff or steep hill

examples.igbo: Ewu ahụ dara na mgbùlùgùdù n'okpuru ugwu.
examples.english: That goat fell into the abyss at the bottom of the hill.

examples.igbo: Anyị hụrụ mgbùlùgùdù nke dị egwu n'okpuru ugwu.
examples.english: We saw a terrible abyss at the bottom of the hill.

examples.igbo: Mwufè ogwe ahụ dị mfe nke ukwuu.
examples.english: Jumping over that log is very easy.

examples.igbo: Mwufè mgbidi ahụ ọ dị mfe?
examples.english: Is jumping over that wall easy?

examples.igbo: Sètị ụkwụ gị tupu ị gbaa ọsọ.
examples.english: Stretch your leg before you run.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-asètị ahụ ha n'ụtụtụ mgbe ọ bụla.
examples.english: Children stretch their bodies every morning.

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ na-akpa ùkpa orī n'oge a.
examples.english: That man is friends with a thief these days.

examples.igbo: Ọ dị njọ ịkpa ùkpa orī.
examples.english: It is bad to be friends with a thief.

examples.igbo: Fa nà isi fā bịara n'oge.
examples.english: They themselves came early.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ fa nà isi fā mere ya?
examples.english: Was it they themselves who did it?

examples.igbo: Nne m nọ na òchìchè banyere nwa ya.
examples.english: My mother is thinking about her child.

examples.igbo: Òchìchè ahụ ọ bara uru n'ezie?
examples.english: Was that thinking really useful?

examples.igbo: Nwa nwoke a nwere isi akwụkwọ nke ukwuu.
examples.english: This boy is very brilliant.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ nwa nwere isi akwụkwọ, ọ́ bụghị?
examples.english: He is a brilliant child, isn't he?

gloss: take or follow a path or pattern or manner; from; through

examples.igbo: O si n'ụzọ dị warara bịa ebe a.
examples.english: He came here through a narrow path.

examples.igbo: Ị si n'okporo ụzọ a bịa?
examples.english: Did you come through this road?

examples.igbo: Nye m otu ǹju osikapa.
examples.english: Give me one full measure of rice.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ otu ǹju ma ọ bụ abụọ?
examples.english: Do you want one full measure or two?

gloss: cut using the hand or a scissors, especially for something that is not thick eg. paper, cloth

examples.igbo: O ji mkpa chàa akwụkwọ ahụ.
examples.english: She used scissors to cut that paper.

examples.igbo: Chàa akwà a ụzọ abụọ.
examples.english: Cut this cloth into two parts.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-agba ọsọahịa n'ịntanetị.
examples.english: He does affiliate marketing on the internet.

examples.igbo: Ị na-agba ọsọahịa maka ngwaahịa ndị a?
examples.english: Are you doing affiliate marketing for these products?

examples.igbo: Nne ya yi akwà ụjū n'oge olili.
examples.english: Her mother wore black cloth during the burial.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eyi akwà ụjū n'olili a?
examples.english: Will you wear black cloth at this burial?

examples.igbo: Obodo anyị nwere ezi ūdo ugbu a.
examples.english: Our town has perfect peace now.

examples.igbo: Ezi ūdo ọ̀ dị n'ezinụlọ gị?
examples.english: Is there perfect peace in your family?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-atụ aro ka anyị gaa ahịa.
examples.english: He is suggesting that we go to the market.

examples.igbo: Gịnị ka ị na-atụ aro maka nri abalị?
examples.english: What do you suggest for dinner?

examples.igbo: Chịta mkpụrụ osisi ndị ahụ.
examples.english: Bring those fruits.

examples.igbo: O chịtara akwụkwọ na pensụl.
examples.english: He brought books and pencils.

examples.igbo: Mmiri na-arùfù n'akụkụ okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: Water is flowing by the roadside.

examples.igbo: Ehi ọ̀ rùfùrù n'ogige?
examples.english: Did the cow run away from the pen?

note: The sense of -rùfù as flow/run away is rendered with common inflections, but the verb is not one I use often.

examples.igbo: Ụlọ ọhụrụ anyị dị mma n'anya.
examples.english: Our new house is pleasant to look at.

examples.igbo: Osisi ndị ahụ dị mma n'anya?
examples.english: Are those trees pleasant to the eye?

gloss: run hither and thither; make fuss

examples.igbo: Ụmụntakịrị na-agbakèrì àlà n'ama.
examples.english: The children are running hither and thither in the compound.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji agbakèrì àlà?
examples.english: Why are you making a fuss?

note: The expression is idiomatic in the sense of restless running about, but the second sentence could also be read as simply running about.

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ nwere ǹtụ n'obi.
examples.english: That man has guile in his heart.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eji ǹtụ aghọgbu ndị mmadụ?
examples.english: Are you using cunning to deceive people?

examples.igbo: Ha na-alụ ụkà n'ahịa.
examples.english: They are arguing at the market.

examples.igbo: Ejila nne gị lụọ ụkà.
examples.english: Do not argue with your mother.

gloss: look around as if in suspicion; stare around

examples.igbo: Ọ na-achagharị anya n'ọhịa.
examples.english: He is looking around suspiciously in the field.

examples.igbo: Chagharịa anya tupu ị gafee okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: Look around before you cross the road.

examples.igbo: Ajụjụ a siri ike.
examples.english: This question is hard.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere ajụjụ ọ bụla?
examples.english: Do you have any question?

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ bịaketere nne ya.
examples.english: The child came nearer to his mother.

examples.igbo: Bịakete ebe a.
examples.english: Come nearer here.

examples.igbo: Ígwè a dị arọ.
examples.english: This metal is heavy.

examples.igbo: Nna m na-ere ígwè n'ahịa.
examples.english: My father sells metal in the market.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-eme potolī n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: The children are having fun at school.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eme potolī?
examples.english: Are you having fun?

note: potolī appears to be colloquial; the examples are simple and idiomatic.

gloss: gather together; collect (in one place) (Emphasizes togetherness more than -kpokọ)

examples.igbo: Ndị ọrụ na-akpokò nkụ n'otu ebe.
examples.english: The workers are gathering firewood in one place.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akpokò akwụkwọ gị n'ime akpa?
examples.english: Are you gathering your books into the bag?

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ zọrọ ụkwụ n'ibelibe ìtè.
examples.english: The child stepped on a potsherd.

examples.igbo: Ibelibe ìtè ndị a dị nkọ.
examples.english: These potsherds are sharp.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka abụọ na-eti ūbū n'ọsọ.
examples.english: Two children are competing in a race.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eti ūbū na nwanne gị?
examples.english: Are you competing with your sibling?

examples.igbo: Nna m mere nrù tupu owuwe ihe ubi.
examples.english: My father performed a rite before the harvest.

examples.igbo: Ndị obodo na-eweta nrù nye eze.
examples.english: The people are bringing homage to the king.

examples.igbo: Egedege irū ya na-agba ọbara.
examples.english: His forehead is bleeding.

examples.igbo: O metụrụ egedege irū nwa ahụ aka.
examples.english: She touched the child's forehead.

gloss: grub found on palm tree and in decaying palm tree trunk (literally palm tree grub)

examples.igbo: Anyị hụrụ àkpa nkwū n'osisi nkwū.
examples.english: We saw palm grubs on the palm tree.

examples.igbo: Nne m ghere àkpa nkwū n'ọkụ.
examples.english: My mother roasted palm grubs over the fire.

examples.igbo: Ụzọ ahụ lọrọ ālọ̄ n'ihi mmiri ozuzo.
examples.english: The road is slippery because of the rain.

examples.igbo: Jide azụ ahụ nke ọma, ọ na-alọ ālọ̄.
examples.english: Hold that fish well; it is slimy.

gloss: gnaw, eat up (clothing, paper, etc., as of rats, ants, etc.)

examples.igbo: Oke takasịrị akwụkwọ m.
examples.english: A rat gnawed my book.

examples.igbo: Ndanda na-atakasị akwụkwọ akụkọ ahụ.
examples.english: Ants are gnawing that newspaper.

examples.igbo: Ikè mmānya dị n'ala ite ahụ.
examples.english: The dregs are at the bottom of that pot.

examples.igbo: Wụpụ ikè mmānya ahụ.
examples.english: Pour away the dregs.

examples.igbo: E tinyere ofiliisī n'isi akwa.
examples.english: They put a pillow at the head of the bed.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-arahụ n'ofiliisī.
examples.english: The child is sleeping on a pillow.

examples.igbo: Dinwenu anyị na-eche anyị nche kwa ụbọchị.
examples.english: Our Lord watches over us every day.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ekele Dinwenu anyị maka ihe o meere gị?
examples.english: Do you thank our Lord for what he has done for you?

examples.igbo: Anyị jiri ụgbọ ala gaa ahịa taa.
examples.english: We went to the market by car today.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere ụgbọ ala ọhụrụ?
examples.english: Do you have a new car?

gloss: camwood (dye-wood from the tree Baphia nitida Lodd. or

examples.igbo: O jiri ufie tee ahụ ya.
examples.english: She painted her body with camwood.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara ufie n'ahịa?
examples.english: Did you buy camwood in the market?

note: Both sentences are idiomatic; the second sentence could also be phrased with etee.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-arịọ mgbaghàlụ n'aka nwunye ya.
examples.english: He is asking his wife for forgiveness.

examples.igbo: Ị gaghị arịọ ya mgbaghàlụ?
examples.english: Won't you ask her for forgiveness?

note: The more usual modern form is 'mgbaghara'; I kept the spelling and tones given.

examples.igbo: Akpụ ndị ahụ fenịrị n'ihi anwụ.
examples.english: Those cassava plants shrivelled because of the sun.

examples.igbo: Osisi ọzọ adịghị afeni.
examples.english: The other plant is not shrivelling.

note: The inflected forms fenịrị/afeni are given without full tone marking; the verb stem itself is uncommon.

gloss: come to a stop, stop walking; end a journey; termination point

examples.igbo: Bọs ahụ jedebe n'ihu ahịa.
examples.english: The bus came to a stop in front of the market.

examples.igbo: Ebee ka ụzọ a jedebe?
examples.english: Where does this road end?

note: The second sentence also occurs with the habitual: 'Ebee ka ụzọ a na-ejedebe?'

examples.igbo: Ọnụ ego akwa a fere okè.
examples.english: The price of this cloth is beyond the limit.

examples.igbo: Ị chere na m fere okè?
examples.english: Do you think I overstepped?

note: The idiom is common; the exact tone on the inflected 'fere' may vary by speaker.

examples.igbo: Kwà ụtùtù, ọ na-aga ọrụ.
examples.english: Every morning, he goes to work.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eri nri kwà ụtùtù?
examples.english: Do you eat every morning?

examples.igbo: O kụrụ aka n'ọnụ ụzọ tupu ọ banye.
examples.english: He knocked on the door before entering.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji kụ m aka n'isi?
examples.english: Why did you hit me on the head?

examples.igbo: Ha ji okpì nkū wuo oche a.
examples.english: They used hard wood to make this chair.

examples.igbo: Okpì nkū ka ị chọrọ, ma ọ bụ osisi dị nro?
examples.english: Is it hard wood you want, or soft wood?

note: The second sentence is a choice question and slightly longer than the usual pattern.

examples.igbo: Ndị na-abụ abụ na-akụ ajà n'ụlọ ụka.
examples.english: The singers play the tambourine in church.

examples.igbo: Kụọ ajà ahụ nwayọ, ka anyị nụ olu ndị ọzọ.
examples.english: Play that tambourine softly so we can hear the other voices.

examples.igbo: Nne m na-esi nri ọma n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: My mother cooks good food in the morning.

examples.igbo: Gwa nne gị ka ọ zụta azụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: Tell your mother to buy fish at the market.

examples.igbo: Ọ nodara ọgwụ ahụ ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: He swallowed that medicine quickly.

examples.igbo: Ekwula okwu, nodaa nri gị ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Don't talk, swallow your food quickly.

examples.igbo: Oge ịwa ji bụ nnukwu emume n'obodo anyị.
examples.english: The yam festival is a big celebration in our town.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-aga oge ịwa ji n'afọ a?
examples.english: Will you go to the yam festival this year?

examples.igbo: Ònyì na-egbu ụmụaka n'oge udu mmiri.
examples.english: Dysentery kills children in the rainy season.

examples.igbo: Gaa ụlọ ọgwụ ma ọ bụrụ na ị nwere ònyì.
examples.english: Go to the hospital if you have dysentery.

gloss: usurp someone's place; take the place of; succeed

examples.igbo: Ọ nọchiri nna ya n'oche eze.
examples.english: He succeeded his father on the throne.

examples.igbo: Nọchie m n'ọrụ taa, ka m gaa ahịa.
examples.english: Replace me at work today so I can go to the market.

examples.igbo: Isi m na-afụ m ụfụ n'abalị a.
examples.english: My head hurts me tonight.

examples.igbo: Ụkwụ gị ọ na-afụ gị ụfụ mgbe ị na-eje ije?
examples.english: Does your leg hurt you when you walk?

examples.igbo: Kpajita m nkụ ka m sie nri.
examples.english: Break and bring me firewood so I can cook.

examples.igbo: O kpajitara nne ya nkụ n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: He broke and brought his mother firewood in the morning.

note: The headword lists several variants; the examples use -kpàjita.

examples.igbo: Ọ kachasị n'ime ụmụ akwụkwọ ahụ.
examples.english: He is the greatest among those students.

examples.igbo: Nke a ọ kachasị nke ahụ?
examples.english: Is this greater than that one?

examples.igbo: Abụ mbido ahụ masịrị m nke ukwuu.
examples.english: I liked that opening song very much.

examples.igbo: Bido abụ mbido ka anyị bido emume.
examples.english: Start the opening song so we can begin the ceremony.

gloss: equally; equal; in an equal way

examples.igbo: Ọ kere achịcha ahụ ǹhàtaǹhà.
examples.english: She divided the bread equally.

examples.igbo: Kee ego a ǹhàtaǹhà n'etiti ụmụaka.
examples.english: Share this money equally among the children.

examples.igbo: Ndị ọrụ na-atụni ụzọ n'elu mmiri.
examples.english: The workers are building up the causeway.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ha ji atụni ụzọ n'elu mmiri?
examples.english: Why are they building up the causeway?

note: Rare verb; used in continuous/gerund constructions.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akwosi ọkụkọ ahụ ugbènè.
examples.english: She is plucking the chicken's feathers.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji akwosi ọkụkọ ugbènè?
examples.english: Why are you plucking chicken feathers?

note: The noun ugbènè is kept as given.

examples.igbo: Nwa ōkolọbìà ahụ na-azụ ehi.
examples.english: That youth herds cattle.

examples.igbo: Nwa ōkolọbìà, gịnị ka ị na-achọ n'ahịa?
examples.english: Boy, what are you looking for in the market?

gloss: cut open, break into two (e.g. coconut)

examples.igbo: Ọ gbuwara akị bekee ahụ.
examples.english: He broke the coconut open.

examples.igbo: Gbuwaa akị bekee a ka anyị rie ya.
examples.english: Break this coconut open so we can eat it.

examples.igbo: Agàmeèbù na-eto n'akụkụ ụzọ ahụ.
examples.english: False thistle grows beside that road.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ewepụ agàmeèbù n'ubi?
examples.english: Are you removing false thistle from the farm?

note: Plant name kept as given.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka kpụrụ ǹdèlè n'ájá.
examples.english: The children made tracks in the sand.

examples.igbo: Kpụọ ǹdèlè gị n'ájá.
examples.english: Make your track in the sand.

examples.igbo: Nri ba ụ̄bā n'ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: Food is plentiful in our house.

examples.igbo: Mmanụ ba ụ̄bā n'ahịa taa?
examples.english: Is oil plentiful in the market today?

examples.igbo: N'izù afīa, ọtụtụ mmadụ na-aga ahịa.
examples.english: During the market week, many people go to the market.

examples.igbo: Kedu ụbọchị izù afīa na-amalite?
examples.english: Which day does the market week begin?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-achọ ìkpeǹkwụ̀mọọtọ n'ụlọ ikpe.
examples.english: He is seeking justice in court.

examples.igbo: Ìkpeǹkwụ̀mọọtọ dị n'obodo a?
examples.english: Is there justice in this town?

examples.igbo: Ụlọ anyị na-eri mmiri n'oge udu mmiri.
examples.english: Our house leaks during the rainy season.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ahụ na tankị ahụ na-eri mmiri?
examples.english: Do you see that the tank is leaking?

note: Headword mmilī is dialectal; standard Igbo uses mmiri.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-aru mmiri n'aka nna ya.
examples.english: The child is pouring water on his father's hands.

examples.igbo: Ruoro m mmiri n'aka.
examples.english: Pour water on my hands for me.

note: Headword mmilī is dialectal; standard Igbo uses mmiri. -ru mmiri means pour water, often for washing hands.

examples.igbo: Onye nkụzi kụrụ mgbarịmgba ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: The teacher rang the school bell.

examples.igbo: Ị kụrụ mgbarịmgba taa?
examples.english: Did you ring the bell today?

examples.igbo: Àghị̀rịị̀ghà nwa ahụ na-akpasu ndị mmadụ iwe.
examples.english: That child's mischief annoys people.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-akwụsị àghị̀rịị̀ghà gị?
examples.english: Will you stop your mischief?

examples.igbo: Ògìli ūgba na-eto n'azụ ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: The castor oil plant grows behind our house.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akụ ògìli ūgba n'akụkụ ubi?
examples.english: Do you plant castor oil plant near the farm?

examples.igbo: Anyanwụ na-acha taa.
examples.english: The sun is shining today.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ anyanwụ n'elu igwe?
examples.english: Did you see the sun in the sky?

note: Headword anyaanwū is dialectal; standard Igbo uses anyanwụ.

examples.igbo: Nwa agbọghọ ahụ ji ejiji mara mma.
examples.english: That girl is beautifully dressed.

examples.igbo: Jiri ejiji gị kacha mma bịa oriri.
examples.english: Come to the party in your best attire.

examples.igbo: Kedu mgbe ị ga-alọta?
examples.english: When will you return?

examples.igbo: Cheta kedu mgbe anyị ga-aga ahịa.
examples.english: Remember when we will go to the market.

note: Headword kèdụ èkpè is dialectal; standard Igbo uses kedu mgbe.

examples.igbo: O kwọrọ ụla n'abalị niile.
examples.english: He snored all night.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akwọ ụla mgbe ị na-ehi ụra?
examples.english: Do you snore when you sleep?

examples.igbo: Ọ bịara sọ otu ugboro.
examples.english: He came only once.

examples.igbo: Sọ otu ugboro ka m gara ebe ahụ.
examples.english: Only once did I go there.

note: Headword sò òfu ùgbòlò is dialectal; standard Igbo uses sọ otu ugboro.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-atụ egwù nkịta ahụ.
examples.english: The children are afraid of that dog.

examples.igbo: Atụla egwù, anyị ga-enyere gị aka.
examples.english: Don't be afraid, we shall help you.

examples.igbo: O sàgbàpùrù akwụkwọ ahụ n'elu tebụl.
examples.english: He opened the book wide on the table.

examples.igbo: Sàgbàpù ákwà ahụ ka anyanwụ kpọọ ya.
examples.english: Spread the cloth open so the sun dries it.

examples.igbo: Nwa ehi ahụ dị gbelele nke ukwuu.
examples.english: That calf is very thin.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji dị gbelele otú a?
examples.english: Why are you so thin?

examples.igbo: Nne ya bara ya m̀ba maka ịkpọ aha ọjọọ.
examples.english: His mother scolded him for calling bad names.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-abara ya m̀ba ma ọ ghara ịrụ ọrụ ya?
examples.english: Will you scold him if he doesn't do his work?

examples.igbo: Nlòta nne m na-enye m obi ụtọ.
examples.english: Remembrance of my mother gives me joy.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere nlòta ọ bụla banyere nna gị?
examples.english: Do you have any remembrance of your father?

examples.igbo: Ọ dīnà n̄kọ̄ n'àkwà ahụ.
examples.english: He lies on his side on that bed.

examples.igbo: Dīnà n̄kọ̄ ka ọkpụkpụ azụ gị zuru ike.
examples.english: Lie on your side so your back rests.

examples.igbo: O kpụgonitere mmiri n'olulu ahụ.
examples.english: She drew water from that well.

examples.igbo: Kpụgonita eriri ahụ ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Pull up that rope quickly.

examples.igbo: Anyị ga-aga ahịa echi.
examples.english: We shall go to market tomorrow.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-abịa n'ụlọ m?
examples.english: Will you come to my house?

examples.igbo: Anyị chọtara ngwọta maka nsogbu mmiri ahụ.
examples.english: We found a solution to that water problem.

examples.igbo: Gịnị bụ ngwọta maka ụkọ mmiri n'obodo a?
examples.english: What is the solution to the water scarcity in this town?

gloss: to advise; counsel; make suggestion; give opinion

examples.igbo: Onye nkuzi tụnyere anyị arò ka anyị gụsie akwụkwọ ike.
examples.english: The teacher advised us to study hard.

examples.igbo: Biko tụnye m arò maka ịzụta ehi.
examples.english: Please advise me about buying a cow.

examples.igbo: Mgbe chi fọrọ, anyị malitere njem.
examples.english: When day broke, we started the journey.

examples.igbo: Chi fọrọla?
examples.english: Has the day broken?

gloss: plant planted to enrich the soil (especially in the Ìgbo agba enū area)

examples.igbo: O kụrụ àràbà n'ubi ya iji mee ka ala dị mma.
examples.english: He planted àràbà in his farm to make the soil good.

examples.igbo: Àràbà na-enyere ala aka ịba ụba.
examples.english: Àràbà helps the soil to become fertile.

gloss: small patch of bush left in middle of cleared area

examples.igbo: Ha hapụrụ mkpù ọfīa n'etiti ubi ahụ.
examples.english: They left a small patch of bush in the middle of that farm.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere mkpù ọfīa ji dị n'ubi gị?
examples.english: Why is there a patch of bush in your farm?

examples.igbo: Ụmụ akwụkwọ na-ebu abụ n'obì.
examples.english: The pupils learn the song by heart.

examples.igbo: Buru ya n'obì tupu ị gụọ ya n'ihu ọha.
examples.english: Learn it by heart before you recite it in public.

examples.igbo: Ọ nọ n'elu top nke klas ahụ.
examples.english: He is at the top of that class.

examples.igbo: Top nke ugwu ahụ dị elu.
examples.english: The top of that hill is high.

note: top appears to be an English loanword, not a standard Igbo noun.

examples.igbo: O jiri akwa chichapụ ntụ n'elu tebụl.
examples.english: She used a cloth to wipe the dust off the table.

examples.igbo: Chichapụ ya nke ọma tupu ị tinye mmanụ.
examples.english: Wipe it off well before you apply oil.

gloss: roof framework before thatching or fixing the sheets

examples.igbo: Ndị ọrụ na-akwado ndụmì ụnò tupu ha etinye akwụkwọ ahụ.
examples.english: The workers are preparing the roof framework before they fix the sheets.

examples.igbo: Ndụmì ụnò ahụ dara mgbe ifufe fesara ya.
examples.english: That roof framework fell when the wind blew it.

examples.igbo: Anyị zụtara ìkpoòkpò nkōlọ n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: We bought ìkpoòkpò nkōlọ at the market today.

examples.igbo: Ị hụla ìkpoòkpò nkōlọ n'osimiri?
examples.english: Have you seen ìkpoòkpò nkōlọ in the river?

note: The fish name is obscure, but the sentences use it as a countable noun in ordinary market and river contexts.

examples.igbo: Ndị okenye na-ekwu maka enu ōghịgha.
examples.english: Elders talk about changes in the world.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ahụ enu ōghịgha n'obodo a?
examples.english: Do you see changes in the world in this town?

note: The phrase is abstract; the examples keep it in everyday speech about what elders discuss and what one observes.

examples.igbo: Onye uwe ojii gbara ya ajụjụọnụ̄.
examples.english: The police officer interrogated him.

examples.igbo: Gbaa ya ajụjụọnụ̄ tupu i kpebie ihe.
examples.english: Interview him before you decide.

gloss: shake the head (side to side), especially in disagreement or refusal

examples.igbo: O fufere isī mgbe m jụrụ ya.
examples.english: He shook his head when I asked him.

examples.igbo: Fufee isī gị ma ị chọghị.
examples.english: Shake your head if you don't want.

note: The inflected forms fufere and fufee are used for the stem fufè; the sense is clearly refusal or disagreement.

gloss: bear witness (usually of native doctor pointing out guilty person)

examples.igbo: Dibia tara ịtà na ya bụ onye ohi.
examples.english: The native doctor bore witness that he was the thief.

examples.igbo: Ọ tara ịtà n'ihu ndị obodo.
examples.english: He bore witness before the villagers.

note: The sense is tied to the native doctor's pointing out of a guilty person; the examples keep that context.

examples.igbo: Ọkụ ahụ na-akwụ anwụlù.
examples.english: That fire is smoking.

examples.igbo: Ọkụ a akwụghị anwụlù.
examples.english: This fire did not smoke.

note: The phrase is handled as an intransitive expression about fire and smoke.

examples.igbo: Chineke nye ya ogonogo ndù.
examples.english: God grant him long life.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ ogonogo ndù?
examples.english: Do you want long life?

gloss: cultivate adjoining farms; be farm neighbours

examples.igbo: Ndị ọrụ ugbo abụọ ahụ na-agba n'ugbō.
examples.english: Those two farmers are farm neighbours.

examples.igbo: Anyị gbara n'ugbō n'afọ a.
examples.english: We cultivated adjoining farms this year.

note: The second sentence uses the past form gbara with n'ugbō; the first uses the continuous na-agba for being farm neighbours.

gloss: ringworm of the head (tinea capitis) (literally barber who receives no pay)

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ nwere ọ̀kpụīsieringo n'isi.
examples.english: That child has ringworm on the head.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ahụ ọ̀kpụīsieringo n'isi nwa a?
examples.english: Do you see ringworm on this child's head?

note: The term is specific and uncommon, but the examples use it plainly as the name of the scalp condition.

examples.igbo: Nwa agbọghọ ahụ nwere mma ārụ.
examples.english: That girl has physical beauty.

examples.igbo: Mma ārụ ọ na-enyere mmadụ aka?
examples.english: Does physical beauty help a person?

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-aga ọ̀taàkàrà n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: Children go to nursery school in the morning.

examples.igbo: Ị debanyere nwa gị aha n'ọ̀taàkàrà?
examples.english: Have you enrolled your child in nursery school?

examples.igbo: Ndị okenye doziri okwu ahụ n'udo.
examples.english: The elders settled that case peacefully.

examples.igbo: Ònye ga-adozi okwu ala a?
examples.english: Who will settle this land case?

gloss: ancestral house, typical of Onitsha and corresponding to the òbi of other areas. It is constructed around a rectangular open- air courtyard, one end of which leads to the ùkpò or throne of the household head and the other to the entrance, beyond which is an open meeting-place (ọnụ ìbà). All rooms are within coursed mud walls (Henderson 1972 167)

examples.igbo: E ji mgbidi ụrọ wuo ìbà anyị.
examples.english: Our ancestral house was built with mud walls.

examples.igbo: Ị hụla ìbà ochie n'Onịcha?
examples.english: Have you seen the old ancestral house in Onitsha?

note: ìbà is a specific Onitsha architectural term; sentences are kept simple and culturally appropriate.

examples.igbo: Nne m zụtara òkpo āba n'ahịa.
examples.english: My mother bought òkpo āba at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị maara esi ofe òkpo āba?
examples.english: Do you know how to cook òkpo āba soup?

note: Fish name is specialist vocabulary; examples are plausible but not common everyday usage.

examples.igbo: Sàghepụ ọnụ ụzọ ka ikuku bata.
examples.english: Open the door wide so air can enter.

examples.igbo: Ị sàghepụrụ ọnụ ụzọ ahụ?
examples.english: Did you open that door wide?

note: Verb stem inflection is given as sàghepụ-/sàghepụrụ; a speaker might prefer a different object.

examples.igbo: Òluku na-eto n'ubi anyị.
examples.english: Cotton grows in our farm.

examples.igbo: Ha na-akọ òluku n'afọ a?
examples.english: Are they planting cotton this year?

examples.igbo: Okwu a nwere nkeji okwu atọ.
examples.english: This word has three syllables.

examples.igbo: Gụọ nkeji okwu ndị a nke ọma.
examples.english: Read these syllables well.

examples.igbo: Ose a na-ekpo nke ukwuu.
examples.english: This pepper is very peppery.

examples.igbo: Ofe a adịghị ekpo.
examples.english: This soup is not peppery.

note: The verb kpò 'be peppery' is less common than related hot/pepper expressions; examples are kept simple.

examples.igbo: O ji nchà ngù saa efere.
examples.english: She used local soap to wash plates.

examples.igbo: Nchà ngù dị n'ahịa taa?
examples.english: Is local soap in the market today?

examples.igbo: Akpa ọka ahụ fụ̀wara n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: That bag of corn burst at the market today.

examples.igbo: Akpa gị fụ̀wara n'ụzọ mgbe ị na-abịa?
examples.english: Did your bag burst on the way when you were coming?

note: The word is uncommon, but the sentences use it in the sense of bursting like a bag.

examples.igbo: Egbè igwē dara nnukwu ụda n'abalị ụnyaahụ.

examples.english: Be careful so that the wall does not collapse.

examples.igbo: O kpàchisịrị ọnụ ụzọ niile tupu ọ pụọ.
examples.english: He locked all the doors before he left.

examples.igbo: Ọ kpàchisịrị ụlọ ahụ niile?
examples.english: Did he lock up the whole house?

gloss: a doll or toy with a human shape usually meant for children

examples.igbo: Nwa m na-egwu nwabèbi n'ụlọ.
examples.english: My child is playing with a doll at home.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara nwa gị nwabèbi?
examples.english: Did you buy your child a doll?

gloss: droppings, dung, of animals (the kind that is rolled in small balls, made especially by goats)

examples.igbo: Ewu ahụ tụrụ akpùlụ n'ogige.
examples.english: That goat dropped dung in the yard.

examples.igbo: Tinye akpùlụ ewu n'ime ala ubi.
examples.english: Put goat droppings into the farm soil.

gloss: enter into mask; wear mask (like a masquerade)

examples.igbo: Ọ bàrà n'ime àwòlò ma pụta n'ama.
examples.english: He put on the mask and came out into the square.

examples.igbo: Ònye ga-abà n'ime àwòlò n'ememme a?
examples.english: Who will wear the mask at this festival?

examples.igbo: E tinyere nnu n'enū nri ahụ.
examples.english: They put salt on that food.

examples.igbo: Akwụkwọ m ọ dị n'enū tebụl?
examples.english: Is my book on the table?

examples.igbo: Ifufe abalị tụrụ oyi n'ahụ nwata.
examples.english: The night wind chilled the child's body.

examples.igbo: Ejila mmiri oyi tụọ nwa oyi.
examples.english: Don't use cold water to chill the child.

examples.igbo: Tụchie ụzọ ahụ tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Bolt that door before you leave.

examples.igbo: O tụchiri ụzọ, ma ọ pụghị.
examples.english: He bolted the door, but he didn't go out.

examples.igbo: Ewu kà ọ bù, ọ naghị ege ntị.
examples.english: He is a fool; he doesn't listen.

examples.igbo: Ewu kà ọ bù? Gịnị mere o ji kwere ihe ahụ?
examples.english: Is he a fool? Why did he believe that?

examples.igbo: Biko nyechi m akwụkwọ m.
examples.english: Please return my book to me.

examples.igbo: O nyechighị m ego m.
examples.english: He did not return my money.

examples.igbo: Nne m na-ede ùlì n'ahụ nwa ya.
examples.english: My mother is decorating her child's body with ùlì.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-ede ùlì n'ahụ gị taa?
examples.english: Will you decorate your body with ùlì today?

gloss: provoke; seek quarrel; look for trouble

examples.igbo: Ọ na-achọ okwu n'ebe ọ bụla.
examples.english: He looks for trouble everywhere.

examples.igbo: Chọla okwu na nwoke ahụ.
examples.english: Don't look for trouble with that man.

examples.igbo: Ogogo mmiri n'osimiri arịgoro elu.
examples.english: The water level in the river has risen.

examples.igbo: Gịnị bụ ogogo mmiri taa?
examples.english: What is the water level today?

examples.igbo: Gè ntị mgbe m na-ekwu okwu.
examples.english: Listen when I am talking.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ege m ntị mgbe m na-ekwu?
examples.english: Are you listening to me when I speak?

examples.igbo: Obere ibelibe nkụ banyere n'ụkwụ ya.
examples.english: A small splinter entered his foot.

examples.igbo: Wepụ ibelibe nkụ ahụ n'aka m.
examples.english: Remove that splinter from my hand.

gloss: settle a matter; resolve a quarrel

examples.igbo: Ndị okenye bìrì okwu ụmụaka n'udo.
examples.english: The elders settled the children's quarrel peacefully.

examples.igbo: Ị bìrì okwu ụmụaka ahụ n'ụtụtụ a?
examples.english: Did you settle those children's quarrel this morning?

gloss: stuff from one position to another

examples.igbo: Faghalịa akpa a n'oche gaa n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: Move this bag from the chair into the room.

examples.igbo: O faghalịrị uwe ya n'igbe gaa n'akụkụ ọzọ.
examples.english: He moved his clothes from the box to another side.

examples.igbo: O bìrì ego n'aka nwanne ya.
examples.english: He borrowed money from his brother.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ebi ego n'aka ndị agbataobi?
examples.english: Are you borrowing money from neighbours?

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ gbụrụ ọnụmmiri n'ala ụlọ.
examples.english: That child spat saliva on the floor of the house.

examples.igbo: Gbụla ọnụmmiri n'ihu nwanne gị ọzọ.
examples.english: Don't spit on your brother's face again.

examples.igbo: O kụgọrọ mkpara ahụ n'ala ka ọ gbọọ.
examples.english: He hit that stick on the ground so it bent.

examples.igbo: Kụgọọ osisi a ka ọ gbọọ.
examples.english: Hit this stick so it bends.

examples.igbo: Anwụ chagburu ahịhịa n'ubi taa.
examples.english: The sun scorched the weeds in the farm today.

examples.igbo: Okpomọkụ na-achagbu akwụkwọ osisi n'ogige.
examples.english: The heat is withering the leaves of the tree in the garden.

examples.igbo: Okonko ahụ dị tọgbọrọ chakoo n'akụkụ ụlọ.
examples.english: That empty container is lying empty beside the house.

examples.igbo: Jupụta okonko a na mmiri dị ọcha.
examples.english: Fill this empty container with clean water.

examples.igbo: Ègbenu ahụ na-akụ n'isi ụtụtụ.
examples.english: That cock crows early in the morning.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ègbenu ji achụ ụmụ ọkụkọ?
examples.english: Why is the cock chasing the chicks?

examples.igbo: Ngosi ahụ malitere n'oge taa.
examples.english: That show started early today.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-aga ngosi a n'abalị a?
examples.english: Will you go to this show tonight?

examples.igbo: Òwu ọkū nke oriọna ahụ kwụrụ ọkụ.
examples.english: The wick of that lamp burned.

examples.igbo: Bee òwu ọkū ahụ ka ọ dị mkpụmkpụ.
examples.english: Cut that wick so it is short.

gloss: be bent or crooked; not be straight, especially in many places

examples.igbo: Osisi ahụ gbagọrọ agbagọ n'ọhịa.
examples.english: That tree is bent crooked in the field.

examples.igbo: Ihe a gbagọrọ agbagọ, gịnị mere i ji zụta ya?
examples.english: This thing is crooked, why did you buy it?

gloss: life-size status of carved wood, representing Ànì

examples.igbo: Ndị okenye kpụrụ ezē Ànì n'ụlọ àlà.
examples.english: The elders carved an Ànì statue in the shrine.

examples.igbo: Ezē Ànì ahụ dị nnukwu ma dị egwu.
examples.english: That Ànì statue is big and fearsome.

note: Cultural term; examples are plausible but usage is specialized.

examples.igbo: Nàa gboo, ka anyị hụ ọzọ.
examples.english: Farewell, until we see again.

examples.igbo: Ọ sịrị nàa gboo ma lawa.
examples.english: She said farewell and went home.

examples.igbo: Rufèga mmanụ ahụ n'elu azụ̀.
examples.english: Pour that oil over the fish.

examples.igbo: Ọ rufègara mmiri n'elu osikapa.
examples.english: She poured water over the rice.

examples.igbo: Padò n'ala ka ike gwụ gị.
examples.english: Lie down if you are tired.

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ padọrọ n'ala n'oge ehihie.
examples.english: The child lay down in the afternoon.

examples.igbo: Mmùmù ọnwa na-enwu n'abalị.
examples.english: Stars shine at night.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ mmùmù ọnwa ahụ n'elu igwe?
examples.english: Did you see that star in the sky?

gloss: fish-fry; small sprat-like fish caught when Niger rises

examples.igbo: Anyị zụtara èlèm n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: We bought fish-fry at the market today.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-ere èlèm ndị a?
examples.english: Will you sell these fish-fry?

note: Specific fish term; examples are plausible.

examples.igbo: Onye dibịa sùrù nsọ ahụ n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: The dibia lifted that taboo in the morning.

examples.igbo: Sùọ nsọ a tupu ụmụaka abanye n'ọhịa.
examples.english: Lift this taboo before the children enter the forest.

examples.igbo: Gịnī kpàtàlù ị bịaghị n'ụlọ akwụkwọ taa?
examples.english: Why didn't you come to school today?

examples.igbo: Gịnī kpàtàlù ọ na-ebe akwa?
examples.english: Why is he crying?

note: The expression is colloquial; both sentences are questions by nature.

gloss: name of a town and its market

examples.igbo: Anyị gara ahịa Ùkè ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: We went to Ùkè market yesterday.

examples.igbo: Ị na-aga Ùkè echi?
examples.english: Are you going to Ùkè tomorrow?

examples.igbo: O jiri cham gbaa nnụnụ ahụ.
examples.english: He used a dane-gun to shoot that bird.

examples.igbo: Cham a bụ nke gị?
examples.english: Is this dane-gun yours?

examples.igbo: Ha kpèchasịrị akpụkpọ osisi ahụ niile.
examples.english: They stripped off all the bark of that tree.

examples.igbo: Kpèchasịa ji ndị a tupu ị tinye ha n'ọkụ.
examples.english: Pare all these yams before you put them on the fire.

examples.igbo: Ọ kpụmịrị oche ya n'ebe ọkụ dị.
examples.english: He moved his chair away from the fire.

examples.igbo: Kpụmịa aka gị n'ite ọkụ ahụ!
examples.english: Move your hand away from that hot pot!

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ere nri tụ m̄gbērē n'ọnụ ụzọ ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: She retails food at the school gate.

examples.igbo: Ị na-azụ ahịa tụ m̄gbērē n'ọma ahịa?
examples.english: Do you do retail trading in the market?

examples.igbo: Gaa gụta ọkụ n'ụlọ agbataobi anyị.
examples.english: Go and fetch fire from our neighbour's house.

examples.igbo: Ọ gụtara ọkụ, o wee kwoọ nri.
examples.english: She fetched fire, and then cooked the food.

examples.igbo: O kpàchiri ụzọ ụlọ ya tupu ọ pụọ.
examples.english: He locked the door of his house before he left.

examples.igbo: Kpachie ọnụ ụzọ ahụ mgbe ị na-apụ.
examples.english: Lock that door when you are leaving.

examples.igbo: O chòrò ọka ya n'ihu ụlọ ahịa.
examples.english: She displayed her maize in front of the shop.

examples.igbo: Ị chòrọ akwa gị n'ahịa taa?
examples.english: Did you display your cloths in the market today?

examples.igbo: Nkịta anyị na-achụ anụ n'ọhịa.
examples.english: Our dog chases animals in the bush.

examples.igbo: Ị na-achụ anụ n'ubi ọka?
examples.english: Do you chase animals in the maize field?

note: ịchụ anụ is less common than ịchụ nta for hunting, so I kept the literal 'chase animals' sense.

examples.igbo: Taàtà bụ ụbọchị ahịa anyị.
examples.english: Today is our market day.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-abịa n'ụlọ anyị taàtà?
examples.english: Will you come to our house today?

examples.igbo: Nwa m nwanyị na-egwu nwa ègwu ya.
examples.english: My daughter is playing with her doll.

examples.igbo: Zụta nwa ègwu maka nwanne gị nta.
examples.english: Buy a doll for your little sister.

examples.igbo: Chidubem bụ enyi m kacha mma.
examples.english: Chidubem is my best friend.

examples.igbo: Chidubem, bịa rie nri.
examples.english: Chidubem, come and eat.

examples.igbo: Igwu akwà na-ata uwe anyị.
examples.english: Cloth-lice eat our clothes.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ igwu akwà n'ime akwa ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see cloth-lice in that cloth?

note: Igwu akwà is a recognised term for the cloth-louse, but it is rare in everyday speech.

examples.igbo: Dozie akwụkwọ gị ndene.
examples.english: Arrange your books properly.

examples.igbo: Ị na-arụ ọrụ gị ndene?
examples.english: Do you do your work properly?

note: Ndene as an adverb of manner is understood, though speakers often say nke ọma instead.

examples.igbo: Mmiri dị n'olulu ahụ dooro edo.
examples.english: The water in that well is clear.

examples.igbo: Lee ka mmiri ahụ dooro edo!
examples.english: Look how clear that water is!

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ zịrị imi ya.
examples.english: That child blew his nose.

examples.igbo: Zịa imi gị, nwa m.
examples.english: Blow your nose, my child.

examples.igbo: Mama gara ịkpa manụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: Mother went to buy oil at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị kpara manụ taa?
examples.english: Did you buy oil today?

gloss: mark something; put a mark on

examples.igbo: Ọ rìbara ewu ya ama na ntị.
examples.english: He marked his goat on the ear.

examples.igbo: Rìbaa akpa gị ama ka ị ghara ịfufu ya.
examples.english: Mark your bag so you don't lose it.

note: The inflected forms rìbara/rìbaa are correct, but the verb is more often heard with ịkwa or ide in daily speech.

gloss: see all; see clearly; see well

examples.igbo: Ahụchara m ihe niile dị n'ahịa ahụ.
examples.english: I saw everything in that market clearly.

examples.igbo: Ị hụcharala ya nke ọma?
examples.english: Have you seen it well?

note: hụcha is uncommon; the reduplicated/extensive form was rendered as best understood.

gloss: perform burial ceremony; keep funeral A gà-àkwa ozu#echi A funeral will take place tomorrow

examples.igbo: Ha na-akwa ozu nna ha taa.
examples.english: They are holding their father's funeral today.

examples.igbo: Ole mgbe ha ga-akwa ozu nwanne gị?
examples.english: When will they hold your brother's funeral?

examples.igbo: Ọnụ ọgụgụ ụmụ akwụkwọ bawanyere n'afọ a.
examples.english: The number of students increased this year.

examples.igbo: Ọ ga-abawanye ma anyị zụta ọkụkọ ọzọ.
examples.english: It will increase if we buy more chickens.

examples.igbo: Ndị mkpọrọ na-eje ije n'ùgom kwa ụtụtụ.
examples.english: The prisoners walk in the prison yard every morning.

examples.igbo: O si n'ùgom pụta mgbe anyị rutere.
examples.english: He came out of the prison yard when we arrived.

examples.igbo: Anatara m letà nna m zitere.
examples.english: I received the letter my father sent.

examples.igbo: Ị natara letà m zitere gị?
examples.english: Did you receive the letter I sent you?

gloss: calm the body; relax the body; rejuvenate the body

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ado àhụ mgbe ọ rụsịrị ọrụ ike.
examples.english: He relaxes his body after doing hard work.

examples.igbo: Dòọ àhụ, ọrụ ahụ agwụla.
examples.english: Relax, that work is finished.

examples.igbo: Anyị ji unyì okwute sie nri.
examples.english: We use coal to cook.

examples.igbo: Ì zụtara unyì okwute maka ọkụ?
examples.english: Did you buy coal for the fire?

gloss: exclamation of sympathy or pity or shock; oh dear; alas; oh

examples.igbo: Ewōō! Ọ dara n'ala.
examples.english: Oh dear! He fell down.

examples.igbo: Ewōō, gịnị mere gị?
examples.english: Oh dear, what happened to you?

examples.igbo: Agadi nwoke ahụ na-eje ije nwayọ.
examples.english: That old man walks slowly.

examples.igbo: Ị maara agadi nwoke ahụ bi n'akụkụ anyị?
examples.english: Do you know that old man who lives near us?

examples.igbo: Nwa nwoke ahụ akaniteela àrụ.
examples.english: That boy has grown in stature.

examples.igbo: Ì hụrụ otú ọ akanitela àrụ?
examples.english: Did you see how he has grown?

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka abụọ ahụ na-alụ ọgụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: Those two children are fighting at the market.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji alụ ọgụ na ya?
examples.english: Why are you fighting with him?

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ àpà n'aka ya ebe ọ dara.
examples.english: He has a scar on his hand where he fell.

examples.igbo: Ị bụ àpà n'ụkwụ gị?
examples.english: Do you have a mark on your foot?

examples.igbo: O ji amà aka tụọ ogologo osisi ahụ.
examples.english: He used a span to measure the length of that stick.

examples.igbo: Ogologo osisi ahụ bụ amà aka abụọ.
examples.english: The length of that stick is two spans.

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ nwere akantachị, ọ naghị azụ ihe.
examples.english: That man is stingy, he does not buy things.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji nwee akantachị otú a?
examples.english: Why are you so stingy like this?

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka ahụ tịkọrọ isi ha ọnụ.
examples.english: Those children knocked their heads together.

examples.igbo: Ị tịkọrọ iko abụọ ahụ ọnụ?
examples.english: Did you knock those two cups together?

examples.igbo: Mkpatụ akwụkwọ ahụ mere ka m teta.
examples.english: The rustling of those leaves woke me up.

examples.igbo: Gịnị na-eme mkpatụ n'ime ọhịa?
examples.english: What is making a rustling in the bush?

examples.igbo: A gụnyere ya na ndị ọrụ ahụ.
examples.english: He was reckoned among those workers.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-agụnye m na ndị otu ahụ?
examples.english: Will you count me as one of that group?

examples.igbo: O lọchịghaara ihe ọjọọ o mere.
examples.english: He repented of the bad thing he did.

examples.igbo: Biko lọchịghaa n'uche gị tupu i mee ihe.
examples.english: Please reflect in your mind before you act.

examples.igbo: O chapụrụ unyi ahụ n'aka ya.
examples.english: He washed the dirt off his hand.

examples.igbo: Chapụ ncha ahụ n'ihu gị ozugbo!
examples.english: Wash that soap off your face right away!

examples.igbo: Onye ahịa gọzụrụ akpụ anyị niile n'ahịa.
examples.english: The trader bought up all our cassava in the market.

examples.igbo: Ị gọzụrụ ihe niile n'ahịa taa?
examples.english: Did you buy everything in the market today?

note: Headword spelling uncertain; I used the common verb gọzụ (buy up) with inflection.

examples.igbo: Kèemesịa, anyị ga-ahụ echi n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: Goodbye, we will see tomorrow at school.

examples.igbo: Kèemesịa, ị ga-alọta n'oge taa?
examples.english: Goodbye, will you return early today?

gloss: rolled tobacco leaves, in small bits for retail

examples.igbo: Onye ahịa na-ere ùtabā èkèlèke n'ọma ahịa.
examples.english: The trader sells rolled tobacco leaves in the market.

examples.igbo: Ree m ùtabā èkèlèke ntakịrị ka m ṅụọ.
examples.english: Sell me a little rolled tobacco to smoke.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-asụ akwà n'ụtụtụ ọ bụla.
examples.english: She washes clothes every morning.

examples.igbo: Sụọ akwà ndị a tupu mmiri ezoo.
examples.english: Wash these clothes before it rains.

gloss: act as, be, a young man

examples.igbo: Ọ na-eme òkolobìà n'ahịa mgbe niile.
examples.english: He always acts like a young man in the market.

examples.igbo: Emela òkolobìà n'ihu ndị okenye.
examples.english: Don't act like a young man before elders.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-anaba n'ụlọ mgbe ahịa mechara.
examples.english: We go home when the market closes.

examples.igbo: Naba n'ụlọ ugbu a, ọ na-ezo.
examples.english: Go home now, it is raining.

examples.igbo: Ha nọ n'ụjū maka nna ha.
examples.english: They are in mourning for their father.

examples.igbo: Ị nọ n'ụjū ụnyaahụ? Gịnị mere?
examples.english: Were you in mourning yesterday? What happened?

gloss: draw; come nearer Achòlù m kà ị kpụdèbe ọkụ I want you to draw near the fire

examples.igbo: Bịa kpụdèbe ọkụ, ọ na-ajụ oyi.
examples.english: Come nearer the fire, it is cold.

examples.igbo: Ọ kpụdèbela n'akụkụ nne ya ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: She has drawn near her mother quickly.

examples.igbo: Fa ncha bịara oriri ahụ n'oge.
examples.english: All of them came to that feast on time.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ fa ncha n'ahịa taa?
examples.english: Did you see all of them in the market today?

note: Fa ncha is dialectal for standard ha niile.

examples.igbo: Osisi ahụ gbara ufìè n'ụzọ.
examples.english: That tree lay across the road.

examples.igbo: Gbaa ufìè n'elu àkwà ahụ.
examples.english: Lie crosswise on top of that bed.

note: Imperative form may vary by dialect; past form is standard.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-atamù n'okpuru ya.
examples.english: He murmurs under his breath.

examples.igbo: Gịnị ka ị na-atamù?
examples.english: What are you murmuring?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-eyi akpụkpọ ụkwū ọhụrụ.
examples.english: She is wearing new shoes.

examples.igbo: Yiri akpụkpọ ụkwū gị tupu anyị apụọ.
examples.english: Wear your shoes before we leave.

examples.igbo: Kwàǹta dị n'etiti ha abụọ.
examples.english: There is a misunderstanding between the two.

examples.igbo: Okwu a kpatara kwàǹta n'ezinụlọ.
examples.english: This matter caused disagreement in the family.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akpọ ùbọ akwalà n'abalị.
examples.english: He plays the guitar-like instrument at night.

examples.igbo: Ùbọ akwalà a na-ada ụda ọma.
examples.english: This guitar-like instrument sounds nice.

examples.igbo: Ha na-akpa àkụ̀ n'ahịa.
examples.english: They make wealth in the market.

examples.igbo: Kpaa àkụ̀ maka ọdịnihu gị.
examples.english: Garner wealth for your future.

examples.igbo: Tinye ǹza n'okpuru osisi ahụ.
examples.english: Put a support under that tree.

examples.igbo: Ǹza ahụ kwụsịrị ike.
examples.english: The support became weak.

note: I am not fully certain of ǹza in this sense; examples assume support/stay as a prop.

gloss: be popular and thus mostly used or talked about; trend; make waves

examples.igbo: Egwu a na-awù ewù n'obodo.
examples.english: This song is trending in town.

examples.igbo: Okwu ya wùrù ewù n'ahịa.
examples.english: His words made waves in the market.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-ezube ịga ahịa echi.
examples.english: We plan to go to market tomorrow.

examples.igbo: O zubeela nri abalị?
examples.english: Has she prepared dinner?

gloss: reincarnate; be born (come into the world)

examples.igbo: O kwenyere na di ya ga-alọ ụ̀wà.
examples.english: She believes her husband will reincarnate.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ lọrọ ụ̀wà n'ụlọ ha.
examples.english: The child came into the world in their family.

note: The reincarnate sense is culturally specific; the examples are plausible but not fully fixed idioms.

examples.igbo: Ọ kweere nísi mgbe o nụrụ aha ya.
examples.english: He nodded when he heard his name.

examples.igbo: Kwee nísi ma ị ghọtara ihe m kwuru.
examples.english: Nod if you understood what I said.

note: The phrase is idiomatic; the exact tone pattern of nísi may vary by dialect.

gloss: the first letter of the Igbo language alphabet; first vowel of the Igbo language alphabet

examples.igbo: A bụ mkpụrụ edemede mbụ n'asụsụ Igbo.
examples.english: A is the first letter in the Igbo language.

examples.igbo: Dee mkpụrụ edemede 'a' ugbu a.
examples.english: Write the letter 'a' now.

examples.igbo: Mama siri ofe ùtàzì taa.
examples.english: Mother cooked ùtàzì soup today.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eri ofe ùtàzì ka ofe ugu?
examples.english: Will you eat ùtàzì soup or ugu soup?

examples.igbo: Ọnụ mmīli na-agba ya n'ọnụ mgbe ọ na-ehi ụra.
examples.english: Saliva runs from his mouth when he sleeps.

examples.igbo: Hichaa ọnụ mmīli ahụ n'ọnụ nwa gị.
examples.english: Wipe that saliva off your child's mouth.

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ na-ama jìjìjì n'ihi oyi.
examples.english: That man is trembling because of the cold.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji ama jìjìjì otú a?
examples.english: Why are you trembling like this?

examples.igbo: Ịkpụ osisi n'ọhịa na-ewe ike.
examples.english: Cutting trees in the bush is hard work.

examples.igbo: Bido ịkpụ ahịhịa n'ubi ugbu a.
examples.english: Start cutting the weeds in the farm now.

note: ịkpụ here is the nominalized form of the verb kpụ; both sentences are natural, though speakers may prefer a full verb phrase.

gloss: Giant or Pouched Rat (Cricetomys gambianus Waterhouse; Yoruba òkètè)

examples.igbo: Otu eyī banyere n'ọgba anyị n'abalị.
examples.english: A giant rat entered our hole in the night.

examples.igbo: Ị riri anụ eyī mgbe ọ bụla?
examples.english: Have you ever eaten giant rat meat?

examples.igbo: Ọ gbara ụta wee gbuo nnụnụ.
examples.english: He shot an arrow and killed a bird.

examples.igbo: Gbaa ụta ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: Shoot that arrow well.

examples.igbo: O nyechara ndị ọbịa ahụ nri niile.
examples.english: She gave all the food to the guests.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-enyecha ego gị niile n'ahịa?
examples.english: Will you give away all your money at the market?

note: nyecha is a completive form of nye; the inflected forms nyechara/enyecha are the idiomatic ones.

examples.igbo: Mmiri ahụ na-agbu fìàfìà n'okpuru anyanwụ.
examples.english: That water glitters under the sun.

examples.igbo: Lee ka ọla aka ya si agbu fìàfìà!
examples.english: Look how her bracelet glitters!

note: Both sentences use gbu fìàfìà for shimmering/glittering, which is the standard sense, but the collocation is somewhat idiomatic and speakers vary.

examples.igbo: Oke ọyà gbara nwanne ya nwoke.
examples.english: Leprosy afflicted his brother.

examples.igbo: Ị na-atụ egwu oke ọyà?
examples.english: Are you afraid of leprosy?

note: Oke ọyà is widely understood as leprosy/great sickness; the second sentence could also be read as fear of serious illness generally.

gloss: put together; stack together in one place

examples.igbo: Tụkọ̀lata nkụ ndị ahụ n'otu ebe.
examples.english: Stack those pieces of firewood together in one place.

examples.igbo: Anyị tụkọ̀latara okwute ndị ahụ n'okpuru osisi.
examples.english: We stacked all those stones together under the tree.

note: The verb is right for gathering things into one place; the exact reduplication may vary by dialect.

examples.igbo: Ndị ahịa na-ana ùtụ n'ọnwa a.
examples.english: The traders are paying the exact tax this month.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ana ùtụ nke ọma?
examples.english: Are you paying the exact tax properly?

note: The headword -na ùtụ is not a form I am confident about; the sentences use ùtụ (tax) with ịna, which may not match the intended sense exactly.

examples.igbo: Pìcha mmiri ahụ niile n'ákwà ahụ.
examples.english: Squeeze all the water out of that cloth.

examples.igbo: O pìchara ihe ọṅụṅụ oroma ahụ n'ime iko.
examples.english: She squeezed the orange juice out into the cup.

examples.igbo: Anyị rụrụ mkpàla maka ụmụaka n'ogige ahụ.
examples.english: We built shelters for the children in that compound.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ mkpàla ndị ọzọ ha wuru n'ọhịa?
examples.english: Did you see the other shelters they built in the field?

note: Mkpàla as 'shelters/rough sheds' fits; the plural form is not one I hear every day.

examples.igbo: O dogburu ọkụkọ ya n'okpuru ite.
examples.english: He killed his chicken by putting it under a pot.

examples.igbo: Ị dogburu ọkụkọ ya n'igbe?
examples.english: Did you kill his chicken by placing it in a box?

note: The sense 'kill/spoil by placing something on or over it' is illustrated, but this stem is rare and my phrasing may not match every speaker.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-enyo ntụ ọka n'ime myò.
examples.english: We sift the flour in the sieve.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ myò m n'ụlọ nri?
examples.english: Did you see my sieve in the kitchen?

gloss: contest for a seat, position, post

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ezọ ọnọdù onye isi oche.
examples.english: He is contesting for the chairman's post.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ezọ ọnọdù ahụ?
examples.english: Are you contesting for that post?

examples.igbo: Ọ debàra aha ya n'akwụkwọ ndekọ.
examples.english: He wrote his name into the record book.

examples.igbo: Debà aha gị n'akwụkwọ tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Write your name into the book before you leave.

examples.igbo: Nna m tara ùgolò tupu ọ gaa n'ọrụ.
examples.english: My father chewed bitter kola before going to work.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara ùgolò n'ahịa?
examples.english: Did you buy bitter kola in the market?

examples.igbo: Ọ wetara ịfùlìfù n'emume ahụ.
examples.english: He brought up-wine to that ceremony.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere ịfùlìfù n'ụlọ?
examples.english: Do you have up-wine at home?

note: rare term; examples constructed around ceremonial use of palm wine

examples.igbo: Onye na-arịa ọrịa na-agụ ndụ.
examples.english: A sick person wants to live.

examples.igbo: Ị gụrụ ndụ mgbe ị fọrọ ntakịrị ịnwụ?
examples.english: Did you want to live when you almost died?

gloss: to dig or make a hole in the ground;

examples.igbo: O gwuru alà tinye mkpụrụ.
examples.english: He dug the ground and put seed.

examples.igbo: Gwuo alà ebe a tupu ị kụọ osisi.
examples.english: Dig the ground here before you plant a tree.

examples.igbo: Anyị kpakwudoro onwe anyị n'ụzọ ahịa.
examples.english: We encountered each other suddenly on the market road.

examples.igbo: Ọ kpakwudoro m n'ụzọ.
examples.english: He overtook me on the road.

gloss: delight; appeal to; also specifically used to refer to practice by some children who gaze steadily at person eating or holding eatable thing which greatly appeals to them

examples.igbo: Ji a na-atọ m àkpịlī.
examples.english: This yam appeals to me.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-atọ nne ya àkpịlī mgbe ọ na-eri nri.
examples.english: That child gazes steadily at his mother while she eats.

note: second sentence reflects the child-gazing usage; phrasing may vary by speaker

examples.igbo: Nne m gwesịrị ji niile n'ọdọ.
examples.english: My mother pounded all the yams in the mortar.

examples.igbo: Gwesịa ọka a tupu anyị apụọ.
examples.english: Pound all this corn before we leave.

gloss: to soak something in water or any form of liquid; soak

examples.igbo: Mama dènyere ji n'ime mmiri.
examples.english: Mother soaked yam in water.

examples.igbo: Dènye ọka a na mmiri ruo ụtụtụ.
examples.english: Soak this corn in water till morning.

examples.igbo: Anwụ chaara anyị n'ụzọ.
examples.english: The sun beat us on the road.

examples.igbo: Anwụ chaara gị n'ubi?
examples.english: Did the sun beat you on the farm?

examples.igbo: O rekọbàrà akwa ndị ahụ n'ime otu ibu.
examples.english: She rolled those clothes up into one bundle.

examples.igbo: Ị rekọbàrị akwụkwọ ndị a n'ime ngwugwu?
examples.english: Did you roll these papers up into a parcel?

note: Sense of 'roll up into' is taken literally; a different idiomatic use may exist.

examples.igbo: Bịa gbaa àzị̀anyàsị̀ taa.
examples.english: Come and take supper today.

examples.igbo: Anyị gbara àzị̀anyàsị̀ ma lakpuo ụra.
examples.english: We took supper and then slept.

note: The idiom is understood as eating the evening meal; wording of the second clause is my own.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ekwu òfegà n'ihu ndị okenye.
examples.english: He talks flippantly in front of elders.

examples.igbo: Kwụsịnụ ịkwu òfegà n'ebe a.
examples.english: Stop talking flippantly here.

gloss: mention someone's name; call by name

examples.igbo: Onye nkụzi kpọrọ ahà m n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: The teacher called my name at school.

examples.igbo: Ị kpọrọ ahà ya n'ihu mmadụ niile?
examples.english: Did you mention his name in front of everyone?

examples.igbo: Ụnù ǹcha bịara n'oge taa.
examples.english: All of you came early today.

examples.igbo: Ụnù ǹcha ga-eri osikapa a?
examples.english: Will all of you eat this rice?

examples.igbo: Adà m na-akọ akụkọ n'abalị.
examples.english: My grandfather tells stories at night.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ adà gị n'ahịa?
examples.english: Did you see your grandfather at the market?

gloss: for or in favor of - used when the verb ends with 'ị'

examples.igbo: Ọ dịrị m mkpa ịbịa ebe a.
examples.english: It was important for me to come here.

examples.igbo: Ọ ga-adịrị gị mma ịṅụ ọgwụ a.
examples.english: It will be good for you to take this medicine.

note: The suffix is shown on a verb stem ending in ị (dị), as the entry specifies.

examples.igbo: Ọ yi m egwù n'abalị ahụ.
examples.english: He frightened me that night.

examples.igbo: Atụla egwu, ihe ahụ agaghị eyi gị egwù.
examples.english: Don't be afraid, that thing will not frighten you.

examples.igbo: Osè agwō a adịghị esi ike.
examples.english: This alligator pepper is not strong.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-eji osè agwō esi ofe ụmụaka.
examples.english: We use weak alligator pepper to cook the children's soup.

note: Understood as the mild variety of alligator pepper; the name would often be used without stressing mildness.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ese èsè igbe ahụ n'ala.
examples.english: He is dragging that box along the ground.

examples.igbo: Sèrè èsè ahụ bata n'ụlọ.
examples.english: Drag that thing into the house.

note: The compound stem -sè èsè is rendered in its inflected forms; the drag/pull sense is illustrated.

examples.igbo: Aka àfè uwe m dọwara adọwa.
examples.english: The sleeve of my dress is torn.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ehicha ọsụ ya n'aka àfè uwe ya.
examples.english: He wipes his sweat with his sleeve.

gloss: clear a path, roads, of weeds

examples.igbo: Anyị bọrọ ezi n'ụzọ na-aga ahịa.
examples.english: We cleared the weeds on the path leading to the market.

examples.igbo: Bọrọnụ ezi n'ụzọ tupu mmiri abịa.
examples.english: Clear the weeds on the path before the rain comes.

examples.igbo: O benyere nwa ya achịcha.
examples.english: She cut off bread and gave it to her child.

examples.igbo: Benyere m obere anụ.
examples.english: Cut and give me a small piece of meat.

gloss: cover something using its thin and, especially, wide cover. For example, books, and curtains

examples.igbo: Sàchì akwụkwọ gị tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Cover your book before you leave.

examples.igbo: O sàchìrì efere nri ahụ n'akwa ọcha.
examples.english: She covered that plate of food with a white cloth.

gloss: slander; back-bite Ọ nà-èkwu m  okwu āzụ He is talking about me behind my back

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ekwu m okwu azụ n'obodo.
examples.english: She back-bites me in the town.

examples.igbo: Ekwula okwu azụ banyere nwanne gị.
examples.english: Do not back-bite about your sibling.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-afụchata okwu ndị okenye.
examples.english: That child is inquisitive about grown-ups' talk.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji afụchata ihe niile?
examples.english: Why do you poke into everything?

examples.igbo: Zìla ya ụlọ ugbu a.
examples.english: Send him home right now.

examples.igbo: O zìlara m ụlọ n'oge.
examples.english: He sent me home early.

examples.igbo: Òbùbù ya na-egbochi ya ịgba ọsọ.
examples.english: His stoutness stops him from running.

examples.igbo: Òbùbù nwanne ya karịrị nke ya.
examples.english: His brother's stoutness is greater than his.

examples.igbo: Ha gbufuru ụzọ n'ime ọhịa.
examples.english: They hacked a way through the bush.

examples.igbo: Gbufo ụzọ n'ọhịa ahụ ka anyị gafee.
examples.english: Hack a way through that bush so we can pass.

gloss: a form of greeting (to more than one person in the same

examples.igbo: Daalụnụ maka ọrụ unu rụrụ n'ubi.
examples.english: Thank you for the work you did on the farm.

examples.igbo: Daalụnụ, ndị ọbịa; batanụ n'ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: Thank you, guests; come into our house.

examples.igbo: O keere mmakwu na eriri ahụ.
examples.english: He made a loop in that rope.

examples.igbo: Gosi m otú e si eke mmakwu.
examples.english: Show me how a loop is made.

gloss: (= step) staircase; ladder to upper room

examples.igbo: O ji ọgbà ụnọ enū rịgoro n'ụlọ elu.
examples.english: He used the staircase to climb up to the upper room.

examples.igbo: Jide mgbidi ahụ mgbe ị na-arị ọgbà ụnọ enū.
examples.english: Hold that wall when you climb the staircase.

examples.igbo: Anyị jidere ọnọnọ buru ibu n'osimiri.
examples.english: We caught a big ọnọnọ in the river.

examples.igbo: Ị hụtụla ọnọnọ buru ibu dị otú a?
examples.english: Have you ever seen such a big ọnọnọ?

examples.igbo: Ọ magolu anyịnya wee gaa ahịa.
examples.english: He mounted a horse and went to the market.

examples.igbo: Magolu anyịnya ahụ ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Mount that horse quickly.

note: Verb stem magolu is uncommon; inflected form used as given in the entry.

gloss: tree with edible brown fruits, used to sweeten wine

examples.igbo: Mkpụrụ ọnọnọō na-atọ mmanya ụtọ.
examples.english: The fruit of ọnọnọō sweetens wine.

examples.igbo: Ị maara ọnọnọō a na-eji atọ mmanya ụtọ?
examples.english: Do you know the ọnọnọō used to sweeten wine?

gloss: charge to a fight or contest; energetic or intimidating display before a fight or contest

examples.igbo: Ndị otu ahụ mere ikpirikpọọgụ tupu egwuregwu amalite.
examples.english: That team did a charge before the match started.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ikpirikpọọgụ ha mere n'ama egwuregwu?
examples.english: Did you see the charge they made at the playground?

examples.igbo: O nyere nwa ya nsụsụ ọnụ tupu ọ lakpuo.
examples.english: She gave her child a kiss before he slept.

examples.igbo: Ị na-enye nne gị nsụsụ ọnụ tupu ị pụọ?
examples.english: Do you give your mother a kiss before you leave?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-eme anya ụlā n'ihi ọrụ ike.
examples.english: He is drowsy because of hard work.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eme anya ụlā n'ehihie?
examples.english: Are you drowsy in the afternoon?

examples.igbo: Nne m zụtara osè oyìbo n'ahịa.
examples.english: My mother bought English pepper at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị tinyere osè oyìbo na ofe?
examples.english: Did you put English pepper in the soup?

gloss: be sensible; have a sense of reasoning

examples.igbo: Nwa a nwere uchè, ọ na-ege ntị.
examples.english: This child is sensible; he listens.

examples.igbo: Nwee uchè, ghara ikwu okwu nzuzu.
examples.english: Be sensible, don't say foolish things.

examples.igbo: Onye ọbịa zònyere n'ime ụlọ wee nọdụ ala.
examples.english: The visitor stepped into the house and sat down.

examples.igbo: Zònye n'ime ụgbọ ahụ ngwa ngwa, anyị na-apụ.
examples.english: Step into that vehicle quickly, we are leaving.

note: Illustrated the 'step in' sense.

examples.igbo: Anyị ji ụgbọ ojō gafee osimiri ahụ.
examples.english: We used a small canoe to cross that river.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ụgbọ ojō n'akụkụ mmiri?
examples.english: Did you see the small canoe by the water?

examples.igbo: Tutu anyị rie nri, anyị ga-asa aka.
examples.english: Before we eat, we will wash our hands.

examples.igbo: Tutu ị pụọ, kpọọ m.
examples.english: Before you leave, call me.

note: Treated as a variant of tupu, meaning 'before'.

examples.igbo: Ànì ebe a na-acha akwụkwọ ndụ.
examples.english: The soil here is green.

examples.igbo: Kpachara anya, ànì ebe ahụ na-amị amị.
examples.english: Be careful, the ground there is slippery.

examples.igbo: Ọgwụ osisi a gbara miri emi n'ala.
examples.english: The root of this tree went deep into the ground.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ọgwụ osisi a n'ala?
examples.english: Did you see the root of this tree on the ground?

note: Used ọgwụ in the sense of root, with osisi for clarity.

gloss: announce news, usually to summon people to a meeting

examples.igbo: Onye isi lìrì òlìlì na e nwere nzukọ echi.
examples.english: The chief announced that there is a meeting tomorrow.

examples.igbo: Lìa òlìlì ka ndị obodo bịa nzukọ ahụ.
examples.english: Announce the news so the villagers come to that meeting.

examples.igbo: O kwụrụ elili n'ime ụlọ ya n'abalị.
examples.english: He hanged himself in his room at night.

examples.igbo: Ị nụla na ọ kwụrụ elili?
examples.english: Have you heard that he hanged himself?

examples.igbo: Ọrụ ànì mmanya ahụ dị n'ala ite.
examples.english: The dregs of that wine are at the bottom of the pot.

examples.igbo: Wepụ ọrụ ànì mmanya ahụ tupu ị ṅụọ ya.
examples.english: Remove the dregs of that wine before you drink it.

examples.igbo: Mmiri ọlụlụ riri ubi ọka anyị niile.
examples.english: The flood water destroyed all our maize farms.

examples.igbo: Mmiri ọlụlụ arịgoro n'osimiri?
examples.english: Has the flood water risen in the river?

note: Headword is written 'mmili ōlulu'; the examples use the standard Igbo form mmiri ọlụlụ.

examples.igbo: Nne m na-akụ ofe n'efere ụmụaka.
examples.english: My mother is scooping soup into the children's plates.

examples.igbo: Kụọ ofe n'efere m, biko.
examples.english: Scoop soup into my plate, please.

examples.igbo: Onye nkuzi ahụ nefere anya mmejọ ụmụ akwụkwọ ya.
examples.english: That teacher overlooked his pupils' offence.

examples.igbo: Nefee anya ihe ọ na-eme, ọ bụ nwata.
examples.english: Overlook what he is doing, he is a child.

examples.igbo: Osimiri ahụ dị ọkara kilomita n'ụfịe.
examples.english: That river is half a kilometre in width.

examples.igbo: Bee osisi ahụ n'ụfịe, ọ bụghị n'ogologo.
examples.english: Cut that wood crosswise, not lengthwise.
