examples.igbo: Anyị na-aga ụlọ akwụkwọ n'ọnwa asatọ.
examples.english: We go to school in the eighth month.

examples.igbo: Ọnwa asatọ bụ oge udu mmiri?
examples.english: Is the eighth month the rainy season?

examples.igbo: Ahụrụ m nwa ahụ n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: I saw that child at the market today.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ụlọ ọhụrụ anyị n'ebe ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see our new house there?

gloss: last till dawn; last till the following morning

examples.igbo: Egwu ahụ fọrọ chi n'abalị ahụ.
examples.english: The dance lasted till dawn that night.

examples.igbo: Egwu ahụ ọ fọrọ chi n'abalị ahụ?
examples.english: Did the dance last till dawn that night?

note: Used the inflected form fọrọ chi; the headword is a phrase.

gloss: cry very much; sob (harder than -kwa akwa)

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ chìrì akwa abalị niile.
examples.english: That child sobbed all night.

examples.igbo: Achìla akwa, ihe ahụ agafeela ugbu a.
examples.english: Don't sob, that thing has passed now.

examples.igbo: Onye ọ bụla n'ùwa mmadù na-achọ ego.
examples.english: Everyone in the world of men seeks money.

examples.igbo: Chee echiche nke ọma banyere ùwa mmadù.
examples.english: Think carefully about the world of men.

examples.igbo: Òtịta ọkụkọ siri ike maka nwa ọhụrụ.
examples.english: Chewing chicken is hard for a baby.

examples.igbo: Ị na-anụ òtịta nkịta n'abalị a?
examples.english: Do you hear the dog's gnawing tonight?

gloss: pierce to have a hole; puncture

examples.igbo: Ọ dụpụrụ taya ụgbọala ahụ.
examples.english: He punctured that car tire.

examples.igbo: Dụpụ akpa ahụ ka mmiri pụta.
examples.english: Puncture that bag so water comes out.

note: The headword's vowel harmony and inflection are uncertain; used dụpụrụ and dụpụ.

examples.igbo: Ọ dịnyelụrụ nwanne ya n'okwu ahụ.
examples.english: He sided with his brother in that matter.

examples.igbo: Dịnyelụ m n'ụlọ ikpe, anyị ga-emeri.
examples.english: Side with me in court, we will win.

note: Inflected the verb stem as dịnyelụrụ and imperative dịnyelụ.

examples.igbo: O ji mma kpị̀rị eriri ahụ.
examples.english: He used a knife to clip that rope.

examples.igbo: Kpị̀ mkpịsị aka gị tupu ị rie nri.
examples.english: Clip your fingernails before you eat.

note: Used kpị̀rị for past and kpị̀ for imperative.

examples.igbo: Ọ mụpùtara nwa nwoke n'ụlọ ọgwụ.
examples.english: She gave birth to a boy in the hospital.

examples.igbo: Osisi ahụ mụpùtara mkpụrụ ọhụrụ.
examples.english: That tree brought forth new seeds.

examples.igbo: Ọ bìniri ọtọ mgbe ọ hụrụ anyị.
examples.english: He stood up when he saw us.

examples.igbo: Bìni ọtọ, oche ahụ dị unyi.
examples.english: Stand up, the seat is dirty.

note: Inflected the stem as bìniri and imperative bìni.

examples.igbo: Ogē òbùnà anyị na-aga ahịa, anyị na-azụ azụ.
examples.english: Every time we go to market, we buy fish.

examples.igbo: Kpọọ m ogē òbùnà ị chọrọ enyemaka.
examples.english: Call me any time you need help.

note: Used the phrase as an adverbial; spelling follows the headword.

examples.igbo: Ọ kpàchara ajị anū ehi ahụ.
examples.english: He cropped that cow's hair.

examples.igbo: Kpàcha ajị anū atụrụ tupu oge oyi.
examples.english: Cut the sheep's hair before winter.

examples.igbo: M na-aga ọrụ n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: I go to work in the morning.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-abịa n'ụtụtụ ma ọ bụ n'ehihie?
examples.english: Will you come in the morning or in the afternoon?

examples.igbo: Nwàne ka ị gaa ebe ahụ taa.
examples.english: Try to go there today.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-anwàne ịga ebe ahụ.
examples.english: He is trying to go there.

note: Nwàne is less common for 'try' than gbalịa; I am not fully certain of the inflections.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-asụ n̄sụ̄ mgbe ọ na-atụ egwu.
examples.english: That child stutters when he is afraid.

examples.igbo: Anọla na-asụ n̄sụ̄, kwuo okwu nwayọọ.
examples.english: Don't stammer, speak slowly.

gloss: suffer; punish; be in suffering, trouble

examples.igbo: Ọ tara afụfụ n'aka ọrịa ahụ.
examples.english: He suffered from that illness.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ha ji ata afụfụ?
examples.english: Why are they suffering?

gloss: launch a fight at someone; attack

examples.igbo: Ndị agha lụsoro obodo ahụ ọ̀gụ̀.
examples.english: The soldiers attacked that town.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji lụsoro nwanne gị ọ̀gụ̀?
examples.english: Why did you attack your brother?

examples.igbo: Buruka osisi ahụ n'akụkụ ụzọ.
examples.english: Carry that log aside from the road.

examples.igbo: Ọ burukara akpa ya n'akụkụ.
examples.english: He moved his bag aside.

gloss: arriving and meeting with luck; encountering luck at arrival (e.g. meeting a friend at table on arrival at his house)

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ ụkwụ ọma ka ọ bịara zute anyị n'ụlọ.
examples.english: It was good luck that he arrived and met us at home.

examples.igbo: Ị bịara zute anyị n'oge nri; ọ bụ ụkwụ ọma gị?
examples.english: You arrived and met us at mealtime; is it your good luck?

examples.igbo: Zo n'ime ụlọ ahụ.
examples.english: Hide in that room.

examples.igbo: Ọ zoro n'azụ osisi.
examples.english: He hid behind the tree.

examples.igbo: Di ọkpala m na-akụ ọka n'ugbo.
examples.english: My first-born son farms corn.

examples.igbo: Di ọkpala gị ọ̀ nọ n'ụlọ?
examples.english: Is your first-born son at home?

examples.igbo: Àkpà a dị arọ.
examples.english: This bag is heavy.

examples.igbo: Buru àkpà ahụ tinye n'ụlọ.
examples.english: Carry that bag into the house.

examples.igbo: Obodo abụọ na-ebu agha.
examples.english: Two towns are waging war.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere obodo anyị ji ebu agha?
examples.english: Why is our town waging war?

examples.igbo: Oge ọ ga-ewe dị nnọọ ụbọchị atọ.
examples.english: The time it will take is just three days.

examples.igbo: Ọ dị nnọọ otu puku naira?
examples.english: Is it just one thousand naira?

note: Used here in the sense of 'just/only' in quantity expressions.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-agbatị onwe ya tupu ọ gbaa ọsọ.
examples.english: He stretches himself before running.

examples.igbo: Gbatịa onwe gị mgbe ọ bụla ị tetara.
examples.english: Stretch yourself whenever you wake up.

examples.igbo: Nkịta tabìsị̀rị̀ ọkpụkpụ ahụ.
examples.english: The dog bit the bone into pieces.

examples.igbo: Tabìsị̀ anụ ahụ ntakịrị.
examples.english: Bite the meat into little pieces.

gloss: ground corn mixed with oil condiments, and fried

examples.igbo: Nne m ghere ịkpàkele maka nri ụtụtụ.
examples.english: My mother fried ịkpàkele for breakfast.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eri ịkpàkele?
examples.english: Will you eat ịkpàkele?

examples.igbo: Ndị nkịtị na-ata ahụhụ n'ihi oké ụtụ isi.
examples.english: Common people suffer because of high taxes.

examples.igbo: Gọọmentị kwesịrị inyere ndị nkịtị aka.
examples.english: Government should help common people.

gloss: a calabash, netted with strings of cowries, which is shaken as a musical instrument (= derived from Yoruba sèkèrè)

examples.igbo: Onye na-akụ ùshàkà n'emume?
examples.english: Who plays the ùshàkà at the ceremony?

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ na-akụ ùshàkà nke ọma.
examples.english: That child plays the ùshàkà well.

examples.igbo: Enweghị m ènyò anya, apụghị m ịgụ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: I don't have glasses, I can't read.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ènyò anya m?
examples.english: Did you see my glasses?

examples.igbo: Ọyā òmìmì mere ka ụkwụ nwa ya gbagọọ.
examples.english: Rickets made her child's legs bow.

examples.igbo: Ị na-enye nwa gị vitamin ka ọ ghara ịrịa ọyā òmìmì?
examples.english: Are you giving your child vitamins so he won't get rickets?

examples.igbo: Mee àsalà nye ndị ọbịa gị.
examples.english: Be polite to your guests.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-eme àsalà nye ndị okenye.
examples.english: That child is polite to elders.

examples.igbo: Okpokolo isī ya gbajiri n'ihi ihe mberede ahụ.
examples.english: His skull broke because of that accident.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-egbu anụ, na-atụfukwa okpokolo isī ya.
examples.english: He kills animals and throws away their skulls.

examples.igbo: Anyị zụtara ìkpoòkpò ụnò dị n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: We bought Tilapia aurea at the market today.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-esi ìkpoòkpò ụnò dị ofe?
examples.english: Will you cook Tilapia aurea soup?

note: Uncertain about exact usage of this fish species name.

examples.igbo: Ha na-arụsi ọrụ ike n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: They are busy at school.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-arụsi ọrụ ike, ọ gaghị eso anyị gaa ahịa.
examples.english: She is busy, she won't go to the market with us.

examples.igbo: Nna m bụ ife nŋòmi maka ụmụ ya.
examples.english: My father is an example for his children.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eso ife nŋòmi nke ndị okenye?
examples.english: Are you following the example of elders?

examples.igbo: O zuru nzuzù n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: He acted foolishly at the market today.

examples.igbo: Ị na-azuzu nzuzù ọzọ?
examples.english: Are you acting foolishly again?

note: Unsure of correct verb inflection for 'zuzù nzuzù'; examples are tentative.

gloss: imitation coffin containing plantain stem representing dead person, thrown away in the bush during the second burial

examples.igbo: Ha mere ìgbùdù maka nwoke ahụ nwụrụ.
examples.english: They made an imitation coffin for that man who died.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ìgbùdù ha tụfuru n'ọhịa?
examples.english: Did you see the imitation coffin they threw away in the bush?

examples.igbo: O nwere nlògha n'obi ya.
examples.english: He had repentance in his heart.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eme nlògha ma i mehiere?
examples.english: Will you repent if you do wrong?

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ ọghà ịkụ nne gị.
examples.english: It is an abomination to beat your mother.

examples.igbo: Ha na-akpọ ya ọghà n'obodo anyị.
examples.english: They call it an abomination in our town.

examples.igbo: O ji mma bọ̀kàsị̀ anụ ahụ.
examples.english: He used a knife to cut that meat in pieces.

examples.igbo: Bọ̀kàsị̀ azụ̀ ahụ tupu ị tinye ya n'ite.
examples.english: Cut that fish in pieces before you put it in the pot.

note: The verb bọ̀kàsị̀ is uncommon; I have used it transitively as 'cut into pieces'.

examples.igbo: Ewu ahụ na-ebe ọnwụ onwụ n'ogige.
examples.english: That goat is crying in death-agony in the compound.

examples.igbo: Ị nụrụ ka ọ na-ebe ọnwụ onwụ?
examples.english: Did you hear it crying in death-agony?

examples.igbo: Anyị hụrụ ozu ehī n'akụkụ ụzọ.
examples.english: We saw a cow carcass by the roadside.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ozu ehī ji dị n'ama?
examples.english: Why is a cow carcass in the compound?

examples.igbo: Ọ rịgoro n'elu osisi.
examples.english: He climbed up the tree.

examples.igbo: Rịgo elu mgbidi ahụ ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Climb up that wall quickly.

examples.igbo: Nwanne m nwoke nọ n'otu ọgbọ m.
examples.english: My brother is in my age group.

examples.igbo: Ị nọ n'otu ọgbọ m?
examples.english: Are you in my age group?

examples.igbo: Anụ ahụ rìdoro m n'akpịrị.
examples.english: That meat choked me in the throat.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka ọkpụkpụ rìdo gị.
examples.english: Don't let a bone choke you.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-aga ahịa n'mgbè efìfìè.
examples.english: We go to market during the afternoon.

examples.igbo: Ị na-abịa n'mgbè efìfìè?
examples.english: Are you coming during the afternoon?

examples.igbo: Ndị gboo rụrụ nnukwu ụlọ.
examples.english: The ancients built big houses.

examples.igbo: Ị na-anụ akụkọ ndị gboo?
examples.english: Do you hear the ancients' stories?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-azọcha èzi īlo ya kwa ụtụtụ.
examples.english: She sweeps her house precincts every morning.

examples.igbo: Ùmụaka na-egwuri egwu n'èzi īlo?
examples.english: Are the children playing in the house precincts?

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ bụ enwe ike, ọ pụghị iburu ibu.
examples.english: That child is a weakling; he cannot carry a load.

examples.igbo: Ị bụ enwe ike ka ọ bụ onye siri ike?
examples.english: Are you a weakling or a strong person?

examples.igbo: Òbòdò anyị dị n'akụkụ osimiri.
examples.english: Our town is by the river.

examples.igbo: Ị maara òbòdò ha ebe ha bi?
examples.english: Do you know their family/town where they live?

note: The sense of òbòdò as both town and family is not fully clear; examples use the town/local-community sense.

gloss: cooked to the extent that there is no water left in the pot on fire; burnt food on fire

examples.igbo: Ofe ahụ takụrụ n'ọkụ.
examples.english: The soup burnt on the fire.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka osikapa takụọ n'ọkụ.
examples.english: Don't let the rice burn on the fire.

examples.igbo: Akwa ahụ tụpọrọ ntụpọ mmanụ.
examples.english: That cloth has oil spots.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ihu ya ji atụpọ ntụpọ?
examples.english: Why does his face have spots?

examples.igbo: Nnà ukwu m nyere m ọrụ taa.
examples.english: My boss gave me work today.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akwanyere nnà ukwu gị ùgwù?
examples.english: Do you respect your boss?

gloss: let one pass, give way to

examples.igbo: Biko, chàlụ m n'ụzò.
examples.english: Please give way to me.

examples.igbo: Ọ chàlụrụ anyị n'ụzò n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: He gave way to us on the road.

gloss: take a somersault into water; dive (= -kpọ ụgbà)

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-apịa ụgbà n'osimiri.
examples.english: The children are diving in the river.

examples.igbo: Pịa ụgbà n'ime mmiri ahụ.
examples.english: Dive into that water.

examples.igbo: Anà m àsụ akwà n'akụkụ ụlọ.
examples.english: I am washing clothes beside the house.

examples.igbo: Anà m àsụ akwà, ị ga-enyere m aka?
examples.english: I am washing clothes; will you help me?

examples.igbo: Anyị zùkọrọ n'ahịa ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: We met at the market yesterday.

examples.igbo: Ndị ọrụ na-ezùkọ n'ụlọ nzukọ kwa ụtụtụ.
examples.english: The workers assemble in the meeting hall every morning.

examples.igbo: O sụtụrụ nwa ya ọnụ.
examples.english: She pecked her child on the lips.

examples.igbo: Sụtụ nwa gị ọnụ tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Peck your child before you leave.

examples.igbo: Ụmụ okorobịa na-akù àkùkù mgbe ha na-akparịta ụka.
examples.english: Young men use slang when they are chatting.

examples.igbo: Akùla àkùkù n'ihu nne gị, ọ gaghị aghọta gị.
examples.english: Don't use slang in front of your mother, she won't understand you.

note: àkùkù as 'slang' is colloquial; spelling and tone may vary.

examples.igbo: Agbọlọ azụ tọrọ n'aka m mgbe m jidere ya.
examples.english: Fish slime stuck on my hand when I held it.

examples.igbo: Saa aka gị nke ọma, agbọlọ azụ ka dị na ya.
examples.english: Wash your hands well, fish slime is still on them.

note: agbọlọ is the usual word for fish slime; tone marks on the second syllable uncertain.

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ dọsọrọ igbe ahụ gaa n'ọnụ ụzọ.
examples.english: That man dragged the box along to the door.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-adọsọ nwa ya n'azụ mgbe ha na-aga ahịa.
examples.english: She drags her child behind her when they go to the market.

examples.igbo: Ndị ọrụ na-ewe nni n'ubi ugbua.
examples.english: The workers are harvesting in the farm now.

examples.igbo: Oge iwe nni erutela, were nkata gaa ubi.
examples.english: Harvest time has come, take a basket and go to the farm.

examples.igbo: Ha chịpụrụ oche niile n'ụlọ nzukọ.
examples.english: They took away all the chairs from the meeting hall.

examples.igbo: Chịpụ ihe ndị ahụ niile tupu mmiri abịa.
examples.english: Take away all those things before the rain comes.

examples.igbo: Ọ fọrọ afà m n'ihu ndị mmadụ niile.
examples.english: He mentioned my name in front of everybody.

examples.igbo: Ị fọrọ afà ya mgbe i kwuru okwu?
examples.english: Did you mention his name when you spoke?

gloss: heat(particularly from a light source) to death;

examples.igbo: Anyanwụ chagburu osisi ọhụrụ anyị kụrụ.
examples.english: The sun scorched the new trees we planted.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ka anyanwụ chagburu akwụkwọ ndị ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see how the sun killed those leaves?

note: chagbū is uncommon; here it is used of being killed by strong sunlight.

gloss: frown; look sullen or sad as if to show disapproval

examples.igbo: O gbarụrụ ihu mgbe m jụrụ ya ajụjụ.
examples.english: She frowned when I asked her a question.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji agbarụ ihu otú a?
examples.english: Why are you frowning like this?

examples.igbo: Nne ya kpara ude n'ahụ nwa ahụ.
examples.english: Her mother rubbed pomade on the child's body.

examples.igbo: Kpaa ude n'aka gị tupu ị pụọ n'ụlọ.
examples.english: Rub ointment on your hands before you leave the house.

examples.igbo: Onye nche ahụ dụrụ ọfọlò bọọlụ ahụ gaa n'ihu.
examples.english: The goalkeeper punted the ball forward.

examples.igbo: Dụọ ọfọlò bọọlụ ahụ gaa n'ihu.
examples.english: Punt the ball forward.

note: Taken in the football sense of 'punt'; ọfọlò is a borrowing and its spelling varies.

gloss: grind dry thing (not thoroughly); break into splinters or pieces

examples.igbo: Kpọlì nkụ ahụ ntakịrị ka ọ mụọ ọkụ ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Break that firewood into small pieces so it catches fire quickly.

examples.igbo: Ọ kpọlịrị ọka ahụ ntakịrị tupu o sie ya.
examples.english: She broke the corn into small bits before cooking it.

note: Rare verb; the two uses (firewood, corn) are my best fit for 'break dry things into small pieces'.

gloss: warn; admonish; exhort (compare -dọ aka na ntì)

examples.igbo: Nna m dọrọ m ntì ka m ghara ịgba ọsọ n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: My father warned me not to run on the road.

examples.igbo: Dọọ ha ntì ka ha na-abịa n'ọrụ n'oge.
examples.english: Warn them to come to work early.

gloss: confess voluntarily to crime, abomination or other bad deeds

examples.igbo: O sara n'ọnū na ya zuuru ego ahụ.
examples.english: He confessed that he stole the money.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-asa n'ọnū gị niile n'ihu ndị obodo?
examples.english: Will you confess everything before the villagers?

examples.igbo: Ònogbò na-ejide oke n'ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: The cat catches rats in our house.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ònogbò pụọ n'ọnụ ụzọ?
examples.english: Did you see the cat run out through the door?

examples.igbo: Nna m pụrụ ijè gaa Aba ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: My father travelled to Aba yesterday.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-apụ ijè n'ọnwa ọzọ?
examples.english: Will you travel next month?

examples.igbo: Ibè nọ n'ụlọ nga kemgbe afọ abụọ.
examples.english: Ibe has been in prison for two years.

examples.igbo: Ì ma na Ibè nọ n'ụlọ nga?
examples.english: Do you know that Ibe is in prison?

note: Written in standard orthography (nọ, ụlọ) rather than the entry's tone-marked ò/ō.

examples.igbo: O ji ọbù akā ya kpuchie anya ya.
examples.english: He covered his eyes with the palm of his hand.

examples.igbo: Ọbù akā ya gbara ọkụ n'ọkụ ahụ.
examples.english: The palm of his hand was burnt by the fire.

gloss: twist yam tendrils round the stake

examples.igbo: Nna m lọjiri ji n'osisi ahụ.
examples.english: My father twisted the yam tendrils round that stake.

examples.igbo: Lọjie ji ndị a n'osisi tupu anyanwụ apụta.
examples.english: Twist these yam tendrils round the stakes before the sun comes up.

note: The inflected forms lọjiri/lọjie are my best rendering of the stem -lọji.

examples.igbo: Ọ chịlịrị ego ahụ niile maka onwe ya.
examples.english: He took all that money for himself.

examples.igbo: Ọ chịlịrị ọkara ala nna ya.
examples.english: He took half of his father's land to himself.

note: I am not fully sure of this verb's exact sense; the examples are tentative and I would check them with a speaker.

examples.igbo: E nwere akwà mgbòchi n'elu windo ụlọ m.
examples.english: There is a curtain on the window of my house.

examples.igbo: Wepụ akwà mgbòchi ahụ saa ya.
examples.english: Take down that curtain and wash it.

examples.igbo: O nyere ndị ọbịa nnù ji.
examples.english: He gave the guests four hundred yams.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara nnù ji n'ahịa?
examples.english: Did you buy four hundred yams at the market?

note: nnù as 400 is uncommon in everyday counting; examples constructed around the numeral sense.

examples.igbo: O bipụtara akwụkwọ ọhụrụ.
examples.english: He published a new book.

examples.igbo: Ị bipụtala akwụkwọ gị?
examples.english: Have you published your book?

examples.igbo: O fichara aka ya na ákwà.
examples.english: He wiped his hand with a cloth.

examples.igbo: Ficha tebụl ahụ tupu anyị rie nri.
examples.english: Wipe that table before we eat.

examples.igbo: O gbajiri achịcha ahụ n'ime mpekere.
examples.english: He broke the bread into pieces.

examples.igbo: O nyere gị mpekere nke ego ahụ?
examples.english: Did he give you a fraction of that money?

examples.igbo: O gụmiri akwụkwọ ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: He read the book deeply.

examples.igbo: Gụmìa akwụkwọ a tupu ị baa ule.
examples.english: Study this book deeply before you take the exam.

examples.igbo: Ògwụgwọ ọrịa ahụ were ọnwa abụọ.
examples.english: The curing of that disease took two months.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ ògwụgwọ ọzọ?
examples.english: Do you want another cure?

examples.igbo: Isi ya chara awō.
examples.english: His hair turned grey.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere isi gị ji na-acha awō?
examples.english: Why is your hair turning grey?

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-egwu egwu n'ùdò osisi.
examples.english: The children are playing in the shade of a tree.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ùdò ya n'ala?
examples.english: Did you see its shadow on the ground?

examples.igbo: Ọ̀hụụ̀zọ̀ gwara ya na ọ ga-enwe nwa.
examples.english: The fortune teller told her that she would have a child.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ ịhụ ọ̀hụụ̀zọ̀ maka ọdịnihu gị?
examples.english: Do you want to see a fortune teller about your future?

note: The word is uncommon; examples are based on the given sense.

examples.igbo: N'ihi ọchịchịrị, anyị na-afụ ìnyègè.
examples.english: Because of the darkness, we see faintly.

examples.igbo: Ị fụrụ ìnyègè ihe ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see that thing faintly?

examples.igbo: Nwa ùyòm ahụ na-eso nne ya.
examples.english: That chick follows its mother.

examples.igbo: Olee ebe nwa ùyòm ọzọ nọ?
examples.english: Where is the other chick?

examples.igbo: Ọtụtụ mba dị na Isi Ōji na-azụ ahịa.
examples.english: Many countries in Africa trade.

examples.igbo: Ndị Isi Ōji kwesịrị ijikọ aka.
examples.english: Africans should unite.

note: Isi Ōji is archaic; I am not fully certain the examples match modern idiomatic usage.

examples.igbo: Ụlọ a bụ ǹkè fa.
examples.english: This house is theirs.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ ịhụ ubi ǹkè fa?
examples.english: Do you want to see their farm?

examples.igbo: O kwọrịrị ọka ahụ n'okwute.
examples.english: She crushed that corn on the stone.

examples.igbo: Kwọrìa ọka a tupu ị sie ya.
examples.english: Grind this corn before cooking it.

examples.igbo: Anyị ga-ebi n'ụlọ a ọkpụ tòlụ ọkpū.
examples.english: We will live in this house forever and ever.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-anọ ebe a ọkpụ tòlụ ọkpū?
examples.english: Will you stay here forever and ever?

gloss: peel; pare (yam, cassava, etc., with knife) (compare -be-cha)

examples.igbo: O bachara ji abụọ maka ofe.
examples.english: She peeled two yams for soup.

examples.igbo: Bacha ji a tupu ị sie ya.
examples.english: Peel this yam before cooking it.

examples.igbo: Ụkwụ m na-asiwa m n'abalị.
examples.english: My leg hurts me severely at night.

examples.igbo: O siwara gị mgbu n'aka?
examples.english: Did it hurt you severely in the hand?

examples.igbo: O wụkwàsịrị mmiri n'elu osisi.
examples.english: She poured water on the plant.

examples.igbo: Wụkwàsị mmanụ n'ahụ ya.
examples.english: Pour oil on his body.

examples.igbo: Orù ahụ na-arụ ọrụ n'ubi.
examples.english: That slave works on the farm.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara orù a n'ahịa?
examples.english: Did you buy this slave at the market?

gloss: variety of ùlì, whose seeds are very small in size

examples.igbo: Anyị kụrụ ùlì nkịlịsị n'ubi.
examples.english: We planted ùlì nkịlịsị in the farm.

examples.igbo: Mkpụrụ ùlì nkịlịsị dị ntakịrị.
examples.english: The seeds of ùlì nkịlịsị are small.

note: Specialized plant term; examples are simple but limited.

gloss: reckon with; regard; care for; consider (as important)

examples.igbo: Ọ na-agbànyè n'ife okwu nna ya.
examples.english: He reckons with his father's word.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ị naghị agbànyè n'ife ọrụ gị?
examples.english: Why don't you care about your work?

examples.igbo: Anyị kwudoro ibe anyị n'ahịa Eke.
examples.english: We met each other at the Eke market.

examples.igbo: Ebee ka ị kwudoro ya?
examples.english: Where did you meet him?

note: Not fully sure of this verb's inflection; the sense 'meet' is uncertain.

examples.igbo: Òka ǹtùgbu banyere n'ụkwụ nwata ahụ.
examples.english: A jigger burrowed into that child's foot.

examples.igbo: Wepụ òka ǹtùgbu dị n'ụkwụ gị.
examples.english: Remove the jigger from your foot.

examples.igbo: Ògba mgba ahụ tụrụ nwa okorobịa ahụ n'ala.
examples.english: That wrestler threw the young man to the ground.

examples.igbo: Kedu onye bụ ògba mgba kacha n'obodo a?
examples.english: Who is the best wrestler in this town?

gloss: a tree whose fruit resembles ụdalā ènwè in shape; when ripe, the fruit is red in colour

examples.igbo: Osisi usukē dị n'ọhịa na-amị mkpụrụ na-acha uhie uhie.
examples.english: The usukē tree in the bush bears fruit that is red.

examples.igbo: Ị hụtụla mkpụrụ usukē chara acha?
examples.english: Have you ever seen a ripe usukē fruit?

gloss: be tame, be domesticated (literally know the house)

examples.igbo: Nkịta anyị ma ụnò, ọ naghị ata mmadụ.
examples.english: Our dog is tame; it does not bite people.

examples.igbo: Ọkụkọ gị ọ ma ụnò?
examples.english: Is your fowl tame?

examples.igbo: Ògwụgwa akụkọ ifo na-atọ ụmụaka ụtọ.
examples.english: Telling folk tales pleases children.

examples.igbo: Ògwụgwa ya enyeghị m obi ụtọ.
examples.english: His telling did not please me.

gloss: (compare -gwò) pluck out; extract (e.g. like eyes); remove, scoop (e.g. coconut flesh from shell)

examples.igbo: O ghụrụ akpụkụ ahụ.
examples.english: He scooped out that coconut.

examples.igbo: Ghụọ akpụkụ a.
examples.english: Scoop this coconut.

note: Uncertain about idiomatic use of -ghụ with coconut; plausible but not common in everyday speech.

examples.igbo: A na-eji ùlume akpū eme ohiri.
examples.english: Kapok is used to make a pillow.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ùlume akpū n'osisi akpū?
examples.english: Did you see kapok on the kapok tree?

note: The term is correct but may be regional; examples are simple and clear.

gloss: be foolish, stupid; act stupidly, foolishly

examples.igbo: Ọ na-eme nzuzù mgbe niile.
examples.english: He always acts foolishly.

examples.igbo: Emela nzuzù, gee ntị.
examples.english: Don't act foolishly, listen.

gloss: joining; seam; collection; joining together, gathering, flowing together (of liquids)

examples.igbo: Mgbàkọ mmiri abụọ ahụ dị egwu.
examples.english: The joining of the two waters is scary.

examples.igbo: Lee mgbàkọ mmiri abụọ ahụ.
examples.english: Look at the joining of the two waters.

note: Used one of the listed senses (flowing together); other senses exist but are not illustrated.

gloss: long bamboo frame for carrying load; stretcher for sick person

examples.igbo: E ji akpàlàtà ebu nnukwu ibu.
examples.english: A bamboo frame is used to carry a heavy load.

examples.igbo: Bugara onye ọrịa ahụ akpàlàtà.
examples.english: Take a stretcher to the sick person.

note: The word is clear but may be less common in some dialects.

examples.igbo: O chụrụ nkịta ahụ.
examples.english: He drove away the dog.

examples.igbo: Chụpụ ụmụ ọkụkọ ahụ.
examples.english: Drive away those chickens.

gloss: snake, about 16" long, black and red, harmless but bad omen

examples.igbo: Anyị hụrụ ọzùgwè n'ụzọ.
examples.english: We saw an ọzùgwè on the road.

examples.igbo: Ị hụla ọzùgwè?
examples.english: Have you seen an ọzùgwè?

gloss: consider; ponder; meditate; put one's mind to

examples.igbo: O chịghalịrị uchè ya.
examples.english: He pondered.

examples.igbo: Chịghalịa uchè gị.
examples.english: Ponder your mind.

note: The verb form is correct, but the phrase may sound slightly formal.

examples.igbo: O chegharịrị wee rịọ mgbaghara.
examples.english: He repented and asked for forgiveness.

examples.igbo: Chegharịa tupu oge agafee.
examples.english: Reconsider before time passes.

examples.igbo: Nkịta ahụ tùrù àkịkà.
examples.english: That dog is spotted.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-atụ àkịkà?
examples.english: Is it spotted?

note: The verb phrase is understood, but the exact tone pattern may vary in speech.

examples.igbo: Nne m na-akpacha ji ọkụ n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: My mother scrapes roasted yam in the morning.

examples.igbo: Kpacha ji ọkụ ahụ tupu i rie ya.
examples.english: Scrape that roasted yam before you eat it.

examples.igbo: O zọrọ osè n'ubi ya n'afọ a.
examples.english: He transplanted pepper in his farm this year.

examples.igbo: Zọọ osè ndị a n'ubi taa.
examples.english: Transplant these peppers in the farm today.

examples.igbo: Òfufo aha ya n'ahịa wetara nsogbu.
examples.english: Mentioning his name in the market caused trouble.

examples.igbo: Òfufo aha ya na-ewe gị iwe?
examples.english: Does mentioning his name annoy you?

gloss: the act of unlocking something with a key; unlocking

examples.igbo: Ntụghe ọnụ ụzọ ya na-ewe oge.
examples.english: Unlocking its door takes time.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eme ntụghe ọnụ ụzọ tupu anyị abanye?
examples.english: Will you do the unlocking of the door before we enter?

examples.igbo: Okè ubi anyị na nke ya dị n'akụkụ osimiri.
examples.english: The boundary between our farm and his is by the river.

examples.igbo: Okè ego gị ruru ihe a?
examples.english: Is the limit of your money enough for this?

examples.igbo: E jidere ya ma tụnye ya n'ụnọ mkpọlọ.
examples.english: They arrested him and put him in prison.

examples.igbo: Olee mgbe ọ ga-esi n'ụnọ mkpọlọ pụta?
examples.english: When will he get out of prison?

examples.igbo: Nne m na-achì akwà ya n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: My mother scrubs her cloth in the morning.

examples.igbo: Chịa akwà ndị a tupu ha akpọọ nkụ.
examples.english: Scrub these clothes before they dry.

examples.igbo: Òwùwè nnī afọ a bara ụba.
examples.english: This year's harvest was abundant.

examples.igbo: Òwùwè nnī gị n'ubi bara ụba?
examples.english: Was your harvest in the farm abundant?

examples.igbo: Ha jaara ya ike mgbe o buliri nnukwu nkume.
examples.english: They praised him for strength when he lifted the big stone.

examples.igbo: Ị na-aja ya ike maka iburu osisi ahụ?
examples.english: Are you praising him for strength for carrying that log?

note: The phrase is somewhat uncommon; the examples follow one plausible idiomatic usage.

gloss: stone or wooden pestle for pepper, egusi, herbs, etc.

examples.igbo: Were aka ngwe kụọ egusi a.
examples.english: Use the pestle to pound this egusi.

examples.igbo: Ị ma ebe aka ngwe dị?
examples.english: Do you know where the pestle is?

gloss: escape; being free from a serious situation; pass any form of examination

examples.igbo: Ọ lafèrè n'ụlọ ọkụ ahụ.
examples.english: He escaped from that fire.

examples.igbo: Ị lafèrè ule a?
examples.english: Did you pass this exam?

note: The tone and inflection of lafè vary; the examples use the common verb form lafèrè.

examples.igbo: Nwa anyị sopùtara n'ụlọ nne ya.
examples.english: Our child grew up in his mother's house.

examples.igbo: Ị sopùtala?
examples.english: Have you grown up?

note: Inflected forms are based on the given stem -sopùta.

gloss: kind of drum played only for kings and chiefs on special occasions

examples.igbo: A kụrụ òzì n'ụbọchị eze ahụ.
examples.english: The òzì drum was played on the king's day.

examples.igbo: A naghị akụ òzì n'ụbọchị nkịtị.
examples.english: The òzì drum is not played on ordinary days.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ ọ̀kàchàmara n'ọrụ ugbo.
examples.english: He is an expert in farming.

examples.igbo: Ị bụ ọ̀kàchàmara n'ihe gbasara ahụike?
examples.english: Are you an expert in health matters?

examples.igbo: Wụba mmiri n'ime ite.
examples.english: Pour water into the pot.

examples.igbo: Ọ wụbàrà mmanụ n'ime karama.
examples.english: She poured oil into the bottle.

gloss: period of òmụgwò (seclusion following birth of a child); observation of òmụgwò

examples.igbo: Nwunye ya nọ n'ǹgwò ugbu a.
examples.english: His wife is in confinement now.

examples.igbo: Ǹgwò ya gwụrụ taa.
examples.english: Her confinement ended today.

gloss: to call upon especially for help; to consult, especially a supernatural being

examples.igbo: Ha kpọkùrù chi ha maka enyemaka.
examples.english: They called upon their chi for help.

examples.igbo: Kpọkù chi gị maka udo.
examples.english: Call upon your chi for peace.

examples.igbo: Ọ gbakwopùrù imē n'ọnwa mbụ.
examples.english: She aborted in the first month.

examples.igbo: Dibia ahụ gbakwopùrù imē ya.
examples.english: That dibia caused her abortion.

note: The examples use inflected forms of -gbakwopù imē.

examples.igbo: O ji amà tụọ ogologo ákwà ahụ.
examples.english: She used a measure to measure the length of that cloth.

examples.igbo: Amà osisi a dị obere.
examples.english: The measurement of this wood is small.

note: The sense of amà as 'measure' is less common; the examples keep it in that sense.

gloss: the thirty-fifth letter of the Igbo language alphabet; the twenty-seventh consonant of the Igbo language alphabet

examples.igbo: Nwa m na-amụ mkpụrụ okwu 'y' n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: My child is learning the letter 'y' at school.

examples.igbo: Depụta 'y' ugboro abụọ n'akwụkwọ gị.
examples.english: Write 'y' twice in your book.

examples.igbo: Nwanne m nwanyị na-ete ùli ārụ n'aka ya.
examples.english: My sister is drawing indigo body designs on her hand.

examples.igbo: Ùli ārụ a dị mma n'ahụ nwa agbọghọ.
examples.english: This indigo body design looks good on the girl.

gloss: leopard which is weaker and less ferocious than the real leopard

examples.igbo: Agụ ọgbà na-eri ọkụkọ anyị n'abalị.
examples.english: The lesser leopard eats our chickens at night.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ agụ ọgbà, ọ gaghị egbu mmadụ.
examples.english: It is a lesser leopard; it will not kill a person.

gloss: take food, eat (especially in early morning)

examples.igbo: Ọ na-agba àzì tupu ọ pụọ n'ụlọ.
examples.english: He eats early morning food before leaving the house.

examples.igbo: Gbaa àzì ngwa ngwa, anyị ga-apụ.
examples.english: Eat your early morning food quickly, we are leaving.

examples.igbo: Ọ kpasàpụrụ aka ya.
examples.english: He spread his hand wide open.

examples.igbo: Kpasàpụ ọnụ gị ka m hụ eze gị.
examples.english: Open your mouth wide so I can see your teeth.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-agba ọka n'anwụ̄ ka ọ kpọọ nkụ.
examples.english: We spread corn in the sun so it dries.

examples.igbo: Gbaa uwe gị n'anwụ̄ tupu ọ daa mmiri.
examples.english: Spread your clothes in the sun before it rains.

examples.igbo: Nnụnụ ahụ febàtara n'ime ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: The bird flew over into our house.

examples.igbo: Gịnị na-afebàta n'ogige anyị n'abalị?
examples.english: What flies over into our compound at night?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-aga òzùzù nkuzi n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: She attends teacher training at the school.

examples.igbo: Òzùzù nkuzi a na-ewe ọnwa atọ?
examples.english: Does this teacher training take three months?

gloss: open; open wide (e.g. hand, mouth, book, but not door)

examples.igbo: Sàghe ọnụ gị ka dọkịta hụ ihe.
examples.english: Open your mouth wide so the doctor can see.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-asàghe akwụkwọ ahụ.
examples.english: He is opening that book wide.

examples.igbo: Ndị uwe ojii jidere onye āghala ahụ n'ọhịa.
examples.english: The police arrested that lawless person in the bush.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ ka onye āghala bịa n'ụlọ gị?
examples.english: Do you want a lawless person to come to your house?

examples.igbo: Ìkùku ọgbarù na-efe site n'akụkụ osimiri.
examples.english: The south wind is blowing from the riverside.

examples.igbo: Ị na-anụ ìkùku ọgbarù na-abịa?
examples.english: Are you feeling the south wind coming?

examples.igbo: O kwusara akụkọ ahụ n'ime obodo.
examples.english: He spread that news in the village.

examples.igbo: Kwusaa ya ngwa ngwa, ka mmadụ niile nụ.
examples.english: Spread it quickly so that everyone hears.

examples.igbo: Àkwa ògàzì dị obere karịa àkwa ọkụkọ.
examples.english: A guineafowl egg is smaller than a chicken egg.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ àkwa ògàzì n'ọhịa?
examples.english: Did you see a guineafowl egg in the bush?

examples.igbo: O gburu ọkìkà n'aka nwanne ya.
examples.english: He tattooed his brother's hand.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ igbu ọkìkà n'ihu gị?
examples.english: Do you want to tattoo your face?

examples.igbo: Ndị mmadụ na-akwò èkwò n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: People are rushing in numbers at the market today.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ka ụmụaka na-akwò èkwò n'ụlọ akwụkwọ?
examples.english: Did you see how the children are rushing in numbers at school?

examples.igbo: Nye m ife ōlịla, akpịrị na-akpọ m nkụ.
examples.english: Give me something drinkable; I am thirsty.

examples.igbo: Ọ dị ife ōlịla n'ụlọ a?
examples.english: Is there something drinkable in this house?

examples.igbo: Ànì ụkwū ya na-egbu ya mgbe ọ na-eje ije.
examples.english: His heel hurts him when he walks.

examples.igbo: Ànì ụkwū gị na-egbu gị?
examples.english: Does your heel hurt you?

gloss: prepare corn meal, i.e. pap, which begins as white watery fluid, then thickens gradually as it becomes more heated, becoming very thick towards the end of the cooking. The cook keeps on stirring it throughout the cooking

examples.igbo: Nne m na-ese ògbàdụ n'ite.
examples.english: My mother is preparing pap in the pot.

examples.igbo: Sèe ògbàdụ ahụ ka ọ ghara ịracha.
examples.english: Stir that pap so it does not burn.

examples.igbo: O chịrị aka jī n'ubi taa.
examples.english: He gathered yam tendrils in the farm today.

examples.igbo: Ị na-achị aka jī?
examples.english: Are you gathering yam tendrils?

examples.igbo: Nne m rụrụ ufie n’ahụ nwa ya.
examples.english: My mother rubbed camwood on her child's body.

examples.igbo: Rụ ufie n’ahụ gị tupu ị gaa ahịa.
examples.english: Rub camwood on your body before you go to market.

examples.igbo: Kèdụ azị, anyị ga-aga ebe ahụ?
examples.english: How then, shall we go there?

examples.igbo: Ọ jụrụ m, kèdụ azị?
examples.english: He asked me, how then?

gloss: kind of lizard, brightly coloured;? Bosc's Monitor (but only about 1' long without tail)

examples.igbo: Ahụrụ m olubulu na-acha ka ọkụ n’ubi.
examples.english: I saw a brightly coloured olubulu on the farm.

examples.igbo: Ị hụla olubulu n’akụkụ osimiri?
examples.english: Have you seen an olubulu by the river?

examples.igbo: Nwa ọhụrụ ahụ na-akụ ume nke ọma.
examples.english: The baby is breathing well.

examples.igbo: Kụọ ume omimi tupu ị na-ekwu okwu.
examples.english: Breathe deeply before you speak.

examples.igbo: Ndị agha ahụ bu ngwọọ̀gụ̀ ha.
examples.english: The soldiers carried their weapons.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara ngwọọ̀gụ̀ ọhụrụ?
examples.english: Did you buy new weapons?

examples.igbo: Mkpàkalakòm na-egwu n’ala ebe ahụ.
examples.english: A centipede is crawling on the ground there.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ mkpàkalakòm n’okpuru akwa ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see a centipede under that bed?

examples.igbo: Uwe m dọkara n’oge ọrụ.
examples.english: My dress got torn during work.

examples.igbo: Dọka akwụkwọ ahụ mee abụọ.
examples.english: Tear that paper into two.

gloss: send payment (of debt or wages, to speaker) Ọ kwụ tagolụ m  ụgwọ o jì m She has sent payment of his debt to me

examples.igbo: Ọ kwụtara m ụgwọ o ji m.
examples.english: She sent me payment of the debt she owed me.

examples.igbo: Kwụtaara m ego ahụ tupu ụbọchị ahụ.
examples.english: Send me that money before that day.

examples.igbo: Ọrụ ugbo siri ikē n’oge ọkọchị.
examples.english: Farming is hard in the dry season.

examples.igbo: Jide eriri ahụ aka siri ikē.
examples.english: Hold that rope firmly.

gloss: a female spirit who gives or withholds husbands and children, and helps men to achieve ambitions such as taking a title

examples.igbo: Nne ya gara Ògwùgwù ịrịọ nwa.
examples.english: Her mother went to Ogwugwu to ask for a child.

examples.igbo: Ọ̀ bụ Ògwùgwù nyere ya aha?
examples.english: Was it Ogwugwu who gave him the title?

note: Ògwùgwù is a local deity; the sentences keep to the sense of granting children and titles.

examples.igbo: Anyị zụtara òbò asā abụọ n'ahịa.
examples.english: We bought two obo asa fish at the market.

examples.igbo: Nne m siri òbò asā n'ofe akwụ.
examples.english: My mother cooked obo asa in vegetable soup.

note: òbò asā is a river fish; the name is not in everyday use everywhere.

gloss: God creates; God is the creator

examples.igbo: Kelee Chinèekè maka nwa a o nyere gị.
examples.english: Thank Chineeke for this child he gave you.

examples.igbo: Chinèekè bụ onye kere elu igwe na ụwa.
examples.english: Chineeke is the one who created heaven and the earth.

gloss: place a load on to someone's head; laden

examples.igbo: O bolu nwanne ya ibū osisi n'isi.
examples.english: She put a load of firewood on her younger sibling's head.

examples.igbo: Boro ya ibū akwụkwọ ndị a.
examples.english: Put this load of books on him.

note: The verb is bo with the object ibū; past form bolu is the usual narration form.

gloss: cook properly (especially of meat, fish); be well cooked

examples.igbo: Anụ ewu a ghekpọrọ nke ọma.
examples.english: This goat meat is well cooked.

examples.igbo: Ghekpọọ azụ ahụ nke ọma tupu ị weta ya.
examples.english: Cook that fish properly before you bring it.

note: Inflected forms of -ghèkpò vary by dialect; ghekpọrọ and ghekpọọ are the forms used here.

examples.igbo: Ọ nọ n'ọnụ ụzò na-eche gị.
examples.english: He is standing at the doorway waiting for you.

examples.igbo: Mechie ọnụ ụzò ahụ ka ikuku ghara ịbata.
examples.english: Close that door so the wind does not come in.

gloss: wooden tool for smoothing house walls and floor

examples.igbo: O ji ǹtī ūnò na-akpụcha mgbidi ụlọ ya.
examples.english: He uses the wall-smoothing tool to smooth his house wall.

examples.igbo: Wetara m ǹtī ūnò ka m rụọ ọrụ.
examples.english: Bring me the wall-smoothing tool so I can work.

note: ǹtī ūnò is a specialized tool name; the sentences keep to its smoothing use.

gloss: make to feel sick; cause nausea

examples.igbo: Isi nri ahụ didere m obi.
examples.english: That smell of food made me feel sick.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-adìdè gị obi mgbe ị nụrụ ụda ya?
examples.english: Does it make you feel sick when you hear its sound?

note: The inflected forms didere and na-adìdè are given; usage may vary by speaker.

gloss: male name (literally life is king or life is most important)

examples.igbo: Ndùbeezè bụ nwa nwoke anyị mụrụ n'ọnwa gara aga.
examples.english: Ndubeeze is the boy we had last month.

examples.igbo: Ndùbeezè, bịa rie nri tupu ọ gbaa ọchịchịrị.
examples.english: Ndubeeze, come and eat before it gets dark.

examples.igbo: Ọ gabidoro ha n'ụzọ tupu ha erute ahịa.
examples.english: He went ahead and intercepted them on the road before they reached the market.

examples.igbo: Gaa gabido ya tupu ọ banye n'obodo.
examples.english: Go and intercept him before he enters the town.

note: gabidoro and the imperative gabido are the forms used; the verb is not common in all dialects.

examples.igbo: Ụlọ ahụ tọgbọrọ ǹkịtị kemgbe ọ hapụrụ.
examples.english: That house has been empty since he left it.

examples.igbo: Ogige ahụ ọ tọgbọrọ ǹkịtị ugbu a?
examples.english: Is that field desolate now?

examples.igbo: Onye ngana anaghị arụ ọrụ ike.
examples.english: A lazy person does not do hard work.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ ịbụ onye ngana?
examples.english: Do you want to be a lazy person?

examples.igbo: Anụ ibū na-ebu ibu dị arọ n'ụzọ.
examples.english: A beast of burden carries heavy loads on the road.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eji ehi dị ka anụ ibū?
examples.english: Are you using a cow as a beast of burden?

examples.igbo: Ànì mmānya dị n'ala ite ahụ.
examples.english: The dregs of wine are at the bottom of that pot.

examples.igbo: Ị na-aṅụ ànì mmānya n'ezie?
examples.english: Are you really drinking the dregs of wine?

gloss: knock the stick representing the god of justice (òfọ) on the ground

examples.igbo: Okenye ahụ sụrụ òfọ n'ala.
examples.english: That elder knocked the ofo stick on the ground.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-asụ òfọ tupu ị kwuo okwu?
examples.english: Will you knock ofo before you speak?

examples.igbo: O kweere ụta ya n'ọhịa.
examples.english: He strung his bow in the bush.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-akwe ụta tupu ị gaa ịchụ nta?
examples.english: Will you string the bow before you go hunting?

examples.igbo: O rọtụrụ igbe ahụ n'elu ụlọ.
examples.english: He lifted that box down from the top of the house.

examples.igbo: Biko rọtụ akpa m n'elu oche.
examples.english: Please lift my bag down from the chair.

examples.igbo: O kpàrà ǹkàtà buru ibu.
examples.english: He wove a big basket.

examples.igbo: Ị maara ịkpa ǹkàtà nke ọma?
examples.english: Do you know how to weave baskets well?

examples.igbo: Nna m rụrụ mọọ ezinụlọ anyị.
examples.english: My father looked after our family deity.

examples.igbo: Ị na-arụ mọọ gị kwa ụbọchị?
examples.english: Do you look after your deity every day?

examples.igbo: O kwaghalịrị oche ndị ahụ n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: He moved those chairs about in the room.

examples.igbo: Kwaghala akpa ndị a n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: Move these bags about in the room.

examples.igbo: Òkụ òkpòkpò jidere nwa m, ọ naghị eri nri.
examples.english: Influenza caught my child, he is not eating.

examples.igbo: Ị dara òkụ òkpòkpò ma ọ bụ naanị oyi na-atụ gị?
examples.english: Did you catch influenza, or is it just cold troubling you?

examples.igbo: Nna m na-ara òlù ụla n'oche ya.
examples.english: My father is dozing on his chair.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji na-ara òlù ụla n'oge ọrụ?
examples.english: Why are you dozing during work?

gloss: commission to buy in the market; order

examples.igbo: O nyere m àtụmafịa ka m zụta azụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: He gave me an order to buy fish at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara m ihe niile dị n'àtụmafịa m zitere gị?
examples.english: Did you buy me everything in the order I sent you?

note: The word is uncommon; sense and framing are sound but a speaker might prefer other wording.

examples.igbo: Nwanne m na-akpọ ụ̀bọọnụ̄ n'oge ezumike.
examples.english: My brother plays the harmonica during break.

examples.igbo: Ị maara ịfụ ụ̀bọọnụ̄?
examples.english: Do you know how to play the harmonica?

note: Spelling with vowel harmony is uncertain but the usage is idiomatic.

examples.igbo: Oke èkwulèkwu ya na-ewe nne ya iwe.
examples.english: His talkativeness annoys his mother.

examples.igbo: Oke èkwulèkwu adịghị mma n'ebe ọrụ.
examples.english: Bragging is not good at work.

gloss: creep, crawl, glide out (to the open)

examples.igbo: Agwọ ahụ kpụpụtara n'ime ahịhịa.
examples.english: The snake crept out from inside the grass.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ka ọ kpụpụtara n'olulu ya?
examples.english: Did you see how it crept out of its hole?

examples.igbo: O na-eme ntụtù ego n'ụlọ ahịa nna ya.
examples.english: He pilfers money in his father's shop.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eme ntụtù ego n'akpa nne gị?
examples.english: Are you pilfering money from your mother's bag?

note: The pilfering sense is the one illustrated; framing is idiomatic.

examples.igbo: Nido ewu ahụ n'osisi ka ọ ghara ịpụ.
examples.english: Tether that goat to the tree so it does not run off.

examples.igbo: O nidoro ewu ya n'ogige tupu ọ pụọ.
examples.english: He tethered his goat in the pen before he left.

note: Past form nidoro assumed; the sense and construction are right.

gloss: reduce to small units; splinter; crush (something softer or more fragile than -gwò)

examples.igbo: Nne m liri ji ahụ maka nwa ọhụrụ.
examples.english: My mother crushed that yam for the baby.

examples.igbo: Lìa ya nke ọma tupu i nye nwa ahụ.
examples.english: Crush it well before you give it to the baby.

note: Inflected forms of the stem -lì are uncertain in tone; the crushing sense is illustrated.

examples.igbo: Abalị ụnyaahụ, m rọrọ nlọ ọjọọ.
examples.english: Last night I had a bad dream.

examples.igbo: Nlọ ahụ m rọrọ tụrụ m egwu.
examples.english: The dream I dreamt frightened me.

note: nlọ as 'dream' is uncommon beside nrọ; usage is idiomatic in the sense shown.

gloss: a speech with a meaning not deducible from those of the individual words; idiom

examples.igbo: Akpaàlòokwū a siri ike nghọta.
examples.english: This idiom is difficult to understand.

examples.igbo: Ị maara ihe akpaàlòokwū a pụtara?
examples.english: Do you know what this idiom means?

gloss: a bowl shaped container, typically made of interwoven strips, that is used for carrying, sieving, or storing things; basket

examples.igbo: Nne m ji ǹkàtà ebu ji n'ubi.
examples.english: My mother uses a basket to carry yams from the farm.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara ǹkàtà ọhụrụ n'ahịa?
examples.english: Did you buy a new basket at the market?

examples.igbo: Ụmụ akwụkwọ ole na ole bịara taa.
examples.english: Few students came today.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ mkpụrụ ole na ole?
examples.english: Do you want a few seeds?

gloss: meet, welcome visitor by deliberately going out to meet him on the way or at a place, e.g. motor park

examples.igbo: Ọ zùtèrè nna ya n'ọdụ ụgbọala.
examples.english: He met his father at the motor park.

examples.igbo: Zùte ndị ọbịa n'ọnụ ụzọ.
examples.english: Meet the guests at the door.

gloss: tenth traditional month in the Nri calendar, in which the ọzō men of each lineage gather their òkìkè in the lineage's temple and offer a bloody sacrifice

examples.igbo: Ndị ọzọ na-achịkọta òkìkè n'Ọnwa Òkìkè.
examples.english: The ọzọ men gather òkìkè in Ọnwa Òkìkè.

examples.igbo: Ị na-aga emume Ọnwa Òkìkè n'afọ a?
examples.english: Are you going to the Ọnwa Òkìkè festival this year?

note: The cultural details are specific; the Igbo is sound but the exact festival phrasing may vary locally.

examples.igbo: Ha na-akpa ùkpa kemgbe ha bụ ụmụaka.
examples.english: They have been friends since they were children.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akpa ùkpa na nwata ahụ?
examples.english: Are you friends with that child?

examples.igbo: Afùlù m ị n'ahịa ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: I saw you at the market yesterday.

examples.igbo: Afùlù m ị n'ọdụ ụgbọala, ị hụghị m?
examples.english: I saw you at the motor park; didn't you see me?

examples.igbo: Onye nkuzi gụkọtara ụmụ akwụkwọ nọ n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: The teacher counted the students inside the classroom.

examples.igbo: Gụkọta ego ahụ niile tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Add up all that money before you leave.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-adọ dọònịdō n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: Children play tug-of-war at school.

examples.igbo: Olee otu e si adọ dọònịdō?
examples.english: How is tug-of-war played?

examples.igbo: Akwa a dị ọnụ ikē n'ahịa.
examples.english: This cloth is expensive in the market.

examples.igbo: Ọ dị ọnụ ikē, mana m ga-azụ ya.
examples.english: It is expensive, but I will buy it.

gloss: tree from which ufie is obtained

examples.igbo: Osisi ukpì na-eto n'akụkụ ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: The ukpi tree grows beside our house.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ nnukwu ukpì n'ọhịa taa?
examples.english: Did you see a big ukpi tree in the bush today?

examples.igbo: Anyị kwekọrịtara n'ọnụ ahịa ahụ taa.
examples.english: We agreed on that price today.

examples.igbo: Ị kwekọrọ na nwanne gị n'okwu a?
examples.english: Did you agree with your sibling on this matter?

examples.igbo: Egwu ụmụaka a nwere ndàkọrịta ụdaume.
examples.english: This children's song has vowel harmony.

examples.igbo: Ị maara ndàkọrịta ụdaume n'egwu a?
examples.english: Do you know the vowel harmony in this song?

gloss: used to identify a person or thing that is close at hand, indicated, or experienced; this

examples.igbo: Nwoke à bụ ezigbo enyi m.
examples.english: This man is my good friend.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ụlọ à n'okporo ụzọ?
examples.english: Did you see this house on the road?

examples.igbo: Aka nnī m na-egbu mgbu ugbu a.
examples.english: My right hand is hurting now.

examples.igbo: Jiri aka nnī dee aha gị.
examples.english: Use your right hand to write your name.

examples.igbo: Anyị ji ụgbọ mmīli gafee osimiri.
examples.english: We used a boat to cross the river.

examples.igbo: Ị hụla ụgbọ mmīli n'ọdụ ụgbọ?
examples.english: Have you seen a ship at the port?

examples.igbo: Osisi ọjì toro ogologo n'ọhịa anyị.
examples.english: The iroko tree grew tall in our bush.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ nnukwu ọjì n'okporo ụzọ?
examples.english: Did you see the big iroko on the road?

examples.igbo: Chinonso bụ ezigbo enyi m n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: Chinonso is my good friend at school.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere Chinonso ji na-ebe akwa?
examples.english: Why is Chinonso crying?

examples.igbo: Gụọ paragraf nke mbụ n'akwụkwọ a.
examples.english: Read the first paragraph in this book.

examples.igbo: O dere paragraf atọ banyere ọrụ ugbo.
examples.english: He wrote three paragraphs about farming.

examples.igbo: Dàalụ ọlū, unu na-arụ ọrụ ike.
examples.english: Well done, you are working hard.

examples.igbo: Mgbe ọ hụrụ ha n'ọrụ, o kwuru, dàalụ ọlū.
examples.english: When he saw them at work, he said, well done.

examples.igbo: Àkpà ụkwalà na-enye ya nsogbu n'abalị.
examples.english: Asthma troubles him at night.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ebu ọgwụ àkpà ụkwalà mgbe niile.
examples.english: He always carries asthma medicine.

examples.igbo: Biko, du aka n'ọrụ ugbo m.
examples.english: Please, help me with my farm work.

examples.igbo: Ha na-edu aka n'ubi ọka anyị.
examples.english: They help in our corn farm.

note: The verb -du aka is less common than inye aka, but this usage is attested.

gloss: seek diligently; search for carefully e.g. -kpa mkpa akụ search for palm kernels in the farm (usually by children)

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-akpa mkpa akụ n'ubi anyị.
examples.english: Children are searching for palm kernels in our farm.

examples.igbo: Kpaa mkpa akwụkwọ gị tupu ule.
examples.english: Search carefully for your books before the exam.

gloss: carry in the mouth; (fig.) be actually, still speaking Akpù m akụ nónụ  I am holding palm kernels in my mouth

examples.igbo: Akpụ m akụ nónụ n'ọnụ m.
examples.english: I am holding palm kernels in my mouth.

examples.igbo: Ọ ka na-akpụ nónụ ya okwu.
examples.english: He is still speaking.

gloss: intrude; enter (a building) forcefully or uninvited

examples.igbo: O mabàtara n'ụlọ anyị n'abalị na-enweghị ikike.
examples.english: He intruded into our house at night without permission.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka onye ọ bụla mabàta n'ebe a.
examples.english: Don't let anyone intrude here.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akaghè mgbe niile n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: He always talks foolishly in school.

examples.igbo: Kaghèkwala, gee ntị n'ihe m na-ekwu.
examples.english: Don't act foolishly, listen to what I'm saying.

examples.igbo: Nzinye ego n'aka ndị enyi na-akpatakarị nsogbu.
examples.english: Lending money to friends often causes trouble.

examples.igbo: Nzinye ego na-enyere ndị ahịa aka.
examples.english: Lending money helps traders.

gloss: mix, prepare (e.g. custard, cornflour, starch, or anything which thickens in hot water)

examples.igbo: O gbèrè custard maka ụmụ ya.
examples.english: She prepared custard for her children.

examples.igbo: Gbèe ntụ ọka ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: Mix that cornflour well.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-eme ùbụ maka achịcha n'ahịa.
examples.english: The children are scrambling for bread at the market.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ùbụ a niile n'ebe a?
examples.english: Why is there all this scrambling here?

gloss: pour away, spill (water or other liquid)

examples.igbo: Wufù mmiri ahụ n'ala, ọ dịghị mma.
examples.english: Pour that water away on the ground, it is not good.

examples.igbo: Mmiri wufùrù n'efere ahụ n'ala.
examples.english: The water spilled from that plate onto the ground.

examples.igbo: M zụtara nne m azụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: I bought fish for my mother at the market.

examples.igbo: Zụtaa m nri n'ahịa, biko.
examples.english: Buy food for me at the market, please.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-agbasa mmiri n'ọdọ.
examples.english: The children are splashing water in the pool.

examples.igbo: Gbasa mmiri ahụ n'ala, ọ dịghị mma.
examples.english: Splash that water on the ground, it is not good.

examples.igbo: Ndị ohi ahụ me n'ike banye n'ụlọ.
examples.english: Those thieves forcefully entered the house.

examples.igbo: Emela n'ike n'ebe nwa ahụ nọ.
examples.english: Do not be violent with that child.

examples.igbo: O rọrọ m mbọ n'aka m.
examples.english: She pinched me on my hand.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji rọọ m mbọ?
examples.english: Why did you pinch me?

examples.igbo: Azịzà anyaanwū na-enwu n'ụlọ.
examples.english: A beam of light is shining in the house.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ azịzà anyaanwū n'elu mmiri?
examples.english: Did you see the beam of light on the water?

gloss: wrap a cloth about the body

examples.igbo: O kowàsịrị akwà n'úkwù ya.
examples.english: She wrapped a cloth about her waist.

examples.igbo: Kowàsị akwà ahụ n'úkwù gị.
examples.english: Wrap that cloth about your waist.

examples.igbo: O bòkapùrù akụkụ akwụkwọ ahụ.
examples.english: He cut out a part of that paper.

examples.igbo: Bòkapù foto ahụ n'ime akwụkwọ.
examples.english: Cut out that photo from the paper.

examples.igbo: Ọdịdị ugwu ahụ dị mmā n'anya.
examples.english: The appearance of that hill is a pleasant sight.

examples.igbo: Ihe a dị mmā n'anya nke ukwuu.
examples.english: This thing is very pleasant to the eye.

examples.igbo: Echefuru m àkpà ego m n'ụlọ.
examples.english: I forgot my purse at home.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ àkpà ego m n'ahịa?
examples.english: Did you see my purse at the market?

gloss: tickle; prod or touch some part of a person's body, lightly, such that it causes the person to laugh

examples.igbo: Nwanne m na-eyi m ǹtọ̀ǹtọrị̄ n'okpuru aka.
examples.english: My brother tickles me under the arm.

examples.igbo: Yie nwa ahụ ǹtọ̀ǹtọrị̄ ka ọ chịa ọchị.
examples.english: Tickle the child so that he laughs.

gloss: watery, light consistency (of soup, broth, etc.; compare gologolo)

examples.igbo: Ofe ahụ dị ghòlòghòlò, o nweghị anụ.
examples.english: That soup is watery, it has no meat.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ofe ji dị ghòlòghòlò taa?
examples.english: Why is the soup watery today?

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka chịkọtara iheesereese n'akụkụ osimiri.
examples.english: The children gathered shells by the river.

examples.igbo: Iheesereese a siri ike nke ukwuu.
examples.english: This shell is very hard.

note: Am not certain of the exact referent and usual collocations of iheesereese as 'shell'.

examples.igbo: O sùrù ya mmà n'ụkwụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: He stabbed him in the leg at the market.

examples.igbo: Ònye sùrù gị mmà n'aka?
examples.english: Who stabbed you in the hand?

examples.igbo: Ndị Isi Ọji bịara obodo anyị ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: The Africans came to our town yesterday.

examples.igbo: Ndị Isi Ọji na-asụ ọtụtụ asụsụ.
examples.english: The Africans speak many languages.

examples.igbo: Òbìbì egwu ahụ ruru ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: The end of that song came quickly.

examples.igbo: Òle mgbe òbìbì ọrụ a ga-abịa?
examples.english: When will the end of this work come?

examples.igbo: Òzụzọ ala nna ya wetara esemokwu.
examples.english: Claiming his father's land brought trouble.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eme òzụzọ ihe na-abụghị nke gị?
examples.english: Are you claiming something that is not yours?

examples.igbo: Ọnụ ọgụgụ ụmụ akwụkwọ ruru narị abụọ.
examples.english: The figure of the students reached two hundred.

examples.igbo: Gịnị bụ ọnụ ọgụgụ ego anyị nwere?
examples.english: What is the figure of the money we have?

examples.igbo: O rụrụ ọrụ ahụ ǹkọ̀ọma.
examples.english: He did that work properly.

examples.igbo: Doo ákwá ahụ ǹkọ̀ọma tupu ị lakpuo.
examples.english: Make that bed well before you sleep.

examples.igbo: Ndụ m gbanwere mgbe m kwagara n'obodo ukwu.
examples.english: My life changed when I moved to the city.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eche na ndụ dị mfe n'ala bekee?
examples.english: Do you think life is easy abroad?

gloss: go out for a stroll in direction of friend(s); go out and visit; call upon

examples.igbo: Nna m pụkwuru òlịlī gaa leta enyi ya n'uhuruchi.
examples.english: My father went out for a stroll to visit his friend in the evening.

examples.igbo: Anyị ga-apụkwu òlịlī gaa ebe nwanne anyị taa.
examples.english: We shall go out and call on our brother today.

note: The phrase is uncommon; I have used the form pụkwu òlịlī 'go out visiting' with a past and a future inflection.

gloss: metal gong used by town-crier, or by titled man on feast-days to summon the ancestors

examples.igbo: Onye ozi kụrụ ìbome, ndị obodo zukọtara.
examples.english: The town crier struck the metal gong, and the villagers gathered.

examples.igbo: N'ụbọchị oriri, ọ na-akụ ìbome akpọọ ndị nna nna ya.
examples.english: On feast days, he strikes the gong to summon his ancestors.

examples.igbo: Nwanne m zọwara anyị n'ụlọ n'abalị ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: My brother came to our house unexpectedly last night.

examples.igbo: Zọwata ebe a mgbe ọ bụla ị gafere.
examples.english: Come by here whenever you pass this way.

note: The sense 'come occasionally and unexpectedly' is clear, but the word is rare in everyday speech.

examples.igbo: Ọ lara, kèdu zi anyị ga-esi rụchaa ọrụ a?
examples.english: He has left; how then shall we finish this work?

examples.igbo: Kèdu zi? Ị gaghị eso anyị gaa ahịa?
examples.english: How then? Won't you come with us to the market?

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-egwu egwu n'ubòm osimiri ahụ.
examples.english: The children are playing on that river sandbank.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ubòm ahụ mgbe mmiri kwụrụ?
examples.english: Did you see that sandbank when the water went down?

gloss: lift a load on to someone's head

examples.igbo: Ọ boro ibu ahụ n'isi nwanne ya.
examples.english: He lifted that load onto his brother's head.

examples.igbo: Boro m ibu a n'isi ka m gaa ahịa.
examples.english: Lift this load onto my head so I can go to the market.

examples.igbo: Ọ chàrà elili ahụ, ehi gbapụrụ.
examples.english: He cut the rope, and the cow ran off.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji chàa elili m kechiri ewu?
examples.english: Why did you cut the rope I used to tie the goat?

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka kwobàrà n'ime ụlọ mgbe mmiri malitere izo.
examples.english: The children rushed into the house when it started raining.

examples.igbo: Kwobà n'ime ụlọ ozugbo ị nụrụ mkpu ya.
examples.english: Rush into the house at once when you hear his shout.

note: I am fairly sure of the verb, but it is a rare word and the exact inflection may vary by dialect.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-amụ sayensị n'ụlọ akwụkwọ anyị.
examples.english: The children study science in our school.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere mmasị na sayensị?
examples.english: Are you interested in science?

examples.igbo: O ji àkụ na ụta chụ nta.
examples.english: He used an arrow and bow to hunt.

examples.igbo: Gbaa àkụ ahụ na nnụnụ.
examples.english: Shoot that arrow at the bird.

examples.igbo: Òfụfụ anya ụzò ya adịghịzi mma.
examples.english: His sight is no longer good.

examples.igbo: Òfụfụ anya ụzò gị ọ dị mma?
examples.english: Is your sight good?

note: Not fully certain of the exact usage of òfụfụ anya ụzò; examples treat it as eyesight/sight.

examples.igbo: Mụnye okụ ukpē ka anyị hụ ihe.
examples.english: Light the lamp so we can see.

examples.igbo: Okụ ukpē na-enwu n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: The lamp is shining in the room.

examples.igbo: Ezinụlọ ya nwere òdìmmā.
examples.english: His family has prosperity.

examples.igbo: Chọọ òdìmmā maka ezinụlọ gị.
examples.english: Seek well-being for your family.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akwutọ̀ ọnụ̄ mgbe ọ na-ewe iwe.
examples.english: He speaks vulgarly when he is angry.

examples.igbo: Ekwutọ̀la ọnụ̄ n'ihu ụmụaka.
examples.english: Don't be vulgar in front of children.

examples.igbo: O dinara n'elu beèdì.
examples.english: He lay on the bed.

examples.igbo: Zụta beèdì ọhụrụ maka ụlọ ọhụrụ.
examples.english: Buy a new bed for the new house.

gloss: general name for cichlid fish, Tilapia and Hemichromis genera, and extended to similar fish

examples.igbo: Anyị zụrụ ìkpoòkpò n'ahịa.
examples.english: We bought cichlid fish at the market.

examples.igbo: Nne m ji ìkpoòkpò sie ofe.
examples.english: My mother used cichlid fish to cook soup.

gloss: pick up (mat, cloth, etc.) and take

examples.igbo: Relu akwà gị, anyị na-apụ.
examples.english: Pick up your cloth, we are leaving.

examples.igbo: Ọ rèlu akwà ahụ gaa n'ọhịa.
examples.english: He picked up that cloth and went to the farm.

note: Verb form and tone of -relu are uncertain; examples use rèlu as the inflected stem.

gloss: èlèlè boiled in tins (e.g. milk tins) instead of being wrapped in leaves

examples.igbo: Anyị na-esi èlèle īko n'ụlọ.
examples.english: We cook tin-boiled èlèlè at home.

examples.igbo: Èlèle īko dị mma karịa nke akwụkwọ.
examples.english: Tin-boiled èlèlè is better than the leaf-wrapped one.

note: Specialized food term; examples are based on the given definition.

gloss: scoop out the inside of something; remove the inner content of a container or covering in order to make it empty

examples.igbo: O g̣hụrụ mmiri niile n'ime ite.
examples.english: He scooped out all the water from the pot.

examples.igbo: G̣hụọ ihe dị n'ime akpa ahụ.
examples.english: Scoop out what is inside that bag.

note: Spelling and inflection of g̣hụ are uncertain; examples use g̣hụrụ and g̣hụọ.

examples.igbo: Chukwu ēmeka, anyị rụchara ọrụ ahụ n'udo.
examples.english: God has done well, we finished that work in peace.

examples.igbo: Chukwu ēmeka, ka anyị kelee ya.
examples.english: God has done well, let us thank him.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ gbatagbata, biko bịa ozugbo.
examples.english: It is an emergency, please come immediately.

examples.igbo: Gbatagbata mere ka ha kpọọ dọkịta.
examples.english: The emergency made them call a doctor.

gloss: (usually òkụkù abùke) kind of fowl which never grows to a large size but is tough (usually used for sacrifice)

examples.igbo: Ha ji òkụkù abùke chụọ àjà.
examples.english: They used an abuke fowl for sacrifice.

examples.igbo: Òkụkù abùke adịghị eto eto.
examples.english: The abuke fowl does not grow big.

examples.igbo: Ọ gbakụtara m azụ mgbe m rịọrọ ya ego.
examples.english: He turned his back on me when I asked him for money.

examples.igbo: Gbakụta ya azụ, ọ gaghị enyere gị aka.
examples.english: Turn your back on him, he will not help you.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-alụ ugbo n'oge ọkọchị.
examples.english: We work a farm in the dry season.

examples.igbo: Lụọ ugbo gị tupu mmiri abịa.
examples.english: Work your farm before the rain comes.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ kụkpọrọ akwa ahụ n'ala.
examples.english: That child smashed the egg on the ground.

examples.igbo: Kụkpọọ akwa ahụ ka anyị rie ya.
examples.english: Break that egg so we can eat it.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-abù abù n'ụka.
examples.english: She sings at church.

examples.igbo: Bụọ abù ọzọ.
examples.english: Sing another song.

gloss: chief next in rank to the king of Ònìchà (and certain other towns), conveniently translated 'Prime Minister', who places the cap on the head of a titled man

examples.igbo: Ònoòwu kpubere okpu n'isi nwoke ahụ.
examples.english: The Onowu placed the cap on that man's head.

examples.igbo: Ndị Ònịchà họpụtara Ònoòwu ọhụrụ.
examples.english: The Onicha people chose a new Onowu.

examples.igbo: Ọka a sara.
examples.english: This corn is ripe.

examples.igbo: Mkpụrụ osisi a ọ sara?
examples.english: Is this fruit ripe?

examples.igbo: Nne m zụtara anụ atụlū n'ahịa.
examples.english: My mother bought mutton at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eri anụ atụlū ma ọ bụ anụ ehi?
examples.english: Will you eat mutton or beef?

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-abụ uri n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: Children are singing songs at school.

examples.igbo: Bụọ uri ahụ ọzọ.
examples.english: Sing that song again.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-agha anya ka ọ hụ ebe ụmụaka nọ.
examples.english: He is looking around to see where the children are.

examples.igbo: Ghaa anya tupu ị zọọ ụkwụ.
examples.english: Look around before you step.

examples.igbo: Ụkwụ ya dara ǹgwụlō, ọ pụghị ije.
examples.english: His leg became lame, he cannot walk.

examples.igbo: Ị dara ǹgwụlō? Gịnị mere?
examples.english: Are you lame? What happened?

examples.igbo: Ha kwajuru osikapa n'ite.
examples.english: They filled the pot with rice.

examples.igbo: Kwajuo m mmiri n'ite.
examples.english: Fill the pot with water for me.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ fụkọrọ akwụkwọ m.
examples.english: That child crumpled my paper.

examples.igbo: Efụkọla uwe gị.
examples.english: Don't crumple your clothes.

examples.igbo: Ọ fụrụ akpa ya n'ahịa.
examples.english: He lost his bag at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị fụrụ mkpịsị ugogbe gị?
examples.english: Did you lose your key?

examples.igbo: Ọ kwọpụrụ n'ụlọ mgbe ọ nụrụ mkpu.
examples.english: He rushed out of the house when he heard a shout.

examples.igbo: Kwọpụnụ n'ụlọ, ọkụ na-agba!
examples.english: Rush out of the house, fire is burning!

examples.igbo: O dara ọkpụ āba n'ala.
examples.english: He fell on his back on the ground.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka ọ daa ọkpụ āba.
examples.english: Don't let him fall on his back.

gloss: fall off; slip off; fall from

examples.igbo: Akwụkwọ ahụ dànarịrị n'elu osisi.
examples.english: The leaf fell off the tree.

examples.igbo: Kpachara anya ka ị ghara ịdànarị n'elu ugwu.
examples.english: Be careful so you don't fall off the hill.

gloss: to disgrace a person or somebody

examples.igbo: Okwu ọjọọ ya mechuru ezinụlọ ya ihū n'ihu ọha.
examples.english: His bad words disgraced his family in public.

examples.igbo: Emechula nwanne gị ihū n'ihu ndị ọbịa.
examples.english: Do not disgrace your sibling before guests.

examples.igbo: Nna m chịrị inyemè abụọ mgbe ọ dị obere.
examples.english: My father married two wives when he was young.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ ịchị inyemè ole n'oge a?
examples.english: How many wives do you want to marry at this time?

note: inyemè is a less common plural form; tone may vary.

gloss: argumentative, difficult, disagreeable person; fretful, testy child

examples.igbo: Nwata a bụ òdọ ǹdùdò, ọ na-akwa ákwá mgbe niile.
examples.english: This child is fretful; he cries all the time.

examples.igbo: Ị bụ òdọ ǹdùdò, gịnị mere i ji na-ese okwu?
examples.english: You are a disagreeable person; why are you quarrelling?

note: Phrase is understood, but exact tone and usage can vary.

examples.igbo: Anyị kwachịrị n'ụlọ ọzọ n'izu gara aga.
examples.english: We moved to another house last week.

examples.igbo: Olee mgbe ị ga-akwachị n'ụlọ ọhụrụ?
examples.english: When will you move to a new house?

note: Inflection kwachịrị is likely correct but not commonly written.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ekwu ọnụ naàbò, otu ihe n'ọnụ, ọzọ n'obi.
examples.english: He speaks hypocritically, one thing in the mouth, another in the heart.

examples.igbo: Kwụsị ikwu ọnụ naàbò, gwa m eziokwu.
examples.english: Stop speaking hypocritically, tell me the truth.

note: Idiom is clear; spelling naàbò may vary in modern texts.

examples.igbo: Ha tụrụ òòbò nkụ n'azụ ụlọ.
examples.english: They piled firewood behind the house.

examples.igbo: Tụọ òòbò ájá ahụ n'akụkụ ụlọ.
examples.english: Pile that sand beside the house.

note: Imperative tụọ is standard; tone on òòbò may vary.

examples.igbo: Ọ tigwòrò ite igwe ahụ n'ala.
examples.english: He broke that iron pot into pieces on the ground.

examples.igbo: Gịnị tigwòrò ite igwe ahụ?
examples.english: What broke that iron pot into pieces?

note: Past inflection tigwòrò is plausible but not certain.

gloss: yellow (color); a yellow dye gotten from vegetables

examples.igbo: Uwe m na-acha èdò dị m mma.
examples.english: My yellow dress looks good on me.

examples.igbo: Were èdò tee uwe ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: Use the yellow dye to dye that dress well.

examples.igbo: Ọ zụtara ùdị ọjọō osikapa n'ahịa.
examples.english: She bought a bad kind of rice in the market.

examples.igbo: Ùdị ọjọō mmadụ ka ọ bụ?
examples.english: Is he a bad kind of person?

note: Phrase is idiomatic; exact tone may vary by dialect.

examples.igbo: Onye ọka ikpe kpere ikpē ahụ n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: The judge passed that judgement in the morning.

examples.igbo: Kpee ikpē ziri ezi, ọ bụghị ikpē ọjọọ.
examples.english: Judge justly, not unjustly.

examples.igbo: Jiri pensụl kàa akàlà n’ala ụlọ.
examples.english: Use a pencil to draw a line on the house floor.

examples.igbo: Ọ kàrà akàlà ogologo n’ala ahụ.
examples.english: He drew a long line on that ground.

note: Past/imperative forms kàrà/kàa are plausible; tone should be checked.

examples.igbo: O keriri ji ahụ n’iberibe nta.
examples.english: He cut that yam into small pieces.

examples.igbo: Kerie anụ ọkụkọ ahụ maka ofe.
examples.english: Cut that chicken meat into pieces for soup.

examples.igbo: O mesoro anyị ihe ọma n’ụbọchị ahụ.
examples.english: He treated us well that day.

examples.igbo: Meso nwanne gị nke ọma mgbe niile.
examples.english: Treat your sibling well always.

examples.igbo: O nyere m ònyìnye n’ụbọchị ọmụmụ m.
examples.english: He gave me a gift on my birthday.

examples.igbo: N’ụka, anyị na-enye ònyìnye mgbe niile.
examples.english: In church, we give offertory always.

examples.igbo: Kèdụ onye kụrụ ụzọ n’ọnụ ụlọ m?
examples.english: Who knocked at my door?

examples.igbo: Kèdụ onye ga-eso gị gaa ahịa?
examples.english: Who will go with you to the market?

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-egwu egwu na-aza èzí n’ụtụtụ.
examples.english: The children are playing in the yard in the morning.

examples.igbo: Anyị nọ na-aza èzí na-akụ osisi.
examples.english: We are in the yard planting trees.

note: Treated as a locative phrase meaning 'in the yard'.

examples.igbo: Ùbụlù ya na-arụ ọrụ nke ọma.
examples.english: His brain works well.

examples.igbo: Nri ọma na-akwalite ùbụlù mmadụ n’ụbọchị niile.
examples.english: Good food boosts a person's brain every day.

examples.igbo: O kụrụ mkpụkpọ n’ime mgbidi ụlọ.
examples.english: He drove a nail into the house wall.

examples.igbo: Mkpụkpọ a dị ogologo ma sie ike.
examples.english: This nail is long and strong.

examples.igbo: O bọ̀rọ akpa ya ka anyị hụ ihe dị n’ime.
examples.english: He spread his bag open so we could see what was inside.

examples.igbo: Bọ̀a akpa ahụ ka m hụ ihe dị n’ime.
examples.english: Spread that bag open so I can see what is inside.

note: Inflections bọ̀rọ/bọ̀a are my best guess.

examples.igbo: Bishọp bìkwàsịrị aka n'isi nwa m n'ụka.
examples.english: The bishop confirmed my child in church.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ ka bishọp bìkwàsị aka n'isi gị n'afọ a?
examples.english: Do you want the bishop to confirm you this year?

examples.igbo: Òbàlàkeèt a na-ekpo ọkụ n'abalị.
examples.english: This blanket is warm at night.

examples.igbo: Weta òbàlàkeèt ahụ n'ọnụ ụlọ.
examples.english: Bring that blanket into the room.

gloss: kind of children’s ailment (rash); tinea carcinata (compare òkpụ īsi tinea capitis)

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ nwere ǹla n'ahụ ya.
examples.english: That child has a rash on his body.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ǹla n'olu nwa ya?
examples.english: Did you see the rash on her child's neck?

examples.igbo: Afà nnà m bụ Ọkeke.
examples.english: My father's name is Okeke.

examples.igbo: Ị maara afà nnà ya?
examples.english: Do you know his father's name?

examples.igbo: O kwuru okwu alū n'ebe ụmụaka nọ.
examples.english: He spoke abominable words where children were.

examples.igbo: Ekwula okwu alū n'ụlọ ụka.
examples.english: Don't speak abominable words in church.

gloss: take mọō when assuming duties of ọkpala

examples.igbo: O kpọrọ mụọ mgbe ọ weere ọkpala.
examples.english: He took mụọ when he assumed the ọkpala title.

examples.igbo: Olee mgbe ị ga-akpọ mụọ?
examples.english: When will you take mụọ?

gloss: motion with hands for silence O kpukpùlù aka ọgè m nà-àkwadebe ikwu#ife ọ mèlù He tried to silence me by gesturing with his hand when I was about to reveal what he had done

examples.igbo: O kpukpùlù aka ka anyị mechie ọnụ.
examples.english: He gestured with his hand for us to be silent.

examples.igbo: Ị kpukpùlù aka ka m mechie ọnụ?

examples.igbo: Ị gụrụ ụmị-edemede nke akwụkwọ a?
examples.english: Did you read the abstract of this book?

examples.english: The door has shut me outside.

examples.english: Press your two hands together.

examples.english: Aniemeka is the boy who lives next to my house.

examples.igbo: Ànìèmeka, bịa rie nri taa.
examples.english: Aniemeka, come and eat today.

examples.igbo: Ị hụla nwa ọfụū a mụrụ n'ụtụtụ taa?
examples.english: Have you seen the newborn born this morning?

gloss: cover by wrapping with paper; cover by placing something on top of the item; knot

examples.english: She wrapped the bread in paper.

examples.igbo: Machie ite ahụ ka ijiji ghara ịbanye.
examples.english: Cover the pot so flies don't get in.

examples.igbo: Nnekọta ụmụaka dị mkpa n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: Supervision of children is important at school.

examples.igbo: Ònye na-ahụ maka nnekọta ọrụ a?
examples.english: Who is in charge of the supervision of this work?

gloss: leopard killer (recently a chieftaincy title for someone who has made a great feat)

examples.igbo: E nyere ya Ògbuāgụ̄ mgbe o gbusịrị agụ.
examples.english: He was given the title Ogbuagu when he killed a leopard.

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ bụ Ògbuāgụ̄, ndị obodo na-asọpụrụ ya.
examples.english: That man is an Ogbuagu; the townspeople respect him.

examples.igbo: Onye ọkwọ ụgbọala ahụ bogburu ụgbọala ya na ngwa ahịa.
examples.english: That driver overloaded his vehicle with goods.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ ibogbu akpa a?
examples.english: Do you want to overload this bag?

gloss: wash out; (fig.) die out (of a family)

examples.igbo: O ji mmiri sapụ ite ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: She washed out the pot well with water.

examples.igbo: Ha na-atụ egwu na ezinụlọ ha ga-esapu.
examples.english: They fear that their family will die out.

examples.igbo: Bọọlụ bụ ògbambùlù e ji egwuri egwu.
examples.english: A ball is a round thing used for playing.

examples.igbo: Gịnị bụ ògbambùlù ahụ dị n'ala?
examples.english: What is that round thing on the ground?

gloss: tap; hit with a quick on and off contact

examples.igbo: Gụọ kpakpando ndị dị n'elu igwe.
examples.english: Count the stars in the sky.

gloss: search for; look for, follow after in direction of thing being followed

examples.igbo: Tuo ǹtutu maka akpa gị furu efu.
examples.english: Search for your lost bag.

examples.igbo: Efi ọfīa na-ata ahịhịa n'ala ọhịa.
examples.english: The buffalo is grazing grass in the bush.

examples.igbo: Ị hụtụla efi ọfīa n'ụzọ mgbe ị na-aga ahịa?
examples.english: Have you seen a buffalo on the road when going to market?

gloss: belch; emit wind noisily from the stomach through the mouth

examples.english: He belched after eating.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ebi ubìrì n'ihu ọha mgbe ị risịrị nri?
examples.english: Do you belch in public after eating?
