examples.english: He understood everything about farming.

examples.igbo: Ị mazùrù ihe m gwara gị?
examples.english: Did you understand fully what I told you?

examples.igbo: Ha na-atù ji n'ubi n'ụtụtụ a.
examples.english: They are digging up yams in the farm this morning.

examples.igbo: Ị tùrù ji ole n'ubi gị?
examples.english: How many yams did you dig up in your farm?

gloss: act in a way that shows self-contentment;

examples.igbo: O na-akpa ǹgàǹgà n'ihi uwe ọhụrụ ya.
examples.english: She is acting self-contented because of her new dress.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji akpa ǹgàǹgà?
examples.english: Why are you acting self-contented?

examples.igbo: Pịakọ uwe ndị a tinye n'igbe.
examples.english: Fold these clothes and put them in the box.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-apịakọ akwụkwọ ya ugbu a.
examples.english: She is folding her papers now.

gloss: be much; be too much; be excessive

examples.igbo: Okpomọkụ hikara taa, anyị anọghị n'ọhịa.
examples.english: The heat is too much today; we are not in the farm.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eche na ego ahụ hikara?
examples.english: Do you think that money is too much?

examples.igbo: Akwụkwọ ọfụū a dị mma nke ukwuu.
examples.english: This new book is very good.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara akwụkwọ ọfụū maka nwa gị?
examples.english: Did you buy a new book for your child?

examples.igbo: Anyị ga-echeta ya ebìghìèbì n'obi anyị.
examples.english: We will remember him forever in our hearts.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-anọ ebe a ebìghìèbì?
examples.english: Will you stay here forever?

examples.igbo: Anyị fịkọrọ ọka n'ụbọchị ahụ.
examples.english: We dried the corn together that day.

examples.igbo: Fịkọ akwa gị na nke m ka ọ kpọọ nkụ.
examples.english: Dry your clothes together with mine so they dry.

examples.igbo: Onye nkuzi anyị nwere ogumogwū ochie.
examples.english: Our teacher has an old thumb-piano.

examples.igbo: Ị pụrụ ịkpọ ogumogwū?
examples.english: Can you play the thumb-piano?

examples.igbo: E nwere ọlà ọcha osisi n'aka ya.
examples.english: There is a wood sliver in his hand.

examples.igbo: Wepụ ọlà ọcha ahụ n' mkpịsị aka gị.
examples.english: Remove that sliver from your finger.

note: The sense 'sliver' for ọlà ọcha is uncommon; usually it means silver. Sentences are plausible but I am not fully certain.

examples.igbo: Akpụ ndị ahụ fịrị afị n'ihi okpomọkụ.
examples.english: Those cassavas withered due to heat.

examples.igbo: Osisi gị fịrị afị, gbaa ya mmiri ozugbo.
examples.english: Your tree has withered, water it immediately.

examples.igbo: O tinyere mkpò anwūlù n'akpa uwe ya.
examples.english: He put the snuffbox in his pocket.

examples.igbo: Mkpò anwūlù m furu efu.
examples.english: My snuffbox is lost.

gloss: craftsman; skilled workman; artist; sculptor; designer

examples.igbo: Onye ǹkà ahụ rụrụ oche osisi.
examples.english: That craftsman made a wooden chair.

examples.igbo: Onye ǹkà m zutere n' ahịa dị mma.
examples.english: The craftsman I met at the market is good.

gloss: patroness of a dancing-club, musical group, etc.

examples.igbo: Nne egwū nyere otu egwū ego.
examples.english: The patroness gave the dance group money.

examples.igbo: Onye bụ nne egwū nke otu a?
examples.english: Who is the patroness of this group?

gloss: rot; be rotten; be corrupt; be lazy

examples.igbo: Ji ndị ahụ lere ùle n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: Those yams rotted in the room.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ele ùle n'ọrụ ugbo.
examples.english: He is lazy in farm work.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-eme òmụmụ nwa anyị.

examples.igbo: Òmụmụ ya mere n'ụlọ ọgwụ.
examples.english: Her birth took place in the hospital.

examples.igbo: O cheere anyị ọjị mgbe anyị bịara.

examples.english: Give them kola before they leave.

examples.english: Madam boss, we have finished that work.

examples.english: Ebelechukwu, come and eat.

examples.english: He struck you back, what will you do?

examples.igbo: Ị na-agba afịa n'ahịa taa?
examples.english: Are you trading in the market today?

examples.english: Did you hear that his father died?

examples.english: That farmer placed a charm on his farm.

examples.igbo: Biko dọọ iyī n'ụlọ gị tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Please place a charm on your house before you leave.

examples.igbo: Akwụkwọ osisi na-akpọ nkụ n’oge ọkọchị?

examples.english: Where did you grow up when you were a child?

examples.english: They postponed that meeting until tomorrow.

examples.english: Remove that splinter from that child's leg.

examples.english: Do you know a carpenter who will build our door?

examples.english: Let us grow old in peace in our town.

examples.english: Don't tell lies in front of your mother.

examples.english: He hit my elbow on the door.

examples.igbo: Ǹkù aka ya na-egbu mgbu mgbe o welitere akpa.
examples.english: His elbow hurts when he lifted the bag.

examples.igbo: Onye ēbelè na-enyere ndị ogbenye aka.
examples.english: The merciful person helps the poor.

examples.igbo: Ị bụ onye ēbelè, gịnị mere i ji jụ enyemaka?
examples.english: You are a merciful person; why did you refuse help?

gloss: go in; pass deeply; travel inland

examples.igbo: Ọ gàmìrì n'ime ọhịa.
examples.english: He went deep into the forest.

examples.igbo: Anyị gàmìrì n'ime ime obodo tupu chi ebie.
examples.english: We travelled inland into the village before dawn.

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ na-achu ụla n'abalị niile.
examples.english: That child is sleepless all night.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji achụ ụla taa?
examples.english: Why are you sleepless today?

examples.igbo: M kwadebere nri maka ndị ọbịa.
examples.english: I prepared food for the guests.

examples.igbo: Anyị kwadebere ịrụ ụlọ ọhụrụ n'afọ a.
examples.english: We plan to build a new house this year.

gloss: barbed spear for hunting or fighting

examples.igbo: Ndị dinta ji àgànà egbu anụ ọhịa.
examples.english: Hunters use a barbed spear to kill wild animals.

examples.igbo: Àgànà a dị nkọ nke ukwuu.
examples.english: This barbed spear is very sharp.

examples.igbo: Anyị nwere ọkpùlùkpù okwū banyere ala.
examples.english: We had a very important discussion about land.

examples.igbo: Ọkpùlùkpù okwū a gbasara ego.
examples.english: This very important discussion concerned money.

gloss: leave, abandon work stealthily, unnoticed or unannounced

examples.igbo: Ọ rèpùrù n'ọlụ n'ehihie.
examples.english: He stealthily left work in the afternoon.

examples.igbo: Arèpụla n'ọlụ n'agwaghị onye isi.
examples.english: Do not leave work without telling the boss.

gloss: fall upon violently; pounce upon (of people fighting)

examples.igbo: Onye iro dàkpọrọ ya n'ala.
examples.english: The enemy pounced on him to the ground.

examples.igbo: Ha dàkpọrọ ibe ha n'ọgụ.
examples.english: They pounced on each other in the fight.

examples.igbo: Obodo mapụrụ ya n'ihi izu ohi.
examples.english: The community ostracised him because of theft.

examples.igbo: Ị mapụrụ ya n'obodo a?
examples.english: Did you ostracise him from this town?

examples.igbo: Sùchi dị n'ụzọ mmiri ahụ.
examples.english: There is a blockage in that waterway.

examples.igbo: Sùchi ikuku na-eme ka iku ume sie ike.
examples.english: Air blockage makes breathing difficult.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-eku ume site n'oghele imi ya abụọ.
examples.english: He breathes through his two nostrils.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ọbara n'oghele imi ya?
examples.english: Did you see blood in his nostril?

note: The more usual modern spelling is 'oghere imi'; 'oghele imi' is understood but less common.

gloss: cut open, break into two (e.g. coconut)

examples.igbo: O gbùwara akị bekee were mma.
examples.english: He cut the coconut open with a knife.

examples.igbo: Gbùwa mkpụrụ ọjị ahụ ka m hụ ihe dị n'ime.
examples.english: Break that kola nut open so I can see what is inside.

examples.igbo: Ànị ōma jìjìjì mere n'abalị ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: An earthquake happened last night.

examples.igbo: Ị nụrụ ànị ōma jìjìjì n'abalị ụnyaahụ?
examples.english: Did you hear the earthquake last night?

note: The expression is rather fixed and literary; everyday speech often says 'ala ma jìjìjì'.

examples.igbo: Anyị ha nhā ahụ n'ọnwa gara aga.
examples.english: We paid that levy last month.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eha nhā ahụ niile?
examples.english: Will you pay all the levy?

note: I am not certain of the correct inflected forms of 'ha' in this sense; the examples are plausible but should be checked by a native speaker.

gloss: alter a plan; abandon a purpose

examples.igbo: O zùsàrà atụmatụ anyị niile.
examples.english: He altered all our plans.

examples.igbo: Zùsà atụmatụ ahụ, ọ dịghịzi mma.
examples.english: Abandon that plan, it is no longer good.

note: The stem is used correctly, but 'zùsà' is somewhat formal and not heard in every dialect.

gloss: enlarged spleen; kind of abdominal disorder in children characterized by swelling of the spleen in the left side of the abdomen. It is felt to be round and hard when pressed. It is wrongly believed by many to be a living thing in the stomach which resembles a crab and walks up and down the stomach

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ na-arịa ụma afō ugbu a.
examples.english: That child has an enlarged spleen now.

examples.igbo: Dọkịta lere ụma afō ya anya.
examples.english: The doctor examined his enlarged spleen.

note: The term is understood in traditional medicine contexts; the clinical register is less common.

examples.igbo: E nyere ya ahōòtūtū Chief n'obodo ya.
examples.english: He was given the title Chief in his town.

examples.igbo: Kedu ahōòtūtū e nyere ya?
examples.english: What title was he given?

note: The word appears rare and may be a variant of 'aha ọtụtụ'; the examples may not match current usage.

examples.igbo: O wetùrù igbe ahụ n'elu ụlọ.
examples.english: He brought down that box from the roof.

examples.igbo: Wetù akwụkwọ ahụ n'elu tebụl.
examples.english: Bring down that book from the table.

gloss: small black edible fruit of ilighìlì

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-ata mbèmbè n'okpuru osisi.
examples.english: Children are chewing mbèmbè under the tree.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ mbèmbè n'ahịa taa?
examples.english: Did you see mbèmbè in the market today?

note: The fruit name is known mainly in areas where ilighìlì grows; the sentences are otherwise straightforward.

examples.igbo: Oyi na-ama ya lìlì n'abalị.
examples.english: Cold makes him shiver at night.

examples.igbo: Ọ nọ na-ama lìlì n'ihi egwu.
examples.english: He was shivering because of fear.

note: The verb phrase is idiomatic, but the reduplicated 'lìlì' may vary in tone across speakers.

gloss: waylay; ambush; fence round; stop up

examples.igbo: Ndị ohi gbachibidoro anyị n'ụzọ obodo.
examples.english: Robbers waylaid us on the village road.

examples.igbo: Gbachibido oghere ahụ tupu mmiri abịa.
examples.english: Block that hole before the rain comes.

examples.igbo: Osisi ukwu ahụ doro ndò n'ihu ụlọ.
examples.english: That big tree is shady in front of the house.

examples.igbo: Nọdụ n'ebe a, ebe ọ doro ndò.
examples.english: Sit here, where it is shady.

examples.igbo: O kweere ụta ya tupu ọ gaa ịchụ nta.
examples.english: He strung his bow before going hunting.

examples.igbo: Kwe ụta gị, anyị ga-aga ọhịa.
examples.english: String your bow, we will go to the bush.

gloss: salutation of respect to an old man (especially a pagan)

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka ahụ kelere ya, sị, 'Ọm!'
examples.english: The children greeted him, saying, 'Ọm!'

examples.igbo: Ọm! Nna anyị, nọdụ ala.
examples.english: Ọm! Our father, sit down.

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ kpuru ìsì, ọ naghị ahụ ụzọ.
examples.english: That man is blind, he cannot see the road.

examples.igbo: Ị kpuru ìsì, ma ị na-ekwu na ị hụrụ ya?
examples.english: You are blind, yet you say you saw him?

examples.igbo: O tasiri obì n'ahụhụ ahụ.
examples.english: He endured that suffering.

examples.igbo: Tasìa obì, anyị ga-erute ebe ahụ.
examples.english: Take heart, we will reach that place.

examples.igbo: Osisi ahụ dàkụlụ n'ụlọ.
examples.english: That tree fell against the house.

examples.igbo: Lezie anya, ka ị ghara ịdàkụlụ n'ọnụ ụzọ.
examples.english: Be careful, so you don't fall against the doorway.

examples.igbo: Ha gara ọhịa gbuo aŋā.
examples.english: They went to the bush to collect cane.

examples.igbo: Gbuo aŋā were rụọ oche.
examples.english: Collect cane and use it to make a chair.

examples.igbo: Mama m zụtara unèlè n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: My mother bought bananas at the market today.

examples.igbo: Wepụta unèlè abụọ n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: Bring out two bananas from inside the room.

examples.igbo: Eze ahụ chịrị ọchịchị n'obodo ya nke ọma.
examples.english: That king governed his town well.

examples.igbo: Ònye na-achị ọchịchị ebe a?
examples.english: Who governs here?

gloss: shake (a container of liquid) around;  to mix well

examples.igbo: ṅàgharịa ite mmiri ahụ ka ọ gwakọta.
examples.english: Shake that pot of water so it mixes.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-aṅàgharị ọgwụ ahụ tupu ya ṅụọ ya.
examples.english: She shakes that medicine before drinking it.

examples.igbo: Ụmù nwaànyà ahụ na-ere ahịa n'ọma.
examples.english: Those women are selling in the market.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ụmù nwaànyà ndị ahụ n'ụzọ?
examples.english: Did you see those women on the road?

examples.igbo: O tiri àrụ n'aka ya mgbe ọ dara.
examples.english: He bruised his hand when he fell.

examples.igbo: Ị tiri àrụ n'ụkwụ gị?
examples.english: Did you bruise your leg?

note: Inflection of -tilù àrụ may vary; used common 'tiri àrụ'.

examples.igbo: Ọgwụ ahụ tụlụ ndù n'ahụ ya.
examples.english: The medicine revived him.

examples.igbo: O nwere ike ịtụlụ ndù n'ahụ gị?
examples.english: Can it revive you?

note: The verb form 'tụlụ ndù' is used; others might prefer 'tụgharịa ndụ'.

examples.igbo: O zànyere ahịhịa ahụ n'ime ọkụ.
examples.english: He swept the grass into the fire.

examples.igbo: Zànye ya n'ime akpa ahụ.
examples.english: Sweep it into that bag.

examples.igbo: O kakworò mkpụrụ osisi ahụ tupu ha eto.
examples.english: He plucked those fruits prematurely before they ripened.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka ụmụaka kakwo mkpụrụ osisi.
examples.english: Don't let children pluck fruits prematurely.

examples.igbo: O kèlụrụ òkè ya n'ime ego ahụ.
examples.english: He took his share of that money.

examples.igbo: Kèlụ òkè gị tupu ha ewere ya.
examples.english: Take your share before they take it.

gloss: ‘up and down’; blouse and wrapper made of same material

examples.igbo: O yiri enū nà ànì nke ọma.
examples.english: She wore a matching blouse and wrapper nicely.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara enū nà ànì ọhụrụ?
examples.english: Did you buy a new matching set?

gloss: stretcher(especially as fabricated used in ancient Igbo land)

examples.igbo: E buuru ya n'uteekwerē gaa ụlọ ọgwụ.
examples.english: They carried him on a stretcher to the hospital.

examples.igbo: O mere uteekwerē site n'osisi.
examples.english: He made a stretcher from wood.

examples.igbo: O wùdàrù n'elu osisi ahụ.
examples.english: He jumped down from that tree.

examples.igbo: Wùdà n'ụgbọ ahụ ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Jump down from that car quickly.

examples.igbo: Ànì obì anyị dị n'akụkụ ụzọ ahụ.
examples.english: Our settlement is beside that road.

examples.igbo: Ọ hapụrụ ànì obì nna ya kwaga obodo ọzọ.
examples.english: He left his father's settlement and moved to another town.

note: àni obì is not common in everyday speech; sentences are grammatical and idiomatic for the sense given.

examples.igbo: Chere ntakịrị ka ofe a jụnata.
examples.english: Wait a little for this soup to cool.

examples.igbo: Ofe ahụ jụnataalarị?
examples.english: Has the soup cooled yet?

gloss: smile, laugh, chuckle, in a gentle way (as a sign of pleasure)

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ kpụrụ ọchị mgbe ọ hụrụ nne ya.
examples.english: The child smiled when he saw his mother.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji akpụ ọchị otú a?
examples.english: Why are you smiling like that?

note: I am fairly sure the stem goes with ọchị (kpụ ọchị), but the exact inflection of this rare stem is less certain.

examples.igbo: Ndị obodo anyị na-agba òfalà kwa afọ.
examples.english: Our people celebrate the òfalà festival every year.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-agba òfalà n'afọ a?
examples.english: Will you celebrate òfalà this year?

examples.igbo: Anyị gazuru ọhịa ahụ dum.
examples.english: We went through the whole forest.

examples.igbo: Ị gazuru akwụkwọ ahụ niile?
examples.english: Did you go through the whole book?

note: -gazu is uncommon; I used it as 'go through/cover a whole extent', which is the sense given.

examples.igbo: Sachata efere ndị ahụ bịa.
examples.english: Wash those plates and bring them.

examples.igbo: Ọ sachatara m efere niile.
examples.english: She washed and brought me all the plates.

note: The 'and bring' part of this compound is assumed in the examples.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka ahụ na-amagharị n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: Those children are jumping about in the house.

examples.igbo: Kwụsị magharị n'ebe a!
examples.english: Stop jumping about here!

note: magharị is used here as the verb 'jump about'; the bare stem in the imperative is slightly unusual.

examples.igbo: E nwere otu nwa àkàkpò n'obodo anyị.
examples.english: There is a dwarf in our town.

examples.igbo: Nne ya na-elekọta nwa àkàkpò ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: His mother takes good care of that dwarf.

note: nwa àkàkpò is a rather blunt term; examples are kept neutral.

examples.igbo: O jere ije wee lue n'osimiri.
examples.english: He walked as far as the river.

examples.igbo: Ị jere ije wee lue n'ọhịa?
examples.english: Did you walk as far as the bush?

note: wèe lue nà is mostly used as a connector; the examples keep it in that 'as far as' frame.

headword: ànì mmanụ anwū nà mmili ala efī
gloss: promised land (land of milk and honey)

examples.igbo: Ha na-atụ anya ịhụ ànì mmanụ anwū nà mmili ala efī.
examples.english: They hope to see the promised land.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ekwu na obodo ya bụ ànì mmanụ anwū nà mmili ala efī.
examples.english: He says his town is a land of milk and honey.

note: The phrase is a fixed biblical expression; I kept it intact as given in the entry.

examples.igbo: Ikèlike ọkū si na ọkụ ahụ wụfere n'ala.
examples.english: A spark flew from the fire to the ground.

examples.igbo: Chebe ụmụaka ka ikèlike ọkū ghara ịdọ ha ọkụ.
examples.english: Watch the children so sparks do not burn them.

examples.igbo: Òkwòli nọ n'akụkụ osimiri na-ele azụ.
examples.english: A kingfisher is by the river watching fish.

examples.igbo: Òkwòli ahụ gbapụrụ mgbe anyị rutere nso.
examples.english: That kingfisher flew away when we came near.

examples.igbo: Ndị ikom ahụ na-akụ ọka n'ugbo.
examples.english: Those men are planting corn on the farm.

examples.igbo: Ndị ikom abịarutela n'ọrụ taa?
examples.english: Have the men arrived at work today?

examples.igbo: Biko kponita akwụkwọ ndị ahụ n'ala.
examples.english: Please gather up those papers on the floor.

examples.igbo: O kponitara ego ndị ahụ n'ala.
examples.english: He gathered up that money on the ground.

examples.igbo: Nkume ahụ na-anwupù n'anyanwụ.
examples.english: The stone glitters in the sun.

examples.igbo: Mma ọla ahụ nwupụrụ n'ìhè.
examples.english: The jewelry glittered in the light.

examples.igbo: Ọnọdụ okpomọkụ taa dị elu.
examples.english: Today's temperature is high.

examples.igbo: Lelee ọnọdụ okpomọkụ tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Check the temperature before you go out.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka larụrụ ụla mgbe ọchịchịrị bịara.
examples.english: The children slept when darkness came.

examples.igbo: Biko larụ ụla nke ọma taa.
examples.english: Please sleep well today.

examples.igbo: Anyị lara n'ụlọ mgbe mmiri bidoro izo.
examples.english: We went home when it started raining.

examples.igbo: Ole mgbe ị ga-ala?
examples.english: When will you go home?

examples.igbo: Nwa akwụkwọ ahụ na-anọchite anya ụlọ akwụkwọ ya n'asọmpi.
examples.english: That student represents his school in the competition.

examples.igbo: Kedu onye na-anọchite anya gị n'ọgbakọ taa?
examples.english: Who represents you at today's meeting?

examples.igbo: Nwantanta anya ya dị oji.
examples.english: The pupil of his eye is black.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ nwantanta anya ya?
examples.english: Did you see the pupil of his eye?

note: The headword appears to be nwantanta anya, the usual term for pupil of the eye.

examples.igbo: Egbugbere ọnụ ya na-acha ọbara ọbara.
examples.english: Her lips are red.

examples.igbo: Kpuchie egbugbere ọnụ gị.
examples.english: Close your lips.

gloss: God thinks for me (God takes care of my worries)

examples.igbo: Chinèechèrēm, ekele m gị maka nchekwa gị.
examples.english: Chineecherim, I thank you for your protection.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akpọ Chinèechèrēm n'oge nsogbu?
examples.english: Do you call on Chineecherim in time of trouble?

note: The entry is a personal name; the examples use it as a name addressed in prayer.

examples.igbo: Nye ya efè ka ọ kwuo okwu.
examples.english: Give him a chance to speak.

examples.igbo: Ị nyere ya efè ịbanye?
examples.english: Did you give him a chance to enter?

examples.igbo: Anyị na-asụ ọhịa n'ubi taa.
examples.english: We are clearing bush in the farm today.

examples.igbo: Sụọ ọhịa ahụ tupu mmiri ezo.
examples.english: Clear that bush before the rain falls.

examples.igbo: Ndị uwe ojii na-ebu ife ògù.
examples.english: The police carry weapons.

examples.igbo: O nwere ife ògù n'ụlọ ya?
examples.english: Does he have weapons in his house?

examples.igbo: Nọdèbe m nso.
examples.english: Stay near me.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-anọdèbe nne ya mgbe niile.
examples.english: She stays near her mother always.

gloss: carry a baby; nurse a baby; look after a baby

examples.igbo: Nne ahụ na-eku nwa ya n'azụ.
examples.english: That mother carries her baby on her back.

examples.igbo: Kuo nwa gị nke ọma.
examples.english: Look after your baby well.

gloss: flatness; lying flat on the back; prone

examples.igbo: O dinara àba n'àkwà.
examples.english: He lay flat on his back on the bed.

examples.igbo: Dina àba n'ala.
examples.english: Lie flat on the ground.

examples.igbo: Èeyī, m ga-abịa echi.
examples.english: Yes, I will come tomorrow.

examples.igbo: Ị na-abịa? Èeyī!
examples.english: Are you coming? Yes!

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ na-enyò ènyò n'ọnụ ụzọ.
examples.english: That child is peeping at the doorway.

examples.igbo: Enyòla ènyò n'ime ụlọ mmadụ!
examples.english: Don't peep into people's rooms!

note: Tone and the shape of the negative imperative enyòla are my best reconstruction.

examples.igbo: Ndị aghā bịara n'obodo anyị ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: The soldiers came to our town yesterday.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ndị aghā n'okporo ụzọ?
examples.english: Did you see soldiers on the road?

examples.igbo: Anyị hụrụ ozu efī n'akụkụ ụzọ.
examples.english: We saw a cattle carcase by the roadside.

examples.igbo: Ozu efī ahụ na-esi isi ọjọọ.
examples.english: That cattle carcase smells bad.

gloss: become lost or disappear by hiding; lose by hiding; be lost by hiding; become forever hidden; hide away

examples.igbo: O zofuru ego ya n'ime ala.
examples.english: He hid his money away in the ground.

examples.igbo: Ọkụkọ m zofuru n'ime ọhịa.
examples.english: My fowl disappeared into the bush.

note: The sense 'lose by hiding / be lost by hiding' is not common; sentences are constructed rather than remembered.

examples.igbo: Nwa agbọghọ ahụ gbalịrị àgbalị.
examples.english: That girl is slim.

examples.igbo: Ị gbalịrị àgbalị, rie nri ọzọ.
examples.english: You are slim, eat more food.

examples.igbo: Anụ eghēleghe a na-atọ ụtọ.
examples.english: This fried meat is tasty.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eri anụ eghēleghe taa?
examples.english: Will you eat fried meat today?

note: The exact tone pattern of eghēleghe varies in speech; kept as given.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka ahụ na-ashọ ùzù n'èzí.
examples.english: Those children are quarrelling noisily outside.

examples.igbo: Kwụsị ịshọ ùzù, ndị agbata obi ga-anụ.
examples.english: Stop quarrelling noisily, the neighbours will hear.

examples.igbo: O kpọrọ ụkwụ ya na nkume.
examples.english: He stubbed his toe on a stone.

examples.igbo: Ị kpọrọ ụkwụ n'ụzọ?
examples.english: Did you stub your toe on the way?

gloss: kind of non-edible shrub resembling tobacco plant in appearance and smell

examples.igbo: Ùtabā mmụọ na-eto n'akụkụ ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: The ùtabā mmụọ shrub grows beside our house.

examples.igbo: A naghị eri ùtabā mmụọ n'ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: Ùtabā mmụọ is not eaten in our house.

note: A plant name restricted to some areas; the sentences are safe but the word itself is not widely used.

examples.igbo: O kwara ibu ya ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: He packed his load quickly.

examples.igbo: Nne m na-akwa ibu n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: My mother is packing the loads in the room.

examples.igbo: Ụmụnne m nọ n'ụzìijè na Britain.
examples.english: My relatives are in the diaspora in Britain.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-aga n'ụzìijè n'afọ a?
examples.english: Will you go to the diaspora this year?

note: ụzìijè is a modern term; the constructions given are common, though one could also say 'n'ala ọzọ'.

examples.igbo: E nwere ife naanọ n'ime igbe ahụ.
examples.english: There are four things in that box.

examples.igbo: Gụọ ife naanọ ndị ahụ dị n'elu tebụl.
examples.english: Count those four things on the table.

note: Modern standard usually has 'ihe anọ'; the headword form 'ife naanọ' was kept as given.

gloss: collect or pluck leaves (mostly for use).

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-akpa akwụkwọ n'ọhịa.
examples.english: The children are plucking leaves in the bush.

examples.igbo: Kpaa akwụkwọ maka ewu ahụ.
examples.english: Pluck leaves for that goat.

examples.igbo: O duru onye ìsì gafee okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: He led a blind person across the road.

examples.igbo: Duru onye ìsì ahụ ruo n'ụlọ ya.
examples.english: Lead that blind person to his house.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-atụ ume ntakịrị n'ihi ọrịa ahụ.
examples.english: He is breathing faintly because of that illness.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ị na-atụ ume ntakịrị?
examples.english: Why are you breathing faintly?

note: 'tụ ume' often means simply 'breathe/rest'; the 'faintly' sense is carried here by ntakịrị.

examples.igbo: Ọkụkọ na-efecha nku ya n'ala.
examples.english: The hen is flapping its wings on the ground.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ka ọkụkọ ahụ fechara nku ya?
examples.english: Did you see how that hen flapped its wings?

examples.igbo: Òbùbè mmiri ahụ bịara na mgbede.
examples.english: The stopping of that rain came in the evening.

examples.igbo: Òbùbè ọrụ a dị anya?
examples.english: Is the end of this work far off?

note: I am not fully sure 'òbùbè' is the usual noun for ending/stopping; 'ngwụcha' or 'njedebe' are more common, so these sentences may not be idiomatic.

examples.igbo: Ọdù akā ya dị mkpụmkpụ ntakịrị.
examples.english: His little finger is a bit short.

examples.igbo: O tinyere mgbaaka n'ọdù akā ya.
examples.english: She put a ring on her little finger.

examples.igbo: Sọọsọ ya bịara ụlọ akwụkwọ taa.
examples.english: Only he/she came to school today.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ sọọsọ ya ka ị hụrụ n'ọhịa?
examples.english: Was it only him/her you saw at the farm?

examples.igbo: O nyere nne ya ọdụ aka.
examples.english: He gave his mother an ivory bracelet.

examples.igbo: Ị zụrụ ọdụ aka n'ahịa?
examples.english: Did you buy an ivory bracelet at the market?

note: Assumed the given sense 'ivory bracelet'; the compound is not common in everyday speech.

examples.igbo: Anyị kwụsiri ike n'okwu anyị.
examples.english: We stood firm by our word.

examples.igbo: Kwụsie ike, egwu atụla gị.
examples.english: Stand firm, do not be afraid.

note: Standard modern form is 'kwụsie ike' / inflected 'kwụsiri ike'; the headword spelling varies.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-abịachi anya n'ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: He comes to our house regularly.

examples.igbo: Ị na-abịachi anya ebe a?
examples.english: Do you come here regularly?

examples.igbo: Anwụ na-enwu enwu n'ụtụtụ a.
examples.english: The sun is bright this morning.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ọnwa ji enwu enwu a?
examples.english: Why is the moon so bright?

gloss: act together; have intercourse with; fraternise with

examples.igbo: Anyị mekọrọ aka rụọ ọrụ ahụ.
examples.english: We worked together to do that work.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-emekọ aka na anyị?
examples.english: Will you join hands with us?

note: Examples illustrate the 'act together' sense; the other senses are not shown here.

examples.igbo: O jiri mma bee achịcha.
examples.english: He used a knife to cut bread.

examples.igbo: Jide aka m ka anyị gafee.
examples.english: Hold my hand so we can cross.

note: Uses inflected/related forms for 'use' and 'hold'.

gloss: desire; like; want; need (with thing desired or needed as subject)

examples.igbo: Agụụ na-agụ m ugbu a.
examples.english: I am hungry now.

examples.igbo: Akpịrị na-agụ ya?
examples.english: Is he/she thirsty?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-agbọ nchà n'ime ụlọ ịsa ahụ.
examples.english: He masturbates in the bathroom.

examples.igbo: Gbọla nchà n'ihu ụmụaka.
examples.english: Don't masturbate in front of children.

note: Assumed the given sense is the intended colloquial usage.

examples.igbo: Dinta gbafịrị mgbada ahụ.
examples.english: The hunter shot and missed that antelope.

examples.igbo: Ị gbafịrị nnụnụ ahụ?
examples.english: Did you shoot and miss that bird?

note: Inflected form 'gbafịrị' used for the verb stem.

examples.igbo: Okwu ya nyere m nkasì obì.
examples.english: His words gave me comfort.

examples.english: Animals live on dry land, not in water.

gloss: spring or prickly Amaranth (Amaranthus spinosus Linn.)

examples.english: We ate cooked prickly amaranth.

note: Plant name; I am fairly sure of the identification but not of everyday usage.

examples.english: Are you vomiting blood?

examples.english: That child is an albino.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ eziokwu na ọ cha anyarị?
examples.english: Is it true that he is an albino?

gloss: Come and play a (board) game with me

examples.english: Will you come and play a board game with me?

examples.igbo: Gbelele ya na-egosi na ọ na-eri nri ọjọọ.

gloss: wander about lazily in the house

examples.igbo: Kwụsị ịpiogharị n'ụlọ, gaa kụọ ahịhịa.
examples.english: Stop wandering lazily in the house, go and clear the weeds.

note: The verb form 'piogharị' is as given; I am not fully certain of its everyday inflection.

gloss: wrinkle; be wrinkled (used for a material which has been stretched beyond its elastic limit, and then relaxed)

examples.english: The cloth wrinkled after we washed it.

examples.igbo: Ị dọnìrì uwe m?
examples.english: Did you wrinkle my cloth?

note: The verb is rare; I have inflected it as 'dọnìrì' for past tense.

examples.igbo: Mùchie anya gị, gịnị ka ị na-ahụ?

gloss: 2nd yam for replanting. At the beginning of yam harvest, the first yams harvested are not quite as firm as those harvested at the end, so some early harvested yams when dug up are not completely rooted out from the soil; the tuber is carefully cut leaving the very tip of the head and the roots in the soil. These are properly covered back in the soil. By the end of the yam harvest these are harvested together with the remaining yams. By this time the small piece of the yam left with the tip of the head of the yam in the soil has grown more yam

examples.igbo: Akpụ jī na-eto n'ala ruo mgbe owuwe ihe ubi gwụrụ.
examples.english: The replanting yam grows in the ground until the harvest ends.

examples.igbo: Ìpo ànwàlì na-atọ ụtọ karịa azụ ndị ọzọ?
examples.english: Is ìpo ànwàlì tastier than other fish?

examples.igbo: Òne ndị bịara n'ụlọ anyị ụnyaahụ?
examples.english: Who came to our house yesterday?

examples.igbo: Òne ndị ka anyị ga-akpọ na oriri?
examples.english: Whom shall we invite to the feast?

examples.igbo: Ọ mere m arìma ka m bịa.
examples.english: He signaled me to come.

examples.igbo: Mee m arìma mgbe ị ruru n'ụlọ.
examples.english: Signal me when you reach home.

examples.igbo: Ọ pụrụ n'ụlọ n'isi ụtụtụ.
examples.english: He left the house early in the morning.

examples.igbo: Pụọ n'ebe a ugbu a!
examples.english: Leave this place right now!

examples.igbo: Ọ na-alo n'ife n'ọrụ ugbo.
examples.english: It is useful in farm work.

examples.igbo: Gịnị ga-alo n'ife nye anyị?
examples.english: What will be useful to us?

examples.igbo: Ọkụ na-acha ufie ūfie.
examples.english: Fire is red.

examples.igbo: Uwe a ọ na-acha ufie ūfie?
examples.english: Is this dress red?

gloss: give permission for any kind of gathering; declare open; open

examples.igbo: Onye isi obodo wughepụrụ emume ahụ.
examples.english: The town chairman declared the festival open.

examples.igbo: Wughepụnụ nnọkọ ahụ ka anyị malite.
examples.english: Declare the meeting open so we can begin.

examples.igbo: Òbịbịa ya wetara anyị ọṅụ.
examples.english: His coming brought us joy.

examples.igbo: Olee mgbe òbịbịa ya ga-eme?
examples.english: When will his coming happen?

examples.igbo: Ụkwụ m gbụrụ agbụ n'ala mmiri.
examples.english: My foot slipped on wet ground.

examples.igbo: Jide mgbidi ahụ, ka ị ghara ịgbụ agbụ.
examples.english: Hold the wall so you don't slip.

examples.igbo: Èkène dìlị Chukwu, anyị ruru n'ụlọ nke ọma.
examples.english: Thanks be to God, we arrived home safely.

examples.igbo: Èkène dìlị Chukwu maka nri a.
examples.english: Thanks be to God for this food.

examples.igbo: Ọ jemìrì n'ime ọhịa ruo ebe mmiri dị.
examples.english: He went far into the forest to where water is.

examples.igbo: Jemì n'ime ubi, ị ga-ahụ ewu.
examples.english: Go far into the farm, you will see a goat.

examples.igbo: Ọ kpụchapụrụ ofe niile dị n'ite.
examples.english: He scraped out all the soup that was in the pot.

examples.igbo: Kpụchapụ mmanụ fọdụrụ n'efere nke ọma.
examples.english: Scrape out the oil left in the plate carefully.

gloss: look aside; neglect; overlook; look away

examples.igbo: Ọ lefuru anya n'ọrụ ya nke ukwuu.
examples.english: He neglected his work greatly.

examples.igbo: Lefuo anya n'ebe ahụ, ị ga-ahụ osimiri.
examples.english: Look away from there, you will see the sea.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ di nwenu ụlọ a.
examples.english: He is the owner of this house.

examples.igbo: Ònye bụ di nwenu ala a?
examples.english: Who is the owner of this land?

examples.igbo: M màtara osikapa atọ n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: I bought three measures of rice in the market today.

examples.igbo: Biko màta mmanụ abụọ n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: Please buy two measures of oil in the market today.

examples.igbo: Òrìmìlì nnū dị omimi nke ukwuu.
examples.english: The sea is very deep.

examples.igbo: Ị hụtụla òrìmìlì nnū mgbe ọ bụla?
examples.english: Have you ever seen the sea?

examples.igbo: Nri gbọfọrọ n'ite bụ nke nwanne m.
examples.english: The food left in the pot is my brother's.

examples.igbo: Ego ole gbọfọrọ mgbe ị zụchara akwa?
examples.english: How much money remained after you bought clothes?

examples.igbo: Ọ nenyere anya n'ime igbe ahụ.
examples.english: He looked into that box.

examples.igbo: Nenye anya n'ime ite ahụ, ọ dị ihe?
examples.english: Look into that pot, is there anything?

examples.igbo: Ndị agha sụkpọrọ ụlọ ahụ kpamkpam.
examples.english: The soldiers destroyed that house completely.

examples.igbo: Sụkpọ ọka a ntụ ntụ n'ụlọ ọrụ.
examples.english: Crush this corn to powder at the mill.

examples.igbo: Icheku-ọkụ na-enwu nke ọma n'ọkụ.
examples.english: Charcoal glows well in the fire.

examples.igbo: Anyị ji icheku-ọkụ sie anụ taa.
examples.english: We used charcoal to cook meat today.

examples.igbo: Gụdēbē akwụkwọ ahụ, anyị ga-aga ahịa.
examples.english: Stop reading that book, we are going to the market.

examples.igbo: Ọ kwesịrị ka ị gụdēbē akwụkwọ ahụ ugbu a.
examples.english: You should stop reading that book now.

gloss: shut in or out; confine by shutting up

examples.igbo: Kpụchibido ụmụaka n'ime ụlọ, ka ha ghara ịpụ.
examples.english: Shut the children inside the house, so they don't go out.

examples.igbo: Anyị kpụchibidoro ọkụkọ n'ụlọ abalị.
examples.english: We shut the chickens in the house at night.

examples.igbo: Ọkpoòfùfù na-agba ya n'ihi ọrụ siri ike.
examples.english: Sweat is pouring from him because of hard work.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ọkpoòfùfù ji agba gị?
examples.english: Why are you sweating?

examples.igbo: Ọ jụrụ m, “Ì nà-èzo ēzo?”
examples.english: He asked me, “Are you hiding?”

examples.igbo: Ì nà-èzo ēzo? Bịa n'ìhè.
examples.english: Are you hiding? Come into the light.

gloss: a cutie, especially humans (women and children); something that should be protected from harm because it is dear and tender

examples.igbo: Nwa ọhụrụ ahụ bụ apụ̀naanwụ̄.
examples.english: That baby is a cutie.

examples.igbo: Chebe apụ̀naanwụ̄ a, ọ bụ ihe dị oké ọnụ.
examples.english: Protect this cutie; she is precious.

examples.igbo: Nnụnụ ahụ fefùrù n'anya anyị.
examples.english: The bird flew away out of our sight.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ka nnụnụ si fefù?
examples.english: Did you see how the bird flew away out of sight?

examples.igbo: O ji mkpịsị kpochaa egbe ya.
examples.english: He used a ramrod to clean his gun.

examples.igbo: Olee ebe mkpịsị egbe m dị?
examples.english: Where is my gun ramrod?

examples.igbo: Mee ya etu afù.
examples.english: Do it that way.

examples.igbo: Etu afù ka anyị na-eme ya.
examples.english: That is how we do it.

gloss: drum beaten for deities at second burial

examples.igbo: Ha kụrụ ùbà n'abalị ahụ.
examples.english: They beat the uba drum that night.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ha ji akụ ùbà taa?
examples.english: Why are they beating the uba drum today?

examples.igbo: O kpejide m n'okwu ahụ.
examples.english: He judged me unfairly in that matter.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ikpejide nwanne gị.
examples.english: Don't judge your brother unfairly.

examples.igbo: Ụmụ akwụkwọ ahụ guzoro n'ǹdìlì n'ihu ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: The students stood in a line in front of the school.

examples.igbo: Dobe akwụkwọ ndị a n'ǹdìlì abụọ n'elu okpokoro.
examples.english: Arrange these books in two rows on the table.

examples.igbo: Ọ kụrụ nwanne ya ọ̀kpọ n'ubu.
examples.english: He punched his brother on the shoulder.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji kụọ ya ọ̀kpọ n'ihu?
examples.english: Why did you punch him in the face?

examples.igbo: M wụfuru mmiri ahụ n'ime ọwa mmiri.
examples.english: I poured that water away into the drain.

examples.igbo: Wụfù mmiri ahụ n'ime ụlọ mposi.
examples.english: Pour that water away into the toilet.

note: The imperative form Wụfù is used as the inflected verb stem.

examples.igbo: Ndị uwe ojii tụrụ ya n'ngòrò abalị ahụ.
examples.english: The police threw him into a cell that night.

examples.igbo: Ọ nọ n'ngòrò ruo mgbe ọ kwụrụ ụgwọ.
examples.english: He stayed in the cell until he paid.

gloss: pipe (for smoking) (word used mostly by old people) (compare òkụ ūtabà)

examples.igbo: Nna m ochie na-ese òkpòkọ n'ụlọ ya.
examples.english: My grandfather smokes a pipe in his house.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji ese òkpòkọ?
examples.english: Why do you smoke a pipe?

examples.igbo: Uwe a pèrè, ọ gaghị eju m.
examples.english: This dress is small, it won't fit me.

examples.igbo: Mkpụrụ osisi ahụ pèrè ma ọ na-etolite.
examples.english: That seed is small but it is growing.

note: The stative form pèrè is used for 'is small/little'.

examples.igbo: O kere ime mgbe ọ dị obere.
examples.english: She aborted when she was young.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ ịke ime?
examples.english: Do you want to abort?

note: The phrase is sensitive; ịke ime is used as the infinitive form.

gloss: a speech that portrays the opposite of what it means; irony

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ekwu ọ̀ghàròokwū mgbe ọ sịrị na ọ dị mma.
examples.english: He speaks ironically when he says it is fine.

examples.igbo: Ị na-aghọta ọ̀ghàròokwū dị n'okwu ya?
examples.english: Do you understand the irony in his speech?

gloss: be in a place (of animate creatures); stay; dwell; be at home (compare -bi, which refers to more permanent living); sit

examples.igbo: Nne m nọ̀ n'ụlọ ọgwụ ugbu a.
examples.english: My mother is in the hospital now.

examples.igbo: Nọdụ ebe a ruo mgbe m lọtara.
examples.english: Stay here until I return.

examples.igbo: Ọ bìrì okwu ya nkenke ka ndị mmadụ ghara ike.
examples.english: He shortened his speech so people wouldn't get tired.

examples.igbo: Bì nkenke okwu gị, anyị na-aga.
examples.english: Shorten your speech, we are leaving.

examples.igbo: Òfifi toro n'ụkwụ m, ọ na-egbu m mgbu.
examples.english: A boil grew on my leg and it is hurting me.

examples.igbo: Biko tinye ọgwụ n'òfifi a taa.
examples.english: Please apply medicine to this boil today.

gloss: cheek; side of the face below the eye and above the jaw

examples.igbo: Ọ kụrụ ya aka n'ǹtì n'ahịa.
examples.english: He slapped him on the cheek at the market.

examples.igbo: Ǹtì gị ọ na-egbu gị mgbu?
examples.english: Does your cheek hurt you?

gloss: shake (especially in a soft or dangling way)

examples.igbo: Osisi ahụ na-eyọgharị n'ifufe n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: That tree is swaying in the wind by the road.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka ọ na-eyọgharị otú ahụ.
examples.english: Don't let it dangle like that.

note: The sense is clear, but this verb is uncommon in everyday speech.

examples.igbo: Ọnụma anyị niile zutere n'ụlọ nna m.
examples.english: Our whole family gathered at my father's house.

examples.igbo: Ọnụma gị ọ dị ukwuu n'ezie?
examples.english: Is your family really large?

examples.igbo: Ifufe na-amarube osisi n'okporo ụzọ n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: The wind is shaking the tree by the road in the morning.

examples.igbo: Ekwela imarube igbe ahụ ka ọ ghara ịda.
examples.english: Don't shake that box so it won't fall.

note: The verb stem is clear, but its inflected forms are not commonly heard.

examples.igbo: Nzusà ya mere ka anyị ghara ịga ahịa.
examples.english: His change of plan made us not go to the market.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara nzusà a na mberede?
examples.english: What caused this sudden caprice?

note: The meaning is understood, but the word is uncommon in ordinary conversation.

examples.igbo: Ndị agha ji mgbòdo echebe onwe ha.
examples.english: The soldiers use shields to protect themselves.

examples.igbo: Mgbòdo ahụ kpuchiri ya pụọ na mmiri ozuzo.
examples.english: That covering shielded him from the rain.

examples.igbo: Eze ahụ rapụrụ ọkwa ya n'afọ gara aga.
examples.english: That king abdicated his throne last year.

examples.igbo: Ole mgbe eze ga-rapụ ọkwa ya?
examples.english: When will the king abdicate his throne?

examples.igbo: O kpụpụrụ okpu ya mgbe ọ banyere n'ụlọ.
examples.english: He removed his cap when he entered the house.

examples.igbo: Kpụpụ okpu gị tupu ị banye n'ụlọ.
examples.english: Remove your cap before you enter the house.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-arụ ugbo n'ala nna anyị.
examples.english: We farm on our father's land.

examples.igbo: Ị na-arụ ugbo n'ubi gị n'oge a?
examples.english: Are you working your farm at this time?

examples.igbo: O kpàjirà ji ahụ ụzọ abụọ.
examples.english: He split that yam into two equal parts.

examples.igbo: Ị kpàjirà ji ahụ ụzọ abụọ?
examples.english: Did you split that yam into two equal parts?

examples.igbo: O gwu ọba n'ubi ya n'afọ a.
examples.english: He made a yam barn in his farm this year.

examples.igbo: Ị gwu ọba n'ubi n'afọ a?
examples.english: Did you make a yam barn in the farm this year?

note: Not fully certain of the verb form 'gwu' in this construction.

gloss: point at someone using the nose and mouth at the same time

examples.igbo: O sū īmī n'ebe nwa ahụ nọ.
examples.english: She pointed at that child with her nose and mouth.

examples.igbo: Ị sū īmī n'ebe m nọ?
examples.english: Did you point at me with your nose and mouth?

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ nọ n'akụkụ ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: That child is at the corner of our house.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ya n'akụkụ ụlọ anyị?
examples.english: Did you see him at the corner of our house?

examples.igbo: Ọdọ mmiri ahụ dị nso n'obodo anyị.
examples.english: That lake is near our town.

examples.igbo: Ị hụtụla ọdọ mmiri dị n'obodo anyị?
examples.english: Have you seen the lake in our town?

examples.igbo: O kwe ọnū maka akwa ahụ.
examples.english: She offered a price for that cloth.

examples.igbo: Ị kwe ọnū maka akwa ahụ?
examples.english: Did you offer a price for that cloth?

examples.igbo: Ụmù nwokē na-akụ ji n'ubi n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: The men are planting yams in the farm in the morning.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ụmù nwokē n'ahịa taa?
examples.english: Did you see the men in the market today?

examples.igbo: Ụmù nnē anyị na-ebi n'otu ụlọ.
examples.english: Our full siblings live in the same house.

examples.igbo: Ị ma ụmù nnē ya nke ọma?
examples.english: Do you know his full siblings well?

examples.igbo: Ji ahụ de èdè n'ihi mmiri.
examples.english: That yam is soft because of water.

examples.igbo: Osikapa a de èdè n'ihi mmiri n'ezie?
examples.english: Is this rice really mushy because of water?

note: Uncertain about the verb 'de' in this phrase.

examples.igbo: Osisi ahụ kpọrọ ìfulu n'afọ a.
examples.english: That tree blossomed this year.

examples.igbo: Osisi a na-akpọ ìfulu n'oge a?
examples.english: Does this tree blossom at this time?

examples.igbo: Rikwu nri tupu ị gawa ọrụ.
examples.english: Eat more food before you go to work.

examples.igbo: Ị na-erikwu nri ugbu a karịa mbụ?
examples.english: Are you eating more food now than before?

examples.igbo: Yikwasị uwe gị ngwa ngwa, anyị na-apụ.
examples.english: Put on your clothes quickly, we are leaving.

examples.igbo: O yikwasịrị nwa ya uwe ọhụrụ.
examples.english: She put new clothes on her child.

examples.igbo: Ọgwụ ụkwụ ya na-egbu ya mgbu.
examples.english: His leg is hurting him.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ nwere ọgwụ ụkwụ dị ogologo.
examples.english: That child has long legs.

note: Entry spelling is ogwè ụkwū; I have written standard modern orthography ọgwụ ụkwụ.

examples.igbo: Ǹgùgù m na-egbu m mgbu.
examples.english: My waist is paining me.

examples.igbo: O jidere ya n'ǹgùgù.
examples.english: He held him by the waist.

note: The word covers ribs, lungs, loins and waist; the examples show the waist/loins sense.

gloss: be a year old; be so many years old

examples.igbo: Nwa m gbara arọ abụọ.
examples.english: My child is two years old.

examples.igbo: Ị gbara arọ ole?
examples.english: How old are you?

examples.igbo: Ọ gbara mmee n'imi mgbe ọ dara.
examples.english: He bled from the nose when he fell.

examples.igbo: Kedu ihe mere aka gị ji agba mmee?
examples.english: Why is your hand bleeding?

examples.igbo: Onye amụma ahụ mara amụma banyere ụnwụ.
examples.english: That prophet prophesied about famine.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ama amụma ihe ga-eme?
examples.english: Are you foretelling what will happen?

examples.igbo: Oke ọbụgbọ na-eto n'akụkụ mmiri.
examples.english: The lily grows near water.

examples.igbo: O ji oke ọbụgbọ chọọ ụlọ ya mma.
examples.english: She decorated her house with lilies.

note: I have taken the word to mean a kind of lily, as given.

examples.igbo: Aha nwa nwanyị ahụ bụ Ekwutọsị.
examples.english: That girl's name is Ekwutọsị.

examples.igbo: Ekwutọsị, bịa rie nri.
examples.english: Ekwutọsị, come and eat.

note: Tone marks on the name are often omitted in ordinary writing; I have written it plainly.

gloss: drop or keep something, especially small or lightweight; drop something (small or lightweight) upon

examples.igbo: Tụsa mkpụrụ osisi ahụ n'ala ebe ahụ.
examples.english: Drop that seed on the ground there.

examples.igbo: Ọ tụsara ego ya n'ime akpa ya.
examples.english: She dropped her money into her bag.

note: The sense of tụsa as dropping small objects is not common in all dialects.

examples.igbo: Nubà uwe ndị a n'ime akpa ahụ.
examples.english: Push these clothes into that bag.

examples.igbo: Ọ nubàra ụkwụ ya n'ime mmiri ọhụrụ.
examples.english: He pushed his leg into fresh water.

examples.igbo: Ndị agha gbara ògbòǹdù abụọ n'emume ahụ.
examples.english: Soldiers fired two cannons at that ceremony.

examples.igbo: Ị nụrụ ụda ògbòǹdù n'abalị ụnyaahụ?
examples.english: Did you hear the sound of a cannon last night?

gloss: pick one's way; move on slowly; step; toddle

examples.igbo: Nwa ọhụrụ ahụ na-ranyè ijè n'ụzọ ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: The baby is toddling on the way to school.

examples.igbo: Ranyè ijè nwayọọ n'okporo ụzọ a na mgbede.
examples.english: Pick your way slowly along this road in the evening.

note: The imperative form may vary by speaker.

examples.igbo: Ọ gwèrè azụ̀ kacha mma n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: She chose the best fish in the market today.

examples.igbo: Ị gwèrè ole n'ime uwe ndị a?
examples.english: How many of these clothes did you choose?

note: The verb gwè is less common than họrọ in some areas.

gloss: stick in; plant going to stick sticks along the boundary between us and the Ụmù Agū people

examples.igbo: Tụọ osisi a n'ókè ubi anyị taa.
examples.english: Stick this stick at the boundary of our farm today.

examples.igbo: Ha tụrụ osisi n'ókè ala ha na Ụmù Agū.
examples.english: They stuck sticks at the boundary between their land and Ụmù Agū.

note: The exact sense of -tu as sticking in is clear, but the tonal inflection may vary.

gloss: befriend, especially as a lover; date (boyfriend/girlfriend)

examples.igbo: Ọ yị̀rị̀ ọ̀yị̀ nwa agbọghọ ahụ n'obodo a.
examples.english: He dated that girl in this town.

examples.igbo: Ị yị̀rị̀ ọ̀yị̀ onye ọ bụla n'oge gara aga?
examples.english: Did you date anyone in the past?

note: I am not fully certain of the tonal and inflectional form of this phrase.

examples.igbo: Anyị gokọtara azụ̀ na agwa n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: We bought fish and beans together in the market today.

examples.igbo: Gokọta mkpụrụ osisi maka ụmụaka n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: Buy fruits together for the children at school.

examples.igbo: Ọ sòrọ ndụmọdụ nne ya n'okwu ahụ.
examples.english: He followed his mother's advice on that matter.

examples.igbo: Sòọ ndụmọdụ dọkịta ahụ banyere ọgwụ a.
examples.english: Follow that doctor's advice about this medicine.

examples.igbo: E nyere m òfe mgbe m zụrụ akwụkwọ n'ahịa.
examples.english: I was given a free gift when I bought a book in the market.

examples.igbo: Ị natara òfe ha nyere gị ụnyaahụ?
examples.english: Did you receive the free gift they gave you yesterday?

examples.igbo: Ngị nà ònwe gī zụtara akwụkwọ a.
examples.english: You yourself bought this book.

examples.igbo: Ngị nà ònwe gī ga-akwụ ụgwọ ya?
examples.english: Will you yourself pay for it?

examples.igbo: Ùdè ndị a toro ogologo n'ubi anyị.
examples.english: These palm-wine trees grew tall in our farm.

examples.igbo: Ònye kụrụ ùdè ndị a n'ubi?
examples.english: Who planted these palm-wine trees in the farm?

gloss: reiterate; repeat (a speech); say what was said, again

examples.igbo: Kwugharị okwu gị ka anyị nụ.
examples.english: Repeat your speech so we can hear.

examples.igbo: Ọ kwugharị okwu ahụ n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: He repeated that speech at school.

examples.igbo: Alā ụla na-enye m nsogbu n'abalị ndị a.
examples.english: Sleeplessness troubles me these nights.

examples.igbo: Gịnị na-akpata alā ụla gị?
examples.english: What causes your sleeplessness?

examples.igbo: Mkpūlu ndị ahụ dị n'ubi anyị.
examples.english: Those mounds of earth are in our farm.

examples.igbo: Kpụọ mkpūlu ọhụrụ n'akụkụ ubi.
examples.english: Make new mounds of earth beside the farm.

examples.igbo: Kpùghe ite ahụ ka anyị hụ ihe dị n'ime.
examples.english: Uncover that pot so we can see what is inside.

examples.igbo: Ọ kpùghere anyị ihe nzuzo ahụ.
examples.english: He revealed that secret to us.

examples.igbo: Onye nā-efe ọlū na-ele ndị ọrụ anya.
examples.english: The overseer supervises the workers.

examples.igbo: Onye nā-efe ọlū bịara n'ọrụ taa?
examples.english: Did the foreman come to work today?

examples.igbo: Ụmụ nnụnụ na-efe ǹkù n'elu osisi.
examples.english: The birds are flapping their wings on the tree.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ka ọkụkọ si efe ǹkù?
examples.english: Did you see how the chicken flaps its wings?

examples.igbo: O ji okpòlò igwè kụọ ihe ahụ.
examples.english: He used an iron rod to hit that thing.

examples.igbo: Kpụta okpòlò igwè ahụ n'ụlọ ọrụ.
examples.english: Bring that iron rod from the workshop.

examples.igbo: Ọ gwelìrì ji ndị ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: She pounded those yams well.

examples.igbo: Gwelìe ji a nke ọma.
examples.english: Pound this yam well.

note: Verb stem -gwelì is not common in everyday speech in my area; forms given are regular.

gloss: both yam and maize (= kà ... kà)

examples.igbo: O nyere anyị mà ji mà ọkà.
examples.english: She gave us both yam and maize.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara mà ji mà ọkà?
examples.english: Did you buy both yam and maize?

gloss: swell and fill (a receptacle); heal up (of wound)

examples.igbo: Agwa ahụ ruchiri ite ahụ.
examples.english: The beans swelled and filled the pot.

examples.igbo: Ọnyá ahụ ọ ruchiri?
examples.english: Has the wound healed up?

note: The two senses (swelling, healing) are kept apart; the form ruchiri is given as a regular past tense.

gloss: music in which ùdù features prominently

examples.igbo: Anyị na-ege egwu ùdù na redio.
examples.english: We listen to ùdù music on the radio.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akpọ egwu ùdù?
examples.english: Do you play ùdù music?

gloss: train or raise someone till the person is grown; raise

examples.igbo: O zụ̀tàrà ụmụ ya ruo mgbe ha toro.
examples.english: She raised her children until they grew up.

examples.igbo: Zụ̀tà nwa gị n'ịhụnanya.
examples.english: Raise your child in love.

note: The low tones on zụ̀tò distinguish it from zụta 'buy'; without tone marks the sentences could be misread.

examples.igbo: Eze nọ n'oche ezè ya.
examples.english: The king is on his throne.

examples.igbo: Ị hụla oche ezè eze ahụ?
examples.english: Have you seen that king's throne?

examples.igbo: Ebenebe mere n'ụlọ ahịa ahụ.
examples.english: A disaster happened in that shop.

examples.igbo: Ị nụla banyere ebenebe ahụ?
examples.english: Have you heard about that disaster?

examples.igbo: Afọ ōlụlụ na-egbu nwa ahụ.
examples.english: The child has a bad stomach-ache.

examples.igbo: Ị na-enwe afọ ōlụlụ?
examples.english: Do you have stomach-ache?

note: The macron on ō in ōlụlụ is retained as given.

examples.igbo: Anyị zụrụ òpàpa n'ahịa.
examples.english: We bought groundnuts at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ere òpàpa?
examples.english: Do you sell groundnuts?

examples.igbo: Di mgba ahụ dị ike nke ukwuu.
examples.english: That wrestler is very strong.

examples.igbo: Ị maara di mgba ahụ?
examples.english: Do you know that wrestler?

examples.igbo: Bilie ngwa ngwa, oge agwụla.
examples.english: Get up quickly, time is up.

examples.igbo: Jizọs biliri n'ọnwụ n'ụbọchị nke atọ.
examples.english: Jesus rose from the dead on the third day.

examples.igbo: Onye nkèta ala ahụ bụ nwa ya nwoke.
examples.english: The inheritor of that land is his son.

examples.igbo: Ònye ga-abụ onye nkèta ụlọ nna gị?
examples.english: Who will be the inheritor of your father's house?

examples.igbo: Nnụnụ ahụ fefere n'elu osimiri ahụ.
examples.english: The bird flew across that river.

examples.igbo: Ì nwere ike ịfefe n'ofe mmiri a?
examples.english: Can you fly across this river?

note: The reduplicated stem is uncommon in everyday speech; the future/infinitive forms chosen are the ones that sound natural.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-enya isi maka ụlọ ọhụrụ ya.
examples.english: He is proud of his new house.

examples.igbo: Enyela isi n'ihu ndị ọbịa.
examples.english: Don't be proud in front of guests.

note: The verbal form of nyà isi varies; enya isi is the one heard in ordinary speech.

examples.igbo: Okporaamā ahụ na-aga Enugu.
examples.english: That highway goes to Enugu.

examples.igbo: Ì hụrụ okporaamā ọhụrụ ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see that new highway?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-amakụta ihe niile gbasara ahịa ahụ.
examples.english: He knows all about that market.

examples.igbo: Ònye na-amakụta ihe niile?
examples.english: Who knows everything?

note: The sense of -makụta is not fully clear to me; the sentences use it as 'know all/everything', which is the gloss given.

examples.igbo: Mechie oghē ahụ ka oyi ghara ịba n'ụlọ.
examples.english: Close that opening so the cold does not enter the house.

examples.igbo: Oghē nke ọgba ahụ dị warara.
examples.english: The opening of that cave is narrow.

examples.igbo: Anyị nwa hụrụ ihe merenụ n'anya anyị.
examples.english: We ourselves saw what happened with our own eyes.

examples.igbo: Anyị nwa ga-aga ahịa taa.
examples.english: We here will go to the market today.

note: The emphatic particle nwa after anyị is regional; the shape is right but usage varies by speaker.

examples.igbo: Mma a nyụrụ nkọ, ọ naghị egbu ihe ọma.
examples.english: This knife is blunt, it does not cut well.

examples.igbo: Mma a ọ nyụrụ nkọ?
examples.english: Is this knife blunt?

note: I have taken the sense as 'lose its edge, be blunt' of a blade rather than the figurative 'speak bluntly'.

examples.igbo: Azụrụ m ife ise n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: I bought five things at the market today.

examples.igbo: Gịnị bụ ife ise ahụ ị zụtara?
examples.english: What are those five things you bought?

examples.igbo: Anwụrụ ọkụ na-akwụni elu n'elu ụlọ ahụ.
examples.english: Smoke is rising above that house.

examples.igbo: Ì hụrụ ka anwụrụ si akwụni elu n'ụtụtụ?
examples.english: Did you see how smoke rises in the morning?

examples.igbo: Ọ bichiri ụlọ nwanne ya mgbe ọ lọtara.
examples.english: He occupied his brother's house when he returned.

examples.igbo: Anyị agaghị ebichi ụlọ onye ọzọ.
examples.english: We will not occupy another person's house.

examples.igbo: Ọ wụfere obere mmiri ahụ ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: He quickly jumped over that small stream.

examples.igbo: Wụfee mgbidi ahụ ngwa ngwa!
examples.english: Jump over that wall quickly!

examples.igbo: Òkpọnkụ nke ala ahụ mere ka osisi kpọọ nkụ.
examples.english: The dryness of that soil made the plants dry.

examples.igbo: Òkpọnkụ na-egbu ahịhịa n'oge ọkọchị.
examples.english: Dryness kills grass in the dry season.

examples.igbo: Ọ fufere isi ya mgbe ọ nụrụ akụkọ ahụ.
examples.english: He shook his head when he heard that story.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ị na-afufè isi?
examples.english: Why are you shaking your head?

examples.igbo: Ọ kpọrọ ọsọ gaa chọta dọkịta.
examples.english: He rushed to look for a doctor.

examples.igbo: Kpọọ ọsọ! Anyị na-egbu oge.
examples.english: Run quickly! We are late.

examples.igbo: Ndị uwe ojii na-edebe ụlọ ahụ abalị niile.
examples.english: The police are observing that house all night.

examples.igbo: Ị na-edebe ka nne gị si esi nri?
examples.english: Are you observing how your mother cooks?

gloss: general name for fish of the genus Distichodus

examples.igbo: Òjò bụ azụ a na-ahụ n'osimiri anyị.
examples.english: Òjò is a fish seen in our river.

examples.igbo: Nne m siri òjò ụtụtụ a.
examples.english: My mother cooked òjò this morning.

examples.igbo: Ọ bufere nwa ya gafee okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: She carried her child across the road.

examples.igbo: Bufee akpa a gafee mmiri.
examples.english: Carry this bag across the water.

examples.igbo: Egwu anyị gụrụ m olu n'abalị ahụ.
examples.english: Our singing made me lose my voice that night.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-eti mkpu nke na-agụ ya olu.
examples.english: He shouts so much that it makes him lose his voice.

examples.igbo: Okùokwè toro n'ubi nna m afọ a.
examples.english: The okùokwè yam grew in my father's farm this year.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-ere okùokwè ole n'ahịa echi?
examples.english: How many okùokwè yams will you sell at the market tomorrow?

examples.igbo: O nyere nwa ya ọkpùlùkpù anū.
examples.english: She gave her child a piece of meat.

examples.igbo: Were ọkpùlùkpù anū ahụ sie ofe.
examples.english: Use that piece of meat to cook soup.

examples.igbo: O kụrụ mkpụlụ osè n'akụkụ ụlọ ya.
examples.english: She planted pepper seeds beside her house.

examples.igbo: Ị kụrụ mkpụlụ osè afọ a?
examples.english: Did you plant pepper seeds this year?

examples.igbo: Gwa ya okwu banyere ihe ahụ.
examples.english: Speak to him about that matter.

examples.igbo: O gwara ụmụ ya okwu tupu ha alaa.
examples.english: She spoke to her children before they left.

examples.igbo: Bịakwete m ntakịrị.
examples.english: Come a little nearer to me.

examples.igbo: Ha bịakwetere anyị n'ọnụ ụzọ.
examples.english: They came nearer to us at the door.

note: The stem -bịakète is written here in its inflected forms bịakwete/bịakwetere.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-egwu egwu n'akụkụ òdọ mmīli.
examples.english: Children play beside the pond.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ azụ n'òdọ mmīli?
examples.english: Did you see fish in the pond?

gloss: go aside; go a little way

examples.igbo: Jerụka n'akụkụ ka ụmụaka gafee.
examples.english: Step aside so the children can pass.

examples.igbo: Anyị jerụka ntakịrị wee kwụsị.
examples.english: We went a little way and then stopped.

examples.igbo: N'oge gara aga, anyị na-akụ osikapa.
examples.english: In the past, we used to plant rice.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akọ akụkọ banyere n'oge gara aga.
examples.english: He tells stories about the past.

examples.igbo: O ji nchèkwube na ọ ga-enweta ọrụ ahụ.
examples.english: She is confident that she will get that job.

examples.igbo: Ị ji nchèkwube na ndị otu gị ga-emeri?
examples.english: Are you confident that your team will win?

gloss: consider; reconsider; reflect; change one's mind

examples.igbo: Tụghalịa uche gị tupu i kwuo ihe.
examples.english: Think it over before you speak.

examples.igbo: O tụghalịrị uche wee kpebie ịnọ.
examples.english: He reconsidered and decided to stay.

examples.igbo: Mmiri na-alusà n'ite ahụ.
examples.english: Water is overflowing from that pot.

examples.igbo: Lezie ofe ahụ anya ka ọ ghara ilusà.
examples.english: Watch that soup carefully so it does not overflow.

examples.igbo: Ahà oyìbo ya bụ John.
examples.english: His English name is John.

examples.igbo: Gịnị bụ ahà oyìbo gị?
examples.english: What is your English name?

gloss: make bad or disagreeable friendship (e.g. as when a person is intimate with another person whose morality and ways are bad or questionable); walk with criminals or suspects; keep bad company

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akpa ajọ ụkpa n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: He keeps bad company at school.

examples.igbo: Akpala ajọ ụkpa, nne gị ga-ewe iwe.
examples.english: Do not keep bad company, your mother will be angry.

examples.igbo: Chikelu bụ nwa nwoke m.
examples.english: Chikelu is my son.

examples.igbo: Chikelu, bịa rie nri.
examples.english: Chikelu, come and eat.

gloss: bicycle (English, compare igwè, òkpọlè, ànyìnyà igwè)

examples.igbo: Ọ zụtara basịkùlù ọhụrụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: He bought a new bicycle at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị na-agba basịkùlù aga ọrụ?
examples.english: Do you ride a bicycle to work?

examples.igbo: Anyị rutere ụlọ n'òdiìnaàbò.
examples.english: We arrived home at midnight.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-alọta n'òdiìnaàbò?
examples.english: Will you return at midnight?

examples.igbo: Ha hụjuru ānyā n'ọrụ ugbo ahụ.
examples.english: They toiled greatly in that farm work.

examples.igbo: Ọ hụjuru ānyā tupu ọ nweta ego.
examples.english: He suffered greatly before he got money.

note: The phrase is understood here as toiling or suffering greatly; phrasing may vary by dialect.

examples.igbo: Ife dị n'aka èkpè m bụ oche.
examples.english: The thing on my left is a chair.

examples.igbo: Lee ife dị n'aka èkpè gị.
examples.english: Look at what is on your left.

examples.igbo: Òkpù m na-egbu mgbu taa.
examples.english: My waist hurts today.

examples.igbo: O kegidere eriri n'òkpù ya.
examples.english: She tied a rope around her waist.

gloss: the concept of being wide and loose by giving extra allowance or space; oversize

examples.igbo: Uwe a dị ùworo n'ahụ m.
examples.english: This dress is loose on me.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ ka m mee ya ùworo?
examples.english: Do you want me to make it oversize?

note: Both sentences are idiomatic; the second is a suggestion of one natural phrasing among several.

examples.igbo: Ụzọ ahụ na-anwàcha mgbe mmiri zịsịrị.
examples.english: That road is slippery when rain falls.

examples.igbo: Kpachara anya, apịtị ebe a nwàchara!
examples.english: Be careful, the mud here is slippery!

examples.igbo: Ònyènyè ahụ na-ere akwụkwọ n'ahịa.
examples.english: That woman sells books at the market.

examples.igbo: Ònyènyè ole bịara nzukọ ahụ?
examples.english: How many women came to that meeting?

note: ònyènyè is a dialectal word beside nwaànyì; sentences are idiomatic but regional.

gloss: saw asunder Ànyqị chòlù ijiì mmà ọdụ  kwọbè osisi dāchilị ụzò We want to saw asunder the tree which fell across the road

examples.igbo: Anyị ji mmà ọdụ kwọbè osisi ahụ dara n'ụzọ.
examples.english: We used a saw to saw asunder the tree that fell on the road.

examples.igbo: Ònye kwọbèrè osisi a dara n'ụzọ?
examples.english: Who sawed asunder this tree that fell on the road?

examples.igbo: O mesòrò m ihe ọjọọ n'ahịa.
examples.english: He did a bad thing to me at the market.

examples.igbo: Gịnị ka ị mesòrò nwa ahụ?
examples.english: What did you do to that child?

examples.igbo: Ha dīnàkọrọ n'àkwà nne ha.
examples.english: They lay together on their mother's bed.

examples.igbo: Gị na nwanne gị dīnàkọrọ n'otu àkwà?
examples.english: Did you and your sibling lie together on one bed?

gloss: (literally beater of walls) instrument for smoothing wet wall, especially of a new building

examples.igbo: O ji ǹti āja mezie mgbidi ụlọ ọhụrụ ahụ.
examples.english: He used the wall-beater to smooth the wall of that new house.

examples.igbo: Wetara m ǹti āja, achọrọ m imezie mgbidi a.
examples.english: Bring me the wall-beater, I want to smooth this wall.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-ejè ejìjē otu nna ya si aga ije.
examples.english: That child mimics the way his father walks.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ejè ejìjē onye ọ bụla ị hụrụ?
examples.english: Do you mimic everyone you see?

note: The exact inflection of jè ejìjē varies; sense given is mimic/copy an action.

examples.igbo: Nwanyị ahụ gbakwọrọ imē mgbe ọ dara n'ụzọ.
examples.english: That woman miscarried when she fell on the road.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere o ji na-agbakwo imē ugboro ugboro?
examples.english: Why does she keep miscarrying again and again?

examples.igbo: O kpere mmanụ n'ahụ nwa ya.
examples.english: She smeared oil on her child's body.

examples.igbo: Kpe mmanụ n'aka gị tupu ị gaa n'ọhịa.
examples.english: Smear oil on your hands before you go to the farm.

examples.igbo: Nwatà ntà ahụ na-egwu n'ájá.
examples.english: That small child is playing in the sand.

examples.igbo: Kpachara anya, nwatà ntà nọ n'ụzọ!
examples.english: Be careful, a small child is on the road!

gloss: break off (leaves or stalks of a plant)

examples.igbo: O dọbèrè akwụkwọ ọka maka ehi.
examples.english: She broke off corn leaves for the cow.

examples.igbo: Dọbè akwụkwọ ole na ole maka ya.
examples.english: Break off a few leaves for it.

note: Inflected form dọbèrè is used; tone marks on inflections may vary by dialect.

examples.igbo: Ǹke ìbùa dị mma karịa nke mbụ.
examples.english: The second is better than the first.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ǹke ìbùa?
examples.english: Did you see the second?

examples.igbo: Ị gà-àta afụfụ ma ị ghara ịga akwụkwọ.
examples.english: You will suffer if you don't go to school.

examples.igbo: Ị gà-àta afụfụ, ọ bụghị ọṅụ.
examples.english: You will suffer, not rejoice.

examples.igbo: Bùli igbe a maka m.
examples.english: Lift this box for me.

examples.igbo: O bùliri nwa ya elu.
examples.english: She lifted her child up.

examples.igbo: Ha gbuwara ụzọ ọhụrụ gaa ahịa.
examples.english: They cut a new road to the market.

examples.igbo: Ị gbuwara ụzọ ọhụrụ?
examples.english: Did you cut a new road?

examples.igbo: O kachasịrị ya na ego.
examples.english: He surpassed him entirely in money.

examples.igbo: Ị kachasịrị ya na ọrụ?
examples.english: Did you surpass him entirely in work?

note: The suffix -chasị is less common; -kasị would be more usual in some areas.

examples.igbo: Abụja bụ isi obodo Naịjirịa.
examples.english: Abuja is the capital of Nigeria.

examples.igbo: Ị maara isi obodo Naịjirịa?
examples.english: Do you know the capital of Nigeria?

examples.igbo: Eke nà ogwùlùgwù pụtara na mbara igwe.
examples.english: A rainbow appeared in the sky.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ eke nà ogwùlùgwù?
examples.english: Did you see the rainbow?

examples.igbo: Uwe m dị mmili mmili.
examples.english: My clothes are wet.

examples.igbo: Ụlọ ahụ dị mmili mmili?
examples.english: Is that house damp?

examples.igbo: Ndị obodo na-aga afịa nkwe ìzù.
examples.english: The villagers go to the weekly market.

examples.igbo: Afịa nkwe ìzù dị n'ụbọchị nke anọ?
examples.english: Is the weekly market on the fourth day?

examples.igbo: Ndị ọrụ na-ezò ajā maka ịrụ ụlọ.
examples.english: The workers are treading mud for building a house.

examples.igbo: Ha zọrọ ajā ahụ maka mgbidi ụlọ ọhụrụ.
examples.english: They trod that mud for the wall of the new house.

note: The stem -zò is uncommon; inflected forms zọrọ/na-ezò are given but tone on the inflections may vary by dialect.

gloss: gather together; accumulate, stockpile (heavy or bulky objects)

examples.igbo: Ha na-ebukọ̀ nkụ n'otu ebe.
examples.english: They are gathering firewood in one place.

examples.igbo: Bukọ̀ọ akwụkwọ ndị ahụ n'ime igbe.
examples.english: Gather those books into the box.

note: Imperative bukọ̀ọ and progressive na-ebukọ̀ are extrapolated from the stem; a speaker might say bukọta instead.

gloss: (slang, usually among school-children) snack, small edibles like àkàlà, groundnuts, èlèlè, bought and eaten by school-children during the recess period by those who can afford it

examples.igbo: Ụmụ akwụkwọ na-eri kwọzè n'oge ezumike.
