examples.igbo: Kedu ka ezi ndụ gị dị ugbua?
examples.english: How is your health now?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-edobe ihe niile n'àkpà uchè ya.
examples.english: He keeps everything in his memory.

examples.igbo: Àkpà uchè m adịghị mma taa.
examples.english: My memory is not good today.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-ekwakọta akwa n'ime otu akpa.
examples.english: We are packing clothes together in one bag.

examples.igbo: Kwakọta ihe ndị ahụ niile n'otu ebe.
examples.english: Pack all those things together in one place.

examples.igbo: O kechiri ife mfiedo n'úkwù ya.
examples.english: He tied a girdle around his waist.

examples.igbo: Ife mfiedo ahụ dị ogologo ma sie ike.
examples.english: That girdle is long and strong.

gloss: kind of stiff bag made by Hausas for packing clothes, etc.

examples.igbo: O tinyere akwa ya niile n'okpulu.
examples.english: He put all his clothes in the okpulu bag.

examples.igbo: Okpulu a siri ike ma na-ebu ibu.
examples.english: This okpulu is stiff and carries loads.

examples.igbo: Obìikē ya mere ka ọ ghara inyere nwa ogbenye aka.
examples.english: His hardheartedness made him not help the poor child.

examples.igbo: Obìikē adịghị mma n'ebe ụmụaka nọ.
examples.english: Hardheartedness is not good towards children.

examples.igbo: Onye nkuzi na-enekọta ụmụ akwụkwọ n'ọmụmụ ihe.
examples.english: The teacher supervises the students in learning.

examples.igbo: Nekọta ọrụ ahụ nke ọma tupu anyị apụ.
examples.english: Supervise that work well before we leave.

gloss: term for the peoples of Idemmīli, Aguata and Awka Divisions

examples.igbo: Ndị Ìgbò Agba Enū bi n'Idemmīli na Aguata.
examples.english: The Igbo Agba Enu people live in Idemmili and Aguata.

examples.igbo: Ị bụ onye Ìgbò Agba Enū?
examples.english: Are you an Igbo Agba Enu person?

examples.igbo: Kechi ọnụ akpa osikapa ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: Tie the mouth of that rice bag well.

examples.igbo: O kechiri ọnụ igbe ahụ, wee buru ya pụọ.
examples.english: He tied the box shut and carried it away.

note: Uses kechi/kechiri for tying shut; standard often kechie.

examples.igbo: Ndị agha kpọdoro ya n'obe.
examples.english: The soldiers crucified him.

examples.igbo: Onye kpọdoro ya n'obe?
examples.english: Who crucified him?

examples.igbo: Ọnyá ahụ gbawara ulùulù aka ya.
examples.english: The wound tore the flesh of his hand.

examples.igbo: Ulùulù ehi ahụ na-acha ọbara ọbara.
examples.english: The cow's flesh is red.

note: ulùulù is a rare word for flesh; standard Igbo more commonly uses anụ/ahụ.

gloss: African Star-apple (Chrysophyllum delevoyi De Wild.) and White Star-apple (C. albidum G. Don)

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-ere ụdalà n'ọma ahịa.
examples.english: Children are selling star-apples at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ụdalà ndị ahụ na-acha akwụkwọ ndụ?
examples.english: Did you see those green star-apples?

examples.igbo: O jiri ngaji kuo eku ofe.
examples.english: She used a spoon to ladle soup.

examples.igbo: Kuo eku mmiri ahụ n'ime ite.
examples.english: Ladle that water into the pot.

examples.igbo: Nwa ọhụrụ na-aṅụ mmili alā.
examples.english: The baby is drinking milk.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ mmili alā ma ọ bụ mmiri?
examples.english: Do you want milk or water?

note: mmili alā appears dialectal for milk; standard Igbo is mmiri ara.

examples.igbo: O runatara ànì iji bulie nwa ahụ.
examples.english: She stooped down a bit to lift the child.

examples.igbo: Runata ànì ka ị hụ ihe dị n'ala.
examples.english: Stoop down a bit so you can see what is on the ground.

examples.igbo: O nwetara àmàlà n'aka onye isi ya.
examples.english: He got favour from his boss.

examples.igbo: Ị na-achọ àmàlà n'aka m?
examples.english: Are you seeking favour from me?

note: àmàlà appears dialectal for favour; standard Igbo is amara.

gloss: shrine; building consecrated to a deity

examples.igbo: Ha gara ụnò alūsị ịchụ àjà.
examples.english: They went to the shrine to sacrifice.

examples.igbo: Ụnò alūsị ahụ dị n'ọhịa.
examples.english: That shrine is in the bush.

note: ụnò is a dialectal form; standard is ụlọ.

examples.igbo: O zere uzerē mgbe o nụrụ ntụ.
examples.english: He sneezed when he smelled dust.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eze uzerē ugboro ugboro?
examples.english: Are you sneezing repeatedly?

examples.igbo: Ndị ohi nùchara ụlọ anyị niile.
examples.english: The thieves looted our entire house.

examples.igbo: Ònye nùchara ego ahụ?
examples.english: Who looted that money?

note: The sense 'loot' for -nùcha is not common in my dialect; examples follow the given gloss.

examples.igbo: Anyị zụtara ngịlị ewu n'ahịa.
examples.english: We bought goat intestines at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eri ngịlị ọkụkọ?
examples.english: Do you eat chicken intestines?

examples.igbo: O nwetara oghele ịga akwụkwọ.
examples.english: He got an opportunity to go to school.

examples.igbo: Oghele ọrụ ọ dị n'obodo anyị?
examples.english: Is there a job opportunity in our town?

examples.igbo: Ògùgò jupụtara n'obi ya.
examples.english: Joy filled his heart.

examples.igbo: Gịnị na-ewetara gị ògùgò?
examples.english: What brings you joy?

examples.igbo: Ndị ọrụ ugbo na-agha mkpụlụ osisi n'ubi.
examples.english: Farmers sow seeds in the farm.

examples.igbo: Ghaa mkpụlụ osisi tupu mmiri abịa.
examples.english: Sow seeds before the rain comes.

note: The phrase is understood, but 'mkpụrụ osisi' is more usual in modern speech than 'mkpụlụ osisi'.

gloss: act of pointing out guilty person by native doctor

examples.igbo: Ịtà dibịa ahụ mere ka e jide ya.
examples.english: The native doctor's pointing him out caused him to be arrested.

examples.igbo: Ndị obodo na-atụ egwu ịtà dibịa.
examples.english: The villagers fear the native doctor's pointing out.

note: This is a culturally specific term; examples follow the given gloss.

examples.igbo: Nne ya na-eme ya nnwa.
examples.english: His mother pampers him.

examples.igbo: Emela nwa gị nnwa otú ahụ.
examples.english: Don't pamper your child like that.

examples.igbo: Ọ guzoro èkèrèsò.
examples.english: He stood upright.

examples.igbo: Guzoro èkèrèsò mgbe a na-akpọ aha gị.
examples.english: Stand upright when your name is called.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-enefèga anya n'ọrụ ya.
examples.english: He neglects his work.

examples.igbo: Nefèga anya mmejọ ya ugbu a.
examples.english: Overlook his fault now.

examples.igbo: Anyị kụrụ edè n'ubi anyị.
examples.english: We planted cocoyam in our farm.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eri edè e siri esi?
examples.english: Do you eat boiled cocoyam?

note: The headword is malformed and the technical sense 'oldest type of Xanthosoma' is obscure; examples use edè as the ordinary cocoyam crop.

examples.igbo: Nna m na-arụ ọrụ ụzụ n’ụlọ ọrụ ya.
examples.english: My father does blacksmithery in his workshop.

examples.igbo: Ị na-arụ ọrụ ụzụ?
examples.english: Do you do blacksmithery?

examples.igbo: Ọ wagotara n’ụlọ anyị n’uhuruchi.
examples.english: He wandered up to our house in the evening.

examples.igbo: Wagota ebe a, ka anyị nụ akụkọ gị.
examples.english: Wander up here, so we hear your story.

examples.igbo: Mgbe ndị iro chụrụ ya, ọ gbanara n’òsu.
examples.english: When enemies chased him, he sought refuge with the deity.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-agbana n’òsu ma ndị mmadụ na-achụ gị?
examples.english: Will you seek refuge with the deity if people are chasing you?

gloss: frog whose cry is a sign of the annual flood of the Niger

examples.igbo: Àkèle na-eti mkpu n’abalị, mmiri ga-eju Osimiri Niger.
examples.english: The àkèle frog cries at night; water will fill the River Niger.

examples.igbo: Ị nụrụ àkèle n’abalị a?
examples.english: Did you hear the àkèle frog tonight?

examples.igbo: Nnụnụ ahụ fedatara n’ala ịchọ nri.
examples.english: That bird flew down to the ground looking for food.

examples.igbo: Fedata ebe a, ka m nye gị ọka.
examples.english: Fly down here, so I can give you corn.

examples.igbo: Obi tara ya mmīli, o jụrụ inyere nne ya aka.
examples.english: He was callous; he refused to help his mother.

examples.igbo: Obi tara gị mmīli, ị gaghị enyere ya aka?
examples.english: Your heart is callous; won’t you help him?

examples.igbo: Enwere m ntụkwàsì obì na ọ ga-abịa.
examples.english: I have confidence that he will come.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere ntụkwàsì obì na ya ga-eme ya?
examples.english: Do you have confidence that he will do it?

examples.igbo: O kèrè nrī ahụ n’etiti ụmụaka.
examples.english: He shared that food among the children.

examples.igbo: Kee nrī a maka ụmụaka.
examples.english: Share this food for the children.

examples.igbo: Ndị ikom na-atụ àkanya n’elu ụlọ.
examples.english: The men are laying thatch on the roof.

examples.igbo: Tụọ àkanya ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: Lay that thatch well.

examples.igbo: Ha kpọkọtara ahịhịa n’òbùbò.
examples.english: They gathered grass into a heap.

examples.igbo: Òbùbò ahụ dị n’ebe a?
examples.english: Is that heap here?

gloss: go; move from one location to another

examples.igbo: Ọ jere ahịa ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: He went to the market yesterday.

examples.igbo: Je n'ahịa, biko.
examples.english: Go to the market, please.

examples.igbo: O zụchapụrụ mkpụrụ niile.
examples.english: He bought all the seeds.

examples.igbo: Zụchapụ azụ niile taa.
examples.english: Buy all the fish today.

examples.igbo: O kwere aka na nna ya.
examples.english: He shook hands with his father.

examples.igbo: Kwe aka na ya.
examples.english: Shake hands with him.

examples.igbo: Ha nachìghachara n'ụlọ.
examples.english: They returned home.

examples.igbo: Nachìgha n'ụlọ ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Return home quickly.

note: The inflected form 'nachìghachara' may vary; the sense is clear.

examples.igbo: O tara kwọzè.
examples.english: He ate snacks.

examples.igbo: Ta kwọzè ndị a.
examples.english: Eat these snacks.

examples.igbo: O wara ọfịa.
examples.english: He wandered in the forest.

examples.igbo: Wa ọfịa ahụ.
examples.english: Wander in that forest.

note: The verb 'wa' for 'wander' is not common; the sense is inferred from the entry.

examples.igbo: O lọrọ osisi ahụ.
examples.english: He bent that stick.

examples.igbo: Lọ eriri a.
examples.english: Bend this rope.

examples.igbo: Osisi ahụ dudoro.
examples.english: That tree took root.

examples.igbo: Dudo ebe a.
examples.english: Take root here.

gloss: ascend; rise or increase; run upward; climb up (stairs)

examples.igbo: O gbago ugwu.
examples.english: He climbed the hill.

examples.igbo: Gbago steepụ ndị a.
examples.english: Climb these stairs.

examples.igbo: Uwe a na akpụkpọ ụkwụ enweghị ndagbà.
examples.english: This dress and shoes have no matching.

examples.igbo: Ndagbà dị n'etiti ha abụọ?
examples.english: Is there compatibility between the two of them?

examples.igbo: Òdìnàànì obodo anyị na-akwanyere ndị ọbịa ùgwù.
examples.english: Our town's custom respects visitors.

examples.igbo: Soro òdìnàànì anyị mee emume a.
examples.english: Follow our custom to perform this ceremony.

examples.igbo: Ji ndị a na-ere ere n'ubi.
examples.english: These yams are rotting in the farm.

examples.igbo: Kpachara anya ka azụ ghara ire ere.
examples.english: Be careful so the fish does not rot.

note: The entry lacks tone marks; examples use the idiomatic ire ere for 'rot'.

examples.igbo: Onye ọ bụla nwere ike ịdoni azụmahịa ya.
examples.english: Anyone can set up his business.

examples.igbo: Dọnịa ọnyà ahụ n'okpuru osisi.
examples.english: Set that trap under the tree.

note: Uses the verb in the sense 'set up', especially a trap or business.

gloss: move into place vacated by another

examples.igbo: Mgbe nwanne m biliri, m kwachiri n'oche ya.
examples.english: When my brother stood up, I moved into his seat.

examples.igbo: Kwachie ebe ahụ tupu mmadụ ọzọ abịa.
examples.english: Move into that place before another person comes.

note: Rare verb; imperative kwachie is used as the command form.

examples.igbo: O sikpuru ọnụ ya mgbe ọ na-achị ọchị.
examples.english: He covered his mouth when he was laughing.

examples.igbo: Sikpuo nkata ahụ ka mmiri ghara ịbanye.
examples.english: Cover that basket so rain will not enter.

note: Verb stem used with past and imperative forms.

gloss: wild animal whose horn is made into an òpì, a transversely blown signal horn

examples.igbo: Nna m ji mpi òchà mee òpì.
examples.english: My father used the horn of òchà to make an òpì.

examples.igbo: Ị hụtụla òchà n'ọhịa?
examples.english: Have you seen an òchà in the bush?

note: Rare animal name; examples keep the specific sense.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-enye ndị okenye nsọpùlụ.
examples.english: Children give respect to elders.

examples.igbo: Nye nne gị na nna gị nsọpùlụ.
examples.english: Give your mother and father respect.

note: Spelling follows the entry nsọpùlụ; standard variant is often nsọpụrụ.

examples.igbo: Ndị afù na-ere akwụkwọ n'ahịa.
examples.english: Those people sell books in the market.

examples.igbo: Ị maara ndị afù?
examples.english: Do you know those people?

gloss: yam which turns red when cut

examples.igbo: Ichekē na-acha uhie uhie ma e bee ya.
examples.english: Ichekē turns red when it is cut.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-azụ ichekē n'ahịa?
examples.english: Will you buy ichekē in the market?

note: Yam variety name; examples use it as the subject and object.

examples.igbo: O ji ngboro ebu mmiri n'ugbo.
examples.english: He uses a calabash to carry water to the farm.

examples.igbo: Weta ngboro ahụ ka anyị ṅụọ mmiri.
examples.english: Bring that calabash so we can drink water.

examples.igbo: Anyị tụlere atụmatụ ahụ tupu anyị ekweta.
examples.english: We examined that plan before we agreed.

examples.igbo: Tụlee ọnụ ahịa ya tupu ị zụta ya.
examples.english: Consider its price before you buy it.

examples.igbo: Igwe ojii na-akpata nsikpù nke anyanwụ.
examples.english: Clouds cause the obscuring of the sun.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara nsikpù anyanwụ taa?
examples.english: What caused the obscuring of the sun today?

gloss: fall in with; correspond; be in agreement with

examples.igbo: Aha ya dàbàrà n'ihe e dere n'akwụkwọ.
examples.english: His name corresponded with what was written in the book.

examples.igbo: Nke a adàbàghị na nke anyị tụrụ anya.
examples.english: This did not agree with what we expected.

examples.igbo: Òtù ụmù òkolọbìà na-ezukọ n'ụlọ nzukọ.
examples.english: The young men's society meets in the meeting hall.

examples.igbo: Ị bụ onye òtù ụmù òkolọbìà?
examples.english: Are you a member of the young men's society?

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ dinaara mmakpù n'àkwà.
examples.english: That child lay on his stomach on the bed.

examples.igbo: Dina mmakpù ka e wee hụ azụ gị.
examples.english: Lie on your stomach so we can see your back.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ nwere anya ùfìè.
examples.english: That child has squint eyes.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ele anya ùfìè mgbe ọ na-agụ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: He squints when he is reading.

examples.igbo: Anyị dunaara ọbịa ahụ ruo n'ọnụ ụzọ.
examples.english: We escorted that guest to the door.

examples.igbo: Duna nwa ahụ gaa ụlọ.
examples.english: Lead that child home.

gloss: baby hair, especially the first hair

examples.igbo: A na-akpụ àbọ̀nlị̀ nwa ọhụrụ.
examples.english: They shave the baby's first hair.

examples.igbo: Àbọ̀nlị̀ ya dị nro.
examples.english: His baby hair is soft.

examples.igbo: Iche òkù na-eṅomi okwu mmadụ.
examples.english: The parrot imitates human speech.

examples.igbo: Ị hụla iche òkù na-acha akwụkwọ ndụ?
examples.english: Have you seen a green parrot?

examples.igbo: Nne m na-asiji akwa oji n'ahịa.
examples.english: My mother dyes cloth black at the market.

examples.igbo: Siji akwa a ojii tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Dye this cloth black before you leave.

note: Verb stem; imperative and continuous forms are sound but the word is uncommon in everyday speech.

examples.igbo: Ha na-azụ ife enunu n'azụ ụlọ ha.
examples.english: They rear domestic animals behind their house.

examples.igbo: Gịnị ka ị na-enye ife enunu gị?
examples.english: What do you feed your domestic animals?

gloss: leave very early in the morning; do something very early

examples.igbo: O mara ụzọ gaa ọrụ taa.
examples.english: He left very early for work today.

examples.igbo: Mara ụzọ ka ị rute ebe ahụ n'oge.
examples.english: Leave very early so that you reach there in time.

examples.igbo: Ụsụ ọgù na-eri mkpụrụ osisi n'abalị.
examples.english: Fruit-bats eat fruit at night.

examples.igbo: Ị hụla ụsụ ọgù n'elu osisi ahụ?
examples.english: Have you seen a fruit-bat on that tree?

examples.igbo: Ògbàdụ anyị kụrụ toro nke ọma n'afọ a.
examples.english: The maize we planted grew well this year.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-ere ògbàdụ ndị a n'ahịa?
examples.english: Will you sell this maize at the market?

note: 'Ọkà' is the more common word; ògbàdụ is a dialectal variant as given.

examples.igbo: O kwutọrọ ya n'ihu ndị mmadụ.
examples.english: He slandered her in front of people.

examples.igbo: Ekwutọla onye ọ bụla n'ụzọ na-ezighị ezi.
examples.english: Do not slander anyone wrongly.

examples.igbo: Anyị ji ụkwụ gaa n'itie ụgbọala.
examples.english: We went on foot instead of by car.

examples.igbo: Ọ kụrụ osikapa n'itie ji.
examples.english: She cooked rice instead of yam.

note: Used chiefly in the phrase 'n'itie' (in place of).

examples.igbo: Ọ nọdụrụ na ekwe dị n'akụkụ ọnụ ụzọ.
examples.english: He sat on the stool beside the doorway.

examples.igbo: Kpọta ekwe ka anyị nọdụ.
examples.english: Bring a stool so that we can sit.

gloss: long, elaborately carved rod used by chiefs in title-taking

examples.igbo: Onye isi ahụ jidere ọsìsì ya wee banye n'ọha.
examples.english: The chief held his carved rod and entered the gathering.

examples.igbo: Ndị ọzọ na-ejide ọsìsì ha mgbe ha na-ekwu okwu.
examples.english: The titled men hold their carved rods when they speak.

gloss: raggedness; contemptible state (more used to refer to people than ngịlịga)

examples.igbo: Ahụrụ m ya n'ọnọdụ nkịlịka n'ahịa.
examples.english: I saw him in a contemptible state at the market.

examples.igbo: Nkịlịka dị n'uwe ya mere ndị mmadụ ji chịa ya ọchị.
examples.english: The raggedness of his clothes made people laugh at him.

examples.igbo: Onye ọrụ ahụ liri ngọ.
examples.english: That worker accepted a bribe.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eli ngọ n'aka ndị mmadụ?
examples.english: Do you accept bribes from people?

examples.igbo: Nkwaghari ya na-eme ka anyị mara na ọ dị ndụ.
examples.english: Its movement lets us know that it is alive.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ahụ nkwaghari ọ bụla n'ime ọhịa?
examples.english: Do you see any movement in the forest?

examples.igbo: M gụrụ ego ahụ niile.
examples.english: I counted all that money.

examples.igbo: Ị gụrụ akwụkwọ ahụ?
examples.english: Did you read that book?

examples.igbo: Ụlọ ahụ nwuru ọkụ n'abalị.
examples.english: That house caught fire at night.

examples.igbo: Lezie anya ka ọ ghara inwu ọkụ.
examples.english: Be careful so it does not catch fire.

examples.igbo: Ọ gbàkutere m n'oge.
examples.english: He ran to me on time.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-agbàkute m mgbe m kpọrọ gị?
examples.english: Will you run to me when I call you?

examples.igbo: O chọfere ya ruo mgbe ọ gwụrụ.
examples.english: He searched excessively for it until he was tired.

examples.igbo: Ị chọfere ya n'ebe niile?
examples.english: Did you search excessively for it everywhere?

gloss: vulture associated with Agwù, an image of which is made

examples.igbo: N'emume Agwụ, ha na-akpụ ùdènè Agwù.
examples.english: In the Agwụ festival, they carve the vulture associated with Agwụ.

examples.igbo: Ị hụtụla ùdènè Agwù na-efe efe?
examples.english: Have you seen the Agwụ vulture flying?

gloss: contract in size (of something long and flexible, e.g. snake or worm, when it draws body together before expanding)

examples.igbo: Mmiri na-agba n'ọnụ ǹgènè dị n'azụ ụlọ anyị.

examples.english: The girls go to the spring to fetch water.

examples.english: Are two people contesting for this one seat?

examples.english: Cut this wood in two before we carry it.

examples.english: Do you sell corn at the market?

examples.english: The dog ran out of the house when we opened the door.

gloss: give out light; radiate or flash (light)

examples.english: The sun is shining brightly today.

gloss: support; hold up; stop from falling

examples.english: Hold up this tree so the wind will not uproot it.

note: Inflected forms kwàdoro/kwàdoo are used; tone marking on the stem is kept.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ ego na-akpà gị mkpà?

examples.igbo: Onye duru gị ụlọ̀?

gloss: be deserving; be fitting; be suitable

examples.english: His behavior was fitting at the gathering.

examples.igbo: Ọ kwesịrị ekwesị ime otú ahụ?
examples.english: Is it fitting to do that?

examples.english: Are the matches in that box?

examples.english: Think before you answer.

examples.igbo: Ọ chọrọ ịlikwu osikapa.
examples.english: He wants to eat more rice.

examples.igbo: Likwu nri ahụ ma ọ dị gị ụtọ.
examples.english: Eat more of that food if you like it.

examples.igbo: Mama m na-eji abù ochiè abụ abụ na chọọchị.
examples.english: My mother uses the old hymn book to sing in church.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ abù ochiè n'ụlọ ụka?
examples.english: Did you see the old hymn book in church?

examples.igbo: Osisi ahụ na-ezè anyị anwū.
examples.english: That tree shelters us from the sun.

examples.igbo: Zèlụ anwū n'okpuru osisi.
examples.english: Shelter from the sun under the tree.

examples.igbo: Ndị omeiwu màrà iwu ọhụrụ na nnọkọ taa.
examples.english: The lawmakers made a new law at today's meeting.

examples.igbo: Gọọmentị na-amà iwu gbasara ụtụ isi?
examples.english: Is the government making a law about taxes?

examples.igbo: Nwa akwụkwọ ahụ mụtara banyere nsòkwụnye taa.
examples.english: That student learned about the enclitic today.

examples.igbo: Ị nụla okwu banyere nsòkwụnye n'Igbo?
examples.english: Have you heard about the enclitic in Igbo?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ata ìkekele ezē mgbe ọ na-ehi ụra.
examples.english: He grinds his teeth when he sleeps.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ata ìkekele ezē n'abalị?
examples.english: Are you grinding your teeth at night?

gloss: tied or rolled tobacco; bits of such tobacco retailed in small

examples.igbo: O tara anwụlū tupu ọ gawa ọrụ.
examples.english: He chewed tobacco before going to work.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ere anwụlū n'ahịa?
examples.english: Do you sell tobacco rolls in the market?

examples.igbo: Ọ dere aha ya n'akwụkwọ.
examples.english: He wrote his name in the book.

examples.igbo: Dee ụbọchị taa n'akwụkwọ.
examples.english: Write today's date in the book.

gloss: It is afternoon; the day draws in; the evening comes on (idiomatic)

examples.igbo: Chi èrulu, anyị ga-ala n'ụlọ.
examples.english: It is afternoon, we will go home.

examples.igbo: Chi èrulu, gịnị ka ị na-eme n'ahịa?
examples.english: It is afternoon, what are you doing in the market?

examples.igbo: Ọ mùnyere ọkụ n'abalị taa.
examples.english: She lit the lamp tonight.

examples.igbo: Mùnye ọkụ, ka anyị hụ ụzọ.
examples.english: Light the lamp so we can see the way.

gloss: stretch oneself (as sometimes done when yawning or during exhaustion or idleness)

examples.igbo: Ọ na-esè ụtịlī mgbe ọ tetara n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: He stretches when he wakes in the morning.

examples.igbo: Ị na-esè ụtịlī maka ike ọgwụgwụ?
examples.english: Are you stretching because of tiredness?

note: The phrase is uncommon; the progressive form should be acceptable.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-efe ọkụ ka nri wee sie.
examples.english: She is fanning the fire so the food cooks.

examples.igbo: Fee ọkụ, ka nri wee sie ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Fan the fire so the food cooks quickly.

examples.igbo: Ekwum dị n'ime mmiri ahụ.
examples.english: The lungfish is in that water.

examples.igbo: Anyị jidere ekwum abụọ n'ọdọ mmiri.
examples.english: We caught two lungfish in the pond.

examples.igbo: Aka ya zara āzā mgbe ọ dara.
examples.english: His hand swelled when he fell.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ụkwụ gị ji aza āzā?
examples.english: Why is your leg swelling?

note: The inflected forms of this phrase are not fully certain.

examples.igbo: Ùgònnwā bụ nwanne m nwanyị.
examples.english: Ugonna is my sister.

examples.igbo: Ùgònnwā, bịa rie nri.
examples.english: Ugonna, come and eat.

gloss: perform a ritual; perform a rite

examples.igbo: Onye dibịa fèrè nrù maka ezinụlọ ahụ.
examples.english: The dibia performed a ritual for that family.

examples.igbo: Ndị obodo na-efe nrù taa?
examples.english: Are the townspeople performing a rite today?

note: The verb form fèrè is likely correct but not common in everyday speech.

gloss: a title given to God by the Igbo people; everlasting God; God till the end of time

examples.igbo: Osebūlụ̄ụ̀wà, anyị na-ekele gị.
examples.english: Everlasting God, we thank you.

examples.igbo: Ha na-abụ abụ maka Osebūlụ̄ụ̀wà.
examples.english: They sing songs about the everlasting God.

examples.igbo: Nne m zụtara ǹshịkọ̄ abụọ n'ahịa.
examples.english: My mother bought two crabs at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị hụla ǹshịkọ̄ n'ime osimiri a?
examples.english: Have you seen a crab in this river?

examples.igbo: Ụmụ akwụkwọ na-amụ mgbàkọnàmwepụ̀ taa.
examples.english: The pupils are studying mathematics today.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-enyere m aka n'ọrụ mgbàkọnàmwepụ̀ a?
examples.english: Will you help me with this mathematics work?

examples.igbo: Ndị ikom na-eke ọbā n'ọba.
examples.english: The men are binding yams in the barn.

examples.igbo: Kee ọbā ndị a tupu mmiri abịa.
examples.english: Bind these yams before the rain comes.

examples.igbo: Nna m nwere nnukwu ǹkù anyā.
examples.english: My father has big eyebrows.

examples.igbo: O sere ǹkù anyā ya ka ọ maa mma.
examples.english: She drew her eyebrows so that she would look beautiful.

gloss: swear one's innocence by a deity

examples.igbo: O dụrụ isi na ọ naghị ezu ohi.
examples.english: He swore his innocence that he does not steal.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-adụ isi n'ihu ndị ọzọ?
examples.english: Will you swear your innocence in front of the others?

gloss: load heavily; become too heavy for Ibu afù anyìdogo Èjìma The load has become too heavy for Ejima. (Ejima has been walking along with the load on her head but now the load has become so weighty that she can no longer move)

examples.igbo: Ibu nkụ ahụ anyịdogo nwa m n'ụzọ.
examples.english: That load of firewood became too heavy for my child on the road.

examples.igbo: Ha nyịdoro ya ibu nke ukwuu.
examples.english: They loaded him with a very heavy load.

examples.igbo: Ha na-ewuli ụlọ ọhụrụ n'obodo anyị.
examples.english: They are building up a new house in our town.

examples.igbo: Wuli mgbidi a elu ntakịrị.
examples.english: Build up this wall a little.

examples.igbo: Okwu ya mere m ifelē n'ihu ndị mmadụ.
examples.english: His words put me to shame in front of people.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ ime nwanne gị ifelē?
examples.english: Do you want to put your sibling to shame?

gloss: dig up earth into beds for planting

examples.igbo: Ha na-abọni abọni n'ubi maka ịkụ akwụkwọ nri.
examples.english: They are digging the earth into beds on the farm to plant vegetables.

examples.igbo: Bọni abọni n'ubi tupu ị kụọ ihe ọ bụla.
examples.english: Dig the earth into beds on the farm before you plant anything.

examples.igbo: Wopụ uwe gị tupu ị banye n'ụlọ.
examples.english: Take off your clothes before you enter the house.

examples.igbo: Ọ wopụrụ uwe ya tupu ọ banye n'ime mmiri.
examples.english: He took off his clothes before he entered the water.

examples.igbo: Ikerike ọkụ na-awụpụ n'ọkụ ahụ.
examples.english: Sparks are flying out of that fire.

examples.igbo: Otu ikerike ọkụ dara n'aka m.
examples.english: A spark fell on my hand.

gloss: cover a hole by filling it up

examples.igbo: Kpochie oghere ahụ na ájá.
examples.english: Fill that hole with sand.

examples.igbo: O kpochiri oghere ahụ na ájá.
examples.english: He filled that hole with sand.

gloss: the variety of Dioscorea dumentorum which is white

examples.igbo: Nne m zụtara ònà mmēe n'ahịa.
examples.english: My mother bought ònà mmēe at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ònà mmēe n'ubi?
examples.english: Did you see ònà mmēe on the farm?

note: The word refers to a specific white yam variety; the sentences are plausible but I am less certain of its everyday collocations.

examples.igbo: Anya mkpọ gbara nwoke ahụ.
examples.english: Blindness struck that man.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ nwere anya mkpọ site n'ọmụmụ.
examples.english: That child has blindness from birth.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka abụọ a na-esò n'òfu.
examples.english: These two children are of the same age.

examples.igbo: Ị na-esò n'òfu nwanne gị nwoke?
examples.english: Are you the same age as your brother?

gloss: what?! (to make someone repeat what s/he said)

examples.igbo: Ee? Gịnị ka ị sịrị?
examples.english: What?! What did you say?

examples.igbo: Ee? Anụghị m nke ọma.
examples.english: What? I didn't hear well.

examples.igbo: Nwa a na-abòcha okwu ndị okenye.
examples.english: This child is inquisitive about adults' conversations.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji na-abòcha ihe gbasara m?
examples.english: Why are you digging out information about me?

examples.igbo: Ala ebe a saa obodobo.
examples.english: The land here is flat.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ebe ala ahụ saa obodobo?
examples.english: Did you see where that land is flat?

note: The phrase is understood, but I would phrase the second sentence a little differently in everyday speech.

examples.igbo: Mma ahụ nyụrụ nkọ.
examples.english: That knife is blunt.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ mma a nyụrụ nkọ ka ị na-eji?
examples.english: Is it this blunt knife that you are using?

examples.igbo: O firi ewu ya n'osisi.
examples.english: He tied his goat to a tree.

examples.igbo: Fie eriri a n'úkwù gị tupu ị banye n'ọhịa.
examples.english: Tie this rope around your waist before you go into the bush.

note: Tone marking on the inflected verb is left plain because the headword carries none.

examples.igbo: Dọkịta lere ya ùle tupu ọ nye ya ọgwụ.
examples.english: The doctor examined him before giving him medicine.

examples.igbo: Le ya ùle tupu i zụta ya.
examples.english: Examine it before you buy it.

examples.igbo: Ndị uwe ojii tụrụ onye ohi ahụ ǹga.
examples.english: The police imprisoned that thief.

examples.igbo: Ebee ka ha tụrụ nwanne gị ǹga?
examples.english: Where did they imprison your brother?

examples.igbo: Ewu bụ ife nsō n'obodo ha.
examples.english: Goat is a forbidden thing in their town.

examples.igbo: Gịnị bụ ife nsō n'obodo gị?
examples.english: What is a forbidden thing in your town?

examples.igbo: Dọkịta lere ọtù nwaanyị ahụ anya.
examples.english: The doctor examined that woman's vulva.

examples.igbo: Nwa agbọghọ ahụ kwuru na ọtù ya na-egbu ya mgbu.
examples.english: The girl said her vulva was paining her.

note: Register is clinical; phrasing is sound but a speaker might prefer a different verb.

examples.igbo: O jidere akpùlù ekwē n'aka ya.
examples.english: He held an unsplit cane in his hand.

examples.igbo: Ebee ka i tinyere akpùlù ekwē ahụ?
examples.english: Where did you put that unsplit cane?

examples.igbo: Ọ dị m n'anya inye ya aka n'ọrụ.
examples.english: I wish to help him with the work.

examples.igbo: Gịnị dị gị n'anya n'ahịa a?
examples.english: What do you desire in this market?

note: The desire/wish sense overlaps with 'to love', so context is doing some work here.

gloss: announcement; notice that may be written or verbal; advance information

examples.igbo: Ọkwà ahụ bụ na ahịa ga-emechi echi.
examples.english: The announcement was that the market will close tomorrow.

examples.igbo: Ị nụrụ ọkwà ahụ ha kwuru?
examples.english: Did you hear that announcement they made?

examples.igbo: Ndị dọkịta kànyere ụmụaka ọgwụ taa.
examples.english: The doctors vaccinated the children today.

examples.igbo: Kànye nwa gị ọgwụ tupu ọ malite akwụkwọ.
examples.english: Vaccinate your child before he starts school.

gloss: put in effort; endeavor; try hard

examples.igbo: Ọ gbalịrị ike, mana ọ dara ule ahụ.
examples.english: He tried hard, but he failed that exam.

examples.igbo: Gbalịa ka ị rute ebe ahụ n'oge.
examples.english: Try hard to reach that place on time.

gloss: behold; look (at); gaze at; look after; mind

examples.igbo: Ne anya nwa gị mgbe ị na-aga ahịa.
examples.english: Look after your child when you go to market.

examples.igbo: O nere anya ubi ya kwa ụtụtụ.
examples.english: He looked after his farm every morning.

gloss: unroof; break up roof; be broken

examples.igbo: Kpùkpòpù ụlọ ochie ahụ tupu mmiri abịa.
examples.english: Unroof that old house before rain comes.

examples.igbo: Ha na-akpùkpòpù ụlọ ahụ.
examples.english: They are unroofing that house.

examples.igbo: Bịachìgha n'ụlọ taa.
examples.english: Come back home today.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-abịachìgha echi?
examples.english: Will you come back tomorrow?

examples.igbo: Nna m na-akpọ ùbọ na chọọchị.
examples.english: My father plays organ in church.

examples.igbo: Kpọọ ùbọ ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: Play that instrument well.

gloss: extol; salute by title, nickname; hail

examples.igbo: Ha tụrụ ya ahà 'Ogbuefi' n'ememme.
examples.english: They hailed him with the title 'Ogbuefi' at the ceremony.

examples.igbo: Tụọ nna gị ahà ya.
examples.english: Hail your father by his name.

examples.igbo: Isi ya chaala aghọ.
examples.english: His hair has turned grey.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ahụ na ntutu ya na-acha aghọ?
examples.english: Do you see that his hair is turning grey?

gloss: end a speech Bikō, kwubìzịa okwu afù Please, end that speech

examples.igbo: O kwubìrì okwu ya na nzukọ.
examples.english: He ended his speech at the meeting.

examples.igbo: Kwubì okwu gị, oge agwụla.
examples.english: End your speech, time is up.

examples.igbo: O nụrụ ọbìà anyị nke ọma.
examples.english: He welcomed us well.

examples.igbo: Nụọ ọbìà ndị ọbịa ahụ.
examples.english: Offer hospitality to those guests.

examples.igbo: Anyị riri nni akpū na ofe akwụ.
examples.english: We ate cassava fufu with vegetable soup.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ nni akpū?
examples.english: Do you want cassava fufu?

examples.igbo: O rìrì amā n'akwụkwọ ahụ.
examples.english: He marked that book.

examples.igbo: Rịa amā ebe ị kwụsịrị.
examples.english: Mark where you stopped.

examples.igbo: Ọ nọ n'eluēlū ugwu ahụ.
examples.english: He is at the topmost part of that hill.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ eluēlū ụlọ ya?
examples.english: Did you see the topmost part of his house?

note: Word form eluēlū is uncommon; I interpreted it as the topmost part.

gloss: very gently, slowly, softly; gradually Na-àkpụ yā nwayòò nwayòò Be pulling it gently or slowly

examples.igbo: Gaa nwayòò nwayòò, ụzọ ahụ dị warara.
examples.english: Go slowly; that road is narrow.

examples.igbo: O bu nnukwu ite ahụ nwayòò nwayòò.
examples.english: She carried that big pot gently.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka ahụ metọrọ mmiri anyị.
examples.english: Those children spoiled our water.

examples.igbo: Ị na-emetọ nri ahụ?
examples.english: Are you spoiling that food?

examples.igbo: Ndị ọnwò bịara n'ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: Some people came to our house.

examples.igbo: Ndị ọnwò na-ekwu okwu banyere gị?
examples.english: Are some people talking about you?

note: Expression ndị ọnwò is not common in all dialects; I used it as 'some people'.

examples.igbo: Ndị nwoke na-eke ji n'ubi.
examples.english: The men are harvesting yam in the farm.

examples.igbo: Kee ji a, anyị ga-esi ya.
examples.english: Cut this yam; we will cook it.

examples.igbo: Osisi ahụ chanwụrụ n'ihi okpomọkụ.
examples.english: That tree withered because of the heat.

examples.igbo: Ahịhịa gị ọ chanwụrụ?
examples.english: Did your grass wither?

examples.igbo: Ọrịa ahụ na-agbasa n'obodo anyị.
examples.english: The disease is spreading in our town.

examples.igbo: Ọkụ na-agbasa n'ọhịa, kpachara anya!
examples.english: Fire is spreading in the bush; be careful!

examples.igbo: O ji òpìà gbuo osisi.
examples.english: He used a matchet to cut the tree.

examples.igbo: Were òpìà gbuo ahịhịa ahụ.
examples.english: Use a matchet to cut that grass.

examples.igbo: Nnụnụ ahụ na-erebiga n'elu osisi.
examples.english: That bird glides over the trees.

examples.igbo: Ụgbọelu ahụ rebìgara n'elu ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: That plane glided over our house.

note: The stem -rebìga is uncommon; I used it with the sense 'glide over'.

examples.igbo: Nwanyị ahụ bụ ọ̀kpàdi, ọ napụrụ di nwanne m.
examples.english: That woman is a husband snatcher; she snatched my sister's husband.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-akpọ ya ọ̀kpàdi n'ihu ọha?
examples.english: Will you call her a husband snatcher in public?

note: Colloquial and insulting term; examples are idiomatic but the word is not used in formal contexts.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-egwu mmiri n'iyī dị n'akụkụ ubi anyị.
examples.english: The children are swimming in the stream by our farm.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ iyī ahụ na-asọ n'akụkụ ụlọ akwụkwọ?
examples.english: Did you see that stream flowing by the school?

examples.igbo: M na-aga ahịa ugbua ịzụta nri.
examples.english: I am going to the market now to buy food.

examples.igbo: Gaa were nnu n'ahịa maka nne gị.
examples.english: Go and get salt in the market for your mother.

examples.igbo: Ahụrụ m ǹzò ụkwū ya n'ájá.
examples.english: I saw his footprint in the sand.

examples.igbo: Ǹzò ụkwū onye dị n'ọnụ ụzọ?
examples.english: Whose footprint is at the doorway?

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ na-adàghàrị̀ mgbe ọ na-eje ije.
examples.english: That man staggers when he walks.

examples.igbo: Jide ya aka ka ọ ghara ịdàghàrị̀ n'ụzọ.
examples.english: Hold his hand so he will not stagger on the road.

note: The verb form is plausible; a speaker might prefer a different inflection in the second sentence.

examples.igbo: Elu igwe jupụtara na mmili òlùlù taa.
examples.english: The sky is full of gathering clouds today.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ mmili òlùlù n'elu igwe?
examples.english: Did you see the gathering clouds in the sky?

note: The term is regional or specialised for clouds that gather before rain.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-asi n̄gọ na nwanne ya ga-alọta.
examples.english: He obstinately doubts that his brother will return.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji si n̄gọ na ọ ga-abịa?
examples.english: Why do you obstinately doubt that he will come?

note: The exact sense and syntax of si n̄gọ are not fully clear to me; examples are my best attempt.

examples.igbo: Onye nkuzi gwara anyị tinye akàrà mkpu n'ahịrịokwu.
examples.english: The teacher told us to put an exclamation mark in the sentence.

examples.igbo: Akàrà mkpu na-egosi mmetụta siri ike n'edemede.
examples.english: An exclamation mark shows strong feeling in writing.

gloss: dry raw tobacco leaves not yet chemically prepared

examples.igbo: Ùtabà ufū dị n'ime akpa ahụ.
examples.english: The dry raw tobacco leaves are in that bag.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ere ùtabà ufū ka ọ bụ nke a kwadebere?
examples.english: Do you sell dry raw tobacco leaves or prepared ones?

note: This is a specialised agricultural term; the examples are sound but somewhat technical.

examples.igbo: Ndị uwe ojii na-eche n̄chē n'abalị.
examples.english: The police keep watch at night.

examples.igbo: Chē n̄chē nke ọma, ndị ohi na-abịa.
examples.english: Keep watch well, thieves are coming.

examples.igbo: Ọrịa ahụ na-efe èfè n'etiti ụmụaka.
examples.english: That disease is contagious among children.

examples.igbo: Zere onye ọrịa na-efe èfè.
examples.english: Avoid someone with a contagious illness.

examples.igbo: Ụmụ okorobịa ahụ mere ife ikē n'ahịa.
examples.english: Those young men committed violence at the market.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji eme ife ikē n'ụlọ?
examples.english: Why are you committing violence in the house?

examples.igbo: O fochapụrụ ahịhịa niile n'ubi.
examples.english: He cleared away all the weeds in the farm.

examples.igbo: Fochapụ efere ndị a niile n'elu tebụl.
examples.english: Clear away all these plates on the table.

examples.igbo: Mama zụtara ịfùlịfū àgwà ọhụrụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: Mother bought fresh bean pods at the market.

examples.igbo: Ghee ịfùlịfū àgwà ndị a tupu i sie ha.
examples.english: Shell these bean pods before you cook them.

note: The tone marking of the headword is unusual; I have kept it as given.

examples.igbo: O ji ǹti na-eti akwa n'osimiri.
examples.english: She uses a beater to beat the clothes at the river.

examples.igbo: Ebé ka ǹti dị?
examples.english: Where is the beater?

note: I am not fully sure of the exact range of ǹti as a shortening of ǹtiti; the sentences use the 'thing you beat with' sense.

examples.igbo: Ibu ọkà ahụ kwàchara n'isi ya daa n'ala.

examples.english: Did you drive that cow far away?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ekwu okwu azụ banyere onye agbata obi ya.
examples.english: He is slandering his neighbor.

examples.igbo: I kwuru okwu azụ banyere m n'ahịa?
examples.english: Did you backbite me at the market?

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ ji egbòokwū kọọ akụkọ ya.
examples.english: That child told his story with hyperbole.

examples.igbo: Egbòokwū adịghị mma n'akụkọ ụmụaka.
examples.english: Hyperbole is not good in children's stories.

examples.igbo: Ọkụkọ na-akọ ala achọ nri.
examples.english: The chicken scratches the ground looking for food.

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ kọrọ aka ya na mgbidi.
examples.english: That child scratched his hand on the wall.

examples.igbo: Mmā obi ya pụtara ìhè n'obodo.
examples.english: The goodness of his heart is evident in the town.

examples.igbo: Ị hụla mmā nke okooko a?
examples.english: Have you seen the beauty of this flower?

examples.igbo: Nwoke a bụ òmeǹkà n'ịkpụ ihe.
examples.english: This man is talented at carving things.

examples.igbo: Ị bụ òmeǹkà n'ịrụ ọrụ aka?
examples.english: Are you talented at handiwork?

examples.igbo: O gbutùrù osisi ukwu ahụ.
examples.english: He felled that big tree.

examples.igbo: Gbutùo osisi a, weta ya n'ụlọ.
examples.english: Cut down this tree and bring it home.

gloss: consider; take counsel; consult together; advise

examples.igbo: Anyị ràrà alò tupu anyị ekpebie ihe.
examples.english: We took counsel before we decided the matter.

examples.igbo: Ị ràrà alò na ndị okenye tupu i lụọ?
examples.english: Did you consult the elders before you married?

note: The phrase is correct; tone marking on the inflected verb may vary by speaker.

gloss: plant with spotted leaves and corm, the juice of which can be used to mark the body (Cynastrum cordifolium)

examples.igbo: Edē ànà na-eto n'akụkụ ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: Ede ànà grows near our house.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka ji edē ànà na-ete ahụ.
examples.english: Children use ede ànà to mark their bodies.

note: Rare botanical term; examples are simple and plausible but not from daily speech.

gloss: traditional presentation of gifts to the ọkpala, especially at great feasts

examples.igbo: Ha mere òfùfe ǹrù n'oge oriri ahụ.
examples.english: They made the òfùfe ǹrù presentation during that feast.

examples.igbo: Ọkpala nabatara òfùfe ǹrù site n'aka ụmụnna.
examples.english: The ọkpala received the òfùfe ǹrù from the kinsmen.

note: Cultural term; examples are constructed from the dictionary sense.

gloss: sow; broadcast; plant seed by scattering

examples.igbo: O ghaara mkpụrụ n'ubi ya.
examples.english: He sowed seeds in his farm.

examples.igbo: Ghaa mkpụrụ tupu mmiri ezo.
examples.english: Scatter the seeds before the rain falls.

examples.igbo: O kọọrọ anyị akụkọ ọchị.
examples.english: He told us a funny story.

examples.igbo: Kọọ m akụkọ gbasara njem gị.
examples.english: Tell me a story about your journey.

examples.igbo: Okwu a bụ ife iwē n'ezie.
examples.english: This matter is truly an annoying thing.

examples.igbo: Ị hụla ife iwē dị otú a?
examples.english: Have you seen such an annoying thing?

gloss: one who takes care of a town or a community

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ òdozi òbòdò anyị.
examples.english: He is the caretaker of our town.

examples.igbo: Òdozi òbòdò na-eleba anya n'ihe gbasara obodo.
examples.english: The town caretaker looks after the community's affairs.

examples.igbo: Anyị fere àkwà mmiri ahụ n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: We crossed that river in the morning.

examples.igbo: Ị fere àkwà mmiri ahụ?
examples.english: Did you cross that river?

examples.igbo: O nyere m otu dollar maka ọrụ ahụ.
examples.english: He gave me one dollar for that work.

examples.igbo: Dollar ole ka ị nwetara?
examples.english: How many dollars did you get?

examples.igbo: Anyị nwere atụrụ teghete n'ụlọ.
examples.english: We have nine sheep at home.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ teghete ka ọ bụ iri?
examples.english: Is it nine or ten?

note: Teghete is a numeral; usage may vary by dialect.

gloss: the washing away of the earth's surface by water or wind; erosion

examples.igbo: Mmiri ozuzo kpatara m̀bùze n'ubi anyị.
examples.english: Rain caused erosion on our farm.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ m̀bùze n'okporo ụzọ ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see erosion on that road?

examples.igbo: Ekwòlò juru ya afọ mgbe ọ hụrụ ụgbọala ọhụrụ m.
examples.english: Envy filled him when he saw my new car.

examples.igbo: Ị na-enwe ekwòlò n'ebe nwanne gị nọ?
examples.english: Do you feel envy toward your brother?

examples.igbo: Onye ọrụ ahụ bughàlịrị igbe ahụ.
examples.english: That worker carried that box badly.

examples.igbo: Ị bughàlịrị akpa m?
examples.english: Did you carry my bag badly?

note: Inflection uncertain; I used bughàlịrị for past.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-emegwalu ndị iro ya.
examples.english: He takes revenge on his enemies.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-emegwalu ya maka ihe o mere?
examples.english: Will you take revenge on him for what he did?

note: Spelling/inflection of -megwalụ may vary.

examples.igbo: Ụgbọelu ahụ fegara Lagos n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: That plane flew over to Lagos in the morning.

examples.igbo: Ụmụ nnụnụ fegara n'elu osisi ahụ?
examples.english: Did the birds fly over to the top of that tree?

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ mìkpọrọ akwa mgbe o dara.
examples.english: The child burst out crying when he fell.

examples.igbo: Ị mìkpọrọ akwa n'ihu ha?
examples.english: Did you burst out crying in front of them?

note: Past form assumed as mìkpọrọ; inflection may vary.

examples.igbo: Ọ yàtọrọ ọnū n'ihu ọha.
examples.english: He was vulgar in public.

examples.igbo: Yàtọla ọnū n'ihu ụmụaka ndị a.
examples.english: Don't be vulgar in front of these children.

examples.igbo: Òfùfù ahịa ahụ wutere anyị.
examples.english: The loss from that market pained us.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ òfùfù anyị tara taa?
examples.english: Did you see the loss we suffered today?

examples.igbo: Ụmụ akwụkwọ ìriàtọ nà otù bịara ule.
examples.english: Thirty-one students came to the exam.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara ìriàtọ nà otù n'ime ọkụkọ?
examples.english: Did you buy thirty-one of the chickens?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-edo Agbàlà kwa ụtụtụ.
examples.english: He performs Agbala sacrifice every morning.

examples.igbo: Doo Agbàlà taa tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Perform Agbala sacrifice today before you leave.

gloss: shower of rain; few drops of rain

examples.igbo: Nsansa mmīli dara n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: A shower of rain fell at the market today.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ nsansa mmīli n'ụtụtụ?
examples.english: Did you see the shower of rain this morning?

examples.igbo: Nne m na-agwe ọkà n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: My mother pounds corn in the morning.

examples.igbo: Gwe ọkà tupu ị sie nri.
examples.english: Pound corn before you cook.

gloss: separate chaff or foreign body; sift; sieve

examples.igbo: Yọcha ọka a tupu ị gwe ya.
examples.english: Sift this corn before you pound it.

examples.igbo: Ọ yọchara osikapa ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: She sifted that rice well.

gloss: cupping; drawing of blood with horn or horn-shaped calabash from any part of the body to relieve congestion, swelling, pain; getting rid of impure or stagnant blood

examples.igbo: O mere òchi n'úkwù nna ya.
examples.english: He performed cupping on his father's waist.

examples.igbo: Òchi na-ewepụ ọbara ruru unyi?
examples.english: Does cupping remove impure blood?

examples.igbo: Ụdọ ahụ na-enunù n'osisi.
examples.english: The rope is entangled in the tree.

examples.igbo: Okwu a na-enunù m nke ukwuu.
examples.english: This matter perplexes me greatly.

examples.igbo: Bịadị, ị hụrụ nwanne m n'ahịa?
examples.english: By the way, did you see my brother at the market?

examples.igbo: Bịadị, echefuru m akwụkwọ m n'ụlọ.
examples.english: By the way, I forgot my book at home.

examples.igbo: O kwere isi mgbe o nụrụ okwu ahụ.
examples.english: He nodded when he heard that word.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akwē isi mgbe a na-akpọ gị aha?
examples.english: Do you nod when your name is called?

examples.igbo: O wụchiri olulu ahụ na okwute.
examples.english: He filled that hole with stones.

examples.igbo: Wụchie olulu ahụ tupu mmiri abịa.
examples.english: Fill that hole before rain comes.

examples.igbo: Alịlị na-aga n'ala mgbe mmiri zoro.
examples.english: Millipede walks on the ground when it rains.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ alịlị n'ime ụlọ?
examples.english: Did you see a millipede in the house?

examples.igbo: Ènwè ọfīa na-eri mkpụrụ osisi n'ọhịa.
examples.english: Wild monkey eats fruit in the forest.

examples.igbo: Anyị hụrụ ènwè ọfīa n'elu osisi.
examples.english: We saw a wild monkey on the tree.

examples.igbo: O sụrụ iwe mgbe a kpọghị ya.
examples.english: He sulked when he was not called.

examples.igbo: Ị na-esù iwe mgbe ọ bụla?
examples.english: Do you sulk every time?

examples.igbo: Gọọmenti tiwanyere ụgwọ ọrụ ndị ọrụ.
examples.english: Government raised workers' salaries.

examples.igbo: Tiwanye nri n'efere ahụ.
examples.english: Put more food in that plate.

gloss: make quarrelsome noise; quarrel noisily; make tumultous noise

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-afịọ ùzù n'èzí.
examples.english: Children are making quarrelsome noise outside.

examples.igbo: Afịọla ùzù n'ebe a!
examples.english: Don't make quarrelsome noise here!

gloss: secure from danger; protect from danger

examples.igbo: O chekwara ụmụ ya pụọ n'ihe ize ndụ.
examples.english: He protected his children from danger.

examples.igbo: Chekwa ego gị nke ọma.
examples.english: Protect your money well.

examples.igbo: Leru anyā ka ị ghara ịdaba.
examples.english: Be careful so you don't fall.

examples.igbo: O leruru anyā n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: He was watchful on the road.

examples.igbo: Tụgharịa osikapa ahụ n’ite.
examples.english: Turn the rice in the pot.

examples.igbo: Ọ tụgharịrị bọọlụ ahụ n’elu ụlọ.
examples.english: He tossed the ball onto the roof.

examples.igbo: Ọ kwukpọrọ mmejọ ya.
examples.english: He covered up his mistake with words.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ikwukpò okwu ahụ.
examples.english: Don't cover up that matter with words.

gloss: abandon; neglect; let go astray; allow too much liberty to (e.g. a child, which leads it to be a trifle spoilt or wild)

examples.igbo: Ọ na-aràfù nwa ya.
examples.english: She is neglecting her child.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ịràfù nwa gị.
examples.english: Don't neglect your child.

examples.igbo: Ọ gọrọ àgìgò na ọ hụrụ ya.
examples.english: She denied that she saw him.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ịgọ àgìgò.
examples.english: Don't deny it.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-apaga nri n’ụlọ nne ya.
examples.english: He is carrying food to his mother's house.

examples.igbo: Paga ya akwụkwọ a.
examples.english: Carry this book to him.

gloss: knock off or hit out (teeth or anything fixed), especially resulting to a shatter or breakage

examples.igbo: Ọ kụwàpụ̀rù ezé ya n’ala.
examples.english: He knocked his tooth out onto the ground.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ịkụwàpụ̀ ezé nwa gị.
examples.english: Don't knock out your child's tooth.

examples.igbo: Ọrụ ya nile bụ ùfolō.
examples.english: All his work is useless.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ime ùfolō n’ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: Don't do useless things at school.

examples.igbo: Nkịta na-asala mmilī n’efere.
examples.english: The dog is lapping water in the bowl.

examples.igbo: Sala mmilī n’efere gị, nkịta.
examples.english: Lap water from your bowl, dog.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-akwụba n’ime mmiri.
examples.english: The child is jumping into the water.

examples.igbo: Kwụbà n’ime mmiri ozugbo!
examples.english: Jump into the water at once!

examples.igbo: Ọ na-arughalị ụgbọ ya n’okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: He is turning his car on the road.

examples.igbo: Rughalịa ihu gị n’akụkụ a.
examples.english: Turn your face this way.

examples.igbo: Ndị agha ahụ kpọgburu onye ohi ahụ n'elu obe.
examples.english: Those soldiers crucified that thief on the cross.

examples.igbo: Ònye ka ha kpọgburu n'elu obe ụnyaahụ?
examples.english: Whom did they crucify on the cross yesterday?

examples.igbo: Nne ya kpara ya ǹtàtabùlabù, nwa ahụ wee chịa ọchị.
examples.english: His mother tickled him, and the child laughed.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji akpa nwa ahụ ǹtàtabùlabù?
examples.english: Why are you tickling that child?

note: Ǹtàtabùlabù is a noun; I have used it with the verb -kpa (ịkpa ntàtabùlabù), which is the usual collocation, but I am not fully certain it is the only verb used.

examples.igbo: O bùnitere osisi ọhụrụ ahụ n'ala.
examples.english: He uprooted that young tree from the ground.

examples.igbo: Bùnite ahịhịa ndị a tupu mmiri abịa.
examples.english: Uproot these weeds before the rain comes.

gloss: the tenth month of the year; October

examples.igbo: N'ọnwa Ọ̀ktobà, anyị na-ewe ihe ubi ọka.
examples.english: In October we harvest the maize.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-abịa n'ọnwa Ọ̀ktobà?
examples.english: Will you come in October?

gloss: child believed to belong to a group in the world of spirits to which he/she returns after dying in infancy, only to go back to his mother's womb again. See ògbanje

examples.igbo: Ha kwuru na nwa ahụ bụ nwa ọgbanje.
examples.english: They said that child is an ọgbanje child.

examples.igbo: Ị kwere na nwa ọgbanje dị?
examples.english: Do you believe ọgbanje children exist?

note: The headword is written with ō (a macron); I have used the ordinary spelling ọgbanje, which is what appears elsewhere in the entry.

examples.igbo: Olu ha abụọ dàkọ̀rị̀tà n'egwu ahụ.
examples.english: Their two voices were in harmony in that song.

examples.igbo: Olee otú olu ha si adàkọ̀rị̀tà otú a?
examples.english: How do their voices harmonise like this?

note: The word is uncommon to me; the sentences use it as a stative verb about voices agreeing, which fits the gloss but I would phrase the second one differently myself.

examples.igbo: O nwere obì mgbalù mgbe ọ nụrụ akụkọ ahụ.
examples.english: He was melancholy when he heard that news.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara obì mgbalù gị?
examples.english: What caused your melancholy?

note: Obì mgbalù is a fairly literary expression; the sentences are idiomatic but a speaker might prefer a plainer word for sadness.

examples.igbo: O zùbere ịga ahịa echi.
examples.english: He planned to go to the market tomorrow.

examples.igbo: Gịnị ka ị zùbere ime n'afọ a?
examples.english: What have you planned to do this year?

note: I have inflected the stem as zùbe / zùbere; the sense of 'determine, purpose' is clear, but the usual everyday verb for 'plan' is -zube in some dialects only.

examples.igbo: Ọ kuru mmiri n'ime ite ahụ.
examples.english: She scooped water out of that pot.

examples.igbo: Kuo osikapa ahụ n'efere gị.
examples.english: Scoop that rice onto your plate.

note: The entry has no hyphen, but the sense 'take by scooping' is verbal, so I have inflected it as ku / kuru / kuo.

examples.igbo: Àkàtaàkà pụtara n'ọma ahịa, ụmụaka na-atụ egwu.
examples.english: The àkàtaàkà masquerade came out in the market square and the children were afraid.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ àkàtaàkà n'ememme ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see the àkàtaàkà masquerade at that festival?

note: Àkàtaàkà is a local masquerade name; the sentences are ordinary, but the word will not be recognised in every Igbo area.

examples.igbo: Onye kpuru ìsì ahụ na-ere ahịa n'ọma.
examples.english: That blind person sells in the market.

examples.igbo: Ị maara onye kpuru ìsì bi n'akụkụ ụlọ gị?
examples.english: Do you know the blind person living near your house?

gloss: gun, especially being portrayed as powerful

examples.igbo: Ekwēnchē ya na-ada ụda n'abalị.
examples.english: His gun resounds at night.

examples.igbo: Ndị uwe ojii bu ekwēnchē gaa n'ọhịa.
examples.english: The police carried guns to the forest.

note: Ekwēnchē is a rare or poetic word for gun.

examples.igbo: Onye dibịa fere mmiri ka ọ ghara ịda.
examples.english: The dibia drove away the rain so it would not fall.

examples.igbo: Fee mmiri ka anyị gaa ahịa.
examples.english: Drive away the rain so we can go to the market.

note: Fe mmiri is a ritual expression for driving away rain.

examples.igbo: Èkènedị̀lịchukwu, anyị lọtara n'udo.
examples.english: Praise be to God, we returned safely.

examples.igbo: O kwuru, Èkènedị̀lịchukwu, mgbe ọ hụrụ nwa ya.
examples.english: He said, Praise be to God, when he saw his child.

examples.igbo: Nri ahụ wèjuru anyị aka, anyị riri ya.
examples.english: That food was enough for us, we ate it.

examples.igbo: Ego a ọ wèjuru gị aka?
examples.english: Is this money enough for you?

note: The construction wèju mmadụ aka is idiomatic for having enough.

examples.igbo: Òkọtọ mmadụ bịara ahịa taa.
examples.english: Very many people came to the market today.

examples.igbo: Ị nwetara òkọtọ ego n'ahịa?
examples.english: Did you get a lot of money at the market?

note: Òkọtọ is less common than ọtụtụ but fits the given sense.

gloss: a moment, minute, very short time

examples.igbo: Chere nwa mkpìlìkpì ogè, m na-abịa.
examples.english: Wait a moment, I am coming.

examples.igbo: Ọ nọrọ nwa mkpìlìkpì ogè wee lawa.
examples.english: He stayed for a very short time and left.

examples.igbo: Òyìyì anyị na-aga n'ubi na-enyere anyị aka.
examples.english: Our going together to the farm helps us.

examples.igbo: Òyìyì ọ na-amasị gị mgbe anyị na-aga ahịa?
examples.english: Do you like going together when we go to the market?

note: Òyìyì is used here as the noun for going together.

examples.igbo: O gbajipụrụ alaka osisi ahụ.
examples.english: He broke off that tree branch.

examples.igbo: Gbajipụ alaka ahụ tupu ọ daa.
examples.english: Break off that branch before it falls.

gloss: sasswood tree (very poisonous) (Erythrophleum guineense G. Don)

examples.igbo: Òrachi dị n'ọhịa anyị, ụmụaka akwụsịla ịra ya.
examples.english: Sasswood is in our forest, children should not chew it.

examples.igbo: Ị maara osisi òrachi?
examples.english: Do you know the sasswood tree?

examples.igbo: Nànwụledè na-eri ọkụkọ n'abalị.
examples.english: The genet eats chickens at night.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ nànwụledè n'ọhịa ụnyaahụ?
examples.english: Did you see a genet in the bush yesterday?

note: Rare word; examples are plausible.

gloss: mix; dilute; run together (of liquids and solids)

examples.igbo: O gbagwara mmanya ahụ na mmiri.
examples.english: He diluted that wine with water.

examples.igbo: Ị gbagwara ofe ahụ na mmiri?
examples.english: Did you dilute that soup with water?

examples.igbo: O ledara m akwa ya n'ahịa.
examples.english: He sold me his cloth cheaply at the market.

examples.igbo: Eledala akwa gị n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: Don't sell your cloth cheaply at the market today.

examples.igbo: O dụrụ bọl ahụ ọfọlò n'egwuregwu.
examples.english: He punted that ball in the match.

examples.igbo: Dụọ bọl ahụ ọfọlò n'ebe ahụ.
examples.english: Punt that ball over there.

examples.igbo: O ji ọnà mee mgbanaka.
examples.english: He used brass to make a ring.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara ọnà ma ọ bụ ọla edo?
examples.english: Did you buy brass or gold?

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ gbara àrụ nke ukwuu.
examples.english: That man is very stout.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ ọ gbara àrụ nke ukwuu?
examples.english: Is that child very stout?

examples.igbo: O tụfegara okwute ahụ n'ofe mmiri.
examples.english: He threw that stone across the water.

examples.igbo: Tụfega bọl ahụ n'ofe mmiri.
examples.english: Throw that ball across the water.

examples.igbo: Gwọ eriri ahụ tọgbọrọ n'ala.
examples.english: The coil of rope lay on the ground.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ gwọ eriri ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see the coil of rope?

examples.igbo: O nyere mgbanaka ya dị ka ibē.
examples.english: He gave his ring as a pledge.

examples.igbo: Nye ibē tupu ha ahapụ gị.
examples.english: Give a pledge before they release you.

examples.igbo: Ụlọ ahụ dọtịrị ruo n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: That house extends to the road.

examples.igbo: O dọtịrị aka ya n'elu tebụl?
examples.english: Did he extend his hand on the table?

examples.igbo: Bọọlụ ahụ dọlụrụ kìlìlì, ọ dị mfe ịgba.
examples.english: That ball is round, it is easy to kick.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ okwute dọlụrụ kìlìlì n'ụzọ?
examples.english: Did you see a round stone on the road?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akwụghalị n'ahịa kwa ụbọchị.
examples.english: He loiters lazily at the market every day.

examples.igbo: Ekwela kwụghalịa n'èzí, bata n'ụlọ.
examples.english: Don't loiter outside, come inside.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ nwere amù ibì, ha kpọgara ya ụlọ ọgwụ.
examples.english: The child has hydrocele, they took him to the hospital.

examples.igbo: Amù ibì na-egbu ya mgbu?
examples.english: Does the hydrocele pain him?

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ nwannē ārụ m, anyị na-ebi n'obodo.
examples.english: He is my close relative, we live in the town.

examples.igbo: Ị kpọrọ nwannē ārụ gị na oriri?
examples.english: Did you invite your close relative to the feast?

examples.igbo: Ọ gbara ọsọ jekwudoro anyị n'ụzọ.
examples.english: He ran and caught up with and overtook us on the road.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-ejekwudo ya ma ị gbaa ọsọ.
examples.english: You will catch up and overtake him if you run.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-ekwu àkùkù ọfụū n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: Children speak new slang at school.

examples.igbo: Gịnị bụ àkùkù ọfụū ha na-ekwu ugbu a?
examples.english: What is the new slang they are saying now?

examples.igbo: Anyị ga-aga ahịa nwanne echī.
examples.english: We will go to the market the day after tomorrow.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-abịa nwanne echī ka anyị hụ?
examples.english: Will you come the day after tomorrow so we can see?

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ nwere afọ ọ̀bara, anyị ga-aga ụlọ ọgwụ.
examples.english: The child has dysentery, we will go to the hospital.

examples.igbo: Ị riri ihe ruru unyi wee nwee afọ ọ̀bara?
examples.english: Did you eat dirty food and get dysentery?

examples.igbo: Mama na-akpa ahịhịa n'ubi maka ọgwụ.
examples.english: Mother is gathering herbs on the farm for medicine.

examples.igbo: Kpaa ahịhịa a, weta ya n'ụlọ.
examples.english: Gather these herbs and bring them home.

examples.igbo: Agadiì nwaànyì ahụ na-ere akwụkwọ n'ahịa.
examples.english: That old woman sells vegetables at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị maara agadiì nwaànyì bi n'akụkụ ụlọ anyị?
examples.english: Do you know the old woman living next to our house?

gloss: abnormally heavy, large and long breasts

examples.igbo: Nwanyị ahụ nwere ọgbòdògbò alā n'obi.
examples.english: That woman has abnormally heavy, long breasts on her chest.

examples.igbo: Ọgbòdògbò alā na-enye gị nsogbu mgbe ị na-azụ nwa?
examples.english: Do the abnormally heavy, long breasts give you trouble when you breastfeed?

examples.igbo: Kpopụta ọka ndị ahụ n'ime ahịhịa.
examples.english: Gather out those corns from the weeds.

examples.igbo: O kpopụtara ego ya niile n'akpa.
examples.english: He gathered out all his money from the bag.

gloss: myth [a literary figure of speech/thought involving supernatural beings or events]; idea/belief that is false

examples.igbo: Ǹkọmị̀rị̀kọ ahụ na-akọ banyere mmụọ na chi.
examples.english: That myth tells about spirits and gods.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ ǹkọmị̀rị̀kọ na mmadụ na-aghọ anụ ọhịa.
examples.english: It is a myth that a person turns into a wild animal.

examples.igbo: Ọ zofuru èzofù n'ime ụlọ nne ya.
examples.english: She hid away in her mother's house.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji zofu èzofù n'ime ọhịa?
examples.english: Why did you hide away in the forest?

examples.igbo: Eke mmīli na-egbu mmadụ n'osimiri.
examples.english: The water python kills people in the river.

examples.igbo: Ị hụla eke mmīli n'akụkụ mmiri?
examples.english: Have you seen a water python by the water?

gloss: share or administer widely or to several people; distribute;

examples.igbo: Kesàa ego ahụ n'etiti ndị obodo.
examples.english: Share that money among the villagers.

examples.igbo: O kesara ha ọka niile.
examples.english: He distributed all the corn to them.

examples.igbo: Kpupụ okpu gị tupu ị banye n'ụlọ.
examples.english: Take off your cap before you enter the house.

examples.igbo: Ị kpupụrụ okpu gị tupu ị banye?
examples.english: Did you take off your cap before entering?

examples.igbo: Kwukwàsịa okwu gị ka m nuo ya nke ọma.
examples.english: Say your speech again so I hear it well.

examples.igbo: O kwukwàsịrị okwu ahụ ugboro abụọ.
examples.english: He spoke that word again twice.

examples.igbo: Wụọ ahụ gị na mmiri ọkụ n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: Wash your body with warm water in the morning.

examples.igbo: Ị wụrụ ahụ gị nke ọma taa?
examples.english: Did you wash your body well today?

gloss: pull against one another; have a tug-of-war

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka ahụ na-adọ dọònịdō n'ụdọ n'ogige.
examples.english: Those children are having a tug-of-war with a rope in the field.

examples.igbo: Ndị otu abụọ ahụ dọrọ dọònịdō ruo ogologo oge.
examples.english: The two teams had a tug-of-war for a long time.

examples.igbo: Osisi dàchiri ụzọ, anyị agaghị aga.
examples.english: A tree fell across the road; we will not go.

examples.igbo: Gịnị dàchiri ụzọ mgbe anyị na-abịa?
examples.english: What fell across the road when we were coming?

examples.igbo: Mpịakọta achịcha a dị ụtọ.
examples.english: This bread roll is delicious.

examples.igbo: Ị zụrụ mpịakọta eriri ole n'ahịa?
examples.english: How many rolls of twine did you buy in the market?

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ kwara mkpukpu, ma o nwere obi ọma.
examples.english: That man is hunchbacked, but he is kind.

examples.igbo: Nwa gị ọ kwara mkpukpu?
examples.english: Is your child hunchbacked?

note: Inflection of -kwà mkpukpu is treated as stative; some speakers may prefer nwere mkpukpu.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ tùbìrì mkpịsị osisi.
examples.english: The child broke a twig.

examples.igbo: Atụbìla mkpụrụ ọka ahụ.
examples.english: Don't break that grain of corn.

examples.igbo: Ọ kpolụrụ ọsọ gaa n'ahịa.
examples.english: He rushed to the market.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji na-akpolụ ọsọ?
examples.english: Why are you rushing?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-eri nri n'ofè, ya mere o ji buru ibu.
examples.english: He eats food in excess, that is why he is fat.

examples.igbo: Emefula ego n'ofè.
examples.english: Don't spend money in excess.

examples.igbo: Ọ bìanyere aka n'ime mmiri.
examples.english: He dipped his hand into water.

examples.igbo: Bìanye mkpịsị aka gị n'ime oghere ahụ.
examples.english: Poke your finger into that hole.

examples.igbo: Ndị uwe ojii gabìgara ndị ohi n'ụzọ.
examples.english: The police intercepted the thieves on the road.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji gabìga m n'ọnụ ụzọ?
examples.english: Why did you intercept me at the doorway?

examples.igbo: Nne ya bekuru ya ka ọ laghachi ụlọ.
examples.english: His mother implored him to return home.

examples.igbo: M na-abeku gị, nyere m aka.
examples.english: I am imploring you, help me.

gloss: smile, laugh, chuckle, in a gentle way (as a sign of pleasure)

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ kpùmùlịrị amụ mgbe o hụrụ nne ya.
examples.english: The child smiled gently when he saw his mother.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji na-akpùmùlị amụ?
examples.english: Why are you smiling gently?

gloss: have or show great joy; rejoice

examples.igbo: Anyị nwere ṅụ̀rị n'obi maka nri ahụ.
examples.english: We have joy in our hearts because of that food.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere ṅụ̀rị maka akwụkwọ ọhụrụ a?
examples.english: Do you have joy for this new book?

examples.igbo: Anyị ruru ahịa n'oge tupu anyị ahụ ọtụtụ mmadụ.
examples.english: We reached the market in time before we saw many people.

examples.igbo: Ruo ebe ahụ ngwa ngwa, anyị na-abịa.
examples.english: Get there quickly, we are coming.

gloss: move over; remove (belongings to another house)

examples.igbo: Anyị kwafere ngwongwo anyị n'ụlọ ọhụrụ.
examples.english: We moved our belongings to a new house.

examples.igbo: Kwafee akpa gị n'ime ụlọ ozugbo.
examples.english: Move your bag into the house immediately.

gloss: run from husband to another man

examples.igbo: Nwanyị ahụ gbara nrịra hapụ di ya.
examples.english: That woman ran from her husband to another man.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-agba nrịra hapụ di gị?
examples.english: Will you run from your husband to another man?

gloss: unknown person; dummy; make-believe; creature of imagination; bogey-man

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-atụ egwu nwantan ta n'abalị.
examples.english: The children are afraid of the bogey-man at night.

examples.igbo: Nwantan ta abụghị mmadụ n'ezie, ọ bụ akụkọ.
examples.english: The bogey-man is not a real person, it is a story.

gloss: tear to pieces; torn to shreds

examples.igbo: Nkịta dọkasịrị uwe m n'ala ụlọ.
examples.english: The dog tore my clothes to shreds on the floor of the house.

examples.igbo: Onye dọkasịrị akwụkwọ m n'ụlọ akwụkwọ?
examples.english: Who tore my paper to shreds at school?

gloss: on the other side of the river

examples.igbo: Ụlọ ha dị n'ùfèsị mmīli, na nso ọhịa.
examples.english: Their house is on the other side of the river, near the forest.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-aga n'ùfèsị mmīli echi ka anyị hụ ya?
examples.english: Will you go to the other side of the river tomorrow so we can see it?

examples.igbo: Ọ zụtara ǹchụ ọhụrụ n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: He bought a new hat at the market today.

examples.igbo: Ǹchụ m dị n'ebe dị, ị hụghị ya?
examples.english: Where is my hat, have you not seen it?

gloss: step on sand(mud) as a process to use it for building

examples.igbo: Ndị ọrụ na-ezọ aja maka ịrụ ụlọ.
examples.english: The workers are treading mud to build a house.

examples.igbo: Zọọ aja ahụ nke ọma tupu anyị ewee ya.
examples.english: Tread that mud well before we use it.

examples.igbo: Onyeisi kpeziri esemokwu ha n'ụtụtụ taa.
examples.english: The chief settled their quarrel this morning.

examples.igbo: Kpezie okwu a tupu ọ kawaa.
examples.english: Settle this matter before it spreads.

examples.igbo: Ọkọwa okwu a na-enyere m aka ịmụ Igbo.
examples.english: This dictionary helps me learn Igbo.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere ọkọwa okwu Igbo ọzọ?
examples.english: Do you have another Igbo dictionary?

examples.igbo: Anyị nwere afụfụ n'ụzọ ahịa taa.
examples.english: We had trouble on the way to market today.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara afụfụ a n'ezinụlọ?
examples.english: What caused this trouble in the family?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-eri ihe niile ma e wezụga azụ.
examples.english: He eats everything except fish.

examples.igbo: Ma e wezụga gị, onye ọzọ bịara?
examples.english: Apart from you, who else came?

examples.igbo: Tudo akwụkwọ a na mgbidi.
examples.english: Stick this paper on the wall.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-atudo akwụkwọ ahụ na tebụl.
examples.english: You will stick that paper on the table.

examples.igbo: Ògbugbe nwa ọhụrụ na-atọ ọchị.
examples.english: The baby's crawling is funny.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ògbugbe agwọ n'ụzọ?
examples.english: Did you see the snake's crawling on the road?

note: Ògbugbe is a noun for crawling; the second sentence uses it in a possessive construction.

gloss: the larger python; African or Rock Python; (Python sebae)

examples.igbo: Eke ukwu hụrụ òké n'ubi.
examples.english: The large python saw a rat in the farm.

examples.igbo: Ì hụla eke ukwu n'ọhịa?
examples.english: Have you seen a large python in the forest?

examples.igbo: Nwa ọkụkọ ahụ nwere ǹtù dị nro.
examples.english: That chick has soft down.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere uwe ǹtù maka oyi?
examples.english: Do you have a down coat for the cold?

note: Ǹtù here means down/soft feathers; uwe ǹtù is a down coat.

gloss: salutation to one starting on a journey

examples.igbo: Jè si ikē, nwanne m.
examples.english: Farewell, my brother.

examples.igbo: Ha sịrị ya jè si ikē tupu ọ pụọ.
examples.english: They said farewell to him before he left.

gloss: the gag used for a dead person

examples.igbo: N'oge olili, e tinyere ngā àgbà n'ọnụ ya.
examples.english: During the burial, the gag used for a dead person was placed in his mouth.

examples.igbo: Ị maara ihe ngā àgbà bụ?
examples.english: Do you know what the gag used for a dead person is?

note: Rare cultural term; the meaning is from the entry, but I am not fully certain of its ordinary usage.

examples.igbo: Ala ahụ tela etela, anyị ga-akụ ya ji.
examples.english: That land is level, we will plant yam on it.

examples.igbo: Ụzọ a ọ tela etela ka anyị jee ọsọ?
examples.english: Is this road level so we can go fast?

note: The phrase tela etela is not common in everyday speech; examples are plausible but uncertain.

gloss: expire; run out; lose validity or come to an end

examples.igbo: Tiketi ụgbọala a gafere, ọ dịghịzi mma.
examples.english: This bus ticket has expired, it is no longer valid.

examples.igbo: Oge ọrụ anyị ọ gafere taa?
examples.english: Has our work time expired today?

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ jesoro nne ya n'ahịa.
examples.english: That child followed his mother to the market.

examples.igbo: Jeso m n'ụzọ a.
examples.english: Follow me on this road.

note: Jeso is less common than soro/eso in standard modern Igbo, but the inflected forms given are plausible.

examples.igbo: Mbacha ji juru na bọket.
examples.english: Yam peelings filled the bucket.

examples.igbo: Ewu na-eri mbacha ji?
examples.english: Do goats eat yam peelings?

examples.igbo: O nụchara okwu m nke ọma.
examples.english: He heard my words well.

examples.igbo: Nụcha ihe m na-ekwu!
examples.english: Hear well what I am saying!

gloss: traditional gymnastics of turning oneself around in the air; turn a somersault

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ kwụrụ ụgbà n'ala ahịhịa.
examples.english: That child somersaulted on the grass.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akwụ ụgbà ebe a?
examples.english: Do you somersault here?

examples.igbo: Mgbu obi na-agbu m kemgbe nne m nwụrụ.
examples.english: Heartache has been paining me since my mother died.

examples.igbo: Mgbu obi na-agbu gị?
examples.english: Does heartache pain you?

note: The phrase is idiomatic, but the exact force of gbu in this expression can vary.

examples.igbo: O dọgọrọ eriri ahụ, ọ gbagọrọ.
examples.english: He pulled the rope wrongly, it bent.

examples.igbo: Adọgọla osisi ahụ! Ọ ga-agbaji.
examples.english: Don't pull that stick wrongly! It will break.

examples.igbo: Mama na-esi nri kwa anyasị.
examples.english: Mother cooks every evening.

examples.igbo: Ị na-abịa ebe a kwa anyasị?
examples.english: Do you come here every evening?

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-egwuri egwu n'ikperé mmiri.
examples.english: Children are playing at the shore.

examples.igbo: Anyị ga-anọ n'ikperé mmiri ruo mgbede?
examples.english: Will we stay at the shore until evening?

gloss: hold to the ground (by lying across, as wrestler); pin down

examples.igbo: Onye mgba ahụ gbàdoro ibe ya n'ala.
examples.english: That wrestler pinned his opponent to the ground.

examples.igbo: Gbàdo ya n'ala ka ọ ghara ịgbapụ.
examples.english: Pin him to the ground so he won't run away.

examples.igbo: Gịnī mèlù n'ụlọ ahịa n'ụtụtụ taa?
examples.english: What happened at the market this morning?

examples.igbo: Gwa m gịnī mèlù n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: Tell me what happened at school.

examples.igbo: Ọ tụkpọrọ āsị̄ na mgbidi ụlọ ahụ.
examples.english: He lay against the wall of that house.

examples.igbo: Tụkpọ āsị̄ n'osisi, ọ dị mma.
examples.english: Lie against the tree, it is fine.

examples.igbo: Uwe mmiri lapadoro n'àrụ ya n'oge ozuzo.
examples.english: The wet clothes stuck to his body during the rain.

examples.igbo: Mmiri ozuzo na-alapado uwe n'àrụ mmadụ.
examples.english: Rain makes clothes stick to a person's body.

gloss: the first rain in the year

examples.igbo: Mmili ǹdà arò bịara n'ọnwa Maachị.
examples.english: The first rain of the year came in March.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ mmili ǹdà arò n'afọ a?
examples.english: Did you see the first rain of the year this year?

gloss: a doer; someone who does something; a performer

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ ezigbo òmeè ihe ọma.
examples.english: He is a good doer of good.

examples.igbo: Òmeè ihe nkiri ahụ bịara n'oge.
examples.english: That performer came on time.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akpa myigbu megide nwanne ya.
examples.english: He plots evil against his brother.

examples.igbo: Ị na-anụ myigbu ha na-ekwu banyere gị?
examples.english: Are you hearing the slander they speak about you?

examples.igbo: Anyị fàbàsịrị n'ime ụlọ ahụ n'oge mmiri ozuzo.
examples.english: We squeezed into that room during the rain.

examples.igbo: Fàbàsị uwe ndị a n'ime akpa.
examples.english: Stuff these clothes into the bag.

examples.igbo: Anyị tara mkpụlū jī n'ụtụtụ taa.
examples.english: We ate small yam this morning.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara mkpụlū jī n'ahịa ụnyaahụ?
examples.english: Did you buy small yam at the market yesterday?

examples.igbo: Nnà ochīè m na-akọ akụkọ ọdịnala.
examples.english: My maternal grandfather tells folk tales.

examples.igbo: Ndị nnà ochīè anyị lụrụ ọgụ maka ala anyị.
examples.english: Our ancestors fought for our land.

examples.igbo: Ọ riri nri, ọ rikwara ya ọzọ.
examples.english: He ate food, he ate it again.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-arikwa nri abalị?
examples.english: Will you eat dinner again?

gloss: path to the back of the compound or outskirts of town

examples.igbo: Ụzọ òwèlè na-aga n'azụ ụlọ.
examples.english: The back path leads behind the house.

examples.igbo: Ị maara ụzọ òwèlè nke ụlọ anyị?
examples.english: Do you know the back path of our house?

gloss: pack (sand, grains) together; collect grains or materials

examples.igbo: Ndị ọrụ na-akpokọ ájá n'ebe ahụ.
examples.english: The workers are packing sand there.

examples.igbo: Kpokọọ ọka ndị a tupu mmiri abịa.
examples.english: Pack these grains together before rain comes.

examples.igbo: Ọ zòrò m n'ibe n'ụlọ ikpe.
examples.english: He stood surety for me in court.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-ezò ya n'ibe?
examples.english: Will you stand surety for him?

gloss: go out for a stroll; go out to another house to stay and play with friends there (usually of children)

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka ahụ pụrụ òlịlī n'ụlọ enyi ha.
examples.english: The children went out to play at their friend's house.

examples.igbo: Pụọ òlịlī, ma laghachi tupu chi ejie.
examples.english: Go out to play, but return before nightfall.

examples.igbo: Ọ tụrụ ụgbụ jide nnụnụ.
examples.english: He set a clap net and caught a bird.

examples.igbo: Ụgbụ ahụ dọwara mgbe anyị na-achụ nnụnụ.
examples.english: The clap net tore while we were chasing birds.

examples.igbo: Ngwụcha arọ na-abịa, anyị na-akwadebe oriri.
examples.english: The end of year is coming, we prepare a feast.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-aga obodo n'ngwụcha arọ a?
examples.english: Will you travel home this end of year?

examples.igbo: Ọ bukwàsịrị akpa ahụ n'elu oche.
examples.english: He placed the bag on the chair.

examples.igbo: Bukwàsịa efere ndị a n'elu tebụl.
examples.english: Place these plates on the table.

examples.igbo: Osisi mango ahụ mìrì mkpụlū n'afọ a.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere o jiri kewapụ n'òtù ahụ?
examples.english: Why did he withdraw from that group?

examples.igbo: Sèka akwụkwọ ahụ ụzọ abụọ.
examples.english: Tear that paper in two.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-esèka akwa ochie ahụ.
examples.english: She is tearing the old cloth.

examples.igbo: O gbukasịrị nkụ ahụ n'obere iberibe.
examples.english: He cut that firewood into small pieces.

examples.igbo: Gbukasịa anụ ahụ tupu ị tinye ya n'ite.
