examples.english: Cut that meat into pieces before you put it in the pot.

examples.igbo: Ntụlụ dara n'ụlọ ha n'afọ a.
examples.english: Misfortune struck their house this year.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere ntụlụ n'oge ọrụ ahụ?
examples.english: Did you have hardship during that work?

examples.igbo: O kpọpụrụ mkpụrụ ahụ n'ime ala.
examples.english: He extracted that seed from the ground.

examples.igbo: Kpọpụ nkịta ahụ n'ime olulu.
examples.english: Extract that dog from the pit.

gloss: afternoon; middle of the day; heat of the day

examples.igbo: Efìfìè na-ekpo ọkụ taa.
examples.english: The afternoon is hot today.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-abịa n'efìfìè?
examples.english: Will you come in the afternoon?

examples.igbo: Anyị na-amị azụ n'oge anwụ.
examples.english: We dry fish in the sunny season.

examples.igbo: O mịrị azụ ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: She dried that fish well.

examples.igbo: Nwa ya akatara àrụ ugbu a.
examples.english: Her child is full-grown now.

examples.igbo: Nwa gị akatara àrụ ugbu a?
examples.english: Is your child full-grown now?

examples.igbo: O nwere onwe ya ugbu a.
examples.english: He is free now.

examples.igbo: Ndị ahụ nwere onwe ha mgbe agha biri.
examples.english: Those people were free when the war ended.

gloss: person bearing same name as oneself; namesake (compare ògbò)

examples.igbo: Agù m bi n'ụlọ dị n'akụkụ ahịa.
examples.english: My namesake lives in the house by the market.

examples.igbo: Ị bụ agù ya n'ụlọ akwụkwọ a?
examples.english: Are you his namesake in this school?

examples.igbo: Nwa ewu ahụ tara àhụ n'oge ọkọchị.
examples.english: That goat grew thin during the dry season.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ata àhụ — ị na-eri nri?
examples.english: You are growing thin — are you eating?

examples.igbo: Nwa ọhụrụ na-agbechìgha azụ n'ọnụ ụlọ.
examples.english: The baby is crawling back into the room.

examples.igbo: Gbechìgha ebe a, ka m tee gị ọgwụ.
examples.english: Crawl back here, so I can apply medicine to you.

examples.igbo: Simestà ọzọ ga-amalite n'ọnwa Ọktoba.
examples.english: Another semester will begin in October.

examples.igbo: Ị gụchara simestà a nke ọma?
examples.english: Did you finish this semester well?

examples.igbo: Ezi nà ụnò anyị niile na-eri nri ọnụ.
examples.english: Our whole household eats together.

examples.igbo: Onye bụ isi èzi nà ụnò gị?
examples.english: Who is the head of your household?

gloss: close; near; a short distance away; proximity

examples.igbo: Ụlọ akwụkwọ dị ǹso ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: The school is near our house.

examples.igbo: Bịa ǹso ka m hụ gị nke ọma.
examples.english: Come close so I can see you well.

examples.igbo: O tere mmanụ n'ahụ nwa ọhụrụ.
examples.english: She rubbed oil on the baby's body.

examples.igbo: Tee ọgwụ n'ọnya gị tupu ị lakpuo.
examples.english: Apply medicine to your wound before you sleep.

examples.igbo: O zuru ohi n'ụlọ ahịa.
examples.english: He stole in the shop.

examples.igbo: Ị zuru ohi ego m?
examples.english: Did you steal my money?

examples.igbo: Ndị mmadụ na-agbāsàpụ̀ n'ama.
examples.english: The people are spreading out in the square.

examples.igbo: Gbāsàpụ̀nụ uwe ndị ahụ n'ahịhịa.
examples.english: Spread out those clothes on the grass.

gloss: scratch, paw the ground (of fowls, dogs)

examples.igbo: Ọkụkọ na-abọ ànì n'azụ ụlọ.
examples.english: The hen is pawing the ground behind the house.

examples.igbo: Nkịta bọrọ ànì n'akụkụ ọnụ ụzọ.
examples.english: The dog pawed the ground near the door.

examples.igbo: Mmadụ ọbụna maara akụkọ ahụ.
examples.english: Everybody knows that story.

examples.igbo: Mmadụ ọbụna ọ maara ihe mere?
examples.english: Does everybody know what happened?

gloss: swing to and fro; be neutral

examples.igbo: Eriri ahụ na-akwụ efe n'ikuku.
examples.english: That rope is swinging to and fro in the air.

examples.igbo: N'okwu a, ọ kwụrụ efe.
examples.english: In this matter, he was neutral.

examples.igbo: Ọchịchị eze ahụ dị ike.
examples.english: The king's rule is strong.

examples.igbo: Ndị obodo chọrọ ọchịchị ọma.
examples.english: The townspeople want good rule.

examples.igbo: Òne mbòsì ka ị ga-aga ahịa?
examples.english: Which day will you go to market?

examples.igbo: Gwa m òne mbòsì ị ga-alọta.
examples.english: Tell me which day you will return.

gloss: support; hold up; stop from falling

examples.igbo: Kwàdò osisi a ka ọ ghara ịda.
examples.english: Support this tree so it does not fall.

examples.igbo: O kwadoro nne ya mgbe ọ na-eje ije.
examples.english: He supported his mother when she was walking.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akpata ego n'ahịa.
examples.english: He earns money at the market.

examples.igbo: Olee otu ị ga-esi kpata ego n'oge a?
examples.english: How will you make money at this time?

gloss: goodnight (this is used as a reply to kà chi fo)

examples.igbo: Kà chi bọọ, rahụ ụra nke ọma.
examples.english: Goodnight, sleep well.

examples.igbo: Mgbe ọ na-apụ, m sịrị ya, 'Kà chi bọọ.'
examples.english: When he was leaving, I said to him, 'Goodnight.'

examples.igbo: Kwa efifie, anyị na-eri nri.
examples.english: Every midday, we eat.

examples.igbo: Ị na-aga ahịa kwa efifie?
examples.english: Do you go to the market every midday?

examples.igbo: Mkpùdo ahụ kpuchiri ite ahụ.
examples.english: That covering covered the pot.

examples.igbo: Weta mkpùdo maka nri a.
examples.english: Bring a covering for this food.

gloss: hate; dislike Ịkpọ  mmadù ibe  ānyị asì bù n jọ Hatred towards our fellow-men is sin Akpòlù m yà asì I hate him, or I dislike him Chukwu Nnà, bikō zọpùta ānyị n’aka ndị niiìne nā-akpọ ānyị asì God the Father, please deliver us from the hands of all that hate us

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akpọ nwanne ya asị.
examples.english: He hates his sibling.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akpọ azụ asị?
examples.english: Do you hate fish?

gloss: give opportunity or chance; give time for something

examples.igbo: Nye m ohere ka m kwuo okwu.
examples.english: Give me a chance to speak.

examples.igbo: O nyere anyị ohere zuru ike.
examples.english: He gave us time to rest.

examples.igbo: Kwuo ezi okwu banyere ihe mere n'abalị ahụ.
examples.english: Tell the truth about what happened that night.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ekwu ezi okwu mgbe niile.
examples.english: She always speaks the truth.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-azụ ego ya site n'ire akwa.
examples.english: He builds up his capital by selling cloth.

examples.igbo: Zụọ ego gị tupu ị malite azụmahịa ọzọ.
examples.english: Build up your capital before you start another business.

examples.igbo: O nyere m sisì abụọ n'ahịa.
examples.english: He gave me two sixpences at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere sisì maka mgbanwe n'akpa gị?
examples.english: Do you have sixpence for change in your bag?

gloss: go for and bring back water; fetch water

examples.igbo: Nne m na-achu mmiri n'iyi kwa ụtụtụ.
examples.english: My mother fetches water from the stream every morning.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-achu mmiri taa maka anyị?
examples.english: Will you fetch water today for us?

gloss: remove the grains from the ear of maize

examples.igbo: Anyị na-akpọ ọkà n'ọdụ ụlọ taa.
examples.english: We are shelling maize behind the house today.

examples.igbo: Kpọọ ọkà a ngwa ngwa tupu chi echie.
examples.english: Shell this maize quickly before nightfall.

gloss: to speak while someone is speaking in order to make that person not to continue; to interrupt someone speaking

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akwuchi ọnụ m mgbe m na-ekwu okwu.
examples.english: He interrupts me when I am speaking.

examples.igbo: Kwụsị ịkwuchi ọnụ m mgbe m na-ekwu!
examples.english: Stop interrupting me when I am speaking!

examples.igbo: Ọtụtụ mmadụ bịara ahịa n'ụtụtụ taa.
examples.english: Many people came to the market this morning.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere ọtụtụ ego n'akpa gị?
examples.english: Do you have a lot of money in your bag?

examples.igbo: O gọnarị na ya maara ihe mere.
examples.english: He denied knowing what happened.

examples.igbo: Ị na-agọnarị na ị maara ya?
examples.english: Are you denying that you know him?

examples.igbo: Imewe uwe a masịrị m nke ukwuu.
examples.english: I like the design of this dress very much.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere imewe ọzọ maka uwe ahụ?
examples.english: Do you have another design for that dress?

examples.igbo: Nnụnụ na-efe n'elu osisi n'ogige anyị.
examples.english: A bird is flying above the tree in our compound.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ nnụnụ na-efe n'elu ụlọ?
examples.english: Did you see a bird flying over the house?

examples.igbo: Ehi ahụ zògburu ọkụkọ m n'ụlọ.
examples.english: That cow trod my chicken to death in the house.

examples.igbo: Ị zògburu ọkụkọ m n'ụzọ ụnyaahụ?
examples.english: Did you tread my chicken to death on the road yesterday?

examples.igbo: Onye ahụ na-eme ànwàǹsì n'ime ọhịa.
examples.english: That person practices wizardry in the forest.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eme ànwàǹsì? Biko kwụsị ya!
examples.english: Do you practice wizardry? Please stop it!

examples.igbo: Ọ kụrụ mmagba atọ na ụbọ.
examples.english: He played three chords on the guitar.

examples.igbo: Mmagba ndị a na-ada ụda ọma.
examples.english: These chords sound good.

gloss: become, render speechless; be dumbfounded Ife Àda mèlù nébe ànyị jèlù kpàlù m ọnụ  What Ada did where we went left me dumbfounded

examples.igbo: Ihe m hụrụ n'ahịa kpàlù m ọnụ.
examples.english: What I saw at the market left me dumbfounded.

examples.igbo: Ọ kpàlù gị ọnụ mgbe ị nụrụ ya?
examples.english: Did it leave you dumbfounded when you heard it?

examples.igbo: O nyere m ọkpùlùkpù anụ buru ibu.
examples.english: He gave me a big lump of meat.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eri ọkpùlùkpù anụ a?
examples.english: Will you eat this lump of meat?

gloss: kind of poisonous mushroom (literally spirits' mushroom) (see also mmụō)

examples.igbo: Elo mmụọ na-egbu mmadụ n'ọhịa.
examples.english: The spirits' mushroom kills people in the forest.

examples.igbo: Erila elo mmụọ; ọ na-egbu egbu.
examples.english: Don't eat the spirits' mushroom; it is poisonous.

examples.igbo: Biko zi m ụzọ̀ gaa ahịa.
examples.english: Please show me the way to the market.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-ezi m ụzọ̀?
examples.english: Will you show me the way?

examples.igbo: Mama na-ede akwà anyị n'ụlọ taa.
examples.english: Mother is ironing our clothes at home today.

examples.igbo: Biko de akwà m ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Please iron my clothes quickly.

examples.igbo: Anya mmīli na-agba m mgbe ọ na-apụ.
examples.english: Tears run from my eyes when he leaves.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere anya mmīli ji agba gị?
examples.english: Why are tears running from your eyes?

examples.igbo: O bèrè nni maka ụmụaka n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: She cut up food for the children in the morning.

examples.igbo: Bèe nni ahụ ngwa ngwa, ụmụaka agụọla agụụ.
examples.english: Cut up that food quickly, the children are hungry.

note: Tone on -bè and inflected form bèrè assumed from the headword.

examples.igbo: Anyị zèrè mmilī n'okpuru osisi ukwu.
examples.english: We sheltered from the rain under a big tree.

examples.igbo: Zèlụ mmilī n'ime ụlọ tupu mmiri ezoo.
examples.english: Shelter from the rain inside the house before it rains.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-atụkwàsa nnu n'elu anụ ahụ.
examples.english: She sprinkles salt on that meat.

examples.igbo: Biko tụkwàsà mmanụ n'elu osikapa.
examples.english: Please sprinkle oil on the rice.

note: Not fully certain of the verb's tone pattern in inflected forms; used straightforwardly in present and imperative.

examples.igbo: Bùù dị n'ụlọ akwụkwọ taa nke ukwuu.
examples.english: There is great quietness in the school today.

examples.igbo: Ọ dịghị bùù n'ụlọ ahụ ma ọlị.
examples.english: There is no quietness at all in that house.

note: bùù as a noun is rare; sentences are simple and idiomatic but the sense is narrow.

gloss: flesh; small piece of meat without bones

examples.igbo: O nyere m urùghùrù anụ ehi.
examples.english: She gave me a piece of beef flesh.

examples.igbo: Urùghùrù anụ ewu dị ụtọ nke ukwuu.
examples.english: Goat meat flesh is very tasty.

examples.igbo: O tinyere mbè aka nni n'ọnụ ya.
examples.english: She put a handful of food in her mouth.

examples.igbo: Mbè aka nni zuru m ezu.
examples.english: A handful of food was enough for me.

examples.igbo: Ọ̀kwaākwà na-akwa uwe ọhụrụ maka nwa agbọghọ.
examples.english: The tailor is sewing a new dress for a girl.

examples.igbo: Ọ̀kwaākwà, kwara m uwe ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Tailor, sew me a dress quickly.

examples.igbo: O kpùrù akwà n'ahụ nwa ya.
examples.english: She covered her child's body with cloth.

examples.igbo: Kpù akwà n'ahụ gị, oyi na-atụ.
examples.english: Cover your body with cloth, it is cold.

examples.igbo: Anyị kụrụ àgwà ọcha n'ubi anyị.
examples.english: We planted cowpea in our farm.

examples.igbo: Àgwà ọcha na-eto ngwa ngwa n'afọ a.
examples.english: Cowpea grows quickly this year.

gloss: chronic severe headache (= ọkìlị mgbawa īsi)

examples.igbo: Ọyà isī na-egbu m mgbu mgbe niile.
examples.english: Chronic headache constantly pains me.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ata ọyà isī kemgbe ole?
examples.english: How long have you been suffering chronic headache?

gloss: secret night society (using agụ ọgbà); Leopard Society

examples.igbo: Ògbà agū bụ òtù nzuzo nke ndị okenye na-ezukọ n'abalị.
examples.english: The Leopard Society is a secret society whose elders meet at night.

examples.igbo: Ị nụla ihe banyere Ògbà agū n'obodo unu?
examples.english: Have you heard anything about the Leopard Society in your town?

gloss: be agitated; swell (as river or sea in gale)

examples.igbo: Osimiri na-atụ èbìlì mgbe ifufe siri ike.
examples.english: The river swells when the wind is strong.

examples.igbo: Mmiri na-atụ èbìlì taa, ụmụaka agala n'osimiri.
examples.english: The water is agitated today; children should not go to the river.

examples.igbo: Nna m emeela okènyè, ọ na-eje ije nwayọọ.
examples.english: My father has become old; he walks slowly.

examples.igbo: Zuo ike, ị meela okènyè.
examples.english: Rest, you have become old.

note: Okènyè is rare; I used it in the sense of becoming old.

examples.igbo: Nye m nsansa mmiri ka m ṅụọ ọgwụ.
examples.english: Give me a little water so I can take medicine.

examples.igbo: Nsansa mmanụ fọdụrụ n'ite ahụ.
examples.english: A little oil is left in that pot.

examples.igbo: Echìchè ya na-agba gburugburu ụbọchị niile.
examples.english: His thoughts wander all day.

examples.igbo: Kedu echìchè gị banyere atụmatụ ahụ?
examples.english: What is your thought about that plan?

examples.igbo: Ọrịa àrụ mmīli na-eme ka ahụ mmadụ zaa.
examples.english: The disease dropsy makes a person's body swell.

examples.igbo: Dọkịta chọpụtara na ọ nwere àrụ mmīli n'ụkwụ ya.
examples.english: The doctor discovered that he has dropsy in his leg.

note: Medical term; I used the dropsy sense.

examples.igbo: Ahịa taa nwere òkpọ ọcha ọhụrụ.
examples.english: The market today has fresh òkpọ ọcha fish.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-azụta òkpọ ọcha ka anyị sie ofe?
examples.english: Will you buy òkpọ ọcha so we can cook soup?

examples.igbo: Nri dị mwèju akā, mmadụ niile ga-eri.
examples.english: There is enough food; everyone will eat.

examples.igbo: Mmiri ọ dị mwèju akā maka ndị ọbịa niile?
examples.english: Is there enough water for all the guests?

gloss: compete (in bad sense); be jealous, envious

examples.igbo: Ọ na-agba ekwòlò maka ihe ụmụnne ya nwere.
examples.english: He is envious of what his siblings have.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji agba ekwòlò maka ọganihu ya?
examples.english: Why are you jealous of his progress?

examples.igbo: Àrụ ūfụ na-akpali anyị ịla ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Urgency makes us leave quickly.

examples.igbo: Ọ dị àrụ ūfụ n'obi ya mgbe ọ nụrụ akụkọ ahụ.
examples.english: There was disquiet in his heart when he heard the news.

note: Rare term; I used the disquiet sense.

examples.igbo: Ọ fụkọ̀rọ akwụkwọ ahụ n'aka ya.
examples.english: He crumpled that paper in his hand.

examples.igbo: Efụkọ̀la akwụkwọ ọhụrụ a n'aka gị.
examples.english: Don't crumple this new paper in your hand.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-agba igwè gaa ọrụ kwa ụtụtụ.
examples.english: He rides a bicycle to work every morning.

examples.igbo: Gbaa igwè nwayọọ, e nwere ụmụaka n'ụzọ.
examples.english: Ride the bicycle slowly; there are children on the road.

gloss: pull together (e.g. branches which have been cut); compress; pack closely together

examples.igbo: O kpụkọ̀natara alaka ndị ahụ ọnụ.
examples.english: He pulled those branches together.

examples.igbo: Kpụkọ̀nata ahịhịa ndị a ọnụ n'ọhịa.
examples.english: Pack these grasses together in the field.

examples.igbo: Nwa bī be anyị na-aga akwụkwọ.
examples.english: The child living in our house goes to school.

examples.igbo: Nwa bī be gị ọ na-enyere gị aka?
examples.english: Does the child living in your house help you?

gloss: renew; renovate; restore or improve to a new and better condition

examples.igbo: O mere ụlọ ya ọhụrụ n'afọ a.
examples.english: He renovated his house this year.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eme ọhụrụ ụlọ akwụkwọ ahụ?
examples.english: Will you renovate that school?

gloss: roll away, off Òlòma naàbò àkpọlèpùgo Two oranges have rolled away

examples.igbo: Bọọlụ ahụ akpọlèpùgo n'ụzọ n'ebe ahụ.
examples.english: That ball rolled off into the road there.

examples.igbo: Kpọlèpù ya pụọ n'akụkụ ụzọ.
examples.english: Roll it away from the roadside.

examples.igbo: O kọwara inu ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: He interpreted that proverb well.

examples.igbo: Kọwaa inu a nye ụmụaka nta.
examples.english: Interpret this proverb for the little children.

examples.igbo: Ịrị elu osisi a bụ ekwēème.
examples.english: Climbing this tree is an impossibility.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ ekwēème ka anyị rụchaa ọrụ a taa?
examples.english: Is it an impossibility for us to finish this work today?

note: Rare noun; examples are constructed from the gloss.

examples.igbo: Ewù ya gbasara n'obodo niile.
examples.english: His fame spread throughout the whole town.

examples.igbo: Ị nụla ewù banyere oriri ahụ?
examples.english: Have you heard the rumour about that feast?

gloss: stretch out; spread out (as a bird its wings)

examples.igbo: Ụmụ nnụnụ gbasàpụrụ nku ha n'elu osisi.
examples.english: The birds spread their wings on the tree.

examples.igbo: Gbasàpụ aka gị ka m hụ ihe ọ na-ejide.
examples.english: Stretch out your hand so I can see what it is holding.

examples.igbo: Chebe ntì, ọ bụ nwanne gị na-akụ aka n'ọnụ ụzọ.
examples.english: Listen, it is your brother knocking at the door.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-echebe ntì mgbe nne ha na-akọ akụkọ.
examples.english: The children listen when their mother tells a story.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka ahụ mịrị ọmịmị n'osimiri.
examples.english: Those children dived deep in the river.

examples.igbo: Ị na-amị ọmịmị n'ime mmiri a?
examples.english: Do you dive deep in this water?

note: ịmị ọmịmị is the usual way of saying 'to dive into deep water'; the verb takes the prefix a- in the continuous.

gloss: an unpleasant smell like the one that comes from a dirty aquarium

examples.igbo: Aghọrị na-esi n'ime mmiri ahụ rụrụ arụ.
examples.english: A foul smell is coming from that dirty water.

examples.igbo: Gịnị na-esi aghọrị n'ime ụlọ a?
examples.english: What is smelling foul in this room?

note: The word is rare and regional; the sentences use isi aghọrị, the normal way of predicating this smell.

gloss: title; respectful form of address to men in general

examples.igbo: Ọmọdị, biko nyere m aka.
examples.english: Sir, please help me.

examples.igbo: N'obodo anyị, a na-akpọ ndị okenye òmòdì.
examples.english: In our town, elders are addressed as ọmọdị.

note: Used here in the respectful address sense; as a title it is also a name, e.g. Ọmọdị.

examples.igbo: Ọ nọ n'etiti ụmụaka ndị ọzọ.
examples.english: She is among the other children.

examples.igbo: Gịnị ka ị na-achọ n'etiti ahịa?
examples.english: What are you looking for in the middle of the market?

examples.igbo: Ife ndapụta a mere n'ahịa tụrụ mmadụ niile n'anya.
examples.english: This event that happened at the market surprised everybody.

examples.igbo: Gịnị bụ ife ndapụta kacha mkpa n'afọ a?
examples.english: What is the most important event of this year?

note: ife ndapụta is a dated/rare term for an occurrence; ife is the older form of ihe.

examples.igbo: Ọ jemịrị n'ime ọhịa tupu ọ laghachi.
examples.english: He went far into the forest before returning.

examples.igbo: Jemịa n'ime ubi ahụ, ka anyị hụ ihe dị n'ebe ahụ.
examples.english: Go far into that farm so we can see what is there.

note: The stem is uncommon; the inflections jemịrị (past) and jemịa (imperative) follow the regular pattern.

examples.igbo: Ọ kwụpụrụ n'ụgbọ ala ahụ na-aga.
examples.english: He jumped off the moving car.

examples.igbo: Kwụpụa n'ụgbọ ala ahụ ngwa ngwa!
examples.english: Jump off that car quickly!

gloss: be observant, watchful, careful; take notice of; watch (literally lay the eyes on the ground)

examples.igbo: Tọọ anya n'ala ka ị ghara ịda.
examples.english: Watch the ground so that you do not fall.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-atọ anya n'ala mgbe ọ na-eje ije.
examples.english: He is careful when he walks.

note: The idiom is transparent in its literal sense 'lay the eyes on the ground'.

examples.igbo: Anụ ahụ ya dị gwègèlègwègèlè mgbe ọ rịachara ọrịa.
examples.english: His body was flabby after his illness.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere anụ ahụ gị ji dị gwègèlègwègèlè?
examples.english: Why is your body so flabby?

note: Ideophone used with dị; the exact reduplicated form is local and I have not met it often in writing.

examples.igbo: Ụlù na-eto ngwa ngwa n'ala efu.
examples.english: The ụlù tree grows quickly on fallow land.

examples.igbo: Kụọ ụlù n'akụkụ ubi.
examples.english: Plant an ụlù tree beside the farm.

gloss: smack; hit or beat up someone or something

examples.igbo: Ọ na-eti ihe mgbe ụmụaka na-eme mkpọtụ.
examples.english: She hits when the children make noise.

examples.igbo: Akwụsịla ịti ihe!
examples.english: Stop hitting!

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ na-akwu èkwulèkwu.
examples.english: That man is talkative.

examples.igbo: Kwụsị ịkwu èkwulèkwu, mee ihe.
examples.english: Stop being talkative, do something.

examples.igbo: Gbaa òwu n'agịga.
examples.english: Thread the needle.

examples.igbo: Ọ gbara òwu ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: She threaded quickly.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akpa nsogbu n'ezinụlọ.
examples.english: He is causing trouble in the family.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akpa nsogbu?
examples.english: Are you causing trouble?

note: The meaning 'sense, cause' is ambiguous; examples illustrate 'cause'. The 'sense' sense is uncertain.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-agụ agụū.
examples.english: The children are hungry.

examples.igbo: Ị na-agụ agụū?
examples.english: Are you hungry?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-eje mgbelè n'ime ọhịa.
examples.english: He walks stealthily in the forest.

examples.igbo: Jiri mgbelè bịa ebe a.
examples.english: Come here stealthily.

examples.igbo: Chi ekùfoo, anyị ga-aga ọrụ.
examples.english: It is getting light, we will go to work.

examples.igbo: Olee mgbe chi ekùfoo?
examples.english: When will it get light?

examples.igbo: Ụdọ ahụ tụsịrị n'osisi.
examples.english: The rope got entangled in the tree.

examples.igbo: Atụsịla eriri ahụ!
examples.english: Don't entangle the thread!

examples.igbo: O rogharịrị osisi ahụ n'ubi ọzọ.
examples.english: He transplanted that tree to another farm.

examples.igbo: Rọghaa ya n'ebe ọzọ.
examples.english: Move it to another place.

gloss: tax; tax receipt, payment (literally head paper)

examples.igbo: Gọọmenti na-anakọta akwụkwọ isi n'aka ndị ahịa.
examples.english: The government collects tax from traders.

examples.igbo: Ị kwụrụ akwụkwọ isi gị n'afọ a?
examples.english: Did you pay your tax this year?

gloss: overdo things; do more than is expected

examples.igbo: Emefela nnu n'ofe ahụ, nri ga-emebi.
examples.english: Don't overdo the salt in that soup; the food will spoil.

examples.igbo: Ọ mefere n'ọrụ ụnyaahụ, ike gwụrụ ya.
examples.english: He overdid work yesterday and got tired.

gloss: press; apply pressure on, especially with the finger;

examples.igbo: Pịa bọtịnụ ahụ ka ọkụ gbanye.
examples.english: Press that button so the light comes on.

examples.igbo: O pịrị bọtịnụ, ma ọkụ abanyeghị.
examples.english: He pressed the button, but the light did not come on.

examples.igbo: Ụgbọala ahụ gabigara anyị n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: That car overtook us on the road.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-agabiga ha n'ọsọ echi?
examples.english: Will you overtake them in tomorrow's race?

gloss: to perform burial ceremony; keep funeral

examples.igbo: Ha kwara ozu nna m n'izu gara aga.
examples.english: They held my father's funeral last week.

examples.igbo: Olee ụbọchị ha ga-akwa ozu nne gị?
examples.english: What day will they hold your mother's funeral?

gloss: broom (considered as a whole bundle of prepared palm fronds)

examples.igbo: Zụta ùkwù azịza ka anyị zaa ụlọ.
examples.english: Buy a broom so we can sweep the house.

examples.igbo: Ùkwù azịza a adịghị mma ma ọlị.
examples.english: This broom is not good at all.

examples.igbo: Ụzọ idei ahụ jupụtara na mmiri ruru unyi.
examples.english: That gutter is full of dirty water.

examples.igbo: Gwuo ụzọ idei n'akụkụ ụlọ ahụ.
examples.english: Dig a gutter beside that house.

examples.igbo: Mmiri n'iyi ahụ dòrò èdò, anyị ṅụrụ ya.
examples.english: The water in that stream was clear, so we drank it.

examples.igbo: Olee ebe mmiri dòrò èdò dị?
examples.english: Where is clear water?

examples.igbo: Ụgbọ mmiri ha gafere oke òrìmìlì nnụ.
examples.english: Their ship crossed the ocean.

examples.igbo: Oke òrìmìlì nnụ dị omimi nke ukwuu.
examples.english: The ocean is very deep.

examples.igbo: Ákwà ahụ mịkọrọ mmiri niile dị n'ala.
examples.english: The cloth absorbed all the water on the floor.

examples.igbo: Osisi na-amịkọ mmiri n'ala mgbe ọ kpọrọ nkụ.
examples.english: The plant absorbs water from the soil when it is dry.

examples.igbo: Nwam̄bụ̄ ha bụ nwa nwanyị.
examples.english: Their first born is a girl.

examples.igbo: Nwam̄bụ̄ gị ọ nọ n'ụlọ?
examples.english: Is your first born at home?

note: Kept the tone marks as given; some speakers say 'ọkpara' for the same sense.

examples.igbo: Ejula gbefere n'elu akwụkwọ.
examples.english: A snail crawled over a leaf.

examples.igbo: Gbefe ebe ahụ, mmiri dị n'ala.
examples.english: Crawl past that spot, there is water on the ground.

examples.igbo: O doziri oche ndị ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: He arranged those chairs well.

examples.igbo: Dozie akwụkwọ gị tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Arrange your books before you leave.

examples.igbo: Òbìrìnajaọcha bụ ọrịa dị ize ndụ.
examples.english: AIDS is a dangerous disease.

examples.igbo: Ì maara ihe òbìrìnajaọcha bụ?
examples.english: Do you know what AIDS is?

examples.igbo: Mbọ aka ya toro ogologo.
examples.english: His fingernails are long.

examples.igbo: Kpachara anya, mbọ nwamba dị nkọ.
examples.english: Be careful, the cat's claws are sharp.

examples.igbo: Nne m kechiri ìchàfù isī ọhụrụ.
examples.english: My mother tied a new head-tie.

examples.igbo: Ònye zụtara gị ìchàfù isī a?
examples.english: Who bought you this head-tie?

examples.igbo: Triangle nwere akụkụ atọ.
examples.english: A triangle has three sides.

examples.igbo: See triangle ahụ dị n'akwụkwọ gị.
examples.english: Look at that triangle in your book.

note: The loanword 'triangle' is used in school maths; some speakers say 'ihe akụkụ atọ'.

examples.igbo: Ònwụnwụ nne ya wutere ezinụlọ ahụ niile.
examples.english: The dying of his mother pained the whole family.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-atụ anyị egwu ịhụ ònwụnwụ atụrụ ahụ.
examples.english: It frightens us to see the dying of that sheep.

examples.igbo: O jikere onwe ya maka njem ahụ.
examples.english: He prepared himself for that journey.

examples.igbo: Jikere ngwa ngwa, anyị na-apụ ugbu a.
examples.english: Get ready quickly, we are leaving now.

note: Wrote with the common inflected form 'jikere'; the stem is given as -jìkelụ.

examples.igbo: Ọ zụtara oru ìbùa ọkụkọ n'ahịa.
examples.english: He bought forty chickens at the market.

examples.igbo: Ì chọrọ oru ìbùa akwụkwọ?
examples.english: Do you want forty books?

note: The counting form 'oru ìbùa' for forty is not one I hear often; most speakers say 'afọ iri anọ' or 'ọgu abụọ'. Use with caution.

examples.igbo: Ndị njem si n'ùwà niīne bịara ahịa anyị.
examples.english: Travellers from all over the world came to our market.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ ka aha gị gbasaa n'ùwà niīne?
examples.english: Do you want your name to spread all over the world?

examples.igbo: Onye ọlū ahụ na-akwọ osisi n'ọhịa.
examples.english: That labourer is splitting wood in the bush.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akwụ onye ọlū ụgwọ taa?
examples.english: Are you paying the labourer today?

examples.igbo: O nyere onye uwe ojii ǹgàlì n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: He gave the policeman a bribe on the road.

examples.igbo: Ị na-enye ǹgàlì ka e were gị n'ọrụ?
examples.english: Are you giving a bribe so that they employ you?

examples.igbo: Ha na-akpọ ùbọ akwālà n'ememme.
examples.english: They play the pluriarc at festivals.

examples.igbo: Ị maara ịkpọ ùbọ akwālà?
examples.english: Do you know how to play the pluriarc?

note: The instrument is rare; the examples are plausible but not common in everyday speech.

gloss: knock òfọ on the ground (of a priest in giving judgement)

examples.igbo: Onye nchụàjà kụrụ òfọ n'ala.
examples.english: The priest knocked òfọ on the ground.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akụ òfọ mgbe ị na-ekpe ikpe?
examples.english: Do you knock òfọ when you are judging?

gloss: make something pass through the mouth into the stomach; swallow; ingest

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ loro ọgwụ ahụ ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: The child swallowed the medicine quickly.

examples.igbo: Loo mmiri tupu ị rie ji.
examples.english: Swallow water before you eat yam.

examples.igbo: Afele ōwịwa dị n'elu tebụl.
examples.english: The breakable dish is on the table.

examples.igbo: E zụla afele ōwịwa n'aka nwaaka.
examples.english: Don't buy a breakable dish for a child.

note: The headword is uncommon; I have used it as given.

gloss: nickname used only by the Igbo to describe the Yoruba

examples.igbo: Ndi Igbo na-akpọ ndị Yoruba ndi ōta ōjị.
examples.english: Igbo people call Yoruba people ndi ōta ōjị.

examples.igbo: Ị maara na ndi ōta ōjị bụ ndị Yoruba?
examples.english: Do you know that ndi ōta ōjị are Yoruba?

note: This is an ethnic nickname and may be considered offensive; use with caution.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ mùghere anya ya n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: The child opened his eyes in the morning.

examples.igbo: Mùghe anya gị nke ọma, ụzọ ahụ dị warara.
examples.english: Open your eyes well; the road is narrow.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka ìli nà ìse nọ n'ogige.
examples.english: Fifteen children are in the compound.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ìli nà ìse n'ime ha?
examples.english: Did you see fifteen among them?

examples.igbo: Nna m na-azọ osisi n'ubi taa.
examples.english: My father is transplanting trees on the farm today.

examples.igbo: Zọọ osisi ndị a n'akụkụ ụzọ.
examples.english: Transplant these trees by the path.

note: The verb zọ with osisi is used for planting or transplanting trees; phrasing is standard but regional use may vary.

examples.igbo: Ndọnì dị n'ihu nne m.
examples.english: There are wrinkles on my mother's face.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara ndọnì n'ihu gị?
examples.english: What caused the wrinkles on your face?

examples.igbo: O kwukpòrò mmejọ ya n'okwu.
examples.english: He covered up his fault with words.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akwukpò mmejọ gị?
examples.english: Are you covering up your fault?

note: This verb is less common; the examples follow the sense 'cover up with words'.

examples.igbo: Kpọwaa okwu a nke ọma.
examples.english: Pronounce this word clearly.

examples.igbo: O kpọwara aha ya n'olu dara ụda.
examples.english: He pronounced his name in a clear voice.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ kachiri ntị, ọ naghị ege nne ya ntị.
examples.english: That child is stubborn; he does not listen to his mother.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji kachie ntị?
examples.english: Why are you stubborn?

examples.igbo: Anyị na-aŋa ọgbàdụ n'ọkụ.
examples.english: We are roasting corn on the fire.

examples.igbo: Ŋaa ọgbàdụ ka anyị rie.
examples.english: Roast corn so we can eat.

note: The verb ŋa is used for roasting; the spelling and inflection are standard.

examples.igbo: Ịfùlụfū àgwà a dị ogologo.
examples.english: This bean pod is long.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ịfùlụfū àgwà n'osisi ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see bean pods on that plant?

note: The noun phrase is specific; the examples reflect common usage.

gloss: lay, offer, wager; make a bet

examples.igbo: O zọrọ ǹzọ̀ na bọọlụ.
examples.english: He placed a bet on football.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-ezọ ǹzọ̀?
examples.english: Will you place a bet?

gloss: heap of sand collected by flood after rainfall

examples.igbo: Aja idèì juru n'ụzọ.
examples.english: Flood-deposited sand filled the road.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ aja idèì n'ụzọ?
examples.english: Did you see the flood-deposited sand on the road?

note: This is a specific environmental term; usage may vary by area.

gloss: wade through the bush; walk through the bush; pass through a bush, especially one without a path

examples.igbo: Ha wara ọhịa ruo n'ụlọ ya.
examples.english: They walked through the bush to his house.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-awa ọhịa ahụ naanị gị?
examples.english: Will you walk through that bush alone?

note: The verb wa with ọhịa is used for passing through bush; the phrasing is idiomatic.

examples.igbo: Ọ dàkwepụrụ amụ mgbe ọ nụrụ akụkọ ọchị ahụ.
examples.english: She burst out laughing when she heard that funny story.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji dàkwepụ amụ otu a?
examples.english: Why did you burst out laughing like this?

examples.igbo: Ada nọ anya nne ya n'ọgbakọ taa.
examples.english: Ada represented her mother at the meeting today.

examples.igbo: Ònye nọ anya gị n'ụlọ akwụkwọ?
examples.english: Who represented you at school?

note: Phrase less common than -nọchite anya; used here in the given sense.

examples.igbo: Ọ sere square n'akwụkwọ ya.
examples.english: He drew a square in his book.

examples.igbo: Ụlọ ahụ bụ square ma ọ bụ okirikiri?
examples.english: Is that house a square or a circle?

note: English loanword used for 'square' as a shape.

examples.igbo: Ọmụ ahụ dị n'okpuru ugwu.
examples.english: That cave is under the hill.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ọmụ dị n'akụkụ osimiri?
examples.english: Did you see the cave by the river?

examples.igbo: Azụ ahụ na-azu isi ọjọọ.
examples.english: That fish stinks.

examples.igbo: Gịnị na-azu n'ime ụlọ ahụ?
examples.english: What is smelling in that room?

note: Used -zu in the stink sense; standard Igbo also uses -si isi.

gloss: small black millipede, usually seen on grass-thatched houses after rain

examples.igbo: Mkpaàkịlịka na-apụta n'ụlọ ahụ mgbe mmiri zọrọ.
examples.english: Millipedes appear on that house when it rains.

examples.igbo: Ị hụtụla mkpaàkịlịka n'elu ụlọ?
examples.english: Have you seen millipedes on the roof?

note: Rare word; examples kept to its specific millipede sense.

examples.igbo: Anyị nọkọbara ọnụ n'ụlọ nne m.
examples.english: We sat together in my mother's house.

examples.igbo: Unu nọkọbara ọnụ n'ahịa taa?
examples.english: Did you all gather together at the market today?

examples.igbo: Ite ahụ tiwara etiwa mgbe ọ dara.
examples.english: That pot broke when it fell.

examples.igbo: Kedu ihe tiwara etiwa n'ụlọ?
examples.english: What is broken in the house?

note: Resultative/reduplicated form used in the 'be broken' sense.

gloss: the period of time after the afternoon (usually from  4p.m. to about 7pm)

examples.igbo: Anyị na-eri nri mgbèdè.
examples.english: We eat in the evening.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-abịa n'ụlọ anyị mgbèdè?
examples.english: Will you come to our house in the evening?

examples.igbo: Onye nsògbu ahụ na-akpata nsogbu n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: That troublesome person causes trouble at school.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji bụrụ onye nsògbu otu a?
examples.english: Why are you such a troublesome person?

gloss: a  type of snack made from ripe or unripe plantain, or fried ripe plantains; plantain chips

examples.igbo: Mama zụtara kpekère na ahịa.
examples.english: Mother bought plantain chips at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eri kpekère ma ọ bụ achịcha?
examples.english: Will you eat plantain chips or bread?

examples.igbo: Ibè ya meriri ya n'ọsọ.
examples.english: His opponent defeated him in the race.

examples.igbo: Ị na-achọ ibè gị?
examples.english: Are you looking for your opponent?

examples.igbo: Anyị nọ n'ime mbala ēzi.
examples.english: We are inside the walled compound.

examples.igbo: Gbanye n'ime mbala ēzi.
examples.english: Enter into the walled compound.

note: The term 'mbala ēzi' is less common; example sentences are plausible but not widely attested.

gloss: take the wife of a dead relation

examples.igbo: O kùchiri nwunye nwanne ya.
examples.english: He took his brother's wife.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-akùchi nwunye nwanne gị?
examples.english: Will you take your brother's wife?

note: Past tense form 'kùchiri' is not fully certain; the cultural practice is specific.

examples.igbo: Mkpụlụ mmīli dara n'abalị ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: Hail fell last night.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ mkpụlụ mmīli ka ọ na-ada?
examples.english: Did you see the hail falling?

examples.igbo: O na-anwànye aka n'ọrụ ahụ.
examples.english: He is trying in that work.

examples.igbo: Nwànye aka n'ọrụ ahụ.
examples.english: Try in that work.

note: The imperative use of 'nwànye' is plausible but tone and usage may vary.

examples.igbo: Ehi ahụ na-atù atùtù.
examples.english: That cow is spotted.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ehi na-atù atùtù?
examples.english: Did you see a spotted cow?

note: The construction 'na-atù atùtù' is likely but not the only way to express being spotted.

examples.igbo: Mama tinyere ujìjì n'ofe.
examples.english: Mother added ujiji leaf to the soup.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-azụta ujìjì n'ahịa?
examples.english: Will you buy ujiji leaf at the market?

gloss: unbolt; open a lock that hinders liquid to flow (eg. a drink or tap).

examples.igbo: Kpọpe tap ahụ ka mmiri daa.
examples.english: Unbolt that tap so water can flow.

examples.igbo: Ị kpọpụrụ tap ahụ?
examples.english: Did you unbolt that tap?

note: Past tense form 'kpọpụrụ' is uncertain; the verb may have alternative inflections.

gloss: urge; force someone to do something against his wish

examples.igbo: Ha na-anu enu ya ka o mee ya.
examples.english: They are urging him to do it.

examples.igbo: Nu enu ya ka o mee ya.
examples.english: Urge him to do it.

note: The verb phrase 'nu enu' is used here as given, but its inflection and imperative may vary.

examples.igbo: Ndị nche atụlū na-eche atụlū ha n'ọhịa.
examples.english: The shepherds are guarding their sheep in the field.

examples.igbo: Ndị nche atụlū, kedu ebe unu na-edu atụlū ugbu a?
examples.english: Shepherds, where are you leading the sheep now?

examples.igbo: Nne nwunyè m na-abịa ile anya anyị n'izu na-abịa.
examples.english: My mother-in-law is coming to visit us next week.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akpọ nne nwunyè gị 'Mama'?
examples.english: Do you call your mother-in-law 'Mama'?

examples.igbo: Òkwùkwe Ndị Ozī na-ekwu banyere Jizọs Kraịst.
examples.english: The Apostles' Creed speaks about Jesus Christ.

examples.igbo: Kedu mgbe anyị na-agụ Òkwùkwe Ndị Ozī n'ụka?
examples.english: When do we recite the Apostles' Creed in church?

examples.igbo: Onye àfè ojiī kwụrụ n'ọnụ ụzọ ahịa.
examples.english: A policeman stood at the market entrance.

examples.igbo: Gwa onye àfè ojiī ihe merenụ.
examples.english: Tell the policeman what happened.

examples.igbo: Olòngōno nọ n'akwụkwọ osisi.
examples.english: A praying mantis is on the leaf.

examples.igbo: Ị na-atụ egwu olòngōno?
examples.english: Are you afraid of a praying mantis?

gloss: blow the nose (expel mucus from the nose)

examples.igbo: Zì imī gị tupu anyị apụ.
examples.english: Blow your nose before we leave.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ nwere ike ịzì imī ya n'onwe ya?
examples.english: Can that child blow his nose by himself?

examples.igbo: O yàtọrọ ụzọ ụlọ ahụ n'abalị.
examples.english: He forced the door of that house open at night.

examples.igbo: Yàtọọ ụzọ ahụ, anyị abanye.
examples.english: Force that door open, let us enter.

note: Inflection of -yà-tọ is uncertain.

examples.igbo: O gbòsàrà ndị na-alụ ọgụ.
examples.english: He parted the fighters.

examples.igbo: Gbòsàa ha tupu ha egbue onwe ha!
examples.english: Separate them before they kill each other!

note: Inflection of -gbòsà is uncertain.

examples.igbo: O dara nwa ya n'aka, ha abụọ gafere okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: She took her child by the hand, and the two crossed the road.

examples.igbo: Ị dara ya n'aka mgbe unu na-aga ahịa?
examples.english: Did you take her by the hand when you were going to the market?

examples.igbo: A mụrụ nwa nwoke, ha kpọrọ ya Òrànàǹche.
examples.english: A baby boy was born, and they named him Òrànàǹche.

examples.igbo: Ì maara ebe Òrànàǹche nọ ugbu a?
examples.english: Do you know where Òrànàǹche is right now?

examples.igbo: Ọ pụrụ òkò ịrụ ọrụ ahụ n'otu ụbọchị.
examples.english: He is able to do that work in one day.

examples.igbo: Ị pụghị òkò ibuli akpa a? Ọ dị arọ.
examples.english: Can't you lift this bag? It is heavy.

examples.igbo: Nŋòmi o mere nke nna ya mere ka anyị chịa ọchị.
examples.english: The imitation he did of his father made us laugh.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụghị egwu n'ezie, ọ bụ naanị nŋòmi.
examples.english: It is not a real dance; it is only an imitation.

note: The spelling nŋòmi is unusual; the common form is nṅomi.

examples.igbo: O ji ùnè akụ egwu n'oge owuwe ihe ubi.
examples.english: He plays the ùnè during the harvest.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere ike ịkụ ùnè?
examples.english: Can you play the ùnè?

examples.igbo: Onye nzinye ya bịara chọọ ego ya n'ụtụtụ taa.
examples.english: His creditor came looking for his money this morning.

examples.igbo: Onye nzinye gị ọ bịala ụlọ?
examples.english: Has your creditor come to the house?

gloss: pull down; let down from a height; lower

examples.igbo: O ji eriri na-aràdà ite ahụ n'elu osisi.
examples.english: He uses a rope to lower that pot from the tree.

examples.igbo: Ị pụrụ ịràdà akpa a n'elu ụlọ?
examples.english: Can you lower this bag from the top of the building?

examples.igbo: Ezinụlọ ahụ dara ogbènyà, ha enweghị ihe ha ga-eri.
examples.english: That family is very poor; they have nothing to eat.

examples.igbo: Ọ dara ogbènyà mana ọ naghị arịọ enyemaka.
examples.english: He is very poor, but he does not beg for help.

examples.igbo: O kwuru okwu alụ n'ihu ndị okenye.
examples.english: He spoke abominable words in front of the elders.

examples.igbo: Ekwula okwu alụ n'ụlọ a!
examples.english: Do not speak abominable words in this house!

examples.igbo: O gbasara akwà ya n'elu ahịhịa ka anyanwụ kpọọ ya nkụ.
examples.english: She spread her cloth on the grass so the sun would dry it.

examples.igbo: Gbasa akwà ahụ n'ala ka anyị nọdụ.
examples.english: Spread that cloth on the ground so we can sit.

examples.igbo: Àpàlị ùdò dị mma maka ịkpa nkata.
examples.english: The fibres of ùdò are good for weaving baskets.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eji àpàlị ùdò akpa nkata?
examples.english: Are you using fibres of ùdò to weave baskets?

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-egwu egwu n'ugbokō.
examples.english: Children are playing in the forest.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ugbokō dị n'azụ ụlọ ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see the thicket behind that house?

examples.igbo: Enwere m ife ōlulo n'ụkwụ.
examples.english: I have pain in my leg.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-enwe ife ōlulo mgbe ọ na-eje ije?
examples.english: Does she have pain when she walks?

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ dakpọrọ àrụ n'abalị.
examples.english: That child felt ill at night.

examples.igbo: Ị na-adakpọ àrụ mgbe ị na-eri nri?
examples.english: Do you feel ill when you eat?

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-atụ nwa ahụ ùlà.
examples.english: Children are teasing that child.

examples.igbo: Ị tụrụ ya ùlà, ọ̀ bụ?
examples.english: You teased him, right?

examples.igbo: Ehi ahụ na-ata afịfịa n'ala ahịhịa.
examples.english: That cow is eating grass in the field.

examples.igbo: Ehi gị ọ tara afịfịa taa?
examples.english: Did your cow eat grass today?

examples.igbo: Onye isi wara ọjị n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: The chief broke kola in the morning.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-awa ọjị taa?
examples.english: Will you break kola today?

examples.igbo: Onye àbọō bịara n'oge.
examples.english: Another person came early.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ onye àbọō n'ụlọ ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see another person in that house?

examples.igbo: Onye dibia gbūrụ nwa ahụ īchī.
examples.english: The native doctor cut ichi marks on that child.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-agbū īchī n'aka nwa gị?
examples.english: Will you cut ichi marks on your child's hand?

examples.igbo: Onye isi gwara okwu n'ọgbakọ.
examples.english: The chief addressed the meeting.

examples.igbo: Ị gwara ya okwu banyere ihe ahụ?
examples.english: Did you address him about that matter?

examples.igbo: Òkwụkwa nna ya dị n'izu a.
examples.english: His father's funeral is this week.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-aga òkwụkwa nwanne gị?
examples.english: Will you go to your sibling's funeral?

examples.igbo: Osisi mango a kpọrọ ìfulū n'afọ a.
examples.english: This mango tree blossomed this year.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere osisi ukwa na-akpọ ìfulū ugbu a?
examples.english: Why is the breadfruit tree blossoming now?

examples.igbo: Okwu ọ gwara kpaniri nne ya iwe.
examples.english: The words he said provoked his mother to anger.

examples.igbo: Ekwula okwu na-akpani nna gị iwe.
examples.english: Do not say words that provoke your father to anger.

gloss: Anything that serves as a legal tender; money

examples.igbo: Egō m nwere ezughị iji zụta osikapa.
examples.english: The money I have is not enough to buy rice.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere egō ị ga-eji zụta akwụkwọ?
examples.english: Do you have money you will use to buy books?

examples.igbo: Mkpasu iwe ya kpasuru ụmụaka ahụ iwe.
examples.english: His provocation angered those children.

examples.igbo: Mkpasu egwuregwu a na-enye ụmụaka obi ụtọ.
examples.english: The excitement of this game gives the children joy.

examples.igbo: Adaba m ruru unyi n'ụzọ ahụ.
examples.english: My shoes got dirty on that road.

examples.igbo: Zụtaara nwa gị adaba ọhụrụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: Buy your child new shoes at the market.

examples.igbo: Okwu ya kwakọrọ isi n'isi n'etiti ụmụnne.
examples.english: His words set the siblings at loggerheads.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akwakọ isi n'isi n'ezinụlọ anyị?
examples.english: Are you setting our family at loggerheads?

examples.igbo: M dọrọ ya aka na ntị banyere ụzọ ahụ.
examples.english: I warned him about that road.

examples.igbo: Dọọ nwa gị aka na ntị ka ọ ghara ịgba ọsọ.
examples.english: Warn your child not to run.

gloss: general name for fish of the Polypterus and Calamoichthys genera (compare òkwo)

examples.igbo: Igwe butere ùkata abụọ n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: Igwe brought two ukata fish to the market today.

examples.igbo: Ùkata a dị oke ọnụ n'ahịa taa?
examples.english: Is this ukata fish expensive at the market today?

note: I am fairly sure of the fish name, but the exact register of ùkata in everyday speech is less certain.

examples.igbo: Ọ gbara buùtù onyinye ahụ m nyere ya.
examples.english: He rejected the gift I gave him.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji gbaa buùtù ọrụ ahụ?
examples.english: Why did you turn down that job?

note: The phrase is understood, but gba buùtù is more colloquial than common in written Igbo.

examples.igbo: Nwa bùù dị mma karịa ọgba aghara.
examples.english: Quietness is better than confusion.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ nwa bùù ka i wee rahụ ụra?
examples.english: Do you want some quiet so you can sleep?

note: The sense of nwa bùù as quietness/ease is known, but it is not a very common everyday expression.

examples.igbo: Ewu ìkòm ahụ na-ata akwụkwọ n'ubi.
examples.english: That male goat is chewing leaves in the farm.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara ewu ìkòm ma ọ bụ nne ewu?
examples.english: Did you buy a male goat or a female goat?

examples.igbo: Onye ohi ahụ mịbara n'ime ụlọ n'abalị.
examples.english: That thief slipped into the house at night.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji mịba n'ime ụlọ n'abalị?
examples.english: Why did you slip into the house at night?

note: The verb stem is clear, but -mịba is less frequent than banye for entering a house.

examples.igbo: Eze nwere òka ìlòlò maara ihe.
examples.english: The king has a wise adviser.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-ajụ òka ìlòlò gị tupu i mee ihe?
examples.english: Will you ask your adviser before you act?

note: òka ìlòlò is understood as counsellor, though some speakers would simply say onye ndụmọdụ.

gloss: scoop water out of a vessel

examples.igbo: O ji efere kuru mmilī n'ite ahụ.
examples.english: She used a plate to scoop water out of that pot.

examples.igbo: Kuo mmilī n'ite ahụ were saa aka gị.
examples.english: Scoop water out of that pot and wash your hands.

note: The construction is sound; -ku mmilī is mostly heard in the compound form as used here.

gloss: fall out; result without being manipulated

examples.igbo: Ego ahụ dapụtara n'akpa ya.
examples.english: The money fell out of his bag.

examples.igbo: Gịnị dapụtara n'ime igbe ahụ?
examples.english: What fell out of that box?

examples.igbo: O ji aka ìkeǹgà ya jide m.
examples.english: He held me with his right hand.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eji aka ìkeǹgà eri nri?
examples.english: Do you eat with your right hand?

examples.igbo: Nna m siri ọnyà n'ubi ọka.
examples.english: My father set a trap in the corn farm.

examples.igbo: Sie ọnyà ebe òke na-agafe!
examples.english: Set a trap where the rats pass!

examples.igbo: Òbùbà ụlọ ahụ dị n'akụkụ aka nri.
examples.english: The entrance of that house is on the right side.

examples.igbo: Gbàa ọsọ gaa n'òbùbà ahịa.
examples.english: Run to the market entrance.

gloss: cause to enter or pierce something by or as if by pushing

examples.igbo: Sụ̀nye ntú ahụ n'ime bọọdụ.
examples.english: Insert that nail into the board.

examples.igbo: Ọ sụ̀nyere osisi n'ala ka ọ kwụ ọtọ.
examples.english: He pushed the stick into the ground so it stands upright.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-ege akụkụụwà n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: We listen to the news in the morning.

examples.igbo: Akụkụụwà taa kwuru banyere ahịa ọhụrụ.
examples.english: Today's news broadcast talked about a new market.

examples.igbo: Gụnye aha m n'ime ndepụta ahụ.
examples.english: Include my name in that list.

examples.igbo: Ọ gụnyere ụmụaka niile n'ọrụ ahụ.
examples.english: He included all the children in that work.

examples.igbo: Onye ōzizi ahụ kụziri anyị egwu ọhụrụ.
examples.english: That instructor taught us a new song.

examples.igbo: Nna m bụ onye ōzizi n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: My father is a teacher at school.

gloss: settle (in a place) Akwāgo m obì n’Enugwu#I’ve settled in Enugu

examples.igbo: Akwāgo m obì n'Enugwu.
examples.english: I have settled in Enugu.

examples.igbo: Ọ kwàra obì n'ime obodo anyị.
examples.english: He settled in our town.

examples.igbo: Ahụrụ m ya n'ọdù anyā m.
examples.english: I saw him from the corner of my eye.

examples.igbo: Gịnị ka ị na-ele n'ọdù anyā gị?
examples.english: What are you looking at from the corner of your eye?

examples.igbo: Nwatakịrị ahụ na-ebe akwa n'ihi agụụ.
examples.english: That child is crying because of hunger.

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ akwaghị akwa taa.
examples.english: That child did not cry today.

gloss: cause a scare; startle; cause the heart to skip a beat due to fear; take the breath away

examples.igbo: Ụda ahụ mapụ̀rụ m obì.
examples.english: That sound startled me.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka ihe mapụ̀ gị obì.
examples.english: Don't let something startle you.

examples.igbo: Sìkwa ofe a, ọ dị oyi.
examples.english: Warm this soup, it is cold.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-esìkwa ofe tupu anyị erie nri?
examples.english: Will you warm the soup before we eat?

note: The verb sìkwa is not very common in some dialects; sentences are idiomatic in Central Igbo.

gloss: for men born on Ǹkwọ, Èke, Oyè, and Àfò respectively, and Nwam̀gbankw̄ ọ, Nwam̀gbeēke, Nwam̀gbaàfò for women born on Ǹkwọ, Èke, and Àfò respectively. It is also used preceding the name of a deity, person, or set of circumstances, etc., after which a person is named: e.g. Nwudō (son of Udō, a deity); Nwọòrà (son of all); Nwoòlìsà (son of Òlìsà, God); Nwachukwu (son of God); Nwiijè (for a son born away from home)

examples.igbo: A mụrụ Nwooyè n'ụbọchị Oyè.
examples.english: Nwoye was born on Oye day.

examples.igbo: Ị ma na Nwooyè pụtara nwa a mụrụ n'ụbọchị Oyè?
examples.english: Do you know that Nwoye means a child born on Oye day?

note: Proper-name entry; examples show the naming context rather than ordinary word use.

gloss: raphia palm wine tapped from raphia palms at the river or stream bank

examples.igbo: Ha na-aba ose ngwò n'akụkụ osimiri.
examples.english: They tap raphia palm wine by the river.

examples.igbo: Ị ṅụrụ ose ngwò si n'akụkụ osimiri?
examples.english: Did you drink raphia palm wine from the riverbank?

examples.igbo: Nwatàkịlị ahụ na-ebe akwa n'ụlọ.
examples.english: That young child is crying in the house.

examples.igbo: Nye nwatàkịlị a mmiri ka ọ ṅụọ.
examples.english: Give this young child water to drink.

gloss: enlarge, extend house (by adding more rooms at either or both ends or sides);

examples.igbo: Ọ gbàkwụnyere ụnò ya ụlọ abụọ ọhụrụ.
examples.english: He extended his house with two new rooms.

examples.igbo: Gbàkwụnye ụnò gị tupu ụmụaka abịa.
examples.english: Extend your house before the children come.

note: The spelling ụnò is retained from the entry; ụlọ is more common in many areas.

examples.igbo: Ọ laghachiri àzụ n'ụlọ mgbe ọrụ gwụsịrị.
examples.english: He returned home after work ended.

examples.igbo: Laghachi àzụ ebe a, echefuru m ihe.
examples.english: Return here, I forgot something.

gloss: to have a conscious mind to some extent of reasoning, remembering experiences and making rational decisions; think

examples.igbo: Ọ na-achè echìchè tupu ọ zaa ajụjụ.
examples.english: He thinks before answering a question.

examples.igbo: Chè echìchè nke ọma tupu i mee mkpebi.
examples.english: Think well before you make a decision.

examples.igbo: Ọ lụrụ nwunye ya n'ụlọ ọgbakọ.
examples.english: He married his wife in church.

examples.igbo: Ha ga-alụ n'ọnwa na-abịa.
examples.english: They will marry next month.

examples.igbo: Ọ kpùrù enu ụnò ya n'afọ a.
examples.english: He roofed his house this year.

examples.igbo: Kpù enu ụnò ahụ tupu mmiri abịa.
examples.english: Roof that house before rain comes.

note: The spelling ụnò is retained from the entry; ụlọ is more common in many areas.

gloss: in order; one after the other

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka bịara n'ùsòlò n'ùsòlò.
examples.english: The children came one after the other.

examples.igbo: Gụọ aha ha n'ùsòlò n'ùsòlò.
examples.english: Read their names one after the other.

examples.igbo: Onye nkụzi kpụkọrọ ụmụaka n'otu ebe.
examples.english: The teacher led the children together in one place.

examples.igbo: Kpụkọọnụ atụrụ ndị ahụ, anyị ga-aga ahịa.
examples.english: Lead the sheep together, we are going to the market.

note: Inflection of -kpụkọ may vary by dialect.

examples.igbo: Eze yiri òkpu ezè ya n'ememe.
examples.english: The king wore his crown at the ceremony.

examples.igbo: Òkpu ezè a dị oke ọnụ?
examples.english: Is this crown very expensive?

examples.igbo: Ụgbọ mmiri na-aga n'oke òrìmìlì.
examples.english: The ship is going on the sea.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-egwu mmiri n'oke òrìmìlì?
examples.english: Will you swim in the sea?

examples.igbo: Nne m tinyere osikapa n'ụgbùgbà ọkū.
examples.english: My mother put rice in the cooking pot.

examples.igbo: Kpuchie ụgbùgbà ọkū ahụ ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Cover that cooking pot quickly.

examples.igbo: Ala ebe a pịtọ̀ nke ukwuu.
examples.english: This land is very swampy.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-aga n'ala pịtọ̀ ahụ?
examples.english: Will you go on that swampy land?

note: pịtọ̀ is uncommon; examples are simple and sense-specific.

examples.igbo: Ọ kwere omume ka m bịa echi.
examples.english: It is possible for me to come tomorrow.

examples.igbo: Ọ kwere omume na ọ ga-abịa taa?
examples.english: Is it possible that he will come today?

examples.igbo: Mmili òzùzò na-ezo nke ukwuu.
examples.english: Rain is falling heavily.

examples.igbo: Were nche anwụ gị, mmili òzùzò na-ezo.
examples.english: Take your umbrella, rain is falling.

examples.igbo: Nne m zụtara ùdò ọcha n'ahịa.
examples.english: My mother bought musk mallow in the market.

examples.igbo: Ùdò ọcha a na-eto n'ubi anyị.
examples.english: This musk mallow grows in our farm.

note: Botanical term; examples are simple but the plant name may vary regionally.

examples.igbo: Onye nchụ àjà na-ezù mọō n'ụlọ arụsị.
examples.english: The priest looks after deities in the shrine.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ezù mọō n'ụlọ arụsị?
examples.english: Do you look after deities in the shrine?

note: Obscure ritual expression; inflection and tone may need checking.

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ sonitara n'aka nne ya.
examples.english: That child grew up in her mother's care.

examples.igbo: Ị sonitara ebe a?
examples.english: Did you grow up here?

note: The sense and inflection of -sonita are uncertain to me.

examples.igbo: N'oge a, ụmụaka na-eji ekwentị akpọ oku.
examples.english: Nowadays, children use phones to make calls.

examples.igbo: N'oge a, ị ka na-akụ ọka n'aka?
examples.english: Nowadays, do you still plant corn by hand?

note: The phrase means 'nowadays/in modern times'; examples treat it as an adverbial expression.

examples.igbo: O wụrara ego ahụ n'etiti ụmụaka.
examples.english: He shared the money out among the children.

examples.igbo: Wụraa ego ahụ n'aka ụmụaka.
examples.english: Share the money out to the children.

note: The sense of spreading out and dividing is illustrated with money; a different object may be more idiomatic in some dialects.

examples.igbo: Enu ụnò ahụ na-egbuke egbuke n'ihi anwụ.
examples.english: The roof is shining because of the sun.

examples.igbo: Ònye ga-arụzi enu ụnò ahụ tupu mmiri abịa?
examples.english: Who will repair that roof before the rain comes?

note: The form ụnò is treated as a variant of ụlọ; standard modern Igbo often says elu ụlọ.

examples.igbo: Chụọ mmiri n'isi mmiri maka ofe.
examples.english: Fetch water from the stream for soup.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-achụ mmiri n'osimiri kwa ụtụtụ.
examples.english: She fetches water from the river every morning.

examples.igbo: Ime ụnò ahụ dị ọcha nke ukwuu.
examples.english: That room is very clean.

examples.igbo: Mechie ọnụ ụzọ ime ụnò ahụ.
examples.english: Close the door of that room.

note: The form ụnò is treated as a variant of ụlọ; standard modern Igbo often says ime ụlọ.

examples.igbo: O tụrụ ụkpolo n'ime osimiri n'oge egwuregwu.
examples.english: He threw a stone into the river during play.

examples.igbo: Atụla ụkpolo n'ebe ndị mmadụ nọ.
examples.english: Don't throw stones where people are.

note: Ùkpolo is rendered as ụkpolo; it can mean a thrown object or missile.

examples.igbo: O fochara ahịhịa n'ubi ahụ tupu ọkọchị.
examples.english: He cleared the weeds in that farm before the dry season.

examples.igbo: Fochaa ebe a tupu anyị akwụ akwa.
examples.english: Clear this place before we lay the bed.

gloss: reverse; changing of position (of something by somebody)

examples.igbo: Ndọgha ụgbọala ahụ n'azụ dị ize ndụ.
examples.english: Reversing that car is dangerous.

examples.igbo: Ndọgha ya na mberede mere ka ọ daa.
examples.english: His sudden change of position made him fall.

note: The noun sense is rendered as reversing or a sudden change of position.

examples.igbo: Nezia anya mgbe ị na-aga n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: Be careful when you go on the road.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-enezi anya mgbe ọ na-anya ụgbọala.
examples.english: He is cautious when he drives.

gloss: gather sand; play in and with the sand (of children)

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-akpo uzuzù n'azụ ụlọ.
examples.english: The children are playing in the sand behind the house.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ị na-akpo uzuzù n'anyanwụ?
examples.english: Why are you playing in the sand in the sun?

note: The verb -kpo uzuzù can mean gather sand or play in sand; the sentences show the playful sense.

examples.igbo: Elili aŋā a siri ike.
examples.english: This cane string is strong.

examples.igbo: O ji elili aŋā kee ọnụ nkata.
examples.english: He used cane string to tie the basket opening.

note: Elili aŋā is a specific kind of cane string; examples are simple but idiomatic.

examples.igbo: Ọ kpọkùrù m ka m bịa echi.
examples.english: He called upon me to come tomorrow.

examples.igbo: Kpọkù nwanne gị ka ọ bịa nyere anyị aka.
examples.english: Call your brother to come and help us.

note: The sense 'call upon/call to' is shown with a person as object.

examples.igbo: Ha kwụrụ ụ̀dọ̀ n'olu ya.
examples.english: They hanged him by the neck.

examples.igbo: E kwụrụ ụ̀dọ̀ n'elu osisi ahụ.
examples.english: A rope was hung on that tree.

note: The first sentence illustrates killing by hanging; the second illustrates hanging an object.

examples.igbo: Kpọtadu nwa gị tupu anyị erie nri.
examples.english: Bring your child first before we eat.

examples.igbo: Ọ kpọtaduru atụrụ ya n'ihu.
examples.english: He brought his sheep first to the front.

note: The word applies to bringing a person or animal first.

examples.igbo: Ọ nà-àgba mbìbì iji zụta nri.
examples.english: He is borrowing money to buy food.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ị na-àgba mbìbì ugbua?
examples.english: Why are you borrowing money now?

examples.igbo: Nkata a chiri anya nke ọma.
examples.english: This basket is well woven.

examples.igbo: Uwe a ọ chịrị anya n'úkwù?
examples.english: Is this dress tight at the waist?

note: The sense covers both well-woven and tight.

gloss: answer to a call, e.g. yes; a low murmuring or exclamation over tragic news or surprise

examples.igbo: Àa, a bịara m.
examples.english: Yes, I have come.

examples.igbo: Àa! Ihe ọjọọ mere n'ahịa.
examples.english: Ah! Something bad happened at the market.

examples.igbo: Ọ jụrụ ajùjụ gbasara ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: He asked a question about the school.

examples.igbo: Jụọ ajùjụ ma ị ghọtara ihe ahụ.
examples.english: Ask a question if you understand that thing.

examples.igbo: Ha kpochiri onùnù n'ụzọ.
examples.english: They filled the hole in the road.

examples.igbo: Kpochie onùnù ahụ tupu mmiri abịa.
examples.english: Fill that hole before the rain comes.

examples.igbo: Ọ zụtara ọnà ọkū n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: He bought brass in the market today.

examples.igbo: Ọnà ọkū ka e ji eme mgbanaka?
examples.english: Is brass what is used to make rings?

note: I am not fully certain 'ọnà ọkū' is the most common term for brass; 'ọla kọpa' may be more usual.

examples.igbo: Òtùtù ogologo tebụl a bụ mita abụọ.
examples.english: The measurement of the length of this table is two meters.

examples.igbo: Jiri òtùtù tụọ ogologo ala a.
examples.english: Use measurement to measure the length of this land.

examples.igbo: O kpọrọ ǹtu n'ime osisi ahụ.
examples.english: He nailed a nail into that wood.

examples.igbo: Kpọọ ǹtu ebe a ka ọ kwụsie ike.
examples.english: Nail here so it stands firm.

gloss: speak in metaphor or slang unintelligible to an outsider

examples.igbo: Ọ na-agwò ile mgbe ụmụaka nọ.
examples.english: He speaks in slang when children are around.

examples.igbo: Kwụsị ịgwo ile, kọọ ya nke ọma.
examples.english: Stop speaking in slang, tell it well.

note: The phrase 'gwò ile' is idiomatic but somewhat rare; I am fairly sure of the sense.

examples.igbo: O gwụrụ ọrụ ubi ahụ taa.
examples.english: He finished that farm work today.

examples.igbo: Gwụọ nri gị ngwa ngwa taa.
examples.english: Finish your food quickly today.

examples.igbo: Kpọchie mmilī ahụ tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Turn off that tap before you leave.

examples.igbo: O kpọchiri mmilī ma ọ dịghị mmadụ n'ụlọ.
examples.english: He turned off the tap when there was no one at home.

gloss: perform duties of a relation by marriage

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ gọrọ ọgò nke ọma.
examples.english: That man performed the in-law duties well.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-agò ọgò n'ụlọ nna gị?
examples.english: Will you perform in-law duties in your father's house?

gloss: hold at the breast; carry in the bosom

examples.igbo: Nne ahụ kùrù nwa ya n'obì.
examples.english: That mother held her child at the breast.

examples.igbo: Kùọ nwa ahụ n'obì ka ọ ṅụọ ara.
examples.english: Hold that child at the breast so she can suckle.

examples.igbo: Ọ yiri àfè ụlā ọhụrụ n'abalị a.
examples.english: She wore a new night-gown tonight.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara àfè ụlā maka nwanne gị?
examples.english: Did you buy a night-gown for your sister?

gloss: go backwards or back; lag; withdraw

examples.igbo: Ụgbọ ala ahụ lara azụ.
examples.english: That car went backwards.

examples.igbo: Laa azụ, ebe ahụ adịghị mma.
examples.english: Go back, that place is not good.

examples.igbo: O zụbìrì nwa ya.
examples.english: She trained her child badly.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ gị zụbìrị nwa ahụ?
examples.english: Was it you who spoiled that child?

examples.igbo: Nwa ya nwoke agbaala okorobịa.
examples.english: Her son has become an adolescent.

examples.igbo: Olee mgbe ọ ga-agba okorobịa?
examples.english: When will he become an adolescent?

gloss: a challenge to fight; a face-off; a head-to-head; duel

examples.igbo: Ha mere ikpọọgụ n'ihu ọha.
examples.english: They had a face-off in public.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ ikpọọgụ?
examples.english: Do you want a duel?

examples.igbo: O yilịrị uwe ọhụrụ.
examples.english: She wore a new dress.

examples.igbo: Yilị uwe ahụ ozugbo.
examples.english: Wear that dress immediately.

note: Unsure whether the inflected past form is 'yilịrị' or 'yiri'; used the stem's expected inflection.

examples.igbo: Onye afù bụ nwanne m.
examples.english: That person is my sibling.

examples.igbo: Ị ma onye afù?
examples.english: Do you know that person?

examples.igbo: O nyere ya nsị n'ime nri.
examples.english: She poisoned him in the food.

examples.igbo: Enyela onye ọ bụla nsị.
examples.english: Don't poison anyone.

examples.igbo: O nọdịrị n'ụlọ.
examples.english: He remained at home.

examples.igbo: Nọdịrị ebe ahụ ruo mgbe m ga-abịa.
examples.english: Remain there until I come.

examples.igbo: Ànyàlì ahụ na-acha ọcha.
examples.english: That albino is fair-skinned.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ànyàlì n'ụlọ ahịa?
examples.english: Did you see the albino at the market?

examples.igbo: O bulu osote n'isi gaa ahịa.
examples.english: She carried a pot on her head to the market.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ebulu akpa n'isi?
examples.english: Are you carrying a bag on your head?

note: The stem -bulu is less common than -bu/-buru; sentences are grammatical but a speaker might use -buru instead.

examples.igbo: Mgbịlịmgba na-ada n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: The bell is ringing at the school.

examples.igbo: Ị nụrụ mgbịlịmgba ahụ?
examples.english: Did you hear that bell?

gloss: herb, Aspilia africana (Pers. C.D. Adams), used to treat slight bruises or injuries

examples.igbo: O tinyere òla ǹjùnà n'ọnya ahụ.
examples.english: She applied òla ǹjùnà to that wound.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-achọ òla ǹjùnà n'ọhịa?
examples.english: Will you look for òla ǹjùnà in the bush?

examples.igbo: Ụlọ a bụ nke aka mkpà ya.
examples.english: This house is his very own.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere ego aka mkpà gị?
examples.english: Do you have your own money?

examples.igbo: O mụrụ ọkụ n'ọnụ ụlọ.
examples.english: She kindled light in the room.

examples.igbo: Mụọ ọkụ, ọchịchịrị dị.
examples.english: Kindle light, it is dark.

note: The common verb for lighting a lamp or fire is mụnye; mụ as a bare stem with ọkụ is less usual.

examples.igbo: Biko kwughepụ ite ahụ.
examples.english: Please uncover that pot.

examples.igbo: O kwughepụrụ akpa ahụ ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: He uncovered that bag quickly.

gloss: close or cover, especially a lid, cork, or cap

examples.igbo: Kwuchie ite ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: Close that pot well.

examples.igbo: O kwuchiri karama ahụ.
examples.english: He corked that bottle.

gloss: bushpig; Red River Hog (Choeropotamus porcus porcus L.)

examples.igbo: Ezì ọfīa na-ata ihe ubi anyị.
examples.english: A bushpig is eating our crops.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ezì ọfīa n'ọhịa?
examples.english: Did you see a bushpig in the bush?

gloss: move, crawl towards Ọ nà-àkpụkwu nwa nne  ya She is moving towards her sister

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-akpụkwu nne ya.
examples.english: That child is crawling towards its mother.

examples.igbo: Kpụkwuo m nso.
examples.english: Crawl towards me.

gloss: head of tobacco; bunch of prepared tobacco leaves (usually black tobacco) containing 5 leaves in one head

examples.igbo: Ọ zụtara isi anwūlù abụọ n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: He bought two heads of tobacco in the market today.

examples.igbo: Nye m isi anwūlù ahụ dị n'ime akpa.
examples.english: Give me that head of tobacco in the bag.

gloss: such a one, so and so (e.g. where a name is unknown); friend

examples.igbo: Di ānyị bịara ebe a ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: So-and-so came here yesterday.

examples.igbo: Ị maara di ānyị nke bi n'ụlọ ahụ?
examples.english: Do you know the so-and-so who lives in that house?

note: The 'friend' sense is uncertain; examples use the 'so-and-so' sense.

examples.igbo: Nkịta tara alụ n'aka nwata ahụ.
examples.english: The dog bit that child's hand.

examples.igbo: Atụla alụ na mkpịsị aka gị!
examples.english: Don't bite your finger!

examples.igbo: Oke nri ha rara ịra n'efere.
examples.english: Their food portions are equal on the plate.

examples.igbo: Ọ̀ rara ịra na nwanne ya n'ọsọ?
examples.english: Was he equal to his brother in the race?

gloss: grind to pulp; reduce by grinding

examples.igbo: Nne kwọzere ọkà ahụ n'ụzụ.
examples.english: Mother ground that corn to pulp in the mortar.

examples.igbo: Kwọzèe ọkà ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: Grind that corn to pulp well.

gloss: borrow (clothes, accessories, etc.) to wear to make a good impression

examples.igbo: Ọ nwutara uwe ọhụrụ iji mee mma n'oriri ahụ.
examples.english: She borrowed a new dress to look good at that party.

examples.igbo: Ị na-anwuta okpu ya mgbe ọ bụla ị na-apụ?
examples.english: Do you borrow his hat whenever you go out?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akwọ ọsọ n'ụzọ ahụ.
examples.english: He is rushing on that road.

examples.igbo: Akwọla ọsọ, anyị ga-erute n'oge.
examples.english: Don't rush, we will arrive in time.

examples.igbo: Ọnwụ nne ya bụ ife mwuta.
examples.english: The death of his mother is a painful thing.

examples.igbo: Kedu ife mwuta mere gị taa?
examples.english: What painful thing happened to you today?

gloss: walk on both hands and knees; walk on the knees; crawl

examples.igbo: Nwa ọhụrụ na-agbe igbē n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: The baby is crawling inside the house.

examples.igbo: Gbe igbē bịa ebe a, nwa m.
examples.english: Crawl and come here, my child.

gloss: prevent (aggravation); stop; staunch (blood); check or relieve, prevent (disease); protect

examples.igbo: Ọgwụ a na-agbò ọbara ọnya ahụ.
examples.english: This medicine stops the bleeding of that wound.

examples.igbo: Ị gbòrò ọrịa ahụ ka ọ ghara igbasa?
examples.english: Did you prevent that disease from spreading?

examples.igbo: Nne m na-ete ùli ede èji n'ahụ ya.
examples.english: My mother paints ùli ede èji on her body.

examples.igbo: Ùli ede èji dị iche na ùli ọzọ?
examples.english: Is ùli ede èji different from other ùli?

examples.igbo: M hụrụ ọfù na m na-ere akwụkwọ n'ahịa.
examples.english: I dreamt that I was selling books in the market.

examples.igbo: Kọọrọ m ọfù ahụ ị hụrụ n'abalị.
examples.english: Tell me that dream you had at night.

gloss: changing of state of things for worse

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ ife ōghụgha, ọ bụghị ọganihu.
examples.english: It is a change for the worse, not progress.

examples.igbo: Ife ōghụgha na-eme n'obodo anyị ugbu a.
examples.english: A worsening change is happening in our town now.

examples.igbo: Ọ mekatara ọrụ ahụ ruo afọ ise.
examples.english: He did that work for five years.

examples.igbo: Ị na-emekata ihe a kemgbe ole?
examples.english: How long have you been doing this?

gloss: be speechless; be unable to speak much, or to speak at all (not pathological, but psychological and/or emotional, disability) be dumbfounded

examples.igbo: Mgbe o nụrụ akụkọ ahụ, ọnụ ya akpàla.
examples.english: When he heard that news, he was speechless.

examples.igbo: Ọnụ gị akpàla, ị pụghị ikwu ihe?
examples.english: Are you speechless, unable to say anything?

gloss: board game with twelve holes, sometimes dug in the earth, played by two persons with nuts, seeds or small stones

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-egwu ǹchòlòkòtò n'okpuru osisi.
examples.english: Children play ǹchòlòkòtò under the tree.

examples.igbo: Ị maara otú e si egwu ǹchòlòkòtò?
examples.english: Do you know how to play ǹchòlòkòtò?

examples.igbo: Nna ya chịrị ìnyemè atọ.
examples.english: His father married three wives.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-achị ìnyemè ole?
examples.english: How many wives will you marry?

examples.igbo: Nna m na-eyi ùgègbè anyā mgbe ọ na-agụ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: My father wears glasses when he reads.

examples.igbo: Ùgègbè anyā m adịghị m, ị hụrụ ya?
examples.english: I don't have my glasses; have you seen them?

examples.igbo: O kwupụtara eziokwu n'ihu ọha.
examples.english: He spoke out the truth in public.

examples.igbo: Kwupụọ ihe dị gị n'obi.
examples.english: Speak out what is in your heart.

examples.igbo: Ọkụkọ anyị na-amụba nke ọma n'afọ a.
examples.english: Our fowls are multiplying well this year.

examples.igbo: Ewu gị ọ na-amụba?
examples.english: Are your goats multiplying?

examples.igbo: Ha chìrì àzụ mgbe ha hụrụ mmiri ozuzo.
examples.english: They turned back when they saw the rain.

examples.igbo: Chìa àzụ, ụzọ ahụ adịghị mma.
examples.english: Turn back, that road is not good.

examples.igbo: Ụmụnne ya gbara ya ọ̀gụ̀ n'ụlọ ikpe.
examples.english: His kinsmen fought for him in court.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-agba m ọ̀gụ̀ n'okwu a?
examples.english: Will you side with me in this matter?

examples.igbo: Nwanne m nwanyị dị èbelè.
examples.english: My sister is kind-hearted.

examples.igbo: Ọ dị èbelè n'ezie?
examples.english: Is he really kind-hearted?

gloss: break; snap (of objects with longer length and smaller width eg. sticks, trees, tubes).

examples.igbo: Ọ gbàjiri osisi ahụ n'aka abụọ.
examples.english: He snapped that stick with both hands.

examples.igbo: Gbàjie osisi a maka nkụ.
examples.english: Break this stick for firewood.

examples.igbo: Ọ zụtara akụ bèkeè atọ n'ahịa.
examples.english: She bought three coconuts at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ akụ oyìbo n'ahịa taa?
examples.english: Did you see coconuts at the market today?

gloss: rub the hands together in supplication

examples.igbo: O kwụkọrọ aka ya arịọ Chineke ebere.
examples.english: He rubbed his hands together asking God for mercy.

examples.igbo: Kwụkọọ aka gị rịọ ya mgbaghara.
examples.english: Rub your hands together and beg him for forgiveness.

note: The verb form is right, but I would phrase the first sentence with 'na-arịọ' in some contexts.

examples.igbo: Isi ọtiti na-egbu m.
examples.english: I have a headache.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara isi ọtiti a?
examples.english: What caused this headache?

gloss: kind of soup which is watery (sometimes with little or no oil); "pepper soup"

examples.igbo: Nne m siri ofe nsala taa.
examples.english: My mother cooked nsala soup today.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eri ofe nsala na ji?
examples.english: Will you eat nsala soup with yam?

examples.igbo: Ụzọ nke a na-aga ahịa dị warara.
examples.english: This path to the market is narrow.

examples.igbo: Soro ụzọ a, ọ ga-edu gị n'ụlọ.
examples.english: Follow this path, it will lead you home.

examples.igbo: Ndị obodo na-aga ụnọ mmọọ ịchụ àjà.
examples.english: The villagers go to the shrine to sacrifice.

examples.igbo: Ụnọ mmọọ ahụ dị n'akụkụ ụzọ?
examples.english: Is that shrine by the road?

note: Obscure term; used headword spelling.

examples.igbo: Dọkịta kwuru na nwa ahụ nwere ịbà ukwù anyā.
examples.english: The doctor said the child has hepatitis.

examples.igbo: Ịbà ukwù anyā ọ na-egbu mmadụ?
examples.english: Does hepatitis kill people?

gloss: step over somebody's outstretched legs; step over

examples.igbo: Biko ṅe òfì m ka m gafee.
examples.english: Please step over my legs so I can pass.

examples.igbo: Ọ ṅere òfì nwanne ya n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: He stepped over his brother's legs in the morning.

note: Normalized the stem to standard ṅ.

examples.igbo: Chegharịa ihe i kwuru banyere ya.
examples.english: Rethink what you said about it.

examples.igbo: Ọ chègharịrị mkpebi ya mgbe ọ nụrụ okwu ahụ.
examples.english: He reconsidered his decision when he heard that news.

examples.igbo: Ògbu mīli na-ebu ụgbọ mmiri ndị ahịa.
examples.english: The sea carries traders' ships.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-agwu mmiri n'ògbu mīli taa?
examples.english: Will you swim in the deep water today?

note: Used headword mīli.

examples.igbo: Ndị ùlà na-aghọgbu ndị mmadụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: Deceivers deceive people in the market.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka ndị ùlà ghọgbuo gị.
examples.english: Don't let deceivers deceive you.

gloss: female palace dwarf associated with Ezē Ǹrì

examples.igbo: Àda Ǹrì bụ obere mmụọ nke ụlọ eze.
examples.english: Ada Nri is a small spirit of the palace.

examples.igbo: Ndị Nri na-akọ akụkọ banyere àda Ǹrì.
examples.english: Nri people tell stories about Ada Nri.

note: Obscure cultural term; examples are generic.

gloss: contain breast milk; have flow of milk from the breast

examples.igbo: Nwanyị ahụ na-agba mmili alā ugbu a.
examples.english: That woman is producing breast milk now.

examples.igbo: Ọ gbara mmili alā mgbe ọ mụrụ nwa.
examples.english: She produced breast milk after giving birth.

note: Used headword mmili alā.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-agba akụ n'afọ a.
examples.english: That child is growing pubic hair this year.

examples.igbo: Nwanne ya nwoke gbara akụ tupu ya.
examples.english: Her brother grew pubic hair before her.

examples.igbo: Afọ ọchịchị jidere ya, ya mere ọ nọghị n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: Diarrhoea caught him, so he was not at school.

examples.igbo: Gaa ụlọ ọgwụ ozugbo ma afọ ọchịchị jide gị.
examples.english: Go to the hospital at once if diarrhoea catches you.

gloss: rinse; fade; change color to a faint one

examples.igbo: ṅàcha ọnụ gị tupu ị lakpuo ụra.
examples.english: Rinse your mouth before you go to sleep.

examples.igbo: Ì ṅàchara ọnụ gị mgbe ị risịrị nri?
examples.english: Did you rinse your mouth after eating?

examples.igbo: Ọzaraọnụ ahụ kwuru na ya emeghị ihe ahụ.
examples.english: The defendant said he did not do it.

examples.igbo: Ònye bụ ọzaraọnụ n'okwu ikpe a?
examples.english: Who is the defendant in this case?

gloss: flow; float; drift to and fro, of a kite hovering in the sky

examples.igbo: Akwa ahụ na-ahùgharị n'elu mmiri ọdọ mmiri.
examples.english: The cloth is floating on the pond water.

examples.igbo: Ifufe fere, akwụkwọ ahụ wee hùgharị n'elu mmiri.
examples.english: The wind blew, and the leaf drifted on the water.

examples.igbo: Ewu na-ata nni n'ala ahịhịa.
examples.english: The goat grazes on the grassy field.

examples.igbo: Kpụrụ ehi ndị ahụ gaa ebe ha ga-ata nni.
examples.english: Take the cows to where they will graze.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-amụ banyere ùwà anụmànù n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
