examples.english: The children learn about the animal world at school.

examples.igbo: Ùwà anụmànù jupụtara n'ọhịa na n'osimiri.
examples.english: The animal world is full in the bush and in the river.

examples.igbo: Ụnò ị dị nnukwu ma dịkwa mma.
examples.english: Your house is big and also beautiful.

examples.igbo: Ebee ka ụnò ị dị?
examples.english: Where is your house?

gloss: regret; be sorry for something done by self

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akwa ụtā maka ihe o mere ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: He regrets what he did yesterday.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akwa ụtā maka okwu ahụ ị kwuru?
examples.english: Do you regret what you said?

examples.igbo: Ọ dara n'ala chìfịa àrụ ikpere ya.
examples.english: He fell and abraded the skin of his knee.

examples.igbo: Kpachara anya ka ị ghara ichìfịa àrụ aka gị.
examples.english: Be careful so that you do not abrade the skin of your hand.

gloss: freshwater flying fish (Pantodon buchholzi) (= òjì n kù)

examples.igbo: Onye ọkụ azụ jidere nwaànyì akpù obì n'osimiri anyị.
examples.english: A fisherman caught a freshwater flying fish in our river.

examples.igbo: Ị hụtụla nwaànyì akpù obì n'ahịa azụ a?
examples.english: Have you ever seen a freshwater flying fish in this fish market?

note: The fish name is rare and local; the sentences are grammatical but I am not fully certain of everyday usage.

gloss: the fourth day of the week; Wednesday

examples.igbo: Wenezde ka anyị na-aga ahịa.
examples.english: It is on Wednesday that we go to the market.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-abịa n'ụlọ anyị Wenezde?
examples.english: Will you come to our house on Wednesday?

gloss: to birth a child; give birth; put to bed; deliver a b

examples.igbo: Nwunye ya mụrụ nwa n'ụlọ ọgwụ.
examples.english: His wife gave birth to a child in the hospital.

examples.igbo: Ị mụrụ nwa n'ụlọ ọgwụ ma ọ bụ n'ụlọ?
examples.english: Did you give birth in the hospital or at home?

examples.igbo: Okokpòlò ahụ ka na-ebi n'ụlọ nne ya.
examples.english: That bachelor still lives in his mother's house.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere okokpòlò ahụ ji alụbeghị nwunye?
examples.english: Why has that bachelor not married a wife?

gloss: medicinal plant, also used for stew

examples.igbo: Anyị ji àlụlù sie ofe taa.
examples.english: We used àlụlù to cook the soup today.

examples.igbo: Ị maara ebe àlụlù na-eto?
examples.english: Do you know where àlụlù grows?

note: Plant name is local; sentences are idiomatic but the exact plant may vary by area.

examples.igbo: Onye dibịa butere àkpà afā ya.
examples.english: The diviner carried his diviner's bag.

examples.igbo: Gịnị dị n'ime àkpà afā a?
examples.english: What is inside this diviner's bag?

examples.igbo: Gbujira osisi a abụọ.
examples.english: Cut this stick into two.

examples.igbo: O ji mma gbujiri anụ ahụ abụọ.
examples.english: He cut the meat into two with a knife.

note: The stem is rare; the inflected forms gbujira/gbujiri are my best reconstruction.

examples.igbo: O gọnarị na ya maara ebe ego ahụ dị.
examples.english: He denied knowing where the money was.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji agọnarị na ị maara ya?
examples.english: Why do you deny knowing him?

note: Sense is clear, but the verb is uncommon and its inflections may vary.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka ahụ lụrụ ụla n'ehihie.
examples.english: The children slept in the afternoon.

examples.igbo: Lụọ ụla, echi ka anyị ga-aga ọrụ.
examples.english: Sleep now, we will go to work tomorrow.

note: The expression is understood but the usual everyday verb for sleep is ịra ọhụ/ụra in many areas.

examples.igbo: Ha ji ewu chụọ àjà n'ụlọ arụsị.
examples.english: They used a goat to offer sacrifice at the shrine.

examples.igbo: Olee mgbe ha ga-achụ àjà ọzọ?
examples.english: When will they offer sacrifice again?

examples.igbo: M na-eteghalị ofe ka ọ ghara ịracha.
examples.english: I am stirring the soup so it does not burn.

examples.igbo: Teghalị ofe ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: Stir that soup well.

examples.igbo: Anyị nwere àrụ ōfufo ugbu a.
examples.english: We have peace of mind now.

examples.igbo: Nne ya na-achọ àrụ ōfufo maka ụmụ ya.
examples.english: His mother seeks security for her children.

examples.igbo: Tụjụ ofe ahụ ntakịrị mmiri.
examples.english: Dilute that soup with a little water.

examples.igbo: Ọ tụjụ ọgwụ ahụ tupu ọ ṅụọ ya.
examples.english: She diluted the medicine before taking it.

examples.igbo: Elu igwe na-acha anụnụ anụnụ taa.
examples.english: The sky is blue today.

examples.igbo: Ọ zụtara uwe na-acha anụnụ anụnụ.
examples.english: She bought a blue dress.

gloss: plant a live stick, slip or cutting

examples.igbo: Maa osisi a n'ala ebe a.
examples.english: Plant this cutting here in the ground.

examples.igbo: Oge ọkọchị adịghị mma maka ịma osisi.
examples.english: The dry season is not good for planting cuttings.

examples.igbo: Nne ochīè m na-akọ akụkọ mgbede.
examples.english: My maternal grandmother tells evening stories.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eleta nne ochīè gị n'oge ezumike?
examples.english: Will you visit your maternal grandmother during the holiday?

examples.igbo: Kpọchie mmiliì ahụ tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Turn off that tap before you leave.

examples.igbo: Ọ kpọchiri mmiliì ma gaa ahịa.
examples.english: She turned off the tap and went to the market.

examples.igbo: Anyị nọdụrụ na mkpìlìsì osisi ahụ.
examples.english: We sat on that tree stump.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ mkpìlìsì osisi n'ụzọ?
examples.english: Did you see the tree stump on the road?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-aghe ugherē n'oge nkuzi.
examples.english: He yawns during the lesson.

examples.igbo: Ị na-aghe ugherē n'ihi na ụra anaghị ezu gị?
examples.english: Are you yawning because you don't get enough sleep?

examples.igbo: Nnụnụ ahụ feliri elu n'elu osisi.
examples.english: That bird flew up onto the tree.

examples.igbo: Feli elu ebe ahụ ka m hụ gị.
examples.english: Fly up there so I can see you.

examples.igbo: Anyị jidere òkwo igwè abụọ n'osimiri.
examples.english: We caught two Polypterus fish in the river.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-ere òkwo igwè a n'ahịa?
examples.english: Will you sell this Polypterus fish at the market?

gloss: Arụsị of the first market day of the Igbo week, associated with east and the element of fire

examples.igbo: Ndị obodo na-efe Èke tupu ha ebido ahịa.
examples.english: The people of the town worship Èke before they start the market.

examples.igbo: Ụbọchị Èke bụ ụbọchị ahịa mbụ n'izu.
examples.english: Èke day is the first market day of the week.

examples.igbo: Ùwà m, ùwà ìsatọ! Gịnị ka m ga-eme ugbu a?
examples.english: Oh my, what a disaster! What am I to do now?

examples.igbo: O tiri mkpu, sị, ùwà m ùwà ìsatọ.
examples.english: She screamed and said, oh my, what a disaster.

examples.igbo: Onye ọzụzụ ịnyịnya pịara ịnyịnya ahụ ụ̀tàrị̀.
examples.english: The horse trainer whipped that horse with a whip.

examples.igbo: Ònye pịara gị ụ̀tàrị̀ n'azụ?
examples.english: Who whipped you on the back?

examples.igbo: O nyere m naanị ịfùlịfū achịcha.
examples.english: She gave me only a scrap of bread.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-enye m ịfùlịfū anụ ahụ?
examples.english: Will you give me a morsel of that meat?

examples.igbo: Ọ bịaghị, yabụ̀ anyị gara n'ihu.
examples.english: He did not come, therefore we went ahead.

examples.igbo: Yabụ̀, ihe ị na-ekwu bụ na ọ ga-abịa echi?
examples.english: So, what you are saying is that he will come tomorrow?

examples.igbo: O rekọbara akwa ahụ tinye ya n'akpa.
examples.english: She rolled up that cloth and put it in the bag.

examples.igbo: Rekọba eriri ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: Roll up that rope well.

examples.igbo: Okpulukpu mbe siri ike nke ukwuu.
examples.english: The tortoise's shell is very hard.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ okpulukpu mbe n'ọhịa?
examples.english: Did you see a tortoise shell in the bush?

examples.igbo: Anyị na-amị azụ n'ọkụ n'oge ọkọchị.
examples.english: We dry fish over the fire in the dry season.

examples.igbo: Mịa ọkà ahụ n'ọkụ ruo echi.
examples.english: Dry that corn over the fire until tomorrow.

examples.igbo: Nne m na-ede akwà n'ụtụtụ ọ bụla.
examples.english: My mother irons clothes every morning.

examples.igbo: De akwà uwe m tupu anyị apụọ.
examples.english: Iron my clothes before we leave.

gloss: noise as of a steamboat; puffing

examples.igbo: Anụrụ m nsụkpe ụgbọ mmiri n'akụkụ osimiri.
examples.english: I heard the puffing of a steamboat by the riverside.

examples.igbo: Gịnị na-eme nsụkpe ahụ n'ime mmiri?
examples.english: What is making that puffing noise in the water?

note: nsụkpe is a rare, onomatopoeic noun; the constructions are natural but the word is uncommon.

gloss: to attack a person or community; to invade a community or city

examples.igbo: Ndị agha wakpọrọ obodo ahụ n'etiti abalị.
examples.english: The soldiers attacked that town in the middle of the night.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ha ji wakpọ obodo anyị?
examples.english: Why did they invade our town?

gloss: (literally an old woman with grey hair) plant used as medicine to

examples.igbo: Agadī nwaànyì isi bụ ọgwụ ndị Igbo ji agwọ ọrịa.
examples.english: Agadī nwaànyì isi is a plant the Igbo use to treat illness.

examples.igbo: Nne m zụtara agadī nwaànyì isi n'ahịa ọgwụ.
examples.english: My mother bought agadī nwaànyì isi at the medicine market.

note: The gloss is cut off ('plant used as medicine to ...') and I am not certain of the plant's exact name and use, so the Igbo is only a cautious guess.

examples.igbo: Mkpòdù na-eto n'azụ ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: Mkpòdù shrubs grow behind our house.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ mkpòdù ndị ahụ n'ụzọ?
examples.english: Did you see those mkpòdù shrubs on the road?

note: The exact species is unknown to me, so the sentences only show it as a shrub.

examples.igbo: Anyị lutere n'ahịa n'elekere asatọ.
examples.english: We reached the market at eight o'clock.

examples.igbo: Ì lutere n'ụlọ akwụkwọ n'oge taa?
examples.english: Did you arrive at school early today?

note: I am fairly sure -lute means 'arrive at, reach', but the inflected past form lutere is the reading I have used.

gloss: push back (gradually pushing object, e.g. on a table, till it falls off it); wipe off

examples.igbo: Ọ ripụrụ efere ahụ na tebụl.
examples.english: He pushed the plate off the table.

examples.igbo: Ripụ ya na tebụl ka ọ daa.
examples.english: Push it off the table so that it falls.

examples.igbo: Nne m zụtara ùlì mkpò n'ahịa.
examples.english: My mother bought ùlì mkpò dye at the market.

examples.igbo: Ùlì mkpò ka ha ji ete akwa ahụ?
examples.english: Is it ùlì mkpò they are using to dye that cloth?

note: The entry only says 'a variety of ùlì' (a dye), so I cannot specify how it differs from other ùlì; the sentences are cautious.

gloss: upset; cause disorderliness in something, especially fluids and the stomach

examples.igbo: Ihe ọṅụṅụ ahụ gbarụrụ m afọ.
examples.english: That drink upset my stomach.

examples.igbo: Gịnị gbarụrụ gị afọ?
examples.english: What upset your stomach?

examples.igbo: Nne m tabìrì anyā mgbe m banyere n'ụlọ.
examples.english: My mother winked when I entered the house.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji tabì anyā n'ebe m nọ?
examples.english: Why are you winking at me?

examples.igbo: O ji nnu ākanwụ sie ofe ahụ.
examples.english: She used potash stone to cook that soup.

examples.igbo: Zụtara m nnu ākanwụ n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: Buy me potash stone at the market today.

examples.igbo: Okwu ya kasìrì obì m nke ukwuu.
examples.english: His words comforted me greatly.

examples.igbo: Kasịa obì nwa gị, ọ na-akwa akwa.
examples.english: Comfort your child, he is crying.

examples.igbo: Ahịhịa n'ubi gbanwụrụ n'ihi ụkọ mmiri.
examples.english: The weeds in the farm withered because of lack of water.

examples.igbo: Aka m na-agbanwụ n'ihi oyi taa.
examples.english: My hands are going numb because of the cold today.

examples.igbo: Ụgbọala abụọ kụkọlịtara n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: Two cars collided on the road.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji kụkọlịta m n'azụ n'ahịa?
examples.english: Why did you bump into me from behind at the market?

gloss: exclamation of assent or pleasure; very good! excellent! fine!

examples.igbo: Ìyaà, anyị ga-aga ahịa taa.
examples.english: Fine, we will go to the market today.

examples.igbo: Ìyaà! Nri a tọrọ ụtọ nke ukwuu!
examples.english: Excellent! This food is very delicious!

examples.igbo: A mụrụ nna nna m na narị afọ nke iri abụọ.
examples.english: My grandfather was born in the twentieth century.

examples.igbo: N'ime narị afọ iri, obodo a gbanwere nke ukwuu.
examples.english: In ten centuries, this town has changed greatly.

examples.igbo: Obi ōkwutē ya mere o jighị enyere nne ya aka.
examples.english: His hard-heartedness made him not help his mother.

examples.igbo: O nwere obi ōkwutē, ma nwanne ya nwere obi ọma.
examples.english: He is hard-hearted, but his brother is kind-hearted.

examples.igbo: Akpụ ahụ erubeghị òghìghè.
examples.english: That cassava is not yet properly cooked.

examples.igbo: Ị chere na osikapa a ruru òghìghè?
examples.english: Do you think this rice is properly cooked?

examples.igbo: Akwụkwọ ahụ makụdoro m n'aka.
examples.english: That paper stuck to my hand.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere osikapa ji makụdo n'ala ite ahụ?
examples.english: Why did the rice stick to the bottom of that pot?

examples.igbo: Ndị ori wakporo anyị n'ụzọ n'abalị.
examples.english: Robbers attacked us on the road at night.

examples.igbo: Ị na-atụ egwu ndị ori n'okporo ụzọ a?
examples.english: Are you afraid of robbers on this road?

examples.igbo: Ọkụ ŋara uwe m n'ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: Fire scorched my clothes yesterday.

examples.igbo: Ị na-aŋa akwụkwọ ahụ n'ọkụ?
examples.english: Are you scorching that paper in the fire?

note: The verb -ŋa is less common; both sentences use it as 'scorch/burn' with an object.

gloss: play the game akụ or òkwè (Yoruba ayò)

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-azụ akụ n'okpuru osisi.
examples.english: The children are playing akụ under the tree.

examples.igbo: Bịa ka anyị zụọ akụ n'ehihie.
examples.english: Come, let us play akụ in the afternoon.

examples.igbo: Òfifie akwụkwọ a siri ike nke ukwuu.
examples.english: The binding of this book is very strong.

examples.igbo: Gbanwee òfifie akwụkwọ ahụ tupu ọ dawa.
examples.english: Change the binding of that book before it falls apart.

note: I have taken òfifie as book binding; if it means binding/tying more generally, the examples may need adjusting.

examples.igbo: Osisi dàchiri n'ụzọ, anyị enweghị ike ịgafe.
examples.english: A tree fell across the road, and we could not cross.

examples.igbo: Gịnị dàchiri n'ọnụ ụzọ ụlọ anyị?
examples.english: What fell across our doorway?

examples.igbo: M na-aga ahịa kwà ùtụtù.
examples.english: I go to the market every morning.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ekpe ekpere kwà ùtụtù?
examples.english: Do you pray every morning?

examples.igbo: M riri òlòma abụọ n'ahịa ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: I ate two oranges at the market yesterday.

examples.igbo: Zụta òlòma atọ n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: Buy three oranges at the market today.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere ike ịnọdụ ebe ọbụnà.
examples.english: You can sit anywhere.

examples.igbo: Anyị ga-ezute ebe ọbụnà ị họọrọ.
examples.english: We will meet at any place you choose.

examples.igbo: Mmiri tụrụ oyi n'ahụ m n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: The water made me feel cold this morning.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-atụ oyi n'ahụ gị ugbu a?
examples.english: Does it make you feel cold right now?

note: The phrase can also be used more broadly; here it is kept to the sense 'cause to feel cold'.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akwudide okwu ruo ogologo oge.
examples.english: He continued speaking for a long time.

examples.igbo: Biko kwudide okwu, anyị na-ege ntị.
examples.english: Please continue speaking, we are listening.

note: The inflected forms na-akwudide and the imperative kwudide are used here for 'continue speaking'.

examples.igbo: Debe ọnụ duu, nwa m.
examples.english: Be silent, my child.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-edebe ọnụ duu mgbe nna ya na-ekwu.
examples.english: He keeps silent when his father is talking.

examples.igbo: O nwere ife nzizo n'azụ ụlọ ahụ.
examples.english: There is a secret thing behind that house.

examples.igbo: Gịnị bụ ife nzizo ị na-ezo?
examples.english: What is the secret thing you are hiding?

note: The entry's spelling is dialectal; standard Igbo often has 'ihe nzuzo'.

gloss: fall short of what was expected

examples.igbo: Ọrụ ya dàlụrụ nke ukwuu.
examples.english: His work fell short greatly.

examples.igbo: Atụmatụ anyị dàlụrụ n'afọ a.
examples.english: Our plan fell short this year.

note: I am fairly sure of the inflection, but the verb is not common in everyday speech.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-akpọ ndị mbụ nà ndị àbò tupu alụmdi na nwunye.
examples.english: We call on the ancestors before marriage.

examples.igbo: Ndị mbụ nà ndị àbò na-eche ezinụlọ anyị nche.
examples.english: The ancestors guard our family.

examples.igbo: O nyere m otu mkpụlụ ego.
examples.english: He gave me one cowrie.

examples.igbo: Mkpụlụ ego ndị ahụ dị n'igbe ochie.
examples.english: Those cowries are in an old box.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ese àmụ̀mà n'elu igwe.
examples.english: Lightning is flashing in the sky.

examples.igbo: Lee, àmụ̀mà na-ese n'ebe ahụ.
examples.english: Look, lightning is flashing there.

examples.igbo: Nyachi oghere ahụ tupu mmiri abịa.
examples.english: Seal that hole before rain comes.

examples.igbo: O ji ụrọ na-anyachi mgbidi ụlọ ya.
examples.english: He is using clay to seal the wall of his house.

examples.igbo: Etu ọ dị nọòfụ, anyị agaghị aga ahịa taa.
examples.english: As it is so, we will not go to market today.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ etu ọ dị nọòfụ, ọ dịghị mkpa ka anyị kwuo ya ọzọ.
examples.english: It is as it is so, there is no need for us to say it again.

examples.igbo: Elùuluū tara m n'ụkwụ.
examples.english: A soldier ant bit me on the foot.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-egbu elùuluū n'ogige.
examples.english: Children are killing soldier ants in the compound.

examples.igbo: Ana m anụfịalụ ihe ha na-ekwu.
examples.english: I overhear what they are saying.

examples.igbo: Ị na-anụfịalụ ka anyị na-akpa nkata?
examples.english: Do you overhear us talking?

note: Rare verb; examples use habitual forms to avoid uncertain past inflection.

gloss: (of a task or problem) get or become tough, unresolvable or unsolvable

examples.igbo: Ọrụ ahụ gbàrà ike, anyị enweghị ike ime ya.
examples.english: That work became tough; we cannot do it.

examples.igbo: Okwu a gbàrà ike, ò nweghị onye ga-edozi ya?
examples.english: This matter has become tough; is there no one to settle it?

examples.igbo: Nkịta ahụ sòchiri m n'azụ.
examples.english: That dog followed me closely behind.

examples.igbo: Sòchie ya nke ọma.
examples.english: Follow him closely.

note: Past form sòchiri and imperative sòchie are assumed from the stem sòchi.

examples.igbo: Nne m ji ǹdụdụ na-eru akwa.
examples.english: My mother uses a needle to sew cloth.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ǹdụdụ m n'ime igbe?
examples.english: Have you seen my needle in the box?

examples.igbo: O kèlụrụ òkè ya n'ahịa.
examples.english: He took his share at the market.

examples.igbo: Kèlụ òkè gị tupu ha ewere ya.
examples.english: Take your share before they take it.

note: Inflected as kèlụrụ in the past and kèlụ in the imperative.

examples.igbo: Anyị sìnere ọnụ ahịa tupu anyị zụta.
examples.english: We compared prices before we bought.

examples.igbo: Ị sìnere ha abụọ?
examples.english: Did you compare the two?

note: Examples show the compare sense of -sìne.

examples.igbo: Ìfulū na-eto n'ubi anyị.
examples.english: Flowers are growing in our farm.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ìfulū ndị ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see those flowers?

examples.igbo: Òlilo dị m n'afọ.
examples.english: I have pain in my stomach.

examples.igbo: Òlilo isi na-akụ ya.
examples.english: Headache pains him.

examples.igbo: Anyị kpapụrụ n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: We went out for a walk in the morning.

examples.igbo: Kpapụọ ntakịrị.
examples.english: Go out for a walk a little.

note: Past and imperative forms are assumed from the stem -kpapù.

examples.igbo: Oko unèlè a dị arọ.
examples.english: This bunch of bananas is heavy.

examples.igbo: Ị zụrụ oko unèlè ole?
examples.english: How many bunches of bananas did you buy?

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ nnà egwū nke òtù egwū anyị.
examples.english: He is the patron of our dance group.

examples.igbo: Nnà egwū nyere ego maka egwū ahụ.
examples.english: The patron gave money for that dance.

examples.igbo: Anyànwụ na-enwu n'ehihie.
examples.english: The sun shines in the afternoon.

examples.igbo: Gịnị na-enwu n'elu mmiri?
examples.english: What is shining on the water?

gloss: walk about stealthily; prowl; loiter; dodge work; malinger

examples.igbo: O na-ehegharị n'okporo ámá abalị.
examples.english: He prowls in the street at night.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ị na-ehegharị n'ebe a?
examples.english: Why are you loitering here?

examples.igbo: Wò uwe gị ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Put on your clothes quickly.

examples.igbo: O wòrò uwe ọhụrụ ya.
examples.english: He put on his new clothes.

gloss: again; other; another another yam, for this first one is not good

examples.igbo: Nye m òzọ ji, nke a adịghị mma.
examples.english: Give me another yam; this one is not good.

examples.igbo: Òzọ mmadụ bịara n'ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: Another person came to our house.

examples.igbo: O nwere ego kịlịkịlị n'akpa ya.
examples.english: He has coins in his pocket.

examples.igbo: Ego kịlịkịlị ole ka ị nwere?
examples.english: How many coins do you have?

examples.igbo: Mgbagwòju anyā juru n'ahịa ahụ.
examples.english: Confusion filled that market.

examples.igbo: Mgbagwòju anyā mere ka ụmụaka tụfuo ụzọ.
examples.english: Confusion made the children lose the way.

examples.igbo: O butere ọyà n'aka enyi ya.
examples.english: He caught a disease from his friend.

examples.igbo: Ị butere ọyà n'ebe ahụ?
examples.english: Did you catch a disease there?

examples.igbo: Ǹke ìzìzì bụ nke m.
examples.english: The first is mine.

examples.igbo: Gịnị bụ ǹke ìzìzì n'ihe ị chọrọ?
examples.english: What is the first thing you want?

examples.igbo: O tinyere akwụkwọ mfụkòba n’ime akpa ya.
examples.english: He put folded paper inside his bag.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ akwụkwọ mfụkòba ahụ n’elu tebụl?
examples.english: Did you see that folded paper on the table?

examples.igbo: Anyị hụzùrù ihe niile n’ahịa taa.
examples.english: We saw everything in the market today.

examples.igbo: Ị hụzùrù mmadụ niile n’ọgbakọ ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see all the people at that gathering?

note: The inflected form hụzùrù may vary by dialect.

examples.igbo: Nomìna ọgwụ a ozugbo, nwa m.
examples.english: Swallow this medicine down immediately, my child.

examples.igbo: Ọ nòmìnàra ya n’otu ọnụ n’ụtụtụ.
examples.english: He swallowed it down in one gulp in the morning.

note: Past form nòmìnàra is my best reconstruction.

examples.igbo: Biko kwụwa okwu gị n’olu doro anya.
examples.english: Please speak your words in a clear voice.

examples.igbo: O kwụwara okwu ya nke ọma n’ọgbakọ.
examples.english: He spoke his words plainly at the meeting.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-eme mmega n’ogige kwa ụtụtụ.
examples.english: He exercises in the garden every morning.

examples.igbo: Mmega a na-agwụ ike ma ọ dị mma.
examples.english: This exercise is tiring but good.

examples.igbo: Gbanye ọkụ ukpē ka anyị hụ ihe.
examples.english: Light the lamp so we can see.

examples.igbo: Ọkụ ukpē ahụ na-enwu n’ime ụlọ.
examples.english: That lamp is shining in the room.

examples.igbo: O wepụrụ ǹtù azù tupu o sie ya.
examples.english: She removed fish scales before cooking it.

examples.igbo: Ǹtù azù ndị ahụ na-egbuke egbuke.
examples.english: Those fish scales are shiny.

examples.igbo: Ụzọ ahụ zoro ezo n’okpuru ahịhịa.
examples.english: The path is hidden under the grass.

examples.igbo: Ego ahụ zoro ezo, ọ dịghị onye hụrụ ya.
examples.english: The money is hidden, nobody saw it.

examples.igbo: Biko nòzi ọdụ gị nke ọma.
examples.english: Please sit properly.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka nòziri ọdụ n’ahịrị n’ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: The children sat properly in a row at school.

note: The nòziri form is uncertain.

examples.igbo: Dọkpụpù ahịhịa ahụ n’ala n’aka gị.
examples.english: Pull that weed out of the ground with your hand.

examples.igbo: O dọkpụpụrụ nkịta ahụ n’ime olulu.
examples.english: He pulled the dog out of the hole.

gloss: complete or finish with the painting of

examples.igbo: O tepùrù ụlọ ahụ ọcha taa.
examples.english: He finished painting that house white today.

examples.igbo: Tepùo mgbidi ahụ tupu mmiri abịa.
examples.english: Finish painting that wall before the rain comes.

note: The verb sense is understood but uncommon; tone marking on inflected forms may vary.

examples.igbo: Mama zụtara okpòrokō n'ahịa.
examples.english: Mother bought stockfish at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-etinye okpòrokō n'ofe?
examples.english: Will you put stockfish in the soup?

gloss: put down load from the head

examples.igbo: O zitùrù ibu ya n'isi.
examples.english: He put down his load from his head.

examples.igbo: Biko zitùo ibu gị n'isi.
examples.english: Please put down your load from your head.

note: The stem is used with the expected inflections, but tone marking may differ in some dialects.

examples.igbo: Nri gbọrọ agbọ n'ite, anyị tụfuru ya.
examples.english: The food remained over in the pot, so we threw it away.

examples.igbo: Gịnị gbọrọ agbọ n'ọrụ a?
examples.english: What is left over in this work?

note: The expression is idiomatic, but the exact construction can vary.

examples.igbo: Nna m bụ ochīè mmadụ.
examples.english: My father is an old person.

examples.igbo: Ụlọ ochīè a ka na-eguzo.
examples.english: This old house is still standing.

gloss: consult the Agbala in Awka, the most famous one

examples.igbo: O gara Agbàlà ịjụ maka ọrịa nwa ya.
examples.english: He went to Agbala to ask about his child's illness.

examples.igbo: Ị jeere Agbàlà, gịnị ka ha gwara gị?
examples.english: You went to Agbala, what did they tell you?

gloss: (also ìpo ànwàlì) a fish (Alestes leuciscus); ìpo is regarded as the larger size of ànwàlì

examples.igbo: Anyị zụtara ànwàlì atọ n'ahịa.
examples.english: We bought three ànwàlì fish at the market.

examples.igbo: Ànwàlì a pere mpe karịa ìpo?
examples.english: Is this ànwàlì smaller than ìpo?

gloss: physic nut (Jatropha curcas Linn.) used for hedging; the sap stains indelibly, seeds are purgative

examples.igbo: Ha kụrụ òwu īduù gburugburu ubi ha.
examples.english: They planted physic nut around their farm.

examples.igbo: Mkpụrụ òwu īduù na-ebute afọ ọsịsa.
examples.english: Physic nut seeds cause diarrhea.

gloss: shine; give light (as a source); come on (electronic device); flare; blaze

examples.igbo: Ọkụ na-enwu n'ime ọhịa.
examples.english: The fire is blazing in the bush.

examples.igbo: Telivishọn enwuola, ị nwere ike ile ya.
examples.english: The television has come on, you can watch it.

note: The sense is clear, but the exact inflection for electronic devices may vary.

examples.igbo: O zara letà ahụ m zitere ya.
examples.english: He replied to the letter I sent him.

examples.igbo: Za letà ahụ tupu izu agwụ.
examples.english: Reply to that letter before the week ends.

examples.igbo: O gosiri afọ òfùfù nye ndị ọbịa.
examples.english: He showed generosity to the guests.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-egosi afọ òfùfù nye ụmụaka?
examples.english: Will you show generosity to the children?

note: Biblical register; examples are simple and idiomatic.

examples.igbo: Òdìnjọ dakwasịrị ezinụlọ anyị n'afọ a.
examples.english: Misfortune befell our family this year.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara òdìnjọ a n'obodo unu?
examples.english: What caused this misfortune in your town?

gloss: bat sp. (very small and not eaten)

examples.igbo: Anyị hụrụ ụsụ kà ǹgwu n'ime ọhịa.
examples.english: We saw a small bat in the bush.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka anaghị eri ụsụ kà ǹgwu.
examples.english: Children do not eat that small bat.

note: Species name; usage is restricted to this small bat.

examples.igbo: O tipìrì ite ahụ n'ala.
examples.english: He smashed that pot on the ground.

examples.igbo: Ònye tipìrì iko ahụ?
examples.english: Who smashed that cup?

examples.igbo: Onye ụkọchukwu na-edo nsọ ụlọ ụka ọhụrụ.
examples.english: The priest is consecrating the new church.

examples.igbo: Bịa doo nsọ ebe a taa.
examples.english: Come and consecrate this place today.

note: Inflection of the phrase do nsọ is not fully certain.

gloss: the eleventh month of the year; November

examples.igbo: N'ọnwa Nọ̀vembà, anyị na-ewe ihe ubi.
examples.english: In November, we harvest.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-alọta n'ọnwa Nọ̀vembà?
examples.english: Will you return in November?

examples.igbo: Mmiri menyụrụ ọkụ ahụ.
examples.english: Water extinguished that fire.

examples.igbo: Ị menyụrụ ọkụ ahụ tupu ị pụọ?
examples.english: Did you extinguish that fire before you left?

note: Past form menyụrụ is assumed.

examples.igbo: Òghù na-awụli elu n'osisi.
examples.english: A flying squirrel jumps high in a tree.

examples.igbo: Ị hụtụla òghù n'ọhịa a?
examples.english: Have you seen a flying squirrel in this bush?

examples.igbo: Uwe ya ruru unyi n'ụzọ.
examples.english: His clothes got dirty on the road.

examples.igbo: Aka gị ruru unyi, gaa saa ya.
examples.english: Your hands are dirty, go wash them.

gloss: cream; lotion, body lotion, hair cream.

examples.igbo: O tinyere ùde n'ahụ ya.
examples.english: She applied lotion to her body.

examples.igbo: Zụta ùde ọhụrụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: Buy new cream at the market.

examples.igbo: Ọrịa ya dọchìghaara àzụ agụmakwụkwọ ya.
examples.english: His illness set back his education.

examples.igbo: Gịnị dọchìghaara àzụ ọrụ ugbo unu?
examples.english: What set back your farming?

note: Sense and phrasing are sound; the past inflection dọchìghaara àzụ is my best rendering.

examples.igbo: Zụta mkpa ọ kụ n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: Buy matches at the market today.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere mkpa ọ kụ m ga-eji mụnye ọkụ?
examples.english: Do you have matches I can use to light the fire?

note: mkpa ọkụ is the more common form; mkpa ọ kụ is understood but sounds dialectal.

gloss: for long; after a long time (denoting a great degree either of smallness or bigness)

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ ràbàrịị tupu o nwee ike ije.
examples.english: That child took a long time before he could walk.

examples.igbo: Ndị ọbịa ahụ ràbàrịị tupu ha apụọ.
examples.english: The visitors stayed long before they left.

note: Used adverbially with ràbàrịị; I am not fully certain of the natural inflection.

gloss: name for a child believed an ọgbanje (literally Are we to count you among our family circle (or are you going to leave us again?))

examples.igbo: Aha nwa ọhụrụ ahụ bụ Agụnyego.
examples.english: The newborn's name is Agụnyego.

examples.igbo: Agụnyego, bịa ebe a ozugbo.
examples.english: Agụnyego, come here at once.

gloss: fine; exact a levy as a penalty by an authority

examples.igbo: E dàara m nhā maka ịzụ ahịa n'ụzọ.
examples.english: I was fined for trading on the road.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere gọọmentị ji dàa gị nhā?
examples.english: Why did the government fine you?

note: The passive e dàara m nhā is the construction I am most sure of.

examples.igbo: Kọtùma wetara akwụkwọ n'ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: The court messenger brought a letter to our house.

examples.igbo: Kọtùma ahụ abịala ọzọ?
examples.english: Has that court messenger come again?

note: English loanword; spelling may vary.

examples.igbo: Mama na-eghe ji n'ite.
examples.english: Mother is boiling yam in the pot.

examples.igbo: Ghee osikapa ahụ ruo mgbe ọ gawara nro.
examples.english: Boil that rice until it becomes soft.

note: In many areas -si is used for cooking, -ghu for boiling.

examples.igbo: Ewu ahụ nanarịrị n'ogige.
examples.english: The goat escaped from the pen.

examples.igbo: Nanarị ebe a tupu mmadụ ahụ gị!
examples.english: Get away from here before that person sees you!

note: Sense is clear but the verb is uncommon in everyday speech.

examples.igbo: Ǹkè irū abịala n'ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: The expected one has come to our house.

examples.igbo: Ònye bụ ǹkè irū n'ọrụ a?
examples.english: Who is the next one for this work?

note: The phrase is understood as 'the next/expected one'; usage is not common in my experience.

examples.igbo: Mmiri ide ahụ tadara n'abalị.
examples.english: The flood subsided at night.

examples.igbo: Olee mgbe mmiri ga-atadà?
examples.english: When will the water subside?

gloss: small child; caressing words used by mothers to their children

examples.igbo: Obele nnwā, bịa ka m nye gị nri.
examples.english: Little one, come so I can give you food.

examples.igbo: Obele nnwā, olee ebe ị na-aga?
examples.english: Little one, where are you going?

note: The phrase is a term of endearment; usage is affectionate address, which the two sentences show.

gloss: expel air from the lungs with a short sharp sound; cough

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akwa ụkwarà n'ihi na oyi tara ya.
examples.english: He is coughing because the cold caught him.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akwa ụkwarà ọzọ?
examples.english: Are you coughing again?

examples.igbo: Dọkịta gbalụrụ ọgwù ọjọọ ahụ n'ahụ nwa ahụ.
examples.english: The doctor neutralized that poison in the child's body.

examples.igbo: Gbalụ ọgwù ahụ tupu o ruo n'obi ya.
examples.english: Neutralize that poison before it reaches his heart.

note: The stem -gbalụ here is inflected as gbalụrụ (past) and gbalụ (imperative).

gloss: send down from far or above

examples.igbo: Ọ zidatara anyị ozi site n'elu ugwu.
examples.english: He sent a message down to us from the top of the hill.

examples.igbo: Zidata akpa ndị ahụ site n'elu ụlọ.
examples.english: Send those bags down from the top of the house.

gloss: be drowsy; be unsmart; be inclined to sleepiness

examples.igbo: Ọ na-eme m anyaụrā mgbe anyanwụ na-ekpo ọkụ.
examples.english: I feel drowsy when the sun is hot.

examples.igbo: Nri ahụ mere nwa ahụ anyaụrā.
examples.english: That food made the child drowsy.

gloss: give little or no attention to something; neglect; overlook; ignore

examples.igbo: Ọ leghaara anya n'ọrụ ugbo ya.
examples.english: He neglected his farm work.

examples.igbo: Alegharala anya n'ụmụ gị.
examples.english: Do not neglect your children.

gloss: move into place vacated by another

examples.igbo: Nwa ya kwachiri oche ya mgbe ọ biliri.
examples.english: His child moved into his seat when he stood up.

examples.igbo: Kwachie oche ahụ mgbe ọ pụtara.
examples.english: Move into that seat when he leaves.

examples.igbo: Arọ ọzọ ka anyị ga-akụ osikapa.
examples.english: Next year we shall plant rice.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-aga ụlọ akwụkwọ n'arọ ọzọ?
examples.english: Will you go to school next year?

note: Arọ ọzọ is the standard expression for 'next year'; afọ ọzọ is also heard.

examples.igbo: Ọ yawara akwa ahụ n'ibe abụọ.
examples.english: She yanked that cloth into two pieces.

examples.igbo: Yawaa osisi ahụ ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Yank that stick apart quickly.

examples.igbo: Ọnụ ole ka ị chọrọ?
examples.english: How many do you want?

examples.igbo: A maghị m ọnụ mmadụ bịara.
examples.english: I don't know the number of people who came.

note: The sense given is quantity/number, kept distinct from ọnụ 'mouth' and ọnụ 'price'.

gloss: be observant, watchful, careful; take notice of; watch (literally lay the eyes on the ground)

examples.igbo: Tọ̀ anyā mgbe ị na-anya ụgbọala.
examples.english: Be careful when you drive.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-atọ̀ anyā n'ebe ụmụ ya nọ.
examples.english: She watches over her children.

examples.igbo: Wèdàta ite ahụ n'elu tebụl ahụ.
examples.english: Bring down that pot from that table.

examples.igbo: Ị wèdàtara m akpa ahụ n'ụlọ?
examples.english: Did you bring down that bag for me in the house?

examples.igbo: Ndị ìkòm na-aga ịkụ azụ n'osimiri.
examples.english: The men are going to fish in the river.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ naanị ndị ìkòm na-abịa ebe a?
examples.english: Is it only men that come here?

examples.igbo: Anyị na-eme Ekeresìmeèsì n'ụlọ nne m.
examples.english: We celebrate Christmas at my mother's house.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-abịa Ekeresìmeèsì n'ụlọ anyị?
examples.english: Will you come to Christmas at our house?

gloss: pull together; pull together to the centre

examples.igbo: Sèkọnata eriri ahụ n'otu ebe ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Pull that rope together to one place quickly.

examples.igbo: Ị sèkọnataala osisi ndị ahụ n'otu ebe?
examples.english: Have you pulled those woods together to one place?

examples.igbo: Nwa di ọtā na-ebu egbe nna ya.
examples.english: The hunter's attendant carries his father's gun.

examples.igbo: Ị bụ nwa di ọtā n'ezie?
examples.english: Are you really a hunter's attendant?

gloss: fall into; match or rhyme; correspond

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ dabànyèrè n'olulu mmiri n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: That child fell into the well in the morning.

examples.igbo: Ị dabànyèrè n'ọnyà n'ụzọ mgbe ị na-ejegharị?
examples.english: Did you fall into the trap on the road while you were walking?

examples.igbo: Enekē ntì ọbā na-efe n'elu ụlọ.
examples.english: The swallow flies over the house.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ enekē ntì ọbā n'osisi ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see the swallow on that tree?

examples.igbo: M zụtara akwụ olū n'ahịa n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: I bought a pineapple at the market in the morning.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eri akwụ olū mgbe ụfọdụ?
examples.english: Do you eat pineapple sometimes?

gloss: strike down; knock down; knock off; bring down

examples.igbo: Onye ọkpọ ahụ kụtùrù ya n'ala.
examples.english: The boxer knocked him down to the ground.

examples.igbo: Kụtù osisi ahụ ka ọ daa.
examples.english: Knock down that tree so it falls.

examples.igbo: Anyị biliri n'emumechī gaa n'ubi.
examples.english: We woke at daybreak and went to the farm.

examples.igbo: Ọkụkọ na-akụ n'emumechī, ị nụrụ ya?
examples.english: The rooster crows at daybreak, did you hear it?

note: Emumechī is uncommon; examples are idiomatic but the word is rare.

examples.igbo: Ala ebe a dị larịị, ọ dị mfe ịgafe.
examples.english: This ground is level, it is easy to cross.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ na tebụl ahụ adịghị larịị?
examples.english: Did you see that the table is not level?

examples.igbo: Akpa ọka a fērē mfe, o bughị arọ.
examples.english: This bag of corn is light, it is not heavy.

examples.igbo: Ọ̀ bụ na akpa gị fērē mfe?
examples.english: Is your bag light?

note: Uncertain whether fē m̄fē is the usual weight sense; many speakers use dị mfe.

gloss: instep of foot (literally the king's baby never licks the sand)

examples.igbo: Ọ tụrụ m ụkwụ n'isi nwa ezè alā ajā.
examples.english: He stepped on my instep.

examples.igbo: Ọ̀ bụ nwa ezè alā ajā ya merụrụ ahụ?
examples.english: Is it his instep that got injured?

note: The phrase is obscure; I am not fully certain of its idiomatic use in a sentence.

examples.igbo: Obi na-atọ m ụtọ na ị bịara.
examples.english: I am glad that you came.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-atọ gị ụtọ na anyị gara ahịa?
examples.english: Are you glad that we went to the market?

examples.igbo: Nne ya kughàchiri nwa ya n'ụlọ.
examples.english: Her mother carried her baby back home.

examples.igbo: Kughàchite nwa ahụ ngwa ngwa, ọ na-ebe akwa.
examples.english: Carry that baby back quickly, he is crying.

note: The verb inflection is plausible, but I would double-check the imperative form.

gloss: road leading from a public road to the entrance of a compound; driveway

examples.igbo: Ụzàamā anyị dị warara, ụgbọ ala agaghị aba.
examples.english: Our driveway is narrow, the car will not enter.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ụzàamā na-eduga n'ụlọ ha?
examples.english: Did you see the driveway leading to their house?

examples.igbo: Anyị na-aga agbamakwụkwọ nwanne m n'izu na-abịa.
examples.english: We are going to my sister's wedding next week.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara akwa ọhụrụ maka agbamakwụkwọ ahụ?
examples.english: Did you buy new clothes for that wedding?

note: Entry spelling appears to be a variant; standard spelling is agbamakwụkwọ.

examples.igbo: O nyere m ọmà mgbe anyị zutere.
examples.english: He gave me a hug when we met.

examples.igbo: Ọmà ya siri ike, ọ fọrọ nke nta ka m daa.
examples.english: His embrace was strong, I almost fell.

note: I am fairly sure of the embrace sense, but the word is not very common in everyday speech.

examples.igbo: Ụlọ ọrụ anyị na-arụ ọrụ n'isi obodo.
examples.english: Our company works in the capital.

examples.igbo: Ị na-arụ ọrụ n'ụlọ ọrụ gị taa?
examples.english: Are you working at your company today?

examples.igbo: O gbaràpụrụ ọrụ ya gaa ahịa.
examples.english: He abandoned his work and went to the market.

examples.igbo: Gbaràpụ ihe ọjọọ ahụ, bido ndụ ọhụrụ.
examples.english: Abandon that bad thing, start a new life.

gloss: tread in any sort of filth; tread till it becomes soft and messy

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka ahụ zọtara apịtị n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: Those children trod mud on the road.

examples.igbo: Zọta apịtị ahụ ka ọ bụrụ nro.
examples.english: Tread that mud so it becomes soft.

note: The verb -zọtọ is not common in everyday speech; I have used it in a plausible context but would phrase one sentence differently.

examples.igbo: O dara ọkụ n'azụ ya n'ụlọ ọgwụ.
examples.english: He branded his back at the hospital.

examples.igbo: Daa ọkụ n'ebe ahụ tupu ọ gbasaa.
examples.english: Cauterize there before it spreads.

note: The compound -da ọkụ is correct, but the context of branding/cauterizing is less common in daily conversation.

gloss: male name (literally life is the head)

examples.igbo: Ndùbiisi bịara ụlọ akwụkwọ n'ụtụtụ taa.
examples.english: Ndubisi came to school this morning.

examples.igbo: Ndùbiisi, kedu ebe ị na-aga ugbu a?
examples.english: Ndubisi, where are you going now?

gloss: wander about lazily in the house

examples.igbo: O na-awaghalị n'ụnò kama ịrụ ọrụ.
examples.english: He wanders lazily in the house instead of working.

examples.igbo: Ị na-awaghalị n'ụnò, ị̀ chọghị ịrụ ọrụ?
examples.english: You are wandering lazily in the house, don't you want to work?

note: The phrase is idiomatic, but the second sentence uses a question form that is slightly colloquial.

examples.igbo: O kèrà ego ahụ n'etiti ụmụaka.
examples.english: He divided the money equally among the children.

examples.igbo: Kèrà nri ahụ n'ụzọ ziri ezi.
examples.english: Divide that food equally.

examples.igbo: O selitere mmiri ahụ n'olulu n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: He drew up the water from the well in the morning.

examples.igbo: Selite aka gị elu, too Chineke.
examples.english: Lift up your hand, praise God.

gloss: be very tough (of person) (i.e. have very tough constitution or body that withstands great hardship, sometimes naturally or through repeated hard experience)

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ siri àrụ, o naghị atụ egwu.
examples.english: That man is very tough, he is not afraid.

examples.igbo: Sì àrụ, egbula ụjọ n'oge ihe isi ike.
examples.english: Be tough, don't be afraid in times of hardship.

note: The expression is understood, but the imperative form 'Sì àrụ' is less common than the descriptive use.

examples.igbo: Kà chi fo, hie ụra nke ọma.
examples.english: Goodnight, sleep well.

examples.igbo: Anyị ga-ahụ gị echi. Kà chi fo!
examples.english: We will see you tomorrow. Goodnight!

examples.igbo: Iwepu wepu ise na iri na-enye ise.
examples.english: Subtracting five from ten gives five.

examples.igbo: Mụta iwepu wepu n'ụlọ akwụkwọ taa.
examples.english: Learn subtraction in school today.

examples.igbo: A na-eji ichèlè akū esi nri.
examples.english: Palm kernel shells are used for cooking.

examples.igbo: Ị chịkọtara ichèlè akū niile?
examples.english: Did you gather all the palm kernel shells?

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ òdìegwù na ọ lọtara ndụ.
examples.english: It is wonderful that he returned alive.

examples.igbo: Ị nụrụ akụkọ òdìegwù ahụ?
examples.english: Did you hear that tragic story?

examples.igbo: O kọọrọ nwanne ya ọgwụ n'ihi ego.
examples.english: He harmed his brother through sorcery because of money.

examples.igbo: Ị kọọrọ m ọgwụ? Gịnị mere?
examples.english: Did you harm me through sorcery? Why?

gloss: tree whose fruit resembles ụdalà in shape, but smaller

examples.igbo: Ụdalā ènwè na-amị mkpụrụ dị ka ụdalà.
examples.english: The ụdala enwe bears fruit like the ụdala.

examples.igbo: Gbaa ụdalā ènwè n'ubi gị.
examples.english: Plant an ụdala enwe in your farm.

examples.igbo: Ewu tara akwụkwọ osisi ahụ tabèsị.
examples.english: The goat bit off all the leaves of that tree.

examples.igbo: Ị tara mkpụrụ osisi ahụ tabèsị?
examples.english: Did you bite off all the fruit of that tree?

gloss: curse; to invoke or angrily call down evil on someone

examples.igbo: O bụrụ nwa ya ọnụ n'ihu ọha.
examples.english: She cursed her child in public.

examples.igbo: Ekwela i bụọ m ọnụ n'efu.
examples.english: Don't curse me for nothing.

examples.igbo: O nwere ezi na ụnọ mgbe ọ lụrụ nwunye.
examples.english: He became a householder when he married a wife.

examples.igbo: Ị nweela ezi na ụnọ ugbu a?
examples.english: Have you become a householder now?

gloss: stir up [dust], rush or come up from the ground;

examples.igbo: Oké ifufe bọliri ájá n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: A strong wind stirred up dust in the market today.

examples.igbo: Lee ka ájá na-abọli n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: Look how dust is rising on the road.

examples.igbo: Ọzò di mgba nọ n'ime ọhịa.
examples.english: The gorilla is inside the forest.

examples.igbo: Anyị hụrụ ọzò di mgba n'ogige anụmanụ.
examples.english: We saw a gorilla at the zoo.

examples.igbo: Ọ dàjụọla mgbe nne ya kpọrọ ya.
examples.english: It quietened when her mother called her.

examples.igbo: Oké ifufe ahụ dàjụọla, anyị nwere ike ịpụ.
examples.english: The storm has quietened; we can go out.

examples.igbo: Nye m nwa odō ka m kuo ji.
examples.english: Give me the pestle so I can pound yam.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ nwa odō n'ụlọ nri?
examples.english: Did you see the pestle in the kitchen?

examples.igbo: Okpulukpu mbè ahụ siri ike dị ka nkume.
examples.english: That tortoise shell is hard as a stone.

examples.igbo: Ị hụla okpulukpu mbè n'ọhịa?
examples.english: Have you ever seen a tortoise shell in the bush?

gloss: be stronger than (literally hand to be greater than hand)

examples.igbo: Chidi kara m aka n'ịgba mgba.
examples.english: Chidi is stronger than me at wrestling.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ekwu na ị kara ya aka?
examples.english: Are you saying you are stronger than him?

note: The idiom is clear, but the tone on the stem -ka varies by speaker.

examples.igbo: Okpodi nọ n'elu mgbidi, na-ele anyị.
examples.english: An agama lizard is on the wall, watching us.

examples.igbo: Lee okpodi ahụ ka ọ na-agba ọsọ n'ogige!
examples.english: Look at that agama lizard running in the yard!

note: Okpodi refers specifically to the male agama; some speakers use it loosely for the lizard.

examples.igbo: Òmịmị azụ na-ewe ụbọchị abụọ.
examples.english: Drying fish takes two days.

examples.igbo: Òmịmị ọka ahụ ezuola?
examples.english: Is the drying of that corn finished?

note: Òmịmị as a noun for 'drying' is used but many speakers prefer a verbal phrase.

examples.igbo: Ọ dèfìrì aha ya n'akwụkwọ.
examples.english: He wrote his name wrongly on the paper.

examples.igbo: Ị dèfìrì okwu ahụ, degharịa ya.
examples.english: You wrote that word incorrectly, rewrite it.

note: The stem is correct; spelling with tone marks varies in print.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ meghèrịrị n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: That child misbehaved at school.

examples.igbo: Meghèrịla n'ihu ndị ọbịa.
examples.english: Do not misbehave in front of guests.

examples.igbo: Onyeisi wedatara ya àlà n'ihu mmadụ niile.
examples.english: The boss humbled him in front of everybody.

examples.igbo: Weda ibu ahụ àlà nwayọọ.
examples.english: Bring that load down slowly.

note: Both the literal and the figurative sense are shown.

examples.igbo: Ha gbara òrịǹgò n'ụlọ nwanne m.
examples.english: They made merry at my brother's house.

examples.igbo: Bịa ka anyị gbaa òrịǹgò n'abalị a!
examples.english: Come, let us have fun tonight!

examples.igbo: Ọ kpọdèbèrè nwa ya n'akụkụ ya.
examples.english: She called her child close to her.

examples.igbo: Kpọdèbe oche ahụ n'akụkụ tebụl.
examples.english: Bring that chair near the table.

note: The verb is understood, but the exact verbal extensions vary by dialect.

examples.igbo: O ji osisi na-efido ụlọ ahụ.
examples.english: He uses a stick to support that house.

examples.igbo: Fidoo mgbidi ahụ ka ọ ghara ịda.
examples.english: Support that wall so it does not fall.

gloss: anoint with oil; paint, coat, smear with oil

examples.igbo: O tere mmanụ n'isi nwa ahụ.
examples.english: She anointed that child's head with oil.

examples.igbo: Tee mmanụ n'ahụ gị tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Apply oil on your body before you go out.

gloss: plant with edible fruit (Aframomum daniellii (Hook. f.) K. Schum.)

examples.igbo: Òkpoǹzàla na-eto n'akụkụ ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: Okponzala grows beside our house.

examples.igbo: Ị hụla mkpụrụ òkpoǹzàla n'ọhịa?
examples.english: Have you seen okponzala fruit in the bush?

gloss: an unpleasant behavior towards people as a result of feeling more important than others; arrogance

examples.igbo: Ǹgàǹgà ya na-ewe ndị ọrụ ibe ya iwe.
examples.english: His arrogance annoys his colleagues.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ị ji eme ǹgàǹgà?
examples.english: Why do you behave arrogantly?

examples.igbo: Ọ gbalara n'ụlọ ozugbo ọ nụrụ oku.
examples.english: He ran home immediately he heard the call.

examples.igbo: Gbalanụ n'ụlọ, mmiri na-ezo!
examples.english: Run home, it is raining!

examples.igbo: Anyị na-akpakọ nkụ ọnụ.
examples.english: We gather firewood together.

examples.igbo: Kpakọọ akwụkwọ ndị a ọnụ.
examples.english: Gather these books together.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-agwu mmiri n'ọdọ mmiri.
examples.english: The children swim in the pond.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere ike igwu mmiri?
examples.english: Can you swim?

gloss: to have mercy on someone of somebody; have mercy

examples.igbo: O meere nwata ahụ ebere.
examples.english: He had mercy on that child.

examples.igbo: Meere nwanne gị ebere.
examples.english: Have mercy on your brother.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-achu mmiri n'iyi kwa ụtụtụ.
examples.english: She fetches water at the stream every morning.

examples.igbo: Chuo mmiri ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Fetch water quickly.

examples.igbo: Onye na-akpụ ígwè na-afụ ekò.
examples.english: The blacksmith blows the bellows.

examples.igbo: Fụọ ekò nke ọma ka ígwè wee gbazee.
examples.english: Blow the bellows well so the iron melts.

examples.igbo: Nne m kwakọdoro akwa abụọ ahụ ọnụ.
examples.english: My mother sewed those two cloths together.

examples.igbo: Ị kwakọdoro akwa abụọ ahụ ọnụ?
examples.english: Did you sew those two cloths together?

examples.igbo: Ndepụta a na-agụnye aha ụmụ akwụkwọ niile.
examples.english: This list includes all the students' names.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-agụnye ụgwọ ọrụ m?
examples.english: Does it include my salary?

examples.igbo: Anyị rara ume n'okpuru osisi.
examples.english: We took some rest under a tree.

examples.igbo: Ị rara ume taa?
examples.english: Did you take some rest today?

note: Used in past-tense constructions; the entry may also be used as a phrase in other forms.

examples.igbo: Ọ mekwàsịrị ọrụ ahụ n'ụlọ.
examples.english: He did that work again at home.

examples.igbo: Ị mekwàsịrị ọrụ ahụ?
examples.english: Did you do that work again?

note: Inflected form mekwàsịrị is used; tone marking may vary.

gloss: grunt; make sound like lorry, automobile or other powered vehicle, machine, etc.

examples.igbo: Ụgbọ ala ochie ahụ na-asù n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: That old vehicle grunts on the road.

examples.igbo: Ị na-anụ ka igwe ahụ na-asù?
examples.english: Do you hear the machine grunting?

note: The verb is used for a low grunting or engine-like sound.

examples.igbo: Ọ yi ìyàji mara mma.
examples.english: She wore a beautiful dyed cloth.

examples.igbo: Ìyàji a ọ dị oke ọnụ?
examples.english: Is this dyed cloth very expensive?

gloss: to have sex or intercourse; to copulate; fornicate

examples.igbo: Ha na-akwa īkō n'ụlọ.
examples.english: They are having sex in the house.

examples.igbo: Ọ kwara īkō na nwunye ya?
examples.english: Did he have sex with his wife?

note: Explicit sense; the phrase is used here in ordinary modern constructions.

gloss: purify; prove; try; refine; be purified, proved, etc. (metals, by fire)

examples.igbo: Ha nùchara ọla ahụ n'ọkụ.
examples.english: They purified that metal in fire.

examples.igbo: Ị nùchara ọla edo a n'ọkụ?
examples.english: Did you purify this gold in fire?

note: Inflected as nùchara; the verb applies especially to metals by fire.

examples.igbo: Ọ ghaghalịrị lee anya n'azụ.
examples.english: He turned round and looked back.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji na-eghaghalị n'ebe a?
examples.english: Why are you turning round here?

note: Inflected as ghaghalịrị and na-eghaghalị.

examples.igbo: Ọ ji mgbaàjàlà pịa nwa ya.
examples.english: He used a whip to flog his child.

examples.igbo: Mgbaàjàlà a ọ dị ogologo?
examples.english: Is this whip long?

examples.igbo: Ụlọ anyị dị n'ebe ọwụwa anyanwụ nke obodo.
examples.english: Our house is in the east of the town.

examples.igbo: Ị na-aga n'ebe ọwụwa anyanwụ ma ọ bụ n'ebe ọdịda anyanwụ?
examples.english: Are you going east or west?

examples.igbo: Ùlòdì na-acha ọcha n'ubi anyị.
examples.english: The ùlòdì lily is white in our farm.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ùlòdì ndị ahụ n'akụkụ osimiri?
examples.english: Did you see those ùlòdì lilies by the river?

note: Ùlòdì is a plant name I know only from wordlists; the sentences are plausible but I cannot fully vouch for the flower's everyday usage.

gloss: occupy another person's house or community; inhabit and occupy everywhere

examples.igbo: Ndị ọbịa bìchìrì ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: The visitors occupied our house.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ha ji abìchì obodo a?
examples.english: Why are they occupying this town?

examples.igbo: Onye ọzō ahụ bụ nna m.
examples.english: That ọzọ title holder is my father.

examples.igbo: Ị maara onye ọzō ọ bụla n'obodo a?
examples.english: Do you know any ọzọ title holder in this town?

examples.igbo: Ọ jụrụ àsè banyere ụlọ ahịa ahụ.
examples.english: He asked about that shop.

examples.igbo: Bịa jụọ àsè maka ọnụ ahịa ya.
examples.english: Come and ask about its price.

examples.igbo: Anyị bàkọtara n'ụlọ ya n'abalị.
examples.english: We entered his house together at night.

examples.igbo: Bàkọtanụ n'ụlọ tupu mmiri amalite.
examples.english: Enter the house together before the rain starts.

examples.igbo: Agbọ ọkụkọ ahụ na-acha mmanụ mmanụ.
examples.english: That chicken's colour is reddish orange.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ihe a ji acha mmanụ mmanụ?
examples.english: Why is this thing reddish orange?

examples.igbo: Anyị biliri n'òfufo chī.
examples.english: We woke at dawn.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-alọta tupu òfufo chī?
examples.english: Will you return before dawn?

examples.igbo: Ọ fụnyụrụ oriọna ahụ.
examples.english: He blew off the light.

examples.igbo: Fụnyụọ oriọna tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Blow off the light before you leave.

examples.igbo: Anyị rịgoro n'ụlọ elu site na ngōlō.
examples.english: We went up to the top floor by the elevator.

examples.igbo: Ngōlō nke ụlọ ahụ adịghị arụ ọrụ taa.
examples.english: The elevator in that building is not working today.

note: ngōlō is a modern borrowing; both sentences are idiomatic but the word is not in everyday rural use.

examples.igbo: Nne m na-emekata nri n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: My mother spends a long time cooking in the morning.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-emekata ọrụ ahụ ruo mgbede?
examples.english: Will you keep doing that work until evening?

note: mekata is uncommon; I have used the habitual/continuous form to bring out the 'for a long time' sense.

gloss: mask of the masquerader; masquerader's cloth

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ yikwasịrị àfe mmọọ pụọ n'ama.
examples.english: That man put on the masquerader's cloth and went out to the square.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-atụ egwu àfe mmọọ.
examples.english: The children are afraid of the masquerader's cloth.

examples.igbo: Anyị hụrụ kpakpaǹdo ūtụtù n'igwe tupu chi abọọ.
examples.english: We saw the morning star in the sky before dawn.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ kpakpaǹdo ūtụtù taa?
examples.english: Did you see the morning star today?

note: Kept the headword's spelling with macrons; the compound is rare in speech, where people often just say kpakpando.

gloss: do or make proper; repair; put right; mend; fix

examples.igbo: Ọ meziiri ụkwụ oche ahụ gbajiri agbaji.
examples.english: He repaired the broken leg of that chair.

examples.igbo: Mezie ụzọ ahụ tupu mmiri abịa.
examples.english: Fix that path before the rain comes.

examples.igbo: Ọrụ anyị na-eje ọfụma ugbua.
examples.english: Our work is going well now.

examples.igbo: Njem gị ọ na-eje ọfụma?
examples.english: Is your journey going well?

gloss: sacred tree (P. Beauv.) Seeman ex Bureau), (Newbouldia laevis much used as a live fence and commonly seen around shrines, especially of Agwù. A white cloth is often tied round its trunk as an offering. It is honoured as a divinity)

examples.igbo: Ha kụrụ ògilìsì gburugburu ụlọ arụsị ahụ.
examples.english: They planted ògilìsì trees around that shrine.

examples.igbo: Ndị obodo na-akwanyere ògilìsì ùgwù.
examples.english: The villagers respect the ògilìsì tree.

note: ògilìsì is known mainly in ritual/plant contexts; sentences are sound but the tree is not part of everyday speech for many speakers.

examples.igbo: Ndị ikom na-atụ òkwè n'okpuru osisi.
examples.english: The men are playing board games under the tree.

examples.igbo: Bịa ka anyị tụọ òkwè.
examples.english: Come so that we can play a board game.

examples.igbo: Ọ tụrụ ala ahụ site na mpàlà.
examples.english: He measured that land by strides.

examples.igbo: Mpàlà ole ka ọ dị n'etiti osisi abụọ a?
examples.english: How many strides is it between these two trees?

note: mpàlà as a unit of length is somewhat specialist; the sentences are natural but a learner may also hear nzọụkwụ.

examples.igbo: Oke ōchịchọ mere ka o zuru ego ahụ.
examples.english: Greed made him steal that money.

examples.igbo: Wepụ oke ōchịchọ n'obi gị.
examples.english: Remove greed from your heart.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-eme ùtụtù tupu ọ gaa ọrụ.
examples.english: He takes breakfast before going to work.

examples.igbo: Mee ùtụtù ngwa ngwa, anyị na-apụ ugbu a.
examples.english: Take breakfast quickly, we are leaving now.

examples.igbo: Teta, anyị ga-aga ahịa taa.
examples.english: Wake up, we will go to market today.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ tetara n'oge taa.
examples.english: That child woke up early today.

gloss: sit down carelessly and uninvited among a group

examples.igbo: Ọ nọwanyere anyị n'oche na-enweghị onye kpọrọ ya.
examples.english: He sat down uninvited among us on the bench.

examples.igbo: Nọwanye n'etiti anyị, anyị akpọghị gị.
examples.english: Sit down among us uninvited, we did not call you.

examples.igbo: O nyere nwa ya ibelibe ji.
examples.english: She gave her child a small piece of yam.

examples.igbo: Ibelibe anụ ahụ ọ fọdụrụ n'efere?
examples.english: Is that small piece of meat left in the plate?

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ kwafùrù mmiri n'ala.
examples.english: The child spilled water on the floor.

examples.igbo: Kwafù mmiri ọjọọ ahụ n'ime ọwa mmiri.
examples.english: Pour away that dirty water into the gutter.

examples.igbo: Ịhụ nkịta ahụ n'abalị bụ iru ọjọọ.
examples.english: Seeing that dog at night is a bad omen.

examples.igbo: Ndị obodo kwuru na ọ bụ iru ọjọọ.
examples.english: The village people said it is a bad omen.

examples.igbo: Mụta osè na ahịa taa.
examples.english: Buy pepper at the market today.

examples.igbo: Osè a na-ekpo ọkụ nke ukwuu.
examples.english: This pepper is very hot.

examples.igbo: Ndị ahịa ahụ kwalụrụ afịa ha gaa ebe ọzọ.
examples.english: Those traders packed and moved their wares to another place.

examples.igbo: Kwalụ afịa gị, ebe a adịghị mma.
examples.english: Pack and move your wares away, this place is not good.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-akpọ etùketù mgbe ọ risịrị nri.
examples.english: The child hiccoughs after eating.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akpọ etùketù, gwa ya ka ọ ṅụọ mmiri.
examples.english: He is hiccoughing, tell him to drink water.

examples.igbo: Onye ahụ lara ya ka ọ zụta ihe ahụ.
examples.english: That person enticed him to buy that thing.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ala m ka m kweta?
examples.english: Are you deceiving me to agree?

examples.igbo: Okwu ya mebọrọ m n’ihu ọha.
examples.english: His words embarrassed me in public.

examples.igbo: Ị na-achọ imebọ m?
examples.english: Are you trying to embarrass me?

examples.igbo: Ọ tụdara osisi ahụ n’ala.
examples.english: He threw that stick down.

examples.igbo: Tụdà ya n’ala!
examples.english: Throw it down!

examples.igbo: Ọ kụziiri ụmụaka ahụ Bekee.
examples.english: She taught those children English.

examples.igbo: Kụziere m ka e si akwa akwa.
examples.english: Teach me how to sew.

examples.igbo: Afọ m na-ederube.
examples.english: My stomach is rumbling.

examples.igbo: Égbè eluigwe na-ederube n’igwe.
examples.english: Thunder is rumbling in the sky.

examples.igbo: Ọ jelụrụ akwà ọhụrụ.
examples.english: She put on a new cloth.

examples.igbo: Jelụ akwà gị ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Put on your cloth quickly.

note: The verb is unfamiliar in some dialects; examples show the girding sense.

gloss: bulge, be distended (like the abdomen of a patient suffering from ascites, an overfed child, or a pregnant woman)

examples.igbo: Afọ ya tepụrụ.
examples.english: His stomach bulged.

examples.igbo: Afọ nwata ahụ na-etepụ.
examples.english: That child's stomach is bulging.

examples.igbo: Ọ tinyere mmanya n’ime ògbè mmānya.
examples.english: He put wine inside the wine calabash.

examples.igbo: Ògbè mmānya ahụ gbawara.
examples.english: That wine calabash broke.

gloss: movement, from one location to another, made on the knees, or hands and knees; crawl; crawling

examples.igbo: Nwa ọhụrụ ahụ amalitela igbē.
examples.english: That baby has started crawling.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-eme igbē n’ala.
examples.english: He is crawling on the ground.

examples.igbo: Òtuū Kraìst bụ okwukwe anyị.
examples.english: Christianity is our faith.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akụzi òtuū Kraìst n’ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: He teaches Christianity in school.

gloss: to deal with someone in a way that hurts them

examples.igbo: Ọ memìna nwa ya n'ihu ọha.
examples.english: He dealt with his child harshly in public.

examples.igbo: Memìna onye na-akparị gị n'ụzọ ọjọọ.
examples.english: Deal harshly with anyone who insults you.

examples.igbo: Eze nwere nnukwu òkikē n'ụlọ ya.
examples.english: The king has a big ivory tusk in his house.

examples.igbo: Òkikē a dị arọ nke ukwuu?
examples.english: Is this ivory tusk very heavy?

examples.igbo: Ọ kpọtụrụ Chineke n'ekpere tupu ọ rahụ.
examples.english: He called upon God in prayer before he slept.

examples.igbo: Kpọtụrụ m mgbe ị bịara n'ahịa.
examples.english: Call upon me when you come to the market.

examples.igbo: Èe'è, agaghị m abịa echi.
examples.english: No, I will not come tomorrow.

examples.igbo: Èe'è, gịnị mere ị ji jụ?
examples.english: No, why did you refuse?

gloss: grow; be long, tall (of living thing)

examples.igbo: Nwa ya na-eso ùso ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Her child is growing tall quickly.

examples.igbo: Osisi a soro ùso n'afọ a?
examples.english: Did this tree grow tall this year?

examples.igbo: Nne m na-ese nni n'ụtụtụ ọ bụla.
examples.english: My mother stirs pap every morning.

examples.igbo: Sè nni ahụ nke ọma tupu ọ gbaa.
examples.english: Stir that food well before it thickens.

examples.igbo: Ọ tara ịta n'egwuregwu bọọlụ.
examples.english: He won stakes in the football game.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-ata ịta n'asọmpi echi?
examples.english: Will you win stakes in tomorrow's competition?

gloss: the twelfth letter of the Igbo language alphabet; the third vowel of the Igbo language alphabet

examples.igbo: Aha m nwere 'i' abụọ.
examples.english: My name has two 'i's.

examples.igbo: Kpọọ 'i' n'olu doro anya.
examples.english: Pronounce 'i' clearly.

examples.igbo: Gawaga n'ihu, ị ga-ahụ ụlọ ahụ.
examples.english: Go straight on, you will see that house.

examples.igbo: Anyị gawagara n'okporo ụzọ ahụ ruo ahịa.
examples.english: We went straight on that road to the market.

gloss: welcome! (greeting to visitors or to someone passed on the way)

examples.igbo: Ǹnọò, bata n'ime ụlọ anyị.
examples.english: Welcome, come into our house.

examples.igbo: Ǹnọò, kedu ka ị mere taa?
examples.english: Welcome, how are you today?

examples.igbo: Akụkọ ifo na-akọ banyere ònwùnwò mmadụ ka ọ ghọọ anụ ọhịa.
examples.english: Folktales tell of a person's transformation into a wild animal.

examples.igbo: Ị hụtụla ònwùnwò dị otú a na ndụ gị?
examples.english: Have you ever seen such a transformation in your life?

note: Ònwùnwò is rare; the sentences are plausible but a speaker might prefer a different verb with this noun.

examples.igbo: Ndapụ̀ akwụkwọ osisi na-eme n'oge ọkọchị.
examples.english: The falling off of leaves happens in the dry season.

examples.igbo: Òle mgbe ka ndapụ̀ akwụkwọ osisi na-amalite?
examples.english: When does the falling off of leaves begin?

note: ndapụ̀ as a noun of the falling-off event is slightly bookish but understood.

gloss: earth; trodden clay; building mud; sand

examples.igbo: Ndị ọrụ na-agwakọta ajā na mmiri eji ewu ụlọ.
examples.english: The workers mix earth with water for building a house.

examples.igbo: Ajā dị n'ụkwụ gị niile, gaa sacha ya.
examples.english: There is sand all over your feet, go and wash it off.

examples.igbo: Enyì nwaàyì ya bịara ileta ya n'ụlọ.
examples.english: Her woman friend came to visit her at home.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eso enyì nwaàyì gị gaa ahịa taa?
examples.english: Will you go to the market with your woman friend today?

examples.igbo: N'ùruluchī, anyị na-anọdụ n'èzí na-akọ akụkọ.
examples.english: In the evening, we sit outside telling stories.

examples.igbo: Bịa n'ụlọ tupu ùruluchī ada.
examples.english: Come home before dusk falls.

examples.igbo: Òsi ìtè ahụ na-esi nri ọma.
examples.english: That cook prepares good food.

examples.igbo: Òsi ìtè, olee mgbe nri ga-adị njikere?
examples.english: Cook, when will the food be ready?

gloss: severe dysmenorrhoea (painful menstruation) which occurs mostly in young women; in severe cases leaves the patient prostrate, and can be disabling

examples.igbo: Ajì enyī na-akpata mgbu n'afọ ụmụ agbọghọ.
examples.english: Severe dysmenorrhoea causes pain in the belly of young women.

examples.igbo: Gaa hụ dọkịta ma ajì enyī na-egbu gị mgbe ọ bụla.
examples.english: Go and see a doctor if the severe dysmenorrhoea pains you every time.

note: The term is specialist; the sentences are respectful and idiomatic but a healer might phrase the cause differently.

gloss: take someone inside a house or a designated place

examples.igbo: Kpọbà ya n'ime ụlọ ka mmiri ghara ịzọ ya.
examples.english: Take him inside so the rain will not beat him.

examples.igbo: Ọ kpọbàrọ anyị n'ime ụlọ ya.
examples.english: He took us inside his house.

examples.igbo: Mama mere ji okō eghe n'abalị ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: Mother made fried plantain last night.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-azụta ji okō n'ahịa taa?
examples.english: Will you buy plantain in the market today?

gloss: herb (for the preparation of native medicine)

examples.igbo: Ọ na-achịkọta afịfịa ọgwụ n'ọhịa.
examples.english: He gathers herbs in the bush.

examples.igbo: Ị maara aha afịfịa ọgwụ a?
examples.english: Do you know the name of this herb?

examples.igbo: Ọ zụtara ìpètèrì ọhụrụ maka ọmụmụ ya.
examples.english: She bought a new maternity dress for her childbirth.

examples.igbo: Ìpètèrì a ọ̀ dị mma n'ahụ gị?
examples.english: Does this maternity dress look good on you?

examples.igbo: Onye òlìlì na-akụ ọkpọ n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: The town-crier beats the gong in the morning.

examples.igbo: Gee ntị n'ihe onye òlìlì na-ekwu.
examples.english: Listen to what the town-crier is saying.

examples.igbo: Ala anyị dị n'obosara.
examples.english: Our land is wide.

examples.igbo: Osimiri ahụ ọ̀ dị n'obosara?
examples.english: Is that river wide?

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ òfu afù ka m hụrụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: It was that very one I saw in the market.

examples.igbo: Nye m òfu afù, ọ bụghị nke ọzọ.
examples.english: Give me that very one, not the other.

examples.igbo: Ụmū ìgòsì na-egwu egwu n'èzí.
examples.english: Young children are playing outside.

examples.igbo: Kpọkọta ụmū ìgòsì ka ha rie nri.
examples.english: Gather the young children so they can eat.

gloss: twenty-second letter of the Igbo language alphabet; eighteenth consonant of the Igbo language alphabet

examples.igbo: Nw bụ mkpụrụ okwu nke iri abụọ na abụọ n'asụsụ Igbo.
examples.english: Nw is the twenty-second letter in the Igbo language.

examples.igbo: Dee nw n'ime okwu 'nwa'.
examples.english: Write nw in the word 'nwa'.

note: Letter name; examples are metalinguistic.

examples.igbo: Ụmụ nnụnụ na-efe n'elu osisi.
examples.english: Birds are flying above the tree.

examples.igbo: Fee elu ka anyị hụ gị.
examples.english: Fly up so we can see you.

gloss: clear away weeds or bush; weed; deforest

examples.igbo: Anyị ga-asụcha ubi tupu oge ọkọchị.
examples.english: We will clear the farm before the dry season.

examples.igbo: Sụchaa ahịhịa dị n'ụzọ.
examples.english: Clear the weeds on the path.

gloss: gather separate things together (especially with the hands)

examples.igbo: Chịkọ mkpụrụ osisi ndị ahụ ọnụ.
examples.english: Gather those fruits together.

examples.igbo: O chịkọrọ ego ya niile n'otu ebe.
examples.english: He gathered all his money in one place.

examples.igbo: Àgwà ochīè na-eme n'ụbọchị ahịa.
examples.english: Old customs are practiced on market days.

examples.igbo: Ndị okenye na-echekwa àgwà ochīè n'obodo.
examples.english: Elders preserve old customs in the town.

examples.igbo: Ụlọ anyị na ụlọ ya dị nchelịta irū.
examples.english: Our house and his house are opposite each other.

examples.igbo: Ha nọ ọdụ nchelịta irū na tebụl.
examples.english: They sat facing each other at the table.

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ bụ onye èkwulèkwu.
examples.english: That man is a talkative.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ ịbụ onye èkwulèkwu?
examples.english: Do you want to be a talkative?

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ gbenatara n'ụlọ nne ya.
examples.english: That child crawled home to its mother.

examples.igbo: Gbenata n'ụlọ ozugbo!
examples.english: Crawl home at once!

examples.igbo: Òchịchịī kpuchiri obodo ahụ.
examples.english: Darkness covered that town.

examples.igbo: Banye n'ụlọ tupu òchịchịī abịa.
examples.english: Enter the house before darkness comes.

examples.igbo: O zoro n'azhi ugbo.
examples.english: He hid behind the door.

examples.igbo: Gaa lee n'azhi ugbo.
examples.english: Go and look behind the door.

examples.igbo: Ọ riri aka azụ n'ọrụ ya.
examples.english: He took a bribe at his work.

examples.igbo: Ndị uwe ojii ahụ na-eri aka azụ.
examples.english: Those policemen take bribes.

examples.igbo: Onye ànì m ka ọ bụ.
examples.english: He is my fellow countryman.

examples.igbo: Ị ma onye ànì gị n'ebe a?
examples.english: Do you know your fellow countryman here?

gloss: a liquid not being available on a surface or body it used to be in or on due to absorption or evaporation; dry up (liquid)

examples.igbo: Mmiri takọrọ n'ala ụlọ ahụ.
examples.english: The water dried up on that room's floor.

examples.igbo: Mmiri ọ takọrọ n'ahụ gị?
examples.english: Did the water dry off your body?

examples.igbo: Nwanne m bitere aka n'England.
examples.english: My brother lives far away in England.

examples.igbo: Ị bitere aka n'ebe a?
examples.english: Do you live far from here?

gloss: relieve need; satisfy want; suffice; be useful

examples.igbo: Ọrụ ugbo na-agbò mkpà ezinụlọ anyị.
examples.english: Farming meets our family's needs.

examples.igbo: Gịnị ga-agbò mkpà gị taa?
examples.english: What will meet your need today?

note: The idiom is common; I am slightly unsure of the exact tone marks on gbò mkpà.

examples.igbo: Ndị mmadụ zèdoro onwe ha n'ụlọ ụka.
examples.english: The people took shelter in the church.

examples.igbo: Zèdo onwe gị n'okpuru osisi a.
examples.english: Shelter yourself under this tree.

gloss: everybody; the public; force of public opinion

examples.igbo: Òrà na-ekwu okwu ya ugbu a.
examples.english: The public is talking about it now.

examples.igbo: Gịnị ka òrà na-ekwu maka ya?
examples.english: What is the public saying about it?

note: Òrà in the sense of 'the public' is a little bookish, but the sentences are idiomatic.

gloss: provoke to anger; annoy; enrage; make violently angry

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ kpasuru nne ya iwe.
examples.english: That child angered his mother.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpasuru gị iwe otú ahụ?
examples.english: What angered you like that?

examples.igbo: Ọ dara aka n'akpa ya wepụta ego.
examples.english: He laid hands on his bag and brought out money.

examples.igbo: Dà aka n'ọrụ gị ozugbo!
examples.english: Lay hands on your work immediately!

note: Ida aka has several shades; both sentences keep to the 'lay hands on' sense.

examples.igbo: Ị nà-àtụ ntụ, ahụghị m gị n'ụlọ ahụ.
examples.english: You are lying, I did not see you in that house.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji nà-àtụ ntụ?
examples.english: Why are you telling a lie?

headword: Onye a kpògbùlù n'obe -kpọ isi ànì

examples.igbo: Ndị Kraịst na-ekpere Onye a kpògbùlù n'obe.
examples.english: Christians pray to the Crucified.

examples.igbo: Onye a kpògbùlù n'obe bụ Onye Nzọpụta anyị.
examples.english: The Crucified is our Savior.

note: This is a religious title; the spelling of the whole phrase varies in texts.

gloss: carved iroko panel in door or wall

examples.igbo: O nyere àzụ ọjì n'ọnụ ụzọ ya.
examples.english: He fixed an iroko panel on his door.

examples.igbo: Ì hụrụ àzụ ọjì ahụ n'ọnụ ụzọ?
examples.english: Did you see that iroko panel on the door?

note: Àzụ ọjì is a rare, specialized term; the sense given is the one used here.

examples.igbo: O kwuchiri ọnụ ụzọ ụlọ ya.
examples.english: He closed the door of his house.

examples.igbo: Kwùchie ọnụ ụzọ ahụ ozugbo!
examples.english: Close that door immediately!

examples.igbo: Ọrụ ya bụ izùto ụmụaka n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: His job is to train children at school.

examples.igbo: Ònye na-azùto ụmụaka n'ụlọ akwụkwọ a?
examples.english: Who trains the children in this school?

note: Zùto is easily confused with zụta 'buy', so I used only progressive/infinitive forms.

gloss: a native doctor who specializes in divination

examples.igbo: Dibìà afā gwara ya ihe ga-eme.
examples.english: The diviner told him what would happen.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-aga dibìà afā maka nsogbu a?
examples.english: Will you go to the diviner about this problem?

examples.igbo: Anụ ugbokō anaghị ege ntị mgbe a na-akụziri ya ihe.
examples.english: A stupid uncivilized person does not listen when being taught.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji akpọ nwanne m anụ ugbokō?
examples.english: Why do you call my sibling a stupid uncivilized person?

examples.igbo: O dina n'àkwà edinà ya na-ezu ike.
examples.english: He lies on his bed resting.

examples.igbo: Nkịta na-ehi ụra n'okpuru àkwà edinà.
examples.english: The dog sleeps under the bed.

examples.igbo: Gịgàdo aka nwa ahụ ka ị ghara ime ya mgbu.
examples.english: Hold that child's hand lightly so you don't hurt him.

examples.igbo: O gịgàdoro aka nwa ya mgbe ha gafere okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: She held her child's hand lightly when they crossed the road.

examples.igbo: Ụdọ ewu ahụ tụfìkọrọ n'ime ọhịa.
examples.english: That goat's rope got entangled in the bush.

examples.igbo: Lezie anya ka eriri ndị a ghara ịtụfìkọ.
examples.english: Be careful so these ropes do not get entangled.

examples.igbo: Ọrụ ugbo bà n'ịfe nye ezinụlọ anyị.
examples.english: Farming is beneficial to our family.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụrụ na ọ bàghị n'ịfe, gịnị mere i ji zụta ya?
examples.english: If it is not useful, why did you buy it?

examples.igbo: Nekpọ anya n'ihe a tupu ị zụta ya.
examples.english: Take a good look at this thing before you buy it.

examples.igbo: O nekpọrọ anya n'ihu ya iji mara ma ọ dị mma.
examples.english: She took a good look at his face to know if he was okay.

examples.igbo: Mmụọ ijelè pụtara n'ọha, ọ na-agba egwu mara mma.
examples.english: The ijele masquerade appeared in public, dancing beautifully.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-atụ egwu mmụọ ijelè?
examples.english: Are the children afraid of the ijele masquerade?

gloss: moving rapidly past, creating a current of air

examples.igbo: Ụgbọala ahụ kùfèrè n'akụkụ anyị.
examples.english: That car sped rapidly past beside us.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kùfèrè n'azụ gị?
examples.english: What sped rapidly past behind you?

gloss: be far away, at a distance; stay away long

examples.igbo: Ụlọ ya nòtèrè aka n'ahịa.
examples.english: His house is far from the market.

examples.igbo: Nòtè aka n'ebe ahụ, ọ dị ize ndụ.
examples.english: Stay away from there; it is dangerous.

examples.igbo: Nwa agbọghọ ahụ na-azụ ọkụkọ n’ụlọ.
examples.english: That girl raises chickens at home.

examples.igbo: Nwa agbọghọ, kedu ebe ị na-aga?
examples.english: Girl, where are you going?

examples.igbo: Ọ rukwàsịrị mmiri n’isi m.
examples.english: He poured water upon my head.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ka ọ rukwàsị nnu n’ofe ahụ.
examples.english: Don’t let him pour salt upon that soup.

note: Tone marking on the inflected verb is uncertain.

gloss: filter (of fibre-sponge, ògbo); tow-like filter (compare ǹzà, gauze filter) (from -zà 2. filter)

examples.igbo: O ji òzà zọọ mmanya tupu ọ ṅụọ ya.
examples.english: She used a filter to strain the wine before drinking it.

examples.igbo: Òzà a adịghị ọcha; sachaa ya.
examples.english: This filter is not clean; wash it.

note: The specific traditional filter sense is specialized.

examples.igbo: Ndị agha ahụ nyere ìkwù n’akụkụ osimiri.
examples.english: The soldiers encamped by the riverside.

examples.igbo: Nye ìkwù n’ebe a, anyị agaghị aga n’ihu.
examples.english: Encamp here, we will not go further.

note: The phrase is uncommon; examples are plausible but not certain.

examples.igbo: Papa m na-akpọwa nkụ n’ọhịa.
examples.english: My father is splitting firewood in the bush.

examples.igbo: Kpọwaa achara ahụ ka anyị kee ya.
examples.english: Split that bamboo so we can tie it.

examples.igbo: Ọ dara ọrịa, nya kpàtàlù ọ ghị akwụkwọ.
examples.english: He fell sick; therefore he did not go to school.

examples.igbo: Oké mmiri na-ezo, nya kpàtàlù anyị agaghị aga ahịa.
examples.english: Heavy rain is falling; therefore we will not go to market.

note: The connector is dialectal or less common in everyday modern Igbo.

examples.igbo: Èèye, m ga-abịa echi.
examples.english: Yes, I will come tomorrow.

examples.igbo: Èèye, ọ bụ m nyere ya ego ahụ.
examples.english: Certainly, it was I who gave him that money.

examples.igbo: Àhaà! Ị bịara ọzọ!
examples.english: Aha! You came again!

examples.igbo: Àhaà! Nke a bụ ihe iju anya!
examples.english: Aha! This is surprising!

examples.igbo: Ùkọ mmiri na-enye anyị nsogbu n’oge ọkọchị.
examples.english: Water scarcity troubles us in the dry season.

examples.igbo: Ùkọ nri ọ dị n’obodo gị ugbua?
examples.english: Is there food scarcity in your town now?

examples.igbo: Nwatakịrị ahụ gbajere nne ya n’ụlọ.
examples.english: The child ran to his mother in the house.

examples.igbo: Gbajee m ngwa ngwa!
examples.english: Run to me quickly!
