note: The macron/tone on the stem is not fully reflected in inflected forms.

examples.igbo: Wèrè nkata ahụ nye m ya.
examples.english: Take that basket and give it to me.

examples.igbo: O wèrè ego gaa ahịa.
examples.english: She took money and went to market.

examples.igbo: Nwa mkpìlìkpì ahụ enweghị ike iru elu tebụl.
examples.english: That tiny child cannot reach the table top.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ nwa mkpìlìkpì n’etiti ụmụaka?
examples.english: Did you see the tiny one among the children?

note: The word is uncommon; sentences show it as a noun for a very small or short person.

examples.igbo: Ha kàghalịrị nzukọ ahụ ruo echi.
examples.english: They postponed that meeting until tomorrow.

examples.igbo: Kàghalịa mgbidi ahụ ka ọ dị mma.
examples.english: Fix that wall again so it is good.

note: Postpone and re-fix are both covered; the re-fix use is less common in some areas.

examples.igbo: Òkelekwū bara n’ọba.
examples.english: A rat entered the barn.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ òkelekwū n’ụlọ?
examples.english: Did you see a rat in the house?

note: The spelling with tone marks is less familiar; the sense as rat is clear.

examples.igbo: Oké ifufe tisara ụlọ ahụ.
examples.english: The strong wind tore that house apart.

examples.igbo: Tisaa osisi ahụ tupu anyị ewere ya rụọ ọrụ.
examples.english: Break that wood apart before we use it for work.

note: The verb is not common in everyday speech, but these uses match separation by destruction.

examples.igbo: O richapụrụ efere niile.
examples.english: She cleansed all the plates.

examples.igbo: Richapụa mmiri ahụ tupu ị ṅụọ ya.
examples.english: Purify that water before you drink it.

examples.igbo: O nwere ọgwù akā n’mkpịsị aka ya.
examples.english: He has whitlow on his finger.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ọgwù akā dị n’aka ya?
examples.english: Did you see the whitlow on his hand?

note: The term is understood as whitlow; the exact tone on akā may vary by speaker.

examples.igbo: Anyanwụ kọrọ mmīrī n’ọdọ ahụ.
examples.english: The sun dried up the water in that stream.

examples.igbo: Kọọ mmīrī n’ime ite ahụ tupu i tinye mmanụ.
examples.english: Dry the water in that pot before you put oil.

note: The verb kọ with mmiri is somewhat specialised; these sentences show drying of liquid.

examples.igbo: Nna m kwuru na ọ hụrụ ùwà ndị mmọọ n’ụra.
examples.english: My father said he saw the spirit world in a dream.

examples.igbo: Ùwà ndị mmọọ dị iche na ụwa anyị?
examples.english: Is the spirit world different from our world?

note: The phrase is clear, though it is not an everyday conversational item.

examples.igbo: Onye ọka ikpe dọkọrọ akwụkwọ ahụ.
examples.english: The judge dismissed the case.

examples.igbo: Dọkaa akwụkwọ ahụ ozugbo.
examples.english: Dismiss the case immediately.

gloss: break off; cut off; chop off; (with knife, matchet)

examples.igbo: O jiri mma gbujipụ alaka osisi ahụ.
examples.english: He used a knife to cut off that tree branch.

examples.igbo: Gbujipụ alaka ahụ ozugbo.
examples.english: Cut off that branch immediately.

examples.igbo: Ndị uwe ojii bichiri ụzọ ahụ.
examples.english: The police blocked that road.

examples.igbo: Bichie ụzọ ahụ!
examples.english: Block that road!

examples.igbo: Ha manyere ya ịga ahịa.
examples.english: They forced him to go to the market.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji amanye nwa gị?
examples.english: Why are you forcing your child?

examples.igbo: Àkụlō na-eto n'akụkụ mmiri.
examples.english: Àkụlō grows near water.

examples.igbo: I hụrụ àkụlō n'ọhịa?
examples.english: Did you see àkụlō in the bush?

note: Selaginella is not a common everyday word; the examples are simple and plausible but not from frequent speech.

examples.igbo: Anyị ji otu unit ọkụ eletrik.
examples.english: We use one unit of electricity.

examples.igbo: Ego ole bụ otu unit?
examples.english: How much is one unit?

gloss: bumps which appear on the skin as reflex to cold, emotional trigger, or fright; goosebumps

examples.igbo: Oyi na-atụ m, akpatooyī pụtara n'ahụ m.
examples.english: I am feeling cold, goosebumps appeared on my body.

examples.igbo: Lee akpatooyī n'ahụ ya!
examples.english: Look at the goosebumps on his body!

gloss: do as, be a young woman

examples.igbo: Nwa agbọghọ ahụ na-eme àgbọò.
examples.english: That girl is acting as a young woman.

examples.igbo: Oge ruru ka ọ malite ime àgbọò.
examples.english: The time has come for her to start being a young woman.

note: I am not fully certain of the exact idiomatic range of -me àgbọò; the sentences are an attempt but may need a native speaker's check.

examples.igbo: Anyị ga-ekebi ego ahụ n'akụkụ abụọ.
examples.english: We will divide that money into two parts.

examples.igbo: Kebie achịcha ahụ maka ụmụaka.
examples.english: Divide that bread for the children.

examples.igbo: Onye na-akwa akwa na-acha akwà.
examples.english: The tailor cuts cloth.

examples.igbo: Chàa akwà a ka anyị kwaa uwe.
examples.english: Cut this cloth so we can sew a dress.

examples.igbo: Pòtòki ahụ na-azụ ahịa n'ọdụ ụgbọ mmiri.
examples.english: That Portuguese man trades at the seaport.

examples.igbo: Ị hụla pòtòki ọ bụla n'obodo a?
examples.english: Have you seen any Portuguese person in this town?

examples.igbo: O were ǹzùròkè ụbọchị atọ rụọ ọrụ ahụ.
examples.english: He spent a whole three days doing that work.

examples.igbo: Ị gụtara ǹzùròkè ego ahụ niile?
examples.english: Did you count the whole of that money?

note: The exact range of ǹzùròkè is not fully clear to me; I used it in the sense of 'entire/whole'.

gloss: tire completely (make body soft, weak, like pap)

examples.igbo: Ọrụ ubi gbèrè m àrụ taa.
examples.english: Farm work tired me out completely today.

examples.igbo: Gịnị gbèrè gị àrụ otú a?
examples.english: What tired you out completely like this?

gloss: calabash (= derived from Yoruba igbá; compare ọbà)

examples.igbo: Ọ wụsara mmiri n'ụgbā.
examples.english: She poured water into the calabash.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara ụgbā ọhụrụ n'ahịa?
examples.english: Did you buy a new calabash at the market?

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka ahụ na-agba àghalā n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: Those children are making trouble at school.

examples.igbo: Unu agbala àghalā n'ebe a!
examples.english: Don't be disorderly here!

gloss: be narrow, tight, pressed together, choked, crowded; restrict;

examples.igbo: Ụgbọ ala ahụ kpàrị àkpà n'ụtụtụ a.
examples.english: That bus was crowded this morning.

examples.igbo: Uwe a ọ kpàrị gị àkpà?
examples.english: Is this dress tight on you?

examples.igbo: O ji ibe nkū rụọ oche.
examples.english: He used a plank to make a stool.

examples.igbo: Bute ibe nkū abụọ n'ụlọ ọrụ.
examples.english: Carry two planks to the workshop.

gloss: build; construct or erect, especially a building

examples.igbo: Ha wuru ụlọ ọhụrụ n'afọ a.
examples.english: They built a new house this year.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-ewu ụlọ gị n'afọ a?
examples.english: Will you build your house this year?

gloss: go to; towards Achò m ije kwu nnà m I want to go to my father

examples.igbo: Achọrọ m ijekwu nne m n'ahịa.
examples.english: I want to go to my mother at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-ajekwu nna gị taa?
examples.english: Will you go to your father today?

gloss: break off a fragment Nyàpelụ nwantịntị àchìchà tàa Break off a small piece of biscuit and eat

examples.igbo: Nyàpelụ m ntà àchìchà.
examples.english: Break off a small piece of biscuit for me.

examples.igbo: Ọ nyàpelụrụ nwa ya ntà àchìchà.
examples.english: She broke off a small piece of biscuit for her child.

note: Inflection of the verb stem may vary; I used imperative and past forms.

examples.igbo: Ọ nwere ife mgbu n'ụkwụ ya.
examples.english: He has an ailment in his leg.

examples.igbo: Gịnị bụ ife mgbu na-akpagbu gị?
examples.english: What is the ailment troubling you?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-azùzù azụ̀ nwa ya.
examples.english: She is massaging her child's back.

examples.igbo: Zùzù m ụkwụ m, biko.
examples.english: Massage my leg for me, please.

note: The reduplicated stem's inflection is uncertain; I used na-azùzù and imperative zùzù.

examples.igbo: Ọ gọrọ agụ̀gọ na ya erighị anụ ahụ.
examples.english: He denied eating that meat.

examples.igbo: Ị na-agọ agụ̀gọ na ị hụghị ya?
examples.english: Are you denying that you saw him?

note: The phrase's exact inflection is assumed to follow standard patterns.

examples.igbo: Ọ dụrụ m aka na agịga.
examples.english: She pricked my hand with a needle.

examples.igbo: Dụ akwa a ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Sew this cloth quickly.

gloss: give back (= -nyechìgha) Ị   nyechìatago yā akwụkwọ yā? Have you given him his book back?

examples.igbo: Nyechìata m ego m.
examples.english: Give me back my money.

examples.igbo: Anyị nyechìatara ya akwụkwọ ya.
examples.english: We gave him back his book.

examples.igbo: Nne m nọ n'ebe a nà-èsi nnī.
examples.english: My mother is in the kitchen.

examples.igbo: Ebe a nà-èsi nnī dị ọcha.
examples.english: The kitchen is clean.

examples.igbo: Ogbènyà na-egbu ndị obodo a.
examples.english: Poverty is killing the people of this town.

examples.igbo: Ogbènyà dị n'obodo ha?
examples.english: Is there poverty in their town?

note: Chose the 'poverty' sense; other senses possible.

examples.igbo: Ọ dị n'isi anyị ilekọta nne anyị.
examples.english: It is our responsibility to care for our mother.

examples.igbo: Ọ dị n'isi gị ịzụ nwa a?
examples.english: Is it your responsibility to raise this child?

examples.igbo: O nwere obī ebele, o nyere m ego.
examples.english: He is kind-hearted, he gave me money.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere obī ebele?
examples.english: Are you kind-hearted?

gloss: take a title; take ọzọ title (literally take honour);

examples.igbo: Ọ chiri ọzọ n’obodo ya afọ gara aga.
examples.english: He took the ọzọ title in his town last year.

examples.igbo: Chie ọzọ ka ndị obodo gị kwanyere gị ùgwù.
examples.english: Take the ọzọ title so your townspeople will respect you.

gloss: yam medicine, obtained from Nri by surrounding peoples

examples.igbo: Ndị Agbaja na-aga Nri ịzụta ọgwụ ji.
examples.english: The Agbaja people go to Nri to buy yam medicine.

examples.igbo: Ọgwụ ji na-eme ka ji mịa nke ọma n’ubi.
examples.english: Yam medicine makes yams do well in the farm.

examples.igbo: Okēlụwà ya bụ ịbụ onye ọrụ ugbo.
examples.english: His fate was to be a farmer.

examples.igbo: Ọ dịghị onye pụrụ ịgbanwe okēlụwà ya.
examples.english: No one can change his fate.

examples.igbo: Ndị ọrụ ugbo na-akọ ji n’ànì olū mgbe mmiri lara.
examples.english: Farmers plant yams on overflowed land when the water recedes.

examples.igbo: Ànì olū anyị na-enye nri ọma n’afọ a.
examples.english: Our overflowed land is giving good crops this year.

examples.igbo: Anyị koniri n’isi ụtụtụ gaa ahịa.
examples.english: We set out early in the morning to the market.

examples.igbo: Koni n’ụzọ ugbu a ka ị ghara ịbịa n’azụ.
examples.english: Start on the journey now so you do not arrive late.

examples.igbo: Nkọtọ bụ nnukwu eju a na-eri eri.
examples.english: Nkọtọ is a big snail that is eaten.

examples.igbo: Anyị hụrụ nkọtọ n’ọhịa taa.
examples.english: We saw a nkọtọ in the bush today.

gloss: thousands upon thousands; million(s) Nnù kwùlu nnù ndi be ānyị nà-èje Òbòdò Oyìbo kwà arò Thousands of our people go to Europe each year

examples.igbo: Nnù kwùlu nnù mmadụ bịara emume ahụ.
examples.english: Thousands upon thousands of people came to that ceremony.

examples.igbo: Nnù kwùlu nnù ụmụ akwụkwọ na-aga ụlọ akwụkwọ anyị.
examples.english: Thousands upon thousands of students attend our school.

examples.igbo: Uwe a pekara m nke ukwuu.
examples.english: This dress is too small for me.

examples.igbo: Ihe ị na-enye nwa ahụ pekara.
examples.english: What you are giving that child is too small.

gloss: fragment, small piece, stump (of something long, e.g. snake, yam, etc.)

examples.igbo: Ọ fọdụrụ naanị mkpìlìkpì ji n’ite.
examples.english: Only a small piece of yam remained in the pot.

examples.igbo: E ji mkpìlìkpì osisi mee ọkụ.
examples.english: They used tree stumps to make fire.

examples.igbo: Ogwu aka na-egbu nwa ahụ mgbu.
examples.english: Whitlow is paining that child.

examples.igbo: Ọ nwere ogwu aka n’isi mkpịsị aka ya.
examples.english: He has whitlow on his fingertip.

gloss: be light in colour; change colour; fade; be bloodless (of person)

examples.igbo: Uwe ọhụrụ ahụ chaghalịrị mgbe m sachara ya.
examples.english: That new dress faded when I washed it.

examples.igbo: Nwa gị chaghalịrị dị ka gị?
examples.english: Is your child light-skinned like you?

note: Sense covers both fading and light complexion; sentences show both.

gloss: dry up; shrivel; wither Ọ bụlụ nà ị gbārọ òdòdo diCníru iìlo mmiliì ọ gà-àkpọnwụ If you do not water the flowering plant in front of the house it will wither

examples.igbo: Osisi ọka m kụrụ akpọnwụla n'ihi okpomọkụ.
examples.english: The maize plant I planted has withered because of the heat.

examples.igbo: Nye akwụkwọ nri ahụ mmiri tupu ha akpọnwụ.
examples.english: Water those vegetables before they wither.

examples.igbo: Anụrụ m olu nne m n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: I heard my mother's voice inside the room.

examples.igbo: Ị nụrụ ụda mgbịrịgba ụtụtụ a?
examples.english: Did you hear the sound of the bell this morning?

gloss: consider; take counsel; consult together; advise; confer; exchange opinions or have a conversation

examples.igbo: Anyị tịkọrọ isi tupu anyị zụta ala ahụ.
examples.english: We consulted together before we bought that land.

examples.igbo: Tịkọ isi gị na ndị ezinụlọ gị tupu i mee mkpebi.
examples.english: Consult with your family before you make a decision.

gloss: be initiated into the masqueraders' cult (and learn its secrets)

examples.igbo: Nna ya mara mmụọ mgbe ọ dị obere.
examples.english: His father was initiated into the masquerade cult when he was young.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ ọ maala mmụọ?
examples.english: Has that child been initiated into the masquerade cult?

gloss: hook attached to window to keep it steady and prevent the glass from being shattered by the wind

examples.igbo: Kee ǹkò ụzò ajā ahụ nke ọma ka ifufe ghara imeghe ya.
examples.english: Fix that window hook well so the wind will not open it.

examples.igbo: Ǹkò ụzò ajā gbawara agbawa, anyị zụrụ nke ọhụrụ.
examples.english: The window hook broke, so we bought a new one.

note: Uncommon technical term; the two sentences keep the window-hook sense.

gloss: entirely; completely Alụ chago m  ọlụ afù kpamkpàm I have finished the work completely

examples.igbo: Anyị rụchara ọrụ ahụ kpamkpàm.
examples.english: We finished that work completely.

examples.igbo: Ị riri nri ahụ kpamkpàm?
examples.english: Did you eat that food completely?

examples.igbo: Ògwùgwù na-atọ ụmụaka ụtọ n'oge okpomọkụ.
examples.english: Swimming pleases children in the hot season.

examples.english: Do you know how to swim?

examples.english: They made him king in their town.

examples.english: When will he become king?

examples.english: That king wore a crown on the day of the ceremony.

gloss: one heart; (fig.) unanimity, co-operation, agreement, unity

examples.english: We are of one heart in this farm work.

examples.igbo: Òfu obì ọ dị n'etiti unu?
examples.english: Is there unity among you?

examples.english: Will the capital given to him be enough to buy goods?

note: The phrase is literal ('money given to him'); examples keep that form.

examples.igbo: Chee ntì mgbe m na-ekwu.
examples.english: Listen when I am talking.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-eche ntì na redio n'abalị.
examples.english: He listens to the radio at night.

examples.igbo: Ọgbòdògbò gị ọ na-egbu mgbu?

examples.english: He uses a tobacco pipe to smoke.

examples.igbo: Were ọkụ ụtaba a nye nna gị.
examples.english: Take this tobacco pipe and give it to your father.

note: Used the pipe sense; the headword's macron is not repeated in standard spelling here.

examples.igbo: Ǹtù akā na-egbu ya mgbu n'aka.
examples.english: Whitlow is paining him in the hand.

examples.igbo: Ị na-etinye ọgwụ n'ǹtù akā?
examples.english: Are you applying medicine to the whitlow?

gloss: a speech in which successive phrases or words are arranged in ascending order of importance; climax

examples.igbo: Okwu ya nwere orurughookwū.
examples.english: His speech had a climax.

examples.igbo: O ji orurughookwū mee ka akụkọ ahụ dị ụtọ.
examples.english: He used climax to make the story interesting.

note: Rare rhetorical term; examples are constructed but follow the given sense.

examples.igbo: Kòni enū akwa ahụ n'ụlọ.

examples.igbo: O kòniri enū akpa ya n'ahụ mgbidi.
examples.english: He hung his bag on the wall.

note: Inflection of the stem follows the given form, but the verb is not common in my active vocabulary.

examples.igbo: Ha na-alụ ọlụ n'ugbo.
examples.english: They work on the farm.

examples.igbo: Lụọ ọlụ gị nke ọma.
examples.english: Do your work well.

note: Standard modern Igbo more often uses 'rụ ọrụ'; these examples follow the entry's form.

examples.english: Write a letter to me, please.

examples.english: She uses a small mortar to grind pepper.

examples.english: Buy a new small mortar at the market.

examples.english: Is this river shallow?

gloss: drool; drop saliva from of the mouth uncontrollably

examples.igbo: O bugara nne ya nri n'ụlọ ọgwụ.
examples.english: He carried food to his mother at the hospital.

gloss: spoil with poor upbringing; train badly; raise poorly

examples.igbo: Ọ zụtọrọ ụmụ ya.
examples.english: She raised her children badly.

examples.igbo: Zụtọọla nwa ahụ.
examples.english: Don't raise that child badly.

examples.igbo: Anyị riri àzamà na ji n'ehihie.
examples.english: We ate beans and yam in the afternoon.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara àzamà n'ahịa taa?
examples.english: Did you buy beans at the market today?

examples.igbo: Odogwu òzàlà tara nwa m n'aka.
examples.english: A scorpion stung my child on the hand.

examples.igbo: Gbuo odogwu òzàlà ahụ tupu ọ taa gị.
examples.english: Kill that scorpion before it stings you.

examples.igbo: Osisi mango m kpọrọ īfūrū n'afọ a.
examples.english: My mango tree blossomed this year.

examples.igbo: Osisi ubé a kpọrọ īfūrū?
examples.english: Has this pear tree blossomed?

note: The verb phrase is likely correct, but tone-marked spelling may vary in modern usage.

examples.igbo: M wụchara àrụ m n'ụtụtụ taa.
examples.english: I washed my body this morning.

examples.igbo: Wụchaa àrụ gị nke ọma tupu ị lakpuo.
examples.english: Wash your body well before you sleep.

examples.igbo: Akwụkọ ahụ dàbepụrụ n'osisi.
examples.english: That fruit fell off the tree.

examples.igbo: Kpachara anya ka akwụkwọ ahụ ghara ịdàbepụ.
examples.english: Be careful so that leaf does not fall off.

note: The stem is clear, but the past/infinitive forms may have dialectal variation.

gloss: be wise; be sensible; have wisdom

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ nwere àkọnùuchè.
examples.english: That child is wise.

examples.igbo: Nwee àkọnùuchè, kpachara anya n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: Be wise, be careful on the road.

examples.igbo: Ọkụ nwulàpụrụ n'eluigwe n'abalị.
examples.english: Lightning flashed in the sky at night.

examples.igbo: Lelee ka ọkụ si anwulàpụ n'èzí.
examples.english: Look at how the light flashes outside.

note: The verb sense is clear, but inflectional spelling may vary.

examples.igbo: Ọkụkọ ndị ahụ na-ehi ụra n'ùla ōkụkò.
examples.english: Those fowls sleep in the fowl-house.

examples.igbo: Mechie ọnụ ụzọ ùla ōkụkò tupu chi ejie.
examples.english: Close the fowl-house door before dawn.

examples.igbo: Nne m na-akpa òkpùkpà isiì nke ọma.
examples.english: My mother plaits hair well.

examples.igbo: Òkpùkpà isiì a ọ dị mma?
examples.english: Is this hair plaiting nice?

note: The phrase is understood, but usage may be more specific than these examples show.

examples.igbo: Ndị uwe ojii na-achọ onye mere ògbugbu mmadù.
examples.english: The police are looking for the person who committed murder.

examples.igbo: Ògbugbu mmadù bụ nnukwu mmehie n'ala anyị.
examples.english: Murder is a great sin in our land.

examples.igbo: O nyere m nsụsù n'aka.
examples.english: He gave me a light jab on the arm.

examples.igbo: Nsụsù ahụ adịghị emerụ ahụ.
examples.english: That light jab does not hurt.

note: The noun sense is clear, but this word may be less common in everyday speech.

examples.igbo: O nyere m isi egō abụọ maka ọjị.
examples.english: He gave me two units of six cowries for the kola nut.

examples.igbo: I nwere isi egō ị ga-eji zụta azụ?
examples.english: Do you have a unit of six cowries to buy fish with?

note: The word is historical currency; sentences are idiomatic but the referent is not everyday.

examples.igbo: Okpokoro osisi ahụ dị òkòlòkọlọ.
examples.english: That piece of wood is round in shape.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ òkòlòkọlọ ka ọ dị ma ọ bụ ogologo?
examples.english: Is it round in shape or is it long?

examples.igbo: Nne m gwara anyị akọmakọ banyere njem ya.
examples.english: My mother told us a narrative about her journey.

examples.igbo: Kọọrọ anyị akọmakọ gbasara obodo gị.
examples.english: Tell us a narrative about your town.

examples.igbo: O jiri òsèkè gwuo olulu n'ubi.
examples.english: He dug a hole in the farm with a native spade.

examples.igbo: Ebee ka i tinyere òsèkè m?
examples.english: Where did you put my native spade?

examples.igbo: Anya ukwu ya mere ka ọ zuo ego ahụ.
examples.english: His greed made him steal that money.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere anya ukwu gị ji akpata gị nsogbu?
examples.english: Why does your greed keep bringing you trouble?

examples.igbo: O kwọlụrụ nwa ya n'azụ gawa ahịa.
examples.english: She carried her child on her back and went to the market.

examples.igbo: Kwọlụ nwa ahụ n'azụ ka ọ daa ụra.
examples.english: Carry that child on your back so he can sleep.

note: Inflected form written as kwọlụrụ; a speaker might also say kwọrọ.

examples.igbo: Nwa ọhụrụ ahụ lamiri ụla mgbe o riri ara.
examples.english: The baby fell fast asleep after suckling.

examples.igbo: Ị̀ lamiri ụla n'oge ọrụ?
examples.english: Did you fall fast asleep during work?

examples.igbo: O gbaziri ụmụ ya okwu n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: He advised his children in the morning.

examples.igbo: Biko gbazi m ma m mehiere ihe.
examples.english: Please correct me if I did something wrong.

note: Illustrates the advise/correct sense only.

examples.igbo: Àda èzè ahụ bịara obodo anyị ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: That princess came to our town yesterday.

examples.igbo: Ị hụla àda èzè n'obí eze?
examples.english: Have you seen the princess in the king's palace?

gloss: something wobbly, especially due to its softness

examples.igbo: Ji esiri esi dị ọyọ̀rị̀mà n'aka.
examples.english: The cooked yam feels wobbly in the hand.

examples.igbo: Ọ dị ọyọ̀rị̀mà, ya mere echere m na ọ ga-ada.
examples.english: It was wobbly, so I thought it would fall apart.

note: Word is uncommon; sentences kept to the soft, wobbly sense.

examples.igbo: Nwanne m nọrọ afọ abụọ n'òdịdọ n'agha.
examples.english: My brother was in wartime captivity for two years.

examples.igbo: Olee mgbe a ga-ahapụ ndị nọ n'òdịdọ n'agha?
examples.english: When will those held in wartime captivity be released?

note: The phrase is literary and rare in everyday speech; sentences build a clear wartime-captivity context.

gloss: compress; squeeze out, express (e.g. juice from a fruit); press together

examples.igbo: Pàa mmiri si n'oroma ahụ.
examples.english: Squeeze the juice out of that orange.

examples.igbo: Ọ napà mmiri si n'ahịhịa ọgwụ ahụ.
examples.english: She squeezes juice from that medicinal leaf.

note: The verb stem is uncommon in daily speech; inflections apà/napà and the imperative pàa are used.

examples.igbo: Ọ biri ego n'aka enyi ya ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: He borrowed money from his friend yesterday.

examples.igbo: Ị biri akwụkwọ a n'aka nwanne gị?
examples.english: Did you borrow this book from your brother?

gloss: open; uncover a cover, cork, or lid

examples.igbo: Kwughèe ite ahụ ka m hụ ihe dị n'ime.
examples.english: Open that pot so I can see what is inside.

examples.igbo: Onye kwughèrè ọnụ karama a?
examples.english: Who opened the mouth of this bottle?

note: kwùghè takes the suffix -e/-rè in these forms; some speakers use kwụghèe/kwụghèrè.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ nwere obodobo irū dịka nna ya.
examples.english: That child has a broad face like his father.

examples.igbo: Lee obodobo irū nwata ahụ!
examples.english: Look at that child's broad face!

note: obodobo irū is a descriptive compound rather than a frequent fixed phrase.

examples.igbo: Naịjirịa bụ ógbè Britain na mbụ.
examples.english: Nigeria was a British colony long ago.

examples.igbo: Mba ole n'Africa bụ ógbè France?
examples.english: How many countries in Africa are French colonies?

examples.igbo: Ụzọ ahụ nọrọ mmiri, kpachara anya.
examples.english: The road was slippery with water, be careful.

examples.igbo: Azụ ahụ nọrọ n'aka ya, o jideghị ya nke ọma.
examples.english: The fish was slimy in his hand, he did not hold it well.

note: The 'slimy, slippery' sense of -nọ is not one I can confirm confidently in modern usage; examples may not match actual idiom.

gloss: wake up; make alive; revive; refresh; resuscitate

examples.igbo: Tụte ndụ, oge eruola ịga ọrụ.
examples.english: Wake up, it is time to go to work.

examples.igbo: Dọkịta ahụ tụtere nwata ahụ ndụ.
examples.english: The doctor revived that child.

note: Both the 'wake up' and 'revive someone' uses are shown; the transitive form with ndụ is less common but understood.

gloss: custom (from -dị be ndi be in the home of people; compare òmenàànì)

examples.igbo: Ọdịbendi Igbo na-enye ndị okenye ugwu.
examples.english: Igbo custom gives respect to elders.

examples.igbo: Ọdịbendi ha dị iche na nke anyị?
examples.english: Is their custom different from ours?

examples.igbo: Mmìkolo bụ anụ na-eri oke ọhịa.
examples.english: A ferret is an animal that eats bush rats.

examples.igbo: Ị hụtụla mmìkolo na ndụ gị?
examples.english: Have you ever seen a ferret in your life?

note: The ferret is not a familiar animal in Igbo life, so the word is rare and the sentences are simply descriptive.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-atụ ụjọ̄ ịga ahịa.
examples.english: He is afraid to go to the market.

examples.igbo: Ị tụrụ ya ụjọ̄?
examples.english: Did you scare him?

examples.igbo: Ha na-agwù unyì n'ọhịa.
examples.english: They are mining coal in the forest.

examples.igbo: Gwuọ unyì n'ebe ahụ.
examples.english: Mine coal there.

note: Not completely sure of 'unyì' for coal; kept as given.

examples.igbo: O mahàrị ụlọ akwụkwọ taa.
examples.english: He skipped school today.

examples.igbo: Ị mahàrịrị nri ụtụtụ?
examples.english: Did you skip breakfast?

note: Past tense form uncertain; used 'mahàrị' and 'mahàrịrị'.

examples.igbo: Okwu nà ụkà adịghị mma.
examples.english: Quarrels are not good.

examples.igbo: Ị na-achọ okwu nà ụkà?
examples.english: Are you looking for trouble?

examples.igbo: O na-atụtù aka n'ahịa.
examples.english: He pilfers at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị tụtùrù aka n'ụlọ ahụ?
examples.english: Did you pilfer in that house?

note: Inflected forms uncertain; used 'tụtùrù'.

gloss: resist; stand in front of; block someone’s view; replace; stand in for

examples.igbo: O kwụchiri m n'ihu, apụghị m ịhụ ihe.
examples.english: He stood in front of me, I couldn't see.

examples.igbo: Kwụchie ya ka ọ ghara ịhụ anyị.
examples.english: Stand in front of him so he won't see us.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ nwere àkọ.
examples.english: That child has sense.

examples.igbo: Ị nweghị àkọ?
examples.english: Don't you have sense?

examples.igbo: Afọ ya tepùrù.
examples.english: His stomach is distended.

examples.igbo: Afọ gị ọ tepùrù?
examples.english: Is your stomach distended?

note: Past tense form uncertain; used 'tepùrù'.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ ife ūfụ ịnwụ nne.
examples.english: It is a painful thing to lose a mother.

examples.igbo: Gịnị bụ ife ūfụ ị na-ekwu?
examples.english: What is the painful thing you are saying?

gloss: activities associated with a particular tradition; rituals

examples.igbo: Àmànsi ezinụlọ anyị dị iche.
examples.english: Our family's rituals are different.

examples.igbo: Ị maara àmànsi nke ezinụlọ ha?
examples.english: Do you know their family's rituals?

examples.igbo: O mesiri ike rụọ ọrụ ahụ.
examples.english: He did that work energetically.

examples.igbo: Emesila m ike n'ihe a.
examples.english: Don't make me suffer over this matter.

examples.igbo: Ubi ya jupụtara ji òyìbò.
examples.english: His farm is full of yellow Guinea yam.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ere ji òyìbò n'ahịa?
examples.english: Are you selling yellow Guinea yam at the market?

examples.igbo: Nke ahụ bụ kpọmkwem ihe m chọrọ.
examples.english: That is exactly what I want.

examples.igbo: Gwa m kpọmkwem mgbe ụgbọ ahụ na-apụ.
examples.english: Tell me exactly when that vehicle leaves.

examples.igbo: Ifufe fepụrụ akwụkwọ m n'aka.
examples.english: The wind blew my paper out of my hand.

examples.igbo: Ikuku na-efepụ ájá n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: The wind is blowing sand away on the road.

examples.igbo: O kpụrụ mmiri n'olulu.
examples.english: She drew water from the well.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-akpụ ụgbụ azụ n'osimiri.
examples.english: We are pulling the fishing net in the river.

gloss: be lazy; be exhausted, worn out, very tired

examples.igbo: Ọ na-adà mbà n'ọrụ ugbo.
examples.english: He is lazy at farm work.

examples.igbo: Ị dara mbà mgbe ị rụchara ọrụ?
examples.english: Were you exhausted after you finished work?

examples.igbo: Chaa m ụzọ.
examples.english: Give way for me.

examples.igbo: O chàrà ya ụzọ n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: He gave way to him on the road.

examples.igbo: O chịrị osisi ndị ahụ niile.
examples.english: He carried all those sticks.

examples.igbo: Chịa nri ahụ gaa n'ahịa.
examples.english: Carry that food to the market.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ejeghèli n'ọhịa.
examples.english: He wanders about in the bush.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ị na-ejeghèli n'okporo ámá?
examples.english: Why are you wandering about in the streets?

gloss: cordon round with rope or fence

examples.igbo: O gèrè ubi ya ǹgìgè.
examples.english: He fenced his farm round.

examples.igbo: Ha na-agè ǹgìgè gburugburu ụlọ ahụ.
examples.english: They are fencing round that house.

gloss: commit abomination; break taboo; do something traditionally forbidden

examples.igbo: Ọ meela alū n'ala nna ya.
examples.english: He has committed an abomination in his fatherland.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji eme alū n'etiti ndị mmadụ?
examples.english: Why are you committing an abomination among people?

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ kwara nwanne ya n'ala.
examples.english: That child pushed his sibling down.

examples.igbo: Ònye kwara gị n'azụ?
examples.english: Who pushed you on the back?

note: kwà as 'push' is attested but less common than compounds like kwagide/kwanye; sentences keep it in the simple sense.

examples.igbo: Mfeni ụgbọelu ahụ were awa abụọ.
examples.english: The flight of that plane took two hours.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ mfeni nnụnụ ahụ n'elu osisi?
examples.english: Did you see that bird's flight up onto the tree?

note: mfeni is rare and its exact sense as a noun for 'flight/flying up' is not fully certain to me; learners should treat these as tentative.

examples.igbo: Ulùkpù ojii jupụtara na mbara igwe.
examples.english: Dark clouds filled the sky.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ulùkpù ndị ahụ n'elu ugwu?
examples.english: Did you see those clouds on the hill?

note: Form ulùkpù follows the entry; the more common Central Igbo word is urukpu/ụlụkpụ.

examples.igbo: Mmiri kwodara n'elu ugwu ahụ.
examples.english: Water poured down with force on that hill.

examples.igbo: Kwodaa mmiri ahụ n'ime ite.
examples.english: Pour that water down into the pot.

examples.igbo: Òfu mkpụlū osikapa fọdụrụ n'efere ya.
examples.english: Only one grain of rice remained in his plate.

examples.igbo: Ị chọrọ òfu mkpụlū ma ọ bụ abụọ?
examples.english: Do you want only one or two?

examples.igbo: Ọrụ uche ogologo na-akpata ùbụlù mgbaka.
examples.english: Long mental work causes brain fatigue.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ahụ ùbụlù mgbaka mgbe ị gụchara akwụkwọ?
examples.english: Do you feel brain fatigue after you finish reading?

note: ùbụlù is a variant form of ụbụrụ 'brain'; the compound is understandable but not in everyday use.

examples.igbo: Onyeisi ahụ gbapụrụ nwa ya n'orù.
examples.english: That chief redeemed his child from slavery.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-agbapụ m n'orù a taa?
examples.english: Will you redeem me from this servitude today?

note: Following the given sense 'redeem'; the plain verb gbapụ more often means 'escape/flee', and mgbapụta is the usual noun for redemption.

examples.igbo: O maliri aka ya elu ka o tụọ vootu.
examples.english: He thrust his hand upwards to cast his vote.

examples.igbo: Malie elu, ka anyị hụ gị!
examples.english: Thrust yourself upwards, so that we can see you!

note: mali (elu) as 'thrust upwards' is not a form I can confirm confidently; suggest treating these examples as provisional.

examples.igbo: Nwa agbọghọ ahụ yiri akà n'úkwù.
examples.english: That girl wore beads on her waist.

examples.igbo: Ebee ka i zụtara akà ọcha ndị a?
examples.english: Where did you buy these white beads?

note: Tone-marked akà (beads) follows the entry; readers should not confuse it with aka 'hand'.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-eze uzelē n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: That child sneezes in the school.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ ose na-eme ka ị na-eze uzelē?
examples.english: Is it pepper that makes you sneeze?

examples.igbo: Ụfọdụ anụmànù dị n'ọhịa na-ata ahịhịa.
examples.english: Some animals in the bush graze on grass.

examples.igbo: Ị hụtụla anụmànù n'ụlọ gị mgbe ọ bụla?
examples.english: Have you ever seen an animal in your house?

examples.igbo: O ji eriri tọ̀gbùrù ọkụkọ ahụ.
examples.english: He strangled that fowl with a rope.

examples.igbo: E tọ̀gbùla ọkụkọ ahụ, ọ ka na-eyi akwa.
examples.english: Do not strangle that fowl, it is still laying eggs.

examples.igbo: Ifufe kụdàrà mgbidi ụlọ ahụ n'abalị.
examples.english: The wind brought down the wall of that house at night.

examples.igbo: Kụdàa akwụkwọ ahụ n'elu tebụl ozugbo.
examples.english: Bring down that book on the table immediately.

examples.igbo: O tinyere ajụ n'isi tupu o buru mmiri.
examples.english: She put a headpad on her head before carrying water.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eji ajụ ebu osikapa n'ụlọ ahịa?
examples.english: Do you use a headpad to carry rice at the market?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-elelì ndị ogbenye n'ahịa ugbu a.
examples.english: He looks down on poor people in the market now.

examples.igbo: E lelìla nwanne gị n'ihi uwe ya.
examples.english: Do not look down on your sibling because of his clothes.

gloss: embark or continue on a journey

examples.igbo: Anyị sètịpụrụ ijè n'isi ụtụtụ taa.
examples.english: We set off on the journey this morning.

examples.igbo: Sètịpụnụ ijè ngwa ngwa tupu chi ejie.
examples.english: Set off on the journey quickly before nightfall.

examples.igbo: Le anya n'okporo ụzọ tupu ị gafee.
examples.english: Look at the road before you cross.

examples.igbo: Ọ lere anya n'ahịa niile ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: He looked at the whole market yesterday.

gloss: a document that proves eligibility; certificate; pass; permit

examples.igbo: Ọ gosiri nzèrē ya n'ọnụ ụzọ.
examples.english: He showed his pass at the door.

examples.igbo: Nzèrē gị ọ ka dị n'akpa gị?
examples.english: Is your permit still in your bag?

examples.igbo: O tụkpọrọ aka ya abụọ n'ekpere.
examples.english: He clasped his two hands in prayer.

examples.igbo: Biko tụkpọọ aka gị abụọ ọnụ.
examples.english: Please clasp your two hands together.

examples.igbo: Ndị uwe ojii pịafùsịrị ìgwè mmadụ ahụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: The police flogged and scattered that crowd at the market.

examples.igbo: Onye nkuzi pịafùsịrị ụmụ akwụkwọ ahụ n'ama.
examples.english: The teacher flogged and scattered those pupils in the field.

note: Rare compound; past-tense inflection used.

examples.igbo: Mkpamkpa dakwasịrị obodo anyị n'afọ a.
examples.english: A disaster befell our town this year.

examples.igbo: Mkpamkpa gịnị mere n'ugbo gị ụnyaahụ?
examples.english: What disaster happened on your farm yesterday?

examples.igbo: Ọdụm na-adekpo n'ọhịa.
examples.english: The lion roars in the forest.

examples.igbo: Gịnị na-adekpo n'azụ ụlọ?
examples.english: What is roaring behind the house?

note: Sense of roar is clear, but the verb's tonal marking is not given.

examples.igbo: Ha na-akpà igwù maka ụlọ ọhụrụ.
examples.english: They are preparing palm-fronds for the new house.

examples.igbo: O nyere anyị aka ịkpà igwù.
examples.english: He helped us prepare palm-fronds.

examples.igbo: Ibe anyị bịara n'ụlọ anyị ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: Our people came to our house yesterday.

examples.igbo: Ibe anyị, kedu ebe unu na-aga?
examples.english: Our people, where are you going?

examples.igbo: Osimiri tụrụ èbìlì n'ụtụtụ a.
examples.english: The river was wavy this morning.

examples.igbo: Oké osimiri na-atụ èbìlì taa.
examples.english: The sea is wavy today.

examples.igbo: Onye ntụ ahụ ghọgburu anyị n'ahịa.
examples.english: That liar deceived us in the market.

examples.igbo: Onye ntụ, akwụsịla ịgha ụgha!
examples.english: Liar, stop lying!

examples.igbo: Anyị na-erikọ nri n'ụlọ nne m.
examples.english: We eat together at my mother's house.

examples.igbo: Bịanụ rikọọ nri taa.
examples.english: Come and eat together today.

examples.igbo: Ihe ọ mere chara n'anwū n'anya mmadụ niile.
examples.english: What he did was obvious to everybody.

examples.igbo: Lelee ya nke ọma, ọ na-acha n'anwū.
examples.english: Look at it well; it is conspicuous.

note: The phrase is idiomatic but somewhat specialized.

examples.igbo: Nwa nwaàyì m nọ n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: My daughter is in school.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ nwa nwaàyì ya n'ahịa?
examples.english: Did you see her daughter at the market?

gloss: be useful, profitable, beneficial, valuable, or important;

examples.igbo: Ọrụ ugbo na-abà urù n'oge a.
examples.english: Farming is profitable these days.

examples.igbo: Zụta ya, ọ ga-abà urù n'oge a.
examples.english: Buy it; it will be useful these days.

examples.igbo: Reni ute ahụ dị n'ala ozugbo.
examples.english: Pick up that mat on the ground immediately.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ereni ute ya n'ala mgbe ọ na-apụ.
examples.english: He is picking up his mat from the ground as he leaves.

note: The verb stem is uncommon; the inflected forms are judged plausible.

gloss: money ritually received for one's chi

examples.igbo: Ọ natara ego chī ya n'aka nna ya.
examples.english: He received his chi money from his father.

examples.igbo: Ị na-edobe ego chī gị n'ụlọ?
examples.english: Do you keep your chi money at home?

note: Cultural usage of ego chī may vary by community.

examples.igbo: Ọ fùrù nkwụ̄ ya n'ọhịa ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: He pruned his palm trees in the bush yesterday.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-afù nkwụ̄ n'ubi gị taa?
examples.english: Will you prune palm trees on your farm today?

examples.igbo: Ọ dị n'aka gị ịkwụ ụgwọ ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: It is your responsibility to pay the school fees.

examples.igbo: Ọ dịkwa n'aka nne ya ilekọta nwa ahụ?
examples.english: Is it also his mother's responsibility to care for that child?

examples.igbo: Ụgùlù na-afụ nke ukwuu n'ọnwa Disemba.
examples.english: The harmattan blows strongly in December.

examples.igbo: Kpuchie ọnụ gị, ụgùlù na-afụ taa.
examples.english: Cover your mouth; the harmattan is blowing today.

gloss: the third day of the week; Tuesday

examples.igbo: Tuuzde bụ ụbọchị nke atọ n'izu.
examples.english: Tuesday is the third day of the week.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-abịa n'ụlọ m Tuuzde n'elekere anọ?
examples.english: Will you come to my house on Tuesday at four o'clock?

examples.igbo: Chịni aka gị elu maka ekpere.
examples.english: Lift up your hands for prayer.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-achịni aka ha elu mgbe ha na-ekpere ekpere.
examples.english: The children are lifting up their hands when they pray.

note: The inflected continuous form is judged plausible but not fully certain.

gloss: abash (literally bring shame to one's face)

examples.igbo: Okwu ya menyeere m ifele n'iru.
examples.english: His words abashed me.

examples.igbo: Emenyela nwa gị ifele n'iru n'ihu ọha.
examples.english: Don't abash your child in public.

note: The phrase is idiomatic; applicative form menyeere is used.

examples.igbo: Eteke na-esi n'ọnya ahụ apụta.
examples.english: Blood is coming out of that wound.

examples.igbo: Olee ebe eteke a siri bịa?
examples.english: Where did this blood come from?

note: Eteke is dialectal for blood; standard Igbo often uses ọbara.

examples.igbo: Ọ gbara ọchịchịrị tupu anyị erute n'ụlọ.
examples.english: It got dark before we reached home.

examples.igbo: Bịa ngwa ngwa, ọ na-agba ọchịchịrị.
examples.english: Come quickly, it is getting dark.

note: Headword has òchịchịī; I use the more familiar standard spelling ọchịchịrị.

examples.igbo: Ǹgị nà ònwe gī bịara n'oge.
examples.english: You yourself came early.

examples.igbo: Ǹgị nà ònwe gī ka ọ na-achọ?
examples.english: Is it you yourself he is looking for?

examples.igbo: O kworo ìlìlò ahụ n'ubi.
examples.english: He uprooted that plant in the farm.

examples.igbo: Kwọọ ìlìlò ahụ na mgbọrọgwụ ya.
examples.english: Uproot that plant with its roots.

examples.igbo: Osisi ahụ bụ ọkpụ ànì n'obodo anyị.
examples.english: That tree is ancient in our town.

examples.igbo: Ọkpụ ànì ka omenaala anyị bụ?
examples.english: Is our culture long-established?

examples.igbo: O kewara ife nkèta n'etiti ụmụ ya.
examples.english: He divided the inheritance among his children.

examples.igbo: Olee ihe ị ga-eme na ife nkèta gị?
examples.english: What will you do with your inheritance?

gloss: incite someone to do something; stir up (trouble), especially something bad

examples.igbo: Ọ kwanyere ya ọkụ ka ọ lụọ ọgụ.
examples.english: He incited him to fight.

examples.igbo: Kwanye ya ọkụ ka ọ lụọ ọgụ.
examples.english: Incite him to fight.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-abụ abụ n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: The children are singing at school.

examples.igbo: Ị na-abụ abụ ọhụrụ?
examples.english: Are you singing a new song?

examples.igbo: Ndị obodo na-agọ arụsị ha n'oge emume.
examples.english: The townspeople venerate their deities during the festival.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji agọ arụsị a?
examples.english: Why do you venerate this deity?

gloss: make a distinguishing mark: recognize or notice something

examples.igbo: Ahụ̀bara m āmā na ọ bụ nwanne m.
examples.english: I recognized that he was my brother.

examples.igbo: Ị hụ̀bara āmā ebe anyị gara?
examples.english: Did you recognize the place we went?

gloss: local medicine prepared and stored in a bottle with palm- kernel oil, used for curing convulsions, poisoning

examples.igbo: O nyere nwa ya ọgwū ū de mgbe ọ dara.
examples.english: She gave her child ọgwū ū de when he had convulsions.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere ọgwū ū de maka nsị?
examples.english: Do you have ọgwū ū de for poison?

examples.igbo: Akwụkọ ahụ takụrụ n'uwe m.
examples.english: That feather stuck to my cloth.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ọ na-atakụ n'aka gị?
examples.english: Why is it sticking to your hand?

gloss: fall against with a little portion of body (especially in a playful way)

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ dàkụ̀rù n'ubu m.
examples.english: That child fell against my shoulder.

examples.igbo: Ị na-adàkụ̀ m mgbe niile!
examples.english: You are always falling against me!

gloss: kind of fowl which never grows to a large size but is tough (usually used for sacrifice)

examples.igbo: E jiri òkụkù abùke chụọ àjà.
examples.english: They used òkụkù abùke for sacrifice.

examples.igbo: Òkụkù abùke adịghị eto ibu.
examples.english: The òkụkù abùke does not grow big.

gloss: the past experience is strength; history is strength; those standing behind (supporters) are strength

examples.igbo: Àzụbụ̀ike bụ ihe anyị ji emeri.
examples.english: Àzụbụ̀ike is what we use to win.

examples.igbo: Ị ghọtara na àzụbụ̀ike bụ ike?
examples.english: Do you understand that the past is strength?

gloss: the temporary numbness, with itchiness, in the limbs caused by bad posture

examples.igbo: M̀kpàǹshịkọ̄ nwere m n'ụkwụ.
examples.english: I have numbness in my leg.

examples.igbo: Olee ebe m̀kpàǹshịkọ̄ a si abịa?
examples.english: Where does this numbness come from?

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ ògụgùa nye ndị na-eru uju.
examples.english: He is a comforter to mourners.

examples.igbo: Chineke bụ ògụgùa anyị.
examples.english: God is our comforter.

examples.igbo: Anyị ga-asucha osikapa echi.
examples.english: We will thresh rice tomorrow.

examples.igbo: Ị suchara ọka ahụ?
examples.english: Did you thresh that corn?

gloss: a general name for fish of the family Schilbeidae (= ideèlè)

examples.igbo: Anyị zụtara ịjaàrì n'ahịa.
examples.english: We bought ịjaàrì in the market.

examples.igbo: Ịjaàrì a dị mma maka ofe.
examples.english: This ịjaàrì is good for soup.

examples.igbo: Jìdèsì ike n'osisi ka ị ghara ịda.
examples.english: Hold firmly to the tree so you don't fall.

examples.igbo: O jìdèsì ike n'aka nne ya mgbe ha na-aga ahịa.
examples.english: She held firmly to her mother's hand when they were going to market.

examples.igbo: O chalàpùrù anya n'ebe m nọ.
examples.english: He stared sternly at me.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji chalàpù anya n'ebe m nọ?
examples.english: Why are you staring sternly at me?

examples.igbo: O ji egbē ādakā gaa ịchụ nta.
examples.english: He took a locally made gun and went hunting.

examples.igbo: Were egbē ādakā gaa ịchụ nta.
examples.english: Take the locally made gun and go hunting.

examples.igbo: Ha fètabara n'osimiri ahụ n'isi ụtụtụ.
examples.english: They began to cross that river in the morning.

examples.igbo: Fètaba n'okporo ụzọ ahụ tupu ụgbọala abịa.
examples.english: Begin to cross that road before a car comes.

gloss: area where a particular thing is plentiful

examples.igbo: Òdọ osikapa bụ obodo anyị niile.
examples.english: Our whole town is an area where rice is plentiful.

examples.igbo: Ị maara òdọ azụ dị nso ebe a?
examples.english: Do you know an area where fish is plentiful near here?

examples.igbo: Ha bidoro ọrụ ahụ n'isi ụtụtụ.
examples.english: They began that work in the morning.

examples.igbo: Bido ịrụ ọrụ ahụ tupu anyanwụ awaa.
examples.english: Begin doing that work before the sun sets.

examples.igbo: O nyere nwa ya n'aka onye nkuzi.
examples.english: He handed his child over to the teacher.

examples.igbo: Nye ego gị n'aka onye na-echekwa ego.
examples.english: Hand your money over to the treasurer.

examples.igbo: O tọrọ ọchị̀ n'oge oriri ahụ.
examples.english: He was funny at that feast.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji na-atọ ọchị̀ ugbu a?
examples.english: Why are you being funny now?

gloss: kindle fire; show light (especially from bright to faint)

examples.igbo: O mụ̀rụ ọkụ n'ọkụ ahụ n'isi ụtụtụ.
examples.english: He kindled fire in that hearth in the morning.

examples.igbo: Mụ̀ ọkụ ka anyị hụ ihe n'abalị.
examples.english: Kindle fire so we can see at night.

examples.igbo: O rịrụkata ya n'akụkụ ụzọ mgbe ha na-aga.
examples.english: He pushed him aside from the path when they were going.

examples.igbo: Rịrụka n'ụzọ m ka m gafee.
examples.english: Move aside from my path so I can pass.

gloss: exclamation - my word! dear me! goodness! (= kaì!)

examples.igbo: Paì! Lee ihe m hụrụ n'ụlọ ahịa.
examples.english: My word! Look at what I saw in the market.

examples.igbo: Paì! Ọ bụ gị mere nke a?
examples.english: Dear me! Was it you who did this?

examples.igbo: O kpukpụrụ aka, anyị niile daara jụụ.
examples.english: She waved her hand for silence, and we all became quiet.

examples.igbo: Kpukpụ aka ka ndị mmadụ wee gbachie nkịtị.
examples.english: Wave your hand for silence so that people keep quiet.

note: The conjugation of this rare verb phrase may vary; the intended sense is clear.

examples.igbo: Ndị agha bu egbē ndù gaa n'ọgbọ agha.
examples.english: The soldiers carried cannons to the battlefield.

examples.igbo: Buru egbē ndù ahụ gaa n'ugwu.
examples.english: Carry that cannon to the hill.

examples.igbo: O kèrè ego ahụ n'ime ụmụaka.
examples.english: He shared that money among the children.

examples.igbo: Kèe achịcha a n'otu n'otu, ka ọ dị mma.
examples.english: Share this bread piece by piece, so it is fair.

examples.igbo: Ịbà tara nwa m, ọ naghị eri nri.
examples.english: Malaria afflicted my child, and he is not eating.

examples.igbo: Ịbà ahụ ọ kwụsịrị, ka ọ ka na-aga?
examples.english: Has that fever stopped, or is it still going on?

gloss: go forward; go in front; progress

examples.igbo: Anyị gara n'iru n'okporo ụzọ ahụ.
examples.english: We went forward on that road.

examples.igbo: Gaa n'iru, anyị ga-eso gị n'azụ.
examples.english: Go forward, and we will follow behind you.

examples.igbo: Ọ zọrọ ọkwa onye isi obodo.
examples.english: He contested for the position of town chairman.

examples.igbo: Ì ga-ezọ ọkwa onye isi oche?
examples.english: Will you contest for the chairman position?

examples.igbo: Anyị nọ n'èzí na-anya ọkụ anyanwụ.
examples.english: We are outside basking in the sunshine.

examples.igbo: Nya ọkụ n'akụkụ ọkụ ahụ, ka ahụ gị dị ọkụ.
examples.english: Warm yourself by that fire, so your body is warm.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ pụpụrụ ire ya n'ụzọ ọchị.
examples.english: That child stuck out his tongue playfully.

examples.igbo: Ire gị ọ na-egbu mgbu mgbe ị na-eri nri?
examples.english: Does your tongue hurt when you are eating?

examples.igbo: Àmùmà na-enwu na mbara igwe n'abalị a.
examples.english: Lightning is flashing in the sky tonight.

examples.igbo: Ì hụrụ àmùmà ahụ n'abalị ụnyaahụ?
examples.english: Did you see that lightning last night?

examples.igbo: Onye dibịa gwọrọ ọgù gwọọ nwata ahụ.
examples.english: The native doctor prepared medicine and treated the child.

examples.igbo: Gwọọ ọgù tinye n’ime mmiri.
examples.english: Prepare poison and put it in the water.

examples.igbo: Nna nna m chịrị ìnyèmè atọ.
examples.english: My grandfather had three wives.

examples.igbo: Ị chịrị ìnyèmè ole?
examples.english: How many wives do you have?

gloss: soup, mentholatum, etc.); sting (of pepper); hurt (of sting)

examples.igbo: Ose a na-akpọ̀ m n’ọnụ.
examples.english: This pepper stings my mouth.

examples.igbo: Mmanụ mentholatum na-akpọ̀ gị n’anya?
examples.english: Does mentholatum sting your eye?

examples.igbo: Nne m na-akpà eriri n’ụlọ.
examples.english: My mother braids thread in the house.

examples.igbo: Kpàa eriri a n’oge.
examples.english: Braid this thread now.

examples.igbo: Ògbùgbà osisi na-egbu m ike.
examples.english: Carrying wood tires me.

examples.igbo: Ògbùgbà akpa a na-ewe oge?
examples.english: Does carrying this bag take time?

examples.igbo: Ọ bọọrọ ụbọọ nna ya.
examples.english: He avenged his father.

examples.igbo: Bọọ ụbọọ gị maka ihe ahụ.
examples.english: Avenge yourself for that matter.

gloss: think that something is the case, especially without being sure; presume; assume

examples.igbo: M na-agba erè na ọ ga-abịa.
examples.english: I assume he will come.

examples.igbo: Egbula erè na m nwere ego.
examples.english: Don’t assume I have money.

examples.igbo: Ha kpakọbara osisi n’otu ebe.
examples.english: They gathered wood in one place.

examples.igbo: Kpakọbata mkpụrụ ahụ n’ime akpa.
examples.english: Gather those seeds into the bag.

examples.igbo: Anyị mere òlịlị n’ahịa.
examples.english: We took a stroll in the market.

examples.igbo: Òlịlị n’ụtụtụ na-atọ gị ụtọ?
examples.english: Does a morning stroll please you?

examples.igbo: Anyị na-eje ọkù n'osimiri mgbe ọ bụla.
examples.english: We go fishing in the river every time.

examples.igbo: Jee ọkù taa, wetara anyị azụ̀.
examples.english: Go fishing today, bring us fish.

examples.igbo: E kpere okwu ahụ n'ụnò ikpē.
examples.english: That case was tried in court.

examples.igbo: Ị maara ebe ụnò ikpē dị?
examples.english: Do you know where the court is?

examples.igbo: Ọnya ahụ asọọla esuso n'aka ya.
examples.english: The wound has formed a boil on his hand.

examples.igbo: Olu ya na-aso esuso ugbu a.
examples.english: His neck is forming a boil now.

note: The verb form asọọla from -so esuso may vary by dialect.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka wụliri elu n'ọṅụ mgbe ha hụrụ ya.
examples.english: The children jumped up in joy when they saw him.

examples.igbo: Wụlìenu elu ka anyị hụ unu.
examples.english: Jump up so we can see you.

examples.igbo: O jụpụtara onye zuru akpa ya.
examples.english: He found out who stole his bag.

examples.igbo: Jụpụta ihe mere o ji abịaghị.
examples.english: Find out why he did not come.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-akpọ ya onye nsọkwù.
examples.english: The children call him a fool.

examples.igbo: Onye nsọkwù, gịnị mere i ji kwere ya?
examples.english: Fool, why did you believe him?

note: The word nsọkwù may be less common in some dialects.

gloss: cheat in marketing or in bargaining for commodity

examples.igbo: Onye ahịa ahụ zụgburu m n'ahịa.
examples.english: That trader cheated me in the market.

examples.igbo: Biko, azụgbula m n'ọnụ ahịa a.
examples.english: Please, do not cheat me in this price.

examples.igbo: O lụniri ọkụ n'ebe a.
examples.english: He built up the fire here.

examples.igbo: Lụnienu ọkụ, nri ka na-etebe.
examples.english: Build up the fire, the food is still cooking.

note: The verb -lụni is often used with ọkụ, meaning to build up a fire.

examples.igbo: Mkpofù nri na-ewute nne m.
examples.english: Throwing away food pains my mother.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eme mkpofù uwe ochie?
examples.english: Are you throwing away old clothes?

examples.igbo: Azụmahịa ya wuluru ike n'oge a.
examples.english: His business is firm now.

examples.igbo: Gbaa mbọ ka ụlọ ọrụ gị wulie ike.
examples.english: Strive so your business becomes established.

note: The sense of -wulu as be firm or established is clear, but usage can overlap with wulie ike.

gloss: breathe slowly, faintly, with difficulty (as one dying)

examples.igbo: Nna m na-atụ ndù nwayọọ n'àkwà.
examples.english: My father is breathing faintly on the bed.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-atụ ndù nwayọọ? Kpọọ dọkịta ozugbo.
examples.english: Is he breathing faintly? Call a doctor immediately.

gloss: for or in favor of - used when the verb ends with 'ụ'

examples.igbo: O kụrụ m osisi n'ubi.
examples.english: He planted a tree for me on the farm.

examples.igbo: Ị kụrụ m osisi?
examples.english: Did you plant a tree for me?

examples.igbo: O yi kootù ọhụrụ n'ọgbakọ.
examples.english: He wore a new suit to the meeting.

examples.igbo: Kootù a dị m mma?
examples.english: Does this suit look good on me?

examples.igbo: Nne m na-ekpe ekpere kwà ùchichì.
examples.english: My mother prays nightly.

examples.igbo: Ị na-aga ahịa kwà ùchichì?
examples.english: Do you go to the market nightly?

gloss: Peugeot 404 (so called because of streamlined shape; literally horn of bamboo)

examples.igbo: O ji òpi àchàlà aga ahịa.
examples.english: He uses a Peugeot 404 to go to the market.

examples.igbo: Òpi àchàlà ya na-eme mkpọtụ?
examples.english: Is his Peugeot 404 noisy?

gloss: take the place of (somebody); represent someone

examples.igbo: O nọchiri anya nne ya n'ahịa.
examples.english: She represented her mother at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-anọchì anya m n'ọgbakọ?
examples.english: Will you represent me at the meeting?

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ wara ite ahụ ibe.
examples.english: That child broke that pot into pieces.

examples.igbo: Ị wara osisi ahụ ibe?
examples.english: Did you break that wood into pieces?

examples.igbo: O gbatìrì ònwe n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: He stretched himself in the morning.

examples.igbo: Gbatì ònwe gị tupu ị gbaa ọsọ.
examples.english: Stretch yourself before you run.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-eche uchè ma ọ ga-abịa.
examples.english: He is wondering whether he will come.

examples.igbo: Chee uchè nke ọma tupu i zaa.
examples.english: Think carefully before you answer.

examples.igbo: Mkpịsị igwè ụgbọala m gbajiri.
examples.english: The spoke of my bicycle is broken.

examples.igbo: Ị pụrụ ịrụzi mkpịsị igwè a?
examples.english: Can you repair this spoke?

gloss: make loose, or widen, a hole by poking or probing

examples.igbo: Ọ na-awokọ oghere ahụ.
examples.english: He is widening that hole.

examples.igbo: Wokọọ oghere ahụ ntakịrị.
examples.english: Widen that hole a little.

note: Unsure about the exact past tense form; used continuous and imperative.

examples.igbo: E mechiri ọnụ ụzō īlo ha.
examples.english: They closed their compound gate.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ọnụ ụzō īlo ọhụrụ ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see that new gate?

gloss: add to; enlarge (e.g. a house) by addition of more rooms; extend

examples.igbo: Ha gbàkwụnyere ụlọ ahụ ọnụ ụlọ abụọ.
examples.english: They added two rooms to the house.

examples.igbo: Gbàkwụnye ụlọ gị ọnụ ụlọ ọzọ.
examples.english: Add another room to your house.

examples.igbo: Nne m na-agwe ose.
examples.english: My mother is grinding pepper.

examples.igbo: Gwe ọka ahụ ka anyị sie ya.
examples.english: Grind that corn so we can cook it.

examples.igbo: O nwere òsusu isī mara mma.
examples.english: She has a beautiful lock of hair.

examples.igbo: Ị na-akpa òsusu isī gị?
examples.english: Are you plaiting your hair lock?

examples.igbo: Ọgò nwaànyì m bịara eleta anyị.
examples.english: My mother-in-law came to visit us.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-aga ile ọgò nwaànyì gị?
examples.english: Will you go to see your mother-in-law?

examples.igbo: Anyị fere ogwè mmiri ahụ.
examples.english: We crossed that bridge.

examples.igbo: Fee ogwè ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: Cross that bridge carefully.

examples.igbo: Dàalụ sọọ maka nri ị nyere anyị.
examples.english: Thank you very much for the food you gave us.

examples.igbo: Dàalụ sọọ, Chineke gozie gị.
examples.english: Thank you very much, may God bless you.

examples.igbo: Sàchie akwụkwọ gị, oge agwụla.
examples.english: Close your book, the time is up.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ sàchiri akwụkwọ ya ozugbo.
examples.english: That child closed his book at once.

examples.igbo: Afọ nnī bụ ajọ àgwà n'ebe ụmụaka nọ.
examples.english: Gluttony is a bad habit among children.

examples.igbo: Afọ nnī ya na-ewe nne ya iwe.
examples.english: His gluttony annoys his mother.

note: The compound is not common in everyday speech; sentences are sound but a speaker might use 'iri nri n'ike' instead.

examples.igbo: Ọ kparịrị nwanne ya mkpalị n'ihu ọha.
examples.english: He insulted his brother in public.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji akparị m mkpalị?
examples.english: Why are you insulting me?

examples.igbo: Anyị riri azị ụtụtụ tupu anyị apụọ n'ụlọ.
examples.english: We ate breakfast before we left the house.

examples.igbo: Gịnị ka ị na-eri dịka azị ụtụtụ?
examples.english: What do you eat for breakfast?

note: 'Nri ụtụtụ' is the more common word for breakfast; 'azị ụtụtụ' seems regional.

examples.igbo: Ọ nwere obi onyinye, ọ na-enyere ndị ogbenye aka.
examples.english: He has a generous mind; he helps the poor.

examples.igbo: Obi onyinye dị mma karịa akụ na ụba.
examples.english: A generous mind is better than wealth.

note: The headword's spelling and tone marks are unusual; 'obi onyinye' is the form I am confident in.

examples.igbo: Kpuchie ite ahụ ka ihe ghara ịbanye na ya.
examples.english: Cover that pot so nothing gets into it.

examples.igbo: O kpuchiri efere nri ahụ n'elu tebulu.
examples.english: She covered the plate of food on the table.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akpa àgwà ọjọọ n'ụlọ akwụkwọ ya.
examples.english: He behaves badly at his school.

examples.igbo: Akpakwala àgwà ọjọọ n'ihu ndị ọbịa.
examples.english: Don't behave badly in front of guests.

note: The negative imperative form 'akpakwala' is standard but less frequent than 'emela àgwà ọjọọ'.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-asụ ji maka nri abalị.
examples.english: She pounds yam for dinner.

examples.igbo: Sụọ ji ahụ ka anyị rie ya.
examples.english: Pound that yam so we can eat it.

gloss: stir; arouse strong feeling in someone;

examples.igbo: Okwu ya kpalitere m iwe nke ukwuu.
examples.english: His words stirred up great anger in me.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpalitere gị iwe otú a?
examples.english: What stirred your anger like this?

note: The sense 'stir up feeling' belongs to the extended form 'kpalite'; I used that form in both sentences.

gloss: sit with the lower limbs drawn up (like a lame person, usually on the floor) (compare -kù ǹgwụlō)

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ gwọrọ ǹgwụlō n'ala.
examples.english: That child sat with his legs drawn up on the ground.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji gwọọ ǹgwụlō?
examples.english: Why are you sitting with your legs drawn up?

note: Unsure about the exact inflection of -gwọ in the past and command forms.

examples.igbo: Nne m na-ehi ụra n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: My mother is sleeping in the room.

examples.igbo: Ị hiri ụra nke ọma n'abalị ụnyaahụ?
examples.english: Did you sleep well last night?

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ bụ òkà ekwukwū n'ụlọ ọrụ.
examples.english: That man is a chatterbox at the office.

examples.igbo: Òkà ekwukwū, kwụsị ịkwa okwu!
examples.english: Chatterbox, stop talking!

gloss: level ground; break ground for planting

examples.igbo: Ndị ọrụ na-akpọbo ànì n'ubi.
examples.english: The workers are leveling the ground on the farm.

examples.igbo: Kpọbọọ ànì ngwa ngwa, oge ọkọchị na-abịa.
examples.english: Break the ground quickly, the dry season is coming.

note: Uncertain about the command form 'kpọbọọ' and the past tense.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-agwupụte ájá n'azụ ụlọ.
examples.english: Children are digging up sand behind the house.

examples.igbo: Gwupụta mkpụrụ osisi ahụ, anyị ga-akụ ya ọzọ.
examples.english: Dig up that seed, we will plant it again.

note: Unsure about the exact verb form for the command.

gloss: ringworm of the head (tinea capitis) (literally barber who receives no pay)

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ nwere òkpụ īsi elī ngo.
examples.english: That child has ringworm of the head.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ òkpụ īsi elī ngo n'isi ya?
examples.english: Did you see ringworm on his head?

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ wùniri enū mgbe ọ hụrụ nne ya.
examples.english: That child jumped up when he saw his mother.

examples.igbo: Wùni enū ka anyị hụ gị.
examples.english: Jump up so we can see you.

note: Unsure about the past tense form 'wùniri'.

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ tachapụrụ ezē n'ihi ọṅụ.
examples.english: That child grinned with joy.

examples.igbo: Tachapụ ezē ka anyị hụ na ị dị mma.
examples.english: Smile so we can see you are fine.

note: Unsure about the past tense form 'tachapụrụ'.

gloss: the act of moving into a man's house without being officially married to him

examples.igbo: Nwanyị ahụ mere kwanangida mgbe ọ bịara n'ụlọ ya.
examples.english: That woman did kwanangida when she came to his house.

examples.igbo: Ị maara ihe kwanangida pụtara?
examples.english: Do you know what kwanangida means?

note: The term is cultural; I am fairly confident but not absolutely sure of its usage in modern speech.

examples.igbo: Nna m na-aja Chineke ike kwa ụtụtụ.
examples.english: My father praises God every morning.

examples.igbo: Jaa nwa gị ike mgbe o mere ihe ọma.
examples.english: Praise your child when he does something good.

examples.igbo: Anyị dakàpụrụ n'ọchị mgbe ọ daara n'ala.
examples.english: We burst out laughing when he fell down.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji dakàpụ n'ọchị otú a?
examples.english: Why did you burst out laughing like that?

gloss: concern oneself with; make friendly advances to; befriend

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akpakwu ndị agbata obi ya mgbe niile.
examples.english: He always concerns himself with his neighbours.

examples.igbo: Akpakwula ya n'okwu a, ọ bụghị nke gị.
examples.english: Do not concern yourself with this matter, it is not yours.

note: The stem is uncommon; inflections na-akpakwu / akpakwula are my best reading of it.

examples.igbo: Nwa di ntā na-ebu egbe nna ya.
examples.english: The hunter's attendant carries his father's gun.

examples.igbo: Ebee ka nwa di ntā na-eche nna ya?
examples.english: Where does the hunter's attendant wait for his father?

note: Tone and spelling of the phrase vary between speakers.

examples.igbo: Onye nkụzi kụrụ mgbịlịmgba ka ụmụaka bata.
examples.english: The teacher rang the bell for the children to come in.

examples.igbo: Kụọ mgbịlịmgba, ụmụaka ga-akwụsị egwu.
examples.english: Ring the bell, the children will stop playing.

gloss: break into tiny pieces; smash; shatter

examples.igbo: Ọ tijàsị̀rị ite ahụ n'ala.
examples.english: He smashed that pot on the ground.

examples.igbo: Kedu ihe tijàsị̀rị iko m n'elu tebụl?
examples.english: What shattered my cup on the table?

note: The inflected form tijàsị̀rị follows the usual -rị pattern; tone on the stem is as given.

examples.igbo: Ha na-asu ekwe n'ụlọ nzukọ.
examples.english: They beat the gong in the meeting hall.

examples.igbo: Sụọ ekwe, ndị obodo ga-ezukọ.
examples.english: Beat the gong, the villagers will gather.

examples.igbo: Mama ji akwa gbòdoro efere nri.
examples.english: Mother covered the plate of food with a cloth.

examples.igbo: Gbòdoo ite ahụ ka ijiji ghara ịbata.
examples.english: Cover that pot so flies will not get in.

note: The verb is uncommon and its tone pattern is not fully certain to me.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ njefìè m, biko gbaghara m.
examples.english: It was my error, please forgive me.

examples.igbo: Ònye mere njefìè a n'ụlọ akwụkwọ?
examples.english: Who committed this error at the school?

note: njefìè is used for both a mistake and a trespass; tone marks as given.

examples.igbo: Akwụkwọ kpalàchiri n'ala ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: Papers were strewn on the school floor.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpalàchiri n'elu akwa a?
examples.english: What is strewn on this bed?

note: Tone on the inflected form is uncertain; the stem tone is as given.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka ahụ na-esògbu nne ha kwa ụbọchị.
examples.english: Those children trouble their mother every day.

examples.igbo: Gịnị na-esògbu gị n'obi?
examples.english: What is troubling your mind?

gloss: deserve; be fitting; be suitable; correspond

examples.igbo: Ọ kwesịrị ịnata ụgwọ ọrụ ya.
examples.english: He deserves to receive his wages.

examples.igbo: Uwe ọhụrụ a kwesịrị gị nke ọma.
examples.english: This new dress suits you well.

gloss: be bold; be undaunted, brave, or audacious

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ na-awa anya n'ebe ndị okenye nọ.
examples.english: That child is bold in the presence of elders.

examples.igbo: Wa anya, ihe ọjọọ agaghị eme gị.
examples.english: Be bold, nothing bad will happen to you.

examples.igbo: Chukwu Òkìkè kere elu na ala.
examples.english: God the Creator made heaven and earth.

examples.igbo: Chukwu Òkìkè, biko chebe anyị.
examples.english: God the Creator, please protect us.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-aga ụlọ akwụkwọ kwa ụtụtụ.
examples.english: The children go to school every morning.

examples.igbo: Ị na-aga ụlọ akwụkwọ taa?
examples.english: Are you going to school today?

gloss: go or leave for a journey; embark on a journey

examples.igbo: Ọ pụrụ ijè gaa Aba ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: He left on a journey to Aba yesterday.

examples.igbo: Ole mgbe ị ga-apụ ijè?
examples.english: When will you leave on a journey?

gloss: row of things or people; arrangement

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka guzoro n'ùsòlò abụọ n'ama.
examples.english: The children stood in two rows in the compound.

examples.igbo: Doo osisi ndị ahụ n'ùsòlò.
examples.english: Arrange those sticks in a row.

examples.igbo: Uwe ya na-acha ntụ ntụ.
examples.english: His cloth is ash-grey.

examples.igbo: Uwe ya na-acha ntụ ntụ, ma nke m na-acha ọcha.
examples.english: His cloth is ash-grey, but mine is white.

gloss: simple, faceless image carved (usually from ògilìsì) to

examples.igbo: Ọ kpụrụ okpōsi n'osisi ògilìsì.
examples.english: He carved an okposi from an ogilisi tree.

examples.igbo: Okpōsi ahụ enweghị ihu.
examples.english: That okposi has no face.

note: The entry's gloss is cut off, but the word refers to a simple faceless carved image; sentences reflect that.

examples.igbo: Bịa n'azụ m, ka anyị gaa ahịa.
examples.english: Come after me, let us go to the market.

examples.igbo: Nwata nta na-abịa n'azụ nne ya.
examples.english: The little child comes after her mother.

examples.igbo: Okwu ahụ ghaara n'obodo niile.
examples.english: That matter spread all over the town.

examples.igbo: Ghaa mkpụrụ ọka n'ala tupu mmiri abịa.
examples.english: Scatter the maize seeds on the ground before the rain comes.

note: The sense 'spread/scatter' is usually expressed with ghasaa/ghaara; the bare stem gha is rarer.

examples.igbo: Nwa ọ̄nogbò na-achụ oke n'abalị.
examples.english: The cat chases rats at night.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ nwa ọ̄nogbò n'ụlọ?
examples.english: Did you see the cat in the house?

note: nwa ọ̄nogbò is a dialectal word for cat; many speakers say pusi.

examples.igbo: O bu afịa ọlile bata n'ahịa.
examples.english: He brought merchandise into the market.

examples.igbo: Ebee ka ị na-ere afịa ọlile gị?
examples.english: Where do you sell your merchandise?

note: afịa ọlile is understood, but ahịa/ngwa ahịa are more common for goods.

examples.igbo: Òghighe azụ na-ewe oge.
examples.english: Frying fish takes time.

examples.igbo: Òghighe akara dị mma n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: Frying akara is nice in the morning.

note: The usual term for frying is ighe; òghighe as a noun is uncommon.

examples.igbo: Ọ tara ime mgbe ọ dị obere.
examples.english: She aborted the pregnancy when she was young.

examples.igbo: Ndị dọkịta na-adọ aka ná ntị megide ite ime.
examples.english: Doctors warn against abortion.

examples.igbo: Ọ zụtara nwunye ya ọdụ ụkwū ọdụ́.
examples.english: He bought an ivory anklet for his wife.

examples.igbo: Ọdụ ụkwū a bụ ọdụ́ ka ọ bụ ọla kọpa?
examples.english: Is this anklet ivory or copper?

note: ọdụ ụkwū also means 'ankle', so the context must show the ornament.

examples.igbo: Afà ị mara mma.
examples.english: Your name is beautiful.

examples.igbo: Olee afà ị?
examples.english: What is your name?

note: More common is afà gị; afà ị sounds formal.

examples.igbo: Ụ̀dùume ndị a bụ a, e, i, o, u.
examples.english: These vowels are a, e, i, o, u.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-amụ ụ̀dùume n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: The children learn vowels at school.

gloss: tread in any sort of filth; tread till it becomes soft and messy; match on to become a pulp

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka zọtara apịtị n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: The children trampled the mud on the road.

examples.igbo: Zọtọ apịtị ahụ ka ọ dị nro.
examples.english: Tread that mud so that it becomes soft.

note: The word is uncommon; zọtọ here is taken as 'trample into a mash'.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụpụrụ osisi ahụ n'ubi.
examples.english: He carried the wood away from the farm.

examples.igbo: Bụpụ akpa ndị a gaa ụlọ.
examples.english: Carry these bags away to the house.

examples.igbo: O dọbìrì ọka ahụ n'osisi ya.
examples.english: He broke that maize cob off its stalk.

examples.igbo: Dọbìa ọka ole na ole maka nri anyị.
examples.english: Break off a few cobs of maize for our food.

examples.igbo: Ọ dị ụsọ n'ọnụ m mgbe m na-ata ya.
examples.english: It tastes sweet in my mouth when I chew it.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-adịkwa gị ụsọ n'ọnụ?
examples.english: Does it also taste sweet in your mouth?

examples.igbo: Nne m na-akwa akwà n'ụlọ.
examples.english: My mother is sewing cloth in the house.

examples.igbo: Kwaa akwà a tupu mgbede.
examples.english: Sew this cloth before evening.

examples.igbo: Dekwu ihe ndị ọzọ gbasara ya.
examples.english: Write more of the other things about it.

examples.igbo: Ọ dekwuru okwu ahụ n'akwụkwọ ozi ya.
examples.english: He wrote more on that matter in his letter.

examples.igbo: Arò ǹkaà, anyị ga-akọ ọka n'ubi.
examples.english: This year, we will plant maize in the farm.

examples.igbo: Arò ǹkaà ka ọ ga-alọta?
examples.english: Is it this year that he will come back?

examples.igbo: Ha wèmìrì ya gaa obodo ọzọ.
examples.english: They took him far away to another town.

examples.igbo: Wèmìa ngwongwo ndị a pụọ ebe a.
examples.english: Take these loads far away from here.

examples.igbo: Mwepu ego ahụ kàchapụrụ uru anyị nwetara.
examples.english: That deduction cancelled out the profit we made.

examples.igbo: Ihe ọ mere kàchapụrụ ọrụ ọma ya niile.
examples.english: What he did cancelled out all his good works.

examples.igbo: Nàba, ụmụaka na-eche gị n'ụlọ.
examples.english: Go home, the children are waiting for you at home.

examples.igbo: O kwuru na ya ga-anàba tupu chi ejie.
examples.english: He said he would go home before nightfall.

examples.igbo: Ọ namìrì gawa, mmadụ amaghị ebe ọ gara.
examples.english: He wandered off, and nobody knows where he went.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji namì aga n'obodo ọzọ?
examples.english: Why are you wandering off to another town?

note: The sense of -namì as going to an unknown destination is not familiar to me, so the examples may not fit the intended sense.

examples.igbo: Anyị buliri ijè n'isi ụtụtụ taa.
examples.english: We set off on the journey early this morning.

examples.igbo: Ole mgbe unu ga-ebuli ijè gaa Enugu?
examples.english: When will you set off on the journey to Enugu?

gloss: withdraw (especially from fire); sit away from

examples.igbo: O nòpùtara efere ahụ n'ọkụ.
examples.english: She moved that plate away from the fire.

examples.igbo: Biko nòpùta n'ebe ọkụ ahụ dị.
examples.english: Please sit away from where that fire is.

note: The verb stem and its inflected forms are somewhat uncertain in tone.

examples.igbo: Echi niīne ka m ga-ere ọka n'ahịa.
examples.english: I will sell maize at the market tomorrow for sure.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-azụta ọkụkọ echi niīne?
examples.english: Will you buy a chicken tomorrow for sure?

note: The emphatic phrase echi niīne is not common in all dialects.

examples.igbo: Chụ̀la ụmụaka ahụ n'ụlọ.
examples.english: Drive those children home.

examples.igbo: Ị chụ̀lara nne gị n'ụlọ?
examples.english: Did you drive your mother home?

note: The exact verbal form chụ̀la is uncertain.

examples.igbo: O gbasịrị ọka ahụ n'ime nkata.
examples.english: She rubbed that corn off the cob into the basket.

examples.igbo: Gbasịa ọka a tupu ị si ya.
examples.english: Rub this corn off the cob before you cook it.

note: Inflected forms gbasịrị and gbasịa are used tentatively.

examples.igbo: O na-echekwa nne ya nke ọma.
examples.english: She takes good care of her mother.

examples.igbo: Chekwa ụmụaka ahụ ruo mgbe m lọtara.
examples.english: Look after those children until I return.

gloss: collect decayed compost for application to crops

examples.igbo: O na-akpo àgbụgbọ maka ubi ya.
examples.english: He collects decayed compost for his farm.

examples.igbo: Kpoo àgbụgbọ tinye n'ubi ọka.
examples.english: Collect decayed compost and put it in the maize farm.

note: The compound noun àgbụgbọ and its tones are not fully certain.

examples.igbo: O na-agụ Àgbà Ọfụū kwa ụtụtụ.
examples.english: He reads the New Testament every morning.

examples.igbo: Ị maara akụkọ dị n'Àgbà Ọfụū?
examples.english: Do you know the stories in the New Testament?

examples.igbo: O kpokọbara ụmụaka ọnū n'ụlọ.
examples.english: She gathered the children together in the house.

examples.igbo: Kpokọba ọnū ebe a, anyị ga-ekwu okwu.
examples.english: Gather together here, we will talk.

note: Tone on ọnū in inflected use may vary.

examples.igbo: O na-agba mbìbì ego n'ahịa.
examples.english: He goes about borrowing money at the market.

examples.igbo: Gbaa mbìbì ego n'aka nwanne gị.
examples.english: Borrow money from your brother.

gloss: hypocrisy; pretence; uncertain state, character (compare iru naàbò)

examples.igbo: Òdìkòọdīrọ ya na-ewe ndị mmadụ iwe.
examples.english: His hypocrisy annoys people.

examples.igbo: Ị maara òdìkòọdīrọ ya?
examples.english: Do you know his hypocrisy?

note: The sense of òdìkòọdīrọ ya is unclear; examples are tentative.

gloss: pack upon; lay(a cloth or mat) upon

examples.igbo: O kwasa akwa n'elu àkwà ndina.
examples.english: She spread the cloth on the bed.

examples.igbo: Kwasa akwa n'elu ala tupu ị nọdụ ala.
examples.english: Spread the cloth on the ground before you sit.

examples.igbo: O chịpụrụ ji niile n'ọba.
examples.english: He took all the yams away from the barn.

examples.igbo: Chịpụ mkpụrụ ndị a niile n'otu ebe.
examples.english: Take all these seeds away together.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ere afịa wayo n'ahịa.
examples.english: He sells inferior goods at the market.

examples.igbo: Azụla afịa wayo n'ahịa.
examples.english: Do not buy inferior goods at the market.

examples.igbo: O tiri nwa ahụ aka n'isi.
examples.english: She hit the child on the head.

examples.igbo: Tie bọl ahụ n'ike.
examples.english: Strike the ball hard.

examples.igbo: Ǹjọ ọ na-eme na-ewute nne ya.
examples.english: The evil he does pains his mother.

examples.igbo: Ịgha ụgha bụ ǹjọ.
examples.english: Telling lies is a sin.

examples.igbo: Ha rọrọ obì kwaga Aba.
examples.english: They migrated to Aba.

examples.igbo: Rọọ obì n'ebe ọzọ.
examples.english: Migrate to another place.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-egwu n'ìlo.
examples.english: The children are playing outside.

examples.igbo: Ha nọ n'ìlo na-akpọ nkụ.
examples.english: They are outside gathering firewood.

note: Examples illustrate the 'outside' sense; the 'without' sense is not confidently idiomatic with this word.

examples.igbo: O tinyere mmiri n'ime ndasì.
examples.english: She put water in the tumbler.

examples.igbo: Ndasì a dị ọcha.
examples.english: This tumbler is clean.

examples.igbo: O jiri nlafù dọpụta nwa agbọghọ ahụ.
examples.english: He used seduction to lure that girl.

examples.igbo: Nlafù adịghị adịte aka.
examples.english: Deceit does not last long.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akwọ ekwòrò maka ọrụ ọhụrụ m.
examples.english: He is envious of my new job.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji akwọ ekwòrò maka ihe nwanne gị nwere?
examples.english: Why are you envious of what your brother has?

examples.igbo: Nwa m na-asu iwe n'ihi na ọ nataghị ego.
examples.english: My child is sulking because he did not get money.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji asu iwe n'ebe m nọ?
examples.english: Why are you sulking at me?

gloss: place where refuse is disposed; dunghill (usually deliberately kept as store of manure for fertilizing land); compost heap; rubbish heap

examples.igbo: Anyị na-atụba ahịhịa n'àgbụgbō dị n'azụ ụlọ.
examples.english: We throw weeds into the dunghill behind the house.

examples.igbo: Àgbụgbō ahụ na-esi ísì ọjọọ n'oge mmiri.
examples.english: That dunghill smells bad in the rainy season.

gloss: unroof; break up roof; be broken A gà-àkpụkpò ụnọ  ānyị ochiìè echi Our old house will be unroofed tomorrow

examples.igbo: A ga-àkpụkpò ụlọ anyị ochie echi.
examples.english: Our old house will be unroofed tomorrow.

examples.igbo: Kpụkpọọ ụlọ ahụ tupu mmiri abịa.
examples.english: Unroof that house before the rain comes.

examples.igbo: Ọrụ ugbo na-enye anyị ego n'oge owuwe ihe ubi.
examples.english: Farming gives us money during harvest.

examples.igbo: Ị na-achọ ọrụ ọhụrụ n'obodo a?
examples.english: Are you looking for a new job in this town?

gloss: clear a path, road, of weeds

examples.igbo: Nna m na-abọ èzi n'ubi ya kwa ụtụtụ.
examples.english: My father clears the path in his farm every morning.

examples.igbo: Bọọ èzi ka anyị wee gafee n'ọhịa.
examples.english: Clear the path so we can pass through the field.

gloss: term for most of the people of Anambra LGA Division or their dialect of Igbo

examples.igbo: Ndị Ìgbò Adàgbè na-azụ ahịa n'ọma ahịa anyị.
examples.english: The Igbo Adagbe people trade in our market.

examples.igbo: Ị na-asụ Ìgbò Adàgbè nke ọma?
examples.english: Do you speak Igbo Adagbe well?
