examples.igbo: O tinyere isi ya n'ofili isī dị nro.
examples.english: She put her head on the soft pillow.

examples.igbo: Nwa m na-ehi ụra n'elu ofili isī ugbu a.
examples.english: My child is sleeping on the pillow now.

examples.igbo: Anyị nọ n'ìkpele mmīli na-akụ azụ.
examples.english: We are at the river bank fishing.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-egwuri egwu n'ìkpele mmīli.
examples.english: Children are playing at the river bank.

examples.igbo: Nòdụ mmā, anyị ga-ahụ gị echi.
examples.english: Goodbye, we will see you tomorrow.

examples.igbo: O kwuru nòdụ mmā tupu ọ lawa.
examples.english: He said goodbye before he left.

examples.igbo: Kekwaa eriri akpa ahụ, ọ tọpụla.
examples.english: Re-tie that bag's rope, it has loosened.

examples.igbo: Ekwesịrị m ịkekwa eriri ibu ahụ tupu anyị apụ.
examples.english: I should re-tie the load's rope before we leave.

note: Some speakers use slightly different past/infinitive forms of -kekwa.

examples.igbo: Nne m nwere ezemfo, ọ naghị ata ọkà.
examples.english: My mother has tooth loss; she doesn't chew corn.

examples.igbo: Gịnị kpatara ezemfo gị?
examples.english: What caused your tooth loss?

note: The exact range of ezemfo (tooth loss vs. toothless state) varies.

examples.igbo: Osimiri ahụ mìrì, anyị agaghị agafe ya.
examples.english: That river is deep; we will not cross it.

examples.igbo: Ọ mìrì n'ime mmiri ruo n'ikpere.
examples.english: He sank into the water up to his knee.

note: Conjugation and sense of -mì can vary by context.

examples.igbo: Nne m zụtara akpụ abụọ n'ahịa.
examples.english: My mother bought two cassavas in the market.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-esi akpụ taa?
examples.english: Will you cook cassava today?

examples.igbo: Wèni aka gị elu.
examples.english: Raise your hand.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ewèni igbe ahụ n'ala.
examples.english: He is lifting that box from the ground.

note: The verb stem is clear, but inflectional tone may differ by dialect.

examples.igbo: Akpa a bụ ǹkè nwanne m.
examples.english: This bag is my brother's.

examples.igbo: Ǹkè ọ ka mma, nke a ma ọ bụ nke ahụ?
examples.english: Which one is better, this one or that one?

examples.igbo: Alaka ụlọ ọrụ anyị dị n'Enugu.
examples.english: Our branch office is in Enugu.

examples.igbo: Alaka ụlọ ọrụ gị dị n'ebee?
examples.english: Where is your branch office?

examples.igbo: Chịdèbe oche ahụ n'akụkụ m.
examples.english: Bring that chair near me.

examples.igbo: Ọ chịdèbèrè akpa ya n'akụkụ ọnụ ụzọ.
examples.english: He brought his bag near the door.

note: Past-tense tone marking of -chịdèbe is uncertain.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka tụsara mmiri n'elu ibe ha.
examples.english: The children splashed water on each other.

examples.igbo: Tụsaa ọkà ahụ n'ala ka ọ kpọọ nkụ.
examples.english: Strew that corn on the ground so it dries.

examples.igbo: Ugbō anyị dị n'akụkụ osimiri.
examples.english: Our farm is by the river.

examples.igbo: Ị na-aga ugbō taa?
examples.english: Are you going to the farm today?

examples.igbo: O lefọrọ ji ahụ, o debere ụfọdụ maka echi.
examples.english: He sold off that yam, keeping some for tomorrow.

examples.igbo: Lefọọ ọka gị, hapụ ụfọdụ maka mkpụrụ.
examples.english: Sell off your maize, keep some for seed.

note: -lefọ is rare in everyday speech; I have treated it as selling part of a stock and leaving the rest, but the sense may be narrower than that.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka kwòbàrà n'ime ụlọ mgbe mmiri bidoro izo.
examples.english: The children rushed into the house when the rain started.

examples.igbo: Kwòbaa n'ime ụlọ, mmiri na-ezo!
examples.english: Rush inside the house, it is raining!

gloss: mislead; deceive; advise wrongly; seduce; push out of the way

examples.igbo: O nufùrù m n'ahịa, m wee zụta ji rere ure.
examples.english: He misled me at the market, so I bought rotten yams.

examples.igbo: Ònye nufùrù gị ka ị zụta ihe ahụ?
examples.english: Who misled you into buying that thing?

note: The word carries several senses; I have written only the 'mislead/deceive' one.

examples.igbo: Uwe ya dọwara, bọ ikè ya pụtara.
examples.english: His clothes tore and his bare buttocks showed.

examples.igbo: Kpuchie bọ ikè gị, mmadụ na-abịa!
examples.english: Cover your bare buttocks, someone is coming!

note: Colloquial expression; written as given, with 'bọ' and 'ikè' separate.

examples.igbo: O bịakpèrè àzụ n'ọsọ ụmụaka ahụ.
examples.english: He came last in that children's race.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji abịakpè àzụ mgbe niile?
examples.english: Why do you always come last?

note: Inflected the stem as bịakpèrè / abịakpè; the compound is not common, so the inflection is my best reading of it.

examples.igbo: O busàsịrị nkume n'okporo ụzọ ahụ.
examples.english: He scattered stones about on that road.

examples.igbo: Ònye busàsịrị osisi ndị a n'ụzọ?
examples.english: Who scattered these heavy logs about on the road?

examples.igbo: O nyere m otu mkpì ọjị.
examples.english: He gave me one section of kola nut.

examples.igbo: Ọjị a nwere mkpì isii.
examples.english: This kola nut has six sections.

gloss: press to bring out liquid or paste(completely)

examples.igbo: O pị̀chara akwa ahụ, mmiri ya niile pụta.
examples.english: She wrung that cloth out and all its water came out.

examples.igbo: Pị̀chaa mkpụrụ ahụ, mmanụ ya pụta.
examples.english: Press that seed thoroughly, let its oil come out.

note: Took the -cha form as the completive of pị̀, matching the gloss 'completely'.

examples.igbo: O gbakùtara àzụ n'ọrụ ahụ.
examples.english: He turned back from that work.

examples.igbo: Ị gbakùtara àzụ n'okwu anyị kwuru?
examples.english: Did you go back on what we agreed?

examples.igbo: O kegidere beèlùtù ọhụrụ n'úkwù ya.
examples.english: He fastened a new belt around his waist.

examples.igbo: Ònye zụtara beèlùtù ọhụrụ a?
examples.english: Who bought this new belt?

examples.igbo: Mmanụ aṅụ na-atụ ụtọ nke ukwuu.
examples.english: Honey is very sweet.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-atụ gị ụtọ ma ị ṅụọ ya?
examples.english: Does it taste sweet to you when you drink it?

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ zụrụ ụzọ n'ike.
examples.english: That man slammed the door hard.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji zụọ ụzọ n'abalị?
examples.english: Why did you bang the door at night?

examples.igbo: Akụkọ ọ kọrọ anyị bụ ǹkọkị̀rịkọ.
examples.english: The story he told us is unrealistic.

examples.igbo: Ị kwenyere n'ǹkọkị̀rịkọ dị otú ahụ?
examples.english: Do you believe such an unrealistic story?

examples.igbo: Ọ na-aga ahịa n'ụtụtụ kwà mbòsì.
examples.english: He goes to market in the morning daily.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ekpe ekpere kwà mbòsì?
examples.english: Do you pray daily?

gloss: boil; produce bubbles due to heat from a source

examples.igbo: Mmiri ahụ na-agbọ n'ite.
examples.english: The water is boiling in the pot.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere mmiri na-agbọ ugbua?
examples.english: Why is the water boiling now?

gloss: peel; yam, orange, or something else

examples.igbo: O bèchara ji maka nri abalị.
examples.english: She peeled yam for dinner.

examples.igbo: Bèchaa oroma ahụ, anyị ga-eri ya.
examples.english: Peel that orange, we will eat it.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-anụ ùnù ịzụ ụmụ ya.
examples.english: She struggles to raise her children.

examples.igbo: Ị na-anụ ùnù maka ego ugbua?
examples.english: Are you struggling for money now?

examples.igbo: Ọ mara n'ime mmiri oyi.
examples.english: He jumped into cold water.

examples.igbo: Ma n'ala, anyị na-eche gị.
examples.english: Jump down, we are waiting for you.

note: The sense of 'ma' as jump is uncommon; the examples are simple and context makes the meaning clear.

gloss: give a present make an offering (especially in church during harvest, and periodically); make donation

examples.igbo: O nyere ònyìnye na chọọchị ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: He gave an offering in church yesterday.

examples.igbo: Nye ònyìnye gị taa, Chukwu ga-agọ gị.
examples.english: Give your offering today, God will bless you.

examples.igbo: O bìkara osisi ahụ ụzọ abụọ.
examples.english: He cut that wood into two.

examples.igbo: Bìka eriri ahụ, ọ dị ogologo.
examples.english: Cut that rope asunder, it is long.

note: 'bìka' is less common; the examples are straightforward but may vary by dialect.

examples.igbo: Ọ sụrụ m òkpọ n'ihu.
examples.english: He punched me in the face.

examples.igbo: Ekwela ị su nwanne gị òkpọ.
examples.english: Don't punch your brother.

examples.igbo: Ha chụdara ewu gbada n'ime ndagwurugwu.
examples.english: They chased the goat down into the valley.

examples.igbo: Chụda ya gbada n'ala!
examples.english: Chase it down to the ground!

gloss: develop into sore or ulcer (of fresh wound)

examples.igbo: Onyá ahụ bara ọnya n'ụkwụ ya.
examples.english: That wound developed into a sore on his leg.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụrụ na ị ghara ịsa ya, ọ ga-aba ọnya.
examples.english: If you don't wash it, it will become a sore.

examples.igbo: O sere eserese nke ụlọ ahụ.
examples.english: He drew a picture of that house.

examples.igbo: See foto anyị n'ihu ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: Take a picture of us in front of the school.

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ mapụrụ imi ya.
examples.english: That child blew his nose.

examples.igbo: Mapụ imi gị tupu ị banye n'ụlọ.
examples.english: Blow your nose before you enter the house.

gloss: cut short; shorten; abbreviate (story, speech, etc.)

examples.igbo: O bere okwu ya nkenke.
examples.english: He shortened his speech.

examples.igbo: Bere akụkọ ahụ nkenke, anyị na-aga.
examples.english: Shorten that story, we are going.

examples.igbo: Onye nkuzi ahụ ghachiri n'ọkwa ya.
examples.english: That teacher returned to his position.

examples.igbo: Anyị ga-aghachi n'ụlọ akwụkwọ echi.
examples.english: We will return to school tomorrow.

gloss: let it be as you have said

examples.igbo: Ìsee, m kwetara.
examples.english: Let it be as you have said, I agree.

examples.igbo: Ìsee, ka anyị gaa.
examples.english: Let it be as you have said, let's go.

examples.igbo: Onye ọji ahụ bụ enyi m.
examples.english: That black person is my friend.

examples.igbo: Ị ma onye ọji ahụ?
examples.english: Do you know that black person?

examples.igbo: Anyị fadara n'ime ụgbọala ahụ.
examples.english: We squeezed into that car.

examples.igbo: Fado akwa ndị a n'ime akpa.
examples.english: Stuff these clothes into the bag.

examples.igbo: Ndị uwe ojii napụtara okwu n'ọnụ ya.
examples.english: The police forced him to speak.

examples.igbo: Gịnị ga-anapụta okwu n'ọnụ ya?
examples.english: What will force him to speak?

note: The phrase is uncommon; examples are tentative.

examples.igbo: Onye na-akpụ ígwè na-arụ ekò n'ọkụ.
examples.english: The blacksmith blows the bellows at the fire.

examples.igbo: Rụọ ekò ọsọ ọsọ ka ọkụ mụnye.
examples.english: Blow the bellows quickly so the fire brightens.

examples.igbo: Azụ̀ òkpọ èbùnù na-egwu n'ala mmiri.
examples.english: The òkpọ èbùnù fish swims at the bottom of the water.

examples.igbo: Ị hụtụla òkpọ èbùnù n'osimiri a?
examples.english: Have you seen òkpọ èbùnù in this river?

note: The fish name is rare; examples are sound but specialized.

examples.igbo: Nne ya kere ya ekike mara mma.
examples.english: Her mother dressed her beautifully.

examples.igbo: Kee nwa ahụ ekike ọma tupu anyị apụọ.
examples.english: Dress the child nicely before we leave.

examples.igbo: Ji ndị ahụ eletọla n'ọba.
examples.english: Those yams have become very rotten in the barn.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụrụ na mmiri abanye, ọ ga-aletọ.
examples.english: If water enters, it will become very rotten.

gloss: subdue; tame; beat very severely (literally beat till the eyes become soft)

examples.igbo: Ha na-atilọ anya ya n'ụlọ mkpọrọ.
examples.english: They are beating him severely in prison.

examples.igbo: Onye na-azụ ịnyịnya na-atilọ anya ha.
examples.english: The horse trainer tames them.

gloss: exercise patience towards someone's offensiveness and waiting for the right time to act

examples.igbo: Nne ya na-edè okwu ọjọọ ya.
examples.english: His mother patiently bears with his offensive words.

examples.igbo: Dè ya, oge ga-abịa mgbe ọ ga-akwụ ụgwọ.
examples.english: Bear with him; the time will come when he will pay.

note: The exact sense and usage of dè/edè are uncertain; examples are tentative.

examples.igbo: O kpụnitara oche ahụ nso tebụl.
examples.english: He drew the chair up to the table.

examples.igbo: Kpụnita ụkwụ gị ka mmiri ghara imetọ gị.
examples.english: Pull up your legs so the water does not wet you.

examples.igbo: O kpụrụ àfù ọnụ ya taa.
examples.english: He shaved his beard today.

examples.igbo: Kpụọ àfù ọnụ gị tupu agbamakwụkwọ.
examples.english: Shave your beard before the wedding.

examples.igbo: Ọdịdị ụlọ ahụ masịrị m.
examples.english: I like the shape of that house.

examples.igbo: Gịnị bụ ọdịdị osisi a?
examples.english: What is the shape of this tree?

gloss: be smooth (of stone); be very smooth and shining

examples.igbo: Nkume ahụ kwọrọ mụlụmụlụ nke ukwuu.
examples.english: That stone is very smooth and shining.

examples.igbo: O kwọrọ mụlụmụlụ dị ka enyo.
examples.english: It is smooth and shining like a mirror.

examples.igbo: Pastọ ahụ bikwàsị̀ aka n'isi onye ọrịa.
examples.english: That pastor laid hands on the sick person's head.

examples.igbo: Bikwàsị̀ aka n'isi nwa gị tupu ị laa.
examples.english: Lay hands on your child's head before you leave.

examples.igbo: O dọnyere ego n'ime akpa.
examples.english: He put money into the bag.

examples.igbo: Dọnye nri ahụ n'ite.
examples.english: Put that food into the pot.

examples.igbo: Ụlọ anyị nwere ọkụ electric.
examples.english: Our house has electric light.

examples.igbo: Waya electric gbawara n'okporo ámá.
examples.english: An electric wire broke on the street.

note: Loanword; modern Igbo often spells it eletrik/eletriki.

gloss: see to the bottom (literally and fig.)

examples.igbo: O fụmìrì mmiri ahụ ruo ala.
examples.english: He saw to the bottom of that water.

examples.igbo: Ị fụmìrì ihe kpatara okwu a?
examples.english: Did you get to the bottom of what caused this matter?

gloss: shallow well; pit, well for collecting rain-water (òmị more common in Onitsha Town)

examples.igbo: Ndị ọrụ na-egwu ùmị n'azụ ụlọ.
examples.english: The workers are digging a well behind the house.

examples.igbo: Mmiri ozuzo jupụtara ùmị ahụ.
examples.english: Rainwater filled that well.

gloss: retch; make feel nausea; cause nausea; cause to throw up

examples.igbo: Ụgbọ ala ahụ mere ka m hụ̀ agbọọ̄.
examples.english: That car made me retch.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ahụ̀ agbọọ̄ mgbe ị na-anụ isi ya?
examples.english: Do you retch when you smell it?

examples.igbo: O nwere èbelè n'ebe nwatakịrị ahụ nọ.
examples.english: He had mercy on that child.

examples.igbo: Gosi èbelè nye ndị ogbenye.
examples.english: Show mercy to the poor.

examples.igbo: O chịkọrọ akwụkwọ ya niile.
examples.english: He gathered all his books.

examples.igbo: Chịkọ mkpụrụ osisi ndị ahụ n'ime nkata.
examples.english: Gather those fruits into the basket.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-adị òbò n'ụlọ kama ịrụ ọrụ.
examples.english: He is idle at home instead of working.

examples.igbo: Adịla òbò, gaa n'ọhịa rụọ ọrụ.
examples.english: Don't be idle, go to the farm and work.

gloss: (Dioscorea praehensilis Benth.) yam cultivar which never grows to a very great size, of inferior quality

examples.igbo: Ji ābị anyị kụrụ erughị oke ibu.
examples.english: The ji abị we planted did not grow very big.

examples.igbo: Ị na-ere ji ābị n'ahịa a?
examples.english: Are you selling ji abị in this market?

gloss: pick out, off (things which stick, e.g. fleas on dog)

examples.igbo: O tụchàpụrụ àkịkị niile dị n'ahụ nkịta.
examples.english: He picked off all the ticks on the dog's body.

examples.igbo: Tụchàpụ̀ àkịkị ndị ahụ n'ahụ nkịta.
examples.english: Pick off those ticks from the dog's body.

examples.igbo: Ànì ụlō siri ike, osisi anaghị eto ya.
examples.english: Clay soil is hard, plants do not grow in it.

examples.igbo: Ị kụrụ ọka n'ànì ụlō?
examples.english: Did you plant corn in clay soil?

examples.igbo: O zọkwàsịrị ụkwụ m n'ụgbọ ahụ.
examples.english: He trod on my foot in that vehicle.

examples.igbo: Azọkwàsịla m n'ụkwụ ọzọ.
examples.english: Don't tread on my foot again.

gloss: mark parts of the body with ùlì

examples.igbo: Nne ya gbùrù ùlì n'aka nwa ya.
examples.english: Her mother marked uli on her child's hand.

examples.igbo: Ị gbùrù ùlì n'ụkwụ gị?
examples.english: Did you mark uli on your leg?

examples.igbo: O nuru ihe mere, o wee chi ikpe.
examples.english: He heard what happened and then complained.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji chi ikpe n'ebe m nọ?
examples.english: Why are you complaining to me?

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-akpọ ụgbà n'ama.
examples.english: The children are turning somersaults in the yard.

examples.igbo: Ị pụrụ ịkpọ ụgbà?
examples.english: Can you turn a somersault?

examples.igbo: O sèkasịrị akwụkwọ ahụ.
examples.english: He tore that paper into pieces.

examples.igbo: Sèkasị ya ntakịrị ntakịrị.
examples.english: Tear it into small pieces.

examples.igbo: M zụtara ùbe oyìbo atọ n'ahịa.
examples.english: I bought three pears in the market.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eri ùbe oyìbo a?
examples.english: Will you eat this pear?

gloss: grind pepper Ọ nà-àkwọ osè She is grinding pepper

examples.igbo: M na-akwọ osè maka ofe.
examples.english: I am grinding pepper for soup.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-akwọ osè taa?
examples.english: Will you grind pepper today?

examples.igbo: Uwe m akakpọla n'ikpere.
examples.english: My clothes have worn thin at the knee.

examples.igbo: Uwe gị akakpọla?
examples.english: Have your clothes worn thin?

examples.igbo: Nnụnụ fekwuru n'elu ụlọ.
examples.english: The bird flew to the roof.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ka nnụnụ na-efekwu n'osisi?
examples.english: Did you see the bird flying to the tree?

examples.igbo: Enekēn̄tị̀ọbā na-efe n'elu ụlọ.
examples.english: The swallow is flying over the house.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ enekēn̄tị̀ọbā n'akwụ?
examples.english: Did you see the swallow in the nest?

examples.igbo: Ọ nọ n'ụ̀fụ n'ihi ụgwọ.
examples.english: He is in distress because of debt.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji nọ n'ụ̀fụ?
examples.english: Why are you in distress?

examples.igbo: Ji a egheela nke ọma.
examples.english: This yam is properly cooked.

examples.igbo: Nri a egheela nke ọma?
examples.english: Is this food properly cooked?

examples.igbo: M zụtara ìpètè erìrì n'ahịa.
examples.english: I bought Citharinus latus at the market.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ìpètè erìrì n'ahịa?
examples.english: Did you see Citharinus latus at the market?

examples.igbo: Kọ ya aka, e jidela ya.
examples.english: Let go of it, do not hold it.

examples.igbo: Ọ kọrọ aka nwa ya.
examples.english: She let go of her child's hand.

examples.igbo: Akwụrụ m ụgwọ ọrụ taa.
examples.english: I was paid my wages today.

examples.igbo: Ị kwụrụ ụgwọ gị?
examples.english: Did you pay your debt?

gloss: wild Canna (Canna indica Linn.), seen in Agwụ shrines

examples.igbo: Agrì na-eto n'ụlọ Agwụ.
examples.english: Wild Canna grows at the Agwụ shrine.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ agrì n'ụzọ?
examples.english: Did you see wild Canna on the road?

gloss: title-name taken by or given to a wealthy person; inexhaustible wealth

examples.igbo: Ndị obodo kpọrọ ya Òdọlụkòọdò n'ihi akụ ya.
examples.english: The townspeople called him Òdọlụkòọdò because of his wealth.

examples.igbo: Òdọlụkòọdò, ị bara ọgaranya n'ezie?
examples.english: Òdọlụkòọdò, are you truly wealthy?

note: Rare title-name; examples show it as a title for a wealthy person.

examples.igbo: O jiri m̀kpareegbè kpochapụ egbe ya.
examples.english: He used a ramrod to clean his gun.

examples.igbo: Were m̀kpareegbè kpochapụ egbe tupu ị gaa ịchụ nta.
examples.english: Use a ramrod to clean the gun before you go hunting.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-enefe nne ya mgbe ọ na-arịa ọrịa.
examples.english: She looks after her mother when she is sick.

examples.igbo: Nefe ụmụaka ndị a nke ọma.
examples.english: Look after these children well.

note: Verb stem is uncommon; the inflected forms used are standard but not widely heard.

examples.igbo: Mkpụlụ obì ya dị ọcha.
examples.english: His heart is pure.

examples.igbo: Okwu ya sitere n'ime mkpụlụ obì ya.
examples.english: His words came from his soul.

note: Spelling follows the headword; some speakers may use mkpụrụ obi for soul.

gloss: stubbornness; habitual disobedience (usually of young person)

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ nwere mkpọchi ntị, ọ naghị anụ ihe a na-agwa ya.
examples.english: That child is stubborn; he does not listen to what he is told.

examples.igbo: Mkpọchi ntị ya na-ewe nne ya iwe.
examples.english: His stubbornness annoys his mother.

note: Normalized to standard mkpọchi ntị from the headword mkpòchi n tì.

examples.igbo: Onye nkịtị ọ bụla kwesịrị ịtụ vootu.
examples.english: Every commoner should vote.

examples.igbo: Ndị agha ahụ gbara ndị nkịtị aka na ntị.
examples.english: The soldiers warned the civilians.

gloss: have an award; be honored for an achievement

examples.igbo: Ọ tụrụ ùgò maka ọrụ ya sịrị ike.
examples.english: He was honored for his hard work.

examples.igbo: Ị tụọla ùgò maka mmeri gị?
examples.english: Have you received an award for your victory?

note: The phrase is less common; the inflected forms used are tụrụ and tụọla.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ ọkà elùlò nke obodo anyị.
examples.english: He is a counsellor of our town.

examples.igbo: Gaa jụọ ọkà elùlò ahụ ihe ị ga-eme.
examples.english: Go ask that adviser what you should do.

note: Tone adjusted to standard ọkà in the examples; headword is ọka elùlò.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-akụ ọkà n'ubi anyị.
examples.english: We plant maize in our farm.

examples.igbo: Kụọ ọkà tupu mmiri abịa.
examples.english: Plant maize before the rain comes.

gloss: be dear; (figurative)be close to the heart

examples.igbo: Nne m dị ree n'obi m.
examples.english: My mother is dear to my heart.

examples.igbo: Ọ dị ree n'obi gị?
examples.english: Is it dear to your heart?

note: The expression is idiomatic but the figurative sense is not used by all speakers.

gloss: be broadminded; clear the mind of prejudice

examples.igbo: Ọ chìchapụrụ obì ya wee nabata ndị ọbịa niile.
examples.english: He cleared his mind and welcomed all the visitors.

examples.igbo: Chìchapụ obì gị tupu i kpee ikpe.
examples.english: Clear your mind before you judge.

note: Rare verb phrase; I am not certain of the exact inflection -chìchapụrụ or whether this is the usual collocation.

examples.igbo: Ose àkwà dị n'Ihịàlà.
examples.english: Ose àkwà is at Ihiala.

examples.igbo: Ndị na-akụ azụ na-aga ose àkwà.
examples.english: The fishermen go to ose àkwà.

note: This appears to be a place name at Ihiala; I am unsure how it is used in everyday speech, so the examples are minimal.

examples.igbo: Ìzù bụ ụbọchị nke atọ n'izu Ẹkpẹyẹ.
examples.english: Ìzù is the third day of the Ẹkpẹyẹ week.

examples.igbo: N'ìzù, ndị obodo anaghị aga ahịa.
examples.english: On ìzù, the people of the town do not go to the market.

note: The four-day Ẹkpẹyẹ week is named differently in different areas, so the day count may vary by locality.

gloss: twist (especially somebody's mouth as punishment); give severe punishment; deal with; turning of bolt etc

examples.igbo: Nna ya hịọrọ ya ọnụ maka ịgha ụgha.
examples.english: His father twisted his mouth for him for lying.

examples.igbo: Hịọa mkpịsị ígwè ahụ ka ọ kwụsie ike.
examples.english: Turn that bolt so that it holds firm.

examples.igbo: Ọ nọ na-afacha eze ya mgbe o risịrị anụ.
examples.english: He was picking his teeth after eating meat.

examples.igbo: Fachaa eze gị tupu i laa ụra.
examples.english: Pick your teeth before you go to sleep.

examples.igbo: Ụkwụ ya fụrụ ọkpīìdùm.
examples.english: His leg swelled with elephantiasis.

examples.igbo: Dọkịta gwara ya na ọkpīìdùm na-akpa ụkwụ ya.
examples.english: The doctor told him that elephantiasis is affecting his leg.

note: The tone-marked vowel length in ọkpīìdùm is unusual; I kept the given spelling.

examples.igbo: Nwa ya nwanyị chaara òcha dị ka nne ya.
examples.english: Her daughter is fair in complexion like her mother.

examples.igbo: Ị na-acha òcha karịa ụmụnne gị?
examples.english: Are you fairer in complexion than your siblings?

examples.igbo: Azụrụ m ọlụ anụ ewu n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: I bought a leg of goat meat at the market today.

examples.igbo: Kee ọlụ anụ ahụ ụzọ abụọ.
examples.english: Cut that leg of meat into two.

examples.igbo: Ha na-akwujọ ya n'azụ ya.
examples.english: They speak evil of him behind his back.

examples.igbo: Ekwujọla mmadụ n'ihi na ị maghị eziokwu.
examples.english: Do not speak evil of anyone, because you do not know the truth.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-achu uchu n'ọrụ ugbo ya.
examples.english: He perseveres in his farm work.

examples.igbo: Chụọ uchu, ihe ga-agara gị nke ọma.
examples.english: Be industrious, and things will go well for you.

examples.igbo: Ụlọ anyị pèrè mpe, ma ọ dị mma.
examples.english: Our house is small, but it is fine.

examples.igbo: Nkịta gị pèrè mpe?
examples.english: Is your dog small?

note: Tonal pattern of pèrè is uncertain; the verb pe mpe is not common in everyday speech.

gloss: do as, be a young man

examples.igbo: Ọ na-eme okolobìà n'ihu ụmụ agbọghọ.
examples.english: He acts like a young man in front of the girls.

examples.igbo: Mee okolobìà n'ihu ndị mmadụ.
examples.english: Act like a young man before people.

examples.igbo: Anyị gabìgà nnukwu mmiri ozuzo n'ụzọ.
examples.english: We encountered heavy rain on the way.

examples.igbo: Ị gabìgàla ụdị nsogbu a?
examples.english: Have you experienced this kind of trouble?

examples.igbo: Ọ kpùchapùtàrà mmanụ niile n'ite.
examples.english: She scraped all the oil out of the pot.

examples.igbo: Kpùchapùta ofe ahụ niile tupu ị saa efere.
examples.english: Scrape out all that soup before you wash the plate.

examples.igbo: Ọ siri ǹgọ na ọ ga-abịa.
examples.english: He obstinately doubted that he would come.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji si ǹgọ n'okwu a?
examples.english: Why do you obstinately doubt this matter?

note: The exact sense and tonal form of -si ǹgọ are not clear to me.

gloss: freeborn children; children of a king or chief

examples.igbo: Ụmù deì zukọtara n'ụlọ eze.
examples.english: The chief's children gathered in the palace.

examples.igbo: Ị bụ nwa deì ma ọ bụ ohu?
examples.english: Are you a freeborn child or a slave?

note: Uncertain of the exact tone on deì.

examples.igbo: O yị̀rị anyị gaa ahịa.
examples.english: He accompanied us to the market.

examples.igbo: Yị̀e m gaa ahịa taa.
examples.english: Accompany me to the market today.

note: This verb is not common in the dialects I know; the forms given follow the gloss but I am unsure of usage.

gloss: be slippery, slip on or off (of rings, bracelets)

examples.igbo: Mgbaaka a na-agbụ àgbụ n'aka m.
examples.english: This bracelet keeps slipping off my hand.

examples.igbo: Jide ya nke ọma, ọ na-agbụ àgbụ.
examples.english: Hold it well, it is slippery.

examples.igbo: O rugòrò ala wepụta ego ahụ.
examples.english: He stooped down and picked up that money.

examples.igbo: Rugò ala ka ị banye n'ọnụ ụzọ.
examples.english: Stoop down so you can get through the doorway.

examples.igbo: O biri ji ahụ n'iberibe.
examples.english: He sliced that yam into pieces.

examples.igbo: Ị biri anụ ahụ n'iberibe?
examples.english: Did you cut that meat into pieces?

examples.igbo: Wụsị mmiri ahụ n'ala.
examples.english: Pour that water onto the ground.

examples.igbo: Ị wụsịrị ofe ahụ n'ala?
examples.english: Did you spill that soup on the ground?

examples.igbo: Anyị riri àzì efìfìè n'ụlọ.
examples.english: We ate lunch at home.

examples.igbo: Ị riri àzì efìfìè taa?
examples.english: Did you eat lunch today?

examples.igbo: O kwuru okwu n'ògbè.
examples.english: He spoke quietly.

examples.igbo: Bịa n'ògbè, nwa ahụ na-ehi ụra.
examples.english: Come quietly, the child is sleeping.

gloss: block road or way; obstruct ; stand in way of something or somebody

examples.igbo: Osisi dara nọchiri ụzọ.
examples.english: A tree fell and blocked the road.

examples.igbo: Gịnị nọchiri ụzọ n'ebe a?
examples.english: What blocked the way here?

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ kpabàtara n'ime ụlọ.
examples.english: The child wandered into the house.

examples.igbo: Kpabàta n'ime ogige ahụ.
examples.english: Walk into that garden.

examples.igbo: Èkpè afù, anyị bi n'ime obodo.
examples.english: At that time, we lived in the village.

examples.igbo: Èkpè afù, ị nọ n'ụlọ akwụkwọ?
examples.english: At that time, were you at school?

gloss: It is evening; the day declines

examples.igbo: Chi ànaā, anyị ga-ala n'ụlọ.
examples.english: It is evening; we will go home.

examples.igbo: Chi ànaā, ị ga-ala n'ụlọ?
examples.english: It is evening; will you go home?

examples.igbo: Detụ ọnụ na ofe a.
examples.english: Taste this soup.

examples.igbo: Ọ detụrụ ọnụ na nri ahụ.
examples.english: She tasted that food.

examples.igbo: Mkpọchi ụzọ ahụ mere ka anyị ghara ịbata.
examples.english: The locking of that door prevented us from entering.

examples.igbo: Ònye na-ahụ maka mkpọchi ụzọ a?
examples.english: Who is in charge of locking this door?

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-agòli n'ihi na echi bụ ezumike.
examples.english: The children are rejoicing because tomorrow is a holiday.

examples.igbo: Gòlienụ, ndị enyi m, oge ọma abịala!
examples.english: Rejoice, my friends, the good time has come!

gloss: mould large morsel of pounded fufu

examples.igbo: O na-ama òkpoko ụtàlà buru ibu.
examples.english: She is moulding a large morsel of pounded fufu.

examples.igbo: Maa òkpoko ụtàlà maka ndị ọbịa.
examples.english: Mould a large morsel of pounded fufu for the guests.

examples.igbo: O dọkpụrụ nwa ahụ sekpụ̀pụ̀ n'aka nne ya.
examples.english: He dragged the child away forcibly from its mother.

examples.igbo: Dọkpụrụ ya sekpụ̀pụ̀ pụọ ebe a.
examples.english: Drag him away forcibly from here.

examples.igbo: Ajō isi wetara ya ọdachi.
examples.english: Bad luck brought him misfortune.

examples.igbo: Ajō isi ọ na-eso gị?
examples.english: Is bad luck following you?

examples.igbo: Dàbere Chī n'oge nsogbu gị.
examples.english: Lean on God in your time of trouble.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-adàbere Chī kwa ụbọchị.
examples.english: He leans on God every day.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ nyụrụ maāmị̄rị̄ n'àkwà.
examples.english: The child urinated in bed.

examples.igbo: Ị nyụrụ maāmị̄rị̄ taa?
examples.english: Have you urinated today?

examples.igbo: Ha na-eru ajā n'akụkụ ụlọ.
examples.english: They are pouring away sand beside the house.

examples.igbo: Ruo ajā ahụ pụọ n'ụzọ.
examples.english: Pour that sand away from the road.

gloss: suck breast (of a mother by an infant, lit. drink breast)

examples.igbo: Nwa ọhụrụ na-aṅụ arā nne ya.
examples.english: The baby is sucking its mother's breast.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ ọ na-aṅụ arā?
examples.english: Is the baby sucking breast?

examples.igbo: Osisi ahụ so ogonogo ruo elu igwe.
examples.english: That tree is tall reaching the sky.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere osisi a ji so ogonogo?
examples.english: Why is this tree so tall?

gloss: make laugh; please; amuse; delight; be funny

examples.igbo: O na-asọ amụ n'oge nzukọ.
examples.english: He makes people laugh during meetings.

examples.igbo: Sọọ anyị amụ!
examples.english: Make us laugh!

examples.igbo: Nna m tụrụ òrùụra n'oche.
examples.english: My father dozed on the chair.

examples.igbo: Atụla òrùụra n'oge ọrụ.
examples.english: Do not doze during work.

examples.igbo: Mfụchata ya mere ka ọ jụọ ọtụtụ ajụjụ.
examples.english: His curiosity made him ask many questions.

examples.igbo: Ajụla ajụjụ niile; mfụchata karịrị akarị.
examples.english: Do not ask all the questions; excessive curiosity is bad.

examples.igbo: Elu igwe na-asè àmùmà n'abalị a.
examples.english: The sky is flashing lightning tonight.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ka ọ sere àmùmà tupu mmiri ezoo?
examples.english: Did you see how it flashed lightning before the rain fell?

examples.igbo: Dinwenu anyị, chebe anyị n'abalị a.
examples.english: Our Lord, protect us tonight.

examples.igbo: Kele Dinwenu anyị maka mmesịa.
examples.english: Thank our Lord for success.

gloss: secret place worshipped by Onitsha people

examples.igbo: Ndị Ònìchà na-efe Ànị Ònìchà.
examples.english: The Onitsha people worship Ànị Ònìchà.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ nanị ndị isi na-abanye n'Ànị Ònìchà.
examples.english: Only elders enter Ànị Ònìchà.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-adulu nwa ya gaa ahịa.
examples.english: She accompanies her child to the market.

examples.igbo: O jiri okwu ụtọ dulu nwa agbọghọ ahụ.
examples.english: He used sweet words to seduce that girl.

examples.igbo: Anyị lijuru afọ n'oriri ahụ.
examples.english: We ate to satiety at that feast.

examples.igbo: Ị lijuru afọ?
examples.english: Are you full?

examples.igbo: Ọ zadoro nwa ya n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: He supported his child in school.

examples.igbo: Zado nwanne gị n'oge ihe isi ike.
examples.english: Support your sibling in difficult times.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-agbagha okwu nne ya mgbe niile.
examples.english: He always argues with his mother.

examples.igbo: Gbaghala okwu m; gee ntị nke ọma.
examples.english: Do not contradict me; listen well.

gloss: keep silence; refrain from answering; endure

examples.igbo: Ọ gbachiri nkịtị mgbe m jụrụ ya ajụjụ.
examples.english: He kept silent when I asked him a question.

examples.igbo: Gbachi nkịtị, ka anyị nụ ihe nna gị na-ekwu.
examples.english: Keep quiet, let us hear what your father is saying.

examples.igbo: Nkịta dọkọrọ anụ n'ụkwụ nwata ahụ.
examples.english: The dog tore flesh on that child's leg.

examples.igbo: Gịnị dọkọrọ anụ ewu gị?
examples.english: What tore your goat's flesh?

gloss: framework of roof (before thatching or fixing the sheets)

examples.igbo: O tinyere ndumì ụnò tupu o were akwụkwọ kpuchie ụlọ.
examples.english: He put up the roof framework before he used sheets to cover the house.

examples.igbo: Ndumì ụnò ahụ ọ dịla njikere?
examples.english: Is that roof framework ready?

gloss: a structure or tree that forms a shade; an umbrella

examples.igbo: Anyị nọdụrụ n'okpuru òcheǹdò osisi ahụ.
examples.english: We sat under the shade of that tree.

examples.igbo: Were òcheǹdò gị pụọ, mmiri na-ezo.
examples.english: Take your umbrella, it is raining.

gloss: a house where prostitutes or sex workers do business in; brothel

examples.igbo: Ndị uwe ojii mechiri ụlāàkwụ̀nà ahụ.
examples.english: The police closed that brothel.

examples.igbo: Ònye nwe ụlāàkwụ̀nà a?
examples.english: Who owns this brothel?

gloss: be stronger or increase in strength (e.g. of growing thing)

examples.igbo: Osisi a na-akata kemgbe anyị nyere ya mmiri.
examples.english: This tree has been growing stronger since we watered it.

examples.igbo: Nwa gị ọ na-akata ugbu a?
examples.english: Is your child getting stronger now?

examples.igbo: Ọ fụfere isi ya mgbe m jụrụ ya ajụjụ.
examples.english: He shook his head when I asked him a question.

examples.igbo: Fụfè isi gị ma ị chọghị.
examples.english: Shake your head if you don't want to.

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ tiwara efere.
examples.english: That child broke a plate.

examples.igbo: Ònye tiwara ite m?
examples.english: Who broke my pot?

gloss: to eject saliva from the mouth; spit

examples.igbo: Ọ gbụrụ asụ̄ n'ala.
examples.english: He spat on the ground.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji agbụ asụ̄ ebe a?
examples.english: Why are you spitting here?

examples.igbo: Mkpà ǹsịkō na-ata m n'ụkwụ.
examples.english: Pins-and-needles is biting me in the foot.

examples.igbo: Mkpà ǹsịkō na-ata gị n'aka?
examples.english: Is pins-and-needles biting you in the hand?

examples.igbo: Okìlì na-eto n'ubi anyị.
examples.english: Guinea-corn is growing in our farm.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara okìlì n'ahịa taa?
examples.english: Did you buy guinea-corn at the market today?

examples.igbo: Òdìgìrì dị n'akụkụ obodo anyị.
examples.english: There is a lagoon beside our town.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ òdìgìrì ahụ n'ụzọ?
examples.english: Did you see that lagoon on the way?

gloss: confess voluntarily to crime, abomination, or other bad deed

examples.igbo: Ọ sàrà ifì n'ihu ndị okenye.
examples.english: He confessed before the elders.

examples.igbo: Sàa ifì gị, ka e wee gbaghara gị.
examples.english: Confess your deed, so that you may be forgiven.

note: Past and imperative tone of -sà ifì may vary.

examples.igbo: Ìnìne mgbolokō toro n'ubi anyị.
examples.english: The ìnìne mgbolokō grew in our farm.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-esi ìnìne mgbolokō n'ofe taa?
examples.english: Will you cook ìnìne mgbolokō in soup today?

note: Rare plant name; examples show the vegetable sense.

examples.igbo: Anyị gafere walala ụzò dị warara.
examples.english: We passed a narrow path.

examples.igbo: Soro walala ụzò a gaa n'ubi.
examples.english: Follow this path to the farm.

note: Rare path term; used as given.

gloss: turn round and round; be undecided

examples.igbo: Ọ nọ na-achìghalị n'okwu ahụ.
examples.english: He is undecided about that matter.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-achìghalị ruo mgbe ebighị ebi?
examples.english: Will you keep wavering forever?

note: Verb sense 'be undecided' used; inflection is approximate.

examples.igbo: Ọ kwatùrù ya n'ala.
examples.english: He knocked him down.

examples.igbo: Kwatụọ osisi ahụ n'ala!
examples.english: Knock that tree down!

note: Imperative form kwatụọ is my best standard rendering.

gloss: squeeze or press to bring out liquid(completely)

examples.igbo: Ọ na-apà mmiri n'akwa ahụ.
examples.english: She is squeezing water out of that cloth.

examples.igbo: Pàa akwa ahụ nke ọma.
examples.english: Wring that cloth well.

note: Inflection of pà is approximate.

gloss: social name of a child in his mother's family, home, locality, village or birthplace e.g. Each of the children of a woman who hails from Obi's family is known as a nwadiànì among Obi's family and kin. If a child's home town is Nneewi but his mother's birthplace is Nnoobi, that child is a nwadiànì at Nnoobi; if the mother's birthplace is the United States the child when in Nigeria is said to be nwadiànì in the United States

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ nwadiànì n'ala nne ya.
examples.english: He is a nwadiani in his mother's land.

examples.igbo: Ị bụ nwadiànì n'obodo nne gị?
examples.english: Are you a nwadiani in your mother's town?

gloss: scramble (for something); rush to consume or get something

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-abụ ụbụ maka nri.
examples.english: Children scramble for food.

examples.igbo: Ị na-abụ ụbụ maka oche?
examples.english: Are you scrambling for a seat?

note: Meaning understood, but exact verb construction and tone of bụ ụbụ are uncertain.

examples.igbo: Nne m zụtara ife mkpofu n'ahịa.
examples.english: My mother bought offal at the market.

examples.igbo: Ì na-eri ife mkpofu n'ụlọ gị?
examples.english: Do you eat offal in your house?

examples.igbo: Anyị jiri nku opere sie ofe.
examples.english: We used palm-tree firewood to cook soup.

examples.igbo: Nku opere ahụ adịghị ọkụ nke ọma.
examples.english: That palm-tree firewood does not burn well.

examples.igbo: Òbùbò ọkū ahụ ka na-enwu n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: That heap of glowing coals is still glowing in the morning.

examples.igbo: Kpuchie òbùbò ọkū ka ọ ghara ịgbasa.
examples.english: Cover the heap of glowing coals so it does not spread.

gloss: the general public, especially including all classes of people

examples.igbo: Ọ̀hànèezè niile bịara ịhụ eze n'ụlọ.
examples.english: The general public all came to see the king in his house.

examples.igbo: Ọ̀hànèezè kwuru okwu banyere ụzọ ahụ.
examples.english: The general public spoke about that road.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka tụrụ ùbùlụ ākwa n'ala ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: The children threw eggshells on the school ground.

examples.igbo: Ùbùlụ ākwa ahụ gbajiri n'aka nwa ahụ.
examples.english: That eggshell broke in that child's hand.

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ na-agbe n'ala dị ka nwa ọhụrụ.
examples.english: That child is crawling on the ground like a baby.

examples.igbo: Gbe nwayọ ka onye ọ bụla ghara ịhụ gị.
examples.english: Crawl slowly so that nobody sees you.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ebo nwa ahụ anya n'ahịa.
examples.english: He is staring at that child at the market.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji na-ebo m anya?
examples.english: Why are you staring at me?

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ na-adị ụjọ nke ukwuu.
examples.english: That child is very cowardly.

examples.igbo: Ị na-adị ụjọ ịgafe mmiri n'abalị?
examples.english: Are you afraid to cross the river at night?

examples.igbo: Nwa m nwanyị na-egwu nnwa egwū n'ụlọ.
examples.english: My daughter is playing with a doll in the house.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara ya nnwa egwū maka ụbọchị ọmụmụ?
examples.english: Did you buy her a doll for her birthday?

examples.igbo: Osisi a gbadoro mkpòlògwù n'ala anyị.
examples.english: This tree took root in our land.

examples.igbo: Osisi a ọ ga-agbado mkpòlògwù n'ala a?
examples.english: Will this tree take root in this soil?

examples.igbo: Nwaàdikē ahụ lụrụ agha n'oge gara aga.
examples.english: That warrior fought in a war in the past.

examples.igbo: Ì maara nwaàdikē nke obodo a?
examples.english: Do you know the hero of this town?

gloss: The children are scrambling over the food given them

examples.igbo: Ụmụ akā nà-àbụ n'efere osikapa ahụ.
examples.english: The children are scrambling over that plate of rice.

examples.igbo: Ụmụ akā nà-àbụ n'ihi na e nyere ha nri?
examples.english: Are the children scrambling because they were given food?

note: The headword is itself a full clause; the examples show it in context.

gloss: Minister in holy orders; pastor; deacon; priest, etc. (literally messenger of God)

examples.igbo: Ụkò Chukwu ahụ ziri anyị ozi ọma.
examples.english: That pastor preached the gospel to us.

examples.igbo: Ì hụrụ ụkò Chukwu n'ụlọ ụka?
examples.english: Did you see the priest in the church?

examples.igbo: Nwa m nwoke gbara òkolobìà ugbua.
examples.english: My son has become an adolescent now.

examples.igbo: Òle mgbe ọ ga-agba òkolobìà?
examples.english: When will he become an adolescent?

note: Rare term; examples use standard inflection.

gloss: run to and from; be going to and from a place (including the world of spirits)

examples.igbo: Ọ na-agba ǹje n'ọhịa.
examples.english: He is running to and fro in the bush.

examples.igbo: Gbaa ǹje n'ụlọ ahịa, weta mmanụ.
examples.english: Run to the market and bring oil.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-ewe ezumike n'òkàlà arò.
examples.english: We take a break at mid-year.

examples.igbo: Òkàlà arò ọ bụ oge okpomọkụ?
examples.english: Is mid-year the hot season?

note: The term is uncommon; the examples are idiomatic.

examples.igbo: O kpụdara osisi ahụ n'ala.
examples.english: He pulled down that tree to the ground.

examples.igbo: Kpụdàa akpa ahụ n'elu ụlọ.
examples.english: Move that bag down from the roof.

examples.igbo: Azụ jùrù aka n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: Fish is plentiful in the market today.

examples.igbo: Anụ ọ na-eju aka n'ahịa ugbua?
examples.english: Is meat plentiful in the market now?

examples.igbo: Nne ya makùtara ya n'obi.
examples.english: His mother embraced him completely to her chest.

examples.igbo: Makùta nwa ahụ mgbe ọ bịara.
examples.english: Embrace that child completely when she comes.

examples.igbo: Ndị uwe ojii na-ebu ife aghā.
examples.english: The police carry weapons.

examples.igbo: Edebela ife aghā n'ime ụlọ gị.
examples.english: Do not keep a weapon inside your house.

note: Rare expression; examples are plausible.

examples.igbo: O na-efe ọlụ ụmụ akwụkwọ n'ụlọ akwụkwọ.
examples.english: He supervises the pupils' work at school.

examples.igbo: Fee ọlụ ha nke ọma taa.
examples.english: Supervise their work well today.

note: Rare verb; construction checked.

examples.igbo: Iru akā m na-egbu mgbu ugbu a.
examples.english: My forearm is aching now.

examples.igbo: O ji nwa ya n'iru akā.
examples.english: She carried her child on her forearm.

examples.igbo: Mechi ụzọ ahụ tupu mmiri abịa.
examples.english: Close that door before the rain comes.

examples.igbo: Ị mechiela ite ahụ nke ọma tupu ị pụọ?
examples.english: Have you covered that pot well before leaving?

gloss: take, remove everything; pack away everything

examples.igbo: O kwakọlụrụ akwa ya niile n'igbe.
examples.english: He packed all his clothes away in the box.

examples.igbo: Kwakọlụ ihe niile tupu anyị apụ.
examples.english: Pack everything away before we leave.

note: Rare verb; inflections are plausible.

examples.igbo: O gbuliri ala ahụ tupu ọ kụọ ihe.
examples.english: He tilled that soil before planting.

examples.igbo: Gbuli ala a maka akwụkwọ ndụ.
examples.english: Till this soil for vegetables.

note: Rare verb; examples are plausible.

examples.igbo: Mkpụmkpụ mmadù ahụ bụ enyi m.
examples.english: That short person is my friend.

examples.igbo: Ị maara mkpụmkpụ mmadù ahụ n'ụlọ akwụkwọ?
examples.english: Do you know that short person at school?

examples.igbo: O fesara nnu n'elu anụ ahụ.
examples.english: She sprinkled salt over the meat.

examples.igbo: Fesa ntakịrị mmiri n'elu akwa ahụ.
examples.english: Sprinkle a little water over that cloth.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ rubegara nna ya isi.
examples.english: That child submitted to his father.

examples.igbo: Rube isi n'ebe nne gị nọ.
examples.english: Submit to your mother.

examples.igbo: Ndị ntā ahụ gbara enyí n'ọhịa.
examples.english: Those hunters shot an elephant in the bush.

examples.igbo: Ndị ntā na-aga n'ọhịa n'abalị mgbe ụfọdụ.
examples.english: Hunters sometimes go to the bush at night.

gloss: has or have not; not yet

examples.igbo: Ọ bèghị abịa n'ụlọ anyị taa.
examples.english: He has not yet come to our house today.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ị bèghị eri nri taa?
examples.english: Why have you not eaten food today?

note: Uses bèghị as the inflected negative-perfect form of -bè.

examples.igbo: Ùkòlò osisi ahụ dị omimi nke ukwuu.
examples.english: The hollow of that tree is very deep.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ ùkòlò dị n'ala ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see the hollow in that ground?

gloss: confuse or play trick on or fool someone

examples.igbo: Ọ ghọgburu nne ya n'ahịa.
examples.english: He fooled his mother in the market.

examples.igbo: Aghọgbula m, abụ m onye nkịtị.
examples.english: Don't fool me, I am an ordinary person.

note: Tone on the inflected forms may vary by dialect.

examples.igbo: O mechara nkwà o kwere.
examples.english: He fulfilled the promise he made.

examples.igbo: Biko mee nkwà gị, egbula oge.
examples.english: Please keep your promise, don't waste time.

note: Uses me nkwà in the sense of fulfilling a promise.

gloss: open space beside a stream or river

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-egwuri egwu n'òwòlì mmiri ahụ.
examples.english: The children are playing in that open space beside the stream.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-akọ ugbo n'òwòlì osimiri?
examples.english: Do we farm in the open space by the river?

gloss: except Mmadù niīne bìàsì, bèelụ sò m All the people came except me

examples.igbo: Mmadụ niile bịara, bèelụ sò m.
examples.english: All the people came except me.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-eri ihe niile, bèelụ sò anụ.
examples.english: He eats everything except meat.

examples.igbo: Nnu a gụrụ mmiri, ọ dị mmiri mmiri.
examples.english: This salt is damp, it is wet.

examples.igbo: Kedu ihe mere nnu ji agụ mmiri?
examples.english: Why is the salt damp?

examples.igbo: Ọbịbịa ya bụ eyī uchè nye anyị.
examples.english: His coming was quite unexpected to us.

examples.igbo: Ọ dị eyī uchè na ọ lọtara taa.
examples.english: It is quite unexpected that he returned today.

examples.igbo: O na-aho ahịhịa n'ubi ya taa.
examples.english: He is pulling weeds in his farm today.

examples.igbo: Hoo ahịhịa ahụ na mgbọrọgwụ ya.
examples.english: Uproot that weed with its roots.

note: Imperative hoo is used for the verb stem ho.

gloss: affliction; distress; great trouble (e.g. court cases); danger; evil

examples.igbo: Osòmà dara n'ezinụlọ anyị n'ụbọchị ahụ.
examples.english: Trouble befell our family on that day.

examples.igbo: Kedu ihe kpatara osòmà a n'obodo?
examples.english: What caused this trouble in the town?

examples.igbo: Ọkụkụ ọ kụrụ n'ugbo toro nke ọma.
examples.english: The crops he planted on the farm grew well.

examples.igbo: Ị kụrụ ọkụkụ ọ bụla n'afọ a?
examples.english: Did you plant any crops this year?

note: ọkụkụ more commonly means 'chicken'; here it is used in the 'crop' sense.

gloss: be friends with a thief or thieves

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akpa ùkpa ori n'obodo a.
examples.english: He is friends with thieves in this town.

examples.igbo: Ọ dị njọ ịkpa ùkpa ori.
examples.english: It is bad to be friends with thieves.

examples.igbo: Onye amụma āsị na-eduhie ndị obodo.
examples.english: The false prophet misleads the people of the town.

examples.igbo: Ndị mmadụ chọpụtara na ọ bụ onye amụma āsị.
examples.english: The people found out that he was a false prophet.

examples.igbo: Ndị obodo na-agba egwu alūsị n'ememme ahụ.
examples.english: The townspeople perform traditional religious dances at that festival.

examples.igbo: Ị hụla egwu alūsị ha na-agba?
examples.english: Have you seen the traditional religious dances they perform?

examples.igbo: Biko sàkụta ozi ahụ nye mmadụ niile.
examples.english: Please reply to all with that message.

examples.igbo: Ọ sàkụtara anyị ozi ahụ n'otu oge.
examples.english: He replied to all of us with that message at once.

note: The exact sense of -sàkụta as 'reply to all' is not fully clear to me.

examples.igbo: Echefuru m ebe m tinyere mkpịsị ụlọ.
examples.english: I forgot where I put the house key.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-echefu ihe ọ bụla ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: He forgets everything quickly.

examples.igbo: O raara m ozi n'ahịa.
examples.english: He sent me on an errand to the market.

examples.igbo: Ị raala ya ozi ọ bụla?
examples.english: Have you sent him on any errand?

examples.igbo: Ha fere ǹzà iji kpebie onye ga-aga.
examples.english: They cast lots to decide who would go.

examples.igbo: Anyị ga-efe ǹzà taa.
examples.english: We shall cast lots today.

gloss: console; rock a baby by singing

examples.igbo: Gụgụ̀ nne ya mere ka nwa ahụ hie ụra.
examples.english: His mother's lullaby made the baby fall asleep.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-abụ gụgụ̀ mgbe nwa ya na-ebe akwa.
examples.english: She sings a lullaby whenever her child cries.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-abịa n'ugbo mgbe nile.
examples.english: He always comes to the farm.

examples.igbo: Ị na-arahụ ụra mgbe nile n'ehihie?
examples.english: Do you always sleep in the afternoon?

gloss: (of fruit) fall from tree before it is ripe

examples.igbo: Mkpụrụ ube ahụ dàkworo n'ala tupu o too.
examples.english: Those pear fruits fell to the ground before they ripened.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere mkpụrụ osisi ji adàkwo n'oge a?
examples.english: Why are the fruits falling prematurely at this time?

gloss: once upon a time; at one time; once

examples.igbo: Òfu mgbè, ọ na-ere ahịa n'ebe a.
examples.english: Once, she used to sell here.

examples.igbo: Òfu mgbè ị gara ebe ahụ, gịnị mere?
examples.english: Once you went there, what happened?

examples.igbo: Mgbe abalị dara, ọ jimìrì n'ime ime ụlọ.
examples.english: When night fell, it was very dark inside the room.

examples.igbo: Gbanye ọkụ, n'ihi na ọ jimìrì ebe a.
examples.english: Light a lamp, because it is very dark here.

examples.igbo: O gbara òsiālị n'ụlọ ikpe.
examples.english: He bore witness in court.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-agba òsiālị maka ya?
examples.english: Will you bear witness for him?

examples.igbo: E nwere ụmụ akwụkwọ bèlị ōfu n'oru n'ọnụ ụlọ.
examples.english: There were nineteen students in the classroom.

examples.igbo: Ị zụtara bèlị ōfu n'oru mkpụrụ?
examples.english: Did you buy nineteen seeds?

examples.igbo: O tinyere aka n'òkpù n'okwò ya.
examples.english: He placed his hand on the back of his head.

examples.igbo: Ọkpù n'okwò ya na-egbu ya mgbu.
examples.english: The back of his head is hurting him.

examples.igbo: Dọtị ụta gị, anụ ọhịa na-abịa.
examples.english: Draw your bow, an animal is coming.

examples.igbo: Ọ dọtịrị ụta wee gbaa arụ.
examples.english: He drew the bow and shot.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ekwu okwu ūgha mgbe niile.
examples.english: He always speaks falsehood.

examples.igbo: Ekwula okwu ūgha n'ụlọ ikpe.
examples.english: Do not speak falsehood in court.

examples.igbo: Eze ahụ chịrị obodo anyị afọ iri.
examples.english: That king ruled our town for ten years.

examples.igbo: Ònye na-achị ala a ugbu a?
examples.english: Who is governing this land now?

examples.igbo: O kwuburu m ihe ga-eme.
examples.english: He said beforehand what would happen.

examples.igbo: Kwubu ya tupu ha abịa.
examples.english: Say it beforehand before they come.

examples.igbo: Meghepụ eriri nke akpa ahụ.
examples.english: Untie the rope of that bag.

examples.igbo: Ị meghepụla ọnụ ụzọ ụlọ ahụ?
examples.english: Have you unfastened the door of that house?

examples.igbo: O jiri àlùlù akwado ji ya.
examples.english: He used yamsticks to support his yams.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-ebu àlùlù gaa n'ugbo.
examples.english: The children are carrying yamsticks to the farm.

examples.igbo: O jiri ewu jụrụ àrụ n'ụlọ ya.
examples.english: He used a goat to purify his house by sacrifice.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-eji ọkụkọ jụọ àrụ taa?
examples.english: Will you use a chicken to purify by sacrifice today?

note: The compound jụ àrụ is uncommon in everyday speech; the past/subjunctive forms jụrụ/jụọ may vary by dialect.

gloss: barge into; enter a place unexpectedly and uninvited

examples.igbo: O tibàtara n'ụlọ m n'abalị.
examples.english: He barged into my house at night.

examples.igbo: Tibàtala n'ụlọ m ọzọ!
examples.english: Don't barge into my house again!

examples.igbo: Ihu ya chakere mgbe ọ nụrụ ozi ọma.
examples.english: Her face brightened when she heard the good news.

examples.igbo: Kpakpando na-achake n'elu igwe n'abalị.
examples.english: Stars glow in the sky at night.

gloss: receive money, reward, or bribe for services

examples.igbo: Ị liri ngo n'aka ya?
examples.english: Did you take a bribe from him?

examples.igbo: O kpàchara ntutu isi ya.

examples.igbo: Kpàcha ahịhịa dị n'ogige ahụ.

gloss: the twenty-ninth letter of the Igbo language alphabet; the twenty-third consonant of the Igbo language alphabet

examples.igbo: Ọ ruchanye mmiri ahụ n'ime ite.

examples.english: Do you sell fish to us?

note: Tone and inflection of -kàfìè are uncertain.

examples.igbo: Ị na-etu nwanne gị afà?

examples.igbo: Òtutu mmanya a siri ike?
examples.english: Is the intoxication of this wine strong?

examples.igbo: Ị ga-ekpopụ eze ahụ?

examples.english: He visits his mother in the hospital.

examples.igbo: Ị na-enega ha n'oge ezumike?
examples.english: Do you visit them during holidays?

gloss: roof framework (before thatching or fixing the sheets)

examples.igbo: Ọ gbàara m umē n'oge ihe isi ike.
examples.english: He encouraged me in a time of difficulty.

examples.igbo: Gbàa nwa gị umē ka ọ gaa n'ihu.
examples.english: Encourage your child to move forward.

gloss: make noise with mouth or horn (especially to attract attention)

examples.igbo: O mere ụŋàlà ka ndị mmadụ bịa.
examples.english: He made a noise so that people would come.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji na-eme ụŋàlà n'ụlọ akwụkwọ?
examples.english: Why are you making noise at school?

examples.igbo: Ụlọ ahịa ahụ nwere ìriàbụ̀ọ nà ìtoolū akpa osikapa.
examples.english: That shop has twenty-nine bags of rice.

examples.igbo: Ì nwere ìriàbụ̀ọ nà ìtoolū akpa?
examples.english: Do you have twenty-nine bags?

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ alụlụ Ànì ịnapụ nwata nri ya.
examples.english: It is injustice to snatch a child's food.

examples.igbo: Ha na-eme alụlụ Ànì n'ahịa.
examples.english: They are doing wickedness in the market.

examples.igbo: Onye nkụzi gụsiri ike ahịrịokwu ahụ.
examples.english: The teacher read that sentence forcefully.

examples.igbo: Gụsie ike ka anyị nụ gị.
examples.english: Read forcefully so that we can hear you.

examples.igbo: Nwata takwosịrị mango ahụ.
examples.english: The child ate that mango unripe.

examples.igbo: Atakwosịla mkpụrụ osisi ọ bụla.
examples.english: Don't eat any fruit unripe.

examples.igbo: Dọkịta lere ujiimī nwata ahụ anya.
examples.english: The doctor examined the child's nasal cavity.

examples.igbo: Ujiimī ya na-egbu mgbu mgbe ọ nwere oyi.
examples.english: His nasal cavity aches when he has a cold.

gloss: fried meal made of ground beans; beans bun; beans fritters

examples.igbo: Anyị riri àkàrà na akamu n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: We ate bean fritters and pap in the morning.

examples.igbo: Nne m na-eghe àkàrà n'ahịa.
examples.english: My mother fries bean fritters at the market.

examples.igbo: Ụlọ anyị hiri mmiri n'oké mmiri ozuzo.
examples.english: Our house leaked during the heavy rain.

examples.igbo: Ogbogu ahụ na-ehi mmiri.
examples.english: That drum leaks water.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akpasu nne ya iwe.
examples.english: He provokes his mother.

examples.igbo: Kpasula nwata ahụ iwe.
examples.english: Don't provoke that child.

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ tidara oche n'ala.
examples.english: The child knocked down the chair.

examples.igbo: Atidala ihe ndị ahụ.
examples.english: Don't knock those things down.

examples.igbo: Ọ raara nwa ya ǹra n'ụtụtụ.
examples.english: She combed her child's hair in the morning.

examples.igbo: Raa nwa gị ǹra tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Comb your child's hair before you go out.

examples.igbo: Ya nà ònwe yā bịara ebe a.
examples.english: He himself came here.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ ya nà ònwe yā mere ya?
examples.english: Is it he himself who did it?

examples.igbo: Aja ngwe ụlọ ya dị ọcha.
examples.english: The wall of her house is clean.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ aja ngwe ọhụrụ ahụ?
examples.english: Did you see that new wall?

examples.igbo: O mejuru ite ahụ na mmiri.
examples.english: He filled that pot with water.

examples.igbo: Oge ọrụ ahụ mejuola n'ụtụtụ taa.
examples.english: The work time has completed this morning.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-anakọta ego n'aka ndị ahịa.
examples.english: She is collecting money from customers.

examples.igbo: Ha na-anakọta mkpụrụ osisi n'ubi taa.
examples.english: They are collecting fruits in the farm today.

examples.igbo: Niī, were ego a n'aka m.
examples.english: Here, take this money from me.

examples.igbo: Niī, jide ya nke ọma, biko.
examples.english: Here, hold it well, please.

examples.igbo: Ha kpochapuru ahịhịa niile n'ubi.
examples.english: They cleaned away all the weeds in the farm.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-ekpochapụ ụmụ ahụhụ n'ụlọ.
examples.english: She is exterminating insects in the house.

gloss: (literally) scrape for the benefit of oneself; (fig.) enjoy; scrounge

examples.igbo: Ọ na-akpachalị ego ụlọ akwụkwọ nwa ya.
examples.english: He is scrounging his child's school fees.

examples.igbo: Ha kpachara ji ahụ niile n'ubi.
examples.english: They scraped all those yams for themselves in the farm.

note: The figurative sense of -kpachalị is somewhat colloquial; the sentences reflect idiomatic usage.

examples.igbo: O nyere m ǹdụ̀mọọdụ banyere ọrụ.
examples.english: He gave me advice about work.

examples.igbo: Onye nkuzi na-enye ụmụaka ǹdụ̀mọọdụ ọma.
examples.english: The teacher is giving the children good advice.

examples.igbo: Osisi ahụ gbamiri mkpòlògwù n'ime ala.
examples.english: That tree sent roots deep into the ground.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-agbami mkpòlògwù n'ime ala ugbu a.
examples.english: It is sending roots deep into the soil now.

examples.igbo: Ọ gbachara nwa ya isi taa.
examples.english: She trimmed her child's hair today.

examples.igbo: Gbacha isi gị tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Trim your hair before you go out.

examples.igbo: Anwụ gbasiri ụrọ ike n'oge ọkọchị.
examples.english: The sun toughened the clay in the dry season.

examples.igbo: Gbasie eriri a ike ka ọ ghara ịdọka.
examples.english: Toughen this rope so it does not break.

note: Used -gbasì in the transitive sense 'make tough/harden'; some speakers may prefer a different construction.

gloss: commit crime, offence; break law; sin

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ mebiri iwu obodo n'abalị.
examples.english: That man broke the law of the land at night.

examples.igbo: Ị mebiri iwu, ị ga-akwụ ụgwọ.
examples.english: You broke the law, you will pay a fine.

examples.igbo: Gotelụ m azụ n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: Buy fish for me at the market today.

examples.igbo: O nwere ike ịgotelụ gị akwa?
examples.english: Can she buy cloth for you?

note: Used imperative and infinitive forms of -gotelụ; benefactive forms can vary by dialect.

examples.igbo: Ọ na-agàla ngàla maka uwe ọhụrụ ya.
examples.english: She is proud because of her new dress.

examples.igbo: Ị na-agàla ngàla n'ihi ego gị?
examples.english: Are you proud because of your money?

examples.igbo: O gụpụrụ ego ahụ n'ihu anyị.
examples.english: He counted out that money in front of us.

examples.igbo: Gụpụ̀ mkpụrụ osisi iri n'ime efere.
examples.english: Count out ten seeds into the plate.

examples.igbo: Mama zụtara agbidi n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: Mom bought solid palm oil at the market today.

examples.igbo: Agbidi a siri ike, ọ dị mma maka ofe.
examples.english: This palm oil is solid, it is good for soup.

examples.igbo: M na-eche echiche banyere njem ahụ.
examples.english: I am thinking about that journey.

examples.igbo: Chee echiche tupu i zaa ajụjụ.
examples.english: Think before you answer the question.

examples.igbo: Aka ntadide ya na-ewe ndị agbataobi iwe.
examples.english: His stinginess annoys the neighbours.

examples.igbo: Aka ntadide adịghị mma n'ezinụlọ ma ọlị.
examples.english: Stinginess is not good in a family at all.

examples.igbo: Anyị gụrụ mkpụrụ osisi ahụ n'ìriga.
examples.english: We counted those seeds in tens.

examples.igbo: Ego ahụ dị n'ìriga, ọ bụghị n'otu n'otu.
examples.english: The money is in tens, not one by one.

note: Ìriga as 'tens' is less common; examples show the grouping-by-tens sense.

examples.igbo: Nne m tinyere ekē ọkụkọ n'ofe ahụ.
examples.english: My mother put the fowl gizzard in that soup.

examples.igbo: Ị riri ekē ọkụkọ ahụ niile?
examples.english: Did you eat all of that fowl gizzard?

note: Tone on 'eke' uncertain; sense and idiom are fine.

examples.igbo: Ọ firi aka n'ihu nwa ya.
examples.english: She wiped her child's face with her hand.

examples.igbo: Fie mmiri ahụ n'ala ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Wipe that water off the floor quickly.

note: The perfective form 'firi' is inferred; meaning is clear from context.

examples.igbo: Ndị ohi gbabidoro anyị n'ụzọ.
examples.english: Thieves waylaid us on the road.

examples.igbo: Gbabido ụzọ ahụ ka ụmụ ewu ghara ịpụ.
examples.english: Block that path so the goats don't get out.

gloss: type of music; set of three ceremonial drums, used with òjà during the Òfalà feast

examples.igbo: Ha kụrụ òkàǹgà n'ememme Òfalà.
examples.english: They played òkàǹgà at the Òfalà festival.

examples.igbo: Ị nụrụ ụda òkàǹgà n'abalị ụnyaahụ?
examples.english: Did you hear the sound of òkàǹgà last night?

note: The drum set's name and use are specialised; the sentences are plausible but I would verify details.

gloss: kind of bean that provokes thirst

examples.igbo: Anyị ji òkpoòdùdù sie ofe taa.
examples.english: We cooked soup with òkpoòdùdù today.

examples.igbo: Olee otú i si rie òkpoòdùdù n'enweghị mmiri?
examples.english: How did you eat òkpoòdùdù without water?

note: A rare bean name; spelling taken as given.

examples.igbo: Akwụkwọ osisi na-acha èdoèdò n'oge ọkọchị.
examples.english: The tree leaves turn yellow in the dry season.

examples.igbo: Olee ihe mere uwe gị ji cha èdoèdò?
examples.english: Why is your dress yellow?

examples.igbo: Agwa ọcha ahụ riri àrì taa.
examples.english: Those white beans fermented today.

examples.igbo: Ị hụla na agwa ahụ riri àrì?
examples.english: Have you seen that those beans have fermented?

note: The collocation 'rì àrì' with beans is specialised; form may vary by dialect.

examples.igbo: Nwa ahụ na-akwa ụkwalà n'abalị niile.
examples.english: That child coughed all night.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji na-akwa ụkwalà?
examples.english: Why are you coughing?

examples.igbo: Ụzọ a gbara ngịrịgọ nke ukwuu.
examples.english: This road has many bends.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere ụzọ ahụ ji agba ngịrịgọ?
examples.english: Why does that road wind so much?

note: The given spelling 'ngị̀rị̀g̣ọ̀' is unusual; I wrote it as 'ngịrịgọ'.

examples.igbo: Ndị ọrụ na-agba ji n'ugbo taa.
examples.english: The workers are staking the yams in the farm today.

examples.igbo: Ị gbara ji niile n'ugbo gị?
examples.english: Have you staked all the yams in your farm?

examples.igbo: Nna m na-akụ mmanya n'ụlọ oriri.
examples.english: My father mixes wine in the restaurant.

examples.igbo: Kụọ mmanya a tupu ndị ọbịa abịa.
examples.english: Mix this wine before the guests come.

gloss: most important part of the story

examples.igbo: Gịnị bụ ànì okwū akụkọ ahụ?
examples.english: What is the main point of that story?

examples.igbo: Ànì okwū ya bụ na ọ dịghị mfe ịzụ ehi.
examples.english: Its main point is that rearing cattle is not easy.

gloss: miss a step; step into a wrong place or spot

examples.igbo: O na-ezòfìe ụkwụ n'ụzọ ahụ.
examples.english: He misses a step on that road.

examples.igbo: Zòfìe ụkwụ n'ebe ahụ, ị ga-ada.
examples.english: Miss a step there, and you will fall.

gloss: small round jingling metal bells worn while dancing; strung bells

examples.igbo: Ìjèlè ya na-ada ụda mgbe ọ na-agba egwu.
examples.english: Her jingling bells sound when she dances.

examples.igbo: Ndị na-agba egwu yi ìjèlè n'ụkwụ.
examples.english: The dancers wear jingling bells on their ankles.

examples.igbo: O gbalụrụ iru mgbe ọ nụrụ akụkọ ahụ.
examples.english: He looked gloomy when he heard that news.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i ji agbalụ iru?
examples.english: Why are you looking gloomy?

examples.igbo: Gịnī zị? Ị chọghị ịga ahịa taa?
examples.english: What? You do not want to go to the market today?

examples.igbo: Gịnī zị? Biko kwuo ihe mere.
examples.english: What then? Please say what happened.

examples.igbo: Nwata ahụ na-ayọta ego n'aka ndị na-aga ahịa.
examples.english: That child begs money from those going to the market.

examples.igbo: Yọta mmiri, anyị ga-aṅụ ya.
examples.english: Beg for water, and we will drink it.

gloss: tell story; tell story in which song features; tell tale, fable

examples.igbo: Nne m na-arọ irọ mgbe anyị nọ n'ọnụ ọkụ.
examples.english: My mother tells stories when we are around the fire.

examples.igbo: Rọọ anyị irọ banyere mbe na agụ.
examples.english: Tell us a story about the tortoise and the leopard.

examples.igbo: O gbòrò akwà n'elu tebụl.
examples.english: She covered the table with cloth.

examples.igbo: Gbòọ akwà n'elu nwa ahụ.
examples.english: Cover the child with cloth.

examples.igbo: Nwoke ahụ dara ǹgwọlō n'ụkwụ aka nri.
examples.english: That man is lame in the right leg.

examples.igbo: Ị dara ǹgwọlō? Gịnị mere gị?
examples.english: Are you lame? What happened to you?

note: The perfect form 'dara ǹgwọlō' is used for the state of being lame; the tone marking of the complement follows the entry.

examples.igbo: Onye ọkpụkpụ pịrị alūsị osisi n'ahịa.
examples.english: The carver carved a wooden image at the market.

examples.igbo: Pịa alūsị a n'ụlọ arụsị ngwa ngwa.
examples.english: Carve this image in the shrine quickly.

examples.igbo: M zipùrù letà nye nwanne m.
examples.english: I posted a letter to my brother.

examples.igbo: Zipù letà a tupu ọ gaa.
examples.english: Post this letter before he leaves.

examples.igbo: Ọ dàjụgo n'ụlọ akwụkwọ mgbe ụmụaka laara.
examples.english: It is quiet in the school when the children have gone home.

examples.igbo: Ọ dàjụgo? Gịnị mere ebe a ji dị jụụ?
examples.english: Is it quiet? Why is this place so quiet?

examples.igbo: O pịachiri akwa ndị ahụ n'igbe.
examples.english: She folded those clothes in the box.

examples.igbo: Pịachie uwe gị tupu ị pụọ.
examples.english: Fold your clothes before you go out.

examples.igbo: O bòkasìrì achịcha ahụ maka ụmụaka.
examples.english: He divided the bread into pieces for the children.

examples.igbo: Bòkasìa anụ ahụ tupu ị sie ya.
examples.english: Divide the meat into pieces before you cook it.

examples.igbo: Afọ ōsịsa na-agba nwa ahụ n'oge ọkọchị.
examples.english: The child has dysentery in the dry season.

examples.igbo: Ị nwere afọ ōsịsa? Gaa ụlọ ọgwụ ozugbo.
examples.english: Do you have dysentery? Go to the hospital immediately.

gloss: mask of the masquerader; masquerader's cloth

examples.igbo: Efe mmụọ̄ ya na-acha ọcha n'emume.
examples.english: His masquerader's cloth is white at the festival.

examples.igbo: Ị hụrụ efe mmụọ̄ ha? Ọ mara mma.
examples.english: Did you see their masquerader's cloth? It is beautiful.

examples.igbo: Nkịta ahụ kpùrù ọkpụkpụ n'ọnū ya.
examples.english: The dog carried a bone in its mouth.

examples.igbo: Kpù ego ahụ n'ọnū ka onye ọ bụla ghara ịhụ.
examples.english: Carry that money in your mouth so that nobody sees it.

gloss: tall standing drum used to play abìà music

examples.igbo: Ha kụrụ ìgbà ogwè n'abalị ahụ.
examples.english: They played the tall standing drum that night.

examples.igbo: Ị nụrụ ụda ìgbà ogwè? Ọ na-ada n'emume abìà.
examples.english: Did you hear the sound of the tall standing drum? It sounds at the abìà festival.

gloss: be extraordinary; be exceptional; be unique; be remarkably different from usual

examples.igbo: Uwe Ada pụrụ ichè n'ahịa taa.
examples.english: Ada's dress is unique in the market today.

examples.igbo: Ọ pụrụ ichè n'ezie, ọ bụghị?
examples.english: It is truly extraordinary, isn't it?

gloss: break (by itself) Àkwa àgbakpọgo The egg has broken (e.g. while being boiled)

examples.igbo: Àkwa ahụ àgbakpọgo n'ite.
examples.english: That egg has broken in the pot.

examples.igbo: Kpuchie ite ahụ ka àkwa ghara ịgbakpọ.
examples.english: Cover that pot so the egg will not break.

examples.igbo: Ha kpọrọ ya n'ǹgàmàsù maka esemokwu ala.
examples.english: They summoned him to the native court over a land dispute.

examples.igbo: Gịnị ka ǹgàmàsù kpebiri n'okwu gị?
examples.english: What did the native court decide in your case?

gloss: spread (a cloth or something intended to dry)

examples.igbo: O ghasara akwa ya n'èzí ka ọ kpọọ nkụ.
examples.english: She spread her cloth outside to dry.

examples.igbo: Ghasaa osikapa ahụ n'àkwà tupu ọ kpọọ nkụ.
examples.english: Spread that rice on the mat before it dries.

examples.igbo: Mèelụ anyị èbelè, Chineke, n'ụbọchị a.
examples.english: Have mercy on us, God, on this day.

examples.igbo: Ndị mmadụ tiri mkpu, 'Mèelụ anyị èbelè!'
examples.english: The people shouted, 'Have mercy on us!'

examples.igbo: O nyefere m ego ahụ n'ahịa.
examples.english: He handed over the money to me at the market.

examples.igbo: Nyefee ya ego ahụ tupu ọ laa.
examples.english: Hand over the money to him before he leaves.

examples.igbo: O bipụtara akwụkwọ ahụ n'ụlọ ọrụ.
examples.english: He printed out the document at the office.

examples.igbo: Bipụta akwụkwọ a tupu nzukọ amalite.
examples.english: Print out this document before the meeting starts.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-eje ije n'ụlọ akwụkwọ kwa ụtụtụ.
examples.english: We walk to school every morning.

examples.igbo: Ị na-eje ije ka ọ bụ ị na-anya ụgbọala?
examples.english: Are you walking or driving?

examples.igbo: Mgbè afù, anyị bi n'ime ime obodo.
examples.english: At that time, we lived in the village.

examples.igbo: Mgbè afù ị nọ n'ụlọ?
examples.english: Were you at home then?

note: afù may be dialectal; standard is mgbe ahụ.

examples.igbo: Ezinụlọ anyị na-ebi n'udo na nkwekọ.
examples.english: Our family lives in peace and harmony.

examples.igbo: Ị ga-akwado nkwekọ a?
examples.english: Will you support this agreement?

examples.igbo: Bìli ọtọ̄, ndị ọbịa abịala.
examples.english: Stand up, the visitors have arrived.

examples.igbo: Gịnị mere i jighị bìli ọtọ̄ mgbe o bịara?
examples.english: Why didn't you stand up when he came?

gloss: take food; eat, especially first in the morning

examples.igbo: Gbaa àzị̀ tupu ị gaa ọrụ.
examples.english: Eat something before you go to work.

examples.igbo: Ị gbara àzị̀ taa?
examples.english: Have you eaten today?

gloss: a speech used instead of another that would be considered harsh, impolite, or unpleasant; euphemism

examples.igbo: Ndị okenye na-eji ǹkwuma ekwu okwu n'ihu ụmụaka.
examples.english: Elders use euphemisms when speaking in front of children.

examples.igbo: Ejila okwu ọjọọ kwuo ya, jiri ǹkwuma.
examples.english: Don't use harsh words for it, use a euphemism.

note: The word is correct but it belongs to a rather formal register, so the everyday examples feel slightly bookish.

gloss: shake off (e.g. dust or sand) by beating the surface with palm of the hand

examples.igbo: Tichaa uzuzu n'uwe gị tupu ị banye n'ụlọ.
examples.english: Shake the dust off your clothes before you enter the house.

examples.igbo: O ji aka na-aticha ájá n'ụkwụ ya.
examples.english: She is beating the sand off her feet with her hand.

gloss: used to express a point often when speaking; exactly

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ ya gbàm ka m kwuru.
examples.english: That is exactly what I said.

examples.igbo: Ị ghọtara ya gbàm?
examples.english: Do you understand it exactly?

note: Gbàm is colloquial and hard to pin down; these two are the commonest ways I hear it used.

examples.igbo: Ụmụaka na-ezizo onye nkụzi ha.
examples.english: The children are mimicking their teacher.

examples.igbo: Ànyị nà ònwe ānyị rụrụ ọrụ ubi ahụ.
examples.english: We ourselves did that farm work.

examples.igbo: Ọ bụ ànyị nà ònwe ānyị zụtara ọkụkọ a?
examples.english: Is it we ourselves that bought this chicken?

note: The phrase is more commonly written 'anyị n'onwe anyị'; I used the expanded form given.

gloss: keep something, especially a object, in the wrong place

examples.igbo: Ọ na-adoghàrị̀ akwụkwọ m n'ime ite.
examples.english: He keeps misplacing my book in the pot.

examples.igbo: Ị na-adoghàrị̀ uwe gị n'ime akpa nri?
examples.english: Do you keep misplacing your clothes in the food bag?

gloss: take someone away or out from somewhere or something

examples.igbo: Ndị uwe ojii kpọpụrụ ya n'ụlọ.
examples.english: The police took him away from the house.

examples.igbo: Kpọpụ ya n'ime ụgbọ ahụ ugbu a.
examples.english: Take him out of that vehicle right now.

examples.igbo: Anyị zuru ike ọrụ taa niile.
examples.english: We rested from work all day today.

examples.igbo: Zuo ike ọrụ tupu ị daa.
examples.english: Rest from work before you collapse.

note: Entry's ọlū appears dialectal; standard modern orthography uses ọrụ for 'work'.

examples.igbo: Isi na-arọ m alụ n'abalị a.
examples.english: My head is throbbing tonight.

examples.igbo: Ụkwụ rọrọ ya alụ n'abalị niile.
examples.english: His leg throbbed all night.

examples.igbo: Anyị gara òkìkà mmānya n'ụlọ nna ya.
examples.english: We went to the ceremonial drinking at his father's house.

examples.igbo: Òkìkà mmānya a ọ ga-adị echi?
examples.english: Will this feast take place tomorrow?

examples.igbo: Osisi ukwu dara gbara n'okporo ụzọ.
examples.english: A big tree fell and lay across the road.

examples.igbo: Gịnị gbara n'ọnụ ụzọ ụlọ anyị?
examples.english: What is lying across our doorway?

note: -gbà has several senses; these examples target the 'lie across' sense.

examples.igbo: Anyị na-atụ nkụ n'èzí ụlọ taa.
examples.english: We are splitting firewood outside the house today.

examples.igbo: Tụọ nkụ ahụ, anyị ga-esi nri.
examples.english: Split that firewood, we will cook.

examples.igbo: Ọ chọbụrụ ịga ahịa n'isi ụtụtụ.
examples.english: She wanted to go to the market early in the morning.

examples.igbo: Anyị chọbụrụ ịpụ, ma mmiri zoro.
examples.english: We intended to leave, but it rained.

note: Uses the inflected past form chọbụrụ.

gloss: swell and cover up something completely

examples.igbo: Iju mmiri zakpọrọ ubi anyị kpamkpam.
examples.english: Floodwater covered our farm completely.

examples.igbo: Ọzịza zakpọrọ ụkwụ ya niile n'abalị a?
examples.english: Did swelling cover his whole leg tonight?

note: This verb is uncommon; examples are based on the sense of swelling/flood covering completely.

examples.igbo: Àkù ya dị n'ime nnukwu ubi ya.
examples.english: His wealth is in his large farm.

examples.igbo: Ị na-achọ àkù ma ọ bụ mmụta?
examples.english: Are you seeking wealth or education?

examples.igbo: Ị lofiri ihe m kwuru ụnyaahụ.
examples.english: You thought wrongly about what I said yesterday.

examples.igbo: Ị lofiri na ọ ga-abịa taa?
examples.english: Did you think wrongly that he would come today?
